question: Which of the following statements concerning extinctive prescription is correct? (In cases of dispute, according to precedents)
A: A claim for damages arising from nonperformance of an obligation does not extinguish together with the original claim even if the original claim is extinguished by prescription.
B: The claim concerning work by a person who has undertaken a contract, to which the 3-year short-term extinctive prescription applies, means only the claim for the price of the work, and the contractor’s claim for the establishment of a mortgage, as a claim incidental to that work, does not fall under a claim concerning the work of a person who has undertaken a contract.
C: A junior secured interest holder is a person who directly benefits from the extinction of the secured claim under the senior secured interest, and therefore may invoke the completion of extinctive prescription concerning the secured claim under the senior secured interest.
D: In a lawsuit seeking performance of the procedure for cancellation registration of mortgage establishment registration, brought by a real guarantor on the ground of the nonexistence or extinction of the secured debt, even if the creditor, who is also the mortgagee, prevails by seeking a judgment dismissing the claim and asserting the existence of the secured claim, the creditor’s said act of responding to the lawsuit does not constitute a "judicial claim," which is a ground for interruption of prescription with respect to the secured claim.
E: Where a creditor attaches or provisionally attaches the debtor’s claim against a third-party obligor, the effect of definitive interruption of prescription arises with respect to the debtor’s claim against the third-party obligor.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2003DA16238]": "The judgment of the lower court is reversed, and the case is remanded to the Seoul High Court."}

{"[2014DA211978]": "We decide the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. In the case of a construction contract concerning real property, the ownership of the subject matter completed by the contractor’s labor and expenditures, in principle, belongs to the contractor; however, if otherwise stipulated by a special agreement between the contractee and the contractor, or if there are other special circumstances, it is originally acquired by the contractee. Accordingly, Civil Act Article 666 grants the contractor, in such a case, a right to demand establishment of a mortgage over the subject matter, thereby enabling the contractor to receive payment of the construction price from the subject matter in a de facto preferential manner (see Supreme Court Judgment rendered on March 27, 2008, 2007DA78616, 78623). In light of this, where, in a contract for building construction, the contractor completes the building through his own labor and expenditures and ownership thereof belongs to the contractor, the subcontractor who was subcontracted part of the building construction from the contractor shall also be deemed to have, against the contractor, a right to demand establishment of a mortgage under Civil Act Article 666 (hereinafter referred to as the “right to demand establishment of a mortgage”).\\n\\nMeanwhile, a claim for construction price arising from the subcontracted work is subject to the short-term extinctive prescription period of 3 years pursuant to Civil Act Article 163 subparagraph 3, and the same applies to claims incidental to such work (see, e.g., Supreme Court Judgment rendered on November 12, 2009, 2008DA41451). Since the right to demand establishment of a mortgage is a claim under the law of obligations seeking performance of the procedure for registration of establishment of a mortgage in order to secure the construction price claim, and thus constitutes a claim incidental to the work, its extinctive prescription period should likewise be deemed to be 3 years.\\n\\nThe subcontractor’s right to demand establishment of a mortgage against the contractor in a building construction project is established when the contractor acquires ownership of the building, and, barring special circumstances, the right may be exercised from that time; however, the holder of ownership of the building is determined according to the contents of the construction contract concluded between the contractee and the contractor without the subcontractor’s involvement, and moreover, even where, after completion of the building, legal disputes continue regarding the attribution of ownership, etc., making it objectively difficult for the subcontractor to know whether he may exercise the right to demand establishment of a mortgage against the contractor, to hold that extinctive prescription runs from the time the claim arose even when the subcontractor did not know this without negligence would not accord with justice and equity, nor would it be consistent with the rationale of the extinctive prescription system. Therefore, in such a case, it is appropriate to deem that extinctive prescription runs from the time when it objectively became knowable that the subcontractor could exercise the right to demand establishment of a mortgage (see Supreme Court Judgment rendered on July 13, 1993, 92DA39822; Supreme Court Judgment rendered on February 11, 2003, 99DA66427, 73371, etc.).\\n\\n2. According to the reasoning of the lower appellate judgment and the record, the following facts can be found.\\n\\n(1) The original co-owners of the instant land, as indicated in the lower appellate court’s decision (hereinafter referred to as the “original co-owners”), obtained a building permit in their own names around August 2, 2002, and around September 2002 entrusted Ecell General Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Ecell General Construction”) with the construction of the instant building; the Plaintiff, around October 14, 2002, subcontracted from Ecell General Construction the structural frame construction of the instant building and proceeded therewith, but around March 20, 2003, suspended it due to Ecell General Construction’s bankruptcy.\\n\\n(2) The co-ownership relation concerning the instant land continued to change due to transfers of shares. Around April 2003, the Defendant entrusted the construction of the instant building to the then share owners of the instant land, and then subcontracted the suspended frame construction to the Plaintiff for construction price of KRW 1,517,945,000.\\n\\n(3) The Plaintiff completed the frame construction of the instant building around July 28, 2003, and around June 1, 2004, the construction price was increased with the Defendant to KRW 1,602,117,200, but the Plaintiff did not receive the construction price from the Defendant, and the Defendant was unable to properly carry out the subsequent processes.\\n\\n(4) Around September 16, 2004, the Defendant agreed with the then share owners of the instant land that, by December 20, 2004, it would pay all expenses incurred by such owners and purchase the instant land, but if it failed to do so, it would waive all rights concerning the construction of the instant building and would not object even if the work were entrusted to a third party. However, it failed to perform the above obligations, including the purchase of the land, by December 20, 2004.\\n\\n(5) Accordingly, around January 10, 2005, the then share owners of the instant land entrusted the construction of the instant building to Seungwon Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Seungwon Construction”).\\n\\n(6) The Plaintiff, while the original co-owners were still listed as the name holders of the building permit as of around August 2005, applied for a provisional attachment against the instant building based on the above frame construction price claim and, on August 29, 2005, obtained a provisional attachment decision from the Seoul Central District Court in Case No. 2005Kadan4352. Pursuant to the entrustment for registration of said provisional attachment, a registration of preservation of ownership in the name of the original co-owners was entered for the instant building, which had not yet been completed, under receipt No. 79305, dated August 30, 2005, at the Seoul Central District Court.\\n\\n(7) Thereafter, around December 1, 2006, 14 persons, including Soin, who were the then share owners of the instant land, alleging that they had originally acquired ownership of the instant building, filed a lawsuit against the above original co-owners seeking cancellation registration of the registration of preservation of ownership concerning the instant building, and against the Plaintiff seeking a declaration of consent to such cancellation registration (hereinafter referred to as the “related case”).\\n\\n(8) In the first instance of the related case (Seoul Central District Court 2006GAHAP103510), the court found that, at the time the Defendant concluded the construction contract concerning the instant building, it intended to vest ownership of the building in the share owners of the instant land; therefore, as of around July 28, 2003, the date on which the Plaintiff completed the frame construction, ownership of the instant building, which had the form and structure of an independent building in social common sense, had vested in the then share owners of the instant land. Accordingly, on November 15, 2007, it rendered a judgment partially accepting the claim, and some parties appealed therefrom.\\n\\n(9) During the pendency of the appellate trial of said case below (Seoul High Court 2008NA17801), on March 4, 2009, the Plaintiff, as a creditor of construction price against the Defendant, filed an independent party intervention action (Seoul High Court 2009NA22282) against some of the original co-owners, subrogating the Defendant, seeking cancellation of the registration of preservation of ownership concerning the instant building and confirmation of ownership.\\n\\n(10) In the appellate trial of the above related case, the court determined that the instant building acquired the form and structure of an independent building through the Defendant’s labor and expenditures, but that it was insufficient to conclude that, at the time the Defendant concluded the construction contract, the parties agreed to vest ownership of the building in the share owners of the instant land. Accordingly, it determined that the Defendant originally acquired ownership of the instant building around July 28, 2003, and on June 25, 2009, it rendered a judgment that accepted the portion of the Plaintiff’s independent party intervention action seeking cancellation of the registration of preservation of ownership, dismissed the remaining claims, and rejected the portion of the principal action claim incompatible therewith. This judgment became final and conclusive when, on August 25, 2011, the Supreme Court, in appeal (Supreme Court 2009DA67443, 2009DA67450), rendered a judgment dismissing the appeal.\\n\\n(11) Meanwhile, Seungwon Construction completed the instant building around June 2007, while the first instance of the above related case was pending.\\n\\n(12) On March 26, 2013, the Plaintiff filed the instant lawsuit seeking performance of the procedure for registration of establishment of a mortgage concerning the instant building, as an exercise of the right to demand establishment of a mortgage against the Defendant.\\n\\n3. We examine the above factual relationship in light of the legal principles stated above.\\n\\n(1) Around April 2003, the Defendant entrusted the construction of the instant building from the original co-owners and subcontracted the frame construction among such work to the Plaintiff. Thus, around July 28, 2003, the date on which the Plaintiff completed the frame construction, the Defendant originally acquired ownership of the instant building, which, though incomplete, had the form and structure of an independent building in social common sense; therefore, the Plaintiff’s right to demand establishment of a mortgage against the Defendant arose around July 28, 2003.\\n\\n(2) However, from the factual relationship stated above, the following circumstances can be found. That is, ① the Plaintiff’s right to demand establishment of a mortgage, which arose from the Defendant, as contractor, originally acquiring ownership of the instant building, depends on whether, in the construction contract for the instant building concluded between the share owners of the instant land and the Defendant, there was a special agreement vesting ownership of the building in the contractee, and thus whether the Plaintiff could exercise the right against the Defendant, as contractor, is determined accordingly; the Plaintiff was in the position of a third party who could not know the detailed contents of said construction contract; ② pursuant to the agreement made with the share owners of the instant land, the Defendant, after December 20, 2004, waived all rights concerning the construction of the building and exercised no rights whatsoever concerning the instant building, and appears not to have been involved at all in the process by which the share owners of the instant land entrusted the remaining work to Seungwon Construction and completed the building; ③ as the Plaintiff’s application for provisional attachment was granted, a registration of preservation of ownership in the name of the original co-owners was entered for the instant building on August 30, 2005, and thus the Plaintiff appears to have believed from around that time that the original co-owners were the owners of the instant building; ④ the instant building was completed through three construction contracts, and the contractee and contractor differed in each construction contract, so the legal relationship regarding original acquisition of ownership cannot be said to have been objectively clear; and ⑤ the above related case, in which such legal relationship was the issue, was already pending in the first instance around June 2007, when the instant building was completed, and only after the first instance judgment holding the share owners of the instant land to be the original acquirers, the appellate judgment holding the Defendant to be the original acquirer, and finally the Supreme Court judgment rendered on August 25, 2011, was the fact that the Defendant was the original acquirer established.\\n\\n(3) Considering these circumstances in their totality, it is reasonable to see that, until the date of the Supreme Court judgment in the above related case was rendered, the Plaintiff was in a situation where it was objectively difficult to know whether it could exercise the right to demand establishment of a mortgage against the Defendant, and that it did not know this without negligence. Nevertheless, holding that the 3-year extinctive prescription runs from the time the Plaintiff’s right to demand establishment of a mortgage arose would not accord with justice and equity. Therefore, it is proper to deem that extinctive prescription runs from August 25, 2011, when the Supreme Court judgment in the above related case was rendered and it was objectively confirmed that the Plaintiff, as subcontractor, could exercise the right against the Defendant, as contractor. Since the instant lawsuit was filed on March 26, 2013, before the lapse of the 3-year extinctive prescription period from that date, it shall be deemed that extinctive prescription regarding the Plaintiff’s right to demand establishment of a mortgage has not been completed.\\n\\nThe lower appellate court, on the same purport, dismissed the Defendant’s defense of extinctive prescription concerning the Plaintiff’s right to demand establishment of a mortgage, and in so doing committed no error, as asserted in the grounds of appeal, in exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the starting point of extinctive prescription, etc.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so decided, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2016DA232597]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Basic factual relations\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be found.\\n\\na. Bulhwi General Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Bulhwi General Construction”) borrowed KRW 250 million from the third party and, on 2005. 8. 19., made in the name of the third party a provisional registration for the right to claim transfer of ownership (hereinafter referred to as “the provisional security registration in this case”) with respect to 19,080 square meters of forest land in Icheon-si (omitted) (hereinafter referred to as “the forest land in this case”) as security therefor. On 2006. 3. 10., the third party made a principal registration (hereinafter referred to as “the principal registration in this case”) based on the provisional security registration in this case with respect to the forest land in this case, without going through the liquidation procedure prescribed by the Act on Provisional Registration Security, etc. (hereinafter referred to as “the Provisional Registration Security Act”).\\n\\nb. Around 2006. 5. 1., Bulhwi General Construction delivered to the Plaintiff a written undertaking stating that “if the Plaintiff performs subrogated payment of KRW 400 million to the third party, it will cancel the principal registration in this case, which is void for lack of cause, transfer the provisional security registration in this case into the Plaintiff’s name, and issue and deliver a promissory note in the amount of KRW 600 million with a term of 1 year (interest at 50% per annum).” It requested subrogated payment of the obligation secured by the provisional security registration in this case. On 2006. 5. 9., the Plaintiff, with the consent of the third party, paid KRW 400 million to the third party and thereby performed subrogated payment of the obligation secured by the provisional security registration in this case.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Bulhwi General Construction and the third party agreed on 2006. 5. 9. to make a registration of transfer of ownership with respect to the forest land in this case in the name of Elim Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Elim Construction”). Accordingly, on 2006. 5. 10., with respect to the forest land in this case, a registration of transfer of ownership was made from the third party to Elim Construction on the basis of a sale dated 2006. 5. 9. On 2008. 7. 25., Elim Construction made a registration of creation of a mortgage over the forest land in this case in the amount of the maximum secured claim of KRW 1.5 billion, with the Defendant as the mortgagee (hereinafter referred to as “the mortgage in this case”).\\n\\nc. As the Defendant filed an application for a voluntary auction based on the mortgage in this case with Suwon District Court Yeoju Branch Case No. 2010TAGYEONG9585, auction proceedings commenced (hereinafter referred to as “the auction proceedings in this case”), and the auction court set the deadline for filing a demand for distribution as 2013. 2. 4. on 2012. 11. 6. The Plaintiff submitted to the auction court on 2013. 10. 14. a “report of rights by a holder of a provisional registration security right.” On 2014. 12. 17., the auction court rendered a decision permitting sale, and on the distribution date of 2015. 2. 25., prepared a distribution schedule providing for the distribution of KRW 1,199,866,145 to the Defendant as the second-ranked creditor, and the Plaintiff appeared on the said distribution date and objected to the entire amount distributed to the Defendant.\\n\\nd. The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit against the Defendant under Suwon District Court Case No. 2010GAHAP12411, seeking cancellation of the mortgage in this case, alleging that the principal registration in this case was a registration void for lack of cause and therefore the registration of transfer of ownership in the name of Elim Construction and the mortgage in this case were invalid. The Plaintiff prevailed at first instance but lost on appeal, and the appellate judgment became final and conclusive as rendered by the Supreme Court. The purport of the appellate judgment was that “although the principal registration in this case is a registration void for lack of cause, Bulhwi General Construction and the third party agreed to make a registration of transfer of ownership with respect to the forest land in this case in the name of Elim Construction, and pursuant to that agreement, they directly made a registration of transfer of ownership from the third party to Elim Construction without omitting the cancellation registration procedure for the principal registration in this case; therefore, this is a valid registration conforming to the substantive legal relationship.”\\n\\n2. Defendant’s grounds of appeal concerning whether the Plaintiff is a creditor entitled to receive distribution\\na. A person who has performed payment for a debtor may, at the same time as the payment, be subrogated to the creditor with the creditor’s consent (Article 480(1) of the Civil Act). Where a third party acquires a right of reimbursement against the debtor by paying the debtor’s obligation, the creditor’s claim and the rights relating to its security, which the original creditor had, are, within the scope of such right of reimbursement, transferred to the payer by operation of law while maintaining their identity (see Supreme Court Decision 95DA11009 delivered on 1997. 11. 14., etc.). In such case, as to the extent of subrogation, if the original creditor could have received distribution without filing a demand for distribution, the subrogated payer may also receive distribution without separately filing a demand for distribution (see Supreme Court Decision 2004DA2762 delivered on 2006. 2. 10., etc.).\\n\\nArticle 15 of the Provisional Registration Security Act provides that “where compulsory auction, etc. is conducted with respect to real property for which a provisional security registration has been completed, the right of provisional security registration shall extinguish by the sale of the real property.” Article 16(1) of the same Act provides that “where a decision to commence compulsory auction, etc. is made with respect to real property for which a provisional registration relating to the transfer of ownership has been made, the court shall, by fixing an appropriate period, urge the holder of the provisional registration to report to the court, if the provisional registration is a provisional security registration, the contents thereof and the existence, cause, and amount of the claim.” Paragraph (2) provides that “where a provisional security registration right made before the registration of attachment extinguishes by sale, the creditor may receive distribution of the sale proceeds or payment only if the claim is reported under paragraph (1).” Under Article 148 of the Civil Execution Act, a “creditor having a mortgage, lease on a deposit basis, or any other preferential right to demand repayment, which was registered before the registration of the first decision to commence auction and extinguishes upon sale” (subparagraph 4) may receive distribution without filing a demand for distribution.\\n\\nb. The court below determined that the Plaintiff is a creditor entitled to receive distribution from the sale proceeds of the forest land in this case in the auction proceedings in this case for the following reasons.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff, pursuant to the agreement for subrogated payment with Bulhwi General Construction, obtained the consent of the third party and performed subrogated payment to the third party of the obligation secured by the provisional security registration in this case. At that time, the principal registration in this case was a registration void for lack of cause and the provisional security registration in this case remained a valid registration; thus, the Plaintiff, having acquired a right of reimbursement against Bulhwi General Construction, legally and automatically acquired the provisional security registration in this case and the loan claim of the third party against Bulhwi General Construction, which was the secured claim.\\n\\nThe provisional security registration in this case had been registered before the decision to commence auction in the auction proceedings in this case, and before the auction court, pursuant to Article 16(1) of the Provisional Registration Security Act, urged the Plaintiff to report its claim, the Plaintiff reported the claim asserting that it was the holder of the provisional security registration right. Therefore, the Plaintiff, as a creditor having a provisional security registration extinguished by the sale of real property, may receive distribution from the sale proceeds of the forest land in this case regardless of whether it filed a demand for distribution before the deadline for demanding distribution in the auction proceedings in this case.\\n\\nThe judgment below is proper in light of the legal principles and factual relations discussed above. The judgment below contains no error affecting the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, going beyond the limits of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, or by misapprehending the legal principles regarding creditors entitled to receive distribution without filing a demand for distribution.\\n\\n3. Plaintiff’s grounds of appeal concerning the scope of the claim from which the Plaintiff may receive distribution\\na. The court below determined that the Plaintiff could exercise the loan claim, etc. of the third party against Bulhwi General Construction within the amount of KRW 576,164,383. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff acquired against Bulhwi General Construction a claim for reimbursement in the amount of “KRW 400 million subrogatedly paid to the third party and, with respect thereto, at the Plaintiff’s request, legal interest or delay damages calculated at the statutory annual rate of 5% under the Civil Act from 2006. 5. 9., the date of discharge (the date of subrogated payment), until 2015. 2. 25., the date of distribution, on the principal amount of KRW 250 million, being KRW 176,164,383; in total, KRW 576,164,383.”\\n\\nThe Plaintiff argues that, since the third party and Bulhwi General Construction agreed to pay double the principal every three months as interest, interest and delay damages calculated at 60% per annum should be added to the principal amount of KRW 250 million. However, the scope within which the Plaintiff may subrogate and exercise the third party’s claim cannot exceed the scope of the reimbursement claim recognized above; therefore, the Plaintiff’s argument cannot be accepted with respect to the portion exceeding the annual rate of 5%.\\n\\nb. However, the determination of the court below is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\n(1) A person who has paid a debt on behalf of the debtor may acquire a right of reimbursement against the debtor, and the right of reimbursement is a separate right whose content differs from the subrogation right of the payer under Article 480(1) of the Civil Act in terms of principal, due date, interest, existence or absence of delay damages, etc. (see Supreme Court Decision 97DA1556 delivered on 1997. 5. 30., Supreme Court Decision 2005DA32418 delivered on 2009. 2. 26., Supreme Court Decision 2013DA214970 delivered on 2015. 11. 12.).\\n\\nArticle 482(1) of the Civil Act provides that, in the case of subrogation by a payer, the payer may exercise the claim and the rights relating to its security within the scope in which he/she may seek reimbursement by virtue of his/her own rights. Since subrogation by a payer is a system to secure the effect of the right of reimbursement held against the debtor by paying the debt, the scope of exercise of the original claim and security rights by subrogation is limited to the scope of the right of reimbursement (see Supreme Court Decision 2003DA24147 delivered on 2005. 10. 13., etc.).\\n\\n(2) Since the Plaintiff acquired a right of reimbursement pursuant to the agreement for subrogated payment with Bulhwi General Construction, the scope of the right of reimbursement must be determined according to the interpretation of that agreement. The principal amount of the claim for reimbursement is KRW 400 million, and if there is an interest agreement, contractual interest or delay damages after the date of subrogated payment must be added to the principal.\\n\\nThe object of the Plaintiff’s exercise of the subrogation right by a payer is the right arising from the provisional security registration in this case and the loan claim of the third party against Bulhwi General Construction, which is the secured claim thereof. Since the principal amount of the third party’s loan claim against Bulhwi General Construction is KRW 250 million, it can be seen that of the KRW 400 million subrogatedly paid by the Plaintiff to the third party, KRW 150 million excluding the principal is interest or delay damages from the date of the loan until the date of subrogated payment. Therefore, the third party’s claim should be understood as KRW 400 million and interest or delay damages thereon accruing after 2006. 5. 10., the day following the date of subrogated payment, with respect to KRW 250 million thereof.\\n\\nSince the scope of the original claim and security rights exercised by the Plaintiff pursuant to the subrogation right by a payer is limited to the scope of the right of reimbursement, the amount that the Plaintiff may receive in distribution in the auction proceedings in this case is the smaller of the reimbursement amount calculated by adding interest or delay damages up to the distribution date and the third party’s claim.\\n\\nAccording to the complaint and the written preparatory brief dated 2016. 4. 4., submitted by the Plaintiff at the court below, the claim the Plaintiff asserted as “KRW 400 million and interest or delay damages thereon with respect to KRW 250 million thereof” may be understood not as a claim for reimbursement but as the original claim (the third party’s claim) subject to exercise of the subrogation right, and as to the claim for reimbursement, there is room to view that the Plaintiff asserted “KRW 400 million and interest or delay damages thereon calculated at the contractual annual rate of 50%.” The court below should first clarify the Plaintiff’s arguments regarding the scope of the claim for reimbursement and the original claim, and then specifically examine the scope of each claim.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below concluded that the Plaintiff’s arguments concerning the scope of the claim were about the claim for reimbursement and determined that the claim for reimbursement was “KRW 400 million and statutory interest at 5% per annum on KRW 250 million thereof.” The judgment below contains an error affecting the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the scope of the claim for reimbursement without fully conducting the necessary examination. The grounds of appeal pointing out this issue are well-founded.\\n\\n4. Defendant’s grounds of appeal concerning completion of the extinctive prescription\\na. Where extinctive prescription has been completed, the person who may invoke it is limited to a person who directly receives a benefit as a result of the debt being extinguished by prescription (see Supreme Court Decision 97DA22676 delivered on 1997. 12. 26., etc.). A junior secured creditor may see the order of his/her security right rise if the secured claim of a senior security right is extinguished, and accordingly the amount distributed for the secured claim may increase; however, such expectation of an increase in distribution is merely a reflexive benefit arising from the rise in the order of the security right. A junior secured creditor does not fall within the category of persons who directly receive a benefit from the extinction of the secured claim of a senior security right, and therefore cannot argue that extinctive prescription has been completed with respect to the secured claim of the senior security right.\\n\\nb. The court below rejected the Defendant’s defense that the Plaintiff’s claim against Bulhwi General Construction had been extinguished by completion of the commercial extinctive prescription, on the ground that the Defendant was merely a junior mortgagee and therefore could not invoke extinctive prescription with respect to the claim against Bulhwi General Construction, which is the secured claim of the senior security right.\\n\\nThe judgment below is proper in light of the legal principles discussed above, and contains no error affecting the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning a junior secured creditor’s right to invoke prescription or by violating the duty to clarify, etc.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\nThe Plaintiff’s appeal is well-founded, and the part of the judgment below against the Plaintiff is reversed, and this case insofar as it relates to that part is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. The Defendant’s appeal is without merit and is dismissed. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices, as stated in the main text."}

{"[2016DA45779]": "The grounds of appeal shall be examined (the statements in the supplemental brief on the grounds of appeal filed after the period for submitting the statement of grounds of appeal has elapsed are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds of appeal).\\n\\n1. Article 163(1) of the Civil Act provides that claims for the payment of interest, alimony, wages, rent, and other money or things payable for a period of not more than 1 year shall become extinguished by extinctive prescription if not exercised for 3 years. This provision sets the statute of limitations for fractional claims arising on the basis of the underlying periodic payment claim (see Supreme Court Decision 93DA21705, rendered on September 10, 1993; Supreme Court Decision 99DA1949, rendered on June 12, 2001, etc.), and the term “claims payable for a period of not more than 1 year” refers to claims payable periodically within 1 year (see Supreme Court Decision 96DA25302, rendered on September 20, 1996; Supreme Court Decision 2013DA20571, rendered on July 12, 2013, etc.).\\n\\nAnd a claim for damages arising from non-performance of obligations is either an extension of the original claim or a change in the content of the original claim, and thus has identity with the original claim. Accordingly, when the original claim is extinguished by prescription, the claim for damages is extinguished as well.\\n\\nMeanwhile, even if a debtor has not performed a contractual obligation, the creditor still retains the claim prescribed in the relevant contract, and thus, absent special circumstances, it cannot be said that the debtor has obtained a benefit without legal cause merely because the debtor has not performed that obligation; even if the claim becomes extinguished by prescription, the same conclusion follows (see Supreme Court Decision 91DA28979, rendered on May 12, 1992; Supreme Court Decision 2005DA3113, rendered on April 28, 2005, etc.).\\n\\n2. According to the reasoning of the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts can be found.\\n\\na. On January 1, 2007, the Plaintiff and the Defendant concluded a music rights publishing contract (hereinafter referred to as the “Contract at Issue”) under which the Plaintiff entrusted to the Defendant the management of copyrights in songs composed by the Plaintiff for overseas territories excluding Korea for 5 years from January 1, 2007 (until December 31, 2011), and the Defendant would pay the Plaintiff copyright royalties for the Plaintiff’s songs.\\n\\nb. Under the Contract at Issue, the Defendant agreed to set the end of June and the end of December of each year as the closing dates for accounting regarding the principal contract, and after distributing and settling the copyright royalties received from overseas by that date at the ratio of 65% to the Plaintiff and 35% to the Defendant, to pay the Plaintiff within 100 days.\\n\\nc. The Defendant received copyright royalties for the second half of 2008 for the Plaintiff’s songs from a Japanese company, Seven Sis Music Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “Non-Party Company”), and paid the Plaintiff 101,404,306 won on October 30, 2008, and 299,147,827 won on April 13, 2009, respectively, as settlement amounts.\\n\\nd. On July 15, 2013, the Plaintiff filed this action on the premise that the Defendant had failed to pay the Plaintiff 147,705,060 won by omitting the copyright royalty income for the second half of 2008 received from the Non-Party Company or by unjustly deducting excessive expenses, and as the causes of action, the Plaintiff asserted ① accounting and distribution of unpaid copyright royalties under the Contract at Issue, ② damages arising from non-performance of the accounting and distribution obligations prescribed in the Contract at Issue, and ③ restitution of unjust enrichment equivalent to the unpaid copyright royalties.\\n\\n3. Examining the above factual relations and the procedural history of the lawsuit in light of the legal principles stated above, the following conclusion follows.\\n\\na. The right held by the Plaintiff against the Defendant under the Contract at Issue should be characterized not as a claim for copyright royalties, in that the Defendant is not the user of the copyright, but as a claim for distribution of copyright royalties. Since the Defendant agreed to settle and pay to the Plaintiff the copyright royalties received from overseas every 6 months, it should be deemed that the Plaintiff acquired a fractional claim to the claim for distribution of copyright royalties every 6 months, which is a period of not more than 1 year, and such claim is subject to the 3-year short-term extinctive prescription period as provided in Article 163(1) of the Civil Act.\\n\\nb. In this case, the claim for distribution of copyright royalties for the second half of 2008 sought by the Plaintiff becomes subject to extinctive prescription at the latest from April 13, 2009, when the Defendant paid the copyright royalties for the second half of 2008, and since this action was filed on July 15, 2013, after 3 years had elapsed from that date, the claim for distribution of copyright royalties for the second half of 2008 was extinguished by completion of extinctive prescription, and since the original claim, namely the claim for distribution of copyright royalties for the second half of 2008, was extinguished by completion of extinctive prescription, the claim for damages, such as delay damages, arising from its non-performance was also extinguished.\\n\\nc. Even if the Defendant did not perform the duty to distribute the copyright royalties as stated above, the Plaintiff still holds the claim for distribution of copyright royalties prescribed in the Contract at Issue, and therefore it cannot be said that the Defendant obtained a benefit without legal cause merely because the Defendant did not perform the duty to distribute the copyright royalties; nor does it matter otherwise even if the claim for distribution of copyright royalties for the second half of 2008 became extinguished by prescription.\\n\\n4. Although it was not appropriate for the court below to determine that the right held by the Plaintiff by virtue of the Contract at Issue was a claim for copyright royalties, and that the cause of action in this case was limited to a claim for copyright royalties, and thereby to decide only the defense of extinctive prescription related thereto, the conclusion dismissing the Plaintiff’s claims for the reasons stated above is correct. Therefore, the judgment of the court below does not contain any error that affected the judgment by violating the rules of logic and experience and going beyond the bounds of free evaluation of evidence, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, or by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the scope of application of the short-term extinctive prescription prescribed in Article 163(1) of the Civil Act.\\n\\n5. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal are to be borne by the losing party; it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Supreme Court Justices participating."}

question:
A, who operates a moneylending business, lent B a total of KRW 300 million in three transactions as shown in the table below.
Date of Loan Principal Interest Principal Repayment Due Date
2018. 1. 1. KRW 100 million 1% per month (payable on the last day of each month) 2018. 12. 31.
2019. 1. 1. KRW 100 million 1% per month (payable on the last day of each month) 2019. 12. 31.
2020. 7. 1. KRW 100 million 1% per month (payable on the last day of each month) 2021. 6. 30.
Because B has made no repayment whatsoever of the above debts, A intends to file a lawsuit on 2024. 1. 12. seeking payment of the principal of each loan and the interest or late payment damages thereon up to 2023. 12. 31. If B is expected to raise a defense of the statute of limitations, what is the maximum amount of the claim that A can have upheld in the lawsuit? (However, late payment damages on accrued interest or late payment damages are not claimed, and it is assumed that the last day of the period is not a Saturday or a public holiday. If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DA1381]": "1. Not only a claim arising from an act that is a commercial act as to both parties, but also a claim arising from an act that constitutes a commercial act only as to one party falls under a commercial claim to which the five-year statute of limitations period prescribed in Article 64 of the Commercial Act applies, and such commercial acts include not only the basic commercial acts falling under each item of Article 46 of the Commercial Act, but also auxiliary commercial acts performed by a merchant for the purpose of business (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 94DA36643, decided April 21, 1995, and Supreme Court Decision 97DA9260, decided August 26, 1997).\\n\\nThe court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence it admitted, found the facts as stated in its opinion, and then determined that, because both the employment contract between the Defendant company and the deceased non-party and the collective agreement concluded by the Defendant company with the labor union fall under auxiliary commercial acts, the five-year commercial statute of limitations applies to the instant claim for consolation money based thereon; in light of the legal principles seen above and the record, such determination by the court below is correct, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality of misapprehending the legal principles concerning commercial claims or the commercial statute of limitations.\\n\\n2. The statute of limitations runs from the time when, objectively, the right has arisen and can be exercised, and does not run only during the period in which the right cannot be exercised; the case of “being unable to exercise the right” refers to a case in which there exists a legal impediment to the exercise of the right, for example, where the period has not yet arrived or a condition has not been fulfilled, and even if one did not actually know of the existence of the right or the possibility of exercising the right and was not negligent in such lack of knowledge, such circumstance does not constitute a legal impediment (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2003DO10763, decided April 27, 2004, and Supreme Court Decision 2005DA3113, decided April 28, 2005).\\n\\nThe court below determined that the ground asserted by the Plaintiffs, namely that before July 27, 2001, on which they obtained a final judgment in the lawsuit they brought against the Korea Workers’ Compensation and Welfare Service seeking revocation of the disposition of disapproval of medical treatment, they could not have expected to exercise the instant claim for consolation money, does not constitute a legal impediment to the exercise of the above right, but merely a factual impediment, and therefore has no effect whatsoever on the running of the statute of limitations with respect to the Plaintiffs’ instant claim for consolation money; in light of the legal principles seen above and the record, such determination by the court below is also correct, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality of misapprehending the legal principles concerning the statute of limitations.\\n\\n3. Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties, and it is so adjudged as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2006DA2940]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Claims for delay damages for the periods from 1999. 10. 27. to 1999. 11. 2. on the principal repaid on 1999. 11. 2., from 1999. 10. 27. to 2000. 12. 29. on the principal repaid on 2000. 12. 29., and from 1999. 10. 27. to 2001. 10. 26. on the principal repaid on 2001. 12. 28.\\n\\na. Interest or delay damages is a subsidiary right that arises at a certain rate in correspondence with the existence of the principal obligation, which is the main claim. Where, after a part of the principal of a monetary claim has been extinguished by repayment, the statute of limitations has expired with respect to the remaining principal, it is possible, given the nature of a divisible monetary claim, to distinguish between the portion of the principal extinguished by repayment and the portion of the principal extinguished by the completion of the statute of limitations. In such a case, since interest or delay damages, which are rights subordinate to the principal, can likewise be distinguished between those arising from the portion of the principal extinguished by repayment and those arising from the portion of the principal extinguished by the completion of the statute of limitations, it is appropriate to view that the effect of the completion of the statute of limitations extends to interest or delay damages that arose before the completion of the statute of limitations from the portion of the principal extinguished by the completion of the statute of limitations, but does not extend to interest or delay damages that arose before repayment from the portion of the principal extinguished by repayment.\\n\\nMeanwhile, delay damages after maturity on a loan extended by a bank as a business act are subject, like the principal claim, to Article 64 of the Commercial Act, which prescribes a 5-year statute of limitations for claims arising from commercial acts (see Supreme Court Decision 79DA1453, decided on 1979. 11. 13.).\\n\\nb. According to the reasons stated in the judgment below, the court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence it admitted, found that the non-party Chohung Bank Co., Ltd., on 1997. 3. 28., loaned Defendant 1 KRW 300 million at an annual interest rate of 15.5%, with maturity set for 1997. 6. 26., on the security of Defendant 2’s joint and several suretyship and two promissory notes issued by the non-party Hanbo Steel Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Hanbo Steel”), and that thereafter the maturity date was extended to 1997. 9. 26.; that Defendant 1 repaid to the bank the interest on the above loan up to 1997. 8. 27. on that same date, and repaid the principal amount of KRW 6,498,000 around 1998. 9. 15.; that the rate of delay damages on the above loan after 1999. 1. 29. was 19% per annum; that the Plaintiff, after taking assignment of the above loan claim from the bank on 1998. 9. 29., received in Hanbo Steel’s corporate reorganization proceedings, which were the issuer of the above promissory notes, KRW 2,902,177 on 1999. 11. 2., KRW 14,912,934 each on 2000. 12. 29., 2001. 12. 28., and 2002. 12. 31., KRW 19,883,913 on 2003. 12. 31., and KRW 222,373,768 on 2004. 11. 8. (it appears that 2002. 12. 31. is a clerical error for 2002. 12. 30., 2003. 12. 31. for 2003. 12. 30., and 2004. 11. 8. for 2004. 11. 18.), totaling KRW 289,898,660, and applied the same to repayment of the principal of the above loan; and on the basis of the above findings, held that the Defendants are jointly and severally liable to pay interest and delay damages from the day following the final date on which interest was received on the above loan, as well as the remaining principal of the above loan in the amount of KRW 3,603,340. Then, with respect to the Defendants’ defense of completion of the statute of limitations, the court below accepted that defense on the ground that the above loan claim is a commercial claim arising from commercial acts, such as the lending business of the merchant Chohung Bank Co., Ltd., and is thus subject to the 5-year commercial statute of limitations; that the maturity date of the above loan claim was 1997. 9. 26.; and that this action was filed on 2004. 10. 27., after 5 years had elapsed from the above maturity date, as is clear from the record, so that the above loan claim and the interest and delay damages claim corresponding to rights subordinate thereto had all been extinguished (Civil Act Articles 167 and 183), thereby dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim in the end.\\n\\nc. However, the above determination by the court below cannot be upheld as it stands.\\n\\nAccording to the legal principle stated above, the above loan claim became extinguished by completion of the statute of limitations upon the lapse of 2002. 9. 26., the day on which 5 years from its maturity date elapsed; however, the effect of the completion of the statute of limitations does not extend to interest or delay damages that arose before each repayment from the principal portions already extinguished by repayment before completion of the statute of limitations, namely, the principal amount of KRW 2,902,177 repaid on 1999. 11. 2., the principal amount of KRW 14,912,934 repaid on 2000. 12. 29., and the principal amount of KRW 14,912,934 repaid on 2001. 12. 28. Therefore, as to interest or delay damages claims for this portion, a separate 5-year statute of limitations must be reckoned from each date on which they arose. Accordingly, as to each principal portion extinguished by the above repayments, the delay damages claims arising during the period from 1999. 10. 27., the day before 5 years had elapsed when counted backward from the date this action was filed, 2004. 10. 27., to each corresponding principal repayment date, cannot be deemed to have become time-barred.\\n\\nNevertheless, the judgment below, which reached a different conclusion, contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principle concerning the effect of completion of the statute of limitations; thus, the ground of appeal on this point is meritorious.\\n\\n2. Claims for delay damages for the period from 2001. 10. 27. to 2001. 12. 28. on the principal repaid on 2001. 12. 28.\\n\\nWhere, with respect to a first-instance judgment that partially upheld the Plaintiff’s claim, only the Plaintiff files an appeal as to the portion dismissed against it, and the Defendant files no appeal or cross-appeal, the portion of the first-instance judgment favorable to the Plaintiff is excluded from the scope of review by the appellate court and becomes final upon the pronouncement of the appellate judgment. If the Plaintiff files a final appeal as to such portion that has already become final in the Plaintiff’s favor, the appeal is improper for lack of standing to appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the remaining portion of the Plaintiff’s appeal, namely, the portion of delay damages for the period from 2001. 10. 27. to 2001. 12. 28. on the principal amount of KRW 14,912,934 repaid on 2001. 12. 28., was upheld at first instance and thereafter excluded from the scope of review by the court below because the Defendants filed no appeal or cross-appeal, and thus became final upon the pronouncement of the judgment below. Accordingly, the Plaintiff’s final appeal as to this portion is improper for lack of standing to appeal, as it concerns a portion that has already become final in the Plaintiff’s favor.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, among the judgment below, the portion dismissing the Plaintiff’s claims for delay damages from 1999. 10. 27. to each repayment date on the principal repaid on 1999. 11. 2. and 2000. 12. 29., and from 1999. 10. 27. to 2001. 10. 26. on the principal repaid on 2001. 12. 28., is unlawful and must be reversed. However, since this case is sufficiently ripe for this Court to decide directly, it shall be adjudicated by this Court pursuant to Article 437 of the Civil Procedure Act. As stated above, apart from the amount ordered to be paid at first instance, the Defendants are jointly and severally liable to pay the Plaintiff delay damages of KRW 10,575, calculated at the annual rate of 19% for the period from 1999. 10. 27. to 1999. 11. 2. on the principal amount of KRW 2,902,177 repaid on 1999. 11. 2. (= 2,902,177 × 7/365 × 0.19), delay damages of KRW 3,330,282 on the principal amount of KRW 14,912,934 repaid on 2000. 12. 29. for the period from 1999. 10. 27. to 2000. 12. 29. at the same rate {= 14,912,934 × (1 + 64/365) × 0.19}, and delay damages of KRW 5,666,914 on the principal amount of KRW 14,912,934 repaid on 2001. 12. 28. for the period from 1999. 10. 27. to 2001. 10. 26. at the same rate (= 14,912,934 × 2 × 0.19), for a total of KRW 9,007,771 (= 10,575 + 3,330,282 + 5,666,914). Since the first-instance judgment is unlawful in that it reached a different conclusion in part, the portion of the first-instance judgment dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim corresponding to this part is reversed, the Defendants are ordered to pay the above amount, the Plaintiff’s remaining appeal is dismissed, and the total litigation costs shall be divided into 9 parts, with 8 to be borne by the Plaintiff and the remainder by the Defendants. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices in attendance."}

{"[2008DA15865]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding Ground 2 of the grounds for final appeal\\n\\nExtinctive prescription runs from the time when a right has objectively arisen and can be exercised, and does not run while the right cannot be exercised. Here, “cannot be exercised” means that there exists a legal impediment to the exercise of the right, for example, where the prescribed period has not yet arrived or a condition has not been fulfilled, and such circumstances cannot be said to constitute a legal impediment even if, in fact, one did not know of the existence of the right or of the possibility of exercising the right, or was not negligent in not knowing such matters.\\n\\nMeanwhile, even if the Supreme Court, by the en banc decision rendered on 2004. 4. 22. in 2000DU7735, changed its prior view that a disposition refusing reappointment of a national or public university faculty member whose term of appointment had expired could not be challenged, such prior view of the Supreme Court shall be deemed not to constitute a legal impediment to a claim for damages based on the tortious nature of the disposition refusing reappointment of a national or public university faculty member (see Supreme Court Decision 93DA3622, rendered on 1993. 4. 13.).\\n\\nOn the premise of the foregoing legal principles, the lower court rejected the Plaintiff’s argument, namely, that the Supreme Court’s prior view as above constitutes a legal impediment and therefore the statute of limitations for a claim for damages on the ground that refusal to reappoint a national or public university faculty member whose term had expired is a tort should run from 2005. 1. 27., the date on which the amended Educational Civil Servants Act, which newly established provisions concerning reappointment review, came into force; and such rejection is just and can be accepted. There is no illegality in the misapprehension of law concerning the starting point of the statute of limitations, as argued in the grounds for final appeal. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court decisions cited by the Plaintiff differ in their facts and issues from this case, and cannot be said to be appropriate for application to this case.\\n\\n2. Regarding Ground 1 of the grounds for final appeal\\n\\nBecause the principle of good faith and fair dealing applies also to the debtor’s assertion that the obligation is extinguished by the completion of the statute of limitations, such assertion may be disallowed on the ground that it violates the principle of good faith and fair dealing. However, to invoke a legal principle such as the principle of good faith and fair dealing in order to exclude or restrict, from outside the relevant legal system, what is determined in accordance with the concrete content of each legal system prescribed by positive law carries a risk of causing a setback to legal stability, which is one of the fundamentally important legal values to be realized in the interpretation and application of the law. In particular, legal relations inevitably contain uncertain aspects; therefore, in the statute of limitations system, which is intended to bring disputes between the parties concerning such legal relations to an end by setting a certain temporal limit on the assertion of such legal relations, the demand for such legal stability is raised even more clearly, considering that the system was originally designed on the premise that the passage of time, which is applied indiscriminately and objectively to anyone, has primary significance. Accordingly, caution is required in invoking the principle of good faith and fair dealing with respect to the statute of limitations (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DA71881, rendered on 2005. 5. 13.).\\n\\nIn particular, evaluating that an assertion of completion of the statute of limitations regarding a claim against the creditor is contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing and thus not allowed on the ground that the creditor had circumstances constituting an impediment that objectively prevented the creditor from exercising his or her own right risks altogether collapsing, through the principle of good faith and fair dealing, the fundamental criterion for distinguishing legal impediments from factual impediments, which has consistently been applied with respect to the starting point of the statute of limitations, since the principle of good faith and fair dealing as a general legal principle is inherently unclear in content and open to the unique elements of each individual case; therefore, even greater caution is required (see Supreme Court Decision 2009DA44327, rendered on 2010. 5. 27.).\\n\\nAlso, the mere fact that the State has a duty to protect the people does not mean that the State’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations itself constitutes an abuse of rights in violation of the principle of good faith and fair dealing; therefore, in order to regard the State’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations as contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing and as an abuse of rights, special circumstances equivalent to those recognized in the debtor’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations must be present (see Supreme Court Decision 2004DA71881, rendered on 2005. 5. 13.).\\n\\nOn the premise of the foregoing legal principles, the lower court rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that the existence of the Supreme Court’s prior view as noted above objectively constituted a special circumstance that prevented the creditor from exercising the right, and on that basis, that the assertion of the statute of limitations in this case is contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing, or that the State’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations should be restricted under the principle of good faith and fair dealing; and such rejection is just and can be accepted. There is no illegality, as argued in the grounds for final appeal, in the misapprehension of the legal principles concerning violation of the principle of good faith and fair dealing in the assertion of the statute of limitations.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the final appeal is dismissed and the costs of the final appeal are assessed against the losing party, and the judgment is rendered as ordered, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[90DA9797]": "With respect to the grounds of appeal by the Defendants’ litigation representatives\\n\\n1. The court below, based on the evidence it admitted, found that the late Choi Byeong-hui purchased, on 1964.9.24. (lunar calendar 8.19), seven parcels of real property, including the real property in this case, from the Defendants, and that the late Im No-seon, the father of the Plaintiffs, purchased the real property in this case from the said late Choi Byeong-hui on the same day, and that the said decedents and the Defendants had agreed to an intermediate omitted registration with respect to the real property in this case; such factual findings are proper, and there is no illegality such as a violation of the rules of evidence appraisal or an error in the legal principles concerning the probative value of dispositive documents, as asserted.\\n\\nAnd, in response to the Defendants’ argument that they had not received payment of the purchase price for the real property in this case from the said Im No-seon and therefore could not comply with the Plaintiffs’ claim for registration of transfer of ownership, the court below rejected the Defendants’ argument by finding that the said Im No-seon had paid the entire purchase price to Defendant Jo Seon-hui by 1964.12.3. (lunar calendar 10.30), the due date for payment of the balance of the purchase price for the above real property, and that, even if not so, the Defendants’ claim for the said purchase price had been extinguished by prescription on 1974.12.3., ten years after the said balance payment due date; however, even upon examining the evidence admitted by the court below as stated above, no material can be found that would justify a finding that the purchase price had been fully paid, and thus the court below’s finding in this regard is erroneous.\\n\\nHowever, the alternative determination that the claim for the purchase price had been extinguished by prescription is proper, and therefore the above error does not affect the result of the judgment. Even if the claim for the purchase price for the real property in this case is in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the claim for registration of transfer of ownership, the seller may demand payment of that price at any time after the due date for payment of the purchase price, and the purchaser may merely refuse such payment until the seller provides performance regarding the transfer registration; accordingly, the claim for the purchase price shall be deemed to have been subject to the running of prescription after its due date. The argument ultimately lacks merit.\\n\\n2. Since a claim for registration of transfer of ownership is a claim in personam, it is subject to a 10-year Statute of Limitations, but as long as the purchaser has taken delivery of and is in possession of the real property that is the subject matter of the sale, the Statute of Limitations does not run regardless of whether the purchase price has been paid (see this Court’s Decision 76DA148, rendered on 1976.11.6.; Decision 79DA1799, rendered on 1980.1.15.; Decision 86DAKA2908, rendered on 1988.9.13.).\\n\\nThe court below’s determination to the same effect is proper, and there is no illegality such as the error of law asserted. The argument lacks merit.\\n\\nFor the foregoing reasons, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating in the case, as stated in the Disposition."}

question: A and B are spouses and have minor children C and D subject to their joint parental authority. Of the explanations concerning this, which is correct? (Each statement is independent, and where there is a dispute, it is based on case law)
A: If A, despite being contrary to B's intent, performed a juristic act representing C in the joint names of B and A, that juristic act is ineffective regardless of whether the other party acted in good faith.
B: If C entered into a credit card use contract with credit card company E and obtained a card without the consent of A and B, and E paid the price for goods purchased from F using that card, then after A and B rescinded the credit card use contract with E, but did not rescind the sales contract with F and C consumed all of the purchased goods, C does not bear an obligation to return unjust enrichment to E.
C: If, at the time of the juristic act, C merely told the other party that he was an adult and did not actively use deception, C may rescind the above juristic act.
D: After A's death, B, in order to secure the debt of a stock company of which B is the representative director, established a mortgage over the co-owned property of B and C in the capacity of C's legal representative without appointing a special agent, and such act is a conflict-of-interest transaction and therefore void.
E: After A's death, even if B, as the legal representative of C and D, reaches an agreement to divide the inherited property so that all of it becomes D's sole property, such division by agreement is lawful.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[71DA2045]": "As to Ground Nos. 2 and 5 of the Defendant’s litigation representative Hong Seung-man’s grounds for final appeal and Ground No. 1 of the same Choi Yun-mo’s grounds for final appeal, the judgment below stated that, taking together the contents stated in Exhibit A-3 (copy of family register), Exhibit A-4 (sale and purchase contract), and Exhibit A-5 (certificate of seal impression), the Plaintiff, a male born on 1948. 8. 5., was still a minor on 1968. 3. 26., when the sale and purchase contract for the subject forest land was concluded, and that it could be recognized that the subject sale and purchase contract was concluded without the consent of the statutory representative, and that there was no rebuttal evidence; and if the evidence selected and the process and contents of fact-finding are reviewed from the record, the above recognized facts can be affirmed, so no error can be found in the judgment below in misjudging the probative value of evidence; and the judgment below’s statement that there was no rebuttal evidence may be understood as having rejected, on the ground that the entries in each of Exhibits B-1 through B-6 cited in the argument and the testimonies of Witness Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 did not amount to evidence sufficient to overturn the presumption that the facts stated in Exhibit A-3 are true, so there is no error of omitting a determination thereon; and since it cannot be said that the trial court erred by not urging the Plaintiff’s request for age appraisal, or by not ordering age appraisal ex officio, or by not exercising the power of clarification as to whether the date on which Exhibits B-1, B-2, and B-3 were delivered to the Defendant was before or after the Plaintiff attained majority, there is no error of incomplete examination, so the arguments presented are merely criticizing the trial court’s proper measures and cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAs to Ground No. 4 of the same Hong Seung-man’s grounds for final appeal and Ground No. 2 of the same Choi Yun-mo’s grounds for final appeal, the judgment below, as seen above, recognized the fact that the Plaintiff, at the time the sale and purchase contract for the subject forest land was concluded with the Defendant, was a minor and concluded the subject sale and purchase contract without the consent of the statutory representative, so the minor Plaintiff may rescind that sale and purchase contract; accordingly, when the counterparty Defendant asserts, in order to exclude the minor Plaintiff’s right of rescission, that the minor Plaintiff as prescribed in Civil Act Article 17 used deceit, the burden of proof for that assertion lies on the Defendant side, the asserting party; in the present case, the Defendant submitted Exhibit B-6 (certificate of seal impression showing that the Plaintiff had become an adult) as one of the proofs, but since the Plaintiff submitted rebuttal evidence that the number portion of the year indicating adulthood had been altered and that the Plaintiff himself had not altered it, the Defendant, returning to the principle of the burden of proof, must bear the burden of proving that the alteration was made by the Plaintiff or by a third party in collusion with the Plaintiff; thus, in the same purport, the judgment below’s disposition rejecting the Defendant’s assertion that the Plaintiff used deceit on the premise that the Plaintiff altered the seal-impression certificate, which was the document required for registration of transfer concerning the subject forest land, for the reason that there was no proof thereof, is proper, and there is no error in shifting the burden of proof or violating the rules of evidence appraisal; further, the term “when a person without capacity has caused another to believe him or her to have capacity by deceit” as used in Civil Act Article 17 refers to a case where the person without capacity actively uses fraudulent means in order to make the other party believe that he or she has capacity, and a mere statement by oneself that one is a person with capacity cannot be said to be having used deceit as referred to in the same Article (see Supreme Court Judgment of 1955.3.31., 1954 MINSANG77); therefore, in the present case, even if the minor Plaintiff stated himself at the time of the sale and purchase contract that he was the president, or even if the non-party present also addressed the Plaintiff to the counterparty Defendant as the president of Jungang Jeonseon Co., Ltd., this alone does not correspond to a case of using deceit as so-called, so the judgment below, which was rendered in the purport of such a view, is proper, and there is no illegality in the judgment below in misinterpreting or misapplying the law, so the arguments cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAs to Ground No. 3 of the same Hong Seung-man’s grounds for final appeal, the trial court stated in the reasons for its judgment that the Plaintiff had no fact of having been the representative director of any company on 1968. 3. 26., when the sale and purchase contract for the subject forest land was concluded, so the Defendant’s assertion premised on the Plaintiff having been the representative director of a company at the time of conclusion of the subject sale and purchase contract lacks merit, and that Civil Act Article 8, which provides that a minor who has received permission to conduct business from the statutory representative, does not make the Defendant’s assertion meritless in the present case where there is no allegation or proof whatsoever of such business permission; and since this case is not a sale of company property and there is no room for application of apparent authority, the argument that there is a misunderstanding of Civil Act Article 8 regarding a minor’s business permission and of the law concerning apparent authority is merely an independent view and is without merit.\\n\\nAs to Ground No. 1 of the same Hong Seung-man’s grounds for final appeal and Ground No. 3 of the same Choi Yun-mo’s grounds for final appeal, if the record is examined, the Defendant’s litigation representative, in the preparatory brief filed on 1971.5.6. (record p. 397), which was deemed to have been stated at the trial court hearing date of 1971.5.7. (record p. 404; the entry in the trial court hearing protocol deeming the answer statement to have been made is a clerical error for deeming the preparatory brief to have been made), stated that “even if the Plaintiff’s assertion is accepted, the Plaintiff reached majority on 1968. 8. 4., and the fact that a considerable amount of time passed until the filing of this action without any objection makes it socially appropriate in light of general commercial practice to deem that the Plaintiff implicitly ratified the subject sale and purchase contract,” and thus clearly asserted that the subject sale and purchase contract can be viewed as having been ratified after the Plaintiff became of age; nevertheless, the trial court made no determination thereon. This constitutes an illegality of omission of determination that may affect the judgment, so the arguments on this point are meritorious and the judgment below cannot escape reversal.\\n\\nTherefore, in accordance with Article 406 of the Civil Procedure Act, the judgment is rendered as follows by the unanimous opinion of the participating judges."}

{"[92DA54524]": "We examine the grounds of appeal by the Plaintiff’s litigation representative.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below determined the following facts: that each of the real properties in this case was originally owned by Non-party 1; that said Non-party 1 died on 1966.5.5., and his wife, Non-party 2, his eldest son, Non-party 3, his second son, the Defendant, and his daughters, Non-party 4, Non-party 5, and Non-party 6, became co-heirs; that again on 1977.9.6. said Non-party 3 died, and his wife, Non-party 7, his eldest son, the Plaintiff, and his daughters, Non-party 8 and Non-party 9, became his co-inheritors of the estate; that with respect to each of the real properties in this case, which had originally been owned by the deceased Non-party 1, a registration of transfer of ownership was completed in the sole name of the Defendant as Receipt No. 112853, filed with the Anyang Registry Office of the Suwon District Court on 1983.11.15., and that this was based on the division of inherited property by agreement of the above co-heirs dated 1982.8.9.; and, further, with respect to the Plaintiff’s assertion that, even if there had in fact been an agreement for division among the above co-heirs, it is void because it violates Article 921 of the Civil Act, namely, that even if the Defendant, in consultation with said Non-party 7, effected inheritance registration of the real properties in this case in the sole name of the Defendant, the act by which said Non-party 7, as the parental authority of said Non-party 8 and Non-party 9, who were minors at the time, represented them and made an agreement for the division of inherited property to place each of the real properties in this case in the Defendant’s sole ownership constitutes an act in conflict of interest between a person with parental authority and a minor, and yet no special representative was appointed, and therefore it is void, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s above assertion as unfounded, holding that an act in conflict of interest between a person with parental authority and his or her child refers to an act that is beneficial to the person with parental authority and disadvantageous to the minor, or an act that is beneficial to one of the persons subject to parental authority and disadvantageous to the other, and that the agreement for division of inherited property by which said Non-party 7, as an heir and also as the parental authority of the above minors, represented them and placed each of the real properties in this case under the Defendant’s sole ownership cannot be said to constitute an act in conflict of interest between a person with parental authority and his or her child, and thus the Plaintiff’s above assertion is without merit.\\n\\nHowever, an act in conflict of interest under Article 921 of the Civil Act refers to an act that, by its objective nature, is likely to create a conflict of interest between a person with parental authority and his or her child, or among multiple children subject to parental authority, and whether the person with parental authority intended such a result or whether a conflict of interest actually arose as a result of the act is not a matter to be considered. Since an agreement for division of inherited property among co-heirs is, by the objective nature of the act, an act that is likely to create a conflict of interest among the heirs, in cases where an agreement for division of inherited property is to be made between a person with parental authority who is also a co-heir and multiple minor children, a special representative must be appointed for each minor, and each such special representative must, on behalf of each minor child, make the agreement for division of inherited property. If, however, the person with parental authority made the agreement for division of inherited property as the statutory representative of multiple minor children, this would violate Article 921 of the Civil Act, and the agreement for division of inherited property formed by such representative act would be void unless ratified by all of the principals. Accordingly, the court below, without determining any fact of such ratification, held the above agreement for division of inherited property valid, and thereby erred by misapprehending the legal principles of Article 921 of the Civil Act and affecting the outcome of the judgment; the argument pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the judgment of the court below shall be reversed and remanded, and it is so adjudged as follows by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[96DA10270]": "As to the grounds for appeal\\n\\n1. An act in conflict of interests under Article 921 of the Civil Act refers to an act, the objective nature of which is such that there is a risk of a conflict of interests arising between the person exercising parental authority and the child or between several children subject to parental authority; whether the person exercising parental authority intended such conflict or whether a conflict of interests actually arose as a result of the act is not a matter to be asked (see, e.g., this Court’s Decision of September 9, 1994, 94DA6680, and Decision of April 13, 1993, 92DA54524).\\n\\n2.
