Regarding Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in the judgment, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that, under the lease agreement at issue, the Defendant was obliged at its own expense to change the land at issue into factory site land and had waived the right to claim reimbursement of useful expenses, and found that the Defendant had expended KRW 383,613,000 in civil engineering work costs to change the classification of the land at issue to factory site land.\\n\\nExamining the reasons in the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the above determination of the court below contains no illegality that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, misapprehending the legal principles regarding the interpretation of the parties’ intent concerning waiver of the right to claim reimbursement of useful expenses, or by violating the rules of logic and experience and thereby exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in erroneously finding facts.\\n\\nB. Regarding Ground 2 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in the judgment, the court below found that the land development charge paid by the Defendant with respect to the land at issue constituted useful expenses to be reimbursed by the Plaintiff.\\n\\nExamining the reasons in the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the above determination of the court below contains no illegality that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, misapprehending the legal principles regarding the interpretation of dispositive documents and the revocation of admission as to the land development charge.\\n\\n2. Regarding the Defendant’s grounds for appeal\\n\\nA. Regarding Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in the judgment, the court below rejected the Defendant’s argument that the portion of the lease agreement at issue concerning the restoration to original condition agreement (Paragraph 5) was void because it was substantially unfavorable to the Defendant.\\n\\nExamining the reasons in the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the above determination of the court below contains no illegality that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, misapprehending the legal principles regarding the validity of an agreement waiving the right to demand purchase of structures on the land, or by violating the rules of logic and experience and thereby exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in erroneously finding facts.\\n\\nB. Regarding Ground 2 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in the judgment, the court below held that the Plaintiff’s election made in the court below to have the Defendant reimburse the lesser amount between the amount expended by the Defendant and the current amount of increased value was valid, and thus determined that the Plaintiff is obligated to pay to the Defendant the current amount of increased value, which is the lesser amount of the above two amounts.\\n\\nExamining the reasons in the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the above determination of the court below contains no illegality that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, misapprehending the legal principles regarding the exercise of the right of election in a claim involving alternative obligations.\\n\\nC. Regarding Ground 3 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\n1) Civil Act Article 495 provides, “If a claim whose extinctive prescription has been completed could have been set off before its completion, the obligee may set it off.” This is intended to protect the trust of the parties, taking into account that where the claims of both parties were in a state permitting setoff, the parties generally think that the claim-debt relationship has already been settled and extinguished. However, this requires that “both claims were in a state permitting setoff before the completion of extinctive prescription of the active claim” (see Supreme Court Decision rendered 2016. 11. 25. 2016DA211309, etc.).\\n\\nCivil Act Article 626(2) provides that, where a lessee has expended useful expenses, the lessor shall, upon termination of the lease, reimburse either the amount expended by the lessee or the amount of the increase in value, only to the extent that such increase in value still exists. Accordingly, the lessee’s claim for reimbursement of useful expenses should be deemed to arise only upon termination of the lease agreement. Therefore, if the extinctive prescription of the lessor’s claim for indemnity was completed during the continuance of the lease, the above claim for indemnity and the lessee’s claim for reimbursement of useful expenses cannot be said to have been in a state permitting setoff; thus, thereafter, the lessor’s setoff of the lessee’s claim for reimbursement of useful expenses by using the already time-barred claim for indemnity as the active claim cannot be recognized even under Civil Act Article 495.\\n\\n2) From the reasons in the court below’s judgment and the record, the following facts can be known.\\n\\na) In or around June 1993, the Plaintiff entered into the lease agreement at issue with the Defendant, leasing the land at issue with the lease term set from July 1, 1993 to July 1, 2013, and at that time the Defendant agreed to pay the taxes and public charges, including taxes, relating to the land at issue, to the Plaintiff.\\n\\nb) In or around June 1994, the Defendant changed the character of the land at issue from its original “forest land” to “factory site land,” and expended KRW 488,530,010 for this purpose.\\n\\nc) From January 1, 1998 to June 30, 2013, the Plaintiff directly paid a total of KRW 27,290,781 in property tax, land tax, education tax, and urban planning tax relating to the land at issue.\\n\\nd) As a result of the expenditure of the costs for the change in character set forth in b) by the Defendant, an increase in the value of the land at issue in the amount of at least KRW 342,432,000 remained in existence at the time of expiration of the term of the lease agreement at issue.\\n\\ne) On November 2, 2015, the Plaintiff indicated to the Defendant, by service of a preparatory brief dated the same day, an intention to set off, at equal amounts, the claim for indemnity against the Defendant in the amount corresponding to the taxes, etc. paid, as the active claim, against the Defendant’s claim against the Plaintiff for reimbursement of useful expenses arising from the change in character of the land at issue, as the passive claim.\\n\\n3) Examining the foregoing facts in light of the legal principles stated above, the Defendant’s above claim for reimbursement of useful expenses arose around July 1, 2013, the time of termination of the lease agreement at issue, so the portion of the Plaintiff’s above claim for indemnity for which extinctive prescription had already been completed during the continuance of the lease agreement at issue cannot be said to have been in a state permitting setoff with the above claim for reimbursement of useful expenses. Accordingly, the court below should have examined the portion of the claim for indemnity for which extinctive prescription had already been completed as of the time of termination of the lease agreement at issue, and should have held that the Plaintiff could not set off the Defendant’s claim for reimbursement of useful expenses by using such already time-barred claim for indemnity as the active claim.\\n\\n4) Nevertheless, in response to the Defendant’s argument that the Plaintiff’s claim for indemnity with respect to taxes imposed from 1998 to 2005 had already become time-barred before the Plaintiff’s manifestation of intent to set off, the court below held that, because the Plaintiff had an interest, even before the completion of extinctive prescription, in reasonably expecting to set off the above claim for indemnity as the active claim against the Defendant’s claim for reimbursement of useful expenses as the passive claim, the Plaintiff could, even after the extinctive prescription of the above claim for indemnity had been completed, set off the above claim for indemnity against the Defendant’s claim for reimbursement of useful expenses. The above determination of the court below contains illegality that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the time of accrual of the claim for reimbursement of useful expenses under Civil Act Article 626(2) and the setoff based on a claim whose extinctive prescription has been completed under Civil Act Article 495. The grounds for appeal pointing this out are well taken.\\n\\nD. Regarding the portion of the claim for return of unjust enrichment\\n\\nAlthough the Defendant appealed against the entirety of the portion of the court below’s judgment that was adverse to it, the petition of appeal and the statement of grounds for appeal did not set forth specific grounds for appeal regarding the portion of the claim for return of unjust enrichment that was upheld in the court below.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nAccordingly, among the portions of the court below’s judgment adverse to the Defendant, the portion concerning the claim for delivery of the land is reversed, and this case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination of that portion; the Plaintiff’s appeal and the remainder of the Defendant’s appeal are each dismissed. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2022DA200089]": "The grounds of appeal are examined (supplementary appellate briefs filed after the expiration of the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal shall be considered only to the extent that they supplement the original grounds).\\n\\n1. Outline of the Case\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts may be found.\\n\\na. The Plaintiff is a company that issues and manages transit cards called “T-money,” and the Defendant is a company that issues and manages transit cards called “Ebicard.” The Plaintiff and the Defendant concluded the agreement at issue on 2007. 10. 15. and have made mutual settlement with respect to fares of users of the other company’s transit cards using terminals installed by their own company. Under the agreement at issue, settlement is made by calculating and billing the portion in which the other company’s transit card was used on its own terminal, and the other company deposits the corresponding amount. In the event of a delay in payment of the settlement amount, delay damages at the rate of 0.25% per day are recognized.\\n\\nb. Sensepass Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Sensepass”) was conducting a transit card payment service business by issuing a transit card called “Top T-money” in some areas of Gyeongsang Province, including Tongyeong. Mybi Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Mybi”) began a payment service through a transit card called “Cashbee Card” in the same area around February 2013. Mybi installed its own terminals in taxis to provide transit card payment services and additionally installed devices so that Top T-money issued by Sensepass could also be used on Mybi terminals. On 2014. 9. 30., the Plaintiff concluded the business transfer agreement at issue with Sensepass and took over Sensepass’s business.\\n\\nc. As of around August 2016, the number of transactions paid with Top T-money on Mybi terminals was 42,087, and the fare amounts therefor (hereinafter “Top T-money usage fares”) totaled 165,323,103 won. The Defendant, entrusted by Mybi to handle settlement duties, repeatedly requested the Plaintiff to settle the Top T-money usage fares paid on Mybi terminals, but the Plaintiff refused on the ground that there was no separate settlement agreement with respect thereto. The Defendant sent the Plaintiff an official notice stating that it would deduct the Top T-money usage fares from the settlement amount to be paid by it in the future.\\n\\nd. Thereafter, the Defendant paid only 5,530,872,809 won, excluding 160,107,945 won, out of the total settlement amount of 5,690,980,754 won that it was required to pay to the Plaintiff pursuant to the agreement at issue, and paid only 199,271,637 won, excluding 2,752,818 won, out of the settlement amount of 202,024,455 won that it was required to pay to the Plaintiff as of 2016. 12. 6. In response, the Plaintiff paid only 1,322,654,606 won, excluding 160,107,945 won, out of the settlement amount of 1,482,762,551 won that it was required to pay to the Defendant pursuant to the agreement at issue. The Defendant again paid only 29,084,379 won, excluding 160,107,945 won, out of the settlement amount of 189,192,324 won that it was required to pay to the Plaintiff as of 2017. 9. 5. pursuant to the agreement at issue.\\n\\ne. On 2020. 7. 7., Mybi assigned the claim for Top T-money usage fares to the Defendant, and on the same day the Defendant, having been delegated the authority to give notice, gave notice of assignment of claim to the Plaintiff (hereinafter “the assignment of claim at issue”).\\n\\nf. The Plaintiff filed the present action seeking payment of the unpaid settlement amount totaling 162,860,763 won (2,752,818 won as of 2016. 12. 6. + 160,107,945 won as of 2017. 9. 5.) and delay damages thereon, alleging that the Defendant’s above-mentioned deduction of the settlement amount was improper.\\n\\n2. Whether the obligation to return unjust enrichment was established (Ground of Appeal 1)\\nThe court below held that the Plaintiff and Sensepass had obtained benefits corresponding to the Top T-money usage fares without legal cause and that, as a result, Mybi suffered loss in the same amount, and thus recognized the establishment of the obligation of the Plaintiff and Sensepass to return unjust enrichment to Mybi.\\n\\nExamining the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below in light of the record and the relevant legal principles, there is no error that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, misapprehending the legal principles on unjust enrichment or the principle of good faith, or by finding facts in violation of the rules of logic and experience and thereby exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\n3. Whether the obligation to return unjust enrichment was assumed (Ground of Appeal 2)\\nThe court below determined that the Plaintiff assumed Sensepass’s obligation to return unjust enrichment to Mybi through the business transfer agreement at issue.\\n\\nExamining the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below in light of the record and the relevant legal principles, there is no error that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, misapprehending the legal principles concerning succession to specific obligations upon business transfer or interpretation of dispositive documents, or by finding facts in violation of the rules of logic and experience and thereby exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\n4. Date on which setoff was ripe where the assigned claim was used as the active claim for setoff (Ground of Appeal 3)\\n\\na. Since Article 493(2) of the Civil Act provides, “An expression of intent to effect setoff shall be deemed to have extinguished both obligations to the extent of the equivalent amount when each obligation becomes capable of setoff,” the effect of setoff arises retroactively as of the time when setoff becomes ripe. Setoff becomes ripe only when the active claim and the passive claim confront each other mutually.\\n\\nWhere the assignee of a claim effects setoff, using the assigned claim as the active claim, against a preexisting claim held by his or her obligor against the assignee, the assignee may exercise the active claim only when the requirements for setting up the assignment of claim against the obligor have been satisfied; therefore, even if the due dates of both claims had already arrived before the assignment of claim, the effect of setoff does not retroact to the due dates but retroacts to the time when the requirements for setting up the assignment of claim against the obligor were satisfied.\\n\\nb. Viewing the facts found above in light of such legal principles, the following conclusion follows.\\n\\n(1) The point in time when the unjust enrichment claim for return that the Defendant assumed from Mybi through the assignment of claim at issue and the Plaintiff’s settlement claim became mutually opposed is 2020. 7. 7., when the Defendant gave the Plaintiff notice of assignment of claim and thereby satisfied the requirements for setting up the assignment against the obligor; accordingly, this time should be regarded as the date on which setoff became ripe.\\n\\n(2) Considering the amounts of the Plaintiff’s settlement claim and the Defendant’s unjust enrichment claim for return, the due dates, periods of delay, and rate of delay damages, etc., there remains room for the Plaintiff’s settlement claim even if setoff appropriation is made by comparing the principal and interest of the Plaintiff’s settlement claim, calculated as of 2020. 7. 6., the day before the date on which setoff became ripe, with the principal and interest of the Defendant’s unjust enrichment claim for return against the Plaintiff.\\n\\n(3) The court below should have examined how much the principal and interest of the Plaintiff’s settlement claim and the principal and interest of the Defendant’s unjust enrichment claim for return were, respectively, as of 2020. 7. 6., the day before the date on which setoff became ripe, and then determined whether there remained any settlement claim owed to the Plaintiff even after setoff appropriation.\\n\\n(4) However, the court below, on the erroneous premise that the time for performance of the original claim was the date on which setoff became ripe, concluded that the Plaintiff’s settlement claim had been extinguished by the Defendant’s unjust enrichment claim for return in the amount of 165,323,103 won, within the scope of the equivalent amount thereof at each due date (2,752818 won as of 2016. 12. 6. and 160,107,945 won as of 2017. 9. 5.), and that no settlement claim remained. The judgment of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the date on which setoff becomes ripe where the assigned claim is used as the active claim for setoff.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\nThe judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices, as stated in the disposition."}

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are true (○) and false (×) regarding obligations involving multiple parties? (Interest and delay damages are not considered. In case of dispute, according to case law.) (a) Where one of the joint and several debtors is released from part of the debt, if the remaining amount that the joint and several debtor must pay exceeds the share of burden, the other joint and several debtor must bear the entire debt. (b) In a cumulative assumption of debt, the obligor and the assumer are, in principle, in a quasi-joint and several liability relationship. (c) If a creditor files an auction application against real property owned by one of the joint and several debtors and, within 6 months thereafter, brings a judicial claim against another joint and several debtor, the extinctive prescription of the claim against that other joint and several debtor is interrupted as of the time of the auction application, and the interrupted prescription begins anew from the termination of the said auction proceedings. (d) A, B, and C caused D damage in the amount of KRW 9 million through a joint tort. Internally, A was without negligence, and the degree of negligence of B and C was equal. If A compensated D for the full KRW 9 million, A may demand performance of the recourse obligation of KRW 9 million against B.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2001DA22840]": "The appeal is dismissed. The costs of appeal shall be borne by the Plaintiff."}

{"[2011DA52727]": "We determine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. As to Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below, after finding the facts as stated in its opinion, held that the flooding accident in this case was caused by the concurrence of, on the one hand, the construction negligence of the Defendant, Youngnam Construction Co., Ltd., and Chil Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “Defendant, etc.”), who were the constructors of the road construction in this case, in that they removed the existing stormwater drain but left the area without installing drainage facilities such as temporary drainage channels, despite having a duty of care to install all facilities or secure drainage channels to prevent flood damage caused by torrential rain, in accordance with the provisions of the special specifications for the road construction in this case and the supervision contents of Korea Technology Development Co., Ltd. for the section of cut-and-fill construction in this case; and, on the other hand, the defect in the installation and management of public structures, in that the Plaintiff, who installs and manages the road in the section of cut-and-fill construction in this case, failed to fulfill the duty of protective measures to prevent flooding accidents caused by torrential rain through the Defendant, etc., the constructors of the road construction in this case, thereby preventing in advance the flooding accident caused by torrential rain. Accordingly, the court below determined that the Plaintiff and the Defendant, etc. bear liability for a joint tort toward the non-party, the victim of the accident in this case.\\n\\nThereafter, the court below held that, where the Plaintiff compensates for damages due to a defect in the installation and management of a public structure, if there is a person separately liable for the cause of the damage, the Plaintiff may seek reimbursement from that person (Article 5(2) of the State Compensation Act); and that, if the Plaintiff were faultless with respect to the occurrence of the flooding accident in this case and the Defendant, etc. had to bear full responsibility, then the Plaintiff could seek reimbursement from the Defendant, etc. for the full amount of compensation paid by the Plaintiff. However, in Case No. 2005NA105103 of the Seoul High Court, which was a case in which the injured non-party claimed damages against the Plaintiff and the Defendant, etc., the basis on which the Plaintiff’s liability for damages was recognized was that the Plaintiff had a defect in the installation and management of a public structure in that it failed to fulfill the duty of protective measures to prevent in advance the flooding accident caused by torrential rain “through the Defendant, etc., the constructors of the road construction in this case”; and this merely means that, as the managing entity of the public structure, the Plaintiff bears liability to compensate the victim for defects caused by the negligence of the constructors, the Defendant, etc., and therefore, the mere fact that the defect in the installation and management of the public structure is recognized does not mean that the Plaintiff’s independent negligence is recognized in the internal reimbursement relationship between the Plaintiff and the Defendant, etc. Further, even based on the evidence, it is difficult to find that the Plaintiff was negligent in any respect concerning the occurrence of the flooding accident in this case, and thus the court below determined that the flooding accident in this case was caused by the negligence of the Defendant, etc., the constructors.\\n\\nIn light of the record, the above determination of the court below is proper, and there is no error such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning liability for public structures or violation of the rules of evidence, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. As to Ground 2 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nWhere there are multiple other joint tortfeasors who bear a duty of reimbursement toward one joint tortfeasor, in the absence of special circumstances, their obligations to the person entitled to reimbursement should be regarded as divided obligations according to each party’s burden share; however, where there is no fault on the part of the joint tortfeasor entitled to reimbursement, that is, where there is no internal burden share at all, the relationship among the multiple duties of reimbursement owed to such person should instead be regarded as an imperfect joint and several relationship (see Supreme Court Decision 2003DA24147, rendered October 13, 2005).\\n\\nConsistent with the same purport, the court below held that, because the Plaintiff was without fault in the internal relationship with the Defendant, etc. and thus had no internal burden share, the Defendant’s duty of reimbursement to the Plaintiff, together with that of the remaining consortium companies, is in the relationship of an imperfect joint and several obligation; accordingly, the court below determined that the Defendant is obligated to pay to the Plaintiff 660,698,203 won, which the Plaintiff paid to the non-party as damages, and the delay damages thereon. Such determination is in accordance with the above legal principles and is proper, and there is no error such as misapprehension of the legal principles alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing Defendant, and it is so adjudged as per the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2019DA216435]": "We examine the grounds of final appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding Grounds for Final Appeal 1 and 2\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the court below rejected the Defendant’s assertion that the Defendant, as a joint and several debtor, had received a release from solidarity from the creditor, Korea Land and Housing Corporation.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the foregoing determination by the court below is just and can be upheld; there is no error that affected the judgment due to any misapprehension of the legal principles regarding the probative value of dispositive documents, the legal principles regarding release from solidarity, or any failure to fully examine the case, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n2. Regarding Ground for Final Appeal 3\\n\\nArticle 419 of the Civil Act provides that “a release from a debt granted to one joint and several debtor shall have effect, only with respect to that debtor’s share of the burden, for the benefit of the other joint and several debtors,” thereby recognizing the absolute effect of release. The purpose is to simplify the legal relationship concerning recourse by avoiding a circular chain of recourse among the parties; accordingly, even where a creditor partially releases one of the joint and several debtors from the debt, that purpose must be respected. Therefore, unless there are special circumstances indicating that a partial release of debt granted to one of the joint and several debtors has only relative effect, the absolute effect of release should also be recognized in the case of a partial release, only with respect to the released portion of the burden.\\n\\nSpecifically, where one of the joint and several debtors is partially released from the debt, if the remaining debt amount that the joint and several debtor must pay exceeds that debtor’s share of the burden, then that joint and several debtor’s share of the burden has not been reduced, and thus the debt of the other joint and several debtors is also unaffected, so the other joint and several debtors must bear the entire amount of the debt. Conversely, if the remaining debt amount of the released debtor due to the partial release is less than that debtor’s share of the burden, then the difference (share of the burden - remaining debt amount) means that the released debtor’s share of the burden has been reduced by that amount, and the absolute effect of release arises to the extent of that difference, so the debt of the other joint and several debtors is also reduced by that difference.\\n\\nThe court below determined that the amount of debt owed to Korea Land and Housing Corporation was 386,743,198 won, and the amount released for the Defendant was 234,620,465 won, but because the debt remaining after the release, 152,122,733 won, exceeds the Defendant’s share of the burden, 116,022,959 won, the partial release of the Defendant’s debt by Korea Land and Housing Corporation does not affect the debt of the other joint and several debtor, Dongbu Construction.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the foregoing determination by the court below is just and can be upheld; there is no error that affected the judgment due to any misapprehension of the interpretation of a dispositive document or of the legal principles concerning Article 419 of the Civil Act, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n3. Regarding Ground for Final Appeal 4\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the court below rejected the Defendant’s defense of set-off, while also not accepting the Defendant’s assertion that the Plaintiff’s claim constitutes an abuse of rights.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the foregoing determination by the court below is just and can be upheld; there is no error that affected the judgment due to any misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the establishment of liability for damages arising from a tort, or the legal principles concerning abuse of rights, or due to any failure to fully examine the case, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the final appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the final appeal shall be borne by the losing party. Accordingly, the judgment is rendered as ordered, by unanimous opinion of the Supreme Court Justices who participated."}

question: Which of the following statements regarding the duty of support are correct? (If there is a dispute, the answer shall be based on case law) (a) Because the duty of support between spouses is intended to make it possible to maintain the spouses’ common life, if the marriage has irretrievably broken down and the spouses are living separately while filing divorce actions against each other, then unless there are special circumstances, the duty of support between the spouses should be deemed extinguished even before the divorce is finalized. (b) With respect to past maintenance among spouses, unless there are special circumstances, the person entitled to support may claim payment only for the period after the obligor fell into delay by failing to perform the duty of support despite a demand for performance of that duty. (c) If one spouse refuses cohabitation without just cause, then unless there are special circumstances such as the other spouse’s claim for cohabitation constituting an abuse of rights, that spouse cannot claim payment of maintenance from the other party. (d) The right of one spouse who has raised the child alone to seek payment of past child-rearing expenses from the other spouse does not run under the Statute of Limitations until, through an agreement of the parties or a family court adjudication, etc., it has become a concrete claim for payment.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2008SEU67]": "We examine the grounds for re-appeal.\\n\\n1. The court below, citing the first-instance decision, held that a claim for child support which one parent has against the other by reason of having previously raised a minor child may be exercised immediately upon its accrual, so long as there is no legal impediment, and that the Statute of Limitations runs from that time; accordingly, it determined that the claim for child support arising before 1996. 10. 17., which is 10 years retroactively calculated from 2006. 10. 17., the date on which the petition for adjudication in this case was filed, had become extinguished by prescription, and rejected the claim for child support in this part.\\n\\n2. However, the above determination by the court below is difficult to accept as it stands.\\nParents have the responsibility to jointly raise their minor child, and the expenses incurred for such upbringing shall, in principle, also be borne jointly by the parents. Such parental duty to raise a child arises at the same time as the child’s birth, and unless there are special circumstances such as where the child-raising parent alone raised the child due to unilateral and selfish purposes or motives, or where doing so is not helpful to the child’s interests, or where burdening the other party with the child support expense would instead be contrary to equity, it should be deemed that, even with respect to the period before the child-raising parent claimed child support, the child-raising parent may claim from the other party the expenses relating to such upbringing. However, the scope of contribution that is deemed appropriate may be determined by considering various circumstances, such as the circumstances under which the child-raising parent came to raise the child and the amount of expenses incurred therefor, whether the other party recognized the duty of support and when, and whether such expenses were ordinary living expenses incurred for upbringing or whether they were extraordinary and unavoidable large special expenses (such as medical expenses), as well as the financial circumstances of the parties, their economic capacity, or the fairness of the burden allocation (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 92SEU21 dated 1994. 5. 13.; Supreme Court Decision 94MEU536 of 1995. 4. 25., etc.).\\nMeanwhile, the right of the child-raising parent to seek payment of child support from the other party was, in the first place, merely an abstract legal status recognized fundamentally on the basis of the family relationship as noted above, and only by being converted into a concrete claim through an agreement between the parties or by a judgment of the Family Court that discretionarily and constitutively determines the contents of the child support, does it come to have, more distinctly, the nature of an independent pecuniary right.\\nThus, before it is established as a concrete right to claim payment by agreement of the parties or by a Family Court judgment, the right concerning past child support cannot be said to constitute a property right that the child-raising parent may exercise, and therefore there is no room for the Statute of Limitations to run against it.\\nHowever, in this case, for which no material indicating that the above-mentioned concrete claim for child support had been established can be found in the record, the court below erred in law, affecting the judgment, by determining that the claim for child support for the period before 1996. 10. 17. had become extinguished by prescription, thereby misapprehending the legal principles concerning the Statute of Limitations for claims for past child support.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the court below’s decision is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so decided by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the Disposition."}

{"[2011DA96932]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Findings of the court below\\n\\nThe court below, after recognizing the facts as stated in its reasoning, held that there is no basis under the Civil Act for viewing the spouse’s duty of support as always taking precedence over the duty of support among relatives, and further, under Civil Act Articles 976 and 977, where a person obligated to support, as prescribed in Civil Act Article 974, has a duty of support, such person, in the abstract, bears the same duty of support when the person to be supported has a need for support, while the specific rights and obligations or the order of support are to be determined by agreement between the parties or by adjudication of the Family Court. On that basis, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s argument seeking return from the Defendant of the support expenses incurred by the Plaintiff as unjust enrichment or reimbursement, on the ground that the Defendant could not be regarded as a prior-ranking obligor of support merely because he was the spouse of the person omitted.\\n\\n2. However, the court below’s determination is difficult to endorse as is for the following reasons.\\n\\nA. (1) The mutual duty of support between spouses, prescribed in Article 826(1) of the Civil Act, is an essential duty of the marital relationship and is the primary duty of support, the substance of which is to secure the living of the person entitled to support at the same level as the life of the support obligor so as to enable maintenance of the spouses’ cohabitation; whereas the duty of support borne by parents, as lineal blood relatives, toward their adult children under Civil Act Article 974(1) and Article 975 is the secondary duty of support, the substance of which is to assist the life of the person entitled to support only where, on the premise that the support obligor is able to live in a manner commensurate with his or her social status while having a surplus in livelihood, the person entitled to support cannot maintain his or her life by his or her own means or labor.\\n\\nSince such primary duty of support and secondary duty of support signify not only the degree of performance of the duty but also the order of performance of the duty, a secondary obligor of support bears the duty of support in a subordinate position to the primary obligor of support.\\n\\nTherefore, where a primary obligor of support and a secondary obligor of support both exist at the same time, the primary obligor of support, absent special circumstances, bears the duty of support in priority to the secondary obligor of support; thus, if the secondary obligor of support has supported the person entitled to support, the expenses thereby incurred may be claimed in reimbursement against the primary obligor of support.\\n\\n(2) However, the amount of past support expenses to be reimbursed by one spouse, as the primary obligor of support, to the relatives of the other spouse, who is the secondary obligor of support, should be deemed limited to the duty of support that one spouse owes to the other spouse; therefore, we examine the scope of that duty of support.\\n\\nFirst, with respect to past support expenses among spouses, absent special circumstances, only those expenses accruing after the person entitled to support requested performance of the duty of support from the support obligor and the support obligor nevertheless failed to perform the duty and thus fell into delay in performance may be claimed as support expenses (see, e.g., Supreme Court Order dated 2008. 6. 12., 2005SEU50). Accordingly, past support expenses prior to the demand for performance must be paid only where they accrued after the spouse, as the support obligor, failed to perform the duty of support and thus fell into delay in performance despite a demand for performance, or, if not so, only where special circumstances exist such that, by the nature of the duty of support or under the notion of fairness, such payment should be permitted.\\n\\nIn addition, the amount of support expenses between spouses must be determined by comprehensively considering the extent of support needed, the corresponding degree of performance of the duty of support, the cause and degree of breakdown of the marital life, and the like, in light of the property status and income, standard of living and economic capacity, social status, etc. of both parties.\\n\\nTherefore, even when examining and determining a claim for reimbursement of past support expenses made by the relatives of the other spouse against one spouse, these factors must all be considered in determining the existence and scope of the duty of reimbursement.\\n\\n(3) Meanwhile, Family Litigation Act Article 2(1)2(b), Case No. 1 of Category Ma cases, separately provides as a non-contentious family case the disposition concerning support between spouses pursuant to Civil Act Article 826, and Family Litigation Act Article 2(1)2(b), Case No. 8 of Category Ma cases separately provides as a non-contentious family case the disposition concerning support pursuant to Civil Act Articles 976 through 978. Therefore, a claim by one spouse against the other for support expenses for failure to perform the duty of support between spouses falls under the non-contentious family case of Case No. 1 of the above Category Ma cases, and a claim by one relative against a relative who failed to perform the duty of support among relatives for support expenses falls under the non-contentious family case of Case No. 8 of the above Category Ma cases; however, a claim for reimbursement of support expenses sought by the relatives of the other spouse against one spouse who failed to perform the duty of support between spouses does not fall under any of the Category Ma cases of Family Litigation Act Article 2(1)2(b), and thus cannot be said to belong to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court as a non-contentious family case, but should be regarded as a civil action case.\\n\\nB. According to the facts lawfully found by the court below and the record, the Plaintiff is the mother of the person omitted, who was born in 1968, and the Defendant is the spouse of the person omitted; the person omitted underwent surgery on 2006. 11. 15. for epidural hemorrhage, etc., and as of 2009. 12. 29. remained in a state of confused consciousness and continuing paralysis symptoms. Considering these circumstances in light of the legal principles stated above, the Defendant, as the primary obligor of support, has, absent special circumstances, the duty to support the person omitted in priority to the Plaintiff, who is the secondary obligor of support; therefore, if, as alleged by the Plaintiff, the Plaintiff supported the person omitted by paying the person omitted’s hospital expenses, etc., then the Defendant would have the duty to reimburse the Plaintiff within the scope of the duty of support that he owes to the person omitted.\\n\\nMeanwhile, in light of the following circumstances ascertainable from the record, namely, that it was difficult for the person omitted to request support from the Defendant because, among other reasons, communication was impossible; that the Defendant was well aware that the person omitted needed support and in fact also provided support; and that the Defendant knew that, even after he ceased providing support, the person omitted still remained in need of support and that the Plaintiff continued providing support, there is considerable room to view that there were circumstances sufficient to find that the Defendant also had the duty to pay past support expenses accruing before receiving any demand for performance of the duty of support from the person omitted.\\n\\nC. Nevertheless, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s claim for reimbursement on the ground that the Defendant could not be regarded as a prior-ranking obligor of support over the Plaintiff and therefore had no duty of reimbursement; this is a misjudgment resulting from an erroneous understanding of the legal principles concerning the order of performance of the duty of support.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination; it is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices, as stated in the Disposition."}
{"[2022SEU771]": "The order of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the Daegu Family Court."}

{"[91MEU245]": "The Court determines the grounds of appeal by the Plaintiff.\\n\\n1. The court below found the following facts: After the Defendant was bereaved of his former wife, he remarried the Plaintiff on November 9, 1984, in order to alleviate his loneliness in old age, and had lived together with her in a rented room located in C, Dobong-gu, Seoul. However, after marital discord arising from differences in personality between the spouses and conflicts between the Plaintiff and the children born of the Defendant’s former wife, the Defendant paid the Plaintiff KRW 3,000,000 as consolation money and, after divorcing by mutual agreement on April 22, 1988, the Plaintiff continued to reside in the same rented room, while the Defendant had been living together with the family of D, the eldest son born of the former wife. Thereafter, around July 1988, the Plaintiff went to Eocheongdo in Jeonbuk, where the Defendant was staying for fishing, and, urging him to remarry her while saying that she would return the money received as consolation money, induced the Defendant to agree thereto, whereupon the Defendant executed and delivered a written pledge containing the purport that he would entrust the procedures for filing the marriage registration to the Plaintiff. Based on this pledge, the Plaintiff completed the marriage registration alone on September 8. The Plaintiff, despite having also executed a written pledge to the effect that, in agreeing to remarry, she “repents that the life of the two persons has not been harmonious during that time and pledges that she will serve the Defendant well without inconvenience from now on,” thereafter refused the Defendant’s request that she live together with the family of the said D, and continued to live alone, did not immediately inform the Defendant of the completion of the marriage registration as stated above, did not perform the promise to return the consolation money, and persisted in refusing to enter the Defendant’s residence unless the Defendant separately moved out and lived elsewhere. The Plaintiff and the children born of the Defendant’s former wife, especially the said D, were not on good terms, and the Plaintiff’s health condition was poor because she was suffering from degenerative spondylitis and the like. On the other hand, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s assertion that the Defendant had abandoned the Plaintiff with malicious intent or that the Plaintiff and the Defendant had agreed to live separately from the children born of the Defendant’s former wife, on the ground that there was no material to support such assertion. It then held that, although spouses generally have mutual duties of support and therefore, if the wife lacks the ability to support herself, the husband is liable to support her, in a case such as this one, where the Plaintiff herself has been persistently refusing, without just cause, the Defendant’s request that she return to the Defendant’s residence and live together with him, and is insisting on living alone, the Plaintiff cannot claim support money from the Defendant (the court below also considered that, as the Plaintiff would not live at the Defendant’s residence, she could not claim support money from the Defendant), and accordingly dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim for support money in this case.\\n\\n2. Since the duties of cohabitation, support, and mutual assistance between spouses prescribed in Article 826(1) of the Civil Act are a concrete expression of the broad duty of cooperation for the maintenance of a normal and harmonious marital relationship, and are not separate and independent duties, if one spouse, without just cause, refuses cohabitation and thereby himself or herself abandons the duty of cooperation, then, unless there are special circumstances such as that the other spouse’s claim for cohabitation constitutes an abuse of rights, it should be deemed that the spouse cannot claim payment of support money from the other spouse (see Supreme Court Decision 75MEU17,18, decided June 22, 1976).\\n\\nConsidering the factual circumstances lawfully established by the court below and the various other circumstances appearing in the record, in particular, the ages and family relationships of the Plaintiff and the Defendant; the motive by which the Plaintiff and the Defendant first married, the cause of the divorce and the life after the divorce, and the circumstances by which they remarried; the fact that Article 826(2) of the Civil Act then in force at the time of their remarriage (as in effect before amendment by Act No. 4199 of January 13, 1990) provided that cohabitation of spouses shall take place at the husband’s domicile or residence; and the fact that it is one of the traditional customs and good morals of our country for children to support and care for elderly parents, it does not appear that the Defendant, who was already over 65 years old at the time of the remarriage and who, after divorcing the Plaintiff, had been living together with the eldest son born of his former wife, the daughter-in-law, and the grandchildren, abused the right to demand cohabitation by asking the Plaintiff to cohabit at his domicile; accordingly, unlike the argument on appeal, the mere fact that the Plaintiff and the Defendant’s eldest son born of the former wife had not been on good terms in the past cannot be deemed to constitute just cause for the Plaintiff to refuse the Defendant’s request for cohabitation.\\n\\nIn the same purport, the court below’s determination dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim for support money in this case is proper, and there is no illegality in the judgment below as argued on appeal; therefore, the argument is without merit.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the Plaintiff’s appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the appeal shall be borne by the losing Plaintiff. The opinions of the judges concurring in the case being unanimous, judgment is rendered as ordered."}

question: A and B entered into a contract under which B would purchase land X owned by A, and agreed that the purchase price would be paid simultaneously with the delivery of land X and the completion of registration of transfer of ownership. C provided a joint and several suretyship for B’s obligation to pay the purchase price to A under the above sales contract. Which of the following statements are incorrect? (Each statement is independent, and where there is a dispute, according to case law) (a) After B pays A the full purchase price, if B assigns the claim for registration of transfer of ownership to D and B notifies A thereof, D may directly demand A’s performance of the procedure for registration of transfer of ownership. (b) A assigned to D the claim for the purchase price against B while explaining the content of the above contract and the fact that registration of transfer of ownership for land X had not yet been completed, and on the same day B gave assent to the assignment of claim without reservation of objection. Thereafter, if D demands B to pay the assigned amount, B cannot refuse D’s demand on the ground that A had not tendered performance of the obligation to register transfer of ownership. (c) Even if A assigned the claim for the purchase price against B to D and notified B thereof by an instrument bearing a fixed date, if A later assigned the claim against B again to E, then after A and D rescinded by agreement the assignment contract between them and D notified B of the rescission by agreement, E acquires the claim for the purchase price against B absent special circumstances. (d) If A assigns the claim for the purchase price against B to D and notifies B thereof, then absent special circumstances not only the claim against B but also the claim against C is transferred to D together. (e) Although A and B agreed in the sales contract not to assign the claim, A assigned the claim for the purchase price to D, who knew of such agreement, and notified B thereof, and thereafter D again assigned the claim for the purchase price to E, who did not know of the agreement between A and B, and notified B thereof, B cannot assert against E the existence of the special agreement prohibiting assignment of claims.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2002DA21509]": "The appeal is dismissed. The costs of appeal shall be borne by the Plaintiff."}

{"[2011DA73472]": "The grounds for final appeal shall be examined. The statements in the supplementary written submissions, etc. filed after the expiration of the period for filing the petition of final appeal shall be considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. In a sale and purchase agreement, unless otherwise agreed, the seller’s obligation to transfer ownership, which has consideration value, and the buyer’s obligation to pay the purchase price are in a relationship of simultaneous performance; and even if one obligation is a prior performance obligation, if the due date for performance has passed, then, unless there are special circumstances such as an agreement to continue to perform first notwithstanding the lapse of the due date, the obligations of both the seller and the buyer, including that obligation, are placed in a relationship of simultaneous performance. Such legal relationship likewise applies to the obligation to lift the execution of a provisional seizure or a provisional disposition prohibiting disposition, etc., where such execution has been made against the subject matter of the sale, or where a provisional seizure or a provisional disposition prohibiting disposition, etc. has been made against the seller’s claim for registration of transfer of ownership, and it is necessary to lift such provisional seizure or provisional disposition execution, etc. in order to perform the obligation to transfer ownership under the sale and purchase agreement (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2001DA27784, 27791, rendered on July 27, 2001).\\n\\nMeanwhile, where the parties to a contract have reduced the contents of the contract into writing constituting a dispositive document, if the objective meaning of the wording is clear, then, unless there are special circumstances, the existence and content of the declaration of intent as stated in such wording must be recognized; however, if the objective meaning of the wording does not clearly emerge, then, regardless of the parties’ internal intent, the contents of the wording, the motive and circumstances leading to the formation of the contract, the purpose the parties seek to achieve through the contract and their true intent, trade customs, etc. must be comprehensively considered, and the contents of the contract between the parties must be reasonably construed in accordance with the rules of logic and experience, and the common sense of society at large and the general understanding of transactions, so as to accord with the ideals of social justice and equity. In particular, where the contents of a contract asserted by one party impose a serious burden on the other party, the wording should be construed even more strictly (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 95DA6465, rendered on May 23, 1995, and Supreme Court Decision 2000DA72572, rendered on May 24, 2002).\\n\\n2. According to the court below and the reasons of the first-instance judgment cited in part by the court below, as well as the evidence lawfully admitted, the following facts may be found.\\n\\na. The designating companies, Samdong GV Tech Co., Ltd. and Sky W Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “designating companies”), of the Defendant (the designated party; hereinafter referred to as the “Defendant”) entered into the trust agreement at issue with Korea Real Estate Trust Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Korea Real Estate Trust”), designating the designating companies as beneficiaries of the trust principal and trust proceeds, and entrusted the real property at issue to Korea Real Estate Trust. On April 8, 2008, the Plaintiff entered into a sale and purchase agreement to purchase the real property at issue from the designating companies for KRW 920 hundred million under the joint and several guarantee of the Defendant’s designating parties (hereinafter referred to as the “sale and purchase agreement at issue”), and on May 15, 2008, paid a down payment of KRW 40 hundred million to the designating companies pursuant to the sale and purchase agreement at issue.\\n\\nb. The sale and purchase agreement at issue provides the following with respect to performance of the contract.\\n\\n(1) Article 4 (hereinafter referred to as “Article 4”), under the title “Closing,” provides in paragraph 1 as follows: “The buyer shall, by May 30, 2008 (the closing date, which was later changed to July 1, 2008 by an agreement to amend the sale and purchase agreement), simultaneously with the satisfaction of the conditions precedent under Article 6 (hereinafter referred to as “Article 6”) of this Agreement and the seller’s provision of the documents and performance under paragraph 3 of this Article, pay to the seller, in cash or by means immediately convertible into cash, the balance amount settled under paragraph 2 of this Article; provided, however, that payment of the balance may be substituted by the seller’s repayment of its debt to the Military Mutual Aid Association. If the total amount of the balance is less than the total amount of the debt, the seller shall cover the shortfall.” Paragraph 2 states: “The settled balance under paragraph 1 of this Article means the remaining amount after the sale price reduced pursuant to Article 2, paragraph 2 of this Agreement is settled in the following manner,” and each item thereof provides for the amounts to be deducted from the sale price. Paragraph 3 states: “The seller shall, on the closing date, simultaneously with the buyer’s performance of the obligations under paragraph 1 of this Article, provide the buyer with the documents and performance set forth below,” and item 1 provides for “all documents necessary for the registration of transfer of ownership of the real property in question,” while item 4 provides respectively for “originals or copies of documents capable of proving full payment of all taxes and public charges, such as national taxes, local taxes, congestion charge, electricity charges, water and sewage charges, city gas charges, environmental improvement charges, road occupation charges, traffic inducement charges, charges related to road occupation, etc.”\\n\\n(2) Article 5 (hereinafter referred to as “Article 5”), under the title “Representations and Warranties,” provides in paragraph 1 as follows: “The seller represents and warrants that, as of the date of execution of this Agreement, none of the matters listed in the following items differs from the facts, and further represents and warrants that the contents so represented and warranted will not differ from the facts until the closing date.” The matters represented and warranted by the seller are set forth in each item thereof; item 14 states that “except for the Military Mutual Aid Association’s first-priority beneficiary right (benefit limit amount: KRW 715 hundred million), the buyer’s second-priority beneficiary right, and the buyer’s preemptive right to purchase, no mortgage right, leasehold right, registered lease right, pledge, lien, commercial lien, security by transfer, security by sale, preemptive purchase right, right of redemption, provisional seizure, provisional disposition, provisional registration, neighborhood relations under the Civil Act, or any other real right, claim, restriction, or encumbrance whatsoever has been created on the real property in question.” Item 22 states that “the seller has paid all national taxes, local taxes, road occupation charges, congestion charges, environmental improvement charges, traffic inducement charges, electricity charges, water charges, various public charges, and similar charges assessed or notified in connection with the real property in question by the closing date, and there are no objections, administrative lawsuits, or other disputes relating thereto, nor is there any possibility that such disputes will arise in the future.” Paragraph 2 states: “The buyer represents and warrants that, as of the date of execution of this Agreement, none of the matters listed in the following items differs from the facts, and warrants that the contents so represented and warranted will not differ from the facts until the closing date.” The matters represented and warranted by the buyer are set forth in each item thereof.\\n\\n(3) Article 6 (hereinafter referred to as “Article 6”), under the title “Conditions Precedent to Closing,” provides in paragraph 1 as follows: “The buyer shall have an obligation to close only if all of the following conditions are satisfied. Provided, however, that even if all of the following conditions are not satisfied, the buyer may waive satisfaction of the conditions and request closing by written notice.” Item 1 provides that “the seller’s representations and warranties shall be consistent with the facts and accurate on the date of execution of this Agreement and/or on the closing date”; item 2 provides that “the seller shall perform all obligations and covenants set forth in this Agreement by the closing date”; item 3 provides that “no right of rescission under Article 12 of this Agreement shall arise in favor of the buyer between the date of execution of this Agreement and the closing date”; and item 4 provides that “no litigation, administrative proceeding, or arbitration that adversely affects the seller in performing the obligations under this Agreement shall arise.” Paragraph 2, on the other hand, provides as follows: “The seller shall have an obligation to close only if all of the following conditions are satisfied. Provided, however, that even if all of the following conditions are not satisfied, the seller may waive satisfaction of the conditions and request closing by written notice.” Item 1 provides that “the buyer’s representations and warranties shall be consistent with the facts and accurate on the date of execution of this Agreement and/or on the closing date”; item 2 provides that “the buyer shall perform all obligations and covenants set forth in this Agreement by the closing date”; and item 3 provides that “no right of rescission under Article 12 of this Agreement shall arise in favor of the seller between the date of execution of this Agreement and the closing date.”\\n\\n(4) Article 8 (hereinafter referred to as “Article 8”), under the title “Covenants,” provides in paragraph 7 as follows: “The seller shall cause all mortgage rights, leasehold rights, and other rights in rem limiting the real property in question, such as lease rights, as well as pledges, liens, commercial liens, security by sale, preemptive purchase rights, rights of redemption, provisional seizure, provisional disposition, provisional registration, neighborhood relations under the Civil Act, and any other real right, claim, or other restriction or encumbrance whatsoever, to be removed by the closing date.”\\n\\nc. On July 1, 2008, the closing date under the sale and purchase agreement at issue, in relation to the real property at issue, in addition to the first-, second-, and third-priority beneficiary rights (aggregate secured debt: KRW 90.52 hundred million), there were attachments by the Gangnam District Office and the Seoul Southern District Tax Office (aggregate amount of the claimed receivables: KRW 1,191,674,230) concerning the beneficiary rights, etc. of the designating companies under the trust agreement at issue, and as to part of the real property at issue, a lease agreement with a lease deposit of KRW 1,953,820,000 had been entered into, naming Barun Law LLC as the lessee.\\n\\nd. On July 1, 2008, the closing date, the Plaintiff served the designating companies with a demand stating that “if the designating companies perform all of the conditions precedent under Article 6 of the sale and purchase agreement at issue, the Plaintiff, simultaneously upon receiving the balance of KRW 672 hundred million and KRW 2,300 ten-thousand (sale price of KRW 920 hundred million - down payment of KRW 40 hundred million - the Plaintiff’s lease deposit of KRW 200 hundred million - the lease deposit of KRW 7 hundred million and KRW 7,700 ten-thousand that Sky W, as a designating party, must pay to the Plaintiff pursuant to Article 11, paragraph 1 of the sale and purchase agreement at issue), shall perform the provision of the documents for registration of transfer of ownership concerning the real property at issue, etc.” The Plaintiff also sent a request for closing, attaching thereto notices of loan approval received from Korea Exchange Bank and Shinhan Bank, each in the amount of KRW 23 hundred million, and balance inquiry statements from each bank proving that deposits of at least KRW 40 hundred million, which the Plaintiff could immediately withdraw, had been deposited.\\n\\ne. However, the designating companies did not cause the attachments by the Seoul Southern District Tax Office and Gangnam District Office concerning the beneficiary rights, etc. of the designating companies to be cancelled by July 15, 2008; rather, additional creditor attachments, etc. were effected at the request of Daelim Industrial Co., Ltd. against Sky W’s beneficiary rights under the trust agreement at issue and its claim for registration of transfer of ownership on the ground of termination of the trust.\\n\\nf. On July 24, 2008, the Plaintiff again demanded the designating companies to remove all attachments, provisional seizures, etc., including the provisional seizure established against Sky W’s beneficiary rights under the trust agreement at issue with claims for construction payments, etc. as preserved claims and the attachments established with tax claims as preserved claims.\\n\\ng. Nevertheless, when the designating companies failed to remove the above attachments and provisional seizures, and instead an additional attachment of claims by Modu & T Co., Ltd. was made against Sky W’s trust beneficiary rights, and even a fourth-priority beneficiary right was additionally created, the Plaintiff notified the designating companies on September 18, 2008 that the sale and purchase agreement at issue had been rescinded.\\n\\n3. As to ground of final appeal No. 1.\\n\\nThe court below and the first-instance judgment cited by the court below found, based on the contents of the sale and purchase agreement at issue, including the content of Article 8, paragraph 7, and the fact that the Plaintiff, even after July 1, 2008, the closing date, demanded the designating companies to remove the attachments or provisional seizures by the Seoul Southern District Tax Office, Gangnam District Office, etc. against the beneficiary rights of the designating companies arising from the trust agreement at issue, and other facts found in the judgment, that the obligation of the designating companies to cancel the attachments or provisional seizures by the Seoul Southern District Tax Office and Gangnam District Office, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the “obligation to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue”) constitutes an obligation of the seller under the sale and purchase agreement at issue.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles and factual circumstances discussed above, as well as the evidence lawfully admitted, the court below’s above determination cannot be said to be erroneous as having misapprehended the legal principles concerning the interpretation of dispositive documents and thereby affected the judgment.\\n\\n4. As to ground of final appeal No. 2.\\n\\na. According to the factual circumstances discussed above, in the sale and purchase agreement at issue, while specifying the closing date and the matters to be performed by both parties by the closing date, Article 6, under the title “Conditions Precedent to Closing,” sets forth the matters to be performed by the seller and the buyer, and Article 4 sets forth the conditions precedent to be fulfilled by the seller by the closing date, as stated in the court below’s judgment.\\n\\nb. However, the factual circumstances discussed above reveal the following.\\n\\n(1) In the sale and purchase agreement at issue entered into on April 8, 2008, the deadline for payment of the down payment is set as May 15, 2008, and the closing date at which all obligations set forth in the sale and purchase agreement are to be performed is set as May 30, 2008, while no other due date for performance is separately specified. Therefore, the closing date set forth in Article 4, paragraph 1 means the final due date by which the seller and the buyer must perform all obligations under the sale and purchase agreement, and it is construed as meaning that by that date both parties are to complete the closing by performing all obligations and covenants set forth in the sale and purchase agreement.\\n\\n(2) Although the term “conditions precedent to closing” is used in Article 6, Article 6 sets forth, together with the seller, the conditions to be performed by the buyer as well before closing; accordingly, it is not clear from the wording whether, in relation to the performance of such conditions precedent, either the seller or the buyer is to perform its own conditions precedent first.\\n\\n(3) In addition, in order to impose on the counterparty the obligation to close pursuant to Article 6, the conditions precedent to be performed by the seller, in addition to consistency of the seller’s representations and warranties with the facts, are “performance of all obligations and covenants set forth in this sale and purchase agreement” and the nonexistence of a right of rescission of contract; likewise, the conditions to be performed by the buyer are, in addition to consistency of the buyer’s representations and warranties with the facts, “performance of all obligations and covenants set forth in this sale and purchase agreement” and the nonexistence of a right of rescission of contract. Thus, Article 6 does not limit the obligations to be performed as conditions precedent in the case of the seller and the buyer to “obligations to be performed prior to closing,” but instead provides for “all obligations and covenants set forth in this sale and purchase agreement,” and all obligations and covenants set forth in this sale and purchase agreement include both the seller’s obligation to transfer ownership and the buyer’s obligation to pay the price. Ultimately, if construed according to the wording, when the sale and purchase agreement at issue is not rescinded, the seller, if the buyer performs all obligations set forth in the sale and purchase agreement, including the obligation to pay the price, will bear the obligation to transfer ownership upon closing; likewise, the buyer, if the seller performs all obligations set forth in the sale and purchase agreement, including the obligation to transfer ownership, will bear the obligation to pay the price upon closing. Conversely, if the counterparty does not perform such obligations, the seller or the buyer should be deemed entitled to refuse its own performance; therefore, it cannot be concluded that the agreement imposes on either party a prior performance obligation for all such obligations and covenants.\\n\\n(4) Further, Article 4, paragraph 1 provides that “the buyer shall, ... by the closing date, simultaneously with the satisfaction of the conditions precedent under Article 6 of this Agreement and the seller’s provision of the documents and performance under paragraph 3 of this Article, ... pay to the seller the balance settled under paragraph 2 of this Article,” thereby, in terms of wording, placing “satisfaction of the conditions precedent under Article 6” and “the seller’s provision of the documents and performance under Article 3 of this Article” on an equal footing, and expressing that they are to occur simultaneously with the buyer’s obligation to pay the price.\\n\\nAlthough Article 6, paragraph 1 provides that all obligations and covenants set forth in this sale and purchase agreement, being conditions precedent, are to be performed “by the closing date,” so long as Article 4, paragraph 1 sets the time for satisfaction of the conditions precedent as “by the closing date,” those conditions precedent need only be satisfied by the closing date. (Also, as noted above, Article 8, paragraph 7 likewise provides that all mortgage rights and other restrictions or encumbrances created on the real property are to be removed by the closing date.) And, as noted above, satisfaction of the conditions precedent under Article 6 means the seller’s performance of all obligations and covenants set forth in this sale and purchase agreement, and this may include matters concerning the seller’s provision of documents and performance under Article 4, paragraph 3. Accordingly, the practical meaning of “satisfaction of the conditions precedent under Article 6” and “the seller’s provision of the documents and performance under Article 4, paragraph 3” may be said to be the same.\\n\\nThe subject matter of the provision and performance under Article 4, paragraph 3, which is undoubtedly set in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the obligation to pay the balance under Article 4, paragraph 1, consists, except for the documents for registration of transfer of ownership and completion of delivery of the real property, mostly of matters necessary for transferring full ownership of the real property at issue, and are merely documents for proving performance of obligations related to the matters stipulated in the representations and warranties under Article 5. Moreover, in light of the fact that the obligation to remove restrictions or encumbrances created on the subject matter of the sale, which are required in order to transfer full ownership, is ordinarily construed as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance with payment of the purchase price under a sale and purchase agreement, there is no need to distinguish, at the closing stage, between such performance of obligations and the obligation to provide documents proving such performance. In other words, even if the obligation to remove restrictions or encumbrances such as provisional seizure and provisional disposition is viewed as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the buyer’s obligation to pay the balance, the buyer may refuse to pay the balance if the obligation to remove such restrictions has not been performed; thus, even if the obligation to remove such restrictions is not regarded as a prior performance obligation, no specially inequitable result arises for the buyer.\\n\\nc. (1) Considering these circumstances relating to the sale and purchase agreement at issue, together with the legal principles concerning simultaneous performance in sales contracts discussed above and the general legal principle of contract interpretation that the wording imposing serious liability on the other party in a contract whose objective meaning is not clear must be construed even more strictly, the sale and purchase agreement at issue is construed not as proceeding through a stage of closing and then moving to a performance stage thereafter, but rather as meaning that closing itself constitutes final performance. The conditions precedent to closing stipulated in Article 6 are matters that both parties must satisfy for final performance, and under Article 4 the sale is deemed completed by satisfying and proving those conditions precedent by the time of final performance, thereby enabling the seller and the buyer to complete the final performance of transferring ownership and paying the balance to each other. Therefore, the obligation of the seller, the designating companies, to perform their obligations under Article 6 to satisfy the conditions precedent to closing, including the obligation to pay in full all taxes and public charges or obligations concerning tax debts, as well as the obligation to remove the attachments and provisional seizures, etc. set forth in Article 4, paragraph 3, item 4 of the sale and purchase agreement at issue, cannot be concluded to be a prior performance obligation that must be performed before closing; rather, like the obligation to provide documents proving such performance, it may be viewed as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the Plaintiff’s obligation to pay the balance, who is the buyer.\\n\\n(2) And even if the obligations set forth in the conditions precedent to closing are of the nature of prior performance obligations, in light of the circumstances relating to the sale and purchase agreement at issue as described above, it appears difficult to conclude that, notwithstanding the passing of the closing date of the sale and purchase agreement at issue, which in this case has the character of the final due date for performance, the parties nonetheless agreed that the obligation to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue would remain a prior performance obligation. Moreover, this is all the more so considering that the obligation to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue is not about attachments, etc. directly created on the real property at issue, which is the subject matter of the sale and purchase agreement at issue, but rather about the beneficiary rights of the designating companies arising under the trust agreement at issue, and is not directly stipulated in the sale and purchase agreement itself but, as noted above, is recognized as an obligation of the seller through interpretation of the sale and purchase agreement.\\n\\n(3) Further, as noted above, in this case the Plaintiff also did not refuse to close on the closing date of the sale and purchase agreement at issue on the ground of nonperformance of the conditions precedent under Article 6 of the sale and purchase agreement at issue; rather, the Plaintiff demanded that the designating companies, if they performed all such conditions precedent, perform the provision of the documents for registration of transfer of ownership at issue, etc., simultaneously upon receiving the balance of KRW 672 hundred million and KRW 2,300 ten-thousand from the Plaintiff, and sent a request for closing attaching thereto notices of loan approval in the amount of KRW 23 hundred million each received from Korea Exchange Bank and Shinhan Bank, together with balance inquiry statements from each bank proving that deposits of at least KRW 40 hundred million, which the Plaintiff could immediately withdraw, had been deposited. Since this factual context also appears to have taken into account the above circumstances that satisfaction of the conditions precedent may be achieved at the final performance stage, it may be said to support the above determination that it is difficult to conclude that the obligation to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue is a prior performance obligation.\\n\\nAnd according to Article 4, the buyer must pay the balance in “cash or a means immediately convertible into cash” in order to close.
