However, according to the evidence lawfully admitted, the loan approval notice from Shinhan Bank, tendered by the Plaintiff, made the removal of collateral restrictions factors, including the first-priority beneficiary right under the real estate security trust agreement, as well as the lease rights and option conditions arising under Article 11 of the sale and purchase agreement at issue, a condition for loan approval upon execution of the loan, including the obtaining of confirmations, etc.; thus, on the face of the wording, it may be said to conflict with the sale and purchase agreement at issue. Accordingly, a question may arise as to whether the loan approval notice from Shinhan Bank with such loan approval conditions attached actually constitutes a means of payment under Article 4, and the Defendant has contested its lawfulness from the first instance onward.\\n\\nIf, as asserted in the Defendant’s grounds for final appeal, the above tender of the balance was unlawful, and nevertheless the Plaintiff continued to insist on such tender of the balance even after the closing date, up to the above demand or notice of rescission, and if, in view of the Plaintiff’s financial capacity, it is difficult to expect other lawful tender of performance, this may constitute a ground under Article 536, paragraph 2 of the Civil Act for refusing to perform one’s own obligation until the counterparty tenders performance of its obligation (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DA24106, 24113, rendered on October 26, 2006, and Supreme Court Decision 2011DA93025, rendered on March 29, 2012). Thus, as noted above, it may also be deemed that there is no prior performance obligation with respect to the obligation to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue after the closing date in this case, or that there is a ground on which liability for nonperformance cannot be imposed.\\n\\nd. Nevertheless, the court below, based solely on the reasons stated in the judgment, concluded that the obligation of the designating companies, who are the sellers, to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue was in a prior performance relationship with the Plaintiff’s, who is the buyer’s, obligation to pay the balance, and on that premise, without examining at all whether the Plaintiff’s tender of performance of the balance payment obligation was lawful, determined that the Plaintiff’s rescission of the sale and purchase agreement on September 18, 2008, based on nonperformance of the obligation to cancel the attachments, etc. at issue, was lawful.\\n\\nAccordingly, the court below’s judgment contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning interpretation of contracts, the principles of simultaneous performance and prior performance in sale and purchase agreements, and the legal principles concerning nonperformance of obligations, and by failing to conduct the necessary review. The assertion in the grounds for final appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds for final appeal, the portion of the court below’s judgment against the Defendant concerning the return of the down payment and the payment of liquidated damages and delay damages thereon is reversed, and this portion of the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged in unanimous agreement of the Justices participating.\\n\\n[[Appendix] List of Designating Parties: Omitted]"}

{"[2015DA46119]": "The grounds for final appeal are examined (the statements in the written submissions filed after the expiration of the period for filing the petition for final appeal are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for final appeal).\\n\\n1. With respect to the assertion in the grounds for final appeal that the subject matter of the second claim assignment agreement is the future claim for return of the lease deposit to be recovered by the assignor, Nonparty 1\\n\\nThe court below, based on the circumstances as stated in its opinion, determined that the subject matter of the second claim assignment agreement is merely the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue, which is identical to the claim assigned under the first claim assignment agreement, and that it is difficult to view it as a future claim for return of the lease deposit that the assignor, Nonparty 1, would recover from the first assignee, Nonparty 2.\\n\\nExamining the reasons for the lower court judgment in light of the record, the lower court’s determination is proper and acceptable, and there is no illegality that affected the outcome of the judgment due to inadequate judicial examination concerning the purpose of the claim assignment agreement and the parties’ intent, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n2. With respect to the assertion in the grounds for final appeal that the Plaintiff has the status of a rightful assignee of the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue\\n\\nA. The assignment of a nominative claim changes the subject to whom the claim belongs by a legal act, and thus has the nature of a so-called quasi-real right act or disposition act (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on Mar. 24, 2011, 2010DA100711), so for it to be valid, the assignor must have the authority to dispose of the claim. If a person without disposal authority assigns a nominative claim, it cannot, absent special circumstances, take effect as an assignment of claim, and the assignee cannot acquire the claim.\\n\\nIf the assignor first assigned a nominative claim to the first assignee, and thereafter the first assignee lawfully satisfied the requirements for opposing third parties by means of a document bearing a fixed date, the claim is thereby transferred to the first assignee and the assignor loses the authority to dispose of the claim. Accordingly, even if the assignor later assigns the same claim to the second assignee, the second assignee cannot acquire that claim. In such case, even if the first assignment agreement was entered into in order to secure another debt, since the claim is transferred externally to the first assignee and the first assignee acquires the claim, the second assignee likewise cannot acquire the claim through the second assignment agreement concluded thereafter.\\n\\nAlso, even if after the second assignment agreement the assignor and the first assignee mutually terminated the first assignment agreement and the first assignee notified the debtor of that fact, thereby causing the claim to revest in the assignor, absent special circumstances, the second assignment agreement made by the assignor without disposal authority cannot become valid as an assignment of claim, and therefore it cannot be said that the second assignee thereby automatically acquires the claim.\\n\\nB. The court below, after recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion, determined in substance that: ① since the assignment of a nominative claim has the nature of a quasi-real right act or disposition act, the assignor must have disposal authority; ② pursuant to the first claim assignment agreement and the notice by a document bearing a fixed date, the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue was definitively transferred to the first assignee, Nonparty 2; ③ as a result, the assignor, Nonparty 1, became a person without rights who had lost disposal authority over the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue, so the second claim assignment agreement concluded thereafter was a disposition act made by Nonparty 1, a person without rights, and therefore void as an assignment of claim; ④ accordingly, the second assignee, the Plaintiff, does not acquire the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue, and the same applies even if the first claim assignment agreement was entered into in order to secure Nonparty 1’s joint and several surety obligation to Nonparty 2; and ⑤ even if the first claim assignment agreement was later mutually terminated, it would only mean that Nonparty 1 again acquires the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue, so the second claim assignment agreement cannot become valid as an assignment of claim by virtue of such subsequent circumstances.\\n\\nC. Examining the reasons for the lower court judgment in light of the legal principles and the record as seen above, although there is a part of the lower court’s reasoning that is not appropriate, the conclusion that the second claim assignment agreement made by the assignor, Nonparty 1, after the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue had been transferred to the first assignee, Nonparty 2, and after the assignor had lost disposal authority over it, has no effect as an assignment of claim, and that the same is true even if the first claim assignment agreement was thereafter mutually terminated, so that the second assignee, the Plaintiff, does not acquire the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue, is proper and acceptable. There is no illegality in the lower court’s determination that affected the outcome of the judgment due to misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the validity of double assignment of a nominative claim, the effect of notice as a requirement for opposing third parties in an assignment of claim, the standard point for determining the relative priority between double assignees of a nominative claim, or the status of a subordinate assignee who has satisfied the requirements for opposing third parties in the case where a double assignment of a nominative claim was made for the purpose of securing a debt, or due to violation of the rules of evidence or inadequate judicial examination, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the final appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the final appeal are to be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question: A has, against B, a matured loan claim in the amount of KRW 200 million (Claim A), and B, who is in an over-indebted state, has, against C, a matured loan claim in the amount of KRW 200 million (Claim B), and B made a gift of the X real property owned by B to D. Which of the following explanations is incorrect? (Each statement is independent, and where there is a dispute, case law shall apply)
A: A may, in order to preserve Claim A, bring an action, by subrogating to B, against C seeking that C pay Claim B directly to A, and if, after the judgment became final and conclusive, A’s creditor E obtained an order of seizure and an order of assignment with respect to such claim of A against C for payment, then both the seizure order and the assignment order are void.
B: Where A, without seeking payment of Claim A against B, brings a creditor’s subrogation action against C seeking payment of Claim B on the basis of Claim A as the preserved claim, C may contest by asserting that Claim A was extinguished by performance, but C may not oppose A by asserting that Claim A was extinguished by prescription.
C: If, after B became aware that A had exercised the creditor’s subrogation right against C, during the pendency of the creditor’s subrogation action an order of seizure and an order of assignment were made with respect to Claim B upon the application of F, another creditor of B, then the order of assignment with respect to Claim B is void unless special circumstances exist, but the order of seizure is valid, so the above creditor’s subrogation action by A against C is dismissed.
D: Where A has, pursuant to an action to revoke a fraudulent act, a claim for compensation of value against D, it is not permissible for D to assert set-off against A on the ground that D has a claim against B and thereby refuse to pay the apportioned amount corresponding to D’s own claim out of the total amount of the claims.
E: If A, using Claim A as the preserved claim, filed an action for revocation of a fraudulent act against D within the preclusive period, and after the preclusive period had expired changed the preserved claim to a claim for return of unjust enrichment against B, this does not constitute an exchange amendment of the action, so the above action for revocation of a fraudulent act is lawful.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2001DA13532]": "A creditor’s adding or substituting the claim it seeks to preserve while seeking revocation of a fraudulent act is merely a change in the assertions concerning the means of attack that make the right of revocation of the fraudulent act well-founded, and is not a change in the subject matter of litigation or in the claim itself; therefore, it cannot be said to be a change of the action (see Supreme Court Decision 64DA564, rendered on November 24, 1964).\\n\\nIn this case, the Plaintiff, on August 9, 1999, filed an action seeking revocation of the gift contract described in the judgment and cancellation of the registration of transfer of ownership described in the judgment, by designating as the preserved right for revocation of a fraudulent act a reimbursement claim of 5,089,753 won held by the Plaintiff against Non-party 2, who was a joint and several guarantor under the small-loan guarantee insurance contract concluded between the Plaintiff and Non-party 1 on September 6, 1995; then, when the said claim was extinguished in the court of first instance due to the Defendant’s deposit of performance, the Plaintiff, in a preparatory pleading dated September 5, 2000, asserted that the reimbursement claim of 18,013,680 won held by the Plaintiff against Non-party 2 under the small-loan guarantee insurance contract concluded between the Plaintiff and Non-party 2 on August 26, 1994 also constituted the preserved right for revocation of a fraudulent act. The court below held that this constituted a substitutive amendment of the action, and determined that the action for revocation of a fraudulent act as thus substitutively amended had been filed after the expiration of one year from the date the fraudulent act was known, and was therefore improper.\\n\\nThis determination of the court below is contrary to the legal principle stated above, and constitutes an illegality that affected the conclusion of the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning amendment of an action.\\n\\nAccordingly, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below; judgment is rendered as stated in the operative part."}

{"[2009DA34160]": "We determine the grounds of appeal (a supplemental brief of grounds of appeal submitted after the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal has elapsed is considered only to the extent that it supplements the grounds of appeal).\\n\\n1. Concerning the argument that the Plaintiff’s right to demand cancellation registration against Non-party 1 and others has been extinguished\\nIn a claim brought by a creditor against a third party by exercising the creditor’s subrogation right, the third-party obligor may not oppose defenses that the debtor has against the creditor, and where the statute of limitations on a claim has been completed, the person who may invoke it is, in principle, only the person who directly receives the benefit of the limitations defense, and the third-party obligor in a creditor’s subrogation action may not exercise it (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2001DA10151 rendered on February 12, 2004).\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, with respect to the Defendant’s argument that this action, which was filed in subrogation of Non-party 1 and others for the purpose of preserving the above rights on the ground that not only had the statute of limitations for the Plaintiff’s right to demand cancellation of the provisional registration and ownership transfer registration against Non-party 1 and others expired, but also more than 10 years had passed since the maturity date of the obligation secured by the above provisional registration, so that the Plaintiff could no longer demand cancellation of the above registrations from Non-party 1 and others, was unlawful, the court below’s conclusion rejecting that argument, although it constructed its reasoning differently, was correct, and there is no illegality such as an error of law that affected the conclusion of the judgment.\\n\\n2. Concerning the argument that the maturity date of the right preserved by the Plaintiff has not arrived\\nWhere an ownership transfer registration has been made for the purpose of securing an obligation, the debtor may, even after the maturity date, repay the creditor the principal and interest of the debt and seek cancellation of the ownership transfer registration, and where the creditor’s ownership transfer registration against a third party is void ab initio, the debtor may, even before repayment of the debt, subrogate the creditor and seek performance of the procedures for cancellation registration of the creditor’s ownership transfer registration against the third party on the ground that it is void ab initio (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 85DAKA1792 rendered on January 19, 1988).\\nSince the Plaintiff has the right to demand cancellation of the provisional registration and ownership transfer registration in the names of Non-party 1 and others on condition that it pays the principal and interest of the secured obligation determined in the prior lawsuit against Non-party 1 and others, the court below’s determination to the effect that the Plaintiff may, even before payment of the above principal and interest, subrogate Non-party 1 and others and seek cancellation of the registrations subsequently made in the names of the Defendants is correct in light of the foregoing legal principles, and there is no illegality such as an error of law concerning the maturity date of the right preserved by a creditor’s subrogation right, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Concerning the argument that the Defendants validly acquired rights from Non-party 1 and others, who held the transfer security right\\nThe court below determined that the agreement at issue in this case between the Plaintiff, Non-party 1 and others, and Defendant 2 was concluded by Non-party 2, who had no authority to represent the Plaintiff, and is therefore void, so the ownership transfer registration in the name of Defendant 2 made pursuant to the agreement at issue is void ab initio, and the remaining Defendants’ registrations successively made on that basis are also void ab initio, and that, in light of the circumstances as stated in its opinion, the agreement at issue in this case cannot be regarded as still valid as content permitting Non-party 1 and others to dispose of the real property at issue to Defendant 2 even if the Plaintiff is excluded; in light of the factual findings established by the court below and the evidence lawfully admitted, the court below’s above determination is acceptable as correct, and there is no illegality such as factual error or error of law caused by violation of the rules governing the weighing of evidence, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n4. Concerning the argument that the agreement at issue in this case is effective against the Plaintiff as well pursuant to the apparent representative director doctrine under Article 395 of the Commercial Act\\nIn order for a stock company’s liability arising from the acts of an apparent representative director prescribed by Article 395 of the Commercial Act to be established, not only the third party’s good faith but also the absence of negligence is not required; however, the purport of that provision is to promote trust and safety in commercial transactions by protecting a third party in good faith who relied on the appearance where an officer who is not the company’s representative director engaged in a transaction using a title that could be recognized as having apparent authority to represent the company, and the company is at fault in causing such appearance. Since such a third party’s reliance must be justifiable and worthy of protection, even if the third party believed that the officer, who is not the company’s representative director, had authority to represent the company in the transaction, if the third party was grossly negligent in so believing, the company is not liable to that third party. Gross negligence of the third party here means a state in which, even though the third party could have known that the act of the apparent representative director was not based on representative authority if only the third party had exercised a little care, the third party nevertheless blindly believed it to be an act based on representative authority, thereby falling markedly short of the duty of care ordinarily required in commercial practice, and it refers to a state in which, from the standpoint of fairness, it is reasonable to conclude that there is no need to protect the third party in particular (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DA65073 rendered on September 26, 2003).\\nThe court below determined that, in light of the circumstances as stated in its opinion, although Non-party 2 falsely held himself out as having the status of representative liquidator of the Plaintiff, there was no attributable cause on the part of the Plaintiff in that regard, or that it is reasonable to conclude that Defendant 2, who was a party to the agreement at issue, knew well that Non-party 2 had no authority to represent the Plaintiff, and therefore the effect of the agreement at issue cannot be deemed to extend to the Plaintiff; in light of the foregoing legal principles and the factual findings lawfully established by the court below, the court below’s above determination is correct and acceptable, and there is no illegality such as an error of law concerning the attribution of liability of an apparent representative director, as asserted in the grounds of appeal (although counsel for Defendant 1 also argues, with respect to Non-party 1 and others, that the Plaintiff should bear liability based on the acts of an apparent representative director, the third-party obligor in a creditor’s subrogation action may not oppose defenses that the debtor has against the creditor).\\n\\n5. Concerning the argument that the Plaintiff’s exercise of rights violates the principle of good faith and therefore cannot be permitted\\nThe principle of good faith under civil law means an abstract norm that parties to a legal relationship must not exercise rights or perform obligations in a manner that is inequitable or that betrays trust, taking account of the other party’s interests; in order to deny the exercise of a right on the ground that it violates the principle of good faith, the other party must have been made to trust, or, objectively viewed, must have reached a state in which it is justified to trust, and the exercise of the right contrary to such trust must have reached a state that is unacceptable in light of the notion of justice (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2003DA18401 rendered on May 26, 2006).\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, the court below’s rejection of the Defendants’ argument on the ground that the circumstances asserted by the Defendants alone were insufficient to show that the Plaintiff had given the Defendants cause to trust that it would not make the claim at issue in this case against them, or that the Defendants had formed such trust, was correct, and there is no illegality such as an error of law concerning the principle of good faith, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n6. Concerning the argument that the court below erred in its understanding of the Defendants’ defense of simultaneous performance or failed to exercise its power to clarify concerning it\\nAccording to the record, it can be seen that the Defendants raised a defense of simultaneous performance only with respect to the amount of 488,372,443 won in response to the Plaintiff’s claim in this case, so the court below’s order that, simultaneously with Defendant 2’s receipt of the above amount from Non-party 1 and others, the Defendants perform the procedures for cancellation registration concerning the real property at issue is correct, and there is no illegality such as misunderstanding the content of the Defendants’ defense or failing to exercise the power to clarify, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n7. Concerning the remaining grounds of appeal\\nThe Defendants’ remaining grounds of appeal merely contend, without justifiable legal basis, that the registrations in the Defendants’ names are valid, or merely dispute the weighing of evidence and fact-finding, which are within the exclusive province of the trial court, and thus all of them are unacceptable.\\n\\n8. Conclusion\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing Defendants; it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2013DA55300]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. As to the grounds of appeal by Defendant 5\\n\\nUpon examination in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the court below’s determination, for the reasons stated in its opinion, that Defendant 5 is obligated to perform the procedure for registration of transfer of ownership, based on the share agreement dated April 22, 1991, with respect to the share set forth in Item 2 of the list attached to the judgment below concerning the land in this case, was proper and persuasive, and there is no error in failing to conduct the necessary examination, in violating the duty to clarify, or in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the interpretation of dispositive instruments.\\n\\n2. As to the grounds of appeal by the Plaintiff\\n\\na. As to the appeal against Defendant 5\\n\\nAn appeal seeks, with respect to a judgment unfavorable to oneself, to obtain its revocation or modification in one’s favor; therefore, an appeal from a judgment in which a party has prevailed in full is not permissible because there is no interest in filing an appeal (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 97DA22676, rendered on December 26, 1997).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, it is clear that the court below fully upheld one of the Plaintiff’s alternative claims against Defendant 5; therefore, the appeal filed by the Plaintiff against Defendant 5, over whom the Plaintiff wholly prevailed, is procedurally improper for lack of interest in appeal.\\n\\nb. As to the grounds of appeal against Defendant 1, Defendant 2, Defendant 3, and Defendant 4\\n\\n(1) In a creditor’s subrogation action, if the debtor’s right against the third-party debtor, which is to be preserved through subrogation, is not recognized, the creditor, acting as Plaintiff on his or her own behalf, lacks standing to exercise the debtor’s right against the third-party debtor; accordingly, such subrogation action is procedurally improper and must be dismissed (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 94DA31549, rendered on November 8, 1994).\\n\\nTherefore, where a creditor brings a creditor’s subrogation action, the third-party debtor may not dispute whether the creditor’s right against the debtor is recognized by asserting grounds that require exercise by the holder of the right, such as the debtor’s defense rights or rights of formation against the creditor; however, it is permissible to dispute whether the creditor’s right against the debtor is recognized by asserting facts such as that the legal act giving rise to the creditor’s right against the debtor is null and void, or that the above right has been extinguished by performance, etc., and in such case, the court must, ex officio, examine and determine whether the creditor’s right against the debtor is recognized, taking into account the third-party debtor’s foregoing assertions.\\n\\nMeanwhile, in a title-trust contract where the trustor and the trustee enter into a title trust agreement, and pursuant thereto the trustee, as a party, concludes a contract for the sale and purchase of real estate with an owner who does not know of the existence of the title trust agreement, if the title trust agreement between the trustor and the trustee becomes void upon the lapse of the grace period prescribed by the Act on the Registration of Real Estate under Actual Titleholder’s Name (hereinafter referred to as the “Real Name Act”), then, absent special circumstances, the mandate agreement for the purchase of the real estate, made together with the title trust agreement between the trustor and the trustee, should also be deemed to have become void (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2007DO766, rendered on March 29, 2007), and in this case, the agreement between the trustor and the trustee to transfer the registered title of ownership of the real estate at the trustor’s request shall likewise be deemed void, as it falls within the category of seeking the return of the title-trusted real estate itself on the premise that the title trust agreement is valid (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2006DA35117, rendered on November 9, 2006).\\n\\n(2) According to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, it can be found that ① the Plaintiff, Defendant 4, Defendant 5, Nonparty 1, and Nonparty 2 (hereinafter the remaining four persons excluding the Plaintiff are referred to as “Defendants 4, etc.”) agreed, around 1988, to jointly bear the purchase price, have Defendant 5 purchase all of the land in this case owned by Nonparty 3, and then resell it and distribute the proceeds in proportion to their shares; ② pursuant to the above agreement, Defendant 5 concluded the sales contract at issue with Nonparty 3 on October 11, 1988, and around that time the Plaintiff, Defendant 4, etc. agreed to title-trust all of the land in this case to Defendant 5, Defendant 1, Defendant 2, Defendant 3, and Nonparty 4, who had familial or relative relationships with Defendant 5 and Defendant 4 (hereinafter the above four persons are referred to as “Defendants 1, etc.”), and on December 29, 1988, completed registration of transfer of share ownership in the names of Defendants 1, etc. for each 1/4 share of all of the land in this case; ③ the Plaintiff and Defendants 4, etc. prepared the joint document at issue dated April 22, 1991, stating: “Address: [address omitted], Daejeon, Chungcheongnam-do, 2,010 pyeong; Owners: Plaintiff 600 pyeong, Defendant 4 450 pyeong, Defendant 5 460 pyeong, Nonparty 1 130 pyeong, Nonparty 2 370 pyeong; we acknowledge and confirm each of the above ownership shares.”\\n\\n(3) Based on these facts, the court below determined that ① the mandate agreement dated August 5, 1988, is a title trust agreement combining a mandate agreement for the purchase of real estate, under which Defendant 5 would purchase and hold all of the land in this case and transfer it to the Plaintiff according to the Plaintiff’s intention, and a title trust agreement, under which the registration name would be placed in the name of a third party designated by the Plaintiff and Defendant 5, but internally ownership would belong to the Plaintiff; and since the title trust agreement became void due to the lapse of the grace period prescribed by the Real Name Act, the mandate agreement for the purchase of real estate made together therewith also became void; and ② the share agreement dated April 22, 1991, expressly agreed upon or reconfirmed among the co-purchasers the internal ownership shares held on the basis of the contractual title-trust relationship with Defendant 5 and the registration title-trust relationship with Defendants 1, etc., and it is difficult to regard it as a separate and independent agreement distinguishable from the title trust agreement, or it falls within the category of seeking the return of the title-trusted real estate itself on the premise of a void title trust agreement, and is likewise void; accordingly, the court below held that the Plaintiff’s claim for registration of transfer of share ownership against Defendant 5, which the Plaintiff asserted as the preserved claim for exercising the right of creditor subrogation, could not be recognized.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles set forth above, the foregoing determination of the court below is proper and persuasive, and there is no error in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the status of the third-party debtor in a creditor’s subrogation action, the validity of a contractual title-trust agreement, or the partial invalidity of a legal act.\\n\\nThe Supreme Court Decisions cited by the Plaintiff in the statement of grounds of appeal, namely, Supreme Court Decision 92DA35899, rendered on November 10, 1992, Supreme Court Decision 93DA59502, rendered on May 12, 1995, and Supreme Court Decision 97DA5749, rendered on July 22, 1997, all concern defenses based on the statute of limitations, or merely involve assertions that the conditions attached to a road occupancy permit received by the creditor from the debtor have not been performed; the factual situations are different, and they are not appropriate to invoke in this case.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the Plaintiff’s appeal against Defendant 5 is dismissed, and Defendant 5’s appeal and the Plaintiff’s appeal against Defendant 1, Defendant 2, Defendant 3, and Defendant 4 are all dismissed as without merit; the portion of the appellate costs incurred between the Plaintiff and Defendant 1, Defendant 2, Defendant 3, and Defendant 4 shall be borne by the Plaintiff, and the portion incurred between the Plaintiff and Defendant 5 shall be borne by each party individually. Accordingly, the judgment is rendered in accordance with the order, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court participating in the decision."}

{"[2015DA236547]": "The grounds for appeal are determined (the statements in the supplementary brief on the grounds for appeal submitted after the expiration of the period for filing the appellate brief shall be considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for appeal).\\n\\n1. a. Where a creditor, in order to preserve its monetary claim, exercises by subrogation a monetary claim of the debtor, the creditor may demand that the third-party obligor perform the payment obligation to the debtor, but may also demand that it be performed directly to the subrogating creditor himself (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DA70024 rendered on 2005. 4. 15.).\\n\\nHowever, even if in a creditor’s subrogation action a judgment ordering the third-party obligor to pay money directly to the subrogating creditor becomes final and conclusive, the right that is the object of subrogation, namely the subrogated claim of the debtor against the third-party obligor, exists as the claim to be executed under that judgment, and the subrogating creditor merely receives payment with respect to the subrogated claim by subrogating the debtor, not as payment of his own claim (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2013DA30301, 30325 rendered on 2015. 7. 23.), so long as the subrogated claim has not been extinguished by payment or otherwise, another creditor of the debtor may attach or provisionally attach it.\\n\\nHowever, once a creditor’s subrogation action has been filed and the subrogating creditor has notified the debtor of the exercise of the subrogation right or the debtor has otherwise become aware thereof, under Article 405(2) of the Civil Act the debtor becomes unable to engage in any dispositive act that would obstruct the creditor’s exercise of the subrogation right, such as assigning or waiving the subrogated claim, and such effect also extends to the third-party obligor. Nevertheless, if it were possible for another creditor of the debtor, who has a position equal to that of the subrogating creditor, to obtain an assignment order against the subrogated claim thereafter, then although the filing of a creditor’s subrogation action is one of the lawful methods by which a creditor exercises rights, and although it has in common with a collection action the point that it seeks collection of a claim belonging to the debtor, it would be nothing more than an useless procedure; moreover, it would produce the result that a creditor who has obtained an assignment order would, excluding the subrogating creditor and without the subrogating creditor even having an opportunity to participate in the claim distribution procedure through attachment, provisional attachment, or a demand for distribution, obtain exclusive satisfaction, thereby contravening the purport of Article 405(2) of the Civil Act, which seeks to secure the practical effect of the creditor’s subrogation right.\\n\\nAccordingly, once a creditor’s subrogation action has been filed and the subrogating creditor has notified the debtor of the exercise of the subrogation right or the debtor has become aware thereof, Article 229(5) of the Civil Execution Act shall apply by analogy, and an assignment order concerning the subrogated claim shall be deemed void, unless there are special circumstances such as that it is based on a claim with priority.\\n\\nb. A subrogating creditor who, in order to preserve his own monetary claim, exercises by subrogation the debtor’s monetary claim may demand that the third-party obligor directly perform the payment obligation to the subrogating creditor himself and may also receive such performance from the third-party obligor; however, since this does not cause the subrogated claim of the debtor against the third-party obligor to be transferred to or vested in the subrogating creditor, the subrogating creditor’s above-mentioned power to collect or power to receive performance against the third-party obligor is, in itself, not independently disposable and convertible into cash and is therefore of a nature not subject to attachment; accordingly, an order of attachment, etc. against such power to collect or power to receive performance is void. Further, even if in a creditor’s subrogation action a judgment ordering the third-party obligor to pay money directly to the subrogating creditor becomes final and conclusive, receiving money on the basis of that judgment also falls within the subrogating creditor’s power to collect or power to receive performance against the third-party obligor, and therefore an order of attachment, etc. against the claim to be received by the subrogating creditor from the third-party obligor pursuant to the judgment finalized in the creditor’s subrogation action must likewise be deemed void (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 96DA54300 rendered on 1997. 3. 14.).\\n\\n2. According to the reasons of the judgment of the first instance cited by the appellate court, the following facts may be ascertained.\\n\\na. Non-party 2, who holds a monetary claim against Non-party 1, filed an action against Plaintiff, exercising subrogation over Non-party 1, seeking return of unjust enrichment, and in that action, on 2012. 10. 24., a judgment was rendered stating, “Plaintiff shall pay Non-party 2 KRW 221,999,653 and an amount calculated at the rate of 20% per annum from 2012. 5. 9. until the date of full payment” (hereinafter referred to as “the Judgment in this Case”), and the Judgment in this Case became final and conclusive on 2013. 8. 13. Non-party 1 appeared and testified as a witness before the court of first instance in the above lawsuit.\\n\\nb. Based on an authenticated copy of an enforceable notarized deed against Non-party 1, Non-party 3 obtained, on 2013. 8. 12., an order of attachment of claim and assignment order against KRW 230,000,000 out of the above claim for return of unjust enrichment of Non-party 1 against Plaintiff, and the above order was served on Plaintiff on 2013. 8. 14. and became final and conclusive on 2013. 9. 6.\\n\\nc. Based again on another authenticated copy of an enforceable notarized deed against Non-party 1, Non-party 3 obtained, on 2013. 8. 20., an order of attachment of claim and assignment order against KRW 250,000,000 out of the above claim for return of unjust enrichment of Non-party 1 against Plaintiff, and the above order was served on Plaintiff on 2013. 8. 22. and became final and conclusive on 2013. 9. 6.\\n\\nd. Meanwhile, based on an authenticated copy of an enforceable payment order against Non-party 2, Defendant obtained, on 2013. 10. 11., an order of attachment of claim and assignment order (hereinafter referred to as “the Attachment and Assignment Order in this Case”) against KRW 220,000,000 out of the claim that Non-party 2 is to receive from Plaintiff pursuant to the Judgment in this Case, and the Attachment and Assignment Order in this Case was served on Plaintiff on 2013. 10. 16. and became final and conclusive on 2014. 4. 3.\\n\\n3. Examining these facts in light of the legal principles set forth above, first, because Non-party 1 appeared and testified as a witness before the court of first instance in the creditor’s subrogation action filed by Non-party 2, it must be deemed that Non-party 1 became aware of the fact that Non-party 2 exercised the subrogation right; thus, at that time, pursuant to Article 405(2) of the Civil Act, the effect of restricting the power of disposition over the debtor, Non-party 1, arose, and accordingly all of the above assignment orders obtained thereafter by Non-party 3, who has a position equal to that of Non-party 2, against the above claim for return of unjust enrichment of Non-party 1 against Plaintiff, which is the subrogated claim, are void.\\n\\nHowever, irrespective of this, because receiving money from Plaintiff pursuant to the Judgment in this Case falls within the subrogating creditor’s power to collect or power to receive performance against the third-party obligor, the Attachment and Assignment Order in this Case, which treated as the attached claim the claim that Non-party 2 is to receive from Plaintiff pursuant to the Judgment in this Case, is void; if so, Plaintiff’s obligation to Defendant based on the Attachment and Assignment Order in this Case does not exist.\\n\\nNevertheless, the appellate court held otherwise, finding that because all of the above assignment orders obtained by Non-party 3 were valid, the entirety of Non-party 1’s claim for return of unjust enrichment against Plaintiff and the claim for delay damages thereon from 2013. 8. 15. (the day after the first assignment order obtained by Non-party 3 was served on Plaintiff) had been transferred to Non-party 3, and that the Attachment and Assignment Order in this Case was also valid with respect to the portion not transferred to Non-party 3 as stated above, and accordingly the claim for delay damages up to 2013. 8. 14. had been transferred to Defendant, and on that basis determined that such claim for delay damages exists as Plaintiff’s obligation to Defendant under the Attachment and Assignment Order in this Case. In such determination by the appellate court, there is an error of law in misconstruing the effect of an assignment order concerning a subrogated claim or the effect of an order of attachment, etc. concerning the subrogating creditor’s power to collect or power to receive performance. However, in this case, in which only Defendant filed an appeal, the principle prohibiting disadvantageous modification prevents this Court from setting aside the appellate judgment and rendering a judgment more unfavorable to Defendant, and therefore the above error by the appellate court does not affect the result of the judgment.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2015DA236547]": "The grounds for final appeal are considered (the statements in the supplemental brief of grounds for final appeal submitted after the period for filing the statement of grounds for final appeal has elapsed are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for final appeal).\\n\\n1. a. Where a creditor, in order to preserve its own monetary claim, exercises by subrogation the debtor’s monetary claim, the creditor may demand that the third-party debtor perform the payment obligation to the debtor, but may also demand that performance be made directly to the subrogating creditor (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2005. 4. 15., 2004DA70024).\\n\\nHowever, even if a judgment becomes final and conclusive in a creditor’s subrogation action ordering the third-party debtor to pay money directly to the subrogating creditor, the right that is the object of subrogation, namely the debtor’s subrogated claim against the third-party debtor, remains in existence as the enforceable claim under that judgment, and the subrogating creditor merely receives performance of the subrogated claim on behalf of the debtor, not as performance of its own claim (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2015. 7. 23., 2013DA30301, 30325), so if the subrogated claim has not yet been extinguished by performance, etc., another creditor of the debtor may attach or provisionally attach it.\\n\\nHowever, once a creditor’s subrogation action has been filed and the subrogating creditor notifies the debtor of the fact that the subrogation right has been exercised, or the debtor becomes aware thereof, under Article 405(2) of the Civil Act the debtor may no longer engage in acts of disposition that would obstruct the creditor’s exercise of the subrogation right, such as assigning or waiving the subrogated claim, and this effect likewise extends to the third-party debtor. Nevertheless, if it were possible that another creditor of the debtor, who thereafter stands in an equal position with the subrogating creditor, could obtain an assignment order with respect to the subrogated claim, then although the filing of a creditor’s subrogation action is one of the lawful methods for a creditor to exercise its rights and has in common with a collection action the fact that it collects a claim belonging to the debtor, it would be reduced to nothing more than a futile procedure; moreover, the creditor who obtained the assignment order would, without even giving the subrogating creditor an opportunity to participate in the claim distribution proceedings through attachment, provisional attachment, or a demand for distribution, exclude the subrogating creditor and obtain exclusive satisfaction, thereby contravening the purpose of Article 405(2) of the Civil Act, which is to secure the substantive effect of the creditor’s subrogation right.\\n\\nAccordingly, once a creditor’s subrogation action has been filed and the subrogating creditor notifies the debtor of the fact that the subrogation right has been exercised, or the debtor becomes aware thereof, it is proper to regard, by analogy, Article 229(5) of the Civil Execution Act as applicable, and to deem an assignment order concerning the subrogated claim invalid, unless there are special circumstances, such as that it is based on a preferential claim.\\n\\nb. A subrogating creditor who, in order to preserve its own monetary claim, exercises by subrogation the debtor’s monetary claim may demand that the third-party debtor perform the payment obligation directly to the subrogating creditor itself and may receive performance from the third-party debtor, but since this does not cause the debtor’s subrogated claim against the third-party debtor to be transferred to or vested in the subrogating creditor, the subrogating creditor’s above-mentioned power to collect from, or power to receive performance from, the third-party debtor is not something that can, by itself, be independently disposed of and monetized, and thus is of a nature not subject to attachment; accordingly, an order of attachment, etc. with respect to such power to collect or power to receive performance is invalid. And even if a judgment in a creditor’s subrogation action ordering the third-party debtor to pay money directly to the subrogating creditor becomes final and conclusive, the receipt of money on the basis of that judgment also falls within the subrogating creditor’s power to collect from, or power to receive performance from, the third-party debtor; therefore, an order of attachment, etc. against the claim that the subrogating creditor is to receive from the third-party debtor pursuant to the final and conclusive judgment in the creditor’s subrogation action is likewise invalid (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision rendered on 1997. 3. 14., 96DA54300).\\n\\n2. According to the reasons for the first-instance judgment cited by the court below, the following facts may be ascertained.\\n\\na. Non-party 2, who held a monetary claim against Non-party 1, filed an action against the Plaintiff seeking restitution of unjust enrichment by subrogating Non-party 1, and in that action a judgment dated 2012. 10. 24. was rendered stating, “The Plaintiff shall pay Non-party 2 221,999,653 won and the amount calculated thereon at the rate of 20% per annum from 2012. 5. 9. until the date of full payment” (hereinafter referred to as the “instant judgment”), and the instant judgment became final and conclusive on 2013. 8. 13. Non-party 1 appeared as a witness and testified in the court of first instance of the above action.\\n\\nb. Based on an authenticated copy of an enforceable notarized deed against Non-party 1, Non-party 3 obtained, on 2013. 8. 12., an order of attachment and assignment in respect of 230,000,000 won of Non-party 1’s claim against the Plaintiff for restitution of unjust enrichment, and the above order was served on the Plaintiff on 2013. 8. 14. and became final and conclusive on 2013. 9. 6.\\n\\nc. Again based on another authenticated copy of an enforceable notarized deed against Non-party 1, Non-party 3 obtained, on 2013. 8. 20., an order of attachment and assignment in respect of 250,000,000 won of Non-party 1’s claim against the Plaintiff for restitution of unjust enrichment, and the above order was served on the Plaintiff on 2013. 8. 22. and became final and conclusive on 2013. 9. 6.\\n\\nd. Meanwhile, based on an authenticated copy of an enforceable payment order against Non-party 2, the Defendant obtained, on 2013. 10. 11., an order of attachment and assignment (hereinafter referred to as the “instant attachment and assignment order”) in respect of 220,000,000 won of the claim that Non-party 2 is to receive from the Plaintiff pursuant to the instant judgment, and the instant attachment and assignment order was served on the Plaintiff on 2013. 10. 16. and became final and conclusive on 2014. 4. 3.\\n\\n3. Examining these factual circumstances in light of the legal principles stated above, first, since Non-party 1 appeared as a witness and testified in the court of first instance in the above creditor’s subrogation action filed by Non-party 2, it should be deemed that Non-party 1 became aware of the fact that Non-party 2 exercised the subrogation right; accordingly, at that time, under Article 405(2) of the Civil Act, the effect of restricting the power of disposition over the debtor Non-party 1 arose, and therefore each of the above assignment orders obtained thereafter by Non-party 3, who stands in an equal position with Non-party 2, with respect to the above claim for restitution of unjust enrichment by Non-party 1 against the Plaintiff, which is the subrogated claim, is all invalid.\\n\\nHowever, regardless of that, since receiving money from the Plaintiff by Non-party 2 pursuant to the instant judgment falls within the subrogating creditor’s power to collect from, or power to receive performance from, the third-party debtor, the instant attachment and assignment order, which designated as the attached claim the claim that Non-party 2 is to receive from the Plaintiff pursuant to the instant judgment, is invalid; if so, the Plaintiff’s debt to the Defendant based on the instant attachment and assignment order would not exist.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, reaching a different conclusion, held that because each of the above assignment orders obtained by Non-party 3 is valid, the entirety of Non-party 1’s claim against the Plaintiff for restitution of unjust enrichment and the claim for delay damages thereon from 2013. 8. 15. (the day after the first assignment order obtained by Non-party 3 was served on the Plaintiff) had been transferred to Non-party 3; meanwhile, the instant attachment and assignment order is also valid with respect to the portion that had not been transferred to Non-party 3 as described above, and accordingly the claim for delay damages up to 2013. 8. 14. had been transferred to the Defendant, and thus determined that this portion of the delay damages exists as the Plaintiff’s debt to the Defendant based on the instant attachment and assignment order. In so holding, the court below erred by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the effect of an assignment order on a subrogated claim and the effect of an order of attachment, etc. on the subrogating creditor’s power to collect or receive performance. However, in the present case, in which only the Defendant appealed, the principle prohibiting a change for the worse prevents the judgment of the court below from being quashed and a more unfavorable judgment from being rendered against the Defendant; therefore, the court below’s above error does not affect the result of the judgment.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the final appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the final appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question: A granted a jeonse right over building X, which A owns, in favor of B. Which of the following statements are incorrect? (Each item is independent, and in case of dispute, according to case law.) (a) After B granted a mortgage over the jeonse right for the benefit of B’s creditor C, if A lent money to B without fixing a maturity date, and if, after the expiration of the term of the jeonse right, C attached B’s claim for return of the jeonse deposit by way of real subrogation, A may assert setoff of the loan claim against the claim for return of the jeonse deposit against C. (b) If B granted a mortgage over the jeonse right for the benefit of B’s creditor C, and after the expiration of the term of the jeonse right, B’s general creditor D provisionally attached the claim for return of the jeonse deposit, and then C obtained an attachment and an order of transfer over B’s claim for return of the jeonse deposit by way of real subrogation, C cannot demand payment of the jeonse deposit from A. (c) B’s jeonse right was established for the purpose of securing a claim for return of a lease deposit under a lease agreement. If B granted a mortgage over the jeonse right for the benefit of B’s creditor C, knowing this circumstance, A may assert against C, who exercises the right of real subrogation, a defense of deduction of overdue rent under the lease agreement. (d) After the term had expired, if B assigned the claim for return of the jeonse deposit together with the jeonse right and made supplementary registration in the name of the transferee E, the priority between E and the creditor who attached the claim for return of the jeonse deposit and obtained an order of transfer is determined according to whether the time of the supplementary registration precedes or follows the time of attachment.
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2003DA35659]": "All appeals are dismissed. The costs of appeal shall be borne by the Defendants."}

{"[2013DA91672]": "The grounds for appeal on points of law are examined (the statements in the supplementary brief on the grounds for appeal on points of law filed after the expiration of the period for submitting the petition of appeal on points of law are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for appeal on points of law).\\n\\n1. Where a mortgage is created with a jeonse right as its object, upon expiration of the term of the jeonse right, the usufructuary power of the jeonse right as a real right in use and benefit is extinguished, so the mortgage can no longer be enforced against the jeonse right itself, and the mortgagee must, by exercising the right of subrogation in rem by such means as obtaining an attachment and collection order or an assignment order with respect to the claim for return of the jeonse deposit, which may be regarded as surviving in place of the jeonse right, the object of the mortgage, or by filing a demand for distribution in compulsory execution proceedings carried out by a third party against the claim for return of the jeonse deposit, seek payment of the jeonse deposit (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DA31301, delivered on September 17, 1999).\\nWhere the mortgagee of a jeonse right has exercised the right of subrogation in rem over the claim for return of the jeonse deposit by the above method, the effect of the former mortgage survives in the claim for return of the jeonse deposit that became the object of subrogation in rem, and the mortgagee has the right to receive preferential satisfaction from that claim for return of the jeonse deposit ahead of other general creditors; thus, even if, at the time the claim for return of the jeonse deposit was attached, the grantor of the jeonse right held a counterclaim against the holder of the jeonse right and that counterclaim and the claim for return of the jeonse deposit were ripe for setoff, such circumstance alone does not allow the grantor of the jeonse right to oppose the mortgagee of the jeonse right by setoff.\\nHowever, because the claim for return of the jeonse deposit can be regarded as having been already scheduled to arise from the time the jeonse right was created, if, at the time the mortgage over the jeonse right was created, the grantor of the jeonse right already held a counterclaim against the holder of the jeonse right and the due date of that counterclaim arrives at the same time as, or earlier than, the due date of the claim for return of the jeonse deposit that will arise in the future, then, where the grantor of the jeonse right can be recognized as having a reasonable expectation interest, absent special circumstances, the grantor of the jeonse right may oppose the mortgagee of the jeonse right by setting off the claim for return of the jeonse deposit using that counterclaim as the active claim.\\n2. According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the record: ① the non-party, while leasing the building at issue from the Defendant, for the purpose of securing the claim for return of the lease deposit under the lease agreement, completed on May 25, 2005, registration establishing a jeonse right over the building at issue with a jeonse deposit of 60,000,000 won and a term from April 30, 2004, to April 29, 2009, and, after renewing the lease agreement, completed on September 13, 2010, registration of alteration of the jeonse right changing the jeonse deposit to 100,000,000 won and the term to from May 1, 2009, to April 29, 2014; ② the Plaintiff, on September 14, 2010, lent 150,000,000 won to the non-party and, as security therefor, received an assignment of the above claim for return of the lease deposit, and on September 20, 2010, completed registration establishing a mortgage over the jeonse right with a maximum secured amount of 100,000,000 won; ③ the non-party agreed with the Defendant on June 15, 2011, to terminate the lease agreement and delivered the building at issue to the Defendant; ④ thereafter, the Plaintiff filed this action and sought return of the lease deposit, and in response the Defendant, alleging that it had lent to the non-party 50,000,000 won on April 9, 2010, and 20,000,000 won on August 31, 2010, for a total of 70,000,000 won, raised a setoff defense at the sixth oral argument date of the first instance, on July 6, 2012, by using the above loan claim as the active claim; ⑤ on July 5, 2012, the Plaintiff obtained, with respect to 80,391,051 won of the non-party’s claim for return of the jeonse deposit against the Defendant, an attachment and collection order based on subrogation in rem, under Daegu District Court No. 2012TACHAE8931, and the above decision was served on the Defendant on July 9, 2012; ⑥ the Plaintiff, at the seventh oral argument date of the first instance on August 17, 2012, changed the above claim for return of the jeonse deposit into the principal claim and the above claim for return of the lease deposit into an alternative claim, and at the tenth oral argument date of the first instance on October 17, 2012, withdrew the alternative claim, but the Defendant continued to maintain the setoff defense.\\nBased on the above factual findings, the court below, with respect to the Defendant’s setoff defense, determined that the jeonse right at issue was created to secure the claim for return of the lease deposit arising under the lease agreement, and that the lease deposit secures only the lessor’s claim that arises as a matter of course under the lease agreement; therefore, the Defendant, as grantor of the jeonse right, could not oppose the Plaintiff, who exercises the right of subrogation in rem over the claim for return of the jeonse deposit with the loan claim against the non-party, the lessee, by way of setoff or otherwise.\\n3. However, the above determination of the court below cannot be upheld as it stands.\\nIn light of the above factual findings and the legal principles stated above, if, at the time the mortgage over the jeonse right at issue was created, the Defendant’s loan claim against the non-party existed and the due date of that claim arrived at the same time as, or earlier than, the due date of the claim for return of the jeonse deposit that will arise in the future, then, absent special circumstances, the Defendant may be said to be able to oppose the Plaintiff, the mortgagee, by setting off the claim for return of the jeonse deposit using the above loan claim as the active claim.\\nTherefore, the court below should have examined the existence or absence of the loan claim asserted by the Defendant and the chronological relationship between the due date of that loan claim and the due date of the claim for return of the jeonse deposit, and then determined whether setoff was permissible; yet, by rejecting the Defendant’s setoff defense solely for the reasons stated in its holding, the above determination of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law on subrogation in rem and setoff and by failing to conduct the necessary examination. The ground for appeal pointing out this issue is well founded.\\nThe Supreme Court Decision 2006DA29372, 29389, delivered on March 13, 2008, cited by the court below, held, in a case where the mortgagee did not know that a jeonse right had been created for the purpose of securing a claim for return of the lease deposit, that claims arising from the lease agreement such as overdue rent, maintenance fees, and damages could not be set off against the claim for return of the jeonse deposit by using them as the active claim; since the present case differs in its facts, it is not appropriate to invoke that decision.\\n4. Therefore, without examining the remaining grounds for appeal, the portion of the judgment of the court below that was adverse to the Defendant is reversed, and this case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the decision."}
{"[98DA12812]": "The judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the Busan High Court."}

question: A lent B 100,000,000 won to B on 2015. 2. 1., setting the due date as 2016. 1. 31., but B, without having repaid the loan at all, sold X land, his only asset, worth approximately 300,000,000 won, to C on 2021. 4. 1., and transferred title registration the following day. On 20232. 2. 21., A filed a lawsuit against C with the following prayer for relief, and the court of first instance rendered a judgment in the operative part below. [Prayer for Relief] 1. The sales contract concluded on 2021. 4. 1. between Defendant and B concerning X land is revoked. 2. Defendant shall comply with the procedure for cancellation registration of the ownership transfer registration completed with Receipt No. 1234, received at the Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court on 2021. 4. 2., concerning the land described in paragraph 1, in favor of B. 3. Litigation costs shall be borne by Defendant. 4. Paragraph 2 may be provisionally executed. [Operative Part] 1. The sales contract concluded on 2021. 4. 1. between Defendant and B concerning X land is revoked within the limit of 100,000,000 won. 2. Defendant shall pay 100,000,000 won to Plaintiff. 3. The remainder of Plaintiff's claim is dismissed. 4. Litigation costs shall be borne by Defendant. 5. Paragraph 2 may be provisionally executed. Which of the following statements are all correct? (Assume that there was no change in the market value of X land, and interest and delay damages are not considered. Each statement is independent, and if there is any dispute, the precedents shall apply.)
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2000DA66416]": "1. The court below’s determination that, although Non-party 1 owed the Plaintiff KRW 30,000,000 as construction price debt and had no other property apart from the real property at issue, he donated the real property at issue to his wife, Defendant 1, and thereby completed the registration of transfer of ownership in her name on 1996. 4. 19., and that, although Defendant 1 established, on 1997. 10. 1., a mortgage over the real property at issue with Defendant 2 as mortgagee, Non-party 1 as debtor, and a maximum secured claim amount of KRW 400,000,000, despite the fact that Defendant 2, who is the brother-in-law of Non-party 1, had no claim against Non-party 1, both Non-party 1’s act of donation of the real property at issue to Defendant 1 and Defendant 1’s act of establishing the mortgage in favor of Defendant 2 constituted fraudulent conveyances, is correct, and there is no error such as a violation of the rules of evidence or incomplete deliberation, as alleged in the grounds of appeal. Accordingly, all of the Defendants’ grounds of appeal on this point are without merit.\\n\\n2. Where an act of donating real property on which a mortgage has been created constitutes a fraudulent conveyance, if the registration of establishment of the mortgage is cancelled after the real property has been donated, it would be inequitable to rescind the gift contract and restore title to the real property itself to the debtor, because that would result in restoring even the portion that was not originally provided as common security for general creditors; therefore, the creditor has no choice but to seek partial rescission of the gift contract and compensation for value within the limit of the balance obtained by deducting the secured debt amount of the mortgage from the value of the real property (see Supreme Court Decisions 98DA41490 decided on 1999. 9. 7., 99DA50101 decided on 1999. 11. 9., etc.). In addition, since the creditor’s assertion seeking to rescind the fraudulent conveyance in its entirety and obtain restoration to the original condition also includes the purport of partially rescinding the fraudulent conveyance and seeking compensation for value, even where the creditor seeks only restoration to the original condition, the court may order compensation for value.\\n\\nThe court below, after finding that on 1996. 8. 16., after Non-party 1 had donated the real property at issue to Defendant 1, it was established that all of the registration of establishment of each mortgage already created on the real property at issue, namely, the mortgages with Non-party 1 as debtor, Non-party 2 as mortgagee, and maximum secured claim amounts of KRW 220,000,000 and KRW 120,000,000, had been cancelled, and then, in accordance with the above legal principle, ordering the Defendants to pay compensation for value was correct, and there is no error such as misapprehension of the law concerning the creditor’s avoidance right or the principle of disposition, as alleged in the grounds of appeal. Accordingly, the Plaintiff’s and the Defendants’ grounds of appeal on this point are also without merit.\\n\\n3. a. Where, after a fraudulent conveyance has been effected with respect to real property on which a mortgage has been created, the mortgage is cancelled and the fraudulent conveyance is rescinded and compensation for value is ordered within the limit of the remaining amount after deducting the secured debt amount of the mortgage from the value of the real property, the calculation of that value must be based on the time of conclusion of oral argument in the fact-finding instance (see Supreme Court Decisions 97DA6711 decided on 1998. 2. 13., 98DA41490 decided on 1999. 9. 7., etc.), and even against a subsequent transferee who acquired rights in the real property through the fraudulent conveyance after the existing mortgage was cancelled, compensation for value may be ordered for the benefit acquired by him within the limit of the amount obtained by deducting the secured debt amount of the cancelled mortgage from the value of the real property at the time of conclusion of oral argument in the fact-finding instance. Meanwhile, when a creditor exercises the creditor’s avoidance right, as a matter of principle he cannot exercise the avoidance right in excess of the amount of his own claim (see Supreme Court Decision 97DA10864 decided on 1997. 9. 9.), and in this context the amount of the creditor’s claim includes interest or delay damages accrued from after the fraudulent conveyance until the conclusion of oral argument in the fact-finding instance.\\n\\n   b. The court below held that the Plaintiff could, within the limit of KRW 120,000,000 remaining after deducting the secured debt amount of KRW 340,000,000 of the mortgage cancelled after the fraudulent conveyance from the value of the real property at the time of conclusion of oral argument, namely KRW 460,000,000, rescind the gift contract between Non-party 1 and Defendant 1 and seek compensation for that amount from Defendant 1; and that, within the limit of KRW 60,000,000 remaining after deducting the secured debt amount of the mortgage cancelled as above from the maximum secured claim amount of KRW 400,000,000 of the mortgage acquired by Defendant 2, the Plaintiff could rescind the mortgage creation contract between the Defendants and seek compensation for that amount from Defendant 2, and accordingly found that the Plaintiff was entitled to payment of KRW 60,000,000 each from the Defendants and KRW 60,000,000 from Defendant 1.\\n\\n   c. However, in this case, in the construction price claim lawsuit filed by the Plaintiff against Non-party 1, on 1997. 5. 22. judgment was rendered and became final and conclusive to the effect that “Non-party 1 shall pay the Plaintiff KRW 30,000,000 and money calculated at the rate of 25 percent per annum thereon from 1996. 6. 25. until full payment,” and therefore the Plaintiff may exercise the creditor’s avoidance right within the limit of KRW 61,516,393, consisting of KRW 30,000,000 and KRW 31,516,393, the amount calculated thereon at the rate of 25 percent per annum from 1996. 6. 25. to 2000. 9. 6., the date of conclusion of oral argument in the court below.\\n\\n   Accordingly, the court below erred by, in excess of the Plaintiff’s above claim amount, rescinding the fraudulent conveyance against Defendant 1 and ordering compensation of KRW 120,000,000, thereby misapprehending the law concerning the scope of the creditor’s avoidance right and affecting the judgment, and Defendant 1’s ground of appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n   Meanwhile, Defendant 2, by acquiring the mortgage after all previously established mortgages had been cancelled, obtained a benefit equivalent to the secured debt amount of KRW 400,000,000, and because the amount obtained by deducting the secured debt amount of the cancelled mortgage from the value of the real property at the time of conclusion of oral argument in the court below also exceeds the Plaintiff’s claim amount, the Plaintiff may exercise the creditor’s avoidance right for the entirety of that claim amount and seek compensation for value. Nevertheless, the court below’s determination that the Plaintiff could exercise the creditor’s avoidance right against Defendant 2 only within the limit of KRW 60,000,000 was an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law concerning the creditor’s avoidance right, and the Plaintiff’s ground of appeal pointing this out is also well-founded.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below, and the Plaintiff’s appeal against Defendant 1 and Defendant 2’s appeal are both dismissed, and judgment is rendered as ordered."}

{"[2017MA499]": "We examine the grounds for the re-appeal.\\n\\n1. According to the record, the following facts may be found.\\n\\nThe non-party, as creditor, brought an action against the Re-Appellant seeking damages and obtained a judgment partly in his favor (Seoul Central District Court Judgment dated June 27, 2014, Case Nos. 2013GAHAP6846, 30061). Thereafter, based on the executory judgment in the above case, the non-party applied in the Incheon District Court, under Case No. 2016TACHAE7594HO, for an order of seizure and assignment with respect to the amount up to KRW 176,606,000, which was the amount claimed, out of the beneficiary's claim for value compensation in the amount of KRW 211,927,530 that the Re-Appellant held against the non-party by reason of the revocation of a fraudulent act (Seoul High Court Judgment dated March 17, 2016, Case No. 2014NA13404; Supreme Court Judgment dated July 7, 2016, Case No. 2016DA17323), and on June 30, 2016, an order of seizure and assignment was issued.\\n\\nThe Re-Appellant appealed against the above order of seizure and assignment on the ground that the law was misconstrued and that it was contrary to the principle of good faith, but the court below dismissed it.\\n\\n2. Where, in an action for revocation of a fraudulent act, the beneficiary, as restitution, makes value compensation to the creditor exercising the creditor's right of revocation, the beneficiary may not, on the ground that he himself is a creditor of the debtor in the action for revocation of a fraudulent act, set off his own claim against the debtor or, by asserting that he paid money to the debtor under the name of value-compensation money, demand that this be deducted from the value compensation payable to the creditor exercising the creditor's right of revocation (see Supreme Court Judgment dated June 1, 2001, 99DA63183). However, for the purpose of enforcing a separate and different claim that the beneficiary has against the creditor exercising the creditor's right of revocation, it is permissible to obtain a title of execution therefor and to seize the creditor's claim for value compensation against the beneficiary and obtain an assignment order. This differs in content and nature from setoff or voluntary deduction based on the beneficiary's claim against the debtor. Also, when a creditor seizes a claim of the debtor against a third-party debtor, seizure is not prohibited even if the third-party debtor is the creditor himself; therefore, it cannot be deemed unlawful that an order of seizure and assignment was issued merely because the creditor and the third-party debtor are the same person.\\n\\nFurthermore, even a claim with respect to which setoff is prohibited may be subject to an assignment order by compulsory execution so long as it does not constitute a claim against which seizure is prohibited (see Supreme Court Decision dated March 16, 1994, 93MA1822, 1823).\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the decision of the court below in light of the foregoing legal principles, the decision of the court below is proper. There is no error in the decision of the court below in that it misapprehended the legal principles concerning the requirements for seizure of claims and an assignment order and thereby affected the judgment contrary to the principle of good faith.\\n\\n3. It is decided, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated, to dismiss the re-appeal in this case, as stated in the disposition."}

question: A entered into a pledge agreement with C, for the purpose of securing A’s monetary debt to C, with respect to A’s claim for return of the lease deposit against B, and notified B of this fact by an instrument bearing a certified date. Which of the following is the correct combination of the true statement (○) and the false statement (×)? (Each proposition is independent, and where there is controversy, according to precedents) (a) If A establishes a pledge in favor of C with respect to a lease deposit return claim secured by a mortgage, and the additional registration of the pledge does not separately state the claim’s delay damages, then this is not included in the scope of the secured claim under the mortgage-backed pledge. (b) Even if B, without C’s consent, set off a claim against A against the lease deposit return claim and thereby extinguished it, C may still directly demand performance of the debt from B. (c) If, with respect to A’s lease deposit return claim, an attachment and assignment order was issued upon the application of D, A’s general creditor, and if C had satisfied the opposability requirements by an instrument bearing a certified date before the day on which the order was served on B, then B may not oppose C on the ground that B paid D. (d) If, after A had granted a pledge to C, a mortgage was established on real property owned by B in order to secure A’s lease deposit return claim, unless C made an additional registration of the pledge in the registration of the above mortgage, the effect of the pledge does not extend to the mortgage.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2016DA235411]": "1. Regarding the Plaintiff's grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe court below determined that, although the Defendant had received a transfer of ownership of the building at issue, it was difficult to find that the Defendant had succeeded to the status of landlord under the lease agreement or had assumed the obligation to return the lease deposit. Accordingly, the court below dismissed the Plaintiff's claim seeking payment of the lease deposit against the Defendant as the pledgee of the claim for return of the lease deposit pursuant to Civil Act Article 353(1).\\n\\nUpon reviewing the record, there is no error in the court below's determination, in that it did not exceed the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, nor did it misunderstand the relevant legal principles.\\n\\n2. Regarding the Defendant's grounds for appeal\\n\\nA. Civil Act Article 361 merely provides that “a mortgage may not be transferred to another person separately from the claim it secures, nor may it be used as security for another claim.” It does not provide that the secured claim may not be transferred separately from the mortgage or used as security for another claim.
