Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, we reverse the judgment below and remand the case to the court below for further trial and determination, and so decide as per the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court who participated."}

{"[2021DA201054]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Relevant legal principles\\n\\nA. Bonds with stock acquisition rights are bonds granted with stock acquisition rights that entitle the holder to request subscription for a fixed number of new shares at a price fixed in advance. Even in the case of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights, because it affects the material basis of a stock company and the interests of existing shareholders, it is substantially similar to the issuance of shares, and thus Article 429 of the Commercial Act concerning an action for invalidation of the issuance of shares applies by analogy. The invalidity of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights may be asserted only by an action brought within 6 months from the date on which the bonds with stock acquisition rights were issued by shareholders, etc., and after the 6-month filing period has elapsed, no additional grounds of invalidity may be asserted (see Supreme Court Decision dated December 10, 2015, 2015DA202919, Supreme Court Decision dated June 25, 2004, 2000DA37326, etc.). Therefore, if no action for invalidation of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights is brought within 6 months from the date of issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights, or if an action for invalidation of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights brought within 6 months becomes final and conclusive in the defeat of the party actively asserting it, the invalidity of the issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights can no longer be asserted thereafter.\\n\\nB. 1) However, with respect to the exercise of the stock acquisition rights granted in bonds with stock acquisition rights, or the issuance of new shares resulting therefrom, Article 429 of the Commercial Act applies by analogy, and they may be challenged by an action for invalidation of the issuance of shares. In such a case, absent special circumstances, only grounds of invalidity inherent in the exercise of the stock acquisition rights or the issuance of new shares resulting therefrom may be asserted, and no assertion may be made that the issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights is invalid or on the premise thereof.\\n\\n2) Meanwhile, Article 418(1) and (2) of the Commercial Act protects shareholders’ right to subscribe for new shares by, in principle, requiring the allotment of new shares to existing shareholders when a company issues new shares, while allowing allotment of new shares to a third party only where provided in the articles of incorporation, and limiting the reasons therefor to cases necessary to achieve a business purpose, such as the introduction of new technology or the improvement of financial structure. Therefore, when a stock company issues new shares, if there are no grounds prescribed in the articles of incorporation within the scope necessary to achieve the company’s business purpose, but the company, in a situation where a dispute over management control has become real, allots new shares to a third party for the purpose of defending the management rights or control rights of a controlling shareholder or management, etc., this violates Article 418(2) of the Commercial Act and infringes the shareholders’ right to subscribe for new shares, and where, as a result, a serious change is caused in the company’s governance structure and a serious consequence occurs whereby the existing shareholders’ control over the company is markedly weakened, such issuance of new shares is void (see Supreme Court Decision dated January 30, 2009, 2008DA50776, Supreme Court Decision dated April 3, 2019, 2018DA289542, etc.). This principle applies equally in cases where bonds with stock acquisition rights are issued to a third party (see the second sentence of Article 516-2(4) of the Commercial Act, the proviso to Article 418(2), Supreme Court Decision dated December 10, 2015, 2015DA202919, etc.).\\n\\n3) In the case of bonds with stock acquisition rights, even if they are issued to a third party for the purpose of defending the management rights or control rights of a controlling shareholder, etc., without a business purpose, the issuance itself does not infringe the existing shareholders’ right to subscribe for new shares, and only when the controlling shareholder, etc. later acquires the new shares by exercising the stock acquisition rights acquired by transfer does the existing shareholders’ right to subscribe for new shares become infringed and the purpose of defending the management rights or control rights of the controlling shareholder, etc. become realized. According to this, if the company issued bonds with stock acquisition rights to a third party for the purpose of defending the management rights or control rights of a controlling shareholder, etc., the issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights may be void, and such grounds may be challenged by an action for invalidation of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights within 6 months from the date of issuance. Furthermore, if the controlling shareholder, etc. transfers the bonds with stock acquisition rights issued in such manner or the stock acquisition rights granted thereby, and thereafter exercises the stock acquisition rights after 6 months have elapsed from the date of issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights and acquires new shares, this is, in substance, the same as the company having issued new shares to the controlling shareholder, etc. without a business purpose; accordingly, the invalidity of the issuance of new shares may also be asserted by an action for invalidation of the issuance of shares, in accordance with grounds of invalidity inherent in the exercise of the stock acquisition rights or the issuance of new shares resulting therefrom.\\n\\nIn this way, the shareholders’ right to bring an action challenging an unlawful issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights or the issuance of new shares based thereon can be substantially protected.\\n\\n4) In the above case, the filing period for an action for invalidation of the issuance of new shares must be calculated from the date of issuance of the new shares, and even if the issuance of new shares resulted from the exercise of stock acquisition rights granted in bonds with stock acquisition rights, it is not to be calculated from the date of issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights.\\n\\n2. Determination in this case\\n\\nA. According to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be found.\\n\\n1) The Defendant’s articles of incorporation provide that, where necessary for urgent financing for business purposes, bonds with stock acquisition rights may be issued to financial institutions, etc. other than shareholders by resolution of the board of directors (Article 23(1)5).\\n\\n2) On June 30, 2016, the Defendant issued privately placed detachable bonds with stock acquisition rights (hereinafter referred to as “the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue”), and Partners No. 4 Growth Investment Association and Gudam Partners LLC each subscribed to the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue in the amounts of KRW 205.6 million and KRW 308.4 million, respectively. At that time, the Plaintiff held 131,449 shares of the Defendant (8.78%), and the non-party, who was the Defendant’s representative director, held 335,393 shares of the Defendant (22.39%).\\n\\n3) In or around September 2016, the non-party acquired by transfer part of the stock acquisition rights granted in the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue from Partners No. 4 Growth Investment Association and Gudam Partners LLC (hereinafter the stock acquisition rights acquired by the non-party are referred to as “the stock acquisition rights at issue”).\\n\\n4) When the non-party exercised the stock acquisition rights at issue on October 21, 2019, the Defendant issued 100,000 common shares with a par value of KRW 500 on the same day to the non-party (hereinafter referred to as “the new shares at issue”).\\n\\n5) No action for invalidation of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights has been brought within 6 months from the date of issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue.\\n\\n6) On November 19, 2019, the Plaintiff filed this action for invalidation of the issuance of new shares, alleging that the Defendant issued the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue for the purpose of strengthening the management rights or control rights of the non-party, who was the representative director, without the need for urgent financing for business purposes, and that the issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue and the issuance of new shares resulting from the non-party’s exercise of the stock acquisition rights at issue are void.\\n\\nB. The above factual relations are examined in light of the legal principles set forth above.\\n\\nThe filing period for this action for invalidation of the issuance of new shares at issue must be calculated from the date of issuance of the new shares at issue, and it is not the case that it must be calculated from the date of issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue merely because the Plaintiff’s allegations include grounds concerning the invalidity of the issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue.\\n\\nHowever, because this action for invalidation of the issuance of new shares at issue was brought on November 19, 2019, within 6 months from October 21, 2019, the date of issuance of the new shares at issue, it is clear that the filing period was complied with.\\n\\nTherefore, the court below should have examined whether the Defendant issued the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue for the purpose of helping to defend the management rights or control rights of the non-party and thereby, in substance, can be evaluated as having issued new shares to the non-party without a business purpose, and whether, as a result, a serious change was caused in the Defendant’s governance structure and a serious consequence occurred whereby the existing shareholder, the Plaintiff, was markedly weakened in its control over the company, and then determined whether the issuance of the new shares at issue was void.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below held that the action for invalidation of the issuance of new shares at issue was inadmissible on the ground that the Plaintiff asserted only grounds for invalidity of the issuance of bonds with stock acquisition rights, and calculated the filing period from the date of issuance of the bonds with stock acquisition rights at issue. In this respect, the court below erred by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the filing period for an action for invalidation of the issuance of shares.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment below is reversed without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so decided by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved, as stated in the operative part."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the court of jurisdiction for an action brought against B pursuant to the following agreement is incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law) <AGREEMENT> Creditor: A (750101-1234567) 125 Seocho-ro, Seocho-gu, Seoul, 305-dong 1301-ho (Seocho-dong, OO Apartment), Debtor: B (850201-2345678) 211 Baekjegobun-ro, Songpa-gu, Seoul, 203-dong 901-ho (Samjeon-dong, XX Apartment), A and B agree as follows. Terms of the agreement: 1. B shall pay 100,000,000 won to A by 2023. 10. 30. 2. B shall perform the registration procedure for transfer of ownership, on the ground of gift as of 2023. 10. 1., with respect to 300㎡ of land at 145 Ohyeon-ro, Gangbuk-gu, Seoul, to A by 2023. 10. 30. \n 2023. 10. 1. A ㊞ B ㊞
A: A may file an action seeking performance of both Item 1 and Item 2 of the agreement in the court having jurisdiction over B's place of residence.
B: A may file an action seeking performance of Item 1 only of the agreement in the court having jurisdiction over A's place of residence.
C: A may file an action seeking performance of Item 2 only of the agreement in the court having jurisdiction over A's place of residence.
D: If, after A and B lawfully enter into an agreement on jurisdiction, A lawfully assigns to C the claim for 100 million won that A has against B under Item 1 above, and C files an action seeking payment of the assigned claim, C is bound by the agreement on jurisdiction between A and B.
E: Even if A files an action seeking performance of Item 1 of the agreement in a court lacking jurisdiction, jurisdiction will arise in that court if B does not assert lack of jurisdiction and argues on the merits.
label: C

{"[2005MA902]": "We examine the grounds for re-appeal (the statement of supplemental grounds for re-appeal submitted after the expiration of the period for submitting the statement of grounds for re-appeal, to the extent that it supplements the grounds for re-appeal).\\n\\nAs a matter of principle, an agreement on jurisdiction, being a procedural act, does not affect third parties other than the parties to the agreement and their general successors; however, when viewed in substantive law terms, a change in jurisdiction by agreement of the parties concerning jurisdiction is a change in the substantive interest inseparably attached to the legal relationship as a condition for the exercise of rights. Therefore, in cases where the parties may freely determine the content of the legal relationship, such as a nominative claim, the specific successor to the relevant legal relationship is to be deemed to have succeeded to the legal relationship as so changed, and thus the effect of the jurisdiction agreement also extends to the specific successor.\\n\\nAccording to the record and the facts found by the court below, Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Kookmin Bank”) executed the loan at issue to the other party 1 from December 29, 1990 to March 21, 1997, and both parties approved the application of the Standard Terms and Conditions for Banking Credit Transactions; Article 21 of the said Standard Terms and Conditions for Banking Credit Transactions provides that “when the need for litigation arises between the bank and the debtor, guarantor, or property guarantor with respect to a credit transaction based on these terms and conditions, the district court having jurisdiction over the location of the bank’s transaction branch shall be the court of competent jurisdiction”; the transaction branch of Kookmin Bank in charge of the loan at issue was the Bucheon Branch located in Wonmi-gu, Bucheon-si; and Kookmin Bank assigned to the re-appellant the claim for the loan at issue against the other party and gave notice of such assignment on September 30, 1998. In light of the foregoing legal principle, in the instant case where Kookmin Bank and the other party 1, at the time of the loan at issue, agreed, by approving the application of Article 21 of the above Standard Terms and Conditions for Banking Credit Transactions, to designate as the court of first instance with jurisdiction the district court having jurisdiction over the location of Kookmin Bank’s transaction branch, with respect to the claim for the loan at issue, which falls under a nominative claim whose content may be freely determined by the parties, the substantive interest inseparably attached to the claim for the loan at issue as a condition for the exercise of rights was changed by the said jurisdiction agreement, and the re-appellant, as the specific successor to the claim for the loan at issue, is to be deemed to have succeeded to the legal relationship as so changed; therefore, the effect of the said jurisdiction agreement also extends to the re-appellant.\\n\\nIf so, the court below, on the ground that the effect of the above jurisdiction agreement between Kookmin Bank and the other party 1 does not extend to the re-appellant, who is merely an assignee of the claim for the loan at issue, determined that the court designated in the said jurisdiction agreement lacks jurisdiction over this action, and thereby erred by misapprehending the legal principle concerning the effect of a jurisdiction agreement, which affected the decision; accordingly, the grounds for re-appeal pointing out this point are well-founded.\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds for re-appeal, we reverse the decision of the court below and remand the case to the court below for further proceedings and a new determination, and it is so ordered by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question: Which of the following combinations correctly matches the statements concerning the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations by the filing of an action, with the true statements marked (○) and the false statements marked (×)? (In cases of dispute, according to case law) (a) After A assigned to C a claim for payment of the price of goods in the amount of KRW 50,000,000 against B, if A’s claim was dismissed in a lawsuit for payment of the price of goods filed against B before the requirements for opposability were satisfied, on the ground, inter alia, that B acknowledged the effect of the assignment of the claim, then if the assignee C filed an action for payment of the assigned amount against B within 6 months thereafter, the statute of limitations was interrupted at the time A filed the action. (b) Even if, in an action for a loan claim filed by plaintiff A against defendant B, A, not knowing that B had died, designated B as the defendant, and a judgment in favor of the claim that overlooked B’s death became final, if plaintiff A thereafter filed again an action for payment of the loan against B’s heir C within 6 months, the statute of limitations of the above loan claim was interrupted at the time plaintiff A filed the action against defendant B. (c) Where a plaintiff who transferred the right that is the subject matter of the action withdrew from the litigation with the defendant’s consent pursuant to the court’s decision on succession to the litigation, and thereafter the effect of the transfer of the right that is the subject matter of the action by the assuming intervenor was denied and a judgment dismissing the claim or dismissing the action against the assuming intervenor became final, if the withdrawn plaintiff again made the same judicial claim as before withdrawal within 6 months from the date of finality of the above judgment, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations caused by the judicial claim filed by the plaintiff before withdrawal remains intact. (d) Where, in the complaint, only part of the claim that was made the subject of the action was claimed and an intention to expand the amount claimed later depending on the progress of the litigation was indicated, but the amount claimed was not actually expanded until the conclusion of the relevant litigation, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations due to the judicial claim does not arise with respect to the remaining portion not claimed; however, unless there are special circumstances, the creditor may interrupt the statute of limitations for that remaining portion by making a judicial claim within 6 months from the time the relevant litigation ended.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2008DU20109]": "We decide the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. On Point 1\\nThe court below, synthesizing the evidence it adopted, determined that the Plaintiffs acquired from the owners stated in the column for “owner on the register” of each itemized table attached as Appendix 2 to the judgment of the court below (hereinafter referred to as the “former owners”), on each purchase date stated in the column for “purchase date” of the same itemized table, other rights including ownership in respect of each parcel of land at issue in this case.\\n\\nReviewing the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the record, the foregoing fact-finding and determination by the court below are well-founded and acceptable, and there is no error of law concerning the interpretation of the sales contract or any violation of law such as inadequacy of deliberation, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. On Point 2\\nBefore the requirements for opposability are satisfied after the assignment of a claim, the assignor remains in the position of a creditor vis-à-vis the debtor, and thus may bring a judicial claim against the debtor that has the effect of interrupting the statute of limitations. In such a case, even if the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations is extinguished under Article 170(1) of the Civil Act because the assignee’s claim is dismissed due to circumstances such as the debtor’s acknowledgment of the effect of the assignment of claim during the litigation brought by the assignor, the assignor’s claim does not thereby become a claim brought ab initio by a person without rights. Therefore, if the assignee brought a judicial claim, etc. against the debtor within 6 months thereafter, the statute of limitations is interrupted by the assignor’s initial judicial claim pursuant to Articles 169 and 170(2) of the Civil Act.\\n\\nAccording to the facts as finally determined by the court below and the record, the non-party who was the decedent of Plaintiffs 1 through 23, 26, and 27-1 through 3 filed suits against the Defendant seeking payment of compensation for loss on March 14 and December 22 of the same year, respectively, before December 31, 2003, when the period of extinctive prescription for the compensation claim for loss at issue in this case expired, on behalf of the former owners; then on April 7, 2006, they applied for intervention by succession in that litigation. In that litigation, the Seoul Administrative Court, on June 22, 2007, dismissed all applications for intervention by succession filed by the said Plaintiffs on the ground that, although they had acquired the claim before the filing of those suits, they did not satisfy the requirements for intervention by succession even if they satisfied the requirements for opposability after filing suit; and, with respect to the claims of the predecessors-in-interest of those Plaintiffs, dismissed all of them on the ground that they had assigned the compensation claim for loss to those Plaintiffs. It can be further understood that the said Plaintiffs did not appeal that judgment and, together with the remaining Plaintiffs in this case, filed the present action on August 14, 2007. Meanwhile, the record does not clearly reveal any materials from which it can be ascertained that the requirements for opposability as to the assignment of the said compensation claim for loss had been satisfied before each of those suits was filed, and it appears that this point was not clearly examined either.\\n\\nIn light of these circumstances and the legal principles stated above, there is room to view the former owners’ above-mentioned claims as claims brought before the requirements for opposability were satisfied after the assignment of claim. Therefore, even if the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations was extinguished because those claims were dismissed, there is room to view the statute of limitations as having been interrupted by the former owners’ filing of suit, since the said Plaintiffs, as successors to the former owners, filed this action within 6 months thereafter.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, on the sole ground that the said Plaintiffs had purchased rights in relation to the lands at issue in this case from the former owners before the former owners filed suit, without examining when the requirements for opposability regarding the assignment of the compensation claim for loss at issue in this case were satisfied, held that the said Plaintiffs do not qualify as successors who receive the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations arising from the former owners’ filing of suit, and thus rejected the said Plaintiffs’ defense in reply based on interruption of the statute of limitations. In so doing, the court below erred by misunderstanding the legal principles regarding the scope of successors under Article 169 of the Civil Act and Article 170 of the Civil Act, and by failing to exercise the right to clarification or to conduct the necessary deliberation, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n3. On Point 3\\nThe debtor’s exercise of the defense based on the completion of the statute of limitations is also governed by the principle of good faith and the principle prohibiting abuse of rights, which are the fundamental principles of our Civil Act. Therefore, where, before completion of the statute of limitations, the debtor made it impossible or markedly difficult for the creditor to exercise the claim or interrupt the statute of limitations, or behaved in a manner that led the creditor to believe that such measures were unnecessary, or there existed objectively an obstructive circumstance that prevented the creditor from exercising the right, or, once the statute of limitations had already completed, the debtor acted in a manner that made it appear that he or she would not invoke the statute of limitations, thereby causing the rights holder to rely on that belief, or where there are special circumstances such as a strong need to protect the creditor and circumstances such that another creditor under the same conditions has received performance of the debt, making it manifestly unjust or unfair to recognize the refusal of performance of the debt, the debtor’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations cannot be allowed as an abuse of rights contrary to the principle of good faith. However, merely because the State has a duty to protect the people, it cannot be said that the State’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations itself constitutes an abuse of rights contrary to the principle of good faith. Therefore, to say that the State’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations is contrary to good faith and constitutes an abuse of rights, the special circumstances stated above must be recognized; moreover, because applying such general principle to exclude operation of the specific system established by law poses a risk of undermining legal stability, which is another fundamental principle in statutory interpretation, its application must be approached with caution (see Supreme Court Decision 2004DA33469, decided May 29, 2008, etc.).\\n\\nThe court below, after recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion based on the evidence it adopted, held that there was no evidence to support a finding that the Defendant had engaged in any words or conduct making it impossible or markedly difficult for the Plaintiffs to exercise their right to claim compensation, or leading them to believe that such measures were unnecessary, and that there also did not appear, objectively, to have been any obstructive circumstance preventing the Plaintiffs from exercising their claim for damages or any significant circumstances under which the exercise of the right could not be expected. On that basis, it determined that the Defendant’s assertion of completion of the statute of limitations and refusal to perform the obligation to pay compensation could not be deemed a case of manifest injustice or unfairness.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles stated above and reviewing the record, the foregoing fact-finding and determination by the court below are well-founded and acceptable, and there is no illegality such as an error of law concerning whether the exercise of the defense of the statute of limitations is contrary to the principle of good faith, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n4. On Point 4\\nWhere part of a debt has been performed before the completion of the statute of limitations, such performance has the effect of acknowledging the debt, and the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations arises only when there is no dispute as to the amount thereof (see Supreme Court Decision 95DA39854, decided January 23, 1996).\\n\\nThe court below, after recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion based on the evidence it adopted, determined that, since the Defendant, who is obligated to provide compensation for loss, was in dispute as to the amount of such compensation and deposited the compensation amount according to the results of its own appraisal, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations or waiver of the benefit of the statute of limitations arises only within the amount deposited.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles stated above and reviewing the record, the foregoing fact-finding and determination by the court below are well-founded and acceptable, and there is no illegality such as an error of law concerning the scope of interruption of the statute of limitations or waiver of the benefit of the statute of limitations arising from partial performance, as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\nTherefore, among the judgment of the court below, the portion concerning Plaintiffs 1 through 23, 26, and 27-1 through 3 is reversed, and that portion of the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. The appeals of Plaintiffs 24, 25, and 28 through 32 are each dismissed, and the costs of appeal by those Plaintiffs shall be borne by the losing parties. It is so adjudged, by unanimous opinion of the judges participating."}

{"[2013DA94312]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to Ground 1 of the grounds for final appeal\\n\\nArticle 170, paragraph 1, of the Civil Act, premised on the fact that a judicial claim constitutes a ground for interruption of prescription under Article 168 of the Civil Act, provides that “a judicial claim shall have no effect of interrupting prescription in cases where the lawsuit is dismissed, rejected, or withdrawn,” and paragraph 2 of the same Article provides that “in the cases set forth in the preceding paragraph, if a judicial claim, participation in bankruptcy proceedings, attachment or provisional seizure, or provisional disposition is made within 6 months, prescription shall be deemed to have been interrupted by the first judicial claim,” thereby recognizing, where the first judicial claim contains a defect such as lack of procedural requirements for the lawsuit, the retroactive effect of interruption of prescription as of the time of the first filing if a new judicial claim, etc. is made within a certain period.\\n\\nHowever, a lawsuit filed against a person who had already died is unlawful, and a judgment rendered by overlooking this and proceeding to a determination on the merits is void ab initio, so its effect does not extend to the heirs (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision rendered on Apr. 26, 2002, 2000DA30578), and such filing by a creditor does not constitute the exercise of a right by a right-holder against an obligor; therefore, unless there are special circumstances such as a correction of the indication of the party designating the heirs as defendants, it is reasonable to regard that there was no effect of interrupting prescription from the outset and that Article 170, paragraph 2, of the Civil Act does not apply, and the same should be deemed true even where the court overlooks this and renders a judgment after proceeding to the merits.\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the judgment below, the court below recognized the following facts: Hanarum Second Asset Securitization Specialized Company, Ltd. filed, against Non-party 1, an action for loan claims seeking payment of the assigned claim amounts of each of the loan claims in this case under Busan District Court Case No. 2002GAHAP5203, and on June 26, 2002, received from the said court a judgment ordering payment of KRW 104,771,787 and delay damages on KRW 20,894,767 thereof (hereinafter referred to as the “related judgment”); the said judgment became final and conclusive on July 27, 2002; Hanarum Second Asset Securitization Specialized Company, Ltd. assigned the claim for the judgment amount under the said judgment to the Plaintiff on October 31, 2003 and notified Non-party 1 of the assignment of the said claim on November 27, 2003; the Plaintiff assigned part of the claim for the related judgment amount to another person; Non-party 1 died on October 18, 2008, and as heirs there were the Defendant, who was the spouse, and Non-party 2 and Non-party 3, who were lineal descendants, but the said Non-parties 2 and 3 obtained a decision on renunciation of inheritance of the deceased Non-party 1’s property on January 20, 2009, and the said decision became final and conclusive around that time. Then, the court below, on the ground that it was clear that the present action was filed on December 3, 2012, more than 10 years after the related judgment became final and conclusive on July 27, 2002, held that the remaining loan claim under the related judgment sought by the Plaintiff had been extinguished by prescription, and further rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that the statute of limitations was interrupted at the time the former action in this case was filed, by finding that the judgment in favor of the Plaintiff rendered on September 7, 2012 by the said court in the action for payment of assigned claims filed by the Plaintiff on May 9, 2012 against the deceased Non-party 1, under the court below Case No. 2012GADAN115142, in order to interrupt the statute of limitations for the claim for the judgment amount under the related judgment (hereinafter referred to as the “former action in this case”), constitutes a void judgment rendered against the already deceased deceased Non-party 1, and therefore the provisions of Article 170 of the Civil Act cannot apply.\\n\\nThe determination of the court below is in accordance with the above legal principle and is proper, and there is no illegality, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, in misunderstanding the legal doctrine concerning the effect of interruption of prescription by a judicial claim.\\n\\n2. With respect to Ground 2 of the grounds for final appeal\\n\\nIn light of the reasoning of the judgment below and the record, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that the former action in this case constituted a “demand” prescribed in Article 174 of the Civil Act and that its effect continued until September 7, 2012, the date of pronouncement of the judgment in the former action, so that, since the present action was filed within 6 months thereafter, prescription had been interrupted, on the ground that there was no evidence to acknowledge that a duplicate of the complaint or a certified copy of the judgment in the former action in this case had reached the Defendant; such rejection is understandable, and there is no illegality, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, such as deviation from the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating logic and the rules of experience.\\n\\n3. With respect to Ground 3 of the grounds for final appeal\\n\\nAs to the Plaintiff’s argument that, although the Defendant came to know of the contents of the former action in this case by receiving, through Non-party 4 acting on behalf of the Defendant, a duplicate of the complaint in the former action in this case, the Defendant’s assertion of the completion of the statute of limitations in this case, without responding at all to the former action in this case, is contrary to the principle of good faith, the court below rejected it on the ground that there was no evidence to find that Non-party 4 received, on behalf of the Defendant, a duplicate of the complaint in the former action in this case, or that the Defendant knew of the filing and contents of the former action in this case around the time the duplicate of the complaint in the former action in this case was served.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the above measures of the court below are proper and understandable, and there is no illegality, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, such as misunderstanding the legal doctrine concerning a violation of the principle of good faith in a defense of prescription, or deviation from the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating logic and the rules of experience.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the final appeal is dismissed, and the appellate costs are borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices of the Supreme Court."}

{"[2016DA35789]": "We decide the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. A judicial claim has no effect of interrupting the statute of limitations in cases of dismissal, rejection, or withdrawal of the action (Civil Act Article 170(1)); however, if a judicial claim, etc. is made again within 6 months thereafter, the statute of limitations is deemed to have been interrupted by the initial judicial claim (Civil Act Article 170(2)).\\n\\nMeanwhile, while an action is pending before the court, if a third party succeeds to all or part of the right that is the subject matter of the action, the court may, upon a party’s motion, cause that third party to take over the action (Civil Procedure Act Article 82(1)); and if the court renders a decision permitting succession to the action, the effect of interrupting the statute of limitations arises retroactively to the time when the action was first pending before the court (Civil Procedure Act Article 82(3), Article 81).\\n\\nA Plaintiff who has assigned the right that is the subject matter of the action may, after the court renders a decision permitting succession to the action, withdraw from the action with the Defendant’s consent (Civil Procedure Act Article 82(3), Article 80). Afterward, if, as a result of the court’s review of the merits of the claim of the intervening successor, the court renders a judgment dismissing the intervening successor’s claim or dismissing the action, and that judgment becomes final and conclusive, the effect of the interruption of the statute of limitations arising from the initial judicial claim filed by the Plaintiff is extinguished. However, withdrawal from the action is different in nature from withdrawal of the action, and a judgment rendered in the remaining action after such withdrawal also has effect against the withdrawing party (Civil Procedure Act Article 82(3), Article 80 proviso). In light of this, where the effect of the intervening successor’s acquisition of the subject matter of the action is denied and a judgment dismissing the claim against the intervening successor or dismissing the action becomes final and conclusive, if the withdrawing Plaintiff makes again, within 6 months from the date on which that final and conclusive judgment was rendered, a judicial claim, etc. identical to that made before withdrawal, it is proper to view the effect of the interruption of the statute of limitations arising from the judicial claim filed by the Plaintiff before withdrawal as remaining intact.\\n\\n2. According to the reasoning of the lower court’s judgment and the record, including the lawfully admitted evidence, the following facts may be found.\\n\\na. On 2011. 6. 20., the Plaintiff filed a suit against the Defendant with the Uijeongbu District Court Goyang Branch (hereinafter referred to as the “Goyang Branch”) seeking payment of the agreed amount stated in the lower court’s judgment dated 2001. 11. 22. (hereinafter referred to as “the agreed amount at issue in this case”) (hereinafter referred to as “the prior action in this case”).\\n\\nb. While the prior action in this case was pending, the Plaintiff alleged that the claim for the agreed amount at issue in this case had been assigned to the Nonparty and, on that basis, applied for succession to the action by the Nonparty. Accordingly, the Goyang Branch, on 2011. 9. 30., rendered a decision permitting succession to the action, making the Nonparty an intervening successor Plaintiff, and the Plaintiff withdrew from the prior action in this case on the same day with the Defendant’s consent.\\n\\nc. Accordingly, the Nonparty continued to conduct the litigation in the prior action in this case. However, the Goyang Branch, on the ground that the assignment of the claim between the Plaintiff and the Nonparty had been effected mainly for the purpose of having the Nonparty perform litigation acts and was therefore invalid, rendered a judgment on 2012. 6. 8. dismissing the action on the basis that “the action of the intervening successor Plaintiff is procedurally improper.” The Seoul High Court, which was the appellate court, dismissed the appeal on the same ground on 2013. 5. 23.\\n\\nIn the final appeal filed by the Nonparty, the Supreme Court, on 2014. 10. 27., held that “even if the assignment of the claim between the Plaintiff and the Nonparty is invalid, that fact alone does not render the Plaintiff’s application for succession to the action or the Nonparty’s action procedurally improper; therefore, although the Nonparty’s claim based on the invalid assignment should have been dismissed, the appellate court erred in determining that the Nonparty’s action was procedurally improper, but under the principle prohibiting a more adverse modification of the judgment, a judgment dismissing the claim that would be more unfavorable to the Nonparty cannot be rendered,” and dismissed the appeal.\\n\\nd. On 2015. 1. 19., the Plaintiff again filed this action against the Defendant seeking payment of the agreed amount at issue in this case.\\n\\n3. Examining these facts in light of the legal principles set forth above, although in the prior action in this case filed by the Plaintiff, the Nonparty took over the action as the assignee of the claim and the Plaintiff withdrew, and although, as a result of the subsequent review, the assignment of the claim to the Nonparty was found invalid and a judgment dismissing the Nonparty’s action became final and conclusive on 2014. 10. 27., since the Plaintiff filed this action, identical to the prior action in this case, on 2015. 1. 19., within 6 months from the date on which that judgment became final and conclusive, the effect of the interruption of the statute of limitations arising from the Plaintiff’s filing of the prior action in this case must be deemed to have remained intact notwithstanding the final and conclusive judgment described above.\\n\\n4. Nevertheless, the lower court, treating the Plaintiff’s withdrawal from the action as equivalent to withdrawal of the action, held that the effect of the interruption of the statute of limitations arising from the Plaintiff’s filing of the prior action in this case had ceased on 2011. 9. 30., when the Plaintiff withdrew from the prior action in this case, and that the statute of limitations for the claim for the agreed amount at issue in this case had been completed on the ground that the Plaintiff filed this action on 2015. 1. 19., after 6 months had elapsed from that time.\\n\\nAccordingly, the lower court judgment contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations arising from a judicial claim filed before withdrawal by a Plaintiff who withdrew after succession to the action. The ground of appeal pointing this out is well founded.\\n\\n5. Therefore, the lower court judgment shall be reversed, and the case shall be remanded to the lower court for further review and determination. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2019DA223723]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. a. Where a lawsuit is filed expressly stating that judgment is sought only with respect to part of one claim, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations by the filing of the action arises only with respect to that part and does not arise with respect to the remaining part (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 74DA1557, decided 1975. 2. 25.), but where, while claiming only part of the claim targeted in the complaint, the party indicates an intention to expand the amount claimed in the future depending on the progress of the litigation, and in fact expands the amount claimed before the litigation in question terminates, it is construed as having sought judgment for the entire claim from the time of filing; therefore, in such a case, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations by a judicial claim arises with respect to the entire claim from the time of filing (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 91DA43695, decided 1992. 4. 10.).\\n\\nb. Where, while claiming only part of the claim targeted in the complaint, the party indicated an intention to expand the amount claimed in the future depending on the progress of the litigation, but did not in fact expand the amount claimed before the litigation in question terminated, then, in light of the progress of the litigation, it cannot be regarded as having sought judgment for the entire claim, and therefore the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations by a judicial claim does not arise with respect to the remaining part.\\n\\nHowever, even in such a case, since a creditor who files a lawsuit while indicating an intention to expand the amount claimed in the future is generally understood to have the intention to claim the remaining part in the future, unless there are other special circumstances, it must be deemed that, while the litigation in question is pending, the intention to exercise the right with respect to the remaining part has been expressed and the state of exercising the right by demand continues, and the creditor may interrupt the statute of limitations with respect to the remaining part by taking the measures prescribed in Article 174 of the Civil Act within 6 months from the time the litigation in question terminates.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the Supreme Court has clarified that, unlike ordinary demand, with respect to demand arising from notice of litigation made through a court act, it is deemed that, while the litigation in question is pending, the state of exercising the right by demand continues, and the statute of limitations may be interrupted by taking the measures prescribed in Article 174 of the Civil Act within 6 months from the time the litigation in question terminates (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2009DA14340, decided 2009. 7. 9.).\\n\\n2. According to the reasoning of the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be ascertained.\\n\\na. The Plaintiff, as a result of providing a residential building due to a public-interest project implemented by the Defendant, received an apartment allotment as part of resettlement measures and paid the sale price in full by 2008. 10. 31.\\n\\nb. The Plaintiff, alleging that the cost of installing basic living facilities was included in the apartment sale price and that the Defendant, as the project implementer, had an obligation to return unjust enrichment, filed the prior action in this case against the Defendant on 2013. 7. 30.\\n\\nc. The complaint in the prior action in this case states under the heading “partial claim” as follows: “The Plaintiff is said to have a claim for return of unjust enrichment, but the exact amount is to be calculated later by receiving materials concerning basic living facilities from the Defendant, and for the time being, only 2,000,000 won, which is part thereof, has been claimed.”\\n\\nd. The Plaintiff did not expand the amount claimed until the prior action in this case terminated, and on 2016. 10. 12. the court rendered a judgment that “the Defendant shall pay to the Plaintiff 2,000,000 won and delay damages thereon.” The above judgment became final and conclusive on 2016. 11. 8.\\n\\ne. The Plaintiff filed this action on 2017. 5. 18., and is claiming the remaining amount of 18,808,243 won, excluding the amount recognized in the prior action in this case, and delay damages thereon.\\n\\nf. The Plaintiff’s claim for return of unjust enrichment against the Defendant is a right against a local government for the purpose of payment of money, and the statute of limitations period is 5 years.\\n\\n3. Examining the above factual relations in light of the legal principles set forth above, since the Plaintiff indicated in the complaint, etc. an intention to expand the amount claimed in the future but did not expand the amount claimed until the prior action in this case terminated, it is reasonable to regard the Plaintiff as having sought judgment only with respect to 2,000,000 won and delay damages thereon in the prior action in this case; therefore, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations by the filing of the prior action in this case arose only with respect to the above 2,000,000 won and delay damages thereon, and with respect to the remaining part, while the prior action in this case was pending, it may be said that the state of exercising the right by demand continued, but unless the Plaintiff took the measures prescribed in Article 174 of the Civil Act, such as filing this action within 6 months from the time the prior action in this case terminated, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations did not arise and the statute of limitations was completed.\\n\\n4. Accordingly, the lower court’s determination that the statute of limitations had run with respect to the remaining part not claimed in the prior action in this case is correct in conclusion, and there is no error that affected the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, misapprehending the legal principles concerning interruption of the statute of limitations.\\n\\n5. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party; it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the principle of good faith in civil procedure is incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: Whether the court will render a decision recommending settlement is an act to be taken ex officio by taking into account the parties’ interests and all other circumstances; however, even though the very existence of the right of claim is clear, if the court renders a judgment dismissing the plaintiff’s claim on the ground of a violation of the principle of good faith, it is unlawful if an amicable resolution was not attempted prior to that judgment.
B: During the pendency of a medical malpractice lawsuit, an act by the physician side of altering medical records constitutes an act obstructing proof contrary to the principle of equality between the parties or the principle of good faith, unless a substantial and reasonable reason for the alteration is presented.
C: Where the court of first instance accepted, at the first preparatory hearing, an improper application for correction of party designation and the defendant expressly consented thereto, and a judgment on the merits was rendered in both the first instance and the appellate instance, the defendant’s subsequent assertion that the above application for correction of designation was improper is not admitted.
D: Since what is contrary to the principle of good faith in civil procedure is in violation of mandatory provisions, the court may determine it ex officio even if there is no party’s assertion.
E: Where the court, with respect to the plaintiff’s abuse of the right of action (including the right of appeal) by repeatedly filing an action in which it is manifest that the claim is without merit, dismisses the action by judgment without oral argument, the presiding judge may, ex officio, order service by publication on the defendant.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2008DA11276]": "We have considered the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to the first ground for appeal\\n\\nAs a matter of principle, correction of party designation is permitted only within the scope in which the identity of the party is recognized; therefore, it is improper to correct the party designation in a lawsuit filed in the personal name of a person who was the representative director of a company so as to substitute the company for that individual (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 85NU953 rendered on September 23, 1986, Supreme Court Decision 94DA61243 rendered on March 22, 1996, and Supreme Court Decision 96DA41496 rendered on January 23, 1998).\\n\\nHowever, if the trial court at the first preparatory hearing accepted such an improper motion for correction of party designation, and the Defendant also expressly consented thereto, and thereafter arguments on the merits proceeded between the corrected Plaintiff, namely, the company, and the Defendant from the first preparatory hearing of the trial court, and judgments on the merits were rendered by the trial court and the court below, then deeming all subsequent arguments and the judgments based thereon as improper or void merely because the motion for correction of party designation was improper would not only undermine the stability of the litigation procedure, but would also not be permissible, in light of litigation economy and the principle of good faith, to raise the issue anew thereafter (see the above Supreme Court Decision 96DA41496).\\n\\nAccording to the record, Nonparty 1, who had been the representative director of the Plaintiff, filed this lawsuit against the Defendant in the trial court on December 19, 2005, and then, at the first preparatory hearing on April 4, 2006, applied to correct the Plaintiff's designation from Nonparty 1 to the Plaintiff, and the Defendant consented thereto; thereafter, after arguments between the Plaintiff and the Defendant, the instant trial court judgment and the judgment below were rendered. In light of the foregoing legal principles, the correction of party designation in this case is improper; however, since the pleading procedures proceeded with the Defendant's consent and the trial court and the court below both rendered judgments, the Defendant's assertion in the grounds for appeal, which now belatedly complains of such impropriety, cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. With respect to the second ground for appeal\\n\\nThe court below, based on the evidence it admitted, found that the Plaintiff entered into the instant construction contract with Nonparty 2, who acted on behalf of the Defendant; such evidentiary selection and factual finding by the court below are proper and reasonable, and no illegality as alleged in the grounds for appeal can be found therein with respect to the authenticity of the dispositive document and the fact of granting authority. The ground for appeal on this point is without merit.\\n\\n3. With respect to the third ground for appeal\\n\\nAn acknowledgment, as a ground for interruption of extinctive prescription, is established when the debtor entitled to the benefit of prescription, or his representative, manifests to the person who will lose the right upon completion of extinctive prescription, or his representative, the meaning that the right exists; the manner of manifestation requires no form and may be either express or implied (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DA63193 rendered on April 25, 2000). Also, when an agent vested with authority to conclude a certain contract performs the authorized juristic act, the legal relationship that gave rise to the agency authority, in principle, achieves its purpose and terminates, and the agency authority conferred by the juristic act is extinguished upon termination of the underlying legal relationship (Civil Act Article 128); therefore, it cannot be immediately said that merely because a person concluded the contract on behalf of another, that person also has all powers of disposition such as rescission of the concluded contract and authority to receive the other party's intention (see Supreme Court Decision 2007DA74713 rendered on January 31, 2008).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment below, the court below, after rejecting the Defendant's assertion that the construction price in this case had been paid, held, with respect to the Defendant's defense that the Plaintiff's claim for the construction price in this case had been extinguished by completion of the statute of limitations, that it was clear from the calculation of time that this lawsuit was filed after three years had elapsed from the time when the Plaintiff completed the construction and delivered the instant building; however, on the other hand, it found that the Defendant had granted Nonparty 2 comprehensive authority to handle all affairs relating to the conclusion of the construction contract for this case, payment of the construction price, registration of preservation of ownership of the instant building, and conclusion of lease contracts concerning the instant building and the land thereunder; that around the end of January 2004, the Plaintiff demanded payment of the construction price from Nonparty 2, the Defendant's agent, and Nonparty 2 promised the Plaintiff payment of the construction price; and then it determined that because the effect of an agent's acknowledgment of debt extends to the principal, the statute of limitations on the claim for the construction price in this case was interrupted around the end of January 2004. However, the evidence relied on by the court below does not directly support the proposition that the Defendant had granted Nonparty 2 authority to pay the construction price, in addition to authority to execute the construction contract document, in connection with the instant construction.\\n\\nRather, according to the reasons stated in the judgment below and the record, Nonparty 3, around August 2000, in partnership with Nonparty 4 and Nonparty 5, agreed with Nonparty 2, the Defendant's agent, to lease the instant land owned by the Defendant, to build a building thereon and operate a restaurant, to obtain a building permit in the Defendant's name, to construct the building at the expense of Nonparty 3 and others, to have the rent free of charge for 7 years, and after the lease period expired, to be granted a preferential right to conclude a lease agreement; accordingly, because the Plaintiff did not wish to enter into the instant building construction contract in the form of making the lessee the contractor, Nonparty 2 prepared the instant construction contract with the Plaintiff in the Defendant's name, and Nonparty 2 believed that Nonparty 3 would pay the construction price, or that Nonparty 2 would receive the construction price from Nonparty 3 and pay it to the Plaintiff; the instant building was completed by the Plaintiff after a building permit was obtained in the Defendant's name and was approved for use on March 27, 2001, and Nonparty 3 also entrusted the interior construction of the instant building to the Plaintiff and paid all interior construction costs; Nonparty 3 registered his business under the name of Nonparty 6 from February 9, 2001, and operated a restaurant, “(trading name omitted),” in the instant building; a registration of preservation of ownership in the Defendant's name was completed with respect to the instant building; when the Plaintiff's representative director urged Nonparty 2 to pay the construction costs on the ground that Nonparty 3 had not paid them, Nonparty 2 said that he would receive them from Nonparty 3 and give them to the Plaintiff; and the Plaintiff also carried out a building construction project on land owned by Nonparty 7, the Defendant's wife, and received all the payment therefor, but did not directly demand payment of the instant construction price from the Defendant. In light of the foregoing legal principles and these circumstances taken together, it is not readily comprehensible that Nonparty 3 built the instant building out of the necessity of operating a restaurant and also entrusted the interior construction to the Plaintiff, who had built the building, while paying only the interior construction costs and not paying the building construction costs. If, from the outset, Nonparty 2 understood that Nonparty 3 would pay the instant construction price and, in order to secure the building permit name, the registration of preservation of ownership, and the instant building after the termination of the lease, concluded the instant construction contract in the Defendant's name, then, absent special circumstances, it would be contrary to general commercial practice and the rules of experience to say that, merely because the landowner, the Defendant, consented for convenience to the lessee's making the lessor under the construction contract for the building construction on the leased land in the Defendant's name when the lessee was building and using the building at his own expense on the leased land, the agent who concluded the construction contract, Nonparty 2, was comprehensively granted authority to pay the construction price after completion of the construction.\\n\\nAccordingly, the court below should have more closely examined the existence or absence of Nonparty 2's authority to pay the construction price, which is the premise of the acknowledgment of debt in this case, whether the construction price was paid, and whether the related evidentiary materials correspond thereto, and then determined whether Nonparty 2, acting on behalf of the Defendant, acknowledged the debt for the instant construction price. However, the court below rejected the Defendant's argument solely on the circumstances as stated above; in such determination by the court below, there are errors of misapprehension of the legal principles concerning acknowledgment of debt and agency authority, failure to conduct the necessary examination and insufficient examination of relevant evidence, and violation of the rules of evidence, and this affected the conclusion of the judgment; therefore, the ground for appeal pointing this out is meritorious.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2008DA78279]": "We review the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. As to Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nWhere a debtor obtains a loan from a financial institution by discounting a bill issued by a third party, the debtor shall be understood to bear, vis-à-vis the financial institution, liability as an indorser of the bill as well as liability for the loan obligation, and a bill issued by a third party and transferred by indorsement shall be regarded as having been subject to the establishment of a security assignment right on the bill to secure the debtor’s loan obligation. In addition, the main clause of Article 123(1) of the former Company Reorganization Act (repealed by Article 2 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act enacted by Act No. 7428 on 2005. 3. 31.; hereinafter referred to as the “Company Reorganization Act”) provides that “a reorganization claim or a claim against a person other than the company arising from a cause before the commencement of reorganization proceedings, to the extent secured by a possessory lien, pledge, mortgage, security assignment right, preliminary registration security right, right of lease, or preferential privilege existing in the company’s property at the time of commencement of reorganization proceedings, shall be a reorganization security right.” There is no reason to exclude only a security assignment in a bill from the security assignment contemplated by the above provision, and if it were regarded as a reorganization claim, the reorganization creditor would be able to exercise the rights under the bill outside the reorganization proceedings and apply the proceeds in satisfaction of the claim, thereby placing the holder of the bill security assignment in a superior position over other reorganization security rights holders, contrary to the principle of equality among creditors. Accordingly, absent special circumstances, a security assignment in a bill also constitutes a reorganization security right as provided in the above provision.\\n\\nMeanwhile, under the Civil Act, the principle of good faith and fair dealing is an abstract norm that parties to a legal relationship must not exercise rights or perform obligations in a manner contrary to equity or in disregard of the other party’s interests and trust. Where one party to a legal relationship has induced trust in the other party, or where the other party is objectively in a state where it is justifiable to hold such trust, and the exercise of rights in contravention of that trust has reached a degree that cannot be tolerated in light of the concept of justice, the exercise of such rights by the former may be denied on the ground of violation of the principle of good faith and fair dealing (see Supreme Court Decision 2000DA13856, rendered on 2002. 3. 15., among others). In a company reorganization proceeding, where a creditor filed a security assignment in a bill as a reorganization security right, yet the receiver took the firm position that its legal nature was a reorganization claim and, by treating the security assignment in the bill as a reorganization claim, induced the creditor to believe that the rights under the bill could be freely exercised because the bill was not the debtor’s property; where, accordingly, the creditor did not file an action to confirm the reorganization security right and instead accepted the disadvantage of having the claim on the loaned amount subject to rights modification as a reorganization claim under the reorganization plan of the reorganization company, which was far less favorable than a reorganization security right; and where the creditor exercised rights under the bill without any objection from the reorganization company or the receiver, it cannot be allowed, as contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing, for the company after the conclusion of the reorganization proceedings to assert that the security assignment in the bill was a reorganization security right but was confirmed as a reorganization claim, and to demand return of the gains obtained by the creditor based on the bill.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, the Plaintiff and Asia Motors Industrial Co., Ltd. applied for commencement of company reorganization proceedings on 1997. 10. 24. and received commencement orders on 1998. 4. 15.; a non-party was appointed as receiver of the reorganization company Kia Motors Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “reorganization company”) and the reorganization company Asia Motors Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Asia Motors”); LG Comprehensive Finance Co., Ltd. (which was absorbed and merged into LG Investment Securities Co., Ltd. on 1999. 10. 21. and whose trade name was changed to the Defendant on 2005. 4. 2.; hereinafter referred to without distinction as “LG Comprehensive Finance”) filed as a reorganization claim in the company reorganization proceedings of the reorganization company 130,477,098,437 won, including discount claims on bills it held pursuant to a bill transaction agreement with the Plaintiff, and thereafter, on 1998. 5. 26., with respect to the claims obtained by discounting the bills at issue among the above reorganization claims, requested that claims in the amount of 17,332,211,739 won, corresponding to the aggregate face value of the bills (hereinafter referred to as the “bill collateral claims”), be recognized as reorganization security rights, and supplemented its filing accordingly; the receiver of the reorganization company, at the first interested persons’ meeting and the date for investigation of reorganization claims and reorganization security rights on 1998. 6. 10., disallowed them in full as reorganization security rights and recognized them only as reorganization claims on the ground that “the holder of a bill cannot be recognized as a secured creditor regardless of whether the bill is issued by a third party”; in response, LG Comprehensive Finance requested on 1998. 6. 17. that the receiver withdraw the objection to the filing as a reorganization security right, but the receiver did not accept this, and LG Comprehensive Finance also did not file an action to confirm the reorganization security right, so that the bill collateral claims were finally determined as reorganization claims; in the reorganization plan of the reorganization company approved on 1998. 12. 28., the bills at issue were stated as being paid to LG Comprehensive Finance pursuant to the repayment plan for reorganization claims, and according to the reorganization plan of the reorganization company, reorganization security rights were to be exempted by 27.81% of principal, converted into equity by 41.08%, and repaid in equal installments over 7 years after a 3-year grace period by 31.11%, whereas reorganization claims were to be exempted by 59.67% of principal, converted into equity by 22.95%, and repaid in equal installments over 7 years after a 3-year grace period by 17.38%; LG Comprehensive Finance filed the bill face amount claims at issue in the reorganization proceedings of Asia Motors as reorganization claims, and the receiver, at the claim investigation date for Asia Motors held on the same day as the reorganization company, recognized all of LG Comprehensive Finance’s claims as reorganization claims; LG Comprehensive Finance received 44,165,017 won as interest on 1999. 3. 31. pursuant to Asia Motors’ reorganization plan and, on 1999. 4. 20., received Asia Motors shares and subscription rights for new shares through debt-to-equity conversion; Asia Motors was merged into the reorganization company by absorption on 1999. 6. 30., and reorganization company shares were allocated in respect of the Asia Motors shares held by LG Comprehensive Finance, while the subscription rights for new shares were also changed into rights to subscribe for reorganization company shares; LG Comprehensive Finance received 479,321,801 won from the reorganization company and the Plaintiff from 1999. 6. 30. to 2002. 6. 27.; and on 2002. 6. 27., after the conclusion of the reorganization proceedings of the reorganization company, the Plaintiff prepaid to the Defendant 23,236,033,625 won, consisting of the aggregate principal amount of the claims that LG Comprehensive Finance was to receive repayment for under the reorganization plans of the reorganization company and Asia Motors, plus interest thereon at 5% per annum from 2002. 4. 1. to 2002. 6. 27., of which the amount of claims based on the bills at issue was 1,342,597,429 won. It can be seen that the receiver of the reorganization company raised no objection at all during the time when LG Comprehensive Finance, as a reorganization creditor against Asia Motors, received repayment, etc. from Asia Motors, and also not during the process in which, after Asia Motors merged with the Plaintiff, reorganization company shares, etc. were allocated in respect of the Asia Motors shares held by LG Comprehensive Finance, and after the conclusion of the reorganization proceedings of the reorganization company, the Plaintiff prepaid to the Defendant the reorganization claims that LG Comprehensive Finance was to receive repayment for under Asia Motors’ reorganization plan, and that the receiver never asserted to LG Comprehensive Finance that the rights under the bills at issue belonged to the reorganization company.\\n\\nAs can be seen from the above factual relationship, although LG Comprehensive Finance filed the bill collateral claims as reorganization security rights in the claim allowance/disallowance procedure of the reorganization company, the receiver of the reorganization company disallowed the reorganization security rights and recognized them as reorganization claims on the ground that the holder of a bill cannot be recognized as a secured creditor regardless of whether the bill issuer is a third party; even though LG Comprehensive Finance requested the receiver of the reorganization company to withdraw the objection to the reorganization security rights, the receiver did not withdraw the objection, and LG Comprehensive Finance also did not file an action to confirm the reorganization security right, leading to the bill collateral claims being finally determined as reorganization claims; and in light of the fact that the same receiver, in Asia Motors’ reorganization proceedings, recognized as finally determined the filing by LG Comprehensive Finance of the bill face amount claims at issue as reorganization claims, it may be viewed that the receiver of the reorganization company held a firm position that the legal nature of the bill collateral claims was that of reorganization claims. In addition, in the reorganization proceedings the receiver had no choice but to recognize or disallow the claim regarding the security assignment in the bill as either a reorganization security right or a reorganization claim; if it were recognized and finally determined as a reorganization security right, the reorganization security right holder could not, in principle, freely collect the bill amount from the issuer of the bill outside the reorganization proceedings and apply it in satisfaction of its own claim, whereas if it were recognized and finally determined as a reorganization claim, the creditor could collect from the issuer of the bill, separately from the reorganization proceedings of the reorganization company, and apply it in satisfaction of its claim; and because there was no other method by which the creditor’s rights under the bill could be extinguished while treating the bill collateral claims as reorganization claims at the claim allowance/disallowance stage, the receiver of the reorganization company, by disallowing the reorganization security rights in the bill collateral claims while recognizing them as reorganization claims and by not responding to LG Comprehensive Finance’s withdrawal of objection, and the same receiver, in Asia Motors’ claim allowance/disallowance procedure regarding the bills at issue, recognizing in full the bill face amount claims at issue as reorganization claims against LG Comprehensive Finance, must be understood to have induced LG Comprehensive Finance to trust that the bill collateral claims would be treated as reorganization claims and that LG Comprehensive Finance could separately collect on the bill face amount claims outside the reorganization proceedings of the reorganization company and would not lose its rights under the bills against Asia Motors. Such conduct by the receiver is also confirmed by the fact, as noted above, that after approval of the reorganization plan, the receiver of the reorganization company raised no objection to LG Comprehensive Finance’s exercise of the reorganization claims based on the bill amounts against Asia Motors pursuant to the reorganization plan, did not assert at all that LG Comprehensive Finance’s rights under the bills against Asia Motors had been extinguished and vested in the reorganization company, and, even after the reorganization proceedings had concluded, the Plaintiff paid LG Comprehensive Finance’s reorganization claims against Asia Motors without any reservation. If so, LG Comprehensive Finance, relying on the receiver’s treatment of the bill collateral claims as reorganization claims, did not file an action to confirm the reorganization security right, and accordingly the bill collateral claims were finally determined as reorganization claims, with rights modification and payment in the reorganization company’s reorganization proceedings being effected on terms less favorable than other reorganization security rights. Therefore, after the conclusion of the reorganization proceedings of the reorganization company, it is contrary to the concept of justice and cannot be permitted under the principle of good faith and fair dealing for the Plaintiff to demand from the Defendant return of the gains obtained on the basis of the bills at issue, on the assertion that the bill collateral claims were reorganization security rights and that the collateral subject matter must therefore be returned. Article 241 of the Company Reorganization Act is a provision aimed at causing all security rights, except those recognized by the reorganization plan or by the provisions of that Act, to lapse on the view that the reorganization company’s rehabilitation and the smooth implementation of the reorganization plan cannot be secured if a creditor fails to file a reorganization security right, or if, despite being a reorganization security right, the creditor files it as a reorganization claim and it is finally determined as such, yet continues to exercise the security right. Where a creditor filed the bill face amount claims as reorganization security rights but the receiver disallowed the reorganization security rights on the basis of the legal nature of the rights and thereby the creditor was instead able to exercise the rights under the bills, which had been treated as collateral subject matter, outside the reorganization proceedings, this cannot be regarded as a case in which the security right was not recognized in the reorganization plan and thus lapsed; therefore, it cannot be said that dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim for restitution of unjust enrichment by applying the principle of good faith and fair dealing is contrary to the above provision.\\n\\nThe lower court’s determination to the same effect is in accordance with the foregoing legal principles and is proper.\\n\\nThe lower court judgment does not contain any error of law regarding the principle of good faith and fair dealing, etc., as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n2.
