The argument is without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal are to be borne by the losing party, and the judgment is rendered as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}
{"[97DA45532]": "All appeals are dismissed. The costs of appeal shall be borne by each Appellant."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning clan associations and other associations without legal personality is incorrect? (In case of dispute, the precedents shall apply.)
A: A clan association is a naturally arising group of descendants, and for its formation it is not necessary that it use a specific name and have written clan association rules, or that it have an organizational structure such as a continuously appointed representative.
B: An individual who is both a member and a representative of an association without legal personality may, upon a resolution of the general meeting of members, become a party in his or her own name in a lawsuit concerning acts of preservation of collectively owned property.
C: In a case in which a clan association is a party, whether the clan association’s representative has lawful authority of representation is a matter concerning litigation requirements and thus is subject to the court’s ex officio investigation; therefore, if the materials already submitted reveal circumstances that may cast doubt on the lawfulness of that authority, the court has a duty to investigate the matter even if the opposing party does not specifically point it out and dispute it.
D: Even where there is no provision in the articles of incorporation or bylaws of an association without legal personality regarding the management and disposition of collectively owned property, a disposition act concerning such property performed by its representative without going through a resolution of the general meeting of members is void.
E: A procedural act performed by a clan association’s representative who lacks lawful representative status becomes effective retroactively from the time of the act if the representative who later lawfully acquires such status ratifies that procedural act, and such ratification may also be made at the stage of final appeal.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2002DA64780]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below found as follows: the Defendant Association is a reconstruction association established pursuant to the Housing Construction Promotion Act, with the owners of the apartment units in Guk-dong Complex No. 1, located at (address omitted) in Yeosu City, as its members; as conditions for its authorization of establishment, it was provided that “where the association selects or changes a joint project implementer, contractor, or designer, or concludes or changes an agreement, it shall do so by a resolution of the general meeting in accordance with the association rules (Article 6),” and that “with respect to matters decided upon involving burdens on the members, it shall do so by a resolution of the general meeting in accordance with the association rules, and it shall be necessary to notify the members of the result and take measures so that they may inspect it at any time”; Article 17 of the Defendant Association’s articles of association provides that matters such as “matters concerning the selection and agreement of the project implementer and construction company, and other matters requiring a resolution of the general meeting under the bylaws or conditions for authorization to establish the association” shall be matters for resolution by the general meeting; Article 27 provides that “the joint project implementer shall procure the project funds and complete all construction within the project implementation period (provided, however, that this shall not apply in the event of force majeure, and where the project implementer has difficulty procuring project funds, it may procure them in consultation with the contractor, but this shall be unrelated to the members)”; and Article 38 provides that “any contract concluded between the association (the association representative) and the project implementer (the contractor) with respect to matters other than the authority (delegation) prescribed in these articles of association (bylaws) shall be void.” It further found that the non-party, who was the representative of the Defendant Association, on January 15, 1997, concluded with the Plaintiff a contract for work by way of mandate (hereinafter referred to as “the instant contract”) concerning design services for new construction work of a reconstruction apartment, with the Defendant Association and Seun Construction Co., Ltd., which had succeeded to the status of Seoyang Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to only as “Seoyang Construction”), as joint parties; and that, in concluding the instant contract, the said non-party did not go through a resolution of the general meeting of members. Having recognized these facts, the court below held that a reconstruction association established pursuant to the Housing Construction Promotion Act falls under an unincorporated association under the Civil Act, and that, with respect to the management and disposition of collective property of a reconstruction association, if there is a provision therefor in the articles of association or bylaws, such provision must be followed, and if there is no such provision in the articles of association or bylaws, it must be done by resolution of the general meeting of members; therefore, if an act of management or disposition of such property is contrary to the provisions of the articles of association or bylaws, or is performed without a resolution of the general meeting of members, then even if the act of disposition was performed by the representative of the reconstruction association, it would have no effect against the reconstruction association. On that basis, the court below determined that because the said non-party did not go through a resolution of the general meeting of members in order to conclude the instant contract on behalf of the Defendant Association, the instant contract was ineffective against the Defendant Association, and thereafter revoked the first-instance judgment and dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim for design service fees.\\n\\nA reconstruction association established pursuant to the Housing Construction Promotion Act falls under an unincorporated association under the Civil Act, and with respect to the management and disposition of collective property, if there is a provision therefor in the articles of association or bylaws, such provision must be followed, and if there is no provision therefor, it must be done by resolution of the general meeting of members; therefore, unless otherwise provided in the articles of association or bylaws, an act of management or disposition of collective property performed without a resolution of the general meeting of members shall be void (see Supreme Court Decision 96DA18656 delivered on August 20, 1996, and Supreme Court Decision 2000DA10246 delivered on May 29, 2001). However, the term “act of management and disposition of collective property” refers to legal or factual acts of disposition and acts of use and improvement concerning the collective property itself, and the Defendant Association’s conclusion of a design service contract for the implementation of the reconstruction project is merely a simple act of assuming obligations and cannot be regarded as an act of management and disposition concerning the collective property itself. Accordingly, the court below, premising that the conclusion of the instant contract constituted an act of management and disposition of collective property, erred in law in determining that the instant contract was void against the Defendant Association solely on the ground that the Defendant Association concluded the instant contract with the Plaintiff without a resolution of the general meeting of members.\\n\\nHowever, in the case of an unincorporated association, there is no means of registration with respect to restrictions on the representative authority of the representative, so Article 60 of the Civil Act cannot be applied mutatis mutandis. Moreover, even where the representative of an unincorporated association fails to go through a resolution of the general meeting of members with respect to an external transaction act that the articles of association provide must be approved by resolution of the general meeting of members, such matters resolved by the general meeting of members are merely internal decision-making of the unincorporated association, and unless the counterparty to the transaction knew or could have known of such restriction on representative authority, it is proper to regard the transaction as valid; in such a case, whether the counterparty to the transaction knew or could have known of the fact of restriction on representative authority must be alleged and proved by the side of the unincorporated association asserting it.\\n\\nAccording to the facts lawfully found by the court below, Article 17 of the Defendant Association’s articles of association provides that matters such as “matters concerning the selection and agreement of the project implementer and construction company, and other matters requiring a resolution of the general meeting under the bylaws or conditions for authorization to establish the association” shall be matters for resolution by the general meeting, and the conditions for authorization to establish the Defendant Association provided that, where the Defendant Association selects or changes a joint project implementer, contractor, or designer, or concludes or changes an agreement, it shall do so by a resolution of the general meeting in accordance with the association rules; accordingly, the conclusion of a design service contract such as the instant contract would also be a matter requiring a resolution of the general meeting of members by virtue of the provisions of the articles of association.\\n\\nIf that is so, the court below should have further examined whether, at the time the Plaintiff concluded the instant contract, the non-party, who was the representative of the Defendant Association, knew or could have known that, in order to conclude the instant contract, a resolution of the general meeting of members was required under the Defendant Association’s articles of association, and then determined whether the instant contract is effective against the Defendant Association.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, premising that the instant contract constituted an act of management and disposition of collective property, dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim solely on the ground that there was no resolution of the general meeting of members; this would be an error of failing to fully examine the matter or of misapprehending the legal principles concerning acts of management and disposition of collective property and the restriction on representative authority in an unincorporated association. The ground of appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\nTherefore, without need to further determine the remaining grounds of appeal, we reverse the judgment of the court below and, in order to have the case retried and determined, remand it to the court below. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2004DA44971]": "1. Findings and Determination of the Lower Court\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the lower court, the lower court, based on a comprehensive review of the evidence it admitted, found that Non-party 1, who had been the representative of the Plaintiff-intervenor, represented the clan association of the Plaintiff-intervenor and sold the land in this case, owned by the clan association of the Plaintiff-intervenor, to the Defendant, and that on February 24, 1999, the registration of ownership transfer in the Defendant’s name was completed on the ground of acquisition by agreement for public land; that the rules of the Plaintiff-intervenor provide that matters concerning the sale of clan property shall be subject to resolution of the general meeting (Article 14), but that in holding the general meeting resolution for the sale of the above land, Non-party 1, without giving any notice of convocation to approximately 600 clan members, gathered about 10 clan members including Non-party 2, Non-party 3, Non-party 4, and Non-party 5, whom he knew well, at his house on July 7, 1998, and adopted a resolution stating, “All matters concerning the land compensation money and related affairs regarding the land in this case are delegated to Non-party 1,” and prepared a written resolution of the general meeting as if Non-party 6, Non-party 7, Non-party 8, Non-party 9, and Non-party 10, who had not even attended, had participated therein; that, based thereon, on January 15, 1999, he prepared a written officers’ resolution stating, “The authority to dispose of the land in this case is delegated to Non-party 1,” and thereafter delivered it to the Defendant as a document constituting the cause of sale; and that the Plaintiff and others, who were the core members of the clan association of the Plaintiff-intervenor, in opposition to the above disposition of property by Non-party 1, held a clan association general meeting after completing the ancestral memorial rite on November 14, 2002 (lunar October 10), elected the Plaintiff as the representative of the clan association, and resolved to recover the clan property, including the land in this case, which had been disposed of by the said Non-party 1. On that basis, the lower court held that, because Non-party 1 sold the property without going through a lawful resolution of the clan association general meeting, the registration of ownership transfer in the Defendant’s name was null and void for lack of cause, and determined that the Plaintiff, as a member of the clan association of the Plaintiff-intervenor, could seek cancellation of the above registration as an act of preservation upon obtaining a resolution of the clan association, and accordingly granted the Plaintiff’s claim.\\n\\n2. Determination of the Supreme Court\\n\\nBefore addressing the grounds for appeal, the Court determines ex officio.\\n\\nArticle 276, paragraph 1 of the Civil Code provides that “the management and disposition of property held in collective ownership shall be by resolution of the general meeting of members,” and paragraph 2 of the same Article provides that “each member may use and derive profits from property held in collective ownership in accordance with the articles of incorporation or other rules,” and does not contain a provision, such as the proviso to Article 265 of the Civil Code or the proviso to Article 272 of the Civil Code, stating that, as in the case of co-ownership or joint ownership, each constituent member may perform acts of preservation. This is the natural consequence arising from the fact that collective ownership, which is the form of ownership of an association not a legal person, has a stronger character as an organization than co-ownership or joint ownership, and that no share right in the property held in collective ownership is recognized for individual members.\\n\\nAccordingly, litigation concerning property held in collective ownership may be brought by an association not a legal person only in its own name upon a resolution of the general meeting of members, or by all of its members as parties in the form of an indispensable joinder; and a member of such association, even if he or she is the representative of the association or has obtained a resolution of the general meeting of members, cannot become a party to such litigation, and this legal principle shall likewise apply where an action is filed as an act of preservation of property held in collective ownership. To the extent contrary thereto, the Supreme Court Decision dated February 6, 1958, rendered 4289MINSANG617, Decision dated May 5, 1960, rendered 4292MINSANG191, Decision dated March 15, 1966, rendered 65DA2465, Decision dated May 27, 1975, rendered 73DA47, Decision dated March 8, 1977, rendered 76DA1029, Decision dated December 9, 1980, rendered 80DA2045, 2046, Decision dated February 28, 1992, rendered 91DA41507, Decision dated April 26, 1994, rendered 93DA51591, and the like shall be modified.\\n\\nTherefore, the lower court’s determination, premised on the conclusion that the instant action brought by the Plaintiff individually, who was merely a member of the clan association of the Plaintiff-intervenor, as an act of preservation of property held in collective ownership, was lawful, contains an error that affected the conclusion of the judgment by misapprehending the legal principle concerning standing to sue in litigation concerning property held in collective ownership.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, without addressing the grounds for appeal, the judgment of the lower court is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination. The decision is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[96DA25227]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. According to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below held that the clan meeting dated 1992. 10. 8., in which the non-party Jeong Won-sik was first appointed as representative of the Plaintiff clan association, cannot be regarded as a clan meeting convened through due procedure by a lawful convener and thus is ineffective; that, on the other hand, it is proper to regard that persons who have branched out into another family line and their descendants do not belong to a clan association whose common ancestor is the paternal great-grandfather of their paternal family line, and that even if they had in fact continuously involved themselves in clan affairs, such circumstance would not newly confer clan-member status upon a person who was not originally a clan member; therefore, the descendants of Jeong In-gwon, who branched out to Jeong Ju-beom, the second descendant of Uk-jong-gong of the same generation as Uk-sang-gong, who is the common ancestor of the Plaintiff clan association, do not have the status of clan members of the Plaintiff clan association; and that the clan meeting dated 1994. 2. 24. was convened by the non-party Jeong Jae-hwan, who is a descendant of the above-mentioned Jeong In-gwon and is not a clan member, and with 15 persons who are descendants of the above-mentioned Jeong In-gwon and not clan members participating therein, a resolution was adopted appointing the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik as representative of the Plaintiff clan association, so that the said resolution was also invalid; therefore, this action was brought by a person lacking the lawful status of representative of the Plaintiff clan association and is thus improper.\\n\\n2. As to Point 1\\n\\nAccording to the record, there is no evidence to support a finding that, at the regular general meeting of the Plaintiff clan association on 1996. 1. 1., the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik was again appointed as representative of the Plaintiff clan association and a resolution was adopted ratifying the litigation acts performed by the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik up to that time; accordingly, this argument lacks merit.\\n\\n3. As to Point 2\\n\\nLitigation acts performed by the representative of an unincorporated association who lacks lawful status as representative become effective retroactively from the time of the act if a representative who later lawfully acquires representative status ratifies such litigation acts, and such ratification may also be made at the appellate stage of final appeal (see Supreme Court Decision 69DA511, rendered on 1969. 6. 24.).\\n\\nAccording to the entries in Plaintiff’s Exhibits Nos. 45 and 46 submitted to this Court, the non-party Jeong Ji-won, who is the most senior among the clan members of the Plaintiff clan association and one of the Plaintiff clan association's clan members excluding those descendants of the above-mentioned Jeong In-gwon, who are descendants of a person who branched out and are not qualified as clan members of the Plaintiff clan association, gave notice to all 19 clan members including the Defendant to the effect that a Plaintiff clan association meeting would be held at 12:00 on 1996. 6. 30. at the house of the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik located at 994 Cheonpo-ri, Geoncheon-eup, Gyeongju-si, and thereafter it can be recognized that a clan association meeting was held at the above date and place, and that at said clan association meeting, 14 clan members gathered and unanimously resolved to elect the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik as representative of the Plaintiff clan association. According to the foregoing findings, the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik was lawfully appointed as representative of the Plaintiff clan association at the Plaintiff clan association meeting on 1996. 6. 30., and since the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik ratified in this Court the litigation acts he had performed as representative of the Plaintiff clan association up to that time, all litigation acts performed by the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik as representative of the Plaintiff clan association at the first instance and in the court below retroactively became effective from the time of their performance; accordingly, the court below's dismissal of this action on the ground that the above-mentioned Jeong Won-sik lacked representative status is ultimately unavoidable as unlawful, and this argument pointing this out has merit.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below; accordingly, it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}
