court of first instance ordered service by public notice on the basis of a reply dated 1995. 10. 9. from the head of Chungmuro 4, 5-ga District to the Plaintiff’s request for issuance of a resident registration certificate, stating that there was no fact that Non-Party 2 whose resident registration number was “(resident registration number omitted)” was registered in the resident registration ledger, and the Defendant disputed in the said case No. 2001GADAN52117 that, because service by public notice had been effected in the aforementioned manner, the party to the first-instance judgment in this case was either Non-Party 2, who has the same name, or another nonexistent person and therefore the res judicata effect of the first-instance judgment does not extend to the Defendant, such circumstances alone cannot be seen as a situation in which it was difficult to determine whether the party to the first-instance judgment in this case was Non-Party 2, who has the same name, or the Defendant, and thus it cannot be said that there were special circumstances in social convention that would warrant the Defendant’s inquiring into the process, such as whether there had been a first-instance judgment against the Defendant and whether the judgment had been served by means of service by public notice.\\n\\nNevertheless, the appellate court, in light of the circumstances that service by public notice had been effected in the aforementioned manner and that the Defendant disputed in the said case No. 2001GADAN52117 that the res judicata effect of the first-instance judgment in this case did not extend to the Defendant, held that, because it was placed in a situation where it was difficult to determine whether the party to the first-instance judgment in this case was the Defendant or Non-Party 2, who has the same name, there were special circumstances in social convention warranting inquiry into the process, and accordingly, that the Defendant first learned on 2003. 3. 22., when he/she was served with the certified copy of the judgment in the said case No. 2001GADAN52117 stating that the res judicata effect of the first-instance judgment in this case extended to the Defendant as the party to this case, that the first-instance judgment in this case had been served on the Defendant by means of service by public notice, and therefore held that the subsequent appeal filed on 2003. 4. 3. was lawful; thus, the appellate judgment contains an error that affected the judgment by failing to fully examine whether the late appeal was lawful or by misunderstanding the legal doctrine concerning completion of procedural acts.\\n\\nTherefore, without further need to determine the remaining grounds of appeal, the appellate judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination; it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court who participated."}

{"[2017DA232105]": "1. Circumstances of the Case\\n\\na. Thirteen co-owners, including the plaintiffs (hereinafter referred to as “the plaintiffs in the judgment at issue”), filed an action for partition of co-owned property against the remaining 34 co-owners, including the defendant (hereinafter referred to as “the defendants in the judgment at issue”), with the Seoul Northern District Court Case No. 2007GAHAP2477, seeking partition of the co-owned property consisting of 69 square meters of land designated as Da, 31 parcels in total, located in Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, (address omitted) (hereinafter referred to as “the land in this case”). The court of first instance in that case rendered a judgment on August 13, 2009, ordering partition in kind of the land in this case and, accordingly, requiring the defendants in the judgment at issue to pay compensation corresponding to the portion by which the plaintiffs in the judgment at issue received a partition in excess of their co-ownership shares (hereinafter referred to as “the judgment at issue”). The portion of the order of the judgment at issue that ordered payment of money stated: “Each plaintiff shall pay the defendant KRW 81,915,047 and, in addition thereto, money calculated at the rate of 5% per annum from the day following the date this judgment becomes final and conclusive until the day of full payment.”\\n\\nb. The plaintiffs and some of the defendants in the judgment at issue appealed the judgment at issue, but due to withdrawal of appeal, only the appeal of some of the defendants in the judgment at issue (hereinafter referred to as “the appellants in the judgment at issue”) remained pending. The Seoul High Court rendered a judgment on August 17, 2012, modifying the judgment at issue and ordering partition by auction. However, on July 10, 2014, the Supreme Court determined that the appellate judgment ordering partition by auction was unlawful and reversed and remanded it. Thereafter, while the appellate proceedings were still pending, on November 19, 2014, and January 15, 2015, the appellants in the judgment at issue successively withdrew their appeals, thereby terminating the action for partition of co-owned property.\\n\\nc. On July 28, 2015, the plaintiffs, designating the defendant as the depositee, deposited KRW 84,080,746, which was KRW 11,221 short of KRW 81,915,047 and, in addition thereto, money calculated at the rate of 5% per annum from January 16, 2015, the day after January 15, 2015, the date on which all appellants in the judgment at issue withdrew their appeals (hereinafter referred to as “the date of withdrawal of appeal in this case”), until the date of deposit, July 28, 2015, and thereafter filed this action for objection to execution seeking exclusion of the enforceability of the judgment at issue.\\n\\n2. The Lower Court’s Determination\\n\\na. The lower court held that the phrase “the date this judgment becomes final and conclusive” in the order of the judgment at issue should reasonably be understood as October 13, 2009 (hereinafter referred to as “the expiration date of the appeal period in this case”), which is 14 days after the appeal period elapsed from the date the authenticated copies of the judgment were served on all parties to the action for partition of co-owned property, which was a necessary joinder action, and therefore determined that the amount that the plaintiffs were required to pay to the defendant pursuant to the order of the judgment at issue appeared to be KRW 81,915,047 and, in addition thereto, money calculated at the rate of 5% per annum from October 14, 2009, the day following the date on which the judgment at issue became final and conclusive, until the day of full payment.\\n\\nb. However, the lower court, citing the following reasons, determined to the effect that requiring the plaintiffs to endure compulsory execution based on the portion of the order of the judgment at issue ordering payment of money calculated at the rate of 5% per annum from October 14, 2009, the day after the expiration date of the appeal period in this case, until January 15, 2015, the date of withdrawal of appeal in this case, would be contrary to the notions of fairness and justice and unacceptable in social life, and thus that compulsory execution of that portion could not be permitted as an abuse of rights.\\n\\n(1) The legal principle that, if an appeal is withdrawn, the judgment of the court of first instance becomes final and conclusive retroactively as of the expiration date of the appeal period is based on procedural-law interpretation to promote the stability of litigation procedure and to clarify, inter alia, the temporal scope of res judicata; therefore, such procedural-law principle cannot immediately lead to the conclusion that, in substantive legal relations, the starting date for default damages that the plaintiffs must pay is the expiration date of the appeal period.\\n\\n(2) The “date this judgment becomes final and conclusive” designated as the starting date for default damages in the judgment at issue should be regarded as setting an indefinite term for the obligation to pay the amount of compensation, and where there is such an indefinite term for performance of an obligation, the obligor is liable for delay from the time he or she knows that the term has arrived (the latter sentence of Article 387(1) of the Civil Act); accordingly, the starting date for default damages for which the plaintiffs bear liability for delay becomes January 16, 2015, the day after the date of withdrawal of appeal in this case.\\n\\n(3) The judgment at issue was terminated by the withdrawal of appeal by the appellants in the judgment at issue, who were parties adverse to the plaintiffs, after a protracted dispute lasting approximately 5 years and 3 months from the expiration date of the appeal period in this case. It should be deemed manifestly unjust and contrary to justice, and therefore unacceptable in social life, that default damages for the period from the expiration date of the appeal period in this case until the date of withdrawal of appeal should also be included within the subject of compulsory execution due to such external circumstances beyond the plaintiffs’ determination and control. If not, it would infringe the plaintiffs’ legitimate reliance and expectation that, owing to a withdrawal of appeal unrelated to their will, they would bear default damages only from after the appellate judgment on remand was rendered in relation to the judgment at issue and that judgment became final and conclusive, and it would also run counter to the principle of self-responsibility.\\n\\n3. The Supreme Court’s Determination\\n\\na. When a judgment becomes final and conclusive, the existence of the claim that was the subject of the judgment is fixed by res judicata, and enforceability arises in accordance with its content. Even rights established by a final and conclusive judgment must be exercised faithfully in accordance with good faith, and where execution based on a judgment constitutes an abuse of rights, such execution is not permitted; therefore, the judgment debtor may seek exclusion of such execution by an action of objection to the claim. However, in light of the purpose of recognizing res judicata for final and conclusive judgments to ensure legal stability, and the fact that, in principle, if one wishes to exclude the effect of a final and conclusive judgment, the proper method is to seek its revocation by an action for retrial, compulsory execution pursuant to a final and conclusive judgment should not be readily recognized as constituting an abuse of rights. In order to recognize this, there must be special circumstances, such as a case where the content of the final and conclusive judgment is contrary to the substantive legal relationship and where it is manifest that execution based thereon is markedly unjust and that requiring the other party to endure such execution is contrary to justice and unacceptable in social life (see Supreme Court Decision 2013DA75717, decided February 21, 2014, among others). And at such time, the fact that the content of the final and conclusive judgment is contrary to the substantive legal relationship must be alleged and proved by the person asserting that compulsory execution based on the final and conclusive judgment constitutes an abuse of rights and seeking denial of such execution (see Supreme Court Decision 2013DA82043, decided May 29, 2014).\\n\\nb. We examine the lower court’s determination in light of the foregoing legal principles.\\n\\nAn action for partition of co-owned property is an action for formation, and the court may, at its discretion, divide the co-owned property by a reasonable method; once a judgment on partition of co-owned property becomes final and conclusive, the legal relations among the co-owners are immediately altered as stated in the order of the final and conclusive judgment on partition of co-owned property. The content of the judgment at issue was to partition in kind the land in this case, which is co-owned by the plaintiffs in the judgment at issue and the defendant, so that the plaintiffs in the judgment at issue would exclusively own the portions stated in the order, while requiring the plaintiffs to pay the defendants in the judgment at issue an amount equivalent to the value of the portion exceeding the shares originally held by the plaintiffs; thus, it cannot be said that the content of the judgment is contrary to the substantive legal relationship.\\n\\nIn addition, when a judgment on partition of co-owned property becomes final and conclusive by way of an action for partition of co-owned property, the co-ownership relationship is extinguished immediately, and each co-owner acquires ownership over the portion apportioned to him or her. The fact that the judgment at issue ordered payment of additional sums from the day following the date on which the judgment at issue became final and conclusive in respect of the portion ordering monetary payment to the plaintiffs in the judgment at issue, who received partition in kind of the land in this case, appears to reflect precisely this point. Therefore, it is also difficult to deem it manifestly unjust to require the plaintiffs to endure compulsory execution with respect to the additional sum portion of the judgment at issue from the day following the expiration date of the appeal period in this case until the date of withdrawal of appeal in this case.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court, citing the reasons stated in its holding, determined that compulsory execution of that portion constituted an abuse of rights and could not be permitted; thus, the lower court’s determination contains an error that misapprehended the legal principles concerning the effect of a final and conclusive judgment and abuse of rights, thereby affecting the judgment. The ground of appeal pointing out this is well taken.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the lower court judgment is reversed and the case is remanded to the lower court for a new trial and determination; it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the decision."}

{"[94DA41010]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n1. As to Point 1,\\nUpon comparing and examining the reasons of the judgment of the lower court against the record, it is reasonable to accept that the lower court found that, in the case of Jeju District Court 86GAHAP146, filed by the Defendant against the Plaintiff for the cancellation of the registration in the Plaintiff’s name concerning the real property at issue, both the duplicate of the complaint and the authenticated copy of the judgment were not duly served on the Plaintiff, and therefore it cannot be said that there was any illegality of erroneous fact-finding in violation of the rules of evidence. Accordingly, this argument is without merit.\\n2. As to Point 2,\\nIn a case where, by falsely stating the address of the opposing party, litigation documents are served at that false address, and as a result another person, not the opposing party, receives those documents, a judgment is rendered in the form of a deemed admission in favor of the party who filed the action, and the authenticated copy of that judgment is likewise sent to and processed as having been served at the false address, service of the judgment on the opposing party is improper and therefore void; thus, the opposing party remains in a state in which the authenticated copy of the judgment has not yet been served, and may not only file an appeal thereagainst, but may also, if a transfer registration of ownership or a cancellation registration concerning real property has been completed based on that judgment, seek cancellation of such registration by a separate action (see Supreme Court Decisions 80DA2220 rendered on March 24, 1981; 91DA38631 rendered on April 24, 1992, etc.). In such a case, if the opposing party attempts to seek restoration through a separate action, the period within which such action may be filed shall not be limited to within 2 weeks from the time when the opposing party came to know of the fact that the fraudulent judgment was rendered. This is because, even if the opposing party came to know of the fact that the fraudulent judgment was rendered by means other than service, if the enforcement of the transfer registration of ownership or cancellation registration based on the fraudulent judgment has not yet been carried out, there is not even any object to be disputed by separate action, and there is also no legal basis to find for limiting the period during which cancellation may be sought with respect to a registration that is void for lack of cause. Therefore, this argument is also without merit.\\n3. As to Point 3,\\nWhere a registration of transfer of ownership was not effected by the direct disposition act of the registered owner of the former registration, but rather a third party was involved in that disposition act, and the current registered owner alleges that such third party was the agent of the former registered owner, or where such third party is a person in a special status relationship such as spouse or parent and child with the former registered owner, even if the current registered owner does not expressly allege that the third party was the former registered owner’s agent, the current registered owner’s registration shall be presumed to have been lawfully made. Therefore, the former registered owner seeking cancellation of such registration on the ground that it is void for lack of cause bears the burden of proving the contrary facts, namely, facts of invalidity such as that the third party had no authority to act as agent for the former registered owner, or that the third party forged the former registered owner’s registration documents (see Supreme Court Decisions 79DA645 rendered on July 10, 1979; 91DA26379, 91DA26386 rendered on April 24, 1992; 93DA18914 rendered on October 12, 1993, etc.).\\nAccording to the facts as determined by the lower court, the Plaintiff received the real property at issue, which had been registered in the Defendant’s name, from the Defendant’s husband, the deceased non-party, and completed the registration of transfer of ownership thereof. The record clearly shows that, at the second hearing date in the lower court, the Plaintiff, by the statement in the preparatory brief dated October 6, 1993, asserted that the real property at issue was only nominally registered in the Defendant’s name, while its actual owner was the said non-party, and that the Plaintiff received it from the person having the power of disposition; and that even if the said non-party was not the actual owner, he transferred it to the Plaintiff in the capacity of the Defendant’s agent or apparent agent. Accordingly, the registration in the Plaintiff’s name is still presumed to have been lawfully made, and therefore the point that the said non-party had no authority to dispose of the real property at issue must be proved by the Defendant.\\nThe lower court, on the same purport and on the premise that the Defendant must prove that the said non-party had no authority to dispose of the real property at issue, held that the mere fact that the box for confirmation by the diplomatic mission in the Defendant’s power of attorney attached by the said non-party when completing the registration of transfer of ownership of the real property at issue in the Plaintiff’s name was left blank is insufficient to find that the said non-party transferred the real property at issue to the Plaintiff without any authority. This is reasonable and acceptable, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality, as alleged, in misapprehending the legal principle on the presumption of agency authority or the legal principle concerning the reversal of the burden of proof, or in failing to conduct a sufficient hearing. Accordingly, this argument is also without merit.\\n4. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Judges participating."}

{"[94DA41430]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nThe court below, after finding that it was not disputed between the parties that the Defendant had loaned KRW 75,000,000 to the deceased non-party and, upon the death of that non-party, had filed an action for return of loan money against the Plaintiffs, who are his heirs, seeking payment of the said loan money and interest thereon, and had obtained a judgment in his favor, and that, once that judgment became final and conclusive, he applied for compulsory execution based thereon and received KRW 117,026,360 as principal and interest in that procedure, held that the Plaintiffs, in this action, alleged that although the Defendant had been repaid KRW 25,000,000 of the said loan money by the said non-party, he concealed that fact, filed a lawsuit for the full amount of the said loan money and obtained a final judgment in his favor, and then received the said amount through compulsory execution, and therefore the principal amount of KRW 25,000,000 out of that amount and an amount equivalent to interest thereon must be returned as enrichment without legal cause, or alternatively, because the Defendant deceived the court and fraudulently obtained money from the Plaintiffs, he must compensate the Plaintiffs for damages equivalent to the said amount; and as to the claim for restitution of unjust enrichment among them, rejected it on the ground that the above repayment allegation is a ground arising before the final judgment in the action for return of loan money and, unless that judgment is revoked by a retrial action or the like, conflicts with the res judicata of that judgment, so that the Plaintiffs cannot assert it, and therefore the money received through compulsory execution of the said final judgment cannot be deemed enrichment without legal cause; and as to the claim for damages among them, rejected it on the ground that there was no evidence sufficient to establish the above repayment allegation.\\n\\nUpon review, the court below’s determination that the res judicata of the final judgment in the action for return of loan money extends to the claim for return of unjust enrichment in this case is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any error of law in misunderstanding the legal principles concerning res judicata or retrial, as alleged, or any contradiction in the reasons. Further, upon examining the relevant evidence in light of the record, the court below’s disposition of rejecting the evidence consistent with the Plaintiffs’ allegation of repayment is also proper and persuasive, and it cannot be said that there is any violation of the rules of evidence as alleged.\\n\\nThe argument is without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties, and the judgment is rendered as ordered by the concurrence of the participating Justices."}
{"[99DA32899]": "The appeal is dismissed. The costs of the appeal shall be borne by the Defendant."}

question: 13th Korean Bar Examination, Civil Law Multiple-Choice Question 63. Which of the following statements concerning the assignment of a nominative claim are correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law) (a) If notice of assignment of a claim by an instrument bearing a fixed date and an order of provisional attachment of the claim are simultaneously served on the third-party obligor, the third-party obligor may make a deposit for performance on the ground that the creditor cannot be identified, by analogy to a case in which the order of service is unclear. (b) If the assignee of the claim is the “debtor of the assigned claim,” and after the assignment of the claim an order of provisional attachment sought by a creditor of the assignor with respect to the assigned claim is served on the assignee, who is the third-party obligor, the above provisional attachment order is valid if there was no notice of assignment of the claim by an instrument bearing a fixed date or acceptance concerning the above assignment of claim. (c) If the assignee of the claim files an application to intervene claiming to be a successor during the pendency of the litigation, whether succession to the status of creditor occurred during the pendency of the litigation is determined based on the time when the requirements for setting up the assignment of claim against third parties were satisfied. (d) If the Plaintiff, while seeking a claim for payment of money based on the creditor’s subrogation right, changed the action into a claim for the assigned amount by subsequently acquiring by assignment the claim subject to subrogation itself, the effect of interruption of the statute of limitations arising from the original creditor’s subrogation action does not cease.
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2010DA17284]": "We consider the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the records, the Defendant purchased the land at issue, namely, the first parcel of land at issue from the late Non-party 1 and the second parcel of land at issue from Non-party 2, pursuant to the Special Measures Act concerning the Reorganization of Expropriated Property, etc., but when it became no longer necessary for military purposes, on 2002. 6. 18. the Defendant notified Non-party 3, who is an heir of the late Non-party 1, and Non-party 2 of the sales plan that the respective parcels of land at issue would be sold by private contract pursuant to the provisions of Article 20-2 of the Special Measures Act concerning the Reorganization of Expropriated Property, etc., and accordingly Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, around 2002. 6. 29., applied to the Defendant for purchase of the respective parcels of land at issue; Non-party 4, intending to purchase and develop the respective parcels of land at issue, on 2002. 11. 22. entered into the “Agreement in this Case” with Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, to the effect that “Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 shall, after completing the registration of transfer of ownership concerning the respective parcels of land at issue, re-transfer them to the Plaintiff, and Non-party 4 shall take responsibility for a series of acts, including entering into a sales contract with the Defendant in the names of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 or paying the purchase price therefor,” and paid to Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 a total of KRW 718,400,000,000 in consideration for the said agreement (money corresponding to a kind of resale profit, hereinafter referred to as “the resale profit in this Case”); accordingly, on 2002. 11. 23. Non-party 4, acting on behalf of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, entered into the “sales contracts in this Case” with the Defendant and paid to the Defendant a total of KRW 914,794,000 in contract money, which corresponds to about 10% of the purchase price (hereinafter referred to as “the contract money in this Case”); however, thereafter, as Non-party 4 failed to pay the balance of the purchase price, etc. under the respective sales contracts in this Case, the respective sales contracts in this Case were rescinded on 2003. 4. 28. due to the purchaser’s fault; on the premise that he held claims for return of the resale profit in this Case and the contract money in this Case against Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, Non-party 4 assigned to the Plaintiff on 2007. 7. 27. the claim for return of the resale profit in this Case and the contract money in this Case against Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 (hereinafter referred to as “the assignment of claims in this Case”), and notified Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 of such assignment on 2007. 9. 18.; thereafter, the Plaintiff, on 2007. 11. 19., sent to the Defendant by content-certified mail a demand (hereinafter referred to as “the demand in this Case”) to the effect that “the Plaintiff, as a creditor of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, seeks the return of the contract money in this Case as restitution following the rescission of the respective sales contracts in this Case by subrogating them,” and it appears that the said mail reached the Defendant on 2007. 11. 22.\\n\\nAlso, according to the records, the Plaintiff, when filing this action on 2008. 3. 14., alleged as the cause of action that, on the premise that Non-party 4 was a party to the respective sales contracts in this Case, the Plaintiff had acquired from Non-party 4 the claim for return of the contract money in this Case that Non-party 4 held against the Defendant; thereafter, in a brief dated 2008. 5. 15., the Plaintiff changed the cause of action to a subrogation claim as creditor of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, on the premise that Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 were parties to the respective sales contracts in this Case, in subrogating the claim for return of the contract money in this Case that Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 held against the Defendant; meanwhile, the Plaintiff filed an action on 2007. 12. 15. against Non-party 3, Non-party 2, etc. seeking return of the resale profit in this Case and the contract money, and although a judgment dismissing the Plaintiff’s claims was rendered at first instance on 2008. 9. 3., while the appeal was pending, on 2009. 1. 20. an amicable settlement was reached to the effect that “Non-party 3, Non-party 2, etc. assign to the Plaintiff all rights they hold against the Defendant in connection with the respective sales contracts in this Case, including the claim for return of the contract money in this Case, and notify the Defendant of said assignment of claims. The Plaintiff abandons the remaining claims against Non-party 3, Non-party 2, etc.”; and accordingly, the Plaintiff, in a brief dated 2009. 1. 28., changed the cause of action in the present suit again from a claim based on creditor subrogation to a claim for the assigned money.\\n\\nBased on the above facts, the court below, without omitting any determination on the cause of action asserted by the Plaintiff, proceeded directly to the Defendant’s defense of the Statute of Limitations and determined that the claim for return of the contract money by Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 against the Defendant, which arose from the rescission of the respective sales contracts in this Case, became exercisable from 2003. 4. 28., when the respective sales contracts in this Case were rescinded, but the Plaintiff, having acquired the claim for return of the contract money in this Case only on 2009. 1. 28., after the 5-year Statute of Limitations prescribed in Article 96 of the National Finance Act had elapsed, sought payment of the assigned money, and therefore held that the claim had been extinguished by prescription; and then rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that the Statute of Limitations with respect to the claim for return of the contract money in this Case was interrupted because the Plaintiff made the demand in this Case to the Defendant before prescription had been completed, on 2007. 11. 22., and, within 6 months thereafter, on 2008. 5. 15., filed a claim seeking return of the contract money in this Case based on creditor subrogation, for the following reasons.\\n\\nFirst, in order for a judicial claim to constitute a ground for interruption of prescription, such claim must be made by the creditor or a person authorized to exercise the claim; however, because the Plaintiff’s claim for restitution of unjust enrichment against Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, and the claim for subrogation of compensation in kind, etc., which the Plaintiff asserts as preserved claims, cannot be recognized, the Plaintiff’s subrogation claim, by which, as creditor of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, the Plaintiff sought return of the contract money in this Case from the Defendant by subrogating them, is merely a judicial claim by an unauthorized person and cannot serve as a ground for interruption of prescription; second, even if prescription were interrupted by the above subrogation claim, as the prior action based on creditor subrogation was withdrawn when the Plaintiff, on 2009. 1. 28., interchangeably changed the cause of action from the subrogation claim to the claim for the assigned money, the effect of interruption of prescription as a judicial claim by the above subrogation claim is not maintained.\\n\\nHowever, the above judgment of the court below cannot be upheld for the following reasons.\\n\\nAccording to the factual relation recognized by the court below, Non-party 4 entered into the Agreement in this Case, to the effect that he would acquire the respective parcels of land at issue from Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 by resale and, in the position of a resale purchaser, would himself act on behalf of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 and perform all acts, including entering into the sales contract with the Defendant and paying the purchase price therefor; and pursuant to the Agreement in this Case, Non-party 4, in addition to paying the resale profit in this Case to Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, directly procured the purchase price under the sales contracts in this Case at his own responsibility and paid the contract money in this Case to the Defendant, but the respective sales contracts in this Case were rescinded. According to this, under the respective sales contracts in this Case, Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 could no longer acquire the respective parcels of land at issue from the Defendant; and, in light of the purport of the Agreement in this Case and the content of the aforesaid amicable settlement, etc., the Agreement in this Case should be understood to include an implied agreement to the effect that, in the event that the respective sales contracts in this Case become invalid or are rescinded for reasons attributable to Non-party 4, the resale profit in this Case paid by Non-party 4 to Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 would not be disputed, while, with respect to the contract money, etc. paid by Non-party 4 to the Defendant on behalf of Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 pursuant to the respective sales contracts in this Case, if Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 acquired the claim for return thereof, such claim would be assigned to Non-party 4, and if the contract money, etc. were actually returned by the Defendant, such money would be returned to Non-party 4. It is also reasonable to view that, through the assignment of claims in this Case, the Plaintiff acquired from Non-party 4 the contractual claim that Non-party 4 held against Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 as above. Therefore, in the creditor subrogation action before the amendment in this Case, it is difficult to hastily deny the existence of the preserved claim in favor of the Plaintiff.\\n\\nMeanwhile, although a creditor may not exercise the creditor’s subrogation right without court permission before the due date of the claim, the creditor may perform acts of preservation (see Article 404(2) of the Civil Act). Accordingly, as a creditor, the Plaintiff may, by using the above contractual right as the preserved claim, make a demand to the Defendant for return of the contract money in this Case and file a judicial claim as an act of preservation to interrupt prescription of the claim for return of the contract money in this Case by subrogating Non-party 3 and Non-party 2.\\n\\nIn addition, through the brief dated 2009. 1. 28., the Plaintiff changed the existing claim based on creditor subrogation to a claim for the assigned money based on assignment of the claim; this should be regarded as the withdrawal of the prior claim based on creditor subrogation as an interchangeable change of the cause of action, but the object of litigation in the creditor subrogation suit is the claim of the debtor, Non-party 3 and Non-party 2, against the Defendant for return of the contract money in this Case, whereas the claim for the assigned money in this Case is based on the Plaintiff’s assertion that the Plaintiff acquired the claim itself for return of the contract money in this Case; thus, the two claims involve only a specific succession of rights and obligations concerning the same object of litigation, and the object of litigation is the same; the effect of interruption of prescription also extends to a specific successor (Article 169 of the Civil Act); where a specific successor who succeeded to all or part of the rights or obligations that are the object of the litigation in a pending lawsuit intervenes in or is substituted into the litigation, the effect of interruption of prescription arises retroactively as of the time when the litigation first became pending before the court (Articles 80 and 82(3) of the Civil Procedure Act); and, as the Plaintiff exercised the claim for return of the contract money in this Case based on creditor subrogation and thereafter, again, directly exercised it after acquiring it, the Plaintiff cannot be regarded as a person “sleeping on his rights” with respect to the claim for return of the contract money in this Case. In light of the foregoing, even if the Plaintiff changed the lawsuit from a claim based on creditor subrogation to a claim for the assigned money after acquiring by assignment the claim subject to subrogation itself, it is reasonable to hold that the effect of interruption of prescription caused by the original creditor subrogation action does not cease.\\n\\nAccordingly, the court below should have reached its conclusion by examining and determining whether the claim for return of the contract money in this Case against the Defendant, which Non-party 3, etc. allegedly assigned to the Plaintiff by Non-party 4, exists, that is, whether there is a liquidated damages clause in the respective sales contracts in this Case, whether the predetermined amount of damages is excessively high and thus subject to reduction, and whether the claim for the assigned money alleged by the Plaintiff satisfies the requirement for opposability of assignment of claims; it should not have rejected the Plaintiff’s claim in this Case solely on the basis of the Defendant’s defense of the Statute of Limitations.\\n\\nThe Supreme Court Decision 2008DA84229 rendered on 2009. 2. 12. or the Supreme Court Decision 82DAKA148 rendered on 1982. 12. 14. cited by the Defendant concern cases in which the creditor directly made a claim on his own title and then subrogated or acquired the debtor’s right and made a claim; those cases differ from the present case, in which the Plaintiff made a subrogation claim and then acquired the claim subject to subrogation itself and made a claim for the assigned money.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, without making any determination on the cause of action asserted by the Plaintiff, immediately accepted the Defendant’s defense of the Statute of Limitations and then held that, because the Plaintiff’s preserved claim against Non-party 3 and Non-party 2 did not exist, the subrogation claim was merely a judicial claim by an unauthorized person and could not serve as a ground for interruption of prescription, and even if it did serve as such ground, since the Plaintiff interchangeably changed the cause of action from the claim based on creditor subrogation to the claim for the assigned money and the prior action was withdrawn, the effect of interruption of prescription had ceased; accordingly, the court rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that prescription had been interrupted, and thus there is an error in the judgment of the court below in that it misunderstood the legal principle concerning interruption of prescription by creditor subrogation and failed to conduct the necessary examination. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing out this point is well-founded.\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so decided by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the decision."}

{"[2019DA272855]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Determination on the Plaintiff’s grounds for appeal\\n\\na. Regarding confusion and the requirements for asserting an assignment of claim against third parties (Point 1)\\n\\nAn assignment of claim means a contract whose purpose is that, between the assignor and the assignee, a claim is transferred from the former to the latter while maintaining its identity. By virtue of an assignment of claim, the claim is transferred from the assignor to the assignee without losing its identity, and the same applies even if the requirements for asserting the assignment of claim against third parties have not been satisfied (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DA41818 rendered on November 10, 2005). The effect of such a change in the subject to whom the claim belongs, in principle, arises at the time of the dispositive act pursuant to the assignment of claim. Accordingly, where the assignee of a nominative claim is the debtor of the assigned claim, the time of the dispositive act pursuant to the assignment of claim corresponds to the time when both the claim and the debt belong to the same subject, and thus the claim is extinguished by confusion under the main text of Article 507 of the Civil Act.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the requirements for asserting an assignment of a nominative claim against third parties set forth in Article 450(2) of the Civil Act apply where there exists a third party who, while the assigned claim continues to exist, has acquired a legal status incompatible with that of the assignee with respect to that claim. Therefore, where the assignee of a nominative claim is the debtor of the assigned claim, and the assigned claim is extinguished by confusion as above, even if an order of attachment or provisional attachment concerning that claim is thereafter served on the third-party debtor, such order of attachment or provisional attachment of the claim is void as pertaining to a non-existent claim, and the creditor of such attachment or provisional attachment does not constitute a third party under Article 450(2) of the Civil Act.\\n\\nThe court below held that, under the second dation-in-payment agreement, Non-party 1 assigned to Narae Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to only as “Narae Enterprise”) and Non-party 2 the claim for registration of transfer of ownership concerning each of the commercial units in this case, and that Narae Enterprise should be deemed to have accepted this through the preparation of the above dation-in-payment agreement; however, there is no evidence to establish that Non-party 1, the assignor, notified Narae Enterprise, the debtor, thereof by an instrument bearing a certified date, or that Narae Enterprise, the debtor, accepted by an instrument bearing a certified date, and thus Narae Enterprise and Non-party 2 cannot assert against the Plaintiff, the creditor of the provisional attachment in this case, the transfer of the pre-sale right under the second dation-in-payment agreement. Nevertheless, the court below further held that, under the second dation-in-payment agreement concluded after the first dation-in-payment agreement (the agreement under which Narae Enterprise undertook the obligation to complete registration of transfer of ownership concerning Commercial Unit No. 103 of the commercial units in this case, etc. vis-à-vis Non-party 1), namely, the agreement under which Non-party 1 agreed to retransferred the claim for registration of transfer of ownership concerning Commercial Unit No. 103 of the commercial units in this case to Narae Enterprise, the claim for registration of transfer of ownership concerning Commercial Unit No. 103 of the commercial units in this case had already, before the provisional attachment decision in this case, been extinguished by confusion because both the claim and the debt had come to belong to Narae Enterprise, the same subject, and thus concluded that the part of the provisional attachment decision in this case attaching the pre-sale right for Commercial Unit No. 103 of the commercial units in this case was void as pertaining to a non-existent claim, and did not accept the portion of the Plaintiff’s claim for damages arising from tort concerning Commercial Unit No. 103 of the commercial units in this case.\\n\\nExamining the reasoning of the judgment below in light of the legal principles set forth above and the record, there is no error in the above determination of the court below that affected the judgment, such as by misconstruing the legal principles concerning the effect of confusion in the case of an assignment of claim or the effect of confusion under Article 507 of the Civil Act and its exceptions, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nb. Regarding the amount available for distribution for the amount of damages (Point 2)\\n\\nThe court below, in calculating the damages amount concerning Commercial Unit No. 104 of the commercial units in this case, regarded the amount available for distribution as an amount equivalent to 80% of the market price (sale price) of Commercial Unit No. 104 of the commercial units in this case.\\n\\nExamining the reasoning of the judgment below in light of the record, there is no error in the above determination of the court below that affected the judgment, such as by misconstruing the legal principles concerning the standard for the amount available for distribution in calculating damages in the case of an unlawful disposition of real property contrary to a provisional attachment decision, or by going beyond the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. Determination on the Defendant’s grounds for appeal\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the court below held that the part of the provisional attachment decision in this case attaching the pre-sale right for Commercial Unit No. 104 of the commercial units in this case was valid, found that the Defendant’s having completed registration of transfer of ownership for Commercial Unit No. 104 of the commercial units in this case in the name of Non-party 3 constituted active participation in, or at least aiding and abetting, Narae Enterprise’s tortious act in contravention of the provisional attachment decision in this case, and determined that the Defendant is liable to compensate the Plaintiff for the damages suffered by the Plaintiff due to the tort concerning Commercial Unit No. 104 of the commercial units in this case, and that the amount of damages is KRW 447,232,511 and delay damages thereon.\\n\\nExamining the reasoning of the judgment below in light of the record, there is no error in the above determination of the court below that affected the judgment, such as by misconstruing the legal principles concerning the content of the trust agreement in this case, the effect of the decision of attachment of claims, the effect of dation in payment in relation to the transfer of pre-sale rights, the assignment of nominative claims, and confusion under Article 507 of the Civil Act, or by going beyond the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2020DA210747]": "We determine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. As to Ground 1 of the Grounds of Appeal\\n\\na. If a claim has been assigned, but the requirements for opposability, namely notice by the assignor or the debtor’s consent, have not yet been satisfied, the assignee of the claim has no legal relationship with the debtor and therefore cannot assert any right against the debtor (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 90DA9452, 9469, decided Aug. 18, 1992), and the assignee may assert the assignment of the claim against the debtor only when the assignor notifies the debtor of the assignment of the claim or the debtor consents thereto (see Supreme Court Decision 90DAKA27662, decided Nov. 27, 1990). Accordingly, where the assignee of the claim filed an application to intervene, asserting that it was a successor during the pendency of litigation, just as the issue of whether the succession to the status as creditor occurred during the pendency of litigation is determined not by the time when the agreement on assignment of the claim was reached, but by the time when the requirements for opposability were satisfied (see Supreme Court Decision 2016DA8589, decided May 16, 2019), whether the assignee of the claim falls under a successor after the conclusion of oral argument to whom the effect of a final judgment extends under Article 218(1) of the Civil Procedure Act must likewise be determined not by the time when the agreement on assignment of the claim was reached, but by the time when the requirements for opposability were satisfied.\\n\\nb. The Court below held that, on the ground that it is reasonable to regard the assignor’s status as creditor as succeeding to the assignee only after the requirements for opposability have been satisfied, the res judicata of the final judgment in the prior lawsuit for return of investment funds filed by the assignor, Taegil Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Taegil Development”), also extends to the Plaintiff, who, after the conclusion of oral argument in that lawsuit, obtained the Defendant’s consent to the assignment of the claim for return of the investment funds in this case and thereby satisfied the requirements for opposability.\\n\\nc. In light of the legal principles discussed above, the Court below’s determination as above is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the subjective scope of res judicata, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. As to Ground 2 of the Grounds of Appeal\\n\\nThe Court below, for the reasons stated in the judgment, rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that, because after the conclusion of oral argument in the prior lawsuit for return of investment funds the Defendant acknowledged the debt to return the investment funds in this case to the Plaintiff, the Plaintiff’s exercise of the claim for return of investment funds in this case against the Defendant does not conflict with the res judicata of the final judgment in the prior lawsuit for return of investment funds.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the Court below’s determination as above is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, violating the laws of logic and experience, thereby exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, or by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the temporal scope of res judicata, etc.\\n\\n3. As to Ground 3 of the Grounds of Appeal\\n\\nThe Court below, for the reasons stated in the judgment, rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that, because after the conclusion of oral argument in the prior lawsuit for return of investment funds the Defendant consented to the assignment of the claim for return of investment funds in this case without reserving objections, the Defendant cannot oppose the Plaintiff, as assignee, by invoking the res judicata of the final judgment in the prior lawsuit for return of investment funds.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the Court below’s determination as above is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, misapprehending the legal principles regarding consent without reservation of objections, etc.\\n\\n4. As to Ground 4 of the Grounds of Appeal\\n\\nThe Court below, for the reasons stated in the judgment, held that, in calculating delay damages on the amount of 1,806,000,000 won, with respect to which the Plaintiff’s claim was partially upheld, the statutory interest rate prescribed by the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as the “Litigation Promotion Act”) applies from the day after the date of pronouncement of the judgment of the Court below.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the Court below’s determination as above is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment by, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, misapprehending the legal principles regarding the interpretation and application, etc. of Article 3 of the Litigation Promotion Act.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved, as stated in the order."}

{"[93DA24223]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal (since the supplemental statement of grounds for final appeal was submitted after the period for filing the statement of grounds for final appeal had elapsed, it shall be considered only to the extent that it supplements the grounds for final appeal).\\n\\n1. According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below acknowledged that Nonparty Ajin Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “the Nonparty Company”) assigned to the Plaintiff on 1992. 8. 2. the claim for the price of goods in the amount of 7,779,750 won against the Defendant, and on the 3rd of the same month notified the said assignment by contents-certified mail bearing a fixed date, and that the said notice reached the Defendant on the 4th of the same month; accordingly, unless special circumstances exist, the Defendant is obligated to pay the said 7,779,750 won to the Plaintiff, the assignee of the claim. The court below further acknowledged that, with respect to 6,290,000 won out of the said claim of the Nonparty Company against the Defendant, the authenticated copy of the decision of the Busan District Court rendered on 1992. 8. 3. in Case No. 92KAHAP489 on prejudgment attachment of claim, in which the creditor was the Defendant’s auxiliary intervenor (Kukje Sangsa Co., Ltd.), the debtor was the Nonparty Company, and the third-party debtor was the Defendant, was served on the Defendant on the 4th of the same month. On that basis, the court below held that the Defendant may oppose the Plaintiff, who as assignee of the claim seeks payment of the above 7,779,750 won in price for goods, with respect to the said 6,290,000 won, which is the amount of the claim subject to attachment, because the Defendant received notice of the said prejudgment attachment decision at the same time as the notice of assignment of claim; therefore, the Defendant is obligated to pay to the Plaintiff only the remaining 1,489,750 won, obtained by deducting the said amount of the attached claim of 6,290,000 won from the said assigned claim amount of 7,779,750 won, together with delay damages thereon.\\n\\n2. In the case where a claim has been assigned twice, the priority between the assignees is not to be determined by the chronological order of the fixed dates attached to the notice or consent, but by the debtor’s knowledge of the assignment of claim, that is, by the chronology of the time when the notice of assignment bearing a fixed date reached the debtor or the time of consent bearing a fixed date; and this legal principle likewise applies in determining the priority between an assignee of a claim and a person who has executed a prejudgment attachment order against the same claim. Therefore, the priority should be determined by the chronology of the arrival at the third-party debtor (in the case of assignment of claim, the debtor; hereinafter the same) of the notice of assignment bearing a fixed date and the authenticated copy of the prejudgment attachment decision.\\n\\nAccordingly, in this case, the court below’s action of determining the priority regarding the opposability of the assignment of claim between the Plaintiff, who is the assignee, and the intervenor, who is the prejudgment attachment creditor, on the basis of the respective times when the notice of assignment bearing a fixed date and the authenticated copy of the prejudgment attachment decision arrived at the Defendant, who is the third-party debtor, is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality therein arising from an erroneous understanding of the legal principle on the standard for determining priority concerning the requisites for opposing an assignment of claim; therefore, the argument criticizing this is without merit.\\n\\n3. Even in cases where a notice of assignment of claim, a prejudgment attachment, or an attachment order is served on the third-party debtor at the same time so that none has priority over the others, the assignee of the claim and the prejudgment attachment or attachment creditor are all deemed to have fully perfected opposability against the third-party debtor; thus, each may demand performance of the assigned claim, the entire amount subject to attachment, or the amount collected, respectively, and may lawfully receive payment thereof. If the third-party debtor pays the entire amount of the debt to any one of them, the debtor is effectively discharged even in relation to the other creditors, and if the total of the assigned claim amount and the amount attached or attached by seizure exceeds the amount of the claim against the third-party debtor, then, as their legal positions are equal inter se, they shall, in accordance with the principle of equity, divide it according to the respective amounts of their claims and internally settle the matter again.\\n\\nHowever, if it is recognized that the notice of assignment of claim and the prejudgment attachment or attachment order were served on the third-party debtor simultaneously, and even after the debtor has lost entirely in a performance action filed by one of the assignee of the claim and the prejudgment attachment or attachment creditor who obtained an order of collection or order of transfer, if another creditor again raises the issue of the chronology of such service, then under the theory of res judicata the third-party debtor may face the risk of double payment; therefore, even in cases of simultaneous service, the third-party debtor should be deemed able to escape legal uncertainty by making a deposit of performance on the ground that the creditor cannot be identified, in the same manner as where the chronology of service is unclear.\\n\\nA precedent of this Court, contrary to the legal principle set forth above, to the effect that where the notice of assignment of claim and the authenticated copy of the prejudgment attachment decision reached the third-party debtor simultaneously, the debtor may oppose the assignee’s claim for the assigned amount by asserting that the notice of assignment of claim and the authenticated copy of the prejudgment attachment decision were served simultaneously (Supreme Court 87DAKA553 decided on 1987. 8. 18.), shall be overruled.\\n\\nIn this case, the notice of assignment of claim naming the Plaintiff as assignee and the authenticated copy of the prejudgment attachment decision naming the intervenor as creditor reached the Defendant on the same day, and since there is no separate proof as to the chronological relation between them, they shall be presumed, as stated in the judgment of the court below, to have arrived simultaneously.\\n\\nTherefore, since the assignee, the Plaintiff, and the prejudgment attachment creditor, the intervenor, simultaneously satisfied the requisites for opposing the assignment of claim, the Plaintiff may demand from the debtor, the Defendant, payment of the entire amount of the assigned claim for the price of goods, 7,779,750 won, and the debtor, the Defendant, cannot oppose the Plaintiff on the ground that there exists a prejudgment attachment creditor who, at the same time as the Plaintiff, has acquired opposability.\\n\\nUltimately, in this case, the Defendant is obligated to pay the Plaintiff the entire amount of the assigned claim, namely 7,779,750 won, together with delay damages thereon. The court below, however, upheld the judgment of the first instance court, which had held that the Defendant was obligated to pay only 1,489,750 won, being the amount remaining after deducting the prejudgment attachment claim amount of 6,290,000 won from the assigned claim amount, together with delay damages thereon, and dismissed the Plaintiff’s appeal. This, in the event that the notice of assignment of claim and the authenticated copy of the prejudgment attachment decision reached the third-party debtor simultaneously, constitutes an error of law concerning the legal relations, and such error affected the conclusion; accordingly, the grounds of final appeal on this point are well taken.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and since this case is sufficiently ready for judgment by this Court based on the facts established by the court below, this Court will render its own judgment. As to 6,290,000 won out of the judgment of the first instance court and delay damages thereon at the annual rate of 5 percent prescribed by the Civil Act from 1992. 9. 27., the day after service of the duplicate of the complaint in this case, which is plainly on the record as the day sought by the Plaintiff, until 1994.4.26., the date of the judgment of this Court in this case, being the day on which it was reasonable to contest the existence and scope of the above performance obligation, and at the annual rate of 25 percent prescribed by the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings from the following day until full payment, the portion of the judgment unfavorable to the Plaintiff is reversed, and the Defendant is ordered to pay the said amount; the Plaintiff’s remaining appeal is without merit and is dismissed; and as to the burden of litigation costs, Articles 89, the proviso to Article 92, Article 94, and Article 96 of the Civil Procedure Act are applied, and, by unanimous opinion of all participating Justices, judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition."}

question: Which of the following are all cases falling under inherent indispensable joint litigation? (Where there is dispute, according to precedent) (a) An action brought against A, B, and C seeking performance of the procedure for registration of transfer of ownership, on the ground of termination of a title trust, with respect to real property for which the registration of transfer of ownership has been made in the form of joint ownership by A, B, and C (b) An action brought by A, B, and C, co-owners of land, against D, the owner of adjacent land, seeking determination of the boundary (c) Where A and B, as business partners, deposit money that each contributed separately for a specific purpose other than their partnership under joint names, and open the deposit under joint names for the purpose of monitoring so that neither A nor B alone can withdraw it before achieving that purpose, an action by A and B against the bank seeking return of the deposit (d) An action brought by A and B, among the co-heirs A, B, and C, as plaintiffs against C, seeking a declaration that certain property is inherited property (e) An action seeking removal of co-owned property, brought against A, B, and C, who are the owners of the co-owned property
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2000DA24207]": "The Court examines ex officio.\\n\\nSince the boundary of land is an important matter that determines the scope and limits of land ownership, and it is necessary that it be conclusively determined among all owners of neighboring land related to the boundary, where either one side or both sides of adjoining land belong to several persons in co-ownership, an action seeking the determination of such boundary should be construed as an indispensable joint action in the strict sense, requiring that all relevant co-owners file suit jointly and that the opposing side also be sued only jointly by all relevant co-owners.\\n\\nHowever, according to the statements in Exhibit A No. 1 (copy of the register), with respect to the ① land in this case as stated in the judgment of the court below, a transfer registration of ownership was completed on 1967. 7. 20. in the names of seven persons, namely, Non-party 1, Non-party 2, Plaintiff 3, Plaintiff 4, Plaintiff 5, Plaintiff 6, and Plaintiff 7; on 1996. 7. 23., Non-party 2’s share was transferred and registered to Plaintiff 2; on 1997. 12. 26., Non-party 1’s share was transferred and registered to Plaintiff 1; and thereby the Plaintiffs in this case came to jointly own the above land. Thereafter, it can be recognized that on 1998. 12. 15., Plaintiff 4’s share was transferred to Non-party 3 on the ground of inheritance by agreement division dated 1998. 7. 16.\\n\\nIf so, the action for boundary determination in this case, filed on 1999. 1. 29. by Plaintiff 4, who was merely a former co-owner, as a co-plaintiff while omitting Non-party 3, a co-owner of the above land, after the co-ownership share right had been transferred to Non-party 3, is unlawful and cannot avoid dismissal (moreover, Plaintiff 4 appears to have already been deceased at the time of filing); therefore, it must be deemed that the judgment of the court below, which overlooked this and proceeded to decide the merits, is unlawful in that it misapprehended the legal doctrine concerning the standing of parties in an action for boundary determination.\\n\\nAccordingly, without examining the grounds for appeal, the judgment of the court below is set aside, and this Court decides to render judgment directly. Since the action in this case is unlawful as seen above, the first-instance judgment that upheld the claim is reversed, the action is dismissed, and the total costs of litigation are borne by the losing party. Judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2006DA40980]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. As to the Plaintiffs’ grounds of appeal\\n\\nWhere, among coheirs, there is a dispute as to whether certain property belongs to the decedent’s inherited property, and some coheirs file an action against other coheirs seeking confirmation that the property is inherited property, this is an action seeking confirmation that the property is currently in a co-ownership relationship among the coheirs before partition of the inherited property; and by a final judgment in favor thereof, it becomes established that the property is subject to partition of the inherited property, so that after the inheritance partition adjudication proceedings or after the partition adjudication becomes final, the parties can no longer dispute again that the property is subject to partition of the inherited property, and as a result the dispute between coheirs as to whether it is subject to partition of the inherited property can be conclusively resolved, and therefore there is an interest in confirmation.\\n\\nUnlike the foregoing, the lower court’s judgment, insofar as it held that the portion of this action seeking confirmation that the movable property at issue in this case is part of the inherited property of the deceased Non-party 1 is improper because there is no interest in confirmation for the reasons stated in the judgment, contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principle concerning the interest in an action for confirmation, and the ground of appeal pointing this out is well-taken.\\n\\nMeanwhile, an action by one coheir against another coheir seeking confirmation that certain property is inherited property is what is called an indispensable joint action, and in an indispensable joint action, unless special circumstances exist, the withdrawal of an action by some of the Plaintiffs or the withdrawal of an action against some of the Defendants does not produce any effect (see Supreme Court Order dated Jan. 23, 2002, 99SEU49). In the court below, the Plaintiffs withdrew the action insofar as it sought confirmation of inherited property against Non-party 2, who is one of the coheirs of the deceased Non-party 1, but it is also noted that, under the foregoing legal principle, that withdrawal did not become effective.\\n\\n2. As to the grounds of appeal by Defendant 1\\n\\na. As to Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment below, the lower court, based on the evidence it adopted, found that the deceased Non-party 1, during his lifetime, owned a large number of antique books and paintings, to the extent of registering some of them as cultural property and exhibiting them at exhibitions held overseas; that, as the property manager of Non-party 3, he was in a position to dispose at will of the property remaining in the name of Non-party 3 in effect; and that, apart from the property remaining in the name of Non-party 3, he also left as his own inherited property 72 parcels of land scattered throughout the country until the time of his death. On the other hand, the lower court found that Defendant 1 had been living in very straitened economic circumstances at the time of marrying the deceased Non-party 1, and that even after the marriage to the deceased Non-party 1, she did not engage in any particular external economic activities and therefore had no independent income whatsoever. After doing so, the lower court, in light of the circumstances stated in the judgment, held that the movable property at issue in this case is presumed to have belonged to the deceased Non-party 1 because it was inherited from his forebears or purchased by him directly or through Defendant 1 with his own money, and that the evidence submitted by the Defendants alone is insufficient to overturn the above presumption and there is no other counterproof, and therefore the movable property at issue in this case is the inherited property of the deceased Non-party 1.\\n\\nIn light of the evidence submitted, the above factual findings and determination by the lower court are reasonable and persuasive, and there is no illegality such as a violation of the rules of evidence evaluation, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe argument in this part of the grounds of appeal cannot be accepted.\\n\\nb. As to Ground 2 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nSince a co-owner who owns a share in co-owned property cannot exclusively possess the co-owned property without agreement with the other co-owners, the other co-owner may demand delivery or surrender of the co-owned property from the person in possession thereof as an act of preservation of the co-owned property even if the share he or she owns is less than a majority (see Supreme Court en banc Decision of Mar. 22, 1994, 93DA9392, 93DA9408, Supreme Court Decision of Dec. 23, 1996, 95DA48308, etc.).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment below, the lower court held that the statutory inheritance shares of the coheirs of the deceased Non-party 1 are 2/13 each for the Plaintiffs, Defendant 2, and Non-party 2, and 3/13 for Defendant 1, and that Defendant 1, who exclusively and to the exclusion of others possesses and manages the movable property at issue in this case, which is the inherited property of the deceased Non-party 1, has the duty to deliver the movable property at issue in this case to the other coheirs, the Plaintiffs.\\n\\nThe lower court’s determination as above is in accordance with the legal principle previously stated and is proper, and there is no illegality such as a misapprehension of the legal principle concerning an act of preservation of co-owned property, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThis part of the grounds of appeal also cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the part of the lower court’s judgment against the Plaintiffs is reversed, and this part of the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination; and Defendant 1’s appeal is dismissed. The judgment is rendered in accord with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as set forth in the disposition."}

{"[69DA609]": "We determine the Plaintiff’s grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the judgment below, while recognizing the fact that, on the ground of the portion marked in red on the attached drawing to the judgment, a levee 18 meters in length and 1 meter in width had been constructed on the ground of the paddy field of 478 pyeong owned by the Plaintiff (on the said drawing, that levee was installed east-west on the ground of the riverbed in order to block the river flowing north-south on the west side of the said paddy, and its eastern end merely adjoins the west side of the said paddy), and that, due to the construction of the levee, the paddy is inundated during floods and the damage is serious, it is clear that, with respect to the Plaintiff’s principal claim seeking removal of the said levee against the Defendants who installed the levee based on ownership of the said paddy, the court below dismissed it on the ground that the said levee is, as the Plaintiff also admits, jointly owned by the Defendants and Nonparty and 3 others, and that a suit seeking its removal, by its nature, had to be conclusively determined uniformly as against all co-owners, and therefore the principal action brought only against the Defendants was improper.\\n\\nHowever, even if the academic world is divided by various views concerning the nature of a suit for removal of co-owned property, this Court, in recent decisions (see Supreme Court Decisions 65DA2455 decided on 66.3.15. and 68DA1102 decided on 68.7.31.), expressly stated the view that a lawsuit concerning the return or removal of co-owned property cannot be said to be necessary joint litigation, and that such a claim should be regarded as seeking delivery or removal against each co-owner within the limit of his share right and should be judged on its merits. Therefore, the view of the judgment below contrary to that precedent cannot but be deemed unlawful, and the argument that criticizes the contents of the holding of that judgment is well-founded; accordingly, by the unanimous opinion of all participating Justices, we render judgment as ordered pursuant to Civil Procedure Act Articles 406 and 400."}

{"[93DA31825]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, in this case in which the Plaintiff, asserting that KRW 16,000,000 out of the ordinary deposit of KRW 30,000,000 deposited with the Defendant Bank on 1988. 2. 17. in joint name with Non-Party 1, a codefendant at first instance, (provided that the Plaintiff was in the name of Non-Party 2), constituted the Plaintiff’s share and seeking against the Defendant payment of that amount and interest thereon, held, with respect to the principal claim portion, that the Plaintiff had previously instituted against the Defendant a suit for return of deposit based on the same factual circumstances as this action, under the case number Seoul Civil District Court 88GAHAP53642, but on 1989. 5. 16. a judgment of dismissal of the action was rendered on the ground that, although deposit creditors in joint name must jointly demand performance or receive payment, and the obligor’s performance must also be rendered to all deposit creditors, the Plaintiff had made the demand alone and therefore lacked standing as a proper party, and that judgment became final and conclusive around that time; accordingly, the action for the claim of KRW 16,000,000 in this case, which is identical to the said final and conclusive judgment in terms of parties and subject matter of litigation, is in conflict with the res judicata of the said final and conclusive judgment, and, with respect to the interest portion, the court below determined and rejected it on the ground that, for the same reason as in the prior action, the Plaintiff’s claim alone was defective for lack of standing as a proper party and thus unlawful.\\n\\n2. Where a deposit is made with a bank in joint name and it is agreed that the rights thereto will be exercised jointly against the bank, it is a principle that the joint-name deposit creditors should jointly demand performance or receive payment from the bank (see Supreme Court Decision 87DAKA8 rendered on 1989. 1. 17.), but it cannot be said that a suit for return of a deposit against the bank by joint-name deposit creditors is always an indispensable joint action requiring all deposit creditors to become parties.\\n\\nSince a deposit made in joint name with a bank may be opened under various and diverse causes and agreements, the legal nature of the deposit claim or who should be regarded as the depositor cannot be uniformly defined.\\n\\nIf, for example, business partners deposited partnership funds in joint name, then, in view of the nature of joint ownership in a quasi-joint ownership relationship of the claim, a claim for return of the deposit against the bank would be deemed an indispensable joint action; however, where one of the joint-name deposit creditors, or funds contributed separately by each, are deposited in joint name for a specific purpose other than partnership, and the deposit is opened in joint name for the purpose of preventing and supervising so that, until that purpose is achieved, even a joint-name deposit creditor cannot unilaterally withdraw his own deposit, then, because management and disposition rights over such deposit cannot be regarded as belonging jointly to all joint-name deposit creditors, a claim for return of the deposit against the bank in such a case cannot be said to constitute an indispensable joint action under the Civil Procedure Act.\\n\\n3. However, even if the latter case does not amount to an indispensable joint action in procedural law, a joint-name deposit creditor, when opening the deposit, is naturally bound by the agreement with the bank that the deposit creditors will jointly make a demand for return of the deposit; thus, if one of such deposit creditors seeks from the bank return of his deposit, he must, of course, follow the procedure of jointly demanding return together with the other joint-name deposit creditor in order to receive return of the deposit from the bank, but this should be viewed as a matter separate from the litigation requirements.\\n\\nIn such case, if the other joint-name deposit creditor does not cooperate in the joint return-demand procedure, the depositor may first file suit against that person and obtain a judgment to the effect that he cooperate in the joint return procedure, such as by expressing an intention of consent regarding the return demand made solely by the depositor, and then receive return of the deposit by presenting that judgment to the bank; and even if, by such means, the requirements for a joint return demand under the agreement have been satisfied, if the bank refuses to return the deposit without just cause, the depositor would have no choice but to sue the bank alone for return of the deposit, and, where prior demand is necessary, it should also be understood that suit may be filed with the other joint-name deposit creditor and the bank as joint defendants for the above-mentioned purpose.\\n\\n4.
