However, the court below’s determination that the Defendant’s act in this case constitutes “forgery” under the offense of forgery of evidence is difficult to accept.\\n\\n(1) Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act punishes a person who destroys, conceals, forges, or alters evidence concerning another person’s criminal case or disciplinary case, or uses forged or altered evidence, and “forgery” here means, unlike the concept of forgery in offenses relating to documents, the creation of new evidence (see Supreme Court Judgment dated June 28, 2007, 2002DO3600). However, if a document prepared for the purpose of proving facts contains no falsity whatsoever in its content concerning those facts or in the name of its maker, it cannot be deemed to constitute “forgery of evidence.” The same applies even if a document concerning factual proof is submitted as evidence of a false claim in a criminal case or disciplinary case and thereby supports that claim. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\n(a) The Constitution prescribes crimes and punishments by law in order to protect individuals’ freedom and rights from the arbitrary exercise of the State’s power to punish (Article 13(1) of the Constitution). Laws restricting fundamental rights of the people or imposing duties must be clear, and in particular laws concerning punishment must be, above all else, clear so that state organs do not exercise their authority arbitrarily. In other words, penal statutes require that the elements of an offense be clearly defined so that an ordinary person can foresee what conduct will be punished and determine his or her own conduct accordingly.\\n\\nA penal provision that cannot be regarded as having a meaning and content sufficient to serve as a standard by which a person of sound common sense and ordinary legal sentiment may determine his or her conduct may violate the principle of clarity under the nulla poena sine lege principle and thus be unconstitutional (see, e.g., Constitutional Court en banc decision dated November 24, 2016, 2015HEONGA23). Therefore, this point must be kept in mind when interpreting unclear provisions in conformity with the Constitution. In addition, the interpretation of penal statutes must be strict, and interpretation beyond the possible meaning of the wording, in a manner unfavorable to the defendant, is not permitted under the prohibition against expansive interpretation, which is part of the nulla poena sine lege principle (see Supreme Court Judgment dated March 10, 2016, 2015DO17847).\\n\\n(b) The offense of forgery of evidence under the Criminal Act protects the State’s judicial function, in particular the functions of criminal adjudication and disciplinary adjudication. However, unlike the offense of obstruction of justice in the United States, which punishes all acts obstructing the performance of duties by persons in charge of judicial procedures or lawful law enforcement, Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act punishes only acts of destroying, concealing, forging, or altering evidence, or using forged or altered evidence. Even if the concept of “forgery” in the offense of forgery of evidence can be construed differently from that in the offense of document forgery, evidence containing no falsity whatsoever in its content, name of maker, or date of preparation cannot be said to have been forged.\\n\\nMeanwhile, even evidence that contains no falsity in itself may in some cases be combined with a false claim and thereby partially support a false fact. And there are cases in which evidence is prepared to prove, originally, another fact for such a purpose. However, deeming evidence that contains no falsity in its content and name of maker to constitute forgery of evidence merely because it was used to support a false fact would exceed the ordinary meaning of the statutory language and improperly expand the scope of punishment, and is therefore impermissible.\\n\\n(c) Since “forgery of evidence” as prescribed by this provision means “forgery of the means of evidence,” whether an act constitutes forgery must be determined based on the means of evidence itself, and whether it is forged should not be decided according to whether the fact sought to be proved thereby is false or true. This is because the authority and duty to evaluate the probative value of the submitted means of evidence and to determine the factual relationship on that basis lie with the court.\\n\\nAccordingly, even if the deposit confirmation certificates submitted by the Defendant were made to prove the false assertion that the relevant funds had all been returned to the Non-party 2 Company side, so long as there is no falsity in the certificates themselves, they cannot be deemed to constitute “false evidence” in relation to the false assertion.\\n\\n(d) As noted above, the “evidence” subject to the offense of forgery of evidence includes, in addition to evidence concerning the establishment of a crime, evidence concerning factual circumstances forming the basis for sentencing. However, the factual circumstances forming the basis for sentencing are not only highly complex and atypical, but also do not constitute the subject of strict proof prescribed by Article 307 of the Criminal Procedure Act. Accordingly, in actual trials, various sentencing materials concerning the defendant’s personal tendencies or the environment in which he or she was raised, in addition to sentencing materials directly related to the facts of the crime such as the motive for the offense or post-offense circumstances, are frequently submitted not only during the trial proceedings but also even after the close of argument.\\n\\nConsidering comprehensively such diversity of evidence, the judicial practice regarding sentencing proceedings, and the principle against expansive interpretation noted above, unless the concept of “forgery” prescribed in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act is interpreted strictly, there is a risk that uncertainty and lack of clarity in the scope of punishment will chill the exercise of the defense rights of defendants, etc.\\n\\n(e) Of course, there is no denying that even though evidence itself contains no falsity, there are cases in which it is combined with a false claim and thereby proves a false fact, and such conduct is deserving of criticism as an act that may cause serious hindrance to the exercise of the State’s power to punish. However, apart from the question of creating a new statutory element criminalizing such conduct, achieving that purpose by expansively interpreting the meaning of “forgery of evidence” prescribed in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act is not permitted under the principle of nulla poena sine lege.\\n\\n(2) Examining the facts found by the court below in light of the above legal principles, although the Defendant repeatedly remitted funds from a □□ Bank account in Non-party 4’s name to a △△ Bank account in the name of Non-party 2 Company and received them back again, then obtained only the remittance materials among them and submitted them to the court together with the false assertion that 350,000,000 won had been repaid, such conduct carries the risk of undermining the judicial function, which is the protected legal interest of the offense of forgery of evidence under the Criminal Act. However, in light of the above legal principles, the deposit confirmation certificates, etc. submitted by the Defendant are documents prepared by a financial institution to prove facts concerning financial transactions, and so long as there is no falsity whatsoever in their content or the name of their maker, they cannot be deemed to constitute “forgery” of evidence, and furthermore cannot be deemed to constitute the act of “using forged evidence.”\\n\\n(3) The court below’s judgment affirming the first-instance judgment, which found the facts charged in this case guilty on a different premise, contains an error affecting the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning “forgery” of evidence prescribed in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the lower-court judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further proceedings and determination. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices, as stated in the order."}

{"[85DO220]": "We judge the Defendant’s grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAs for the offense of false accusation, it suffices to report facts without being certain of their truth for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal or disciplinary punishment, and it is not necessary to be certain that the reported facts are false; according to the evidence relied upon in the first-instance judgment upheld by the court below, the fact may be recognized that the Defendant, without being certain that the facts were true, submitted to the Chuncheon District Prosecutors’ Office a complaint stating the false fact that the persons complained against 1 and 2 had forged and used the Defendant’s guaranty portion of the loan certificate in this case; therefore, the court below’s disposition recognizing the establishment of the offense of false accusation with respect to the act as stated in the judgment is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as a factual error due to violation of the rules of evidence or any misapprehension of legal principles concerning the offense of false accusation as alleged. The argument is without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition, by unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the territorial scope of application of the Criminal Act are correct? (In case of dispute, according to precedents) (a) In the case where a British national murdered an American on a vessel of the Republic of Korea operating in the territorial waters of the United States, the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea applies. (b) In the case where a Japanese national forged a U.S. $100 banknote in China for the purpose of uttering it, the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea applies. (c) Under the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea, the offense of kidnapping, enticement, and trafficking in persons also applies to a foreigner who committed the offense outside the territory of the Republic of Korea, except for its preparation and conspiracy. (d) In the case where a Chinese national, in order to enter the Republic of Korea, forged a passport application form kept at the Consulate of the Republic of Korea located in China, the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea applies under the protective principle. (e) With respect to a person who has had all or part of a sentence executed abroad by reason of an offense, the sentence may be mitigated or remitted.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DO5010]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Judgment on the Prosecutor’s Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nWith respect to the application of the Criminal Act, Article 2 of the same Act provides that it applies to nationals and foreigners who commit crimes within the territory of the Republic of Korea, and the main clause of Article 6 of the same Act provides that it applies to foreigners who commit, outside the territory of the Republic of Korea, crimes other than those listed in Article 5 of the same Act against the Republic of Korea or a national of the Republic of Korea. The interior of the Consulate of the Republic of Korea located in Beijing, China, still belongs to Chinese territory and cannot be regarded as falling within the territory of the Republic of Korea, nor is it obvious that the crime of forging private documents constitutes a crime committed against the Republic of Korea or a national of the Republic of Korea under Article 6 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\nTherefore, the court below’s determination that it had no jurisdiction over the Defendant on the indictment alleging that a Defendant who was not a national of the Republic of Korea forged, within that Consulate, one passport application form in the name of a person other than the accused, on the ground that this constituted an extraterritorial offense by a foreigner, is correct, and there is no error, such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning jurisdiction, as argued in the grounds for final appeal. The grounds for final appeal cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. Judgment on the Defendant’s Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nIn this case, in which a sentence lighter than 10 years’ imprisonment was imposed, the argument that the sentencing is improper does not constitute a lawful ground for final appeal. The argument in the final appeal on this point is also without merit.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all final appeals are dismissed, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court who participated, as stated in the order."}

question: Which of the following statements regarding the offense of interference with business is incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: If it is not the performance of the business itself but only the propriety or fairness of the business that has been obstructed, the offense of interference with business is not established.
B: If brokerage business operated by a person who is not a licensed real estate agent is obstructed by force, the offense of interference with business is not established.
C: In order for the offense of interference with business by disruption of computer, etc. under Article 314(2) of the Criminal Act to be established, an actual disturbance to information processing is required; however, so long as a risk has arisen that the result of interference with business will occur by causing a disturbance to information processing, the offense is established even if the result of interference with business did not actually occur.
D: With respect to the act of, in the civil complaint office of the National Police Agency, complainants demanding an interview with the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency in connection with the handling of a petition case, and shouting abuse at and causing a disturbance toward police officers who were restraining them, the offense of interference with business is not established.
E: The offense of interference with business by force may be established even where the victim's free will was not actually suppressed by the force.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DO6599]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. The judgment of the court below  \\nBased on the evidence it admitted, the court below found that the Defendant, without obtaining the consent of the Victim, filed a report of closure concerning the licensed real estate brokerage office at issue in this case, which was registered under the Defendant’s name but was in fact being principally operated by the Victim, who was the Defendant’s business partner; then, on the grounds that the Victim’s operation of the licensed real estate brokerage office could not be regarded as unlawful, and that even if, as the Defendant alleged, the Victim intended to operate the licensed real estate brokerage office unilaterally, such circumstance alone did not suffice to find that the illegality was so grave that it had an antisocial nature reaching the level of being utterly intolerable in social life, the court below determined that the Defendant, by abusing the status of having the licensed real estate brokerage office registered in his name and arbitrarily filing a report of closure, obstructed the Victim’s business by force.\\n\\n2. The judgment of this Court  \\nHowever, the foregoing determination of the court below is difficult to endorse for the following reasons.\\n\\nA. The “business” protected under the offense of interference with business under the Criminal Act means an occupation, or work or business engaged in continuously, and must be something worthy of protection under criminal law from another person’s unlawful infringement; therefore, where a certain work or activity itself bears an antisocial nature to such an extent that its illegality is grave and it is utterly intolerable in social life, it cannot be regarded as “business” protected under the offense of interference with business (see Supreme Court Decision 2001DO2015, rendered on November 30, 2001).\\n\\nB. Under the former Real Estate Brokerage Act (before its full amendment by Act No. 7638 of July 29, 2005; hereinafter referred to only as the “Act”), Article 4 and Article 5 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act, only a licensed real estate agent or a juristic person whose officers are licensed real estate agents or brokers may obtain registration for the establishment of a brokerage office, and Article 38(1)1 of the Act provides that a person who engages in brokerage business without obtaining registration for the establishment of a brokerage office shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 20,000,000 won, while Article 38(2)3 of the Act provides that a person who transfers or lends to another person, or acquires or borrows from another person, a brokerage business registration certificate or a licensed real estate agent certificate shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10,000,000 won; accordingly, the act of engaging in brokerage business by a person who is not a licensed real estate agent, etc. is an act prohibited by the Act and constitutes a criminal act subject to criminal punishment.\\n\\nC. According to the record, the Victim, being a person who was not a licensed real estate agent, requested the Defendant, who was a licensed real estate agent, to lend his licensed real estate agent certificate, but the Defendant refused; thereafter, the Victim invested capital and the Defendant provided his certificate, while they agreed to operate as business partners by having the Defendant commute directly to the brokerage office at issue in this case and review the final documents concerning real estate contracts, and then completed registration for the establishment of the brokerage office under the Defendant’s name; after that, the Victim, contrary to the foregoing agreement, requested the Defendant not to make final confirmation of the real estate documents and to entrust his seal stamp to the Victim, which led to a dispute, and the Defendant came to file a report of closure concerning the brokerage office at issue in this case. From this, it can be seen that the business partnership relationship between the Defendant and the Victim concerning the operation of the brokerage office at issue in this case was terminated due to the Victim’s own fault, and since the Defendant, who was a licensed real estate agent, had decided to discontinue the real estate brokerage business at issue in this case upon termination of the partnership relationship, the Victim’s brokerage business, being that of a person who was not a licensed real estate agent, is an act prohibited by the Act and constitutes a criminal act subject to criminal punishment, and, as such, falls within a case bearing an antisocial nature to such an extent that it is utterly intolerable in social norms, and therefore cannot be regarded as “business” protected under the offense of interference with business.\\n\\nD. Nevertheless, the judgment of the court below, on the ground that even if the Victim had intended to operate the licensed real estate brokerage office unilaterally, such circumstance alone did not suffice to find that the illegality was so grave that it had an antisocial nature reaching the level of being utterly intolerable in social life, held that the Defendant, by abusing the status of having his name registered and arbitrarily filing a report of closure, obstructed the Victim’s business by force. In so doing, the judgment of the court below contains an error of law by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the business that is protected under the offense of interference with business, and such error affected the outcome of the judgment; therefore, the appellant’s argument pointing out this issue is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, without needing to examine the remaining grounds for appeal, the judgment of the court below shall be reversed and the case remanded to the court below, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2008DO11978]": "We decide the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\nThe court of original instance, based on the statements of the witness, the non-indicted person, as recorded in the transcript of the fifth trial session in the court of original instance, etc., found the Defendant guilty of the charged facts that, as stated in the judgment, the Defendant interfered with the search service operations of NHN Co., Ltd. and Daum Communications Co., Ltd.\\n\\nHowever, among the statements of the witness, the non-indicted person, as recorded in the transcript of the fifth trial session in the court of original instance, the part stating that “the witness confirmed that ranking manipulation was being carried out in the same manner through IP address 211.43.217.55” is a statement concerning facts experienced by that witness and thus cannot be said to be hearsay evidence, whereas the part stating that “the Defendant was confirmed to be using the above IP address” is content heard from the prosecutor and therefore constitutes hearsay evidence; accordingly, unless the Defendant agrees to its use as evidence, it is in principle inadmissible as evidence pursuant to Article 310-2 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nTherefore, the court of original instance’s adoption as evidence of the entire statement of the witness, the non-indicted person, as recorded in the transcript of the fifth trial session in the court of original instance, including the part constituting hearsay evidence, was erroneous; however, even according to the remaining evidence adopted by the court of original instance, the admissibility of which is recognized (including the written reply to the fact inquiry prepared by the Head of the Korea Internet Data Center), there is sufficient basis to find that the Defendant used IP address 211.43.217.55, and thus the court of original instance’s finding the charged facts of the offense of interference with business by hindering computers, etc. guilty is ultimately justifiable, so the above error by the court of original instance does not affect the conclusion of the judgment.\\n\\n2. With respect to Ground 2 of the grounds for appeal\\nArticle 314(2) of the Criminal Act provides for punishment of “a person who, by damaging a computer or other information-processing device, or special media records such as electronic records, or by inputting false information or an unlawful command into an information-processing device, or by any other means, causes an obstacle to information processing and thereby interferes with another’s business”; to constitute the above offense, it is required that, as a result of such act of infringement, the information-processing device fails to perform its function in accordance with its intended purpose or performs a function different from its intended purpose, thereby actually causing an obstacle to information processing (see Supreme Court Decision 2002DO631, rendered on July 9, 2004), but once a risk arises of causing an obstacle to information processing and thereby resulting in interference with business, the above offense is established even if the result of interference with business does not in fact occur.\\n\\nAccordingly, if false click information is transmitted to the statistics aggregation system server of a portal site operator and, in the process of determining search rankings, the false click information so transmitted is actually reflected in the statistics, thereby actually causing an obstacle to information processing, then the offense of interference with business by hindering computers, etc. is established even if this does not in fact cause any change in the search rankings.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence admitted by it and finding the facts stated in the judgment, held that the Defendant’s act of transmitting false click information to the statistics aggregation system server of the portal site operator constitutes inputting false information or an unlawful command, and that since the false click information transmitted by the Defendant was reflected in the statistics, an obstacle to information processing actually occurred, and the victims’ search service provision operations should be deemed to have been interfered with; on that basis, the court below found all of the charged facts of interference with business by hindering computers, etc. against the Defendant guilty.\\n\\nUpon examination in light of the above legal principle and the record, the above factual finding and determination by the court below are proper, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality of factual error, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, or any misapprehension of the legal principle concerning the causal relationship for the occurrence of an obstacle to information processing.\\n\\n3. With respect to Ground 3 of the grounds for appeal\\nUpon examining the evidence lawfully admitted by the court below in light of the record, the court below’s finding the Defendant guilty of the offense against Daum Communications Co., Ltd. is proper. Since there is no illegality in the judgment of the court below in violation of the rules governing the weighing of evidence, the argument in the grounds for appeal, which merely criticizes the selection of evidence or the finding of facts, matters within the exclusive authority of the court below as the trier of fact, cannot constitute a lawful ground for appeal or is otherwise unacceptable.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2008DO9049]": "We consider together the grounds for appeal filed by the Defendant and the court-appointed defense counsel.\\n\\n1. As to the point of violation of the Act on Assemblies and Demonstrations\\nThe Act on Assemblies and Demonstrations provides that a person who intends to organize an outdoor assembly or demonstration must notify the chief of the competent police station in advance of certain matters, thereby enabling the chief of the competent police station, based on such notification, to ascertain in advance the nature and scale of the outdoor assembly or demonstration and to make advance measures for maintaining public peace and order by protecting lawful outdoor assemblies or demonstrations while preventing infringement upon the interests of others or the community through outdoor assemblies or demonstrations (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DO315, decided April 27, 2004, etc.), and it cannot be said that the above notification duty is waived merely because the opinion sought to be expressed through an outdoor assembly or demonstration is legitimate (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 90DO870, decided August 14, 1990, etc.).\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the court below's determination, for the reasons stated in its opinion, to find the Defendant guilty of this part of the facts charged is proper, and there is no illegality such as a violation of the rules of evidence, incomplete examination, or misapprehension of legal principles, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n2. As to the point of obstruction of business\\nThe crime of obstruction of business under Article 314(1) of the Criminal Act is an offense established when a person obstructs another's business by disseminating false facts or by other deceit or force, and its protected legal interest lies in protecting a person's social and economic activities through business. However, the Criminal Act separately provides, as one of the \"Crimes Concerning Obstruction of Public Duties,\" the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties for acts that obstruct a public official's performance of duties by force, intimidation, or deceit (Article 136(1), Article 137), and its protected legal interest lies in protecting the functions of the State or public institutions concretely carried out by public officials.\\nIn this way, the crime of obstruction of business and the crime of obstruction of performance of official duties differ not only in their protected legal interests and protected objects, but also in that the types of conduct constituting obstruction of performance of official duties are more limited than those constituting obstruction of business. In light of these points, the fact that the Criminal Act separately provides for the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties apart from the offense of obstruction of business should be understood as meaning that, by distinguishing private business from public duties, only in cases where, with respect to public duties, execution is obstructed by force, intimidation, or deceit against a public official will punishment be imposed; accordingly, it is proper to construe that acts obstructing public duties performed by a public official in the course of duty cannot be charged as obstruction of business (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2009DO4166, decided November 19, 2009).\\nThe court below, by comprehensively considering the evidence stated in its opinion, affirmed the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged of obstruction of business guilty on the ground that the Defendant, together with First-instance Co-defendant 2, caused a disturbance by scattering horse manure on the desk and floor of the Civil Complaints Office of the National Police Agency and shouting, thereby obstructing police officers' duties of receiving civil petitions by force; however, in light of the legal principles discussed above, the court below's determination misapprehended the law concerning the scope within which the crime of obstruction of business is established, and it is clear that this affected the outcome of the judgment. The assertion in the grounds for appeal including this point is well-founded.\\n3. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the portion of the court below's judgment concerning obstruction of business must be reversed; since the court below treated this offense as a concurrent offense under the first sentence of Article 37 of the Criminal Act together with the remaining offenses and imposed a single sentence, the entire judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the case, as stated in the order."}

{"[2009DO8506]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. The lower appellate court, in this case where it was recognized that, in connection with the hiring work for new employees in 2008 by ○○ City Fisheries Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as “the Cooperative at issue”), the employees described in the judgment who were involved in grading the written examination pursuant to the instructions of the Defendant, the president of the Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as “the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue”), manipulated the scores by newly preparing the written-examination answer sheets of Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2, who had applied for the restricted competitive recruitment portion, and thereby caused Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2 to pass the recruitment examination, held, in view of the various circumstances as stated in the judgment, that since both the Defendant and the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue had all conspired in or acquiesced to the above score manipulation act (hereinafter referred to as “the score manipulation at issue”), it could not be deemed that the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue or the Cooperative at issue had been deceived, and therefore the score manipulation at issue did not constitute “deception” in the offense of obstruction of business by deceptive means; and, on the other hand, on the grounds that, in the interview examination conducted for those who passed the written examination, there was no procedure to verify the written-examination scores or reconfirm the evaluation contents of the written examination, and that, in the case of restricted competitive recruitment limited to the children of members, the interview examination was conducted merely as a formality by hiring all interview candidates unless special circumstances existed, it also could not be deemed that the interview duties of some interview panel members who did not know of the score manipulation at issue were obstructed, the lower appellate court rejected all of the prosecutor’s grounds of appeal and affirmed the first-instance judgment that had acquitted the Defendant of the facts charged in this case.\\n\\n2. However, the lower appellate court’s determination is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nIn the offense of Obstruction of Business by deceptive means, deception means that a person employs and takes advantage of inducing the other party to make a mistake, be confused, or be unaware, in order to achieve the purpose of the act, and the establishment of the offense of obstruction of business does not require that the result of obstruction of business actually occur; it is sufficient if a risk of causing such a result arises, and the offense of obstruction of business is established even where not the performance of the business itself but the propriety or fairness of the business is obstructed (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2006DO1721 rendered on January 17, 2008).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the lower court judgment, when Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2, who applied for new employee recruitment at the Cooperative at issue, received scores below the passing line in the written examination, the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue, pursuant to the Defendant’s instructions, caused Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2 to pass the written examination through the score manipulation at issue, thereby enabling them to take the interview examination conducted for those who passed the written examination. In such a case, if the score manipulation at issue enabled Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2, who would not have been qualified to take the interview examination based on the unmanipulated written-examination scores, to take the interview examination, then the score manipulation at issue constitutes deception that causes the interview panel members to make a mistake, be confused, or be unaware as to whether the examinees are lawfully qualified, and, unless there are special circumstances such as the interview panel members having conspired in or acquiesced to the score manipulation at issue, it must be deemed that the propriety or fairness of the interview duties performed by the interview panel members was impaired by such deception.\\n\\nEven if the interview duties are of a passive nature, serving only to determine whether a person will ultimately pass or fail, and even if they were performed in a merely formal manner, they cannot be said to be business that lacks protectable value in relation to the Cooperative at issue. Moreover, by the score manipulation at issue, the interview panel members were made to conduct interviews with persons lacking qualification to take the examination, while persons who did possess the corresponding qualification to take the examination were unable to be interviewed; the very fact itself impairs the propriety or fairness of the interview duties, and because such a result occurs regardless of whether the performance of the interview duties was passive or formal, it cannot be said that there was no obstruction of the interview duties.\\n\\nIf that is so, in this case where there is no material in the record from which it can be deemed that some of the interview panel members conspired in or acquiesced to the score manipulation at issue, the interview duties performed by them as part of the new employee recruitment work of the Cooperative at issue must be deemed to have been obstructed by the score manipulation at issue.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower appellate court, finding otherwise and holding that there was no such obstruction of business, merely affirmed the first-instance judgment that had acquitted the Defendant of the facts charged in this case. Thus, there is an illegality that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles on obstruction of business by deceptive means. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the judgment of the lower appellate court is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower appellate court for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2021DO9055]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Part concerning violation of the Act on Punishment of Violences, etc. (joint trespass to a residence)\\n\\na. The crime of trespass to a residence protects the peace and tranquility of a de facto residence as its protected legal interest. Since the act element of trespass in the crime of trespass to a residence must be interpreted in relation to the protected legal interest of the crime of trespass to a residence, trespass means entering a residence in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace of the residence, and, as a general rule, whether it constitutes trespass is to be determined based on the objectively and externally manifested manner of the act at the time of entry. If a person enters a residence in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace, this will generally be contrary to the resident’s intent, but it cannot be said to constitute trespass merely on the basis of the subjective circumstance that the act of simply entering the residence itself is contrary to the resident’s intent (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2020DO12630, rendered on September 9, 2021). Accordingly, whether the act constitutes trespass must be determined not by whether it is contrary to the resident’s intent, but by whether it is a manner of act that disturbs the actual state of peace.\\n\\nWhere an actor enters a residence with the resident’s consent, but the entry is for the purpose of committing a crime, etc., or where it is recognized that the resident would not have consented to the entry had the resident known the actor’s actual purpose of entry, in order for the actor’s entry to constitute the trespass prescribed in the crime of trespass to a residence, it must be evaluated, in light of the objectively and externally manifested manner of the act at the time of the actor’s entry, by comprehensively considering such circumstances as the form, use, and nature of the residence to be entered, the mode and status of control and management of entry by outsiders, and the circumstances and method of the actor’s entry, that the actual state of peace of the residence was infringed (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2017DO18272, rendered on March 24, 2022; Supreme Court Decision 2021DO7087, rendered on June 16, 2022, etc.).\\n\\nAccordingly, if a person enters, by an ordinary method, a building that is generally open and freely accessible, in a state where there is no restriction or interference by the manager as to entry, it cannot be deemed that the person entered the building in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace, and therefore such conduct does not constitute the act of trespass prescribed in the crime of trespass to a building (see Supreme Court Decision 2022DO2907, rendered on May 12, 2022; Supreme Court Decision 2021DO7087, rendered on June 16, 2022, etc.).\\n\\nb. The facts charged in this part are that the Defendants, jointly, on May 28, 2020, at around 11:00 a.m., entered the second floor of the △△△△ ○○ branch through the main gate, against the victim’s intent, the victim being the branch manager of the △△△△ ○○ branch, in order to protest against the dismissals and transfer personnel orders to the representatives, etc. of △△△△ who visited the △△△△ ○○ branch in Seoul ○○ District, and thereby trespassed into a building.\\n\\nc. The court below, on the ground that the Defendants entered the △△△△ ○○ branch against the presumed intent of the manager and thereby disturbed the actual peace of the building, affirmed as it stood the first-instance court’s determination that found this part of the facts charged guilty.\\n\\nd. However, according to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts are established.\\n\\n1) The second-floor store of the △△△△ ○○ branch into which the Defendants, who were executives and union members of the Mart Industry Workers’ Union, entered is a place that is generally open without restrictions such as entry qualifications during business hours.\\n\\n2) The Defendants, as stated in the facts charged, entered the second-floor store by sequentially passing through the main gate and store entrance used by customers during business hours, but they did not take any special measures such as being restrained by security personnel or sneaking in when the security personnel were away.\\n\\ne. In light of the foregoing facts in conjunction with the legal principles discussed above, once it is seen that the Defendants entered, by an ordinary method, the store of the △△△△ ○○ branch, which is generally open and freely accessible, in a state where there was no restriction or interference by the manager as to entry, it cannot be deemed that they entered in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace, and therefore this does not constitute the act of trespass prescribed in the crime of trespass to a building. The explicit intent of the manager of the △△△△ ○○ branch to prohibit entry has not been confirmed, and even if the Defendants’ act of entering the store of the △△△△ ○○ branch, as charged in this part, was contrary to the manager’s presumed intent, such circumstance alone cannot be assessed as an entry made in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace. Therefore, the crime of trespass to a building is not established against the Defendants.\\n\\nf. Nevertheless, the court below’s determination, which recognized the establishment of the crime of trespass to a building on the main ground that the manager’s presumed intent existed, contains an error that misapprehended the legal principles regarding the establishment of the offense and affected the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing this out is well taken.\\n\\n2. Part concerning obstruction of business\\n\\na. The “force” in the crime of obstruction of business means any power sufficient to suppress or confuse a person’s free will, regardless of whether it is tangible or intangible; it is not necessary that the victim’s free will be actually suppressed, but it must be of such degree that, in light of the offender’s arrogance, number of persons, surrounding circumstances, etc., it is sufficient to suppress the victim’s free will. Whether it constitutes such force must be determined objectively by considering all circumstances, including the time and place of the offense, the motive and purpose of the offense, the number of persons, the manner of the force, the type of business, and the status of the victim, etc. (see Supreme Court Decision 2016DO10956, rendered on October 27, 2016, etc.), and it is not determined by the will of the victim, etc.\\n\\nb. The facts charged in this part are that the Defendants, who entered the second-floor store of the △△△△ ○○ branch as above, jointly, by holding placards bearing the words “unfair dismissal,” and by following the victim (the branch manager of the ○○ branch) and the officers and employees of △△△△, including the representative director (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “victim, etc.”), and shouting loudly, “Stop forced transfers, stop integrated operation, employees are suffering, stop unfair dismissal,” obstructed the victim’s on-site inspection duties for about 30 minutes by force.\\n\\nc. The court below, on the ground that the first-instance court’s determination that a number of Defendants, while holding placards in the store, continuously followed the victim, etc., shouted loudly, and recorded this by camera, constituted the exercise of force sufficient to suppress the victim’s free will, affirmed as it stood the first-instance court’s determination that found this part of the facts charged guilty.\\n\\nd. However, according to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts are established.\\n\\n1) The acts as charged occurred at around 11:00 a.m. on a weekday in the food sales area of a large mart, and the Defendants, who were union executives and union members who had heard that the officers and employees, including the representative director of △△△△, were coming to conduct an on-site inspection of the △△△△ ○○ branch (some of them had been discharged several months earlier for failing to comply with transfer personnel orders), sought to directly request the representative director to reinstate them and to withdraw the transfer personnel orders in relation to the dismissals and transfer personnel orders, etc.\\n\\n2) The persons who carried out the acts as charged were all seven of the Defendants, of whom four were women, and among the three men, one was in his 50s. On the other hand, the number of persons who participated in the on-site inspection of the store at that time was more than about 20, including the victim, etc., and most of them, including the representative director, were senior-level management.\\n\\n3) While the Defendants followed the victim, etc., who were performing inspection work in the food sales area, they stood in the surrounding area holding placards at a distance of about 1 to 2 meters or more, or shouted, “Please stop forced transfers,” “I want to work,” and the like, but the victim, etc. continued the on-site inspection work for about 30 minutes.\\n\\n4) Defendant 2 filmed the activities of the other Defendants in order to inform the union members, and did not intend to film the appearance of the victim, etc.\\n\\ne. In light of the foregoing facts in conjunction with the legal principles discussed above, it is difficult to conclude that the Defendants, jointly, exercised force sufficient to suppress the free will of the victim, etc. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\n1) Whether the Defendants’ acts were sufficient to suppress the victim’s free will must be determined objectively by considering not only the victim’s will or statements, but also the manner of the Defendants’ acts, the number of Defendants, their sex and age, and the number and status of the victim’s side, etc.\\n\\n2) While carrying out the acts as charged, the Defendants stood holding placards at a distance of about 1 to 2 meters or more from the victim, etc., and followed them according to the victim’s, etc. progress, but they did not approach the victim, etc. any closer, nor did they physically block the victim’s, etc. progress or work.\\n\\n3) The Defendants did not use abusive language or threats toward the victim, etc., and contrary to the facts charged, they even used honorific speech while shouting their demands. There is also no objective evidence to the effect that the voices of the Defendants were noise sufficient to make it difficult for the victim’s on-site inspection work in the food sales area of a large mart where many customers visit and sales promotion events are also held.\\n\\n4) The Defendants were seeking, on the occasion of being able to meet directly the representative director who possessed decision-making authority over personnel policy and discretionary authority over personnel matters, to protest the dismissals and transfer personnel orders, etc., or to request reinstatement and withdrawal of the transfer personnel orders, and it cannot be said that they carried out the acts as charged with the intent to obstruct or suspend the management work of the ○○ branch of the victim, who is the branch manager of the △△△△ ○○ branch.\\n\\n5) Notwithstanding the Defendants’ acts as charged, the representative director’s on-site inspection work proceeded for about 30 minutes.\\n\\n6) In the court below, counsel for the Defendants also argued that, at other branches of △△△△, union members carried out similar activities in line with the representative director’s on-site inspection schedule, but no separate measures such as criminal complaints were taken there.\\n\\nf. Nevertheless, the court below’s determination, which recognized the establishment of the crime of obstruction of business on the view that the Defendants exercised “force,” contains an error that misapprehended the legal principles concerning “force” in the crime of obstruction of business and affected the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing this out is well taken.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nThe judgment below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning crimes of omission are incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents) (a) Since the duty to act must be a legal duty, a legal duty to act is recognized where it arises from statutes, legal acts, or prior conduct, but where only a duty to act is expected under the principle of good faith and fair dealing, social norms, or the principles of reason, a legal duty to act cannot be recognized. (b) The intent for an improper omission offense must necessarily include a purpose or planned intent to commit the offense with respect to the occurrence of the constituent result. (c) The crime of breach of trust in the course of business can also be established by omission, and in order for such omission to be regarded as commencement of execution, the omission must occur in a situation in which, if the duty to act is not fulfilled, it is objectively foreseeable that the person who conferred the duty of handling affairs would be unable to exercise property rights, and the risk of the occurrence of the constituent result has become concrete. (d) In the sale of a used automobile, since the seller's installment debt to the installment finance company or guarantee insurer is automatically succeeded to by the buyer, failing to notify the buyer of the existence of that installment debt constitutes deception by omission. (e) Co-principal liability among crimes of omission is established only when a common duty is imposed on multiple offenders by omission and when that duty can be performed jointly.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2008DO89]": "Article 3(1), first sentence, of the Public Health Control Act provides that “a person who intends to engage in a public health business shall equip the facilities and equipment prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare for each type of public health business and shall report to the Mayor, County Governor, or District Head,” and Article 20(1) item 1 provides that it punishes “a person who has not made the report pursuant to the provisions of the first sentence of Article 3(1)”; in light of the form and purport of those provisions, a violation of the Public Health Control Act resulting from a breach of the duty to report should be regarded as a true omission offense, the constituent elements of which can be realized only by omission, and, meanwhile, co-perpetration among omission offenses should be regarded as established only when a common duty is imposed upon multiple omission offenders and that duty can be performed in common. And the duty to report for a public health business is imposed upon “a person who intends to engage in a public health business,” and here, the phrase “a person who engages in business” means a person who is the subject to whom rights and obligations arising from the business accrue; therefore, it is reasonable to interpret that, in the case of an employee or assistant of the business operator, such person is not included within “a person who engages in business.”\\n\\nThe court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence it adopted and recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion, determined that the Defendants, who held the position of manager at each branch of the company Care Korea in this case (trade name omitted), were merely wage earners of the said company and were not the subject to whom the rights and obligations arising from the business belonged, and thus did not fall within the category of persons burdened with the duty to report under the said provision; and further determined that, unless the Defendants were given a common duty to report, co-perpetration of the offense of violation of the Public Health Control Act resulting from a failure to report, which is a true omission offense, could not be established. In light of the legal principle discussed above, the court below’s determination as such is correct, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality of misapprehension of law as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the Disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2015DO15227]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nWhere a person who bears a legal duty to act to prevent the occurrence of a result infringing a legally protected interest prohibited by the Criminal Act can easily prevent the occurrence of that result by performing that duty, yet, having tolerated and stood by the occurrence of the result, fails to perform the duty, if such failure to act is deemed to be conduct of execution of the crime, he may be punished as an omission offense. Here, the duty to act is recognized not only where it arises from statutes, legal acts, or prior conduct, but also where, under the principle of good faith and fair dealing, social norms, or as a matter of reason, a duty to act is expected (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2007DO9354 rendered on February 28, 2008).\\n\\nThe court below held that the Defendant, as an employee managing the store at the store in this case, had a duty, within the possible scope, to immediately remove any danger if it arose in the above store, and that, given the form of the Defendant's work, at a time when working hours and rest hours were not clearly distinguished, while smoking with A in the passage next to the store in this case, where the Defendant had usually been in charge of cleaning and other management, the Defendant witnessed A throw a cigarette butt whose embers had not been completely extinguished toward the side where there was plastic for packaging clothes that was easily combustible and then enter the store; accordingly, the court below determined that the Defendant had a duty to act under the employment contract or as a matter of reason to check whether embers remained in the above cigarette butt and to eliminate the danger, but, by negligence in leaving the scene without performing that duty, caused the plastic, etc. to catch fire and spread the fire to the occupied building, including the store in this case, thereby committing the offense of negligent fire setting.\\n\\nThe court below, considering the contents of the Defendant's employment contract, the time and place where the fire in this case occurred, the Defendant's usual duties, the circumstances leading to the outbreak of the fire, and the ease of the act for preventing infringement of a legally protected interest, determined that the Defendant, at the time the fire in this case occurred, had, as a duty under the principle of good faith and fair dealing pursuant to the employment contract, a duty to act to check whether embers remained in the cigarette butt and eliminate the danger, but failed to perform it and thereby committed the offense of negligent fire setting; this is in accordance with the legal principle stated above, and therefore the allegation in the grounds of appeal that the law concerning the guarantor status of an offense by improper omission was misunderstood cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAccordingly, the appeal is dismissed, and, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, judgment is rendered as stated in the order."}
{"[2015DO6809]": "All appeals are dismissed."}

{"[2020DO15529]": "The grounds of appeal are determined (supplementary briefs on the grounds of appeal submitted after the filing period for the statement of grounds of appeal are considered only to the extent that they supplement it).\\n\\n1. Summary of the Charged Facts\\n\\nThe summary of the charged facts is as follows.\\n\\nThe Defendant is a person who carried out the overall work necessary for the progress of the instant project, including the formulation of the replotting plan, for the Goyang Siksa District Urban Development Project Association (hereinafter referred to as the “Victim Association”), which was promoting an urban development project by the land readjustment method (hereinafter referred to as the “instant project”) in an area of 989,377 square meters in and around (address omitted), Goyang City (hereinafter referred to as the “instant project area”).\\n\\nAround Aug. 30, 2011, the amendment to the urban development and implementation plans concerning the instant project was approved (the implementation plan as amended in this manner is hereinafter referred to as the “2011 Implementation Plan”). As a result, the development method for the public open space between part of the land scheduled for replotting within the instant project area (land referred to as “Zone C”; hereinafter referred to as the “instant land scheduled for replotting”) and the major road (daero) was changed from a “screened type,” in which access to buildings on the land scheduled for replotting was substantially blocked, to an “open type,” in which such access was easy, and accordingly the economic value of the instant land scheduled for replotting increased. Therefore, the Defendant had an occupational duty, pursuant to the relevant statutes, to take measures such as reappraisal of the instant land scheduled for replotting, amendment of the replotting plan, and redesignation of the land scheduled for replotting, so that the Victim Association could reflect the increase in value of the instant land scheduled for replotting in the settlement procedure and collect an appropriate settlement money.\\n\\nNevertheless, by failing to take measures such as reappraisal of the instant land scheduled for replotting immediately after the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, the Defendant intended to allow his relatives by blood or marriage, acquaintances, and others who were to receive replotting of the instant land scheduled for replotting to obtain the benefit of the increase in land value, and to cause the Victim Association to suffer damage in the amount of KRW 3,470,766,900, which is the aggregate amount of the aforesaid increase in land value, but this remained at the stage of an attempt because the Victim Association proceeded with the procedure for an application for approval of an amendment to the replotting plan around May 2016.\\n\\n2. The Court of Appeals’ Judgment\\n\\nFor the following reasons, the court below reversed the first-instance judgment, which had found the instant charged facts not guilty, and found them guilty.\\n\\nThe Defendant, as a person who was entrusted with and entirely handled the affairs of the Victim Association, had the duty to appropriately assess the increase in value resulting from changes in the appraisal factors for the instant land scheduled for replotting and to enable the Victim Association to collect an appropriate settlement money. With respect to the above work, the Defendant was most familiar with it through active involvement, and it was difficult for others to easily confirm it.\\n\\nHowever, by resigning from Non-party 1 Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Non-party 1 Company”), which had been performing work concerning the instant project on behalf of the Victim Association, on Dec. 31, 2011, without fulfilling such duty or handing over the relevant matters to his successor and while remaining silent, the Defendant caused a situation in which the Victim Association, without recognizing the necessity of such reappraisal for several years, was exposed to the risk of failing to properly undergo the settlement procedure. The Defendant’s such omission was committed while recognizing that it could confer economic benefits on himself, his relatives by blood or marriage, and acquaintances who had received replotting concentrated in the main area of the project, and cause damage to the Victim Association. Therefore, it is proper to recognize that the Defendant had commenced the execution of the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty.\\n\\n3. The Supreme Court’s Judgment\\n\\nThe judgment of the court below cannot be upheld for the following reasons.\\n\\na. The crime of breach of trust in the course of duty is established when a person who handles another’s affairs, by an act in violation of his occupational duty, acquires pecuniary benefits or causes a third party to acquire such benefits, thereby causing damage to that other person (Articles 356 and 355(2) of the Criminal Act). Article 18 of the Criminal Act provides, with respect to the requirements for the establishment of an offense by omission, that “a person who has a duty to prevent the occurrence of danger or who, by his own act, has caused the source of danger to arise, shall be punished by the resulting consequence if he fails to prevent the occurrence of such danger.”\\n\\nThe crime of breach of trust in the course of duty may also be established by omission of a person who, in a relationship of trust with another, has a legal duty to handle affairs in accordance with a certain mandate, by failing to perform an act that is legally required in the circumstances (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision of Nov. 29, 2012, 2012DO10139). In order for such omission to be regarded as the commencement of execution, the omission must occur in a situation where the risk of the occurrence of the constitutive result has been concretized, for example, where it can be objectively foreseen that, if the duty to act is not performed, the person who entrusted the handling of affairs will be unable to exercise property rights. And the actor must have recognized, at the time of omission, that he was violating the duty assigned to him and that there was a risk of damage arising from such omission.\\n\\nb. According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the duly admitted evidence, the following circumstances can be found.\\n\\nDuring the process of promoting the instant project, a disagreement arose between the Victim Association and Goyang City regarding the development method of the public open space in the instant case, and the development method of the public open space in the instant case emerged as one of the major issues of the instant project from the end of 2009. Therefore, the fact that the development plan for the public open space in the instant case was changed pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan was something that the executives of the Victim Association, who bore primary responsibility for the decision-making of the Victim Association, could sufficiently recognize.\\n\\nSince the development plan for the public open space in the instant case was changed pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, the fact that this necessitated a reappraisal of the value of the instant land scheduled for replotting is not something that only the Defendant could know. Moreover, even after the Defendant, around Dec. 31, 2011, lost his position to perform work concerning the instant project by resigning from the position of representative director of Non-party 1 Company, officers and employees including Non-party 2, a certified urban planning engineer, continued to work at Non-party 1 Company, and among them Non-party 3, who was mainly in charge of replotting work, was in a position to know, no less than the Defendant, that amendment of the replotting plan was necessary pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan.\\n\\nAround the time of the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, the Victim Association was suffering severe financial difficulties due to delays in the sale of reserve land, and in order to overcome such problems, it continuously promoted changes to the development plan and implementation plan concerning the instant project from around 2012 to around 2015. In light of this, it cannot be seen that, at the time of the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, there was an urgent situation in which, if the amendment of the replotting plan was not expedited, the replotting disposition would soon be made and the legal relations among the association members would be fixed.\\n\\nThe former Urban Development Work Guidelines (Directive No. 680) established by the Minister of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs contain the following: “If, during project implementation, the implementer needs to amend the replotting plan due to changes in public facilities or the determination of group reserve land, the replotting plan shall be amended immediately” (see Article 4-5-1). However, since the transfer of rights to land scheduled for replotting or the determination of settlement money is effected only upon a replotting disposition, it does not necessarily follow that the failure to take measures for amending the replotting plan “immediately” after the approval of the implementation plan will directly create a risk of adverse effects on the property relations of the Victim Association.\\n\\nc. When these circumstances are examined in light of the legal principles set forth in paragraph a. above, even if, as stated in the charged facts, the Defendant is deemed to have had a duty to act to take follow-up measures pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, it is difficult to view that the Defendant violated such duty to act in a situation where the risk that the Victim Association would fail to reflect the increase in value of the instant land scheduled for replotting in the settlement procedure had been concretized; accordingly, it cannot be said that the Defendant commenced the execution of the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty by omission.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below found the charged facts guilty on the ground that the Defendant had commenced the execution of the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty. The judgment of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal doctrine concerning the requirements for recognizing the commencement of execution in the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty by omission. The Defendant’s ground of appeal pointing this out is meritorious.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nWithout addressing the remaining grounds of appeal by the Defendant, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court."}

{"[98DO231]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe gist of the fraud charge against the Defendants, whom the court below found not guilty, is that the Defendants conspired to purchase vehicles on which installment payments remained and then sell those vehicles as if they were vehicles free of installment payments, thereby appropriating the purchase price, and that, although Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 had purchased the Credos passenger car from Nonindicted Person 1 and installment payments remained thereon, on February 21, 1997, Defendant 2, while impersonating Nonindicted Person 1, falsely told Victim Nonindicted Person 2 that there were no installment payments remaining on the above passenger car, and, thereby deceiving the victim, concluded on the spot a contract to sell the above passenger car for 9,500,000 won and received 9,500,000 won thereunder under the name of the purchase price, thereby obtaining it by fraud; and that, although Defendant 1 purchased an Avante passenger car from Nonindicted Person 3 for 1,000,000 won on condition that he assume the installment payments, on the 22nd of the same month Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 falsely told Victim Nonindicted Person 4 that there were no installment payments remaining on the above vehicle, and, thereby deceiving the victim, concluded on the spot a contract to sell the above passenger car for 6,000,000 won and received 6,000,000 won thereunder under the name of the purchase price, thereby obtaining it by fraud. According to the reasons stated in the judgment below, the court below held that even according to all the evidence adduced by the Prosecutor, there was no evidence to establish that the Defendants had conspired and lied to the victims that there were no installment payments remaining on the above Credos passenger car and Avante passenger car, concluded each vehicle sale contract with the victims thereby deceived, and received the sale proceeds and thereby obtained them by fraud, and accordingly rendered a judgment of not guilty on each of the above charges. Upon examination of the record, the above determination of the court below is acceptable, and there is also no evidence that the Defendants, in selling the above Credos passenger car to Nonindicted Person 2, impersonated Nonindicted Person 1. Therefore, the above determination of the court below cannot be said to be unlawful as a violation of the rules of evidence evaluation, as argued.\\n\\nOn the other hand, in a transactional relationship concerning property rights, if one party, knowing that by failing to notify the other party of some matter related to the transaction there may arise a risk that the rights to the contractual subject matter will not be secured in the future, nevertheless does not notify the other party of such matter, enters into the transaction, and receives delivery of property or obtains property benefits from the other party, and if it is clear from common experience that the other party would not have entered into the transaction had he or she been notified of such circumstances, then the recipient of the property has, under the principle of good faith, a duty to notify the other party of such circumstances, and the recipient’s failure to do so constitutes deceit by concealing a fact that should have been disclosed, and thus constitutes fraud (see Supreme Court Decision of September 25, 1984, 84DO882; Supreme Court Decision of March 12, 1985, 84DO93; Supreme Court Decision of December 24, 1991, 91DO2698, etc.). However, upon examination of the record, Defendant 1 purchased the above Credos passenger car from Nonindicted Person 1 and the above Avante passenger car from Nonindicted Person 3, each on condition that he assume the installment-payment debt, and when the Defendants sold them to Nonindicted Person 2 and Nonindicted Person 4, respectively, they are seen not to have notified them that there was an installment-payment debt; as to whether such act constitutes a fraudulent act by deceiving the other party in breach of a duty to notify, the record shows that Nonindicted Person 1 obtained financing from Nonindicted Person 5 Co., Ltd. and purchased the above Credos passenger car, thereby owing an installment-payment debt to Nonindicted Person 5 Co., Ltd., and that Nonindicted Person 3 purchased the above Avante passenger car by installment under the surety insurance coverage of a guarantee insurance company, but there appears to have been no circumstance such as that a mortgage had been created on the above Credos passenger car and Avante passenger car themselves, or that a provisional seizure had been executed thereon (see the entries in the respective motor vehicle registration registers at pages 25 and 284 of Book 5 of the investigation record). Nor is there any basis in the record to conclude that the installment-payment debt of Nonindicted Person 1 or Nonindicted Person 3 would naturally be assumed by the purchaser under a motor vehicle sale contract. If the circumstances are as such, then even if the former owners, Nonindicted Person 1 and Nonindicted Person 3, respectively, owed installment-payment debts in relation to the motor vehicles that were the subject matter of the sales, such fact would not create a risk that the purchasers of the vehicles, Nonindicted Person 2 and Nonindicted Person 4, would fail in the future to secure ownership of the vehicles that were the subject matter of the contract; therefore, it cannot be said that, had Nonindicted Person 2 or Nonindicted Person 4 been notified of the circumstance that such installment-payment debts existed, it would have been evident from common experience that they would not have purchased the respective vehicles. Accordingly, the Defendants cannot be said to have owed a duty to notify them thereof, and the Defendants’ such omission cannot be said to constitute a deceptive act.\\n\\nHowever, as to the point that Defendant 1, while purchasing the above Credos passenger car from Nonindicted Person 1 on condition that he assume Nonindicted Person 1’s installment-payment debt, deceived Nonindicted Person 1 and received Nonindicted Person 1’s seal, and without Nonindicted Person 1’s knowledge affixed a seal thereto on the power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle and forged it, and that the Defendants delivered and used it in selling the above Credos passenger car to Nonindicted Person 2, the court below found this guilty and that judgment was left undisturbed and became final. According to the record, the Defendants sold the above Credos passenger car to Nonindicted Person 2 while posing as agents of Nonindicted Person 1 (see the receipt on page 568 of the investigation record, case No. 1997 HYEONGJE29186 of the Seoul District Prosecutors’ Office), and if so, there may be suspicion that the Defendants, having no authority from Nonindicted Person 1 to sell the above Credos passenger car, deceived Nonindicted Person 2 by acting as if they had such authority, and that Nonindicted Person 2, deceived thereby, purchased the above Credos passenger car. However, on the other hand, Nonindicted Person 2 states that when purchasing the above Credos passenger car, he or she received, in addition to the above power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle, the seal certificate, motor vehicle inspection certificate, resident registration extract, compulsory insurance receipt, and other documents in Nonindicted Person 1’s name necessary for transfer registration (see the statement record of Nonindicted Person 2 prepared by the judicial police officer, page 91 of the above investigation record), and the record does not show how the Defendants came into possession of those documents (in the criminal complaint filed by Nonindicted Person 1 against the Defendants, Nonindicted Person 1 states that after selling the above Credos passenger car to Defendant 1, Defendant 1 said that he urgently needed the car, so without going through the procedure for succession to the installment-payment debt, Nonindicted Person 1 first delivered the above Credos passenger car, and that at the time of delivery he kept the seal certificate, motor vehicle inspection certificate, resident registration extract, compulsory insurance receipt, and other documents necessary for transfer registration inside the above passenger car, but later, thinking that nothing special would happen, he delivered the car as it was. However, that complaint was not adopted as evidence, and the Defendants deny such facts).\\n\\nIn addition, a fraud offense based on the allegation that, despite having no power of agency, the Defendants deceived Nonindicted Person 2 by posing as though they had such power of agency is different in its factual content from the fraud offense stated in the above indictment, and finding the Defendants guilty of fraud of such content without going through the procedure for amendment of the indictment would go beyond the scope of adjudication limited by the facts charged and would substantially infringe the Defendants’ right of defense, and thus cannot be permitted. Meanwhile, according to the record, Nonindicted Person 3 sold the above Avante passenger car to Defendant 1 on condition that Defendant 1 assume the installment-payment debt, and appears to have delivered the power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle and the seal certificate necessary for transfer registration before Defendant 1 went through the procedure to assume the installment-payment debt. There is no material in the record to ascertain in what form the Defendants sold the above Avante passenger car to Nonindicted Person 4, but considering that the ownership transfer registration for the above Avante passenger car was made directly from Nonindicted Person 3 to Nonindicted Person 4, it may also be presumed that the Defendants posed as agents of Nonindicted Person 3. Even though the manifestation of intent was defective due to deceit, it is appropriate to view that Nonindicted Person 3, by delivering the power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle and the seal certificate to Defendant 1, granted authority to sell the above Avante passenger car, and so long as such authority existed, even if the purchaser, Nonindicted Person 4, bought the above Avante passenger car believing that the Defendants had been granted authority by Nonindicted Person 3, there can be no mistake arising from deceit.\\n\\nIn the end, there can also be no legal error in misapprehension of law regarding fraud, as argued by the Prosecutor, in the judgment below. All arguments are without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices as follows."}

question: Which of the following statements regarding the case below is correct? (Where there is a dispute, the precedents are followed.) Party A climbed over a wall into a neighbor’s house with the intent to commit theft, but before he even had time to look for anything to steal, he was immediately discovered by A, who had just returned home. When A shouted, “Who are you?” and tried to seize him, Party A assaulted A in order to escape.
A: If the above case occurred during the daytime, the offense of attempted theft is established against Party A.
B: If the above case occurred during the daytime, even if Party A was carrying a knife with the intent to use it in the offense when he climbed over the wall and entered, if Party A did not actually use the knife when assaulting A, the offense of special residential intrusion or the offense of aggravated assault is not established.
