Case 2011HEONMA141\\n\\nPetitioner No ○ Min, on 2009. 7. 29., at the Seoul High Court, was sentenced to 3 years’ imprisonment for the offense of rape causing injury, and after that sentence became final, while he was confined in △△ Prison, on 2011. 3. 21., filed this constitutional complaint seeking a determination that Articles 5, 8, and 13 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional, alleging that they infringe his fundamental rights. While the Petitioner was confined in □□ Prison, on 2012. 11. 5., he refused the collection of a DNA sample by the warden of □□ Prison, who had been entrusted by a prosecutor with collecting a DNA sample pursuant to Article 5 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information; accordingly, on 2013. 1. 29., buccal epithelial cells, which are a DNA sample, were collected by execution of a DNA sample collection warrant.\\n\\nd. Case 2011HEONMA156\\n\\nPetitioner Ahn ○ Wook, on 2002. 3. 28., at the Seoul High Court, was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment for violations of the Act on the Punishment of Sexual Crimes and Protection of Victims, etc. (the offense of bodily injury caused by rape, etc.) and other crimes, and after that sentence became final, while he was confined in ○○ Prison, on 2010. 12. 7., he refused the collection of a DNA sample by the warden of ○○ Prison, who had been entrusted by a prosecutor with collecting a DNA sample pursuant to Article 5 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information; accordingly, on 2011. 1. 10., buccal epithelial cells, which are a DNA sample, were collected by execution of a DNA sample collection warrant. On 2011. 3. 25., the Petitioner filed this constitutional complaint, alleging that Article 2(1) of the Addenda of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information, which permits collection of DNA samples even from persons whose sentences have already become final and who are confined, infringes his fundamental rights.\\n\\ne. Case 2011HEONMA326\\n\\n(1) Petitioner Seo ○ Mun, on 2010. 3. 30., at the Pyeongtaek Branch of the Suwon District Court, was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months’ imprisonment with a 2-year suspended sentence for violations of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (the offense of refusal to leave premises in a group or armed with deadly weapons, etc.), violations of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (the offense of bodily injury in a group or armed with deadly weapons, etc.), and other crimes, based on criminal facts including that he, with the power of a multitude, remained in possession of a dangerous object, disregarded the victim’s demand to leave, and inflicted injury on the victim. After that sentence became final, when the prosecutor of the ○○ Branch Office of the Suwon District Prosecutors’ Office requested the Petitioner on 2011. 3. 18. to appear in order to collect DNA pursuant to the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information, the Petitioner appeared at the prosecutor’s office, consented to the collection of a DNA sample, and submitted to the collection of the DNA sample.\\n\\n(2) Petitioners Kim ○ Su, Cheon ○ Seok, Kim ○ Ho, and Kim ○ Hwan were, on 2009. 10. 28., at the Seoul Central District Court, sentenced by the Seoul High Court on 2010. 5. 31. to 4 years’ imprisonment each for violations of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (the offense of trespass into a residence in a group or armed with deadly weapons, etc.), violations of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (the offense of damaging property, etc. in a group or armed with deadly weapons, etc.), arson of general buildings, and other crimes, based on criminal facts including that they conspired jointly to intrude into a building by the power of a multitude, damaged property while displaying the power of a group or multitude or while carrying dangerous objects, and committed arson of a general building; after those sentences became final, Petitioner Kim ○ Su, while confined in △△ Prison, refused around 2011. 3. 12. the collection of a DNA sample by the warden of △△ Prison, who had been entrusted by a prosecutor with collecting a DNA sample, and accordingly, around 2011. 3. 31., a DNA sample was collected by execution of a DNA sample collection warrant; Petitioner Cheon ○ Seok, while confined in ▽▽ Prison, refused around 2011. 2. 15. and around 3. 14. the collection of a DNA sample, and accordingly, around 2011. 3. 22., it was collected by execution of a DNA sample collection warrant; Petitioner Kim ○ Ho, while confined in □□ Prison, refused around the beginning of 2011. 3. the collection of a DNA sample, and accordingly, on 2011. 3. 21., it was collected by execution of a DNA sample collection warrant; and Petitioner Kim ○ Hwan, while confined in ×× Prison, refused around the beginning of 2011. 3. the collection of a DNA sample, and accordingly, around 2011. 3. 24., it was collected by execution of a DNA sample collection warrant.\\n\\n(3) The above Petitioners, on 2011. 6. 16., filed this constitutional complaint seeking a determination that the act of collecting DNA samples and Articles 2, 5, 8, and 13 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional, alleging that they infringe the Petitioners’ fundamental rights.\\n\\nf. Case 2013HEONMA215\\n\\nPetitioner Kim ○ Gyu was sentenced on 2011. 9. 28., at the Anyang Branch of the Suwon District Court, to 6 months’ imprisonment with a 1-year suspended sentence for criminal facts including that he threatened the victim while holding a baseball bat, a dangerous object, and after that sentence became final, when he received a notice of appearance for DNA sample collection from the ○○ Branch Office of the Suwon District Prosecutors’ Office several times from around 2012. 2. 15., he filed this constitutional complaint on 2013. 4. 5., alleging that Article 5 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information infringes his fundamental rights.\\n\\ng. Case 2013HEONMA360\\n\\nPetitioner Kim ○ Young was sentenced on 2011. 10. 14., at the Seoul Central District Court, to 6 months’ imprisonment with a 2-year suspended sentence for criminal facts including trespass into a structure by the power of a multitude, and after that sentence became final, when the Seoul ○○ Prosecutors’ Office sent him a notice of appearance for DNA sample collection on 2013. 1. 31. and repeatedly telephoned him to request his appearance, he filed this constitutional complaint on 2013. 5. 21., alleging that the act of attempting to collect a DNA sample and Articles 2, 5, 8, and 13 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information infringe his fundamental rights.\\n\\n2. Case 2011HEONMA28\\n\\nPetitioner Kim ○ Ho seeks an adjudication on whether Article 5(1)6, Article 5(2), Article 6, Article 8, Article 10, Article 11, and Article 2(1) of the Addenda of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional. The subject matter of adjudication is the portions applicable to the Petitioner: ① among Article 5(1)6, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of bodily injury under Article 2(1)3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act committed while carrying a deadly weapon or other dangerous object under Article 3 of the Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act; ② among Article 8(1), the portion concerning persons subject to collection of DNA samples pursuant to Article 5; ③ Article 10(1); ④ Article 11(1); and ⑤ among Article 2(1) of the Addenda, the portion concerning persons who, having received and had finalized an actual sentence of imprisonment or confinement or more for offenses in concurrence with any offense falling under any item of Article 5(1), are confined. Case 2011HEONMA106\\n\\nPetitioner Seo ○ Hun seeks an adjudication on whether Articles 5, 6, and 9 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional. The remaining provisions are excluded from the subject matter of adjudication because they are either unrelated to the Petitioner (Article 6) or are merely procedural provisions and the Petitioner has not made any specific claim as to their unconstitutionality (Article 5(2), Article 9).\\n\\nc. Case 2011HEONMA141\\n\\nPetitioner No ○ Min seeks an adjudication on whether Articles 5, 8, and 13 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional. The subject matter of adjudication is the portions applicable to the Petitioner: ① among Article 5(1)4, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses under Article 301 of the Criminal Act; and ② among Article 8(1), the portion concerning persons subject to collection of DNA samples pursuant to Article 5. Case 2011HEONMA156\\n\\nPetitioner Ahn ○ Wook seeks an adjudication on whether Article 2(1) of the Addenda of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information is unconstitutional; accordingly, the subject matter of adjudication is the portion of Article 2(1) of the Addenda applicable to the Petitioner, namely, the portion concerning persons who, having received and had finalized an actual sentence of imprisonment or confinement or more for offenses in concurrence with any offense falling under any item of Article 5(1), are confined.\\n\\ne. Case 2011HEONMA326\\n\\nPetitioners Seo ○ Mun, Kim ○ Su, Cheon ○ Seok, Kim ○ Ho, and Kim ○ Hwan seek an adjudication on whether the act of collecting DNA samples and Articles 2, 5, 8, and 13 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional. The subject matter of adjudication is, with respect to Petitioner Seo ○ Mun, ① among Article 5(1)6, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of refusal to leave premises under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act and the offense of bodily injury under Article 2(1)3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act committed in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act by the force of a multitude while carrying a dangerous object; and ② Article 8(3). In addition, with respect to Petitioners Kim ○ Su, Cheon ○ Seok, Kim ○ Ho, and Kim ○ Hwan, the subject matter of adjudication is ① among Article 5(1)1, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of arson of general buildings under Article 166(1) of the Criminal Act and, among Article 5(1)6, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of trespass into a residence, damage to property, etc. under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act, committed in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act by the force of a multitude or while displaying the power of a group or multitude or while carrying a dangerous object; and ② among Article 8(1), the portion concerning persons subject to collection of DNA samples pursuant to Article 5. The Petitioners challenge, in connection with Article 13, the retention of DNA identification information until death, and therefore the portion of Article 13(3) concerning convicted prisoners, etc., which is the most directly relevant, is included in the subject matter of adjudication.\\n\\nThe act of collecting DNA samples was carried out, in practice and without room for discretion, either by the Petitioners’ consent or by execution of a collection warrant pursuant to some provisions of the above Act, and because the statutory provisions that formed the basis thereof are to be deemed part of the subject matter of adjudication, there is no need to separately include the act of collecting DNA samples in the subject matter of adjudication; accordingly, it is excluded from the subject matter of adjudication. The remaining provisions are excluded from the subject matter of adjudication because, as definitional provisions, they cannot be said to result in any restriction of freedom, imposition of duties, or deprivation of rights or legal status (Article 2), or because they are unrelated (Article 8(2)), or because they are merely procedural provisions and no specific claim has been made as to their unconstitutionality (Article 5(2); Article 8(4) through (9)).\\n\\nf. Case 2013HEONMA215\\n\\nThe subject matter of adjudication is the portion applicable to Petitioner Kim ○ Gyu, namely, among Article 5(1)6 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for the offense of intimidation under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act, committed in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act while carrying a dangerous object.\\n\\ng. Case 2013HEONMA360\\n\\nPetitioner Kim ○ Young seeks an adjudication on whether the act of demanding appearance for DNA sample collection and Articles 2, 5, 8, and 13 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information are unconstitutional. The subject matter of adjudication is, with respect to the Petitioner, ① among Article 5(1)6, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for the offense of trespass into a residence under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act, committed by the force of a multitude in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act; and ② among Article 8(1), the portion concerning persons subject to collection of DNA samples pursuant to Article 5, and because the Petitioner challenges, in connection with Article 13, the retention of DNA identification information until death, the portion of Article 13(3) concerning convicted prisoners, etc., which is the most directly relevant, is included in the subject matter of adjudication. The act of demanding appearance for DNA sample collection and the remaining provisions are excluded from the subject matter of adjudication for the same reasons as above.\\n\\nh. Subject Matter of Adjudication in This Case\\n\\nThe subject matter of adjudication in this case is ① among Article 5(1)6 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information (enacted by Act No. 9944 on 2010. 1. 25.; hereinafter referred to as “the Act in this case”), the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of bodily injury under Article 2(1)3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act committed while carrying a deadly weapon or other dangerous object in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (2011HEONMA28); among Article 5(1)8 of the Act on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information (as amended by Act No. 10258 on 2010. 4. 15.), the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with offenses under Article 8(1) of the Special Act on the Punishment, etc. of Sexual Violence Crimes (2011HEONMA106); the portion among Article 5(1)4 of the Act in this case concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses under Article 301 of the Criminal Act (2011HEONMA141); among Article 5(1)6 of the Act in this case, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of refusal to leave premises under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act and the offense of bodily injury under Article 2(1)3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act committed in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act by the force of a multitude or while carrying a dangerous object (2011HEONMA326); among Article 5(1)1 of the Act in this case, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for the offense of arson of general buildings under Article 166(1) of the Criminal Act and, among Article 5(1)6 of the Act in this case, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for offenses in concurrence with the offense of trespass into a residence, damage to property, etc. under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act, committed in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act while displaying the power of a group or multitude or while carrying a dangerous object (2011HEONMA326); among Article 5(1)6 of the Act in this case, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for the offense of intimidation under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act, committed in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act while carrying a dangerous object (2013HEONMA215); and among Article 5(1)6 of the Act in this case, the portion concerning persons who have received and had finalized a sentence for the offense of trespass into a residence under Article 2(1)1 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act, committed by the force of a multitude in Article 3 of the same Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (2013HEONMA360) (hereinafter, the above portions of Article 5(1) of the Act in this case that provide for the collection of DNA samples in these cases are referred to collectively as “the collection provisions at issue”); ③ Article 8(3) of the Act in this case (2011HEONMA326; hereinafter “the collection-by-consent provision at issue”); ④ Article 10(1) of the Act in this case (2011HEONMA28; hereinafter “the DNA analysis, recording, and management provision at issue”); ⑤ Article 11(1) of the Act in this case (2011HEONMA28; hereinafter “the search-and-report provision at issue”); ⑥ among Article 13(3) of the Act in this case, the portion concerning convicted prisoners, etc. (2011HEONMA141, 326, 2013HEONMA360; hereinafter “the Addenda provision at issue”), and whether they infringe the Petitioners’ fundamental rights. The contents of the challenged provisions and related provisions are as follows.\\n\\n[Provisions Subject to Adjudication]\\n\\nAct on the Use and Protection of DNA Identification Information (enacted by Act No. 9944 on 2010. 1. 25.)\\n\\nArticle 5 (Collection of DNA Samples from Convicted Prisoners, etc.) ① A prosecutor (including a military prosecutor; hereinafter the same) may collect a DNA sample from a person who has received and had finalized a sentence, an order of probation under Article 59-2 of the Criminal Act, a sentence of protective custody under the Act on the Treatment and Custody of Offenders, or a protective disposition falling under Article 32(1)9 or 10 of the Juvenile Act, for any of the following crimes or crimes in concurrence therewith (hereinafter referred to as “convicted prisoners, etc.”): Provided, that this shall exclude cases where a DNA sample has already been collected pursuant to Article 6 and the DNA identification information has already been recorded.\\n\\n1. Crimes under Articles 164, 165, 166(1), 167(1), and 174 (limited to attempts under Article 164(1), Article 165, and Article 166(1)) among the crimes of arson and negligent fire under Chapter 13 of Part II of the Criminal Act\\n\\n4. Crimes under Articles 297 through 301, 301-2, 302, 303, and 305 among the crimes of rape and indecent assault under Chapter 32 of Part II of the Criminal Act\\n\\n6.
