supporting_precedents: {"[2010HEONGA82]": "[Appendix] Related Provisions\\n\\nFormer Act on the Attachment, etc. of Electronic Devices for Location Tracking of Specific Criminal Offenders (as amended by Act No. 10257 on April 15, 2010, and before amendment by Act No. 11558 on December 18, 2012)\\n\\nArticle 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to protect the people from specific crimes by taking the additional measure of attaching to the body an electronic device that can track the offender’s movements and determine his or her location, for the prevention of recidivism by specific offenders and for their resocialization through the correction of their conduct.\\n\\nArticle 2 (Definitions) The definitions of terms used in this Act are as follows:\\n4. “Location-tracking electronic device (hereinafter referred to as ‘electronic device’)” means a series of mechanical equipment, as determined by Presidential Decree, that identifies location or detects a movement route by using the principle of emitting and tracking electromagnetic waves.\\n\\nArticle 4 (Scope of Application) When an attachment order is sentenced against a person under 19 years of age, an electronic device under this Act may not be attached until the person reaches 19 years of age.\\n\\nArticle 5 (Petition for an Attachment Order) ① A prosecutor may file with the court a petition for an order to attach an electronic device (hereinafter referred to as an “attachment order”) against a person who falls under any of the following subparagraphs and is deemed likely to commit a sexual violence offense again.\\n1. Where a person who has been sentenced to an actual term of imprisonment with labor for a sexual violence offense commits a sexual violence offense within 10 years after the execution thereof has been completed or exempted\\n2. Where a person who has previously been attached with an electronic device under this Act for a sexual violence offense again commits a sexual violence offense\\n3. Where a person has committed a sexual violence offense two or more times (including cases where a final and conclusive judgment of conviction has been rendered) and thus a habitual pattern is recognized\\n4. Where a sexual violence offense is committed against a person under 16 years of age\\n④ A petition for an attachment order under paragraphs 1 through 3 shall be filed by the time the appellate proceedings of a specific crime case in which an indictment has been instituted are concluded.\\n⑤ When the court deems it necessary to sentence an attachment order as a result of hearing a specific crime case in which an indictment has been instituted, it may require the prosecutor to file a petition for an attachment order.\\n⑥ No petition for an attachment order may be filed if 15 years have elapsed from the institution of an indictment without a final judgment in a specific crime case under paragraphs 1 through 3.\\n\\nArticle 6 (Investigation) ① When deemed necessary in order to file a petition for an attachment order, a prosecutor may request the head of the probation office (including its branch office; hereinafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over the residence of the suspect or the location of the prosecutor’s office to which the suspect belongs (including its branch office; hereinafter the same shall apply) to investigate matters necessary regarding the suspect, such as the motive for the crime, the relationship with the victim, mental state, and the risk of recidivism.\\n④ In filing a petition for an attachment order, the prosecutor shall, if necessary, refer to the results of a psychiatric evaluation of the suspect or other expert diagnosis.\\n\\nArticle 9 (Judgment on Attachment Order, etc.) ① When the court deems a petition for an attachment order to be well-founded, it shall sentence an attachment order by judgment, setting the attachment period within the following periods. Provided, however, that where a specific crime is committed against a person under 13 years of age, the lower limit of the attachment period shall be twice the lower limit of the attachment period under the following subparagraphs.\\n1. Specific crimes for which the upper limit of the statutory punishment is death or life imprisonment: not less than 10 years and not more than 30 years\\n2. Specific crimes for which the lower limit of the term of imprisonment among the statutory punishments is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 3 years (excluding specific crimes falling under subparagraph 1): not less than 3 years and not more than 20 years\\n3. Specific crimes for which the lower limit of the term of imprisonment among the statutory punishments is fixed-term imprisonment of less than 3 years (excluding specific crimes falling under subparagraph 1 or 2): not less than 1 year and not more than 10 years\\n③ A person sentenced to an attachment order shall be subject to probation under the Act on Probation, etc. during the attachment period.\\n④ The court shall dismiss a petition for an attachment order by judgment when it falls under any of the following subparagraphs:\\n1. When the petition for an attachment order is deemed to be without merit\\n2. When a judgment or decision of acquittal (excluding cases where medical treatment and custody is sentenced on the ground of mental incapacity), extinguishment of prosecution, or dismissal of prosecution is rendered in a specific crime case\\n3. When a fine is imposed in a specific crime case\\n4. When a suspended sentence or suspension of execution is imposed in a specific crime case (excluding cases where attachment of an electronic device is ordered pursuant to Article 28(1))\\n⑤ A judgment in a case involving a petition for an attachment order shall be rendered simultaneously with the judgment in the specific crime case.\\n⑦ The pronouncement of an attachment order shall not be considered favorably in sentencing for the specific crime case.\\n\\nArticle 9-2 (Compliance Requirements) ① When sentencing an attachment order pursuant to Article 9(1), the court may, within the scope of the attachment period, set a compliance period and impose one or more of the following compliance requirements. Provided, however, that the compliance requirement under subparagraph 4 shall have its period set within the scope of 500 hours.\\n1. Restriction on going out during nighttime or at specific times\\n2. Prohibition of entry into specific areas or places\\n2-2. Restriction on residential areas\\n3. Prohibition of approach to specific persons, such as victims\\n4. Completion of a specific crime treatment program\\n5. Other matters necessary for the prevention of recidivism and the correction of conduct of a person sentenced to an attachment order\\n\\nArticle 14-2 (Extension, etc. of Attachment Period) ① If a person subject to attachment falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the court may, upon a petition by a prosecutor filed at the request of the head of the probation office, extend the attachment period within the limit of 1 year or make a decision to add or modify the compliance requirements under Article 9-2(1).\\n1. Where a compliance requirement under Article 32 of the Act on Probation, etc. has been violated without justifiable grounds\\n2. Where the report has not been made in violation of Article 14(2) without justifiable grounds\\n3. Where, in violation of Article 14(3), the person moved residence, traveled within the country, or departed from the country without permission, or obtained permission by false means, without justifiable grounds\\n② Even where there is a change in circumstances other than those prescribed in the subparagraphs of paragraph 1, the court may, if it deems there to be reasonable grounds, make a decision to add, modify, or delete the compliance requirements under Article 9-2(1) upon a petition by a prosecutor filed at the request of the head of the probation office.\\n\\nArticle 16 (Preservation, Use, Destruction, etc. of Received Data) ① The head of the probation office shall receive the electromagnetic waves emitted from the electronic device of a person subject to attachment and preserve the data therefrom (hereinafter referred to as “received data”).\\n② The received data may not be inspected, queried, or disclosed except in the following cases:\\n1. Where used as investigation or trial materials concerning a suspicion of a specific crime committed by the person subject to attachment\\n2. Where used by a probation officer for the purpose of guidance and assistance\\n3. Where used for the review of the provisional suspension of an attachment order and its revocation by the Probation Review Committee under Article 5 of the Act on Probation, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the “Review Committee”)\\n④ When a prosecutor or judicial police officer inspects or queries the received data, they shall present a warrant of seizure and search issued by a judge.\\n⑤ The head of the probation office shall destroy the received data when it falls under any of the following subparagraphs:\\n1. Where the sentence imposed together with the attachment order becomes extinguished under Article 81 of the Criminal Act\\n2. Where the sentence imposed together with the attachment order loses its effect due to pardon\\n3. Where five years have elapsed since the person whose attachment of the electronic device has ended has completed the attachment of the electronic device without having been subjected to a sentence of suspension of qualifications or to attachment of an electronic device under this Act\\n⑥ Necessary matters concerning the preservation, use, destruction, etc. of received data shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.\\n\\nArticle 17 (Application for Provisional Suspension of Attachment Order, etc.) ① The head of the probation office, the person subject to attachment, and his or her legal representative may apply to the Review Committee having jurisdiction over the relevant probation office for provisional suspension of the attachment order.\\n② The application under paragraph 1 shall be made after 3 months have elapsed from the date on which execution of the attachment order commenced. If the application is dismissed, a new application may be made after 3 months have elapsed from the date of dismissal.\\n\\nArticle 19 (Revocation of Provisional Suspension, etc.) ① The head of the probation office may apply to the Review Committee for revocation of provisional suspension when a person whose attachment order has been provisionally suspended is deemed to pose a risk of recidivism, such as by committing a specific crime or failing to comply with reports on residence changes. In such case, when the Review Committee deems that the risk of recidivism of the person whose provisional suspension has been granted is significant, it shall revoke the provisional suspension.\\n② A person whose provisional suspension is revoked pursuant to paragraph 1 shall attach the electronic device during the remaining attachment period. In such case, the period of provisional suspension shall not be included in the attachment period.\\n\\nArticle 36 (Penalties) ① Where a person in charge of electronic device attachment duties, without justifiable grounds, releases or damages the electronic device of a person subject to attachment, he or she shall be punished by fixed-term imprisonment with labor for not less than 1 year.\\n② Where a person in charge of electronic device attachment duties receives, demands, or promises money, valuables, or other benefits and commits the offense under paragraph 1, he or she shall be punished by fixed-term imprisonment with labor for not less than 2 years.\\n③ Where a person who manages received data violates Article 16(2), he or she shall be punished by fixed-term imprisonment with labor for not less than 1 year.\\n\\nArticle 38 (Penalties) Where a person subject to attachment violates Article 14 (including cases where it applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Articles 27 and 31) and, during the attachment period of the electronic device, arbitrarily detaches or damages the electronic device from the body, interferes with radio waves, tampers with the received data, or otherwise impairs its utility, he or she shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 7 years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won.\\n\\nArticle 39 (Penalties) ① Where a person subject to attachment violates the compliance requirement under Article 9-2(1) subparagraph 3 or 4 without justifiable grounds, he or she shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.\\n② Where a person subject to attachment violates the compliance requirement under Article 9-2(1) subparagraph 1, subparagraph 2, subparagraph 2-2, or subparagraph 5 without justifiable grounds, he or she shall be punished by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.\\n\\nSupplementary Provisions to the Act on the Attachment, etc. of Electronic Devices for Location Tracking of Specific Criminal Offenders (Act No. 9112 of June 13, 2008, as amended by Act No. 10257 of April 15, 2010)\\n① Omitted\\n② The procedures for an attachment order against a person scheduled for release under paragraph 1 shall be as follows:\\n1. The head of a prison, detention house, treatment and custody facility, or protective custody facility (hereinafter referred to as “custodial facility”) shall notify the prosecutor of the local district public prosecutors’ office having jurisdiction over the location of the custodial facility and the head of the probation office of the personal details, correctional performance, and other necessary matters no later than 6 months before the execution of the term of imprisonment, etc. for the person scheduled for release is completed.\\n2. The prosecutor may request the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the location of the prosecutor’s office to which he or she belongs or over the residence of the person scheduled for release to conduct an investigation under Article 6 concerning the person scheduled for release under paragraph 1.\\n3. The head of the probation office shall submit the investigation report under Article 6(3) no later than 4 months before the execution of the term of imprisonment, etc. for the person scheduled for release is completed.\\n4. The prosecutor shall file a petition for an attachment order with the court no later than 3 months before the execution of the term of imprisonment, etc. for the person scheduled for release is completed, with respect to a person among those scheduled for release who meets the requirements for petitioning an attachment order under paragraph 1.\\n5. When the court deems a petition for an attachment order under subparagraph 4 to be well-founded, it shall issue an attachment order by decision no later than 1 month before the execution of the term of imprisonment, etc. for the person scheduled for release is completed.\\n6. An appeal against a decision under subparagraph 5 shall not have the effect of suspending execution of the attachment order.\\n③ The procedures for an attachment order against a person nearing release and a released person under paragraph 1 shall be as follows:\\n1. The head of a custodial facility shall notify the prosecutor of the local district public prosecutors’ office having jurisdiction over the location of the custodial facility and the head of the probation office of the personal details, correctional performance, and other necessary matters for persons nearing release and released persons within 1 month from the date this Act enters into force.\\n2. The prosecutor may request the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the location of the prosecutor’s office to which he or she belongs or over the residence of persons nearing release and released persons to conduct an investigation under Article 6 concerning persons nearing release and released persons.\\n3. The head of the probation office shall submit the investigation report under Article 6(3) concerning persons nearing release and released persons within 2 months from the date of receipt of the request.\\n4. The prosecutor shall file a petition for an attachment order with the court within 1 year from the date this Act enters into force with respect to a person among those nearing release or released persons who meets the requirements for petitioning an attachment order under paragraph 1. Provided, however, that if a person nearing release or a released person flees, the period shall be 3 years.\\n5. When necessary for the investigation under subparagraph 2 or the petition under subparagraph 4, the prosecutor or the head of the probation office may require the released person to appear and hear his or her statement.\\n6. When a released person fails, without justifiable grounds, to comply with a request to appear under subparagraph 5, or is likely not to comply, the prosecutor may petition the judge of the competent district court to issue a warrant for apprehension and apprehend the released person, and the head of the probation office may apply to the prosecutor of the competent local public prosecutors’ office, obtain a warrant for apprehension issued by the judge of the competent district court upon the prosecutor’s petition, and apprehend the released person.\\n7. When the prosecutor or the head of the probation office apprehends a released person pursuant to subparagraph 6, he or she shall complete the necessary investigation within 48 hours from the time of apprehension, and shall immediately release the released person when the investigation is completed.\\n8. When the court deems a petition for an attachment order under subparagraph 4 to be well-founded, it shall issue an attachment order by decision within 2 months from the date of the petition.\\n9. The head of the probation office may summon the released person for the execution of the decision under subparagraph 8.\\n10. If the released person fails to comply with the summons under subparagraph 9, the head of the probation office may apply to the prosecutor, obtain a writ of execution of the attachment order, and apprehend the released person.\\n11. An appeal against a decision under subparagraph 8 shall not have the effect of suspending execution of the attachment order.\\n④ The statute of limitations for an attachment order under paragraphs 2 and 3 shall be 5 years from the date the attachment order becomes final and conclusive, and when the statute of limitations is completed, execution shall be exempted. Provided, however, that the statute of limitations shall be interrupted by the arrest of the person scheduled for release, the person nearing release, or the released person.\\n\\nFormer Act on the Attachment of Electronic Devices for Location Tracking of Specific Sexual Violence Offenders (Act No. 9112 of June 13, 2008, as amended, and before amendment by Act No. 10257 of April 15, 2010)\\n\\nArticle 5 (Petition for an Attachment Order) ① A prosecutor may file with the court a petition for an order to attach an electronic device (hereinafter referred to as an “attachment order”) against a person who falls under any of the following subparagraphs and is deemed likely to commit a sexual violence offense again.\\n1. Where a person who has been sentenced to actual terms of imprisonment with labor for sexual violence offenses two or more times, and whose aggregate term of imprisonment is 3 years or more, commits a sexual violence offense within 5 years after the execution thereof has been completed or exempted\\n2. Where a person who has previously been attached with an electronic device under this Act again commits a sexual violence offense\\n3. Where a person has committed a sexual violence offense two or more times and thus a habitual pattern is recognized\\n4. Where a sexual violence offense is committed against a person under 13 years of age\\n② The petition under paragraph 1 shall be filed before the pronouncement of the first-instance judgment in a sexual violence offense case in which an indictment has been instituted.\\n④ No petition for an attachment order may be filed if 15 years have elapsed from the institution of an indictment without a final judgment in a sexual violence offense case under each subparagraph of paragraph 1.\\n\\nArticle 9 (Judgment on Attachment Order, etc.) ① When the court deems a petition for an attachment order to be well-founded, it shall sentence an attachment order by judgment, setting the attachment period within the limit of 10 years.\\n② The court shall dismiss a petition for an attachment order by judgment when it falls under any of the following subparagraphs:\\n1. When the petition for an attachment order is deemed to be without merit\\n2. When a judgment or decision of acquittal (excluding cases where medical treatment and custody is sentenced on the ground of mental incapacity), extinguishment of prosecution, or dismissal of prosecution is rendered in a sexual violence offense case\\n3. When a fine is imposed in a sexual violence offense case\\n4. When a suspended sentence or suspension of execution is imposed in a sexual violence offense case (excluding cases where attachment of an electronic device is ordered pursuant to Article 28(1))"}

{"[2012HEONMA686]": "[Annex] Relevant Provisions\\n\\nAct on the Protection of Personal Liberty (Enacted by Act No. 8724 on 2007. 12. 21.)\\nArticle 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to protect the fundamental rights of the people guaranteed by the Constitution by establishing relief procedures for individuals whose personal liberty is unjustly restricted due to an unlawful administrative disposition or commitment to a facility by a private person.\\n\\nAct on the Protection of Personal Liberty (Amended by Act No. 10364 on 2010. 6. 10.)\\nArticle 3 (Petition for Relief) When detention of a detainee has commenced unlawfully or, after lawful detention, the ground therefor has ceased to exist but the person is still being detained, the detainee, his or her statutory representative, guardian, spouse, lineal relative, sibling, cohabitant, employer, or person working at the detention facility (hereinafter referred to as “petitioner for relief”) may petition the court for relief as prescribed by this Act. Provided, that where another Act provides a relief procedure, it must be clearly impossible to obtain relief under that Act within a reasonable period.\\n\\nImmigration Control Act (Amended by Act No. 12421 on 2014. 3. 18.)\\nArticle 46 (Persons Subject to Deportation) ① The head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office may deport from the Republic of Korea any foreigner who falls under any of the following items in accordance with the procedures prescribed in this Chapter.\\n(Items omitted)\\nArticle 51 (Detention) ① An immigration control officer may detain a foreigner by obtaining a detention order from the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office if there are reasonable grounds to suspect that the foreigner falls under any of the items of paragraph 1 of Article 46 and if there is a risk of flight.\\n③ In an urgent case where there are reasonable grounds to suspect that the foreigner falls under any of the items of paragraph 1 of Article 46 and there is a risk of flight or a possibility of flight, and there is no time to obtain a detention order from the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office, the immigration control officer may detain the foreigner urgently by informing the person of the reason therefor.\\nArticle 52 (Period and Place of Detention) ① The period of detention for examining and determining whether a foreigner detained under Article 51 is subject to deportation shall be within 10 days. Provided, that where there is an unavoidable reason, the period may be extended only once within the extent not exceeding 10 days with the permission of the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office.\\nArticle 55 (Objection to Detention) ① A person detained pursuant to a detention order or his or her statutory representative, etc. may file an objection to detention with the Minister of Justice through the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office.\\n② Upon receiving an objection under paragraph 1, the Minister of Justice shall, without delay, examine the relevant documents and, if the objection is found to be without merit, dismiss it by decision, and if it is found to be well-founded, order, by decision, release from detention of the detained person.\\n③ Before making a decision under paragraph 2, the Minister of Justice may, if necessary, hear the statements of persons concerned.\\nArticle 63 (Detention and Release from Detention of a Person Who Has Received a Deportation Order) ① If the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office cannot immediately repatriate a person who has received a deportation order outside the Republic of Korea due to reasons such as not having a passport or not having transportation secured, he or she may detain the person in a detention facility until the person can be repatriated.\\n② When detaining a person pursuant to paragraph 1, if the period exceeds 3 months, the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office shall obtain prior approval from the Minister of Justice every 3 months.\\n③ If the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office fails to obtain the approval under paragraph 2, he or she shall release the person from detention without delay.\\n④ If it becomes clear that a person who has received a deportation order cannot be repatriated due to reasons such as being denied entry by another country, the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office may release the person from detention.\\n⑤ Where the head of a local immigration office or foreigners' office releases a person from detention pursuant to paragraph 3 or 4, he or she may attach a restriction on residence or any other necessary conditions.\\n⑥ In the case of detention under paragraph 1, Articles 53 through 55, Articles 56-2 through 56-9, and Article 57 shall apply mutatis mutandis.\\n\\nImmigration Control Act (Amended by Act No. 10282 on 2010. 5. 14.)\\nArticle 51 (Detention) ② When applying for issuance of a detention order under paragraph 1, materials sufficient to establish the necessity of detention shall be attached and submitted.\\n④ If an immigration control officer urgently detains a foreigner pursuant to paragraph 3, he or she shall immediately prepare an emergency detention notice and show it to the foreigner.\\n⑤ If an immigration control officer detains a foreigner pursuant to paragraph 3, he or she shall obtain a detention order within 48 hours and show it to the foreigner; if a detention order is not obtained, detention shall be released immediately.\\nArticle 52 (Period and Place of Detention) ② The places where detention may be made shall be a foreigner detention room, a foreigner detention center, or any other place designated by the Minister of Justice (hereinafter referred to as “detention facility”)."}

{"[2013HEONMA129]": "The Petitioner filed this constitutional complaint case seeking revocation of the non-prosecution disposition of suspension of indictment, which the Respondent determined on 2012. 11. 30. in relation to the assault case No. 2012HYEONGJE15580 at the Pohang Branch Office of the Daegu District Prosecutors’ Office, alleging that it infringes the Petitioner’s fundamental rights, including the constitutionally guaranteed right to equality.\\n\\nHowever, even upon close examination of the record of this case, it does not appear that the Respondent conducted an investigation with respect to the above case that was manifestly contrary to equity, or that there was any serious error in the interpretation of the Constitution, application of law, or evaluation of evidence that affected the decision to issue the non-prosecution disposition, and there is otherwise no material from which to conclude that the Respondent’s disposition in this case is an arbitrary disposition to such an extent that the Constitutional Court would be concerned; therefore, it cannot be said that the fundamental rights asserted by the Petitioner were infringed thereby.\\n\\nAccordingly, since the petition for adjudication in this case is without merit, it is decided to dismiss it, and the decision is made as stated in the Order, by the unanimous opinion of all Justices participating.\\n\\n2013. 7. 25."}

{"[2015HEONMA1204]": "1. Summary of the Case  \\nA. Suspect Yun XX-hyeon was arrested pursuant to an arrest warrant at around 19:00 on 2015. 10. 5., and a detention warrant was sought. The Claimant, an attorney, was entrusted by the family of the above suspect and, after inquiring by telephone at around 17:00 on 2015. 10. 6. to the Respondent prosecutor of the XX District Prosecutors’ Office who was investigating the case (hereinafter referred to as the “Respondent Prosecutor”) whether a counsel visitation was possible, visited the prosecutor’s office room No. XX at the XX District Prosecutors’ Office at around 19:00 on the same day, carrying a visitation application, and applied to the Respondent Prosecutor for a counsel visitation.  \\nB. The Respondent correctional officer of the XX Detention Center who was in charge of escorting the above suspect (hereinafter referred to as the “Respondent Correctional Officer”) received custody of the above suspect from the Respondent Prosecutor’s office at around 17:00 on the same day and kept him waiting in the detention room within the Prosecutors’ Office, and then, at around 19:10 on the same day, upon receiving a request from the Respondent Prosecutor to summon the suspect for night questioning, brought the above suspect into the prosecutor’s office.  \\nC. The Respondent Prosecutor informed the Respondent Correctional Officer that the Claimant had made an application for visitation, and the Respondent Correctional Officer, after inquiring with the official in charge of counsel visitation at the XX Detention Center regarding the procedures for handling it, informed the Claimant that, pursuant to Article 58(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Prisoners, counsel visitation could not be permitted because the working hours under the Regulations on the Service of National Public Officials (“09:00 to 18:00”) had elapsed.  \\nD. Thereafter, the Respondent Prosecutor took no further action regarding the Claimant’s application for visitation, and the Claimant remained in the prosecutor’s office but ultimately left without having visited the above suspect. After the Claimant left, the Respondent Prosecutor continued questioning the above suspect, and the Claimant was not retained as counsel for the above suspect.  \\nE. The Claimant filed the present constitutional complaint on 2015. 12. 28., alleging that the acts of the Respondents in denying the application for counsel visitation, and Article 58(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Prisoners, which the Respondent Correctional Officer relied upon as the legal basis therefor, infringed his fundamental rights.  \\n\\n2. Subject Matter of Adjudication  \\nThe subject matter of this case is whether: ① the acts of the Respondents in failing to take measures to permit visitation between the Claimant and suspect Yun XX-hyeon at prosecutor’s office room No. XX of the XX District Prosecutors’ Office at around 19:00 on 2015. 10. 6. (hereinafter, the Respondent Prosecutor’s denial of visitation shall be referred to as the “Prosecutor’s denial of visitation in this case,” the Respondent Correctional Officer’s denial of visitation shall be referred to as the “Correctional Officer’s denial of visitation in this case,” and these acts collectively as the “denial of visitation in this case”), and ② Article 58(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Prisoners (wholly amended by Presidential Decree No. 21095 on 2008. 10. 29.; hereinafter referred to as the “Visitation Hours Provision in this case”) infringe the Claimant’s fundamental rights (hereinafter, the “Act on the Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Prisoners” shall be referred to as the “Execution of Sentences Act”).  \\nThe provision subject to adjudication and related provisions are as follows:  \\n\\n[Provision Subject to Adjudication]  \\nEnforcement Decree of the Act on the Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Prisoners (wholly amended by Presidential Decree No. 21095 on 2008. 10. 29.)  \\nArticle 58 (Visitation) (1) Visitation by a prisoner shall take place every day (excluding public holidays and days designated by the Minister of Justice) within working hours pursuant to Article 9 of the Regulations on the Service of National Public Officials.  \\n\\n[Related Provisions]  \\nCriminal Procedure Act (enacted by Act No. 341 on 1954. 9. 23.)  \\nArticle 34 (Visitation, Communication, and Medical Treatment with Defendant or Suspect) A defense counsel or a person who intends to become defense counsel
