concerning the attribution of rights to land or buildings created as a result of the implementation of the redevelopment project and matters concerning the members’ burden of costs, thereby directly and concretely affecting the property rights and obligations of the members, etc.; accordingly, it constitutes a binding administrative plan and an independent administrative disposition made by the reconstruction association (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 94DA31235 decided February 15, 1996, Supreme Court Decision 2005DU11951 decided September 6, 2007, etc.).\\n\\nHowever, since the management and disposal plan becomes effective only when the reconstruction association prepares a draft management and disposal plan based on the status of the members’ applications for allotment, obtains a resolution of the association’s general meeting thereon and undergoes the procedure for public inspection by owners of land, etc., and then receives authorization and public notice from the competent administrative agency (Article 24(3)10, Article 48(1), and Article 49 of the Urban Improvement Act), the resolution of the association’s general meeting on the draft management and disposal plan is one of the procedural requirements leading to the administrative disposition called the management and disposal plan, and if it is unlawful and thus invalid, the management and disposal plan becomes defective.\\n\\nTherefore, a lawsuit brought against the reconstruction association, which is an administrative subject, to contest the validity, etc. of the association’s general meeting resolution on the draft management and disposal plan is a lawsuit concerning the existence or validity of a procedural requirement leading to an administrative disposition, and since it concerns a public-law legal relationship that directly affects whether the administrative disposition is unlawful depending on the outcome of the litigation, it constitutes a party litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act.\\n\\nAnd such a lawsuit, if filed before the management and disposal plan is authorized and publicly notified, may prevent a defective management and disposal plan from reaching the stage where it is authorized and publicly notified and thereby becomes effective as an administrative disposition by obtaining a judgment confirming the nullity of the unlawful general meeting resolution and submitting it as material to the competent administrative agency, or by causing the reconstruction association to prepare a new lawful draft management and disposal plan and undergo the general meeting resolution procedure again; moreover, even where the management and disposal plan is authorized and publicly notified notwithstanding a judgment confirming the nullity of the general meeting resolution, the dispute may be promptly resolved by utilizing the judgment and evidence from the lawsuit for confirmation of the nullity of the general meeting resolution as litigation materials in an administrative appeal litigation contesting the validity of the management and disposal plan; therefore, it needs to be permitted before authorization and public notice of the management and disposal plan.\\n\\nHowever, once the competent administrative agency authorizes and publicly notifies the management and disposal plan, the management and disposal plan becomes effective as an administrative disposition; therefore, on the ground of defects in the general meeting resolution, the party must seek revocation of, or confirmation of nullity of, the management and disposal plan by means of an administrative appeal litigation contesting the validity of the administrative disposition, and, separately, it should be deemed impermissible, absent special circumstances, to sever only the general meeting resolution, which is merely one of the procedural requirements leading to the administrative disposition, and bring an action for confirmation contesting its validity.\\n\\nIn contrast, Supreme Court Decision 2004DA13694 decided July 22, 2004, and the Supreme Court decisions to the same effect, which held that a lawsuit for confirmation of nullity of a general meeting resolution on a draft management and disposal plan of a redevelopment association under the Urban Redevelopment Act (repealed by Article 2 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Act No. 6852, the Act on the Improvement of Urban Areas and Residential Environments, of December 30, 2002) is a civil action and that, even after authorization and public notice of the management and disposal plan, one may still seek confirmation by lawsuit of the nullity of the general meeting resolution, are all to be changed to the extent that they conflict with the view of this decision.\\n\\n2. According to the reasons for the judgment of the court below and the record, it can be seen that the lawsuit in this case, which was brought against the Defendant, a reconstruction association under the Urban Improvement Act, seeking confirmation of the nullity of the general meeting resolution on the draft management and disposal plan, was filed on March 11, 2005, before authorization and public notice of the management and disposal plan; therefore, as seen above, it constitutes a party litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act, and accordingly, the court of exclusive jurisdiction of first instance in this case should be the Seoul Administrative Court.\\n\\nNevertheless, the first-instance court and the court below proceeded to a judgment on the merits while overlooking that this case was filed with the Seoul Central District Court in violation of exclusive jurisdiction; thus, the determinations of the first-instance court and the court below contain an error of law in misunderstanding the legal principles concerning party litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act and thereby violating the provisions on exclusive jurisdiction.\\n\\nMeanwhile, since the competent administrative agency authorized and publicly notified the management and disposal plan at issue on March 18, 2005, after the filing of this lawsuit, it may be said that a separate request for confirmation of the nullity of the general meeting resolution alone can no longer be made. However, considering that the action may be changed, after transfer and with the permission of the administrative court, into an action for revocation, etc. concerning the management and disposal plan, it is difficult to regard such circumstance alone as corresponding to a case where it is evident that, after transfer, the lawsuit in this case would become unlawful and be dismissed. Accordingly, it is appropriate to transfer this case to the court of competent jurisdiction (see Supreme Court Decision 95DA28960 decided May 30, 1997, Supreme Court Decision 2007DA25261 decided July 24, 2008, etc.).\\n\\n3. Therefore, without examining the grounds of appeal, the Court, ex officio, reverses the judgment of the court below, cancels the judgment of the first instance, and transfers the case to the court of competent jurisdiction so that it may be retried and determined, and so adjudicates as per the Disposition by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[2011DA95564]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Article 17, paragraph 1, of the Value-Added Tax Act provides that \"the amount of value-added tax payable by a business operator shall be the amount obtained by deducting the tax amounts under the following items (hereinafter referred to as 'input tax') from the tax amount on goods or services supplied by the taxpayer (hereinafter referred to as 'output tax'). Provided, the input tax exceeding the output tax shall be the tax amount to be refunded (hereinafter referred to as 'refund tax amount').\" It further provides in item 1 for \"the tax amount on the supply of goods or services used or to be used for the business of the taxpayer,\" and in item 2 for \"the tax amount on the import of goods used or to be used for the business of the taxpayer,\" while Article 24, paragraph 1, provides that \"the head of the tax office having jurisdiction over the place of business shall, for each taxable period, refund to the business operator the refund tax amount for that taxable period in accordance with the Presidential Decree.\" Meanwhile, Article 72, paragraph 1, of the Enforcement Decree of the Value-Added Tax Act pursuant to such delegation provides that \"the refund tax amount prescribed in Article 24, paragraph 1, of the Act shall be refunded to the business operator within 30 days after the lapse of the deadline for filing the final return for each taxable period.\" Paragraph 4 provides that \"the tax amount to be refunded under Article 24 of the Act shall be limited to the amount confirmed by the return filed pursuant to Articles 18, 19, or Article 73, paragraph 4, of this Decree and the documentary evidence attached thereto, and the aggregate table of tax invoices by supplier and the statement of receipts of credit card sales slips, etc., filed pursuant to Article 20 of the Act.\"\\n\\nAs such, the reason the Value-Added Tax Act and its subordinate legislation, together with the definitional provisions of refund tax amounts and the specific provisions concerning the timing and method of calculation thereof, prescribe the State's duty to pay the refund tax amount to the business operator bearing the value-added tax payment obligation (hereinafter referred to as the \"taxpayer\") is that, through a legislative determination to achieve tax-policy objectives such as facilitating taxation and collection and preventing double taxation, the legislature adopted the pre-stage tax credit system, under which the business operator supplying goods or services at each transaction stage before the final consumer collects the output tax from the business operator receiving the supply and pays it to the State, and the business operator from whom that tax has been collected deducts and is refunded that amount from the State as input tax, thereby successively passing the burden of the tax to the business operator in the next stage and ultimately making the final consumer bear it; as a result, where, in a taxable period, the amount of tax collected by transaction collection exceeds the amount of tax collected by transaction collection, tax exceeding the amount corresponding to the value added created by the taxpayer is collected, and thus it can be said that, according to tax-administration and tax-policy demands for adjustment, it is specially recognized on that basis (see Supreme Court Decision 92DA20002, rendered on 1992. 11. 27.; Supreme Court en banc Decision 2009DU13474, rendered on 2011. 1. 20.; etc.).\\n\\nTherefore, in light of the content, form, and legislative purpose of the foregoing Value-Added Tax Act and its subordinate legislation, the State's duty to pay the refund tax amount of value-added tax to the taxpayer arises directly under the provisions of the Value-Added Tax Act and its subordinate legislation, irrespective of whether the State has actually received from that taxpayer the amount corresponding to taxes collected in excess in a given taxable period; and its legal nature is not a duty to return unjust enrichment, which is recognized for the adjustment of property status between the person enriched and the person suffering loss in the concepts of justice and fairness, but rather a public-law duty whose existence and scope are specifically fixed by the Value-Added Tax Act and its subordinate legislation and which is specially recognized from a tax-policy perspective. This is the proper view.\\n\\nAccordingly, a taxpayer's claim against the State for payment of the value-added tax refund amount, corresponding to the State's duty to pay the value-added tax refund amount to the taxpayer, must follow the procedure for a party suit prescribed in Article 3, item 2, of the Administrative Litigation Act, rather than civil litigation.\\n\\nNevertheless, Supreme Court Decision 94DA34005, rendered on 1996. 4. 12.; Supreme Court Decision 95DA4063, rendered on 1996. 9. 6.; Supreme Court Decision 97DA26432, rendered on 1997. 10. 10.; Supreme Court Decision 2000DU7520, rendered on 2001. 10. 26.; and, in relation to the interpretation of Article 51, paragraph 1, of the Framework Act on National Taxes concerning the refund of national tax refunds, Supreme Court Decision 85NU565, rendered on 1987. 9. 8.; Supreme Court Decision 87NU479, rendered on 1988. 11. 8.; and other decisions to the same effect, which held that the return of refund tax amounts prescribed by individual tax statutes is uniformly a return of unjust enrichment and consequently that the return of value-added tax refund amounts is also a return of unjust enrichment, are all to be changed to the extent they conflict with the view of this judgment.\\n\\n2. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the lower court's action in revoking the first-instance judgment, which had tried and determined the plaintiff's claim on the premise that the plaintiff's action, asserting that it had acquired the right to claim payment of the value-added tax refund amounts that arose respectively under Article 24, paragraph 1, of the former Value-Added Tax Act (as in force before amendment by Act No. 9915 on 2010. 1. 1.), applicable to the value-added tax refund amounts for the second period of 2008, the first period of 2009, and the second period of 2009 in this case, and under Article 24, paragraph 1, of the Value-Added Tax Act, applicable to the value-added tax refund amount for the first period of 2010 in this case, was the subject of civil litigation, and in transferring this case to the Uijeongbu District Court, the competent court for administrative cases, is proper, and there is no illegality in having misunderstood the legal nature of the right to claim payment of the value-added tax refund amount and the legal principles concerning the form of litigation, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. Judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition. Except for the dissenting opinion of Supreme Court Justice Park Bo-young with respect to this judgment, the opinions of the participating Justices are unanimous.\\n\\n4. The dissenting opinion of Supreme Court Justice Park Bo-young is as follows.\\n\\na. I find that the logic of the majority opinion, to the effect that the legal nature of the State's duty to pay the value-added tax refund amount is a public-law duty of the State whose existence and scope are specifically fixed by the Value-Added Tax Act and its subordinate legislation and which is specially recognized from a tax-policy perspective, has some aspects that are understandable. However, I cannot agree, for the following reasons, with the majority opinion's view that the taxpayer's claim against the State for payment of the value-added tax refund amount corresponding to such duty must follow the procedure for a party suit prescribed in Article 3, item 2, of the Administrative Litigation Act rather than civil litigation, and that Supreme Court decisions to the contrary should therefore be changed.\\n\\nb. Article 3, item 2, of the current Administrative Litigation Act abstractly defines a party suit as \"a lawsuit concerning a legal relationship arising from an administrative agency's disposition, etc., or any other lawsuit concerning a legal relationship under public law, in which one party to that legal relationship is named as the defendant,\" leaving the concrete form of litigation and the allocation of judicial jurisdiction to judicial interpretation. Accordingly, it cannot be said that a logical and necessary imperative exists to make it necessarily the subject of a party suit merely because there is a public-law element in the legal nature of the right.\\n\\nRather, the value-added tax refund amount is one that the State returns because, when the value-added tax paid by a business operator at the time of purchase (input tax) exceeds the value-added tax received at the time of sale (output tax), the State has no just cause to retain the additional value-added tax paid by the business operator; thus, it is also possible to frame the legal nature of the claim for payment as a claim for return of unjust enrichment under the Civil Act. In addition, even if the State has not actually received the amount corresponding to taxes collected in excess from a given business operator, it can normatively be evaluated that there is a direct connection and causal relationship between loss and gain because, by virtue of the business operator's contribution, the State acquires a tax claim against the business operator that collected the tax. The provisions of Article 24, paragraph 1, of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 72, paragraph 1, of the Enforcement Decree of the Value-Added Tax Act, etc., may also be understood as special provisions on unjust enrichment that relax the requirement, among the requirements for the establishment of unjust enrichment, that the State's gain arise.\\n\\nUltimately, as to the value-added tax refund amount, for which it is originally just and fair for the State to return it immediately as unjust enrichment, the fact that the Value-Added Tax Act and its subordinate legislation prescribe the requirements, procedures, and timing of payment, and that the duty of payment has the character of a public-law duty, does not mean that the claim for payment of the refund amount must be made as a party suit under the Administrative Litigation Act, which is within the exclusive jurisdiction of the administrative courts.\\n\\nc. Although our judicial system separately establishes administrative courts (Articles 40-2 through 40-4 of the Court Organization Act), regional administrative courts have still not been established other than the Seoul Administrative Court, so the main office of the relevant district court and the Gangneung Branch of Chuncheon District Court have jurisdiction over administrative cases [Article 2 and the proviso to Article 1, paragraph 1, of the Addenda to the Court Organization Act (1994. 7. 27.)], and thus, outside the Seoul area, the main office of the relevant district court and the Gangneung Branch of Chuncheon District Court handle civil and administrative cases together. In addition, the personnel system for judges also adopts a rotational assignment system in which positions are periodically changed between judges belonging to administrative courts and judges belonging to district courts.\\n\\nMoreover, unlike an appeal litigation, a party suit under the Administrative Litigation Act is not recognized as having effect against all persons (see Article 44, paragraph 1, and Article 29, paragraph 1, of the Administrative Litigation Act), and although ex officio review is possible (see Article 44, paragraph 1, and Article 26 of the Administrative Litigation Act), traditional Supreme Court precedents have held that \"the court may investigate evidence ex officio only with respect to matters appearing in the record of the case, and may determine the case on that basis; even then, it may investigate evidence and determine the case only within the scope of the claim and only when the court deems it necessary,\" thereby limiting the application of ex officio review (see Supreme Court Decision 94NU4820, rendered on 1994. 10. 11.; etc.). Furthermore, since joinder of an appeal litigation and a claim for return of unjust enrichment is permitted (see Article 10 and Article 38, paragraph 1, of the Administrative Litigation Act; Supreme Court Decision 2008DU23153, rendered on 2009. 4. 9.; etc.), the unreasonable aspects that may arise from treating a claim for payment of the value-added tax refund amount as the subject of civil litigation can also be resolved through litigation management.\\n\\nFrom the perspective of the foregoing judicial system and litigation practice, the practical benefit of distinguishing between civil litigation and a party suit is not very great.\\n\\nIn addition, through Supreme Court precedents accumulated over several decades, it appears not only that the perception has firmly taken root among the general public that a claim for payment of the value-added tax refund amount is, like a claim for return of overpaid amounts or a claim for State compensation arising from unlawful dispositions, etc., the subject of civil litigation, but also that such practical practice has been established. Therefore, as the majority opinion does, to change the precedent only with respect to claims for payment of the value-added tax refund amount and to regard them as the subject of a party suit is not desirable in that it may only cause confusion in the public's choice of remedies and in litigation practice.\\n\\nIf so, at present, when even an amendment to the Administrative Litigation Act is being discussed in the direction of expanding the subjects of party suits, I think it is more appropriate, in that it can promote stability in the people's legal life, to maintain the Supreme Court precedents that regarded claims for payment of the value-added tax refund amount as the subject of civil litigation and await a legislative, comprehensive solution through statutory amendment, rather than newly changing claims for payment of the value-added tax refund amount into the subject of a party suit.\\n\\nd. Therefore, the lower court's judgment, which regarded the plaintiff's claim asserting that it had acquired the right to claim payment of the value-added tax refund amount as the subject of a party suit, revoked the first-instance judgment, and transferred this case to the Uijeongbu District Court, the competent court for administrative cases, contains an error that affected the conclusion of the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the form of litigation for a claim for payment of the value-added tax refund amount. Accordingly, the lower court judgment should be reversed.\\n\\nFor the foregoing reasons, I do not agree with the majority opinion, and I state my dissent."}

{"[2012DA102629]": "We consider the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Local Public Officials Act provides that “Public officials of local governments shall be classified into career-service public officials and special career-service public officials.” Paragraph 2 provides that “’Career-service public officials’ means public officials appointed on the basis of merit and qualification and whose status is guaranteed, and the categories thereof are as follows,” and item 2 includes local fire public officials as one type of specific public officials.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 44, paragraph 4 of the Local Public Officials Act provides that “No money or valuable goods may be paid as remuneration to public officials except in accordance with the provisions concerning remuneration prescribed by this Act or other statutes,” and Article 45, paragraph 1 provides that “The following matters concerning the remuneration of public officials shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree,” while item 2 includes “matters concerning allowances.” Article 30 of the Regulations on the Remuneration of Local Public Officials provides that “Public officials may be paid, within the limits of the budget, the necessary allowances in addition to salary (paragraph 1).”, and “The types, scope of payment, amount of payment, and other necessary matters concerning the payment of allowances paid pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be separately prescribed by Presidential Decree (paragraph 2).” In addition, the Regulations concerning Allowances, etc. for Local Public Officials provide that overtime work allowances under Article 15 shall be paid, within the limits of the budget, to persons who work beyond the working hours prescribed by work orders; night work allowances under Article 16 shall be paid, within the limits of the budget, to persons who perform night work as alternating day-and-night shift workers, etc.; and holiday work allowances under Article 17 shall be paid, within the limits of the budget, to persons who work on holidays, with overtime work allowances, night work allowances, and holiday work allowances hereinafter collectively referred to as “overtime allowances,” calculated in the manner prescribed in the relevant provisions.\\n\\nThe relationship between such local governments and local fire public officials who are career-service public officials belonging thereto, that is, the working relationship of local fire public officials, falls under a public-law working relationship rather than a private-law employment contract relationship, and the legal relationship concerning the remuneration of local fire public officials, which is one of the principal contents of that working relationship, must be deemed a public-law legal relationship. Furthermore, Article 44, paragraph 4 and Article 45, paragraph 1 of the Local Public Officials Act adopt the so-called principle of statutory employment conditions with respect to the remuneration of local public officials, and, when the content, form, and system of the relevant statutes and regulations are comprehensively considered, including the fact that Articles 15 through 17 of the Regulations concerning Allowances, etc. for Local Public Officials contain specific and direct provisions regarding the recipients of overtime allowances, the hourly amount payable, the limit on working hours, and the method of calculating working hours, the right of local fire public officials to claim payment of overtime allowances is directly determined as to its existence and scope by the provisions of the statutes and arises immediately when the conditions for payment of the allowances prescribed by the statutes are satisfied. Accordingly, an action by which a local fire public official seeks against the local government to which he or she belongs the payment of overtime allowances must follow the procedure for a party litigation prescribed in Article 3, item 2 of the Administrative Litigation Act.\\n\\n2. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the action in this case filed by the Plaintiffs, who are former and current fire public officials belonging to the Defendant, seeking payment of overtime allowances, is a matter subject to civil litigation; therefore, the measures taken by the lower court to revoke the first-instance judgment, which had heard and determined the case through civil litigation procedures on the premise that the action in this case was subject to civil litigation, and to transfer this case to the Seoul Administrative Court, the court having jurisdiction over administrative litigation, are proper, and there is no illegality in them such as the misapprehension of the legal nature and procedural form of the right of local fire public officials to claim payment of overtime allowances, as alleged in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n3. Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court participating.\\n\\n[[Separate Sheet] List of Plaintiffs: Omitted]"}

{"[94DA55019]": "1. First, ex officio examining the matter, according to the reasoning of the judgment below, the appellate court recognized, based on the evidence cited therein, that each of the buildings at issue newly constructed by the Plaintiffs was permitted to be built in accordance with the construction standards for detached houses for multiple households established by the Minister of Construction and Transportation, and was also registered in the Building Register as a detached house; and, in the register, ownership preservation registration had been completed with respect to the first and second buildings at issue in the joint names of Plaintiff 1, who was the builder, and Nonparties 1 and 2, and with respect to the third building at issue in the name of Plaintiff 2, who was the builder; however, the structure of each building was divided by household unit, and in terms of its structure living space was provided, so that each could conduct independent residential life, and the area of each household unit was 41.01㎡ or 41.39㎡ for each unit in the first building at issue, 40.57㎡ or 41.14㎡ for each unit in the second building at issue, and 43.38㎡ or 40.625㎡ for each unit in the third building at issue, and the site, walls, stairs, corridors, and other facilities of each building at issue were designed and constructed so that each household unit would use them jointly; that around 1990 the Plaintiffs sold each of the above units to Nonparty 3 and five others, and thereafter completed registration of transfer of ownership to each purchaser in the form of transfer of shares according to the area of each household unit in relation to the total floor area of the building (provided, however, that each unit number was indicated after each share description, such as Unit 2 on the first floor, Unit 2 on the second floor, etc.); that thereafter each purchaser moved into the respective household unit and has been carrying on an independent residential life; and that the Head of the Western District Tax Office under the Defendant, with respect to the Plaintiffs’ sale of each of the above units, imposed on Plaintiff 1 value-added tax of 33,510,350 won on 1992.6.16., and on Plaintiff 2 value-added tax of 13,992,070 won on 1991.8.16., on the grounds, inter alia, that each building at issue exceeded the size of national housing as a detached house and therefore did not fall within national housing under Article 74(1)1 of the Tax Exemption and Reduction Control Act; and that Plaintiff 1 paid, over six occasions from 1992. 9. 29. to 1993.6.30., value-added tax of 34,169,350 won and additional tax of 6,065,140 won, totaling 40,234,490 won, while Plaintiff 2 paid, over four occasions from 1993.3.26. to 1993.6.30., value-added tax of 14,575,680 won and additional tax of 2,914,080 won, totaling 17,489,760 won; and then, in response to the Plaintiffs’ claim that, since each building at issue is in substance multi-unit housing and the area of each household unit falls within the size of national housing, value-added tax should have been exempted with respect to its sale under Article 74(1)1 of the Tax Exemption and Reduction Control Act, and that notwithstanding this the disposition of the Western District Tax Office imposing the above value-added tax was void ab initio, the Defendant obtained benefits in an amount equivalent to the above value-added tax and additional tax paid by the Plaintiffs without legal ground and thereby caused the Plaintiffs damage in an equivalent amount, and thus the Defendant is obligated to return to the Plaintiffs an amount equivalent to such benefits, the court below, on the ground that the present action seeking refund of the overpaid tax against the Defendant on the premise that the taxation disposition at issue is void is an action whose content is a public-law right and therefore may be the subject of party litigation, which is administrative litigation, but cannot be the subject of a civil action, dismissed it ex officio as unlawful (the court below further held, by way of an alternative determination, that even if it proceeded to examine the merits, the above taxation disposition, though unlawful, could not be said to be void ab initio, and therefore the Plaintiffs’ claim premised on its being void ab initio lacked merit), but it is the established view of the Supreme Court that a claim for return of taxes already paid on the premise that a tax imposition disposition is void ab initio is a civil claim for restitution of unjust enrichment and must follow civil procedure (see Supreme Court en banc Decision of 1989.6.15. rendered in 88NU6436; Decision of 1990.2.13. rendered in 88NU6610; and Decision of 1991.2.6. in 90PEU2, etc.), so the dismissal of this action by the court below was ultimately erroneous in that it misconstrued the law on unjust enrichment concerning refund of overpaid tax.\\n\\n2. Next, the grounds of appeal are examined.\\nIn order to deem a taxation disposition void ab initio, it is not sufficient that the disposition contain a grave defect; the defect must also be objectively (externally) apparent (see Supreme Court Decision of 1993.5.22. rendered in 91NU12196).\\nAs lawfully found by the court below, although each building at issue is registered in the public records as a “detached house,” it is divided by household unit, and each household unit is independently equipped with living facilities, so that each can conduct an independent residential life; the site, stairs, etc. are to be used jointly by each household unit; and the area of each household unit is 85㎡ or less, so that if it is national housing size, then each unit sold by the Plaintiffs must be deemed to fall under national housing, which is exempt from value-added tax under Article 74(1)1 of the Tax Exemption and Reduction Control Act (as in effect before amendment by Act No. 4666 of 1993.12.31.), and therefore the taxation disposition at issue, by which the Head of the Western District Tax Office under the Defendant imposed value-added tax and additional tax on each of the Plaintiffs’ above sales, had a grave defect; however, under Article 3(3) of the Housing Construction Promotion Act and Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act, the types of multi-unit housing are limited to three: apartment houses, row houses, and multi-family housing, and in light of the fact that each building at issue was registered in the public records as a detached house, and that the very concept of national housing under the Tax Exemption and Reduction Control Act or the Housing Construction Promotion Act is not clear, and that there may be room for dispute in interpreting the statutes as to whether a detached house for multiple households such as the houses at issue constructed by the Plaintiffs should be regarded as multi-unit housing similar to multi-family housing, the taxation disposition at issue is merely a misapprehension of the legal relationship or factual relationship concerning the taxable object, and its defect cannot be said to be objectively apparent (see Supreme Court Decisions of 1995.3.14. rendered in 94DA50106 and of 1995.1.20. rendered in 94DA50113, etc.), and therefore the Plaintiffs’ claim in this action for unjust enrichment premised on the taxation disposition at issue being void ab initio can only be dismissed.\\nThe argument in the grounds of appeal based on a contrary view is independent and cannot be accepted, and the Supreme Court Decision of 1992.3.31. rendered in 91DA32053, cited in support of the grounds of appeal, concerns a different factual situation and is not appropriate for invocation in this case.\\n\\n3. Accordingly, the court below erred in dismissing the present action on the ground that it was unlawful, but, as noted above, because the taxation disposition at issue is not void ab initio, the Plaintiffs’ claim in this action must be dismissed; however, in this case, in which only the Plaintiffs appealed, setting aside the judgment below and dismissing the Plaintiffs’ claim would result in a disadvantage to the Plaintiffs, so the judgment below shall be maintained as is.\\n\\n4. Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal are to be borne by the losing parties. The judgment is so rendered by the concurrence of the Judges participating in the case."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning administrative vicarious execution and compulsion fines are correct? (In case of dispute, according to case law) (a). Where a statute recognizes administrative vicarious execution and a compulsion fine as means of enforcing performance, the administrative agency may use administrative vicarious execution and the compulsion fine selectively, and so long as it selects and uses them in accordance with reasonable discretion, it cannot be regarded as constituting cumulative sanctions. (b). Under the "Building Act," the permitting authority shall set a reasonable deadline necessary for compliance with the corrective order for a building owner, etc. who has failed to comply with a corrective order within the correction period, and if the corrective order is not complied with by that deadline, it shall impose a compulsion fine. (c). An administrative agency may repeatedly impose a compulsion fine until the obligor performs the administrative duty; however, once the obligor performs the duty, it must immediately cease imposing new compulsion fines, and it cannot collect compulsion fines already imposed. (d). Under the "Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects," the obligation of a landowner to deliver land to the project implementer by the commencement date of expropriation or use is not subject to administrative vicarious execution under the "Administrative Vicarious Execution Act."
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2004DA2809]": "The former Land Expropriation Act (which was repealed pursuant to Article 2 of the Addenda to the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects enacted by Act No. 6656 on February 4, 2002 and enforced from January 1, 2003, hereinafter the same) Article 63 provides that “the landowner, interested persons, and any other person who has rights with respect to the land to be expropriated or used, or articles on that land, shall deliver or transfer the land or articles to the project operator by the time of expropriation or use.” Article 64 provides that “when any of the following subparagraphs applies, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall, upon the request of the project operator, arrange for the delivery or transfer of the land or articles,” and subparagraph 1 provides “when the person obligated to deliver or transfer the land or articles is unable to perform the obligation without intent or negligence,” while subparagraph 2 provides “when the project operator is unable, without negligence, to know the person obligated to deliver or transfer the land or articles,” respectively; Article 77 provides that “where a person fails to perform an obligation under this Act or under a disposition pursuant to this Act, or where there is no prospect of completion within the prescribed period, or where there are grounds recognized as significantly harming the public interest by causing the obligor to perform such obligation, the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Do Governor, or the head of the Si/Gun/Gu may, upon the application of the project operator, have such obligation vicariously executed in accordance with the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act.” In the above provisions, “delivery” should be understood to include vacation of possession as well, and such obligation to vacate is one that requires direct exercise of force in order to compulsorily realize it, and therefore cannot be deemed a substitute obligation to perform an act; thus, absent special circumstances, it cannot be subject to vicarious execution under the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act (see Supreme Court Decision 97NU157, decided October 23, 1998). Furthermore, although the obligation of the expropriatee, etc. under Article 63 of the former Land Expropriation Act to deliver the land subject to expropriation or to vacate obstacles thereon to the project operator is a legal relationship under public law, a provisional disposition ordering delivery, with the right to such delivery serving as the preserved right, should be deemed permissible when necessary to avoid serious damage to that right, to prevent imminent danger, or for other necessary reasons.\\n\\nThe court below, on the basis of the factual relations as determined in the judgment and recognized through a comprehensive consideration of the evidence cited in its reasoning, first determined that the Debtors have the obligation, pursuant to the expropriation ruling in this case and Articles 31 and 32 of the Urban Redevelopment Act and Article 63 of the former Land Expropriation Act, to vacate the respective occupied portions of the building in this case in favor of the Creditor. It then addressed the Debtors’ argument that, because the Creditor has been provided with a separate remedy by which such a right to demand delivery may be realized through administrative vicarious execution, there is no benefit of filing in this provisional disposition application, and rejected it by determining that the obligation to vacate separately borne by the Debtors to the Creditor is, by its nature, a so-called non-substitutable obligation to perform an act that cannot be vicariously executed in accordance with Article 77 of the former Land Expropriation Act and the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act. Further, in light of the various circumstances set forth in its reasoning, it found that the necessity for preservation was sufficiently established for this provisional disposition application and thus granted the Creditor’s application for a provisional disposition ordering delivery in this case. Upon review of the record, the court below’s measures are consistent with the foregoing legal principles and are therefore justifiable, and there is no illegality such as a misapprehension of law concerning the procedural requirements, necessity for preservation, or Articles 63 and 77 of the former Land Expropriation Act in an application for this type of provisional disposition ordering delivery, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the ground for appeal asserting that the court below committed an error in jurisdiction by treating and disposing of the application for a provisional disposition ordering delivery, with the right to demand delivery arising under Article 63 of the former Land Expropriation Act as the preserved right, as a general civil case despite the clear administrative nature of the case, is likewise merely an independent view and cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAccordingly, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties, and judgment is rendered as ordered."}

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are true (○) and those that are false (×) regarding administrative subjects and administrative agencies in administrative-law relations? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law) (a). Under the Urban and Residential Environment Maintenance Act, a housing reconstruction and maintenance project association, if it becomes established as a corporation by registration after obtaining authorization for establishment of the association from the competent administrative agency, has the status of an administrative subject that, within the scope of the purpose of implementing the housing reconstruction project, performs certain administrative acts in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. (b). Seoul Housing and Communities Corporation, as a public corporation established by Seoul Metropolitan City through a 100% capital contribution pursuant to the Local Public Enterprises Act, may be regarded as an administrative agency to which Seoul Metropolitan City has delegated the authority to implement Seoul Metropolitan City's development projects through its act of establishment, etc. (c). The granting or revocation of a trainer's or jockey's license by the Korea Racing Authority is the exercise of authority as an administrative agency entrusted by the State or any other administrative agency. (d). A local association of judicial scriveners is a public juridical person whose establishment and membership in the judicial scrivener association are compulsory by law in order to perform supervisory affairs for judicial scriveners, and, insofar as it concerns approval for the hiring of a judicial scrivener's clerk, it should be regarded as the subject of the exercise of public authority. (e). Korea Land Corporation is a person empowered to carry out substitute execution by virtue of the entrustment under the Act on the Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects, the former Korea Land Corporation Act, and the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and it should be regarded as having the status of an administrative subject to whom the rights, duties, and liabilities arising from carrying out substitute execution by public officials accrue, rather than as a public official under Article 2 of the State Compensation Act as an organ of a local government, etc.
