As a result, the general public cannot, from this provision under review alone, even predict the basic outline of the content and scope to be prescribed by the Korean Standard Industrial Classification, apart from the fact that the delegated subject concerns the classification of business types.\\n\\nAs noted above, considering that depending on how a business type is classified, the content and scope of the tax obligations of the general public engaged in that business type may differ, this is excessively abstract and comprehensive; such an attitude of the legislator is nothing other than a relinquishment of the task entrusted to it by the Constitution, and in the end it will result in giving the executive branch excessively broad legislative discretion, thereby exposing the people to an unstable state vulnerable to arbitrary administrative legislation.\\n\\nThe majority opinion states that even if the classification of business types follows the Korean Standard Industrial Classification, it does not infringe the public’s predictability, but this can only be possible on the premise that, after the classification was first publicly notified, it does not change except for minor matters.\\n\\nSince its enactment in 1963, the Korean Standard Industrial Classification has undergone nine revisions to reflect revisions to the International Standard Industrial Classification and changes in domestic industrial structure and technology. Looking at the major revisions, during the second revision on 1 February 1968, a comprehensive reorganization of the commercial sector was carried out, and during the third revision on 13 March 1970, the classification system and its contents were completely reorganized in accordance with the revision of the International Standard Industrial Classification; during the fourth and fifth revisions, the classification contents were substantially improved to respond to changes in industrial structure due to economic growth; and during the sixth revision on 9 September 1991, the classification system and contents were reorganized again in accordance with the revision of the International Standard Industrial Classification. Thereafter, during the eighth revision on 7 January 2000, in order to reflect changes in industrial structure due to the specialization and diversification of industrial activities, the overall classification system was adjusted, including the creation of new industries such as semiconductor-related industries, telecommunication industries, and financial service industries, the upgrading of communication industries and service industries to major categories, and the creation of repair business as a medium category; and during the ninth revision on 28 December 2007, information and communication-related industries scattered across various industries were newly established as a single major category, while, in light of the importance of environment-related industries, sewage and wastewater treatment, material recycling, and environmental restoration business were newly established as a separate major category.\\n\\nAs such, the Korean Standard Industrial Classification is subject to large-scale revisions by the Commissioner of Statistics Korea from time to time in order to reflect the emergence of new industries, changes in industrial structure, and the linkage among related classifications, and it may be said that its classification system and contents are being substantially reorganized or changed as a result of such revisions. Considering the nature of administrative rules that can be established quietly without being subjected to review, correction, control, or supervision by other agencies in the process of their formation, and without debate or amendment by the people or their representative body, it is all the more difficult to expect ordinary persons to sufficiently predict the general outline of the content and scope to be prescribed in the Korean Standard Industrial Classification.\\n\\nFor the foregoing reasons, the provision under review also violates the prohibition on blanket delegation set forth in Article 75 of the Constitution.\\n\\nc. Therefore, the provision under review not only fails to satisfy the form of delegated legislation prescribed by the Constitution, but also violates the prohibition on blanket delegation, and thus cannot but be said to be in violation of the Constitution. However, if simple unconstitutionality were declared with respect to the provision under review, there is concern that a serious legal vacuum would arise in which heavy taxation or tax reduction would not be possible before ameliorative legislation is prepared; in order to prevent this, it is desirable to declare the provision under review inconsistent with the Constitution and urge ameliorative legislation."}

{"[2019DU35695]": "We decide the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Outline of the case\\n   a. The Plaintiffs, together with their parents, own all issued shares of Duyang Housing Co., Ltd. and Duyang Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “each of the companies in this case”).\\n   b. The Defendants, deeming that the Plaintiffs, as shareholders, obtained a benefit prescribed in Article 41 of the former Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (before amendment by Act No. 12168 of January 1, 2014 and before amendment by Act No. 13557 of December 15, 2015, hereinafter referred to as “the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act”) because the Plaintiffs’ father, the non-party, gratuitously loaned money to each of the companies in this case in 2014 and 2015, calculated the value of the gifted property pursuant to Article 31(6) of the former Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 25195 of February 21, 2014 and before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 26960 of February 5, 2016, hereinafter referred to as “the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act”), and imposed gift tax on the Plaintiffs respectively on gifts dated January 1, 2014 and January 1, 2015 (hereinafter referred to as “each of the dispositions in this case”).\\n\\n2. Amendment of the related statutes and regulations following the Supreme Court decision declaring Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment null and void\\n   a. Supreme Court decisions\\n      1) Article 41(1) of the former Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (before amendment by Act No. 9916 of January 1, 2010, hereinafter referred to as “the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2010 amendment”) provided that “where a person in a special relationship with shareholders, etc. of a corporation with a deficit or under temporary suspension of business or closure (a specified corporation) enters into a transaction, etc. of gratuitous provision of property or services with the specified corporation and, as a result, the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation obtain a benefit, the amount equivalent to such benefit shall be deemed the value of the gifted property of the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation.” Article 31(6) of the former Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 18177 of December 30, 2003 and before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 25195 of February 21, 2014, hereinafter referred to as “the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment”), enacted pursuant to the delegation under Article 41(2) of the same Act, provided that the benefit under Article 41(1) of the Act shall be calculated by multiplying the value of the gifted property, etc. of the specified corporation by the ratio of the shares, etc. held by its largest shareholder, etc.\\n\\n         The en banc Supreme Court decision rendered on March 19, 2009 in Case No. 2006DU19693 held that, although Article 41(1) of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2010 amendment delegated only the calculation of the benefit to the Enforcement Decree on the premise that the largest shareholder, etc. obtained a benefit through certain transactions with the specified corporation, Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment treated the benefit obtained by the specified corporation itself as the benefit obtained by the shareholders, etc. and calculated the value of the gifted property accordingly, and for that reason, the said provision of the Enforcement Decree not only ran contrary to the purpose of the parent statute but also exceeded the scope of delegation, and was therefore null and void.\\n\\n      2) Article 41(1) of the former Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (amended by Act No. 9916 of January 1, 2010 and before amendment by Act No. 12168 of January 1, 2014, hereinafter referred to as “the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment”) changed the existing phrase “where the shareholders, etc. of a specified corporation obtain a benefit” to “where they obtain a benefit prescribed by Presidential Decree,” but Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment, which the Supreme Court had held null and void as above, remained in force until it was amended by Presidential Decree No. 25195 of February 21, 2014.\\n\\n         The en banc Supreme Court decision rendered on April 20, 2017 in Case No. 2015DU45700 held, on substantially the same reasoning as the above Supreme Court decision in Case No. 2006DU19693, that Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment, enacted pursuant to the delegation under Article 41(1) of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment, likewise not only ran contrary to the purpose of the parent statute but also exceeded the scope of delegation, and was therefore null and void.\\n\\n   b. Amendment of the statutes and regulations related to 2014 and their content\\n      1) Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act provides that “where a person in a special relationship with the shareholders, etc. of a corporation with a deficit or under temporary suspension of business or closure, or with the controlling shareholder and his/her relatives under Article 45-3(1), engages in a transaction, etc. of gratuitous provision of property or services with the specified corporation (a specified corporation) and, as a result, the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation obtain a benefit prescribed by Presidential Decree, the amount equivalent to such benefit shall be deemed the value of the gifted property of the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation.” The said provision, while being identical in structure to Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment, added “a profit-making corporation controlled by the controlling shareholder and his/her relatives under Article 45-3(1)” to the definition of a specified corporation.\\n\\n      2) Accordingly, Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act provides that the phrase “benefit prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 41(1) of the Act means “the amount calculated by multiplying the amount obtained by deducting from the value of the gifted property, etc. the amount calculated by multiplying the amount obtained by subtracting the amount of corporate tax credits, reductions, and exemptions from the calculated tax amount under Article 55(1) of the Corporate Tax Act of the specified corporation (excluding the corporate tax amount on gains from transfer of land, etc. under Article 55-2 of the same Act) by the ratio that the amount of income for each business year bears to the value of the gifted property, etc. (if it exceeds 1, then 1), by the ratio of shares, etc. held by the largest shareholder, etc. (limited to cases where the relevant amount is not less than 100 million won).”\\n\\n3. Regarding Ground of Final Appeal No. 2\\n   a. Determination on whether Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act is null and void\\n      1) The principle of statutory taxation means that matters concerning the taxpayer’s duty to pay taxes, such as tax requirements, must be prescribed by statute enacted by the National Assembly, the representative organ of the people, and that, even when such statute is executed, it must be strictly construed and applied, and that administrative interpretations or analogical applications for the convenience of administration are not permitted. Therefore, prescribing matters concerning tax requirements, etc. by administrative legislation such as orders or rules without statutory delegation, or preparing interpretive provisions that arbitrarily construe or expand the contents provided in a statute, is contrary to the principle of statutory taxation (see Supreme Court en banc decision rendered on May 17, 2007 in Case No. 2006DU8648).\\n\\n      2) In light of such legal principles, it is reasonable to regard Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act as null and void, since it not only runs contrary to the purport of Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, which is the parent statute, but also exceeds the scope of delegation. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\n         a) Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act merely expanded the scope of specified corporations, while the remaining tax requirements were regulated identically to the pre-amendment version, and thus it must still be viewed as a provision premised on the fact that the shareholders, etc. obtained a benefit from the gratuitous provision of property, etc. to the specified corporation, which constitutes gifted property under the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act; and since the counterparty to the gratuitous provision of property, etc. is the specified corporation, the benefit that the shareholders, etc. may obtain thereby can hardly be conceived as anything other than the increase in the value of the specified corporation shares, etc. they hold.\\n\\n         b) Accordingly, despite the partial amendment of its wording, Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act should be regarded, like the pre-amendment version, as a provision delegating to the Presidential Decree only matters concerning the proper method of calculating the benefit, namely, “the increase in the value of the specified corporation shares, etc. held by the shareholders, etc.”, on the premise that the shareholders, etc. obtained a benefit through transactions, etc. with the specified corporation, such as the gratuitous provision of property.\\n\\n         c) Meanwhile, even where a person in a special relationship with the shareholders, etc. of a specified corporation enters into a transaction gifting property to the specified corporation, if the value of the shares, etc. held by the shareholders, etc. does not increase before and after the transaction, there is no benefit obtained by such shareholders, etc., and therefore gift tax cannot be imposed on the basis of Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act. Even if the value of the shares, etc. held by the shareholders, etc. increases before and after such a transaction, if the value of the gifted property to the specified corporation exceeds the increase in the value of the shares, etc., it must likewise be deemed that the shareholders, etc. have no benefit with respect to the excess portion, and gift tax cannot be imposed on that portion.\\n\\n         d) However, Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act was partially changed in content by deducting from the value of the gifted property a certain amount of corporate tax borne by the specified corporation, in consideration that, as Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act expanded the scope of specified corporations, corporate tax on the corporation’s income and gift tax on the benefits of its shareholders, etc. may be imposed together in relation to the relevant transaction. Nevertheless, it remains the same as Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment in that, where there is a transaction involving the gratuitous provision of property, etc. to a specified corporation, it deems that the shareholders, etc. have obtained a benefit by that fact alone and imposes the duty to pay gift tax regardless of whether the shareholders, etc. actually obtained any benefit or the extent thereof.\\n\\n         e) Ultimately, Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act likewise runs contrary to the purport of Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, which is the parent statute, and also exceeds the scope of delegation, thereby creating a tax requirement that, under the principle of statutory taxation, ought properly to be prescribed by the National Assembly by statute; it is therefore reasonable to regard it as null and void.\\n\\n      3) On the same reasoning, the court below correctly held that Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act is null and void, in accordance with the legal principles discussed above, and there is no error such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the limits of delegated legislation, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n   b. Determination on whether the disposition imposing gift tax on the 2014 gift portion is unlawful\\n      The court below, for the reasons stated in the judgment, held that among each of the dispositions in this case, the disposition imposing gift tax on the 2014 gift portion was made on the view that the non-party’s gratuitous loan of money to each of the companies in this case constituted a gift of benefits to the Plaintiffs on January 1, 2014; however, since only the invalid Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before the 2014 amendment was in force at the time of the said gift date, the disposition was made solely on the basis of the said statutory provision, which delegated tax-imposition requirements to the Enforcement Decree in a situation where no Enforcement Decree had yet been enacted for taxation related to the specified corporations expanded under Article 41 of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, and thus was unlawful in light of the principle of statutory taxation and the principle against retroactive taxation.\\n\\n      Examining the facts found by the court below in light of the relevant provisions and legal principles, the court below’s determination is proper, and there is no error such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the scope of application of Article 41 of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n   c. Determination on whether the disposition imposing gift tax on the 2015 gift portion is unlawful\\n      1) The court below held that the disposition imposing gift tax on the 2015 gift portion among each of the dispositions in this case was unlawful because it was based on Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, which is null and void, for the following reasons.\\n\\n         a) The disposition imposing gift tax on the 2015 gift portion was made on the view that there was a gift of benefit to the Plaintiffs on January 1, 2015; however, Article 31(6) of the 2014-amended Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, which was in force at the time, is null and void because it runs contrary to the purport of Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, the parent statute, and exceeds the scope of delegation. Accordingly, the method of calculating the increase in the value of the specified corporation shares, etc. held by the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation, which is the “benefit prescribed by Presidential Decree” under Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, falls into a lacuna not specifically provided for by Presidential Decree.\\n\\n         b) In such a case, gift tax cannot be imposed in accordance with the principle of statutory taxation. By contrast, applying supplementary valuation methods under the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act in order to calculate the increase in the value of the specified corporation shares, etc. held by the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation would arbitrarily construe or expand the wording of Article 41(1) and (2) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, which states, “where the benefit prescribed by Presidential Decree is obtained, the amount equivalent to such benefit shall be deemed the value of the gifted property of the shareholders, etc. of the specified corporation, and the calculation thereof, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree,” and would therefore be contrary to the principle of statutory taxation.\\n\\n      2) In light of the relevant provisions and legal principles, the court below’s determination is proper, and there is no error such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the scope of application of Article 41 of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n4. Regarding Ground of Final Appeal No. 1\\n   The gist of this ground of final appeal is that, as of January 1, 2014 and January 1, 2015, Duyang Housing Co., Ltd. had no deficit, and therefore did not fall under a specified corporation prescribed in Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, but the court below held otherwise.\\n\\n   However, as stated above, since each of Article 31(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act before and after the 2014 amendment is null and void, gift tax cannot be imposed on the Plaintiffs based solely on Article 41(1) of the 2014-amended Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act, which is the parent statute. Therefore, the Defendants’ above ground of final appeal cannot affect the conclusion of the judgment and is without merit, without need for further review.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\n   Accordingly, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices, as stated in the judgment."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning constitutional complaints and administrative litigation is incorrect? (In cases of dispute, according to precedents)
A: Even if an administrative rule, as a standard for the exercise of discretionary power, is repeatedly implemented in accordance with its terms and thereby forms an administrative practice, the administrative agency, in its relationship with the other party, is subject to self-binding to follow that rule; accordingly, such an administrative rule constitutes the exercise of public power with external binding force and is subject to a constitutional complaint.
B: In a detention review case, when the defense counsel for a suspect requested inspection and copying of the complaint and the suspect interrogation record among the investigative records, and the chief of the police station issued a decision not to disclose the information, if the counsel filed a constitutional complaint seeking a ruling that the non-disclosure decision is unconstitutional without filing administrative litigation, the principle of subsidiarity, which is a requirement for filing a constitutional complaint, is satisfied.
C: Since an omission of administrative legislation may be challenged by an action to confirm the illegality of omission under the Administrative Litigation Act, a petition for constitutional adjudication concerning an omission of administrative legislation is an unlawful petition that violates the principle of subsidiarity.
D: Since a decision by the head of a Veterans Affairs Office that a person does not qualify as a person of distinguished service to the State constitutes a disposition, there are relief procedures of administrative appeal and administrative litigation against it, and if a constitutional complaint adjudication is filed without going through such procedures, the petition is unlawful because it was filed without exhausting all relief procedures under other statutes.
E: If a person filed administrative litigation seeking revocation of a tax assessment disposition and then withdrew the action or the withdrawal was deemed to have occurred, a petition for constitutional adjudication seeking revocation of the tax assessment disposition cannot be regarded as having gone through lawful relief procedures under other statutes and is therefore unlawful.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2000HEONMA474]": "[Separate Attachment]\\nSummary of the Opinions of the Respondent and Related Agency\\n\\n1. Summary of the Respondent’s Response\\nArticle 47 of the Criminal Procedure Act provides that documents relating to litigation may not be disclosed before the opening of the trial unless there is a need in the public interest or other substantial reason. The Petitioner, on 2000. 5. 29., before the prosecutor instituted a prosecution against Kim ○-eok, requested inspection and copying of the complaint and the suspect interrogation report among the investigation records concerning Kim ○-eok. Since the Petitioner’s request for disclosure of information in this case was for defense as counsel and preparation for review of the legality of detention, and it is difficult to say that there is a need in the public interest or other substantial reason, the Respondent made the decision not to disclose the information in this case; therefore, the decision not to disclose the information in this case is lawful because it is based on the law.\\n\\n2. Summary of the Opinion of the Prosecutor General of the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office\\nIf inspection and copying of investigation records before indictment are allowed to the suspect, the following problems arise.\\nFirst, while the suspect is guaranteed the right to remain silent and may conceal means of defense, all of the prosecutor’s means of attack, for which the prosecutor bears the full burden of proof with respect to the facts charged, would be disclosed, thereby upsetting the balance of power and placing the prosecutor in an unfairly disadvantageous position, in violation of the principle of equality of arms.\\nSecond, allowing the suspect or his or her counsel to inspect evidence documents or exhibits for which the prosecutor has not yet decided whether to submit as evidence before indictment is not appropriate even in light of the principle of adversarial proceedings, under which each party must collect and prove evidence at its own responsibility.\\nThird, if inspection of investigation records is allowed before indictment, it will create the risk of leakage of investigative secrecy, and such leakage of investigative secrecy will encourage fugitives to flee, conceal evidence, and aid accomplices in escape, thereby impeding investigations of related cases and supplementary investigations after indictment. In particular, if accomplices or key informants are disclosed, further progress in the investigation will become impossible. There is also concern that the suspect side may use the leaked evidence to induce informants, tamper with evidence, or conceal evidence, and if statements of persons related to the case are reported through the media, there is a risk of adverse side effects, such as improperly influencing witnesses or the court later. In particular, in crimes such as gang violence crimes and sexual violence crimes, victims, witnesses, and others may frequently hesitate to report or testify for fear of retaliation from the suspect, his or her family, or members of the organization.\\nBecause of the above problems, Article 47 of the current Criminal Procedure Act also provides the principle of non-disclosure of litigation documents by stipulating that litigation documents may not be disclosed before the opening of the trial, and therefore the decision not to disclose the information in this case cannot be said to be unconstitutional."}

A manufacturing enterprise that has completed factory registration (small enterprises falling under Article 4(1) of the Special Measures Act for the Support of Small Enterprises and Small-Scale Businesses may do so through business registration)\\n\\nArticle 32 (Allocation of industrial trainees, etc.) ① The President of the Federation shall allocate industrial trainees in consideration of the requirements of training enterprises, the abilities of industrial trainees, and the industries of the sending countries.  \\n② The number of trainees, etc. of a training enterprise shall not exceed the permissible number by size of small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprise determined by the Minister of Justice pursuant to Article 24-2(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Control Act (Attached Table 2).\\n\\nArticle 33 (Training at training enterprises) ① - ② omitted  \\n③ Training enterprises shall provide, for at least 8 hours, education on industrial safety, methods of operating machinery and equipment, and local living information, etc. to newly allocated industrial trainees; during the industrial training and trainee-employment periods, they shall regularly provide education on industrial safety, etc.\\n\\nArticle 35 (Training management expenses, etc.) ① When the President of the Federation concludes, pursuant to Articles 31 and 34, a contract concerning the introduction and management of training enterprises and industrial trainees, he/she may receive training management expenses from the training enterprise.  \\n② - ⑤ omitted\\n\\nArticle 38 (Conclusion of contracts) ① The Federation, sending agencies, training enterprises, and trainees, etc. shall conclude between the parties the contracts necessary in relation to the implementation of the business under these Guidelines, and the President of the Federation shall establish standard contracts so that the contracting parties may use them. Provided, that with respect to contracts concerning trainee-employment when an industrial trainee is converted into a trainee-employment person, the “Regulations on the Protection and Management of Foreign Trainee-Employment Persons” shall apply.  \\n② The contents of the contracts between the parties concluded pursuant to paragraph 1 shall not be contrary to the contents of these Guidelines as in force at the time of conclusion.\\n\\nc. The Ministry of Labor Directive in this case\\n\\nThe Petitioner seeks adjudication with respect to the entire Ministry of Labor Directive in this case, but the provisions relevant to the fundamental rights infringement alleged by the Petitioner are as follows.\\n\\nArticle 4 (Status of trainees) Trainees shall have the status of sojourners as trainees under the Immigration Control statutes and regulations, but in cases where, during the training process, they receive compensation for labor under any designation, such as wages or allowances, by providing de facto labor due to the characteristics of on-site training, they shall have rights and duties as workers within the scope prescribed by these Guidelines.\\n\\nArticle 8 (Protection of trainees) ① Trainees shall be protected with respect to the following matters, in reference to the basic legislative spirit of the Labor Standards Act, the Minimum Wage Act, the Industrial Safety and Health Act, the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act, and the Medical Insurance Act.  \\n1. Prohibition of assault and compulsory labor  \\n2. Periodic, direct, full, and cash payment of training allowances and settlement of monetary claims  \\n3. Training period, recess and holidays, overtime, night work, and holiday training  \\n4. Guarantee of minimum wage level  \\n5. Securing industrial safety and health  \\n6. Benefits under industrial accident compensation insurance and medical insurance  \\n② omitted\\n\\nArticle 17 (Supervision and sanctions) ① The head of the local labor office shall provide administrative guidance so that employers comply with these Guidelines.  \\n② If the head of the local labor office determines that an employer does not comply with the administrative guidance under paragraph 1, he/she may request the head of the trainee-recommending organization to take necessary measures, such as suspension of trainee allocation, with respect to the relevant workplace, and the head of the trainee-recommending organization may not refuse such request without justifiable grounds.  \\n③ Notwithstanding the administrative guidance under paragraph 1, if the employer continues to violate these Guidelines, the head of the local labor office may conduct special supervision, and as a result of such special supervision, with respect to violations of Articles 6, 7, 36, 42, 49, 53 through 55, 104 through 116 of the Labor Standards Act, the Minimum Wage Act, the Industrial Safety and Health Act, and the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act, measures shall be taken in accordance with the relevant statutes and regulations.\\n\\n2. Relevant statutory provisions\\n\\na. Immigration Control Act (as amended by Act No. 7034 on December 31, 2003)\\n\\nArticle 17 (Scope of sojourn and activities of foreigners) ① A foreigner may sojourn in the Republic of Korea within the scope of his/her status of sojourn and period of sojourn.  \\n\\nArticle 18 (Restrictions on the employment of foreigners) ① When a foreigner intends to work in the Republic of Korea, he/she shall obtain a status of sojourn permitting work activities, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.  \\n② A foreigner having the status of sojourn under paragraph 1 shall not work outside the designated workplace.  \\n③ No person shall employ a person who does not have the status of sojourn under paragraph 1.  \\n④ - ⑤ omitted\\n\\nArticle 19-2 (Protection, etc. of industrial trainees) ① The Government shall take necessary measures to protect foreigners (hereinafter referred to as “industrial trainees”) who have the status of sojourn permitting industrial training activities pursuant to Article 10 and are training at designated industrial enterprises.  \\n② Matters necessary for the designation of industrial enterprises under paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.\\n\\nArticle 19-3 (Management of industrial trainees, etc.) ① The Minister of Justice shall investigate whether industrial trainees have departed from their training places, engaged in activities other than the purpose of training, or violated other permitted conditions, and shall take necessary measures for the management of industrial trainees, such as departure of the foreigner.  \\n② Matters necessary concerning the management of industrial trainees and the recruitment related to their entry into the country under paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.  \\n③ The Minister of Justice may grant permission to change the status of sojourn so that industrial trainees who satisfy the requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as “trainee-employment persons” in this paragraph) may engage in work activities. In such case, the provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the management of trainee-employment persons.\\n\\nArticle 21 (Change or addition of workplace) ① When a foreigner staying in the Republic of Korea intends to change or add his/her workplace within the scope of his/her status of sojourn, he/she shall obtain prior permission from the Minister of Justice.  \\n② No person shall employ, or arrange employment for, a foreigner who has not obtained permission for change or addition of workplace under paragraph 1. Provided, that this shall not apply where employment is arranged under other statutes.  \\n\\nArticle 22 (Restriction on scope of activities) Where the Minister of Justice deems it necessary for the public peace and order or important interests of the Republic of Korea, he/she may restrict the place of residence or scope of activities of a foreigner staying in the Republic of Korea or establish other necessary observance matters.\\n\\nb. Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Control Act (as amended by Presidential Decree No. 15764 on April 1, 1998, and before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 18934 on July 5, 2005; although it was partially amended several times during the above period, its basic content is not significantly different)\\n\\nArticle 23 (Employment of foreigners and status of sojourn) ① The term “status of sojourn permitting work activities” in Article 18(1) of the Act means the status of sojourn set forth in Attached Table 1, 9. Short-Term Employment (C-4), 19. Professor (E-1) through 25. Specific Activities (E-7), and 25-2. Trainee Employment (E-8).\\n\\nArticle 24-2 (Industrial trainee enterprises, etc.) ① Pursuant to Article 19-2 of the Act, the industrial enterprises where foreigners may engage in industrial training activities shall be as follows:  \\n1. Industrial enterprises directly invested in foreign countries pursuant to Article 3(1)15 of the Foreign Exchange Control Act  \\n2. Industrial enterprises exporting technology to foreign countries pursuant to Article 10-2 of the Technology Development Promotion Act  \\n3. Industrial enterprises exporting industrial facilities to foreign countries pursuant to Article 22(1) of the Foreign Trade Act  \\n4. Industrial enterprises recommended by the head of an industrial enterprise-related organization or association designated and publicly notified by the head of the competent central administrative agency (hereinafter referred to as the “trainee-recommending organization”), other than those under items 1 through 3  \\n② Where the scale of introduction of industrial trainees is determined pursuant to Article 24-3(2)1, the head of the trainee-recommending organization shall determine the scale of industrial trainees to be allocated to each industrial enterprise in accordance with the standards determined by the Minister of Justice and shall notify the head of the competent central administrative agency thereof.\\n\\nArticle 24-3 (Foreign Industrial Workforce Policy Deliberation Committee) ① In order to deliberate and coordinate important matters concerning foreign industrial training and trainee-employment systems, the Foreign Industrial Workforce Policy Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Committee” in this Article and Article 24-4) shall be established under the Prime Minister.  \\n② The Committee shall deliberate and coordinate the following matters:  \\n1. Determination of the scale of introduction of industrial trainees who intend to train at industrial enterprises pursuant to Article 24-2(1)4 and important matters concerning recruitment management  \\n2. Important matters concerning the management of persons who, as industrial trainees, satisfy the trainee-employment requirements under Article 24-5(1) and are permitted to work (hereinafter referred to as “trainee-employment persons”) and matters concerning trainee-employment requirements, etc.  \\n3. Other matters which the chairperson of the Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Chairperson” in this Article) or a member deems necessary regarding foreign industrial training or trainee-employment and refers to the Committee  \\n③ The chairperson of the Committee shall be the Minister for Government Coordination, and the members shall be the Vice Ministers of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Science and Technology, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Energy, the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the Ministry of Labor, the Ministry of Construction and Transportation, and the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, and the Administrator of the Small and Medium Business Administration.  \\n④ In order to process the affairs of the Committee, one executive secretary shall be assigned to the Committee, and the executive secretary shall be designated by the Chairperson from among the directors-level public officials of the institution to which the Chairperson belongs.  \\n⑤ A working council may be established within the Committee to preliminarily review matters subject to the Committee’s deliberation and to process matters delegated by the Committee.  \\n⑥ Other matters necessary for the operation of the Committee and the composition and operation of the working council shall be determined by the Chairperson after deliberation by the Committee.\\n\\nArticle 24-5 (Trainee-employment requirements, etc.) ① A person who intends to obtain permission to change status of sojourn pursuant to Article 19-3(3) of the Act shall satisfy the following requirements:  \\n1. He/she shall have passed a technical qualification examination under the National Technical Qualifications Act or a technical qualification examination equivalent thereto  \\n2. He/she shall have trained for 2 years as an industrial trainee at an industrial enterprise under Article 24-2(1)4  \\n3. He/she shall satisfy other trainee-employment requirements determined by the head of the competent central administrative agency  \\n② A person who receives permission to change status of sojourn into trainee-employment status pursuant to paragraph 1 shall work at the industrial enterprise where he/she worked as an industrial trainee. Provided, that this shall not apply where the consent of the head of that industrial enterprise has been obtained or where other justifiable grounds are recognized.\\n\\n[Appendix 2] Summary of the Petitioner’s claims and the opinions of the relevant agencies\\n\\na. Summary of the Petitioner’s claims\\n\\n(1) The current industrial trainee system, which makes industrial trainees who entered the country with a status of sojourn for training under the Immigration Control Act actually engage in employment without any legal basis, determines the domestic legal status of foreigners without relying on international law or treaties, and thus violates Article 6(2) of the Constitution.\\n\\n(2) Under the current industrial trainee system, although foreign industrial trainees are in substance engaging in employment activities as workers rather than as trainees, by preventing them from freely choosing their workplace during the training period, it infringes the freedom to choose one’s workplace in violation of Article 15 of the Constitution.\\n\\n(3) Foreign workers who enter the country in the status of industrial trainees and are in fact engaging in employment activities as workers have no freedom to choose their workplace and therefore cannot negotiate wages; consequently, they can receive only the minimum wage. Such an industrial trainee system violates the social market economy order under Article 119 of the Constitution.\\n\\n(4) Meanwhile, the Ministry of Labor Directive in this case excludes the application of important provisions of the Labor Standards Act to industrial trainees (for example, the retirement allowance system and preferential satisfaction of wage claims), thereby discriminating against industrial trainees as compared with Korean workers or foreign workers who are not industrial trainees, and thereby infringing the right to equality.\\n\\nb. Opinion of the Administrator of the Small and Medium Business Administration\\n\\n(1) Regarding the admissibility requirements\\n\\n(a) Because the Petitioner is a foreigner and cannot be recognized as a bearer of fundamental rights, this constitutional complaint is unlawful. That is, since the Petitioner is a foreign industrial trainee, in the absence of a legislative decision recognizing industrial trainees as workers under the current law, he/she cannot be recognized as a worker in the legal system of the Republic of Korea; ultimately, the Petitioner cannot assert a right to equal treatment with workers of the Republic of Korea in terms of working conditions or the freedom to choose an occupation.\\n\\n(b) In order for an infringement of fundamental rights to occur with respect to industrial trainees, a series of contractual acts (a contract in which the industrial trainee enters into a contract with the sending agency, receives entry permission into the country, and receives training at the training enterprise) and acts of contract execution by related organizations such as the Korea Federation of Small and Medium Business Cooperatives must exist; therefore, the Petitioner’s fundamental rights are not directly infringed by the Public Notice of the Small and Medium Business Administration in this case alone.\\n\\n(c) The measures of the Deliberation Committee in this case are merely non-binding administrative plans and do not constitute an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint. In addition, the Public Notice of the Small and Medium Business Administration in this case is merely an internal work-processing guideline of the Small and Medium Business Administration that specifies matters related to the overall operation of the industrial trainee system pursuant to delegation under the Immigration Control statutes and regulations, and cannot be said to have regulatory effect; the Ministry of Labor Directive in this case was also enacted by the Ministry of Labor for the protection and management of industrial trainees without delegation from statutes and regulations, and therefore has no external binding force, so all of them cannot be subject to constitutional complaint proceedings.\\n\\n(d) The Ministry of Labor Directive in this case prescribes the minimum level of protection that training enterprises must observe, and does not compel training enterprises to treat industrial trainees only within the scope set forth in the Ministry of Labor Directive in this case; therefore, the Petitioner’s fundamental rights are not infringed thereby.\\n\\n(e) The Petitioner is an illegal sojourner who departed without authorization while receiving training at a training enterprise in the status of industrial trainee. The Petitioner, as an illegal sojourner without public-law status to stay in the Republic of Korea, is filing this constitutional complaint for the purpose of evading compulsory departure; this is an unlawful action contrary to the principle of good faith and should be dismissed pursuant to the Civil Procedure Act, as applied mutatis mutandis by Article 40 of the Constitutional Court Act.\\n\\n(f) The Petitioner is deemed to have already known, at the time of entry into the Republic of Korea, the status of industrial trainees prescribed in the Public Notice of the Small and Medium Business Administration and the Ministry of Labor Directive in this case; accordingly, this constitutional complaint was filed in August 2004, more than 90 days after March 16, 2004, when the Petitioner entered the country, and therefore the filing period has been exceeded.\\n\\n(2) Regarding the merits\\n\\n(a) Even if the Government, by setting a certain scope (guidelines) for the industrial trainee relationship, which is a private contract between private persons, has made a distinction in the application of the Labor Standards Act between industrial trainees and workers at workplaces with five or more employees, this is merely a rational distinction arising from the characteristics of the industrial trainee system (for example, the fact that rational discrimination may be widely recognized in the realm of social fundamental rights, and the fact that foreign industrial trainees have a special status different from domestic workers).\\n\\n(b) Since even foreign professionals and technical workers can perform their occupations only at the times and places determined under the Immigration Control Act and do not have the same freedom of occupational choice and performance as Korean nationals, it cannot be said that restricting the training place for industrial trainees fundamentally undermines the freedom to choose an occupation.\\n\\n(c) Since the hourly labor cost paid to industrial trainees is, in fact, higher relative to productivity even though industrial trainees have lower productivity than domestic workers, the industrial trainee system does not infringe the Petitioner’s right to equality or run counter to the market economy principle.\\n\\nc. Opinion of the Minister of Justice\\n\\n(1) The current industrial trainee system operates as a trainee-employment system consisting of 1 year of training and 2 years of employment, and may be said to be a compromise between the industrial training system and the employment permit system; during the 1 year of training, they receive treatment equivalent to that of domestic workers except for retirement allowances and monthly and annual leave allowances, and during the 2 years of employment, they receive treatment equivalent to that of domestic workers. Even if working conditions are applied differently to foreign workers in the status of industrial trainees during the training period, the training period before employment is necessary for acquiring the Korean language and technology, and thus this cannot be regarded as unreasonable discrimination.\\n\\n(2) As to the introduction of foreign labor, the selection of which system to adopt falls within the legislative discretion of the legislature. Restricting the period of stay and the freedom to choose an occupation in order to prevent the settlement of foreign industrial trainees is an appropriate method, and because changes of training enterprise are permitted when an industrial trainee can no longer continue training at the original training enterprise due to reasons such as bankruptcy, closure, deterioration of management, transfer, or acquisition of the training enterprise, the principle of minimum infringement is satisfied. Furthermore, if the freedom of occupational choice of industrial trainees is recognized in its entirety, it would disturb order in the domestic employment market and make effective government management of foreign labor difficult; therefore, the public interest obtained by restricting the freedom of workplace movement of industrial trainees is greater than the private interest of industrial trainees that is thereby infringed, so the requirement of balance of legal interests is also satisfied."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the incidental clauses attached to an administrative act are incorrect? (If there is any dispute, the case shall be determined in accordance with precedents) (a) Even where, due to a change in circumstances, the purpose of the relevant administrative disposition cannot be achieved unless a new incidental clause is attached or the existing incidental clause is modified, if there is no consent of the party concerned, attaching a new incidental clause or modifying the existing incidental clause is not permitted. (b) If a burden is lawful based on the statutes in force at the time of the disposition, then even if, after the disposition, the statutes that served as the basis for the main administrative disposition underlying the burden are amended so that the administrative agency can no longer attach incidental clauses, it does not immediately become unlawful or lose its effect. (c) Among the contents of an incidental clause, the part concerning a non-suit agreement stating that no administrative lawsuit will be filed thereafter is permitted under the principle of freedom of contract. (d) If an incidental clause that is a burden attached to an administrative disposition is void, and the person who received the disposition performs a legal act under private law, such as a sale, in performance of the burden, then, absent special circumstances, the burden merely functioned as the motive for causing the legal act; therefore, apart from whether it can serve as a ground for rescission of the legal act, it does not naturally render the legal act itself void. (e) If a burden becomes fixed due to the lapse of the filing period and acquires unchallengeability, the validity of a legal act under private law, such as a sale, performed as performance of that burden also cannot be disputed.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DA18174]": "We determine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to the claim that the sales contract in this case is void on the premise that the condition attached to this case is void\\n\\nWhere a burden-imposing condition is attached to an administrative disposition, the invalidation of that condition may affect the validity of the administrative disposition itself, which is the principal act; however, where the person who received that disposition has performed a juristic act under private law, such as a sale, as fulfillment of that burden, the condition, absent special circumstances, merely operated as the motive or reason for causing that juristic act to be performed, and thus, although it may constitute a ground for rescission of that juristic act, it does not automatically render the juristic act itself void (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on June 13, 1995, 94DA56883; Supreme Court Decision rendered on December 22, 1998, 98DA51305). Moreover, if a burden-imposing condition attached to an administrative disposition has become final due to the lapse of the filing period and therefore has already acquired non-contentious finality, no one may deny its effect except where the defect is so serious and obvious that it must be regarded as null and void ab initio. However, since a juristic act under private law, such as a sale, undertaken as fulfillment of that burden is, in any event, a juristic act entirely separate from the administrative disposition that attached that burden, the validity of that juristic act must be determined separately by examining, apart from the issue of the non-contentious finality of the burden, whether the juristic act violates social order or mandatory provisions, and the like.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, the Plaintiff is a reconstruction association composed of residents living in apartments and detached houses on the land lots in Gangseo-gu, Seoul (dong and lot number omitted) and 48 other parcels. The Plaintiff obtained approval for the establishment of a housing association from the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor of Seoul Metropolitan Government (hereinafter referred to as the “Gangseo-gu Office Mayor”) on December 23, 2000, and approval for a housing construction project plan on May 6, 2002. When approving the above housing construction project plan pursuant to Article 33 of the former Housing Construction Promotion Act (as amended by Act No. 6655 on February 4, 2002, and before it came into force on January 1, 2003; hereinafter the same), the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor attached the following conditions: “The state- and public-owned land included in the project site (106,198.7㎡) (all owned by the Defendant, with a total area of 14,415.2㎡; hereinafter referred to as ‘the land parcels in this case’) shall be the subject of a sales contract by the time of filing notice of commencement of construction”; and “When installing relief lanes and widening roads on the east, west, south, and north sides of the project site, they shall be opened in accordance with the Rules concerning the Structure and Facilities of Roads and the general guidelines for road works of the Seoul Metropolitan Government, and all roads and facilities shall be donated gratuitously to Gangseo-gu and the Defendant by the time of application for use inspection; when carrying out corner improvement of roads, all land and facilities shall be donated gratuitously to Gangseo-gu by the time of use inspection.” It is further established that the Plaintiff applied to the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor for abolition of use regarding the land parcels in this case, which are roads and parks within the project site, and when the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor accepted this and requested the Defendant on September 11, 2002 to abolish the use of the roads and on November 25, 2002 to abolish the use of the parks, the Defendant abolished the use of the land parcels in this case as roads and parks, and accordingly the land category of each of the land parcels in this case was changed to building site; and that the Plaintiff, on March 30, 2004, entered into a sales contract with the Defendant to purchase the land parcels in this case for KRW 32,535,106,400 (hereinafter referred to as “the sales contract in this case”), and paid the down payment of KRW 3,253,510,640 on the same day and the balance of KRW 29,281,595,760 on May 31, 2004.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, the Plaintiff’s assertion that, on the premise that the condition attached by the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor when approving the housing construction project plan in this case, requiring the Plaintiff to purchase the land parcels in this case, was void or had subsequently lost its effect, the sales contract in this case concerning the land parcels in this case, which the Plaintiff entered into in order to perform that condition, must also be deemed void, cannot be accepted without considering whether the condition itself is effective or not; therefore, the judgment of the court below, which rejected the Plaintiff’s argument on the same reasoning, is proper, and there is no error of law, such as misapprehension of legal principles concerning deviation from and abuse of discretionary power in conditions attached to administrative acts, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. With respect to the assertion that the sales contract in this case is void for violation of mandatory provisions\\n\\nA. Article 7(1) of the Supplementary Provisions of the former Act on the Maintenance and Improvement of Urban Areas and Dwelling Conditions for Residents (before amendment by Act No. 6893 on May 29, 2003; hereinafter referred to as the “former Urban Improvement Act”) provides, under the heading “Transitional Measures Concerning the Project Implementation Method,” that “matters being implemented with approval of the project plan or authorization of project implementation under the former Act shall be governed by the former provisions.” In the case of a reconstruction project prior to the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act, once approval of the project plan is obtained, in principle, administrative involvement ends, and the members of the association thereby acquire the right to receive the allocation of units (the status of having been selected as occupants) (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on June 15, 2007, 2005DU5369). Considering various circumstances, including the fact that matters such as the operation of a reconstruction association, the distribution of rights among its members, and the method of transferring ownership of the newly constructed building or land were originally intended to be carried out autonomously under the general Civil Act, it is difficult to deem it necessary or reasonable that, with respect to a reconstruction association that had already obtained approval of its project plan before the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act, the remaining project should be implemented according to the procedures or methods under the former Urban Improvement Act. However, Article 3 of the Supplementary Provisions of the former Urban Improvement Act, under the heading “General Transitional Measures,” provides that dispositions, procedures, and other acts carried out under the former Housing Construction Promotion Act’s provisions relating to reconstruction at the time the former Urban Improvement Act entered into force (hereinafter referred to as the “former Act”) shall be deemed to have been carried out under the provisions of the former Urban Improvement Act; and Article 6 of the Supplementary Provisions of the former Urban Improvement Act, under the heading “Transitional Measures Concerning Urban Environment Improvement Projects, etc.,” provides that reconstruction projects being implemented after having obtained approval of the project plan or authorization of project implementation under the former Act shall be deemed housing reconstruction projects under the former Urban Improvement Act. Therefore, with respect to a reconstruction association, matters that do not fall under the “project implementation method” prescribed by Article 7(1) of the Supplementary Provisions of the former Urban Improvement Act should be deemed subject to the main provisions of the former Urban Improvement Act or other supplementary provisions.\\n\\nArticle 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act provides that “infrastructure facilities newly installed as a result of the implementation of an urban improvement project by a project implementer other than the Mayor, the Governor, or a housing corporation, etc., shall vest gratuitously in the State or local government that manages those facilities, and infrastructure facilities owned by the State or local government whose use is abolished as a result of the implementation of the urban improvement project shall be transferred gratuitously to the project implementer within the extent corresponding to the cost of installing the newly installed infrastructure facilities.” This provision was enacted to eliminate the constitutional controversy and the issue of potential deviation from discretionary power by the administrative authority surrounding former Article 33(8) of the former Housing Construction Promotion Act (before amendment by Act No. 6655 on February 4, 2002; hereinafter the same), which granted the administrative authority discretion to allow ownership of public facilities and their site to vest in the State or local government without any compensation when a private project implementer installed public facilities within the project district, and former Article 52(2) of the former Urban Planning Act (completely amended by Act No. 6243 on January 28, 2000 and repealed by Act No. 6655 on February 4, 2002; hereinafter the same). Considering the private project implementer’s property loss caused by the fact that newly installed infrastructure facilities by the private project implementer vest gratuitously in the managing authority pursuant to the former sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act, the latter sentence of the same paragraph provides that infrastructure facilities owned by the State or local government whose use is abolished as a result of the implementation of the urban improvement project shall be transferred gratuitously to such private project implementer within the extent corresponding to the cost of installing the newly installed infrastructure facilities, thereby compensating for the above property loss within a reasonable scope and more equitably and reasonably adjusting the proprietary legal relations between the private project implementer and the State or local government. Accordingly, this is a provision that prescribes substantive legal relations concerning the transfer or vesting of infrastructure facilities owned by the State or local government whose use is abolished as a result of the implementation of the urban improvement project, and cannot be regarded as a provision concerning the “project implementation method.” Therefore, where, after the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act, a private project implementer of a reconstruction project that had obtained approval of the project plan before the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act enters into a contract with the State or local government regarding the transfer or vesting of infrastructure facilities owned by the State or local government whose use is abolished as a result of the implementation of the urban improvement project, it is appropriate to deem that the latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act applies.\\n\\nFurthermore, in light of the legislative purpose of the above latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act, it is a mandatory provision that compels gratuitous transfer of infrastructure facilities to be abolished in use within the scope corresponding to the cost of installing the infrastructure facilities newly installed by the private project implementer (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on July 12, 2007, 2007DU6663), and sales contracts, etc. concluded in violation of that provision between the project implementer and the State or local government are void.\\n\\nIn addition, whether infrastructure facilities are transferred gratuitously or vest gratuitously is determined by Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act, and Article 65(3) of the former Urban Improvement Act merely provides that the approving authority shall hear the opinion of the managing authority in advance for the adjustment of interests, while Article 65(4) of the former Urban Improvement Act is also a procedural provision requiring that, before completion of the urban improvement project, the types and details of the infrastructure facilities that will vest in the managing authority pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) of the same Article, and the property that will vest in or be transferred to the project implementer, be notified to the managing authority. Therefore, the mere fact that the procedures under Article 65(3) and (4) of the former Urban Improvement Act were not followed does not mean that infrastructure facilities whose use is abolished are not subject to gratuitous transfer, nor is a contract concluded in violation of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act rendered valid merely because such procedures were not followed (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on June 28, 2007, 2007DU1699). Further, since the subject matter and price in a sales contract need not necessarily be specifically identified at the time the sales contract is concluded, and it is sufficient if a method and standard by which they can be specifically identified even after the fact are determined (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on June 8, 1993, 92DA49447; Supreme Court Decision rendered on July 12, 2002, 2001DA7940, etc.), even if the cost of installing the infrastructure facilities newly installed by the private project implementer has not yet been fixed at the time of concluding the sales contract, the contract may still be concluded by establishing a method and standard by which that cost can later be specified; and if the private project implementer needs to acquire possession and use rights over the infrastructure facilities whose use is to be abolished, it is entirely possible to conclude a sales contract and acquire such possession and use rights by, for example, establishing a method and standard by which the future installation cost can be specified as described above and deducting from the sale price an amount corresponding thereto. Therefore, neither the fact that the installation cost of the newly installed infrastructure facilities was not fixed at the time of concluding the sales contract, nor the necessity of acquiring possession and use rights over the infrastructure facilities whose use is to be abolished, can render valid a sales contract that purports to require the private project implementer to purchase for consideration from the State or local government the infrastructure facilities whose use is to be abolished and which should be transferred gratuitously to the private project implementer.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the factual circumstances set forth above, the statutory provision applicable to the sales contract in this case concluded between the Plaintiff and the Defendant after the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act is the latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act. The sales contract in this case, under which the Plaintiff purchases for consideration from the Defendant the road and park portions of the land parcels in this case corresponding to the installation cost of the roads and parks newly installed by the Plaintiff, is void for violating the mandatory provision of the latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act. In the absence of any material in the record indicating that the portion of the land parcels in this case that becomes void as above can be specified, no part of the sales contract in this case can be held void in this case.\\n\\nThe judgment of the court below, which held otherwise, erred in law by misapprehending the interpretation and application of Article 65(2) through (4) of the former Urban Improvement Act and the legal principles concerning the requirements for validity of a sales contract, and such error affected the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing out this issue is well founded.\\n\\nB. The principle of good faith and fair dealing under the Civil Act is an abstract norm that a party to a legal relationship must not exercise rights or perform obligations in a manner contrary to equity or in a way that betrays trust, by taking the interests of the other party into account. In order to deny the exercise of a right on the ground that it violates the principle of good faith and fair dealing, the other party must have been given cause to rely on good faith, or objectively be in a state where it is justified to have such good faith, and the exercise of the right contrary to that good faith of the other party must have reached a degree that cannot be tolerated in light of the notion of justice.\\n\\nAbsent special circumstances, where a person who, knowing that a juristic act is void as being in violation of law, nevertheless performed that juristic act, later asserts voidness on the ground of violation of a mandatory law, such assertion cannot be regarded as contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing or the principle of estoppel, nor as constituting an abuse of rights (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on May 10, 1996, 95DA12217; Supreme Court Decision rendered on August 22, 2003, 2003DA19961, etc.).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below held that, before July 1, 2003, the date of enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act, Article 33(8) of the former Housing Construction Promotion Act and Article 52(2) of the former Urban Planning Act applied to the vesting of public facilities whose use is abolished as a result of the implementation of a housing reconstruction project, so if the Plaintiff and the Defendant had concluded a sales contract concerning the land parcels in this case before June 30, 2003, its validity could not be denied. However, the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor, when approving the housing construction project plan in this case on May 6, 2002, attached a condition that the sales contract concerning the land parcels in this case be concluded before filing notice of commencement of construction (the Plaintiff filed notice of commencement of construction on December 27, 2002), and, although more than one year elapsed thereafter until the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act on July 1, 2003, the Plaintiff delayed without entering into a sales contract concerning the land parcels in this case with the Defendant, and the court below held that it would be impermissible under the principle of good faith and fair dealing for the Plaintiff to assert that the sales contract in this case, on the ground that it was concluded after July 1, 2003, is void as being contrary to the former Urban Improvement Act.\\n\\nIn light of the record, it is apparent that in order for the Defendant to enter into a sales contract concerning the land parcels in this case, procedures such as a decision to abolish use, approval by the city council, and determination of the sale price through appraisal were necessary; that, when it became foreseeable that concluding the sales contract with the Defendant would take a considerable amount of time and thereby impede the prompt progress of the project, the Plaintiff deposited KRW 27,535,140,000 on December 26, 2002 with the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor as an amount in the name of the sale price, obtained the Gangseo-gu Office Mayor’s consent, filed notice of commencement of construction on December 27, 2002, and then proceeded with construction; that among the land parcels in this case, each of the parcels listed in Nos. 2 through 11 of the attached list cited in the judgment below, which had been used as roads, had already had their land category changed to building site before the above notice of commencement of construction, whereas the parcel listed in No. 1 of the attached list cited in the judgment below, which had been used as a park, was not subjected to a decision to abolish use until March 4, 2003, after the enforcement of the former Urban Improvement Act, and its land category was changed to building site only on August 1, 2003; that after the Plaintiff submitted an application for purchase concerning the land parcels in this case to the Defendant on August 18, 2003, the contract was finally concluded on March 30, 2004, after going through procedures such as approval by the city council and appraisal; and that there is little basis in the record to find that the Plaintiff otherwise delayed the conclusion of the sales contract by, without justifiable cause, refusing or delaying the Defendant’s request to conclude the sales contract in order to obtain the application of the latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act. If so, based only on the circumstances cited by the court below or those cited above, it cannot be said that the Plaintiff gave the Defendant any cause to rely on good faith with respect to the fact that, in concluding a sales contract with the Defendant concerning public facilities whose use is abolished as a result of the housing reconstruction project in this case, the former Housing Construction Promotion Act Article 33(8) and former Urban Planning Act Article 52(2) would apply; nor can it be said, objectively, that the Defendant had justified good faith. Nor can it be said that the Plaintiff’s assertion that the latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act applies to the sales contract in this case has reached a degree that cannot be tolerated in light of the notion of justice. Therefore, it cannot be said that the Plaintiff’s assertion that the sales contract in this case is void for violating the latter sentence of Article 65(2) of the former Urban Improvement Act is contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing.\\n\\nThe judgment of the court below, which held otherwise, erred in law by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the principle of good faith and fair dealing, and such error affected the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing out this issue is well founded.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds for appeal, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged as the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices of the Supreme Court."}

{"[2006DA18174]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding the Plaintiff’s assertion that the sales contract at issue is void on the premise that the condition attached to this case is void\\n\\nWhen a burdensome term is attached to an administrative disposition, the invalidation of that term may affect the validity of the administrative disposition itself as the principal act; however, where the person who received the disposition has performed a legal act such as a sale under private law as performance of that burden, such term, absent special circumstances, served only as the motive or cause for the legal act, and thus, leaving aside that it may constitute grounds for rescission of the legal act, it does not automatically render the legal act itself void (see Supreme Court Decisions 94DA56883, decided June 13, 1995, and 98DA51305, decided December 22, 1998), and if a burdensome term attached to an administrative disposition has become final and already acquired preclusive force due to the lapse of the filing period, then, except where its defect is serious and apparent so that it should be regarded as void ab initio, no one may deny its effect; however, a legal act such as a sale under private law performed as performance of that burden is, in any event, a legal act separate from the administrative disposition to which the burden was attached, and therefore, apart from the issue of the preclusive force of that burden, the validity of such legal act must be determined by examining, among other things, whether that legal act violates public policy or mandatory provisions.\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the judgment below, the Plaintiff is a reconstruction association composed of residents living in apartments and detached houses on the ground of 48 lots, including Seoul Gangseo-gu (dong, lot number omitted), that the Plaintiff received approval for the establishment of a housing association from the Head of the Gangseo-gu Office, Seoul Metropolitan City, on December 23, 2000, and approval of the housing construction project plan on May 6, 2002, that when the Head of the Gangseo-gu Office approved the above housing construction project plan pursuant to Article 33 of the former Housing Construction Promotion Act (before amendment by Act No. 6655 on February 4, 2002, and before its enforcement from January 1, 2003; hereinafter the same), he attached the following terms: “With respect to the state- and public-owned land included in the project site (106,198.7㎡) (all owned by the Defendant, with a total area of 14,415.2㎡; hereinafter referred to as ‘each of the lands at issue’), a sales contract shall be concluded by the date of the commencement report”; “When implementing the relief lanes and road expansion on the east, west, south, and north sides of the project site, the project shall be opened in accordance with the Rules concerning the Structure and Facilities of Roads and the various guidelines for road construction of Seoul City, and all roads and facilities shall be gratuitously dedicated to Gangseo-gu and the Defendant by the date of the application for inspection for use; when carrying out corner-rectification of roads, all land and facilities shall be gratuitously dedicated to Gangseo-gu by the date of inspection for use”; that the Plaintiff applied to the Head of the Gangseo-gu Office for the abolition of the designated use of each of the lands at issue, which were roads and parks within the project site, and when the Head of the Gangseo-gu Office accepted this and requested the Defendant on September 11, 2002, to abolish the designated use with respect to the roads and on November 25, 2002, to abolish the designated use with respect to the parks, the Defendant abolished the designated use of the roads and parks with respect to each of the lands at issue, and accordingly the land classification of each of the lands at issue was changed to site;
