It can also be seen that the Plaintiff lived together with the Defendant on the land at issue, took charge of housework and childrearing, helped with farming, and thereby contributed directly and indirectly to the maintenance of the land at issue.\\n\\nIn light of the above factual relations, although the land at issue is registered as joint ownership of the Defendant and Non-party 1, it cannot be said that there is no room to view it as property that is substantially and solely owned by the Defendant as a result of an agreement on division of inherited property, etc. Therefore, the appellate court needed to examine the actual status of the use and disposition of the lands acquired by the deceased Non-party 2 and registered as jointly owned by the Defendant and Non-party 1, and the status of the attribution of the benefits from such use or disposition, and to determine whether the Defendant substantially owns the entirety of the land at issue.\\n\\nFurthermore, even if the land at issue is in fact jointly owned by the Defendant and Non-party 1, the appellate court should, pursuant to the legal principles set forth above, reflect this in the division of property by examining, inter alia, the value of the Defendant’s share in the land at issue.\\n\\nNevertheless, the appellate court judgment, which held merely on the ground that the land at issue is joint ownership that it is not included in the subject of division of property, erred by misapprehending the legal principles regarding division of property in divorce and thereby affected the conclusion of the judgment. The grounds of appeal asserting this point are meritorious.\\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the appellate court judgment concerning division of property shall be reversed, and this part of the case shall be remanded to the appellate court for further proceedings and determination, and it is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[2017DA246180]": "We consider the grounds of appeal (a preparatory brief submitted after the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal has passed shall be considered only to the extent that it supplements them).\\n\\n1. Determination on the appeal in cassation against Defendant 1 and Defendant 3\\nAn appeal seeks revocation or modification in one's favor of a judgment unfavorable to oneself. An appeal in cassation against a judgment of complete victory is not permitted because there is no object or interest whatsoever in filing an appeal in cassation (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 99DA61378, rendered June 14, 2002).\\nAccording to the record, the court below dismissed the appeals of Defendant 1 and Defendant 3; therefore, the appeal in cassation filed by the Plaintiff, who wholly prevailed, against Defendant 1 and Defendant 3 is inadmissible for lack of interest in appeal.\\n\\n2. Determination on the grounds of appeal concerning Defendant 2\\nA. Pursuant to Article 4 of the Act on the Registration of Real Estate under Actual Titleholder's Name, a title trust agreement concerning real estate and the resulting change in real rights in real estate are void; however, where, in a contract for acquiring a real right in real estate, the title trustee becomes one party to the contract and the other party does not know the fact that there is a title trust agreement, the title trustee acquires full ownership of the real estate, but merely bears an obligation to return unjust enrichment to the title truster (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DA66922, rendered January 28, 2005).\\nWhere real estate purchased by the partners for a joint business was not registered in joint ownership but ownership transfer registration was made in the name of one of the partners, it should be deemed that the partnership entity made a title trust to the partner (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2003DA25256, rendered April 13, 2006). The ownership of real estate title-trusted by the partnership entity to a partner vests, according to the legal principle stated above, in the seller when the change in real rights is void, and in the title trustee when it is valid. In such case, the partnership property consists of the right to claim registration of transfer of ownership or the claim for return of unjust enrichment, and the trust real estate itself cannot become partnership property.\\n\\nB. (1) The court below rejected the Plaintiff's assertion seeking registration of transfer of a share in real estate on the ground of termination of the partnership relationship for the following reasons.\\nThe Plaintiff, the Non-party, Defendant 1, and Defendant 2 formed a partnership for the purpose of investing in and developing real estate and purchased forest land in Gwangju City (address 1 omitted); they prepared a sales contract naming Defendant 2 as the purchaser and completed the registration of transfer of ownership in the name of Defendant 2. (Thereafter, the above forest land was subdivided into Gwangju City (address 2 omitted) and (address 3 omitted); hereinafter, before and after the subdivision, it is referred to as 'the forest land in this case'.) The Plaintiff withdrew from the partnership by expressing an intention to terminate the partnership agreement. As a result, ownership of the forest land in this case vested in joint ownership of the remaining partners. The Plaintiff must, together with the remaining partners, make calculations based on the state of the partnership property at the time of withdrawal pursuant to Article 719 of the Civil Act, and cannot, without making such calculations, seek performance of the procedure for registration of transfer of a 1/4 share in the forest land in this case, which constitutes partnership property.\\n(2) Examining the factual findings recognized by the court below in light of the legal principles stated above, the following can be said.\\nSince the partnership entity formed by the Plaintiff and Defendant 2, etc. purchased the forest land in this case and completed registration of transfer in the name of Defendant 2, it must be deemed that the partnership entity made a title trust of the forest land to Defendant 2. In this case, the partnership property consists of a claim for return of unjust enrichment corresponding to the purchase price paid to Defendant 2, etc., and the forest land in this case, which is trust real estate, cannot become partnership property. Therefore, even if the partnership relationship terminated due to the Plaintiff's withdrawal or dissolution, the Plaintiff cannot seek registration of transfer of a share on the premise that the forest land in this case is partnership property.\\nAlthough the court below erred in regarding the forest land in this case as partnership property, thereby misapprehending the legal principles concerning the establishment of title trust and the transfer of ownership of trust real estate, the court below's conclusion that the Plaintiff cannot seek registration of transfer concerning a share in the forest land in this case is correct. There is no error in the court below's determination that affected the judgment, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning the termination of the partnership relationship and the interpretation of Article 719 of the Civil Act, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\nThe Plaintiff's appeal in cassation against Defendant 1 and Defendant 3 is dismissed as inadmissible, and the Plaintiff's appeal in cassation against Defendant 2 is dismissed as without merit; and the appeal costs are to be borne by the losing party. Accordingly, the judgment is rendered as stated in the order by unanimous agreement of the Justices of the Supreme Court."}

question: A, for the purpose of securing a loan claim against B, acquired a mortgage and, together with it, a superficies without ground rent over X land owned by B, while causing B to continue to possess and use the land. Which of the following statements is incorrect? (Each proposition is independent, and where there is a dispute, case law shall apply)
A: If B installed a retaining wall and opened a road on X land, which had been vacant land on which a building could be constructed, A cannot claim from B restitution of unjust enrichment equivalent to rent for X land.
B: If B installed a retaining wall and opened a road on X land, which had been vacant land on which a building could be constructed, and as a result the exchange value of X land decreased, A may claim damages for tort against B.
C: If B consented to C's gratuitous use of X land and, accordingly, C planted a maple tree on X land, that maple tree does not accede to X land.
D: If the secured obligation of the mortgage in A's name over X land is extinguished by completion of the Statute of Limitations, the superficies in A's name over X land also, as an accessory thereto, is extinguished, and therefore B is recognized as having an interest in seeking confirmation of the nonexistence of the debt secured by the superficies in A's name.
E: If, at the time the mortgage and superficies in A's name were established over X land, a Y Building owned by B had already been newly constructed on X land, and if X land is sold at auction pursuant to A's application for a voluntary auction based on the above mortgage and D pays the purchase price in full, a statutory superficies for the Y Building is established.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2005DA3243]": "1. The Lower Court’s Determination\\n\\nThe lower court, after finding that an ownership transfer registration in the name of Non-party 1 had been made with respect to Unit 301 on the 3rd floor of the 3-story multi-family house on 229.4㎡ of land at (address 1 omitted), Namdong-gu, Incheon (hereinafter, when referring to the multi-family house, “the multi-family house at issue,” and when referring to Unit 301 on the 3rd floor of the multi-family house at issue, “the house at issue”), rejected the Defendant’s contention that the registration was erroneous because, in the course of subdivision registration by the Non-party corporation Daehan Housing, which had newly constructed the multi-family house at issue, (address 3 omitted) had been registered as (address 1 omitted), and (address 1 omitted) as (address 3 omitted), by mistake while dividing and registering (address 2 omitted) in Namdong-gu, Incheon; and that, after purchasing Unit 301 at (address 3 omitted) from Non-party 2, who had acquired the unit, the Defendant was residing in Unit 301 of (address 1 omitted), which was marked as Building A on the exterior wall of the building, and therefore the Defendant had lawful title to possess the house at issue. The lower court held that the Defendant had purchased Unit 301 at (address 3 omitted) from Non-party 2 and merely completed the ownership transfer registration, and that there was no evidence of any mistake in the subdivision or registration process. On that basis, the lower court found that the Defendant’s possession asserting ownership of the house at issue after the decision to commence auction proceedings had been rendered infringed the mortgage right of the Plaintiff, who was the mortgagee established by Non-party 1, and accordingly granted the Plaintiff’s claim in this case seeking the Defendant’s eviction from the house at issue based on the mortgage right.\\n\\n2. The Supreme Court’s Determination\\n\\nHowever, the above determination of the lower court is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nThe Defendant’s above contention should ultimately be understood as a contention that Non-party 1’s sale object and the registration do not correspond. According to the record, on the land adjacent to the multi-family house at issue, at (address 3 omitted) in Guwol-dong, a multi-family house of the same structure as the multi-family house at issue had also been newly constructed, and both multi-family houses (hereinafter, the “adjacent multi-family house”) had preservation registrations completed on September 27, 1989; as to Unit 301 on the 3rd floor of the adjacent multi-family house (hereinafter, the “adjacent building”), ownership transfer registration in the name of Non-party 2 was sequentially completed, followed by ownership transfer registration in the name of the Defendant, but in fact Non-party 1, the registered titleholder of the house at issue, was residing there; the exterior wall of the multi-family house at issue was marked as Building A, and the exterior wall of the adjacent multi-family house was marked as Building B; the addresses in the registry and resident registration of Non-party 1 were “Unit 301, Building B, XX Housing, (address 1 omitted), Namdong-gu, Incheon,” while the addresses of Non-party 2 and the Defendant were “Unit 301, Building A, XX Housing, (address 3 omitted), Guwol-dong, Namdong-gu, Incheon”; and Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 were the persons to whom ownership transfer registrations were first completed after the preservation registrations of each of the multi-family houses at issue.\\n\\nIn light of the above facts, as well as the facts that, when purchasing or buying a multi-family house, it is generally the case that the location is identified and the purchase or sale is made accordingly, and that the resident registration addresses of Non-party 1, Non-party 2, and the Defendant correspond to the building wing markings on the exterior wall of the building, it is difficult to readily conclude that both Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 made a mistake and moved into the wrong units. Therefore, the lower court should have examined the sale and move-in process, including the sale contract, and should also have examined the registration and occupancy relations of the other occupants, in order to determine whether the houses purchased by Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 corresponded to the registrations.\\n\\nb. Meanwhile, a mortgage right is a real right whose content is to receive repayment of the secured claim in priority to other creditors from the exchange value of the mortgaged real property realized through foreclosure proceedings; it is established without transferring possession of the real property to the mortgagee. In principle, the mortgagee cannot interfere with the use or profit-making of the mortgaged real property by the owner of the mortgaged real property. However, if the possession of the mortgaged real property exceeds the scope of use and profit-making according to the original mode of use of the mortgaged real property and thereby reduces its exchange value, or if it is recognized that possession was commenced in order to obstruct realization of the mortgage right, and if there are circumstances making realization of the mortgage right difficult, such as where the auction sale price falls compared with the price in the case of normal possession, or the foreclosure proceedings do not proceed, due to such possession, infringement of the mortgage right may be recognized.\\n\\nThe lower court determined that the Plaintiff’s mortgage right had been infringed on the ground that the Defendant was possessing the house at issue while asserting ownership, and that, as a result, a decision disallowing the highest bid was rendered by the auction court and the auction date was postponed, so that the foreclosure proceedings were not properly proceeding. However, the auction court’s decision disallowing the highest bid for the house at issue was based on the auction court’s determination that the auction would be conducted after clarifying the legal relations concerning the ownership of the house at issue and the effect of the Plaintiff’s mortgage right based thereon, and cannot be regarded as having been caused by the Defendant’s assertion of ownership. In addition, the record does not show any circumstance from which it can be found that the Defendant’s possession is inappropriate as possession of the house at issue, or that such possession makes it difficult to proceed with the foreclosure proceedings or the auction sale and thereby lowers the exchange value below the normal auction sale price, thus infringing the Plaintiff’s mortgage right. Accordingly, it appears difficult to accept the Plaintiff’s claim seeking the Defendant’s eviction from the house at issue based on the mortgage right at issue, either by subrogating to the right to demand removal of interference based on the mortgage right at issue or to the owner’s right to demand removal of interference.\\n\\nc. Therefore, the lower court judgment failed not only to fully examine the ownership relations of the house at issue, but also erred in law regarding the right to demand removal of interference based on the mortgage right, thereby affecting the judgment outcome; the ground of appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the lower court judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court who participated."}

{"[2006DA586]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. As to the Plaintiff’s grounds of appeal\\n\\nThe owner or person entitled to use and derive profits from real property subject to unlawful possession may seek from the unlawful possessor compensation for damages equivalent to the rent therefrom or restitution of unjust enrichment; however, even if no fact of unlawful possession has occurred, where special circumstances exist such that the owner or person entitled to use and derive profits from the real property could not have derived any benefit equivalent to rent or any other income, a claim for damages or restitution of unjust enrichment may not be brought (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2000DA57375 rendered on December 6, 2002).\\n\\nWhen a financial institution acquires a mortgage over land owned by the debtor or a person who furnishes security in rem in order to secure a loan debt, and at the same time acquires a superficies right over the land without paying ground rent, while allowing the debtor, etc. to continue to possess and use the land, unless special circumstances exist, such superficies right is intended to secure the collateral value of the mortgaged real property by excluding third parties from acquiring use and profit rights or committing infringing acts that diminish the collateral value of the subject land until the mortgage is executed; and in such a case, since it is difficult to view the possession and use of the subject land of the superficies right as having enabled the acquisition of benefits equivalent to rent or any other income, the mere circumstance that the owner of the subject land or a third party possesses and uses the land subject to the mortgage and superficies right cannot be said to have caused any damage to the financial institution.\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the judgment of the court below, after recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion, the court below determined that the superficies right acquired by the Plaintiff together with the mortgage over the first and second parcels of land in this case was intended to secure the collateral value of the object of the mortgage by excluding third parties from acquiring use and profit rights or committing infringing acts that diminish the collateral value of the subject land; therefore, even though the Defendants constructed a road on the first parcel of land in this case and installed a retaining wall between the first and second parcels of land in this case, thereby making it impossible to use and derive profits from the first and second parcels of land in this case, which were the subject of the superficies right, the Plaintiff could not separately claim damages equivalent to rent for the first and second parcels of land on the ground of infringement of the superficies right itself, apart from seeking damages for the reduction in collateral value. In light of the foregoing legal principles, the foregoing determination of the court below is proper, and there is no illegality such as misapprehension of the principle of numerus clausus of real rights, or misapprehension of the legal principles on the formation and effect of superficies rights or the scope of damages, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. As to the Defendants’ grounds of appeal\\n\\nA mortgage is a real right that provides for receiving, in preference to other creditors, payment of the secured claim from the exchange value of mortgaged real property realized through foreclosure proceedings, and it is created without transferring possession of the real property to the mortgagee; thus, as a matter of principle, the mortgagee cannot interfere with the use or profits of the mortgaged real property by its owner. However, where the possession of the mortgaged real property by the owner or a third party exceeds the scope of use and profits in accordance with the original use of the mortgaged real property and thereby diminishes its exchange value, or where it is recognized that the possessor commenced possession in order to obstruct the realization of the mortgage, and there are circumstances such that the realization of the mortgage becomes difficult, for example, because the price is reduced compared with the auction sale price when ordinary possession exists or the foreclosure proceedings do not proceed, infringement of the mortgage may be recognized (see Supreme Court Decision 2005DA3243 rendered on April 29, 2005).\\n\\nAccording to the facts found by the court below and the record, Defendant Daejoo Construction Co., Ltd. altered the configuration of the first parcel of land in this case, whose land category had originally been “field,” constructed an asphalt-paved road with a width of 8m thereon, and installed a concrete retaining wall with a height of 2m to 6m and a length of 89.5m at the boundary between the first and second parcels of land in this case, and then provided the same for use as a road by the general public; Defendant Gimhae City also, having received the first parcel of land in this case by donation from the non-party, approved the amendment to Defendant Daejoo Construction Co., Ltd.’s housing construction project plan as the owner standing in the position of a real security provider in relation to the Plaintiff, thereby causing Defendant Daejoo Construction Co., Ltd. to engage in an act of damaging the first parcel of land in this case; and the market value of the first parcel of land in this case, as of March 16, 2002, would have been around KRW 63,460,000 if a road and retaining wall had not been installed, but by the Defendants’ construction of the road and installation of the retaining wall as above, its market value fell to around KRW 31,396,000, less than half that amount. In light of the foregoing legal principles, the Defendants’ conduct of constructing a road on land whose land category is “field” and providing it to the general public cannot, in light of social norms, be regarded as a normal act of use and profit in accordance with the original use of the land; therefore, the Defendants’ conduct, by damaging the first parcel of land in this case and thereby diminishing its exchange value, constitutes an unlawful act infringing the Plaintiff’s mortgage and thus a joint tort in relation to the Plaintiff.\\n\\nThe determination of the court below, which found the Defendants liable for damages on the same basis, is proper and can be affirmed, and the judgment of the court below cannot be deemed to contain illegality arising from misapprehension of the legal principles on tort under the Civil Act or on Article 2 of the State Compensation Act.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by each party, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the panel of judges participating in the decision."}

{"[2015DA65042]": "The grounds of appeal are determined as follows.\\n\\n1. Factual Findings\\n\\nAccording to the reasons for the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts may be ascertained:\\n\\n(1) On 2006. 2. 9., the Plaintiff entered into a contract for the creation of a mortgage, with the Debtor, Non-party 1, the Maximum Claim Amount of 350,000,000 won, and the Defendant as the mortgagee, with respect to three parcels of land, including 5,000 square meters of forest land in Incheon, Ganghwa-gun, on the former land before partition owned by the Plaintiff and the Defendant at (Address 1 omitted) (hereinafter referred to as “the land in this case”), and completed the registration of creation of a joint mortgage in the name of the Defendant (hereinafter the above contract is referred to as “the mortgage creation contract in this case,” and the above registration is referred to as “the registration of creation of a mortgage in this case”). On the same day, the Plaintiff also completed a registration of creation of superficies in the name of the Defendant, for a term of 30 years from 2006. 2. 9. on the land in this case (hereinafter referred to as “the registration of creation of superficies in this case”).\\n\\n(2) On 2006. 2. 10., the Defendant lent 250,000,000 won to Non-party 1, fixing the loan maturity date as 2009. 2. 10.\\n\\n(3) On 2006. 5. 29., the Plaintiff sold to Non-party 2 part of the land in this case, namely 1,219 square meters of forest land in Incheon, Ganghwa-gun, at (Address 2 omitted), and completed the registration of transfer of ownership in the name of Non-party 2 on 2006. 9. 20. On 2006. 10. 2., the Defendant received repayment of 80,000,000 won, which constituted principal among the secured obligations under the above mortgage, from Non-party 2, and cancelled the registration of creation of the mortgage and the registration of creation of superficies established on the land owned by Non-party 2.\\n\\n(4) As to the remaining land owned by the Plaintiff, excluding the land sold to Non-party 2, after subsequent conversion of registration and partition, etc., except for 586 square meters of forest land in Incheon, Ganghwa-gun, at (Address 3 omitted), the registration of transfer of ownership was completed in the names of Non-party 3 and Non-party 4 on 2006. 11. 7. Among the attached list to the judgment of the court below, the real property in paragraph (3) became owned by the Plaintiff, the remaining real property in the same list became owned by Non-party 4, and 180/360 shares of 750 square meters of forest land at (Address 4 omitted), 700 square meters of forest land at (Address 5 omitted), and 360 square meters of forest land at (Address 6 omitted) in Incheon, Ganghwa-gun became owned by Non-party 3.\\n\\n(5) Meanwhile, with respect to the land owned by Non-party 3 on which the joint mortgage was created, the Defendant: ① on 2006. 11. 13., with respect to 750 square meters of forest land at (Address 4 omitted) and 700 square meters of forest land at (Address 5 omitted), completed, respectively, on 2006. 11. 10., the registration of cancellation of the registration of creation of the mortgage on the ground of partial waiver, and the registration of cancellation of the registration of creation of superficies on the ground of termination; ② on 2011. 2. 9., with respect to 360 square meters of forest land at (Address 6 omitted), completed the registration of change of the mortgage on the ground of waiver of 180/360 shares owned by Non-party 3.\\n\\n2. Determination on the Main Claim\\n\\na. A mortgage refers to a mortgage created by fixing only the maximum amount of the secured claim and reserving the final determination of the debt for the future. If the mortgage creation contract or the underlying contract sets a settlement date, or if the mortgage has a term of existence, in principle the secured obligation is finalized when the settlement date arrives or the term of existence expires. The designation of a settlement date here generally means the time and method for the final determination of the obligation secured by the mortgage, and is distinguished from an agreement regarding the time for performance of the secured obligation.\\n\\nWhere no term of existence or settlement date is set for the mortgage, if there is another agreement concerning the method of final determination of the secured obligation, such agreement shall govern; if there is no such agreement, the mortgagor may, at any time, finalize the secured obligation by manifesting an intent to terminate the contract against the mortgagee (see Supreme Court Decision 2002DA7176, decided on 2002. 5. 24., etc.).\\n\\nb. The Plaintiff sought against the Defendant the cancellation of the registration of creation of the mortgage in this case and the registration of creation of superficies in the Defendant’s name on the ground that the secured obligation of the mortgage in this case had been extinguished by completion of the Statute of Limitations. The Plaintiff argued that, since the settlement date was set as a future-determined type in the mortgage creation contract in this case, the secured obligation was an obligation without a fixed due date and thus the Statute of Limitations runs from the time the claim arises.\\n\\nThe court below, on the ground that when the Plaintiff entered into the mortgage creation contract in this case, the settlement date of the mortgage was set as a future-determined type and it was stated in the mortgage creation contract that “after three years have passed from the date of the contract, the mortgagor may designate the settlement date of the mortgage by written notice; provided, however, that such settlement date must be at least 14 days after the arrival of the notice, and if it falls short of that, the day 14 days after the arrival of the notice shall be the settlement date,” rejected the Plaintiff’s argument regarding the commencement date of the Statute of Limitations, on the basis that this was merely an agreement concerning the time of final determination of the secured obligation and not an agreement concerning the time of performance thereof.\\n\\nIn light of the above legal principles and the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below’s determination rejecting the Plaintiff’s argument concerning the starting point of the Statute of Limitations is proper. The judgment of the court below contains no error, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in exceeding the limits of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rule of logic and experience, or in misapprehending the legal principles regarding the interpretation of standard terms and the starting point of the Statute of Limitations.\\n\\nc. The Plaintiff argues that the mortgage in this case was not intended to secure an unspecified claim that would increase, decrease, or change in the future, but rather to secure a specific claim, or that the maturity date of the secured obligation could be extended only with the Plaintiff’s consent as a real surety. However, this is a new argument raised for the first time at the appellate level and is not a proper ground of appeal. Even upon examining the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the record, the judgment of the court below contains no error, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the binding effect of admission and the interpretation of declarations of intent, thereby affecting the outcome of the judgment.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff argues that Non-party 1, the Debtor, agreed to waive the right to refinancing, but the court below did not recognize this; however, this merely amounts to disputing the selection and assessment of evidence and the finding of facts, which fall within the exclusive authority of the court below as the trier of fact, and thus is not a proper ground of appeal. Even upon examining the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the record, the court below did not err in its interpretation of standard terms by holding that, merely because the loan contract did not designate a settlement date, it is difficult to view Non-party 1 as having agreed not to refinance.\\n\\n3. Determination on the Alternative Claims\\n\\na. Claim concerning the registration of creation of superficies in this case\\n\\n(1) The Plaintiff filed an action seeking confirmation of the scope of the secured obligation concerning the registration of creation of the mortgage in this case and the registration of creation of superficies in this case, as the first alternative claim and the second alternative claim additionally raised at the court below; among them, this Court shall examine ex officio the claim concerning the registration of creation of superficies.\\n\\n(2) An action for confirmation must satisfy the requirement of a current interest in confirmation as a prerequisite for protection of rights, and such interest is recognized when there exists an present uncertainty or danger concerning the Plaintiff’s right or legal status, and obtaining a declaratory judgment is the most effective and appropriate means to remove that uncertainty or danger (see Supreme Court Decision 2006DA68650, decided on 2007. 2. 9., etc.).\\n\\nSuperficies, being a right to use and benefit, is not a security right; therefore, there can be no such thing as a secured obligation thereof. A superficies created together with a security right such as a mortgage, for the purpose of preventing the reduction of the secured value of the land by the later creation of a right to use and benefit on the land provided as security or by the construction or installation of a building or structure, is so-called a superficies for security. In such a case, the continuity of the security right and the continuity of the superficies are merely linked with each other pursuant to the agreement of the parties, and even in such a case there does not exist a secured obligation for the superficies.\\n\\nAccordingly, the Plaintiff’s claim seeking confirmation of the scope of the secured obligation concerning the registration of creation of superficies is difficult to regard as a claim concerning the Plaintiff’s right or legal status, and therefore there is no current interest in confirmation, so this part of the action is unlawful. Nevertheless, the court below held that this part of the action was lawful and ruled on the merits; therefore, the court below erred by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the procedural requirements and the interest in confirmation, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n(3) An alternative claim must be in a relationship of mutual incompatibility with the main claim; thus, a claim that, while using the same cause of action and the same object as the main claim, partially reduces the main claim quantitatively or qualitatively, is merely absorbed into the main claim and cannot be regarded as an alternative claim in litigation (see Supreme Court Decision 98DA61463, decided on 1999. 4. 23.; Supreme Court Decision 2007DA88507, decided on 2008. 3. 27., etc.).\\n\\nThe Plaintiff’s second alternative claim, predicated on the rejection of the argument that the secured obligation was extinguished due to the infringement of the Plaintiff’s so-called “right of proportional sharing (understood to refer to a right or expectation that the property subject to the joint mortgage will bear the secured obligation in proportionate shares; hereinafter the same applies),” is merely a claim that partially reduces the first alternative claim quantitatively, and therefore cannot be regarded as an alternative claim in litigation; it should not have been separately adjudicated. The court below erred by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the joinder of alternative claims in dismissing the second alternative claim separately as a claim added at the court below.\\n\\nb. Part concerning the registration of creation of the mortgage in this case\\n\\n(1) The Court examines the remaining alternative claim of the Plaintiff, namely, the claim seeking confirmation of the scope of the secured obligation concerning the registration of creation of the mortgage in this case.\\n\\nWhere there exists a person entitled to subrogation under the provisions of Civil Act Article 481, if security is lost or reduced due to the creditor’s intention or negligence, the subrogee is exempt from liability to the extent that reimbursement cannot be obtained due to such loss or reduction (Civil Act Article 485). This is intended to protect the recourse right and expectation of subrogation of persons entitled to statutory subrogation, such as guarantors, by imposing on the creditor a duty to preserve security (see Supreme Court Decision 2013DA91788, decided on 2014. 10. 15., etc.).\\n\\nA real surety is a person who has a legitimate interest in paying the secured obligation of a mortgage and has a right of statutory subrogation to subrogate the creditor by such payment. When the creditor, intentionally or negligently, causes the security to be lost or reduced, absent special circumstances, this infringes the real surety’s subrogation right, and the real surety may assert exemption from liability pursuant to Civil Act Article 485 to the extent that reimbursement cannot be obtained due to such loss or reduction (see Supreme Court Decision 97DA1013, decided on 2000. 1. 21.; Supreme Court Decision 2012DA106218, decided on 2013. 3. 28., etc.). Here, the fact that the real surety may assert exemption from liability does not mean that the secured obligation of the mortgage borne by the debtor itself is extinguished, but means that the real surety’s liability concerning the secured obligation is extinguished.\\n\\n(2) The Plaintiff asserted that, on the premise that the secured obligation of the mortgage in this case had been extinguished by repayment or assumption of debt with exemption from liability, leaving a balance of 58,868,504 won, the Defendant, by waiving the joint mortgage concerning the real property owned by Non-party 3, infringed the Plaintiff’s right of proportional sharing and thereby extinguished the secured obligation to the extent of 29,434,252 won, which corresponds to one-half of the above amount, and therefore sought confirmation that the remaining secured obligation amount of the mortgage is 29,434,252 won.\\n\\nThe court below held that because the mortgagee Defendant may freely waive part of the security right, the Plaintiff’s argument is unfounded on its face, and that even if the Defendant waived the security right and thereby infringed the Plaintiff’s expected benefit, it cannot be deemed that the secured obligation amount of the mortgage correspondingly decreased; accordingly, it rejected the Plaintiff’s argument that “the right of proportional sharing was infringed.”\\n\\nHowever, in light of the legal principles stated above, where there exists a person entitled to statutory subrogation, such as a guarantor, the creditor bears a duty to preserve security under Civil Act Article 485, and therefore the creditor Defendant cannot at any time freely waive part of the security and obtain satisfaction for the entire claim from the remaining security. Also, if the creditor Defendant, by waiving part of the joint mortgage, infringed the real surety Plaintiff’s subrogation right, then although the secured obligation itself is not extinguished, the Plaintiff is exempt from liability as a real surety to the extent that reimbursement cannot be obtained pursuant to Civil Act Article 485.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff’s claim seeking confirmation that the secured obligation was extinguished to a certain extent on the ground that the right of proportional sharing was infringed can be construed as including the purport of seeking confirmation of the extinction of liability pursuant to Civil Act Article 485. The court below should have clarified the purport of the Plaintiff’s claim and then examined and determined the extent to which the Defendant’s partial waiver of the mortgage extinguished the real surety’s liability.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s argument solely for the above reason, and this was erroneous. The judgment of the court below contains error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the duty to preserve security under Civil Act Article 485, without conducting the necessary examination. However, in the event that the mortgage in this case is executed in the future and the secured real property is sold in the auction proceedings so that a distribution schedule is prepared, filing an action to object to distribution, etc., regarding the existence or scope of the substantive right to receive distribution on the premise of liability extinction, rather than seeking confirmation of such liability extinction, may constitute an effective and appropriate means of directly resolving the dispute.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nAmong the judgment of the court below, the part concerning the alternative claim with respect to the registration of creation of superficies is unlawful, and therefore the first and second alternative claims are reversed; however, since this Court can directly render judgment on this part, it shall do so pursuant to Article 437 of the Civil Procedure Act. The judgment of the court of first instance concerning the first alternative claim relating to the registration of creation of superficies is reversed, and the corresponding action is dismissed, but the action concerning the second alternative claim, which is absorbed into the first alternative claim, shall not be separately dismissed. The Plaintiff’s appeal against the judgment of the court below regarding the first alternative claim concerning the registration of creation of the mortgage is, within the recognized scope above, well-founded; therefore, among the first alternative claim concerning the registration of creation of the mortgage in the judgment of the court below, the part seeking confirmation, on the ground of partial waiver of the joint mortgage, of the non-existence of the secured obligation to the extent of 29,434,252 won, and the second alternative claim absorbed into the first alternative claim concerning the registration of creation of the mortgage, are reversed together, and this part of the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. The Plaintiff’s remaining appeal, namely the appeal concerning the main claim, is without merit and is dismissed. Accordingly, the judgment is rendered as ordered, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2015DA69907]": "We determine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Civil Act Article 256 provides, “The owner of immovable property acquires ownership of things acceded to such immovable property. However, this shall not apply to things attached by another’s title.” The “title” referred to in the proviso to the above provision means a right to use one’s own movables by attaching them to another person’s immovable property, such as a superficies, a jeonse right, or a leasehold right; therefore, if a person lacking such title plants trees on another person’s land, absent special circumstances, that person cannot assert ownership of the trees against the landowner (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 1989. 7. 11., 88DAKA9067, etc.).\\n\\nBecause a superficies holder has the right to use another person’s land in order to own buildings or other structures or trees on that land (Civil Act Article 279), once registration of the creation of a superficies is completed, the right to use and derive profits from the land belongs to the superficies holder, and the landowner who created the superficies cannot use or derive profits from the land so long as the superficies subsists (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 1974. 11. 12., 74DA1150). Therefore, even if a person has acquired a right to use the land from the landowner who created the superficies, such right does not, in principle, constitute the “title” provided in the proviso to Civil Act Article 256 so long as the superficies subsists.\\n\\nHowever, where a financial institution, for the purpose of securing a loan claim, creates a mortgage and a superficies without ground rent on land while not excluding the debtor, etc.’s right to use and derive profits, the purpose of such superficies is to secure the mortgage’s security value in the mortgaged real estate by excluding third parties from acquiring usufructuary rights or engaging in infringing acts that lower the security value of the subject land until the mortgage is enforced (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2008. 1. 17., 2006DA586). Thus, absent special circumstances such as a risk of lowering the security value of the mortgaged real estate, the landowner should be regarded as able to use and derive profits from the land. Accordingly, if one acquires from such landowner the right to use and derive profits from the land, such right may be deemed to constitute the “title” provided in the proviso to Civil Act Article 256.\\n\\n2. a. According to the reasons of the lower court judgment and the record, the following facts can be ascertained.\\n\\n(1) On 1997. 6. 24., Nonparty 1 completed registration of transfer of ownership with respect to a 1,008/2,763 share of the 2,763㎡ field in Goyang-si (address omitted) (hereinafter referred to as “the land in this case”), and Nonparty 2 completed registration of transfer of ownership with respect to a 1,755/2,763 share of the land in this case on the same date.\\n\\n(2) The Geumchon Agricultural Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as “Geumchon Agricultural Cooperative”) entered into a mortgage creation agreement with Nonparty 2 on 2005. 8. 11. concerning Nonparty 2’s share in the land in this case, with a maximum secured amount of KRW 500,000,000, and completed registration thereof; on the same date, it entered into a superficies creation agreement with Nonparty 2 and Nonparty 1 (hereinafter referred to as “Nonparty 2, etc.”) concerning the entire land in this case, with no ground rent and a term of 30 years, and completed registration of creation of a superficies on the land in this case on 2005. 8. 18. (hereinafter referred to as “the superficies in this case”).\\n\\n(3) The Plaintiff, after entering into a loan for use agreement with Nonparty 2, etc. concerning the land in this case for the ownership of trees, planted approximately 300 maple trees (hereinafter referred to as “the maple trees in this case”) on the land in this case from around 2007. 10. to around November of the same year.\\n\\n(4) Thereafter, on 2010. 12. 8., foreclosure proceedings for involuntary auction were commenced as Case No. 2010TAGYEONG34414 of the Uijeongbu District Court Goyang Branch with respect to Nonparty 2’s share in the land in this case, and in the above auction proceedings, the Defendant purchased the above share of Nonparty 2 and paid the sale price on 2011. 7. 15.\\n\\nb. The lower court, on the premise that the maple trees in this case, which the Plaintiff planted on the land in this case pursuant to the loan for use agreement concluded with Nonparty 2, etc., who are co-owners of the land in this case, are owned by the Plaintiff and have not acceded to the land in this case, dismissed the present claim seeking damages based on tort against the Defendant, who had arbitrarily collected and sold some of the maple trees in this case, for the following reasons.\\n\\n(1) By completing registration of creation of a superficies concerning the entire land in this case with Nonparty 2, etc., Geumchon Agricultural Cooperative, as the superficies holder, acquired the right to use the land in this case, and at the same time, Nonparty 2, etc., as the owner of the land in this case, lost the right to use the land in this case.\\n\\n(2) Even if the Plaintiff thereafter entered into a loan for use agreement with Nonparty 2, etc. and planted the maple trees in this case, insofar as Nonparty 2, etc. did not have the right to use the land in this case for the ownership of trees, the Plaintiff likewise did not acquire such lawful right.\\n\\n(3) Accordingly, the above loan for use agreement does not constitute the “title” provided in the proviso to Civil Act Article 256, and the maple trees in this case acceded to the land in this case at the same time the Plaintiff planted them and thereby became owned by Nonparty 2, etc., who are the owners of the land in this case.\\n\\n(4) Therefore, the Plaintiff’s claim, premised on the assertion that the maple trees in this case are owned by the Plaintiff, is without merit without need for further review.\\n\\nc. In light of the legal principles examined above, we review the lower court’s determination.\\n\\nGeumchon Agricultural Cooperative acquired a mortgage over Nonparty 2’s share in the land in this case in order to secure the loan claim against Nonparty 2, and in addition acquired a superficies over the entire land in this case without paying ground rent in order to prevent the security value of the subject land from diminishing, so it is apparent that the purpose of the superficies in this case was to secure the security value of the mortgaged real estate, namely, the land in this case, until Geumchon Agricultural Cooperative’s mortgage is enforced. In such a case, there is room to view the superficies holder, Geumchon Agricultural Cooperative, as having granted the landowner of the land in this case, etc. the right to continue using and deriving profits from the land in this case. If the circumstances are as such, it is reasonable to regard the loan for use agreement that the Plaintiff concluded with the owner of the land in this case for the ownership of trees as constituting the “title” provided in the proviso to Civil Act Article 256; accordingly, the maple trees in this case should be deemed not to have acceded to the land in this case.\\n\\nIf so, the lower court should have examined whether the superficies holder, Geumchon Agricultural Cooperative, had allowed the owner of the land in this case, Nonparty 2, etc., to use and derive profits from the land in this case, by scrutinizing the purpose and circumstances of the creation of the superficies in this case and the terms of its creation, among others.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court, without properly examining the above circumstances, concluded merely from the fact that the superficies in this case had been created that Nonparty 2, etc., who are the owners of the land in this case, lost the right to use the land in this case, and determined that the loan for use agreement concluded by the Plaintiff with Nonparty 2, etc. did not constitute the “title” provided in the proviso to Civil Act Article 256; the lower court judgment thus contains an error that affected the result of the judgment by misapprehending the law on a superficies acquired together with a mortgage in order to secure the security value thereof, or on the proviso to Civil Act Article 256, without fully conducting the necessary examination. The grounds of appeal arguing to this effect are well-founded.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, we reverse the part of the lower court judgment concerning the principal claim and remand this part of the case to the lower court for further trial and determination; by unanimous opinion of the Justices involved, we render the judgment as stated in the decretal part."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning indivisible claims and obligations are correct? (Where there is dispute, according to precedents)
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2021DA264253]": "We determine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Outline of the case\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts may be found.\\n\\na. On August 2, 2016, the Plaintiffs and Nonparty 1 (hereinafter referred to as “Nonparty 1, etc.”) entered into the lease agreement at issue with the Defendant, under which the building at issue was jointly leased for a deposit of KRW 200,000,000, monthly rent of KRW 14,000,000, and a lease term from August 17, 2016 to August 21, 2018. The lease agreement at issue included, as a special provision, the following: “All responsibility for this contract shall be jointly and severally borne by the joint names holders.”\\n\\nb. On August 3, 2016, Nonparty 1, etc. entered into the operating agreement at issue necessary for the operation of the restaurant at issue located in the building at issue. Its content was that Nonparty 1, etc. would each contribute equal amounts to raise the lease deposit, etc., while Nonparty 1 would exclusively operate the restaurant, the Plaintiffs would receive KRW 5,000,000 each month regardless of the restaurant’s management situation, Nonparty 1 would keep the remaining profits, and Nonparty 1 would bear all monetary expenditures arising from the operation of the restaurant, such as labor costs and material costs. Accordingly, Nonparty 1 completed business registration in his own name alone and operated the restaurant at issue.\\n\\nc. Nonparty 1 was in arrears in the payment of rent due to poor business performance, and Nonparty 1 and the Defendant agreed to terminate the lease agreement at issue around September 30, 2017. In the course of that process, Nonparty 1 and the Defendant agreed to deduct from the lease deposit of KRW 200,000,000 a total of KRW 149,985,396, consisting of overdue rent, certain debts assumed by the Defendant among the debts and wage debts arising from Nonparty 1’s operation of the restaurant at issue, and the restaurant operating funds loaned by the Defendant to Nonparty 1 (hereinafter referred to as “the setoff agreement at issue”).\\n\\nd. Meanwhile, Nonparty 2, the creditor of Nonparty 1, obtained on December 1, 2017, from the Daejeon District Court, Case No. 2017TACHAE14602, an order of seizure and assignment (hereinafter referred to as “the seizure and assignment order at issue”) with respect to KRW 43,404,524 out of Nonparty 1’s claim for return of the lease deposit against the Defendant, and it became final as is.\\n\\n2. Regarding the Plaintiffs’ first ground for final appeal and the Defendant’s ground for final appeal\\nThe court below held, for the reasons stated in the judgment, that it is difficult to view Nonparty 1, etc. as having formed a partnership externally and thereby holding, in quasi-co-ownership, the claim concerning the operation of the restaurant at issue, and that the claim for return of the lease deposit under the lease agreement at issue (hereinafter referred to as “the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue”) is an indivisible claim of the Plaintiffs and Nonparty 1, who are joint lessees.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the judgment below in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the court below’s determination is understandable, and it contains no error that, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, exceeded the limits of free evaluation of evidence in violation of logic and rules of experience, or that misapprehended the legal principles concerning the legal nature of a joint lessee’s claim for return of a lease deposit, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n3. Regarding the Plaintiffs’ second ground for final appeal\\na. The court below’s determination\\nThe court below deducted the amount of the setoff agreement at issue from the lease deposit at issue to be returned to the Plaintiffs, on the premise that the effect of the setoff agreement at issue between Nonparty 1 and the Defendant also extended to the Plaintiffs.\\n\\nb. The Supreme Court’s determination\\nHowever, the court below’s determination cannot be upheld as is for the following reasons.\\n\\nDebts of Nonparty 1 concerning the operation of the restaurant at issue, which are not directly related to the lease agreement at issue, cannot be viewed as secured by the lease deposit at issue unless there was a separate agreement between the Defendant and Nonparty 1, etc., the joint lessees under the lease agreement at issue. However, the setoff agreement at issue was entered into solely by Nonparty 1, who is one of the indivisible creditors, and the Defendant, without the involvement of the Plaintiffs, who are the other indivisible creditors, and therefore, in principle, its effect does not extend to the Plaintiffs. If the effect of the setoff agreement at issue were to extend to the Plaintiffs, circumstances such as Nonparty 1 having been granted authority of representation by the Plaintiffs in relation to the setoff agreement at issue would separately need to be recognized. Nevertheless, without examining whether Nonparty 1 had been granted authority from the Plaintiffs to conclude the setoff agreement at issue, the court below held that the effect of the setoff agreement at issue entered into between Nonparty 1 and the Defendant extended to the Plaintiffs on the ground that Nonparty 1, as the substantive lessee under the lease agreement at issue, has internal and external rights and obligations. This determination by the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the legal relationship related to the lease deposit of a joint lessee and by failing to conduct the necessary examination.\\n\\n4. Regarding the Plaintiffs’ third ground for final appeal\\na. The court below’s determination\\nThe court below held, for the reasons stated in the judgment, that the effect of the seizure and assignment order at issue also extended to the Plaintiffs, and on that premise, determined that the scope of the claim for return of the lease deposit to be returned to the Plaintiffs would likewise be reduced by the amount assigned to Nonparty 2.\\n\\nb. The Supreme Court’s determination\\nHowever, the court below’s determination cannot be upheld for the following reasons.\\n\\n1) Where a monetary claim belongs indivisibly to multiple creditors, if a seizure and assignment order is issued with respect to one of the indivisible creditors as the execution debtor, that indivisible creditor’s claim is transferred to the assignee creditor. However, since the seizure and assignment order has no effect on other indivisible creditors who are not execution debtors, there is no change in the attribution of the claims of the other indivisible creditors. Accordingly, the other indivisible creditors may demand performance of the entirety of the indivisible claim against the debtor for all creditors, and the debtor may perform the entirety to the other indivisible creditors for all creditors. This legal principle applies equally where, if the subject matter of the indivisible claim is a monetary claim, a seizure and assignment order is issued only with respect to part of it.\\n\\n2) Examining the reasons of the judgment below in light of these legal principles, by the seizure and assignment order at issue, KRW 43,404,524 out of Nonparty 1’s claim for return of the lease deposit against the Defendant is transferred to Nonparty 2. However, since the effect of the seizure and assignment order at issue does not extend to the Plaintiffs, the Plaintiffs may seek performance of the claim for return of the lease deposit regardless of the seizure and assignment order at issue. Nonparty 2 merely acquires the status of an indivisible creditor vis-à-vis the Plaintiffs with respect to the claim for return of the lease deposit, within the scope of the amount of the claim assigned by the seizure and assignment order at issue.\\n\\n3) Nevertheless, the court below, on the premise that the effect of the seizure and assignment order at issue also extends to the Plaintiffs, held that the Plaintiffs’ claim for return of the lease deposit is reduced by as much as the amount assigned, merely because part of the indivisible claim was assigned to Nonparty 2 pursuant to that assignment order. This determination by the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the scope of the effect of an indivisible claim and a seizure and assignment order.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the portion of the judgment below that ruled against the Plaintiffs is reversed, and this case, insofar as it pertains thereto, is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. All of the Defendant’s final appeal is dismissed. Accordingly, it is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[78DA2088]": "We address the first ground of appeal asserted by the Defendant’s litigation representative.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below duly found that the Plaintiff and a third party acquired the land in this case on 1975.11.20., completed registration of the transfer of ownership, and that the Plaintiff acquired the said third party’s share interest on 1976.4.17. and completed registration of the transfer of that share interest, and held that the Defendant, who is in possession thereof without title, must return to the Plaintiff 824,393 won, being unjust enrichment equivalent to rent for the entire 224 pyeong of the land in this case for the period from 1975.11.20. to 1976.11.20.\\n\\nHowever, according to the facts found by the court below, the Plaintiff was, from 1975.11.20. until 1976.4.17., when it acquired the said third party’s share interest, merely a co-owner of the land in this case, and a co-owner, absent special circumstances, may exercise a claim for return of unjust enrichment equivalent to rent only within the scope of the ratio corresponding to its share. If so, unless special circumstances exist, in calculating the unjust enrichment equivalent to rent of the Defendant that the Plaintiff could claim during the above co-ownership period, the court below should first have determined the ratio of the Plaintiff’s share and then calculated the amount equivalent to rent within the scope of the ratio corresponding to that share; notwithstanding this, the court below did not proceed in that manner and, without even examining whether such special circumstances existed, calculated the entire amount equivalent to rent for the land in this case from 1975.11.20. to 1976.11.20. and ordered the Defendant to pay it. This constitutes an error of incomplete hearing or insufficiency of reasons, which affected the outcome of the judgment; accordingly, the argument on this point is well-founded, and the judgment below cannot escape reversal without the need to examine the remaining grounds of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the judgment below adverse to the Defendant is reversed, and the case is remanded to the Gwangju High Court, the court below, for further proceedings. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating, as stated in the disposition."}

question: A, the owner of X real property, had on 2010. 2. 1. a provisional registration of the right to claim transfer of ownership made in favor of B with respect to X real property based on a sales reservation dated 2010. 1. 20., but A and B did not separately agree on the period for exercising the right to complete the reservation. C, a creditor of A, made a lawful provisional attachment registration on X real property on 2011. 2. 1. Which of the following statements concerning this is incorrect? (Each statement is independent, and where there is a dispute, the precedents apply)
A: If A sold X real property to B on 2024. 1. 10. and, pursuant to an agreement between A and B to utilize the provisional registration, principal registration of ownership transfer in B's name for X real property was made on 2024. 2. 1., B acquires ownership of X real property.
B: If A sold X real property to B on 2024. 1. 10. and, pursuant to an agreement between A and B to utilize the provisional registration, principal registration of ownership transfer in B's name for X real property was made on 2024. 2. 1., thereby the provisional attachment registration in C's name was cancelled, B bears the duty to make a declaration of intent of consent to the procedure for restoration registration of C's provisional attachment registration.
C: If A concluded a sales reservation concerning X real property with D on 2024. 2. 1. and, pursuant to an agreement between A and D to utilize the provisional registration, an additional registration of the transfer of the provisional registration in D's name was made, D may oppose A's claim for cancellation of the provisional registration.
D: If A concluded a sales reservation concerning X real property with D on 2024. 2. 1. and, pursuant to an agreement between A and D to utilize the provisional registration, an additional registration of the transfer of the provisional registration in D's name was made, D cannot assert the validity of the provisional registration against C.
E: If C, by subrogation to A, claims cancellation of the provisional registration, D cannot oppose C by the agreement to utilize the provisional registration between A and D.
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2009DA4787]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Where a provisional registration has been completed for the preservation of a claim for registration of transfer of ownership based on a pre-contract for the sale of real property, if the right to complete the sales reservation has been extinguished, such provisional registration shall also lose its effect and be cancelled; however, if the owner of the real property enters into a new pre-contract for sale with a third party and agrees to utilize the already ineffective provisional registration in order to preserve the claim for registration of transfer of ownership arising therefrom, and the supplementary registration transferring the provisional registration is in fact made, then such third party, who has had the supplementary registration transferring the provisional registration made, may at any time assert against the owner of the real property the said agreement to utilize the provisional registration and resist a claim for cancellation of the provisional registration, but, as against a person who, before the supplementary registration transferring the provisional registration, has come to have an interest in the register, it cannot assert the validity of the provisional registration on the basis of the fact of the agreement to utilize the provisional registration (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision rendered on 1998. 3. 24., 97DA56242).\\n\\nMeanwhile, because the creditor’s subrogation right consists of exercising the debtor’s right against the third-party debtor, the third-party debtor may oppose the creditor with any defense available against the debtor; however, the creditor may assert only within the scope of the grounds that the debtor himself or herself could assert, and may not assert grounds based on independent circumstances between itself and the third-party debtor.\\n\\n2. Based on the evidence it admitted, the court below found that First-Instance Co-Defendant 1, on 1991. 4. 26., entered into a debenture guarantee insurance contract with the Plaintiff (under which the insured were each of the debenture creditors, the insured amount was 1,450,000,000 won, and the insurance period was from 1991. 4. 25. to 1994. 4. 25.; hereinafter “the instant guarantee insurance contract”), and that First-Instance Co-Defendant 5 jointly and severally guaranteed, on the same day, all debts, including reimbursement debt, that First-Instance Co-Defendant 1 would owe to the Plaintiff under the instant guarantee insurance contract; that thereafter an insured event occurred and the Plaintiff performed the guaranteed obligation, and the amount of the resulting reimbursement claim as of 2006. 2. 28. reached KRW 1,502,133,292; that, however, on 1981. 7. 1., First-Instance Co-Defendant 5 entered into a pre-contract for sale with respect to the instant real property owned by him, with the non-party as the person entitled to the rights under the pre-contract (hereinafter “the instant sales reservation”), and then on 1981. 7. 6. had a provisional registration of claim for transfer of ownership (hereinafter “the instant provisional registration”) completed in the name of the non-party; that thereafter First-Instance Co-Defendant 5, on 2006. 7. 19., had a supplementary registration transferring the instant provisional registration to Defendant completed (hereinafter “the instant supplementary registration”); that, however, before the supplementary registration was completed, on 1991. 12. 18., a provisional attachment registration in the name of the Plaintiff (under its former trade name, “Korea Guarantee Insurance Co., Ltd.”) had already been completed with respect to the instant real property; and that, at the time the instant supplementary registration was completed, First-Instance Co-Defendant 5 was insolvent, with his negative assets exceeding his positive assets.\\n\\nThe court below further held that the right to complete the sales reservation under the instant sales reservation between First-Instance Co-Defendant 5 and the non-party had been extinguished by the expiration of the ten-year peremptive period from the date of the reservation, and thus the instant provisional registration had lost its effect; however, because Defendant and First-Instance Co-Defendant 5 agreed to utilize the instant provisional registration, Defendant could also oppose the Plaintiff, who seeks cancellation of the instant provisional registration by subrogating First-Instance Co-Defendant 5, by reason of the agreement to utilize the registration; but since the utilization of a registration is permitted only where no third party having an interest in the register has arisen before the agreement to utilize the registration was reached, Defendant could not oppose the Plaintiff, who had completed a provisional attachment registration with respect to the instant real property before the supplementary registration transferring the instant provisional registration pursuant to the agreement to utilize the instant provisional registration between Defendant and First-Instance Co-Defendant 5, by reason of the agreement to utilize the provisional registration, and on that ground, granted the Plaintiff’s primary claim seeking cancellation of the instant provisional registration by subrogating First-Instance Co-Defendant 5.\\n\\n3. However, if the factual findings made by the court below are examined in light of the foregoing legal principles, Defendant may oppose First-Instance Co-Defendant 5 by virtue of the said agreement to utilize the provisional registration, and may also oppose the Plaintiff, who seeks cancellation of the instant provisional registration by subrogating First-Instance Co-Defendant 5; furthermore, because Plaintiff had provisionally attached the instant real property before the supplementary registration transferring the provisional registration was completed pursuant to the agreement to utilize the provisional registration, Defendant cannot, within that scope, oppose the Plaintiff by virtue of the said agreement to utilize the provisional registration; nevertheless, it should be deemed that the Plaintiff, who seeks cancellation of the instant provisional registration by subrogating First-Instance Co-Defendant 5, cannot assert against Defendant such grounds as the Plaintiff itself, rather than First-Instance Co-Defendant 5, has against Defendant.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, on a different premise, granted the Plaintiff’s primary claim in this case on the ground that Defendant could not oppose the Plaintiff by virtue of the said agreement to utilize the provisional registration; accordingly, the judgment below constitutes a case where there was an error affecting the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the utilization of a void registration, or a case where there is a contradiction in the grounds for the judgment. The ground of appeal on this point is meritorious.\\n\\n4. Therefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination; and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2017DA204629]": "The grounds of appeal (including a supplemental brief on the grounds of appeal, etc. submitted after the expiration of the period for submitting the statement of grounds of appeal, but only to the extent that it supplements them) are examined.\\n\\n1. Whether the Plaintiff’s provisional seizure is extinguished upon completion of acquisitive prescription\\n\\na. Facts\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the judgment below and the record, the following circumstances can be ascertained.\\n\\nNon-party 1, on 1985. 11. 25., granted Non-party 2 a preliminary registration of the right to claim transfer of ownership based on a sales reservation with respect to the real property in this case owned by Non-party 1 (hereinafter referred to as “the preliminary registration in this case”). The Plaintiff, a creditor of Non-party 1, made a registration of provisional seizure in this case with respect to the real property in this case on 2005. 8. 29. Non-party 2 completed the principal registration based on the preliminary registration in this case on 2005. 9. 15. and commenced possession around that time; as a result, the registration of provisional seizure in this case was canceled ex officio on 2005. 10. 24. The Defendants purchased the real property in this case from Non-party 2 and, on 2015. 7. 3., made registrations of transfer of ownership with respect to the real property in this case based on sale, in shares of 1/2 each.\\n\\nb. The judgment of the court below\\n\\nThe preliminary registration in this case became ineffective because the right to complete the sales reservation was extinguished by the expiration of the peremptory period; however, since Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 thereafter agreed to the use of the preliminary registration and accordingly completed the principal registration in the name of Non-party 2, the registrations of transfer of ownership in the names of the Defendants based thereon are valid. However, the ex officio cancellation of the registration of provisional seizure in this case due to the preliminary registration in this case was effected without legal cause and is void, and the Defendants, who are the owners of the real property in this case, as third parties having interests in the registry, are obligated to express their consent to the procedure for the restoration registration of the registration of provisional seizure in this case.\\n\\nThe Defendants contend that, with respect to the real property in this case, they acquired ownership free of any restrictions because the acquisitive prescription based on the registry was completed; however, even if the Defendants acquired ownership of the real property in this case upon completion of acquisitive prescription based on the registry, the retroactive effect thereof has no effect on the registration of provisional seizure in this case, which was completed before the date on which Non-party 2 commenced possession, and thus the Defendants’ defense is without merit.\\n\\nc. The judgment of the Supreme Court\\n\\n(1) The reason for the existence of the acquisitive prescription system for real property lies in the fact that, where the state of possession of real property continues for a long period, the law seeks to stabilize the legal order by respecting the factual state that bears the outward appearance of a right and elevating it to the true legal relationship for protection; and, taking into account the fact that a factual state continuing for a long period is highly likely to correspond with the true legal relationship, the system aims to relieve the possessor’s difficulty of proof when a dispute arises concerning the legal relationship.\\n\\nWhere a person who has lawfully and validly effected registration concerning real property and acquired ownership possesses real property owned by that person, such possession, absent special circumstances, cannot be regarded as possession serving as the basis for acquisitive prescription. This is because, in such a case, there is no need to protect the factual state by elevating it to a legal relationship, and there is no need to relieve the difficulty of proving ownership, since the registered owner of the real property is presumed to lawfully hold title to ownership of the real property (see Supreme Court Decision 88DAKA26574, rendered on 1989. 9. 26., and Supreme Court Decision 2016DA224596, rendered on 2016. 10. 27., etc.). However, even a person possessing real property on the basis of ownership may, in exceptional cases where he or she has not registered such ownership and thus finds it difficult to prove his or her ownership, or where such ownership cannot be asserted against third parties, and where it is necessary to elevate and protect the factual state of possession to a legal relationship and to relieve the difficulty of proof, have possession of his or her own real property regarded as possession serving as the basis for recognizing acquisitive prescription.\\n\\n(2) We examine this in light of the foregoing legal principles. Since the real property in this case is owned by the Defendants after they have completed lawful and valid registrations of transfer of ownership, their possession cannot constitute possession serving as the basis for acquisitive prescription. The Defendants’ defense premised on completion of acquisitive prescription with respect to the real property in this case cannot be accepted without need for further consideration. Although there are parts of the reasoning of the judgment below that are improper, the conclusion of the court below rejecting the Defendants’ defense is correct, and there is no error of law, such as the misapprehension of legal principles, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. Whether there was a violation of the principle of good faith or an abuse of rights\\n\\nThe court below determined that the Plaintiff’s alternative claim cannot be deemed manifestly unfair, and that requiring the other party to endure it is clearly contrary to equity, but does not rise to a degree unacceptable in social life.\\n\\nExamining the reasoning of the judgment below in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the judgment below in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the principle of good faith or abuse of rights, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nThe Defendants’ appeal is without merit and is therefore dismissed in its entirety, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices, as stated in the operative part."}

question: The ordering party A and the contractor B entered into a contract for the construction of a building on 2023. 2. 1., agreeing to pay the construction price immediately upon completion, and B completed the work on 2023. 9. 1. Which of the following statements is incorrect? (Each item is independent, and where there is a dispute, it is governed by precedents)
A: If B's claim for the construction price under the contract and A's claim for the defect repair deposit are in a relationship of simultaneous performance, even if B assigned to C on 2023. 5. 1.
