{"[71DA1727]": "Decision on the Grounds of Appeal by the Plaintiff’s Litigation Representative\\n\\nThe judgment below, as the reason for dismissing the Plaintiff’s alternative claim, held that the res judicata of the final judgment rendered earlier than this case extends only to the existence or non-existence of the procedure for registration of transfer of ownership and the right to demand cancellation registration concerning the land in this case, and does not determine the existence or non-existence of ownership of the said land; however, as to the Plaintiff’s present claim for confirmation of ownership, the cause on which it is conditionally sought is exactly the same as the cause claimed by the Plaintiff in the said final judgment, and even if the Plaintiff has ownership of the land in question, cancellation of the registrations effected in favor of the Defendants cannot again be sought in view of res judicata; therefore, since the Plaintiff’s alternative claim for confirmation of ownership over the same subject matter of litigation already lacks the so-called legal interest in confirmation, the Plaintiff’s claim for confirmation of ownership should be dismissed as groundless. \\n\\nHowever, where one’s own right is denied by another person, or where it is threatened or obstructed by a conflicting assertion made by such other person, there is an interest in seeking confirmation of that right or legal relationship against that other person; and the res judicata of a final judgment dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim in an action seeking performance of the procedure for registration of transfer of ownership and cancellation registration extends only to the existence or non-existence of the right to demand registration of transfer of ownership and cancellation registration itself, and does not extend to the existence or non-existence of ownership, which was not the subject matter of litigation. Therefore, in this case, even if the parties to the Plaintiff’s alternative claim, namely the action seeking confirmation of ownership of the land in this case, and the underlying facts are the same as the parties and underlying facts in the already finalized judgment, the present action is a separate action with a different subject matter of litigation; and clarifying the Plaintiff’s ownership of the land in this case should be regarded as conferring an interest on the Plaintiff in the exercise of his rights, even apart from such a claim, since there already exists a case concerning performance of the procedure for cancellation of registration of transfer of ownership that has become final; and so long as the Defendants are disputing the Plaintiff’s ownership of the land in this case, the Plaintiff has a legal interest in immediately confirming that ownership. Nevertheless, the judgment below, on the reasons stated above, dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim on the ground that there was no legal interest in confirmation, and thus erred by misunderstanding the legal principle concerning the legal interest in confirmation or the legal principle concerning res judicata, thereby affecting the judgment; accordingly, the argument is well-founded, and the portion of the judgment below adverse to the Plaintiff concerning the claim for confirmation of ownership must be reversed. \\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the judgment below adverse to the Plaintiff concerning the claim for confirmation of ownership is reversed, and this part of the case is remanded to the Daegu High Court. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[96DA36210]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to violation of the rules on weighing evidence\\n\\nUpon review of the record, the court below correctly found that the provisional registration in the Plaintiff’s name concerning the land at issue, as of May 6, 1985, was a provisional registration for security purposes, under which, if the Defendant delayed performance of the loan debt owed to the Plaintiff, the Plaintiff could at any time manifest an intent to complete the sale and thereby complete the principal registration on that basis, and that the principal registration was completed by the final judgment in Case No. 86GADAN253 of the Suwon District Court Seongnam Branch, on the ground that the Plaintiff had filed an action seeking the principal registration of ownership transfer based on that provisional registration, because the Plaintiff had manifested an intent to complete the precontract of sale against the Defendant due to the Defendant’s delay in performing the loan debt, which was the secured obligation of the provisional registration security; and, unlike what is asserted in the grounds of appeal, it does not hold that the principal registration was completed for security purposes, so it cannot be said that the court below erred in its fact-finding in violation of the rules on weighing evidence as alleged.\\nThe grounds of appeal on this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. With respect to the remaining grounds of appeal\\n\\nEven if, as the Plaintiff asserts in the grounds of appeal, the due date for repayment of the Defendant’s loan debt was September 30, 1985, and 10 years had elapsed therefrom so that the Plaintiff definitively acquired ownership of the land at issue pursuant to the proviso of Article 11 of the Act on Security by Provisional Registration, etc., at the time the Plaintiff, on March 26, 1994, sought extinguishment of the statutory superficies concerning the building owned by the Defendant on the land at issue, as the court below held, the Plaintiff had completed only the principal registration with respect to the land at issue and had not gone through the liquidation procedure prescribed by that Act, and therefore had not definitively acquired ownership of the land at issue, so there was no room for the statutory superficies concerning the Defendant-owned building to have arisen; accordingly, the Plaintiff’s claim for extinguishment of the statutory superficies had no effect, and thus the Plaintiff’s claim in this case, premised on the statutory superficies concerning the Defendant-owned building having been extinguished on March 26, 1994, is likewise to be rejected; therefore, even if the court below’s judgment on this point contains, as alleged by the Plaintiff, an omission of adjudication, it does not affect the conclusion of the judgment.\\nAnd because the Defendant’s raising, in this separate action, the argument that the Plaintiff’s provisional registration in Case No. 86GADAN253 of the Suwon District Court Seongnam Branch was a provisional registration for security purposes cannot be deemed a belated means of attack or defense, it cannot be said that the court below acted unlawfully in not dismissing it, and even if a judgment ordering the principal registration based on the provisional registration had become final and conclusive in the prior action, the res judicata of that final judgment extends only to the existence or nonexistence of the right to demand principal registration, which was the subject matter of the lawsuit, and does not extend to the existence or nonexistence of the ownership itself, which is the premise thereof; accordingly, it cannot be said that the Defendant’s allegation that the Plaintiff’s provisional registration was a provisional security registration, thereby denying the Plaintiff’s acquisition of ownership, conflicts with the res judicata of the final judgment in the prior action.\\nThe grounds of appeal on this point likewise cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged as stated in the order by the unanimous opinion of the judges involved."}

{"[96DA8666]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\nEven where a person is in a position to claim registration of ownership transfer against the owner of real property, if, before such registration of ownership transfer has yet been completed, a third party obtains a final judgment against the owner of the real property ordering performance of the procedure for registration of ownership transfer concerning the real property and completes the registration of ownership transfer, then, unless that final judgment is null and void ab initio or has been vacated by an action for retrial, it would be contrary to the res judicata of that final judgment for the person who holds the prior right to claim registration of ownership transfer to, in order to preserve the claim for registration of ownership transfer against the owner of the real property, assert that the registration of ownership transfer in the name of the third party is void for lack of cause and seek cancellation of that registration by subrogating the owner of the real property; and furthermore, it would likewise be contrary to the res judicata of that final judgment to seek cancellation of another registration of ownership transfer that was completed based on the registration in the name of the third party (see this Court's Decisions 74DA2229 of Aug. 19, 1975, 80DA1836, 1837 of Dec. 9, 1980, 87DAKA777 of Feb. 23, 1988, etc.).\\nAs duly established by the court below, a non-party filed, around July 1991, against Nowon-gu an action for registration of ownership transfer concerning the land at issue, based on an agreement to transfer dated Aug. 2, 1989, obtained a winning judgment on Jan. 17, 1992, and, as Nowon-gu's appeal against that judgment was subsequently dismissed and the said judgment became final and binding, a registration of ownership transfer in the name of the said non-party was completed with respect to the land at issue on Oct. 23 of the same year, and thereafter a registration of ownership transfer in the name of the Defendant was completed on the same day, then even if the Plaintiff has a right to claim registration of ownership transfer concerning the land at issue against Nowon-gu, it would be contrary to the res judicata of the said final judgment between the said non-party and Nowon-gu, and thus impermissible, for the Plaintiff to subrogate Nowon-gu, assert that the registration of ownership transfer in the name of the said non-party is void for lack of cause, and seek cancellation of the registration of ownership transfer in the name of the Defendant that was completed based on that registration.\\nMeanwhile, the remaining argument in the grounds of appeal is that, for the Plaintiff, there is no need to subrogate Nowon-gu, and the Plaintiff may directly seek, in the status of an interested party, cancellation of the registration of ownership transfer in the name of the Defendant; however, this is merely an independent view and cannot be accepted.\\nAlthough the explanation given by the court below is somewhat insufficient, the conclusion of the court below dismissing the Plaintiff's claim is correct, and therefore the argument that there is an error such as violation of the rules of evidence or misapprehension of legal principles cannot be accepted. The grounds are without merit.\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party; it is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[99DA3501]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nWhen the judgment on the merits in an action objecting to distribution brought by a creditor becomes final and conclusive, res judicata arises as to the determination of the existence or nonexistence of the substantive right to receive distribution with respect to the amount distributed to which objection was made; and where, after the judgment on the merits in such action objecting to distribution has become final and conclusive, the party who received the judgment on the merits against him in that action files an action against the opposing party seeking return on the ground that the amount distributed that was finalized by that judgment constitutes unjust enrichment, the existence or nonexistence of the right to receive distribution, as determined in the judgment on the merits in the prior action, becomes a preliminary issue in determining whether a claim for return of unjust enrichment has arisen. Accordingly, the parties may not make arguments concerning the existence or nonexistence of the right to receive distribution that differ from the determination in the judgment on the merits in such action objecting to distribution, and the court likewise may not make a different determination.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the first-instance judgment cited by the lower court and the record, on 1991. 7. 10. a registration of establishment of a mortgage by way of security was completed in the amount of KRW 2,000,000,000 as the maximum secured claim, with the said Non-party 1 as debtor and Miwon Co., Ltd. as mortgagee, with respect to 526㎡ of religious land located in Sokcho-si (address omitted), owned by Non-party 1 (hereinafter referred to as the land at issue); on 1994. 2. 28. a supplementary registration of partial transfer of the said mortgage right was completed in the name of the Plaintiff; Miwon Co., Ltd. filed an application for an auction of real property with the Sokcho Branch of the Chuncheon District Court on 1994. 5. 24. with respect to the land at issue, and thereafter the above auction procedure was conducted with respect to the land at issue and on 1995. 1. 5. it was sold by auction to Non-party 2 for KRW 510,900,000; on the distribution date of 1995. 3. 31. the said court prepared a distribution schedule for the distribution amount of KRW 498,745,808, obtained by deducting execution costs, etc. from the successful bid price of the land at issue, regarding Miwon Co., Ltd. as a creditor having priority over the Plaintiff, distributed the entire said distribution amount to Miwon Co., Ltd., and made no distribution to the Plaintiff; thereupon, the Plaintiff filed an action objecting to distribution as Case No. 95GAHAP367 in that court and sought alteration of the distribution schedule by canceling KRW 305,364,602 out of the said distribution amount against the Defendant and distributing that amount to the Plaintiff, but a judgment dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim became final and conclusive on the ground that, in executing the mortgage right over the real property at issue between the Plaintiff and the Defendant, it had been agreed that the Defendant would receive repayment in priority and that the Plaintiff would not raise any objection thereto; and it can be seen that on 1997. 11. 1. while this litigation was pending, the said Miwon Co., Ltd. was absorbed and merged into the Defendant. Thus, in this action, the Plaintiff contends that although the Plaintiff received from Miwon Co., Ltd. the portion of KRW 1,000,000,000 out of the secured claim under the said mortgage right together with the mortgage right thereon, and the Plaintiff and Miwon Co., Ltd., as quasi-co-owners of the said mortgage right, had substantive legal rights to receive distribution in proportion to their respective amounts of secured claims, Miwon Co., Ltd., by obtaining a final and conclusive judgment in the action objecting to distribution enabling it to receive priority distribution, obtained as a matter of substantive law an enrichment of KRW 305,364,602, the amount that the Plaintiff was to receive by distribution, thereby causing the Plaintiff a loss equivalent to the same amount, and therefore the Defendant, who absorbed and merged Miwon Co., Ltd., is obligated to return the above amount to the Plaintiff.\\n\\nIf the factual relationship is as above, then in light of the legal principles stated above, the res judicata of the judgment on the merits dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim in the action objecting to distribution also operates in this action in which the Plaintiff asserts that the above disputed distribution amount of KRW 305,364,602, finalized by that judgment as belonging to Miwon Co., Ltd., constitutes unjust enrichment; therefore, a different determination from the judgment on the merits dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim, to the effect that the substantive right to receive distribution in the above disputed distribution amount belonged not to the Plaintiff but to Miwon Co., Ltd., cannot be made, and thus the fact that the above disputed distribution amount was distributed to Miwon Co., Ltd. cannot be regarded as unjust and without legal cause.\\n\\nFor the same reasons, since the res judicata of the judgment on the merits dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim in the action objecting to distribution extends to this action as well, the lower court’s disposition dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim in this action on the ground that the court could not make a different determination contrary to that judgment is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as an error in misunderstanding the legal principles on the objective scope of res judicata, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe grounds of appeal on this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAnd, insofar as the lower court’s determination that the res judicata of the judgment on the merits dismissing the Plaintiff’s claim in the action objecting to distribution extends to this action is proper, the propriety of the lower court’s alternative determination premised on the assumption that the res judicata of that judgment does not extend to this action does not affect the result of the judgment; therefore, the grounds of appeal asserting that the alternative determination violated the rules of evidence, etc., as alleged, are without merit and need not be further examined.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating."}

question: A lent 100 million won to B, and C and D, creditors of A, each obtained an order of seizure and collection with respect to the above loan claim. Each of the above orders of seizure and collection was lawfully served on B. Thereafter, C filed against B an action for collection (hereinafter, “the present action”). Which of the following statements is incorrect? (Each statement is independent, and where there is any dispute, the precedents apply.)
A: After C was rendered a judgment dismissing the claim at the first instance in the present action and appealed, only to withdraw the action at the appellate instance, if D thereafter files an action for collection against B, D’s action violates the rule prohibiting refiling.
B: If, in the present action, a judicial settlement is reached between C and B to the effect that “C shall receive KRW 80 million from B and waive the remaining claim,” the res judicata effect of that judicial settlement does not extend to D.
C: In the present action, B cannot argue that C’s execution claim against A has been extinguished by payment.
D: Even if, before the present action became pending, A had already filed an action against B for a loan claim and that action was pending, the present action does not constitute duplicative litigation.
E: B may apply to the court, by the date of the first oral argument in the present action, for an order that D join on C’s side as a co-plaintiff.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2013DA202120]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. The purport of prohibiting duplicate institution of an action under Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act is that filing an action again with respect to a case already pending before the court constitutes an abuse of the litigation system; if permitted, it would impose on the opposing party the burden of defending two suits, duplicate adjudication would be contrary to procedural economy, and thus the purpose is to avoid such irrationality and prevent contradictory or conflicting judgments.\\n\\nHowever, where there is an order of seizure and collection with respect to a monetary claim, etc. of the debtor against a third-party obligor, only the seizing creditor who has received the order of seizure and collection (hereinafter referred to only as the “seizing creditor”), pursuant to Articles 238 and 249(1) of the Civil Execution Act, may file an action against the third-party obligor demanding performance of the seized claim, and the debtor loses standing to sue against the third-party obligor with respect to the claim subject to the order of seizure and collection; accordingly, an action for performance filed by the debtor with respect to a claim subject to an order of seizure and collection is an unlawful action and must be dismissed without the need for examination and determination on the merits (see Supreme Court Decisions of April 11, 2000, 99DA23888; September 25, 2008, 2007DA60417, etc.), and such circumstances are matters subject to ex officio investigation, so the court must investigate and determine them ex officio even if no party raises them (see Supreme Court Decisions of March 26, 2004, 2001DA51510; February 25, 2010, 2009DA85717, etc.).\\n\\nTherefore, even if the action for performance filed by the debtor against the third-party obligor is already pending before the court, it cannot be said that adjudicating the merits of the collection action filed by the seizing creditor against the third-party obligor imposes an unreasonably excessive burden of double litigation on the third-party obligor, duplicates the merits proceedings, runs counter to the litigation economy of the parties and the court, or creates a significant risk of contradictory or conflicting judgments.\\n\\nRather, dismissing the collection action filed by the seizing creditor against the third-party obligor on the ground that it constitutes a duplicate institution of an action, and then waiting for the debtor’s action for performance, filed without standing to sue, to become finally dismissed so that the seizing creditor may again file a collection action, not only runs counter to procedural economy, but also amounts to refusing, on the basis of the debtor’s action for performance, which is prohibited by the very order of seizure and collection, the exercise of the right to file a collection action guaranteed to the seizing creditor by Articles 238 and 249(1) of the Civil Execution Act and the aforementioned Supreme Court precedents, as well as substantive adjudication thereon; this cannot but be deemed unjust.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the seizing creditor may also intervene in the action for performance filed by the debtor against the third-party obligor pursuant to Articles 81 and 79 of the Civil Procedure Act; however, where the debtor’s action for performance is pending before the court of final appeal, intervention by a successor in the action is not permitted, and thus intervention by the seizing creditor is not always possible, nor is the seizing creditor under any obligation to intervene in the debtor’s action for performance.\\n\\nTherefore, even where the debtor’s action for performance against the third-party obligor is pending before the court, the seizing creditor may file a collection action against the third-party obligor seeking performance of the seized claim, and it is appropriate to view that the collection action filed by the seizing creditor against the third-party obligor does not constitute a duplicate institution of an action prohibited by Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act in relation to the debtor’s action for performance.\\n\\n2. a. According to the reasons stated in the first-instance judgment cited by the court below and the record, ① on November 10, 2010, the non-party filed against the Defendant, in the Seoul Southern District Court Case No. 2010GAHAP23129, an action for payment of refund performance money, asserting that he had purchased an apartment from Rotuen Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Rotuen Construction”) and paid KRW 247.6 million to Rotuen Construction as a down payment and intermediate payments, but a guarantee accident had occurred in which the new apartment construction work was suspended, so the Defendant had an obligation to pay the said KRW 247.6 million and delay damages thereon as refund performance security under the housing sale guarantee contract concluded with Rotuen Construction; a first-instance judgment fully accepting the non-party’s claim was rendered on May 24, 2011, but due to the Defendant’s appeal, the case is currently pending in the appellate instance before the Seoul High Court Case No. 2011NA47321; ② based on the final judgment in the Seoul Central District Court Case No. 2010GADAN432560 for reimbursement against the non-party, the Plaintiff applied to the Changwon District Court, Case No. 2011TACHAE10363, for an order of seizure and collection against the non-party as debtor and the Defendant as third-party obligor, and on July 6, 2011, received an order of seizure and collection (hereinafter referred to as the “collection order in this case”) transferring a provisional attachment into a principal attachment with respect to “the amount up to KRW 121,593,944 among the claim for return of the down payment and intermediate payments that the non-party holds against the Defendant under the Defendant’s housing sale guarantee contract and that the non-party seeks payment from the Defendant in the action for payment of refund performance money,” and on July 8, 2011, the collection order in this case was served on the Defendant; and ③ on November 25, 2011, the Plaintiff, based on the collection order in this case, filed the present action, which is a collection action, with the court of first instance against the Defendant, who is the third-party obligor.\\n\\nb. Based on the above factual relations, the court below held that even if, with respect to the portion subject to the collection order in this case among the action for payment of refund performance money filed by the non-party against the Defendant, the non-party had lost standing to sue and the action for that portion was unlawful, so long as the prior action, namely the above action for payment of refund performance money, remained pending before the court, the present action, being the subsequent action filed by the seizing creditor, violated the prohibition on duplicate institution of an action and was unlawful; on the same ground, the court below upheld the first-instance judgment dismissing the present action.\\n\\nc. However, according to the foregoing legal principles, the present action filed by the Plaintiff, who is the seizing creditor, does not constitute a duplicate institution of an action prohibited by Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act; therefore, the court below’s judgment, which reached a different conclusion, erred by misapprehending the legal principle on the prohibition of duplicate institution of an action in relation to a collection action, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed; however, since this case is sufficiently ready for this Court to decide directly, the Court will render its own judgment. Accordingly, the first-instance judgment is reversed, and in order to remand the case to the court of first instance for a new trial and determination pursuant to the main text of Article 418 of the Civil Procedure Act, the Court renders the following judgment. In this judgment, the opinions of the participating Justices were unanimous except for the dissenting opinions of Justices Shin Young-chul, Min Il-young, and Lee In-bok.\\n\\n4. The dissenting opinions of Justices Shin Young-chul, Min Il-young, and Lee In-bok are as follows.\\n\\nThe majority opinion holds that, where the debtor has filed an action for performance against the third-party obligor and the case is pending before the court, a collection action filed by the seizing creditor against the third-party obligor does not constitute a duplicate institution of an action prohibited by Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act. However, for the following reasons, we cannot agree with such majority opinion.\\n\\na. The prohibition on duplicate institution of an action prescribed by Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act is an effect of filing an action that arises naturally from the pendency of litigation. Therefore, even if the action already pending before the court (the prior action) is an unlawful action that lacks the requirements for litigation, so long as the pendency of the action is not extinguished by withdrawal, dismissal, etc., the action newly filed during such pendency (the subsequent action) cannot escape dismissal as an unlawful action that contravenes the prohibition on duplicate institution of an action (see Supreme Court Decision of February 27, 1998, 97DA45532).\\n\\nThis principle prohibiting duplicate institution of an action applies where the prior action and the subsequent action are the same case. Now, when an order of seizure and collection is issued with respect to a claim, the seizing creditor may file an action against the third-party obligor seeking performance of the seized claim, and the debtor loses standing to sue against the third-party obligor with respect to that claim; however, the order of seizure and collection merely confers upon the seizing creditor the authority to collect the debtor’s claim against the third-party obligor, and it does not transfer or vest in the seizing creditor the claim held by the debtor against the third-party obligor (see Supreme Court Decision of December 23, 2010, 2010DA56067). Accordingly, the debtor’s prior action for performance against the third-party obligor and the seizing creditor’s subsequent collection action against the third-party obligor are, although the parties differ, substantially the same case, and thus the subsequent action constitutes a duplicate action.\\n\\nMeanwhile, where a creditor, pursuant to Article 404(1) of the Civil Act, brings an action against a third-party obligor on behalf of the debtor by subrogation and that litigation is pending before the court, if the debtor files an action against the third-party obligor concerning the same subject matter of litigation, or conversely, if an action brought by the debtor against the third-party obligor is pending before the court and the debtor’s creditor files a creditor’s subrogation action concerning the same subject matter of litigation, or further, if a creditor’s subrogation action is pending before the court and another creditor of the same debtor files a creditor’s subrogation action concerning the same subject matter of litigation, all litigation pending before the court later in time is an unlawful action brought in violation of the prohibition on duplicate institution of an action under Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act and cannot escape dismissal (see Supreme Court Decisions of January 29, 1974, 73DA351; July 7, 1981, 80DA2751; September 27, 1988, 87DAKA1618, etc.), and in such cases, even if the prior action is unlawful because it lacks the requirements for litigation, the Supreme Court has held that so long as that litigation remains pending, the subsequent action is also in violation of the principle prohibiting duplicate institution of an action and cannot avoid dismissal (see the above Supreme Court Decision 97DA45532).\\n\\nIf so, there is no difference between a seizing creditor filing a collection action against the third-party obligor and a creditor, pursuant to Article 404(1) of the Civil Act, filing an action for performance against the third-party obligor by subrogating the debtor, in that the creditor exercises the debtor’s rights against the third-party obligor. There is no reason why the legal principles of the above precedents should not apply when, in particular, the debtor has filed an action for performance against the third-party obligor and the case is pending before the court, and the seizing creditor files a collection action against the third-party obligor.\\n\\nb. The majority opinion states that it would run counter to procedural economy to dismiss the seizing creditor’s collection action on the ground that it already violates the prohibition on duplicate institution of an action in relation to the debtor’s action for performance filed against the third-party obligor, and then wait for the debtor’s action for performance, lacking standing to sue, to become finally dismissed before allowing the seizing creditor to file a collection action again.\\n\\nHowever, since the seizing creditor has the avenue of intervening in the debtor’s action for performance against the third-party obligor pursuant to Articles 81 and 79 of the Civil Procedure Act, there is no need to allow the seizing creditor to file, separately from the debtor’s action for performance, a collection action, even at the cost of undermining the basic legal principle expressly provided by the Civil Procedure Act, namely the principle prohibiting duplicate institution of an action. Of course, as the majority opinion points out, where the debtor’s action for performance against the third-party obligor is pending before the court of final appeal and the order of seizure and collection for the claim is received, it is impossible for the seizing creditor to intervene in the court of final appeal as a successor in the action; however, even then, the court of final appeal must, ex officio, investigate the circumstance that the debtor has lost standing to sue due to the order of seizure and collection and reverse the action as to the portion subject to the order of seizure and collection (see Supreme Court Decision of March 26, 2004, 2001DA51510, etc.), and the seizing creditor may then intervene as a successor in the action in the remanded proceedings after reversal.\\n\\nFurthermore, as can be seen from this case alone, permitting a creditor who has already received an order of seizure and collection while the debtor’s filed action for performance is pending to refrain from intervening in that action and instead separately file a collection action would result in imposing on the third-party obligor the burden of defending two suits, which would be undesirable.\\n\\nc. According to the reasons stated in the court below’s judgment, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s following argument: namely, that where an order of seizure and collection with respect to a claim is issued, only the seizing creditor may file an action for performance against the third-party obligor, and the debtor loses standing to sue concerning the claim subject to seizure; therefore, once the collection order in this case was served on the Defendant, the action for payment of refund performance money filed by the non-party, who is the debtor, against the Defendant, who is the third-party obligor, is an unlawful action filed by a person lacking standing as a plaintiff, and even if the action for payment of refund performance money was filed before the present action, the present action filed by the Plaintiff, who is the seizing creditor, does not constitute a duplicate institution of an action, by reasoning that even if the prior action, namely the above action for payment of refund performance money, was an unlawful action filed by a person lacking standing as a plaintiff, so long as that action remains pending, the subsequent action, namely the present action, still violates the principle prohibiting duplicate institution of an action and is unlawful.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, the above determination of the court below is proper, and there is no error in misapprehending the legal principles concerning standing to sue in a collection action or the prohibition on duplicate institution of an action.\\n\\nAnd the remaining grounds of final appeal all presuppose that the present action is lawful, so insofar as the present action constitutes a duplicate institution of an action and is unlawful, they cannot be accepted without further examination.\\n\\nTherefore, this final appeal should be dismissed.\\n\\nd. For the foregoing reasons, we state that we cannot concur with the majority opinion."}

{"[2016DA35390]": "1. Facts and Issues\\n\\na. According to the reasons of the lower court judgment, the following facts may be found.\\n\\n(1) On 2012. 3. 19., the Plaintiff obtained an order of seizure and collection against the Defendants, as third-party debtors, with the Defendant Debtor, Non-party 1, and a claim amount of KRW 183,309,000, with respect to Non-party 1’s claim for return of sauna partnership funds against the Defendants (Seoul Southern District Court 2012TACHAE4914, hereinafter referred to as the “First Order of Seizure and Collection”), and around that time an authenticated copy of the above order was served on the Defendants.\\n\\n(2) On 2012. 6. 22., Non-party 1 filed a lawsuit against the Defendants (Seoul Central District Court 2012GAHAP52477) seeking payment of KRW 559,219,358 on the ground of withdrawal from the sauna partnership. On 2013. 6. 21., the above court rendered a judgment that, although the value of the share that the Defendants were required to refund upon Non-party 1’s withdrawal from the partnership was KRW 99,806,683, Non-party 1 had lost standing as a party to the performance action within the scope of KRW 183,309,000, which was the attached claim under the First Order of Seizure and Collection, and therefore “dismissed the part of Non-party 1’s claim seeking payment of KRW 183,309,000 and delay damages thereon, and rejected the remainder of Non-party 1’s claims,” and around that time the above judgment became final and conclusive.\\n\\n(3) On 2014. 5. 22., Non-party 2, the uncle-in-law of Non-party 1, obtained an order of seizure and collection with respect to Non-party 1’s claim for return arising from withdrawal from the sauna partnership against the Defendants, as third-party debtors, with a claim amount of KRW 1,896,000,000, against the Defendant Debtor, Non-party 1, and the Defendants, as third-party debtors (Gwangju District Court 2014TACHAE8869, hereinafter referred to as the “Second Order of Seizure and Collection”), and around that time an authenticated copy of the above order was served on the Defendants.\\n\\n(4) On 2015. 3. 4., Non-party 2 filed a lawsuit for collection money against the Defendants (Seoul Central District Court 2015GADAN38536, hereinafter referred to as the “Prior Collection-Money Action”), on the basis of the Second Order of Seizure and Collection, seeking “joint and several payment by the Defendants to Non-party 2 of KRW 99,806,683 and delay damages thereon.” In that lawsuit, a decision recommending settlement stating that “the Defendants shall jointly and severally pay Non-party 2 KRW 90,000,000 as collection money by 2015. 7. 31., and Non-party 2 shall waive the remaining claims against the Defendants” (hereinafter referred to as the “Settlement Recommendation Decision in This Case”) became final and conclusive on 2015. 7. 15. In accordance with the above Settlement Recommendation Decision, the Defendants made an execution deposit of KRW 90,000,000 on 2015. 7. 24.\\n\\n(5) On 2015. 7. 14., the Plaintiff filed the present action for collection money against the Defendants on the basis of the First Order of Seizure and Collection. The Plaintiff alleged that Non-party 1’s claim for return against the Defendants amounted to KRW 99,806,683, but because the Defendants deposited only KRW 90,000,000, the Defendants must pay the Plaintiff the remaining KRW 9,806,683 and delay damages thereon.\\n\\nb. The main issue in this case is whether, where a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim becomes final and conclusive in a collection-money action, the effect of that decision extends to another collecting creditor who had previously obtained an order of seizure and collection.\\n\\n2. Whether, where a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim becomes final and conclusive in a collection-money action, the effect of that decision extends to another collecting creditor who had previously obtained an order of seizure and collection\\n\\na. Where an order of seizure and collection is issued against a monetary claim, the creditor acquires, pursuant to Article 229(2) of the Civil Execution Act, the authority to collect the attached claim directly without subrogation proceedings. A collecting creditor may waive the right of collection (Article 240(1) of the Civil Execution Act), but in such case there is no effect whatsoever on the execution claim or the attached claim. Meanwhile, a collecting creditor may not engage in acts beyond the purpose of collection, such as release, waiver, extension of the due date, or assignment of the attached claim.\\n\\nWhere, in a collection-money action, a collecting creditor and a third-party debtor enter into a judicial settlement stating that “a part of the attached claim shall be paid and the remaining claim shall be waived,” the “waiver of the remaining claim” portion should be understood as relating to the collecting creditor’s own “right of collection,” which he or she may lawfully waive, and should be construed as meaning that the creditor will no longer exercise the right of collection against the third-party debtor and will terminate the litigation. Conversely, even if the collecting creditor used the expression that the remaining claim is waived, it cannot be regarded as a waiver of the “attached claim” itself, over which the creditor originally had no authority of disposition. Accordingly, the effect of the above judicial settlement does not extend to another creditor who exercises the right of collection based on a separate order of collection.\\n\\nb. Where multiple creditors have obtained orders of seizure and collection with respect to the same claim, the res judicata of a final and conclusive judgment rendered in a collection-money action filed by one creditor does not extend to another collecting creditor who had obtained an order of seizure and collection before the close of pleadings in that action. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\n(1) The subjective scope of the res judicata of a final and conclusive judgment is, as a general rule, limited to the parties, a successor after the close of pleadings, or, where a plaintiff or defendant obtained a final and conclusive judgment while holding the subject matter of the claim for another person, that other person, except where there is a special provision in law, such as in actions concerning status relations or corporate relations (Articles 218(1) and 218(3) of the Civil Procedure Act), and does not extend to other third parties (see Supreme Court Decision 2010DA58889, decided 2010. 12. 23.). Therefore, even if the subject matter of collection-money actions brought by collecting creditors is the existence or nonexistence of the debtor’s attached claim against the third-party debtor, since the litigants are different, it cannot be said that the res judicata of the final and conclusive judgment extends to one another.\\n\\n(2) Articles 249(3) and 249(4) of the Civil Execution Act provide that, in a collection action, a third-party debtor against whom an action has been filed may, by the date of the first oral argument, apply for an order that a creditor holding an enforceable authenticated copy be allowed to join the plaintiff side as a co-litigant, and that even if such a creditor who has received an order to join does not join the litigation, the effect of the judgment in that action shall extend to that creditor. These provisions likewise presuppose that the effect of a final and conclusive judgment in a collection-money action does not extend to a creditor who has not received an order to join, and therefore allow the scope of the effect of the judgment to be expanded through an order to join.\\n\\n(3) A third-party debtor may avoid being continuously sued by another creditor by, in a collection action, making such an application for an order to join with respect to another attaching creditor, or by making payment or an execution deposit with respect to the portion on which the debtor lost. Accordingly, it is not unfair to the third-party debtor even if the effect of a final and conclusive judgment rendered in a collection-money action filed by one creditor does not extend to another creditor.\\n\\nc. A final and conclusive decision recommending settlement has the same effect as a judicial settlement (Article 231 of the Civil Procedure Act). The legal principle concerning the final and conclusive judgment in a collection-money action discussed above applies equally where a decision recommending settlement becomes final and conclusive in a collection-money action filed by a collecting creditor against a third-party debtor. Accordingly, even if a decision recommending settlement becomes final and conclusive in a collection-money action filed by one creditor, the res judicata of that decision recommending settlement does not extend to another collecting creditor who had obtained an order of seizure and collection before the date on which the decision recommending settlement became final and conclusive.\\n\\n3. Determination in this case\\n\\na. The lower court, based on the factual relations set forth above, determined as follows. The legal principle of Supreme Court Decision 93DA52808, decided 1994. 8. 12., concerning the res judicata of a judgment in a creditor’s subrogation action, applies as it stands to this case, in which a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim became final and conclusive in a collection-money action. Since the Debtor, Non-party 1, knew that the Prior Collection-Money Action had been filed, the res judicata of the Settlement Recommendation Decision in This Case extends to the Plaintiff, and the Plaintiff may not assert the part of Non-party 1’s claim against the Defendants exceeding KRW 90,000,000, in contravention of the res judicata of the above Settlement Recommendation Decision.\\n\\nb. The lower court’s determination appears to have been premised on the understanding that the waiver-of-claim portion of the Settlement Recommendation Decision in This Case concerned the attached claim itself that Non-party 1 held against the Defendants. However, even though the Settlement Recommendation Decision in This Case, which provided for payment of KRW 90,000,000 and waiver of the remaining claim, became final and conclusive in the Prior Collection-Money Action between Non-party 2 and the Defendants, the waiver of the remaining claim means that Non-party 2 would no longer exercise the right of collection based on the Second Order of Seizure and Collection against the Defendants, and it cannot be regarded as a waiver by Non-party 2 of Non-party 1’s claim against the Defendants itself. Non-party 2’s waiver of the right of collection does not extend to the Plaintiff, who filed the present collection action on the basis of the separate First Order of Seizure and Collection. Even if, as the lower court held, Non-party 2 is regarded as having waived the attached claim itself in the Prior Collection-Money Action, the res judicata of the Settlement Recommendation Decision does not extend to the Plaintiff, who obtained the First Order of Seizure and Collection over that claim before the date on which the Settlement Recommendation Decision in This Case became final and conclusive. Therefore, if there remains a claim beyond the KRW 90,000,000 deposited and paid by the Defendants, the Plaintiff may demand payment thereof from the Defendants.\\n\\nThe above Supreme Court Decision 93DA52808 cited by the lower court concerned a case in which a judgment against a creditor in a creditor’s subrogation action had become final and conclusive, and thus differs from this case, in which the issue is the meaning of the waiver in a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim in a collection-money action. Furthermore, although it may be said that the subject matter of a creditor’s subrogation action and that of a collection-money action is the same in that it concerns the existence or nonexistence of the debtor’s claim against the third-party debtor, they are not necessarily to be treated identically in terms of res judicata, because the statutory bases and the requirements for standing differ. Therefore, it is not appropriate to apply the above decision to this case.\\n\\nAs such, the lower court judgment contains an error that affected the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principle concerning the effect of a final and conclusive decision recommending settlement in a collection-money action. The ground of appeal pointing this out is well founded.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nWithout examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the lower court judgment is reversed and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination. The judgment is rendered by unanimous agreement of the Justices as follows."}

{"[2016DA35390]": "1. Factual Background and Issue  \\na. According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the following facts may be found.  \\n(1) On 2012. 3. 19., the Plaintiff obtained, against the Debtor, Non-Party 1, and the Third-Party Debtors, the Defendants, an order of seizure and collection in the amount of 183,309,000 won with respect to Non-Party 1’s claim for return of sauna partnership funds against the Defendants (Seoul Southern District Court 2012TACHAE4914, hereinafter referred to as the “First Order of Seizure and Collection”), and around that time a certified copy of the above decision was served on the Defendants.  \\n(2) On 2012. 6. 22., Non-Party 1 filed an action against the Defendants (Seoul Central District Court 2012GAHAP52477) seeking payment of 559,219,358 won on the ground of withdrawal from the sauna partnership. On 2013. 6. 21., the above court rendered a judgment “dismissing Non-Party 1’s claim for 183,309,000 won and the claim for payment of delay damages thereon, and dismissing the remainder of Non-Party 1’s claims,” on the ground that the value of the share to be refunded by the Defendants upon Non-Party 1’s withdrawal from the partnership was 99,806,683 won, but that Non-Party 1 had lost standing as a party to an action for performance within the scope of 183,309,000 won, which was the claim seized under the First Order of Seizure and Collection, and around that time the above judgment became final and conclusive.  \\n(3) On 2014. 5. 22., Non-Party 2, the maternal uncle of Non-Party 1, obtained, against the Debtor, Non-Party 1, and the Third-Party Debtors, the Defendants, an order of seizure and collection in the amount of 1,896,000,000 won with respect to Non-Party 1’s claim for return arising from withdrawal from the sauna partnership against the Defendants (Gwangju District Court 2014TACHAE8869, hereinafter referred to as the “Second Order of Seizure and Collection”), and around that time a certified copy of the above decision was served on the Defendants.  \\n(4) On 2015. 3. 4., Non-Party 2 filed an action against the Defendants for collection money, based on the Second Order of Seizure and Collection, seeking that “the Defendants jointly and severally pay Non-Party 2 99,806,683 won and delay damages thereon” (Seoul Central District Court 2015GADAN38536, hereinafter referred to as the “Prior Collection Money Action”). In that action, a decision recommending settlement was finalized on 2015. 7. 15., stating that “the Defendants shall jointly and severally pay Non-Party 2 90,000,000 won as collection money by 2015. 7. 31., and Non-Party 2 shall waive the remainder of her claims against the Defendants” (hereinafter referred to as the “Decision Recommending Settlement in this Case”). The Defendants deposited 90,000,000 won for execution on 2015. 7. 24. in accordance with the above decision recommending settlement.  \\n(5) On 2015. 7. 14., the Plaintiff filed the present action for collection money against the Defendants, based on the First Order of Seizure and Collection. The Plaintiff alleged that Non-Party 1’s claim for return against the Defendants was 99,806,683 won, but since the Defendants had deposited only 90,000,000 won, the Defendants must pay the Plaintiff the remaining 9,806,683 won and delay damages thereon.  \\nb. The principal issue in this case is whether, where a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim becomes final and conclusive in an action for collection money, the effect of the decision recommending settlement extends to another collecting creditor who had received an order of seizure and collection prior thereto.\\n\\n2. Whether, where a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim becomes final and conclusive in an action for collection money, the effect of the decision recommending settlement extends to another collecting creditor who had received an order of seizure and collection prior thereto  \\na. Where an order of seizure and collection is issued with respect to a monetary claim, the creditor acquires the power, pursuant to Article 229(2) of the Civil Execution Act, to collect the claim subject to seizure directly without subrogation proceedings. A collecting creditor may waive the right of collection (Article 240(1) of the Civil Execution Act), but in such case there is no effect whatsoever on the claim underlying execution or on the claim subject to seizure. Meanwhile, a collecting creditor may not engage in acts beyond the purpose of collection, such as exemption, waiver, extension of due date, or assignment of the claim subject to seizure.  \\nWhere, in an action for collection money, a collecting creditor and a third-party debtor effect a judicial settlement to the effect that “a part of the amount of the claim subject to seizure shall be paid and the remainder of the claim shall be waived,” the part stating “waiver of the remainder of the claim” must be understood as relating to the collecting creditor’s own “right of collection,” which the collecting creditor may lawfully waive, meaning that the collecting creditor will no longer exercise the right of collection against the third-party debtor and will terminate the litigation. By contrast, even if the collecting creditor uses the expression that the remainder of the claim is waived, it cannot be regarded as a waiver of the “claim subject to seizure” itself, over which the creditor initially has no power of disposition. Accordingly, the effect of such judicial settlement does not extend to another creditor who exercises the right of collection based on a separate order of collection.  \\nb. Where multiple creditors have obtained orders of seizure and collection with respect to the same claim, the res judicata effect of a final judgment rendered in an action for collection money brought by one creditor does not extend to another collecting creditor who had received an order of seizure and collection before the closing of argument in that action. The reasons are as follows.  \\n(1) The subjective scope to which the res judicata effect of a final judgment extends is, in principle, limited to the parties, successors after the closing of argument, or, where a plaintiff or defendant has become a party for the benefit of a person who holds the subject matter of the claim for that person, such other person, except where there is a special statutory provision, as in actions concerning status relations or company relations (Article 218(1) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Act); it does not extend to other third parties (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2010. 12. 23., 2010DA58889). Accordingly, even if the subject matter of the action in collection money actions brought by collecting creditors is the existence of the claim subject to seizure that the debtor has against the third-party debtor and is thus the same, it cannot be said that the res judicata effect of the final judgment extends to one another merely because the parties to the action are different.  \\n(2) Articles 249(3) and (4) of the Civil Execution Act provide that, in an action for collection, a third-party debtor sued in the action may, by the first date for pleading, apply for an order that a creditor holding an enforceable authenticated copy be admitted on the plaintiff’s side as a co-litigant, and that, even if such creditor who has received an order of joinder does not participate in the action, the effect of the judgment in that action shall extend to that creditor. These provisions also presuppose that the effect of a final judgment in an action for collection money does not extend to a creditor who has not received an order of joinder, and thus permit expansion of the scope of the judgment’s effect through an order of joinder.  \\n(3) A third-party debtor may avoid having another creditor continue to sue it by, in an action for collection, making an application for such an order of joinder against another seizure creditor, or by making payment or depositing for execution as to the part on which it lost. Accordingly, even if the effect of a final judgment rendered in an action for collection money brought by one creditor does not extend to another creditor, this is not unfair to the third-party debtor.  \\nc. A finalized decision recommending settlement has the same effect as a judicial settlement (Article 231 of the Civil Procedure Act). The legal principles regarding the res judicata effect of a final judgment in an action for collection money, as discussed above, apply equally where a decision recommending settlement becomes final and conclusive in an action for collection money brought by a collecting creditor against a third-party debtor. Accordingly, even if a decision recommending settlement becomes final and conclusive in an action for collection money brought by one creditor, the res judicata effect of that decision recommending settlement does not extend to another collecting creditor who had received an order of seizure and collection before the date on which the decision recommending settlement became final and conclusive.\\n\\n3. Determination in This Case  \\na. Based on the factual relationship set forth above, the court below determined as follows. The legal principle of Supreme Court Decision rendered on 1994. 8. 12., 93DA52808, concerning the res judicata effect of a judgment in a creditor’s subrogation action, applies equally to this case, where a decision recommending settlement containing a waiver of part of the claim became final and conclusive in an action for collection money. Since the Debtor, Non-Party 1, knew that the Prior Collection Money Action had been filed, the res judicata effect of the Decision Recommending Settlement in this Case extends to the Plaintiff, and the Plaintiff may not claim, in contravention of the res judicata effect of the above decision recommending settlement, the portion of Non-Party 1’s claim against the Defendants exceeding 90,000,000 won.  \\nb. The above determination of the court below appears to have been premised on the assumption that the part of the Decision Recommending Settlement in this Case waiving the claim concerned the claim subject to seizure itself that Non-Party 1 had against the Defendants. However, even if the Decision Recommending Settlement in this Case, which provided for payment of 90,000,000 won and waiver of the remainder of the claim in the Prior Collection Money Action between Non-Party 2 and the Defendants, became final and conclusive, the part waiving the remainder of the claim means that Non-Party 2 will no longer exercise the right of collection based on the Second Order of Seizure and Collection against the Defendants, and cannot be regarded as Non-Party 2 having waived the claim itself that Non-Party 1 held against the Defendants. Non-Party 2’s waiver of the right of collection does not extend to the Plaintiff, who filed the present action for collection based on the separate First Order of Seizure and Collection. Even if, as the court below held, Non-Party 2 is regarded as having waived the claim subject to seizure itself in the Prior Collection Money Action, the res judicata effect of the Decision Recommending Settlement does not extend to the Plaintiff, who had received the First Order of Seizure and Collection with respect to that claim before the date on which the Decision Recommending Settlement in this Case became final and conclusive. Accordingly, if there remains a claim beyond the 90,000,000 won deposited and paid by the Defendants, the Plaintiff may seek payment thereof against the Defendants.  \\nThe above Supreme Court Decision 93DA52808 cited by the court below concerns a case in which a judgment against a creditor became final and conclusive in a creditor’s subrogation action, and is different from this case, where the issue is the meaning of the waiver in a decision recommending settlement that became final and conclusive in an action for collection money. Furthermore, although a creditor’s subrogation action and an action for collection money may be viewed as having the same subject matter, namely the existence of the debtor’s claim against the third-party debtor, the statutory basis and the requirements for party standing differ, so the res judicata effect in a creditor’s subrogation action and the res judicata effect in an action for collection money need not necessarily be treated identically. Accordingly, it is not appropriate to apply the above decision to this case.  \\nAs such, the judgment of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the effect of a finalized decision recommending settlement in an action for collection money. The ground of appeal pointing this out is well taken.\\n\\n4. Conclusion  \\nWithout further examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so decided in unanimous agreement of the Justices."}

{"[2018DA259213]": "The grounds of appeal are considered.\\n\\n1. Overview of the Case\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the following facts may be found.\\n\\nDongmyeong Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Dongmyeong Industrial Development”) filed an action against Defendant 1, Defendant 2, and Non-party 1 (hereinafter referred to as “Defendant 1, etc.”) seeking payment of construction costs. On July 21, 2004, the court rendered judgment ordering that “Dongmyeong Industrial Development shall pay to Dongmyeong Industrial Development Co., Ltd. 27,462,600 won from Defendant 1, 67,352,000 won from Defendant 2, and 16,588,000 won from Non-party 1, and, with respect to each of those amounts, money calculated at the rate of 20% per annum from February 13, 2004 until the day of full payment.” That judgment became final and conclusive around that time (hereinafter, the claim arising from the above final and conclusive judgment is referred to as “the settlement amount claim at issue in this case”).\\n\\nNon-party 2 filed an action against Dongmyeong Industrial Development seeking payment of loans and other amounts and obtained a final and conclusive judgment in his favor. On March 11, 2014, the Plaintiffs received an assignment from Non-party 2 of the above judgment receivable and filed an action against Dongmyeong Industrial Development seeking payment thereof. On October 22, 2015, the court rendered judgment ordering that “Dongmyeong Industrial Development shall pay the Plaintiffs 219,500,000 won, and, with respect thereto, an amount calculated at each of the rates of 5% per annum from February 16, 2002 to November 21, 2005, 20% per annum from the following day to September 30, 2015, and 15% per annum from the following day until the day of full payment.” That judgment became final and conclusive around that time (hereinafter referred to as “the final and conclusive judgment in the prior action”).\\n\\nThe Plaintiffs, using the final and conclusive judgment in the prior action as an execution title, designated Dongmyeong Industrial Development as the debtor, Defendant 1, etc. as the third-party obligors, and the claim subject to seizure and collection as 388,813,336 won (95,848,976 won against Defendant 1, 235,069,521 won against Defendant 2, and 57,894,839 won against Non-party 1), and applied for an order of seizure and collection with respect to the settlement amount claim at issue in this case. The amount of the claim indicated at the time as the claim to be seized and collected corresponds to the principal amount of the settlement amount claim at issue in this case and the delay damages accrued thereon from February 13, 2004 to July 26, 2016, around the time of the above application. On December 13, 2016, the court issued an order of seizure of claims and collection (hereinafter referred to as “the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case”) stating that “the above claim of Dongmyeong Industrial Development against Defendant 1, etc. shall be seized, and the Plaintiffs may collect the seized claim,” and the above decision was served on Defendant 1, etc. around that time.\\n\\nOn March 7, 2017, the Plaintiffs filed the present action against Defendant 1, etc. seeking the collection amount and delay damages thereon pursuant to the order of seizure and collection in this case. Meanwhile, Non-party 1 died on May 15, 2017, while this action was pending; as to his inherited property, his spouse, Defendant 3, accepted the inheritance with limited liability, and the children renounced the inheritance.\\n\\n2. Whether it constitutes duplicative litigation or violates the principle of prohibition against refiling (Grounds of appeal No. 1)\\n\\nA. Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act provides that “A party may not file again an action with respect to a case pending before the court.” In civil procedure, the prohibition against duplicative litigation concerns the litigation requirements and must be determined as of the close of oral argument in the fact-finding instance; accordingly, if the prior action ceases to be pending by withdrawal, dismissal, etc. until the close of oral argument in the later action, the later action does not violate the prohibition against duplicative litigation (see Supreme Court Decisions 97DA45532, rendered February 27, 1998, 2017DA23066, rendered November 14, 2017, etc.).\\n\\nArticle 267(2) of the Civil Procedure Act provides that “A person who has withdrawn an action after a final judgment on the merits has been rendered may not bring the same action again.” This is a sanctioning provision aimed at preventing an unjust situation in which the court’s efforts expended on the judgment are rendered futile by withdrawal of the action and the same dispute is again raised, thereby abusing the litigation system. Here, “the same action” is not necessarily identical to what is meant by the scope of res judicata or by the prohibition against duplicative litigation, and even if the parties and the object of litigation are the same, an action may be brought again if there is a legitimate circumstance requiring the filing of the action and not contrary to the purpose of this provision (see Supreme Court Decisions 2009DA22037, rendered June 25, 2009, 2015DA16620, rendered April 13, 2017, etc.).\\n\\nB. According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts may be found. Non-party 3, a creditor of Dongmyeong Industrial Development, obtained a separate order of seizure and collection with respect to the settlement amount claim at issue in this case on May 1, 2006, and filed an action for collection money against Defendant 1, etc. (hereinafter referred to as “the prior collection action”). The court of first instance in the prior collection action rendered judgment fully granting the claim against Defendant 2, granting most of the claim against Defendant 1 and Non-party 1, and dismissing only part of the delay damages. Thereafter, as to the claim against Defendant 1, the first-instance judgment became final and conclusive on October 28, 2008, and as to the claims against Defendant 2 and Non-party 1, Non-party 3 withdrew the action at the appellate stage on June 13, 2009.\\n\\nBased on these facts, the Defendants argued that the present action and the prior collection action involve the same object of litigation and substantially the same parties, and therefore constitute duplicative litigation, and in particular, that the claims against Defendant 2 and against Defendant 3, the heir of Non-party 1, are also unlawful as they violate the provision prohibiting refiling. In response, the court below rejected the Defendants’ argument, stating that “the prior collection action had already ceased to be pending before the present action was filed, and therefore does not constitute duplicative litigation; and because the Plaintiffs filed the present action separately from the prior collection action to enforce their claim against Dongmyeong Industrial Development, it may be deemed that a new protectable legal interest arose, so it cannot be said to violate the provision prohibiting refiling.”\\n\\nIn light of the facts above, together with the circumstance that it is difficult to conclude that Non-party 3 withdrew the prior collection action after the final judgment for the purpose of avoiding an adverse judgment or that the Plaintiffs filed the present action with intent to abuse the litigation system, and considering the legal principles stated above, the judgment of the court below is proper, and there is no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law concerning duplicative litigation or the prohibition against refiling, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Whether delay damages accrue on the finalized interest claim (Grounds of appeal No. 2)\\n\\nDelay damages on a monetary obligation are liability for damages arising from delay in performance of a monetary obligation and constitute an obligation with no fixed due date; therefore, the debtor bears liability for delay with respect to the finalized delay-damages obligation from the time he receives a demand for performance from the creditor (see Supreme Court Decision 2009DA59237, rendered December 9, 2010).\\n\\nAs seen above, when the Plaintiffs applied for the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case, they specified, as the claim to be seized and collected, the principal amount of the settlement amount claim at issue in this case plus the delay damages accrued thereon from February 13, 2004 to July 26, 2016, and filed the present action by treating the entire above claim as the principal amount of the collection money sought from Defendant 1, etc.\\n\\nConsidering these circumstances in light of the legal principles stated above, the delay-damages portion of the settlement amount claim at issue in this case, which was indicated as the claim to be seized and collected at the time of the application for the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case, may be deemed a finalized delay-damages obligation, and thus Defendant 1, etc. bear liability for delay from the time they received a demand for performance regarding the collection money from the Plaintiffs.\\n\\nOn the same reasoning, the judgment of the court below, which determined that delay damages accrue on the entire claim subject to the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case from the day following service of the complaint in this case, is proper, and there is no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law concerning delay damages, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n4. Whether it constitutes payment to the quasi-possessor of a claim, etc. (Grounds of appeal No. 3)\\n\\nThe Defendants argue as follows. Before Non-party 2 assigned the claim to the Plaintiffs, he had already applied for and obtained an assignment order against Defendant 2 and Non-party 1, and accordingly Defendant 1, etc. paid money to Non-party 2 through Non-party 4; therefore, the settlement amount claim at issue in this case should be regarded as having been extinguished to that extent by payment. Even if the assignment order was invalid and therefore had no effect as payment, the above payment should at least be recognized as payment to the quasi-possessor of the claim.\\n\\nHowever, the court below rejected the Defendants’ argument for the following reasons. There was insufficient evidence to conclude that the transfer of money to Non-party 4 constituted payment of the settlement amount claim at issue in this case, and even if viewed otherwise, the assignment order obtained by Non-party 2 was invalid because it was issued while the collection order and seizure obtained by Non-party 3 as of May 1, 2006 were concurrent; therefore, no effect of payment arises under the above assignment order. Furthermore, considering that Defendant 1, etc. were served with Non-party 3’s order of seizure and collection of claims before they were served with Non-party 2’s assignment order, and that they delivered money to Non-party 4 while the prior collection action based on the above collection order was pending, it cannot be concluded that Defendant 2 and Non-party 1 made payment believing Non-party 2 to be the quasi-possessor of the claim, or at least they were negligent in so believing.\\n\\nReviewing the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the relevant legal principles, the judgment below contains no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the effect of an assignment order in the event of competing seizures or payment to the quasi-possessor of a claim, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the Plaintiffs argue that even if the portion paid by Non-party 1 and Defendant 2 to Non-party 2 was invalid, the prior collection action filed by Non-party 3 was withdrawn and the related provisional seizure was also lifted, so the negligence regarding payment disappeared; therefore, the above payment should again be regarded as payment to the quasi-possessor of the claim. However, this is an unsupported argument and cannot be accepted.\\n\\n5. Whether the defense of simultaneous performance is sustained (Grounds of appeal No. 5)\\n\\nThe Defendants argued that the settlement amount claim at issue in this case and Defendant 1, etc.’s claim against Dongmyeong Industrial Development for defect repair costs and the like were in a relationship of simultaneous performance. However, the court below rejected the above argument, holding that it is difficult to conclude that the settlement amount claim at issue in this case and the defect repair-cost claim and the like asserted by Defendant 1, etc. are in a counter-performance relationship under a bilateral contract or are in a performance-related connection in terms of their substance.\\n\\nAccording to the record, in the action brought by Dongmyeong Industrial Development against Defendant 1, etc. seeking payment of the settlement amount claim at issue in this case, Defendant 1, etc. had never argued that the defect repair-cost claim and the like were in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the above settlement amount claim, and moreover, there is no direct evidence that Defendant 1, etc. actually hold defect repair-cost claims and the like against Dongmyeong Industrial Development.\\n\\nReviewing the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the relevant legal principles and the circumstances stated above, the judgment below contains no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law on simultaneous performance or by finding facts beyond the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n6. Whether there was a violation of the principle of good faith (Grounds of appeal No. 6)\\n\\nThe Defendants argued that the Plaintiffs received an assignment of the settlement amount claim at issue in this case from Non-party 2, who was at that time in a state of dementia, solely for litigation purposes, and that considering the circumstance that Defendant 1, etc. made partial payments to Non-party 2, the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case and the present action constitute an abuse of rights or were used as means of an antisocial legal act and therefore cannot be permitted.\\n\\nHowever, the court below rejected the Defendants’ argument for the following reasons. Even if the assignment of claim between the Plaintiffs and Non-party 2 is invalid, it does not, in principle, affect the validity of the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case, which was issued on the basis of a valid execution title. There are no circumstances indicating that the above assignment of claim constitutes a crime subject to criminal punishment, and the Defendants’ assertion of payment is difficult to accept. In light of these circumstances, it is insufficient to conclude that the enforcement based on the order of seizure and collection of claims at issue in this case is manifestly unjust, that requiring the other party to accept its enforcement is clearly contrary to justice, and that it is socially unacceptable.\\n\\nReviewing the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the judgment below contains no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law on the principle of good faith or abuse of rights, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n7. Remaining grounds of appeal (Grounds of appeal Nos. 3 and 4)\\n\\nAll of the remaining grounds of appeal merely contest the selection and assessment of evidence and the fact-finding, which are matters within the exclusive province of the fact-finding court below, and therefore cannot constitute lawful grounds of appeal. Furthermore, even upon review of the record, there is no error in the judgment below that affected the judgment by failing to conduct the necessary examination or by finding facts beyond the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n8. Conclusion\\n\\nThe Defendants’ appeal is without merit, and all of it is dismissed. The appellate costs shall be borne by the losing parties. Since it is manifest that the amount of “28,947,420 won” in item 1.(b).3) of the operative part of the judgment below is a clerical error for “28,947,419 won,” the Court corrects it ex officio, and accordingly renders judgment as stated in the operative part, by unanimous opinion of the Justices."}

{"[96DA13781]": "1.
