We consider the grounds for final appeal advanced by the Plaintiff’s counsel.\\n\\nThe court below, while dismissing more than one-fourth of the Plaintiff’s claim in the court of first instance, reversed that part on the ground that the court of first instance had erroneously determined that delay damages at the rate of 25% per annum prescribed in Article 3(1) of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Promotion, etc. of Legal Proceedings applied from the day following service of a duplicate of the complaint; and one may sufficiently infer that, pursuant to Article 3(2) of the said Special Act, it regarded it as reasonable to contest, until the date of pronouncement of the appellate judgment, the existence or scope of the obligation to perform, and applied delay damages at the rate of 25% per annum prescribed in Article 3(1) of the said Special Act from the day following such pronouncement. There is no illegality such as an error of law in the interpretation of Article 3 of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Promotion, etc. of Legal Proceedings, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n2. We consider the grounds for final appeal advanced by the Defendant’s counsel.\\n\\na. On Issue 1\\n\\nAccording to the notarial deed of a contract for payment of debts (Exhibit A-1) relied upon as a ground for final appeal, the debtor, the non-party Daekyung Precision Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the non-party company), acknowledged that the unpaid wages, bonuses, and retirement allowances owed to the creditors, namely the company’s employees represented by Selected Party 2 and 128 others (the list of the 129 employees is attached), accrued between November 1, 1991 and January 30, 1992, amounting to KRW 368,869,241 (the individual wage details of the 129 employees are attached), and consented that it would pay the creditors (the employees) by February 6, 1992 and that, if it failed to do so, there would be no objection to immediate compulsory execution. It further states that, as of February 8, 1992, a writ of execution is issued to Selected Party 2, the representative of the employees, for the purpose of executing against the debtor, the non-party company, in respect of the attached employees (apparently with the list of the 129 employees and their individual wage details attached). Accordingly, the said notarized deed shall be deemed to constitute an enforceable title, or to have executory force, not only for Selected Party 2 but also for the remaining 128 employees listed in the attached schedule. And, according to the authenticated copy of the order of attachment and collection made on the basis of the said writ of execution (Exhibit A-2), it states that the creditor’s selected party, Selected Party 2, and those listed in the attached schedule are the selected parties, and in the dispositive part it states that the attached claims may be collected by the creditors in proportion to the amount of the claims set forth in the attached schedule, while specifying in the attached list of creditors (selected parties) the names of the 129 employees and their individual claim amounts. Therefore, the action for collection brought by the 129 employees listed in the attached schedule, including Selected Party 2, after newly selecting the Plaintiff (selected party) as the selected party, is lawful. Accordingly, it cannot be said that the court below erred in law, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, with respect to the subjective scope of executory force in a notarized deed or the Plaintiff’s standing in an action for collection, or that it failed to fully examine whether the Plaintiff lacked standing.\\n\\nb. On Issues 2 and 3\\n\\nEven if reorganization proceedings are commenced with respect to a company, thereby vesting in the administrator the exclusive right to manage and dispose of the company’s business and property, the company’s legal personality itself remains unchanged, and unless there is any special other provision or circumstance, the legal relations between the company and third parties arising before the commencement order remain intact. Therefore, even if, after the workers of the debtor company obtained an order of attachment and collection against the claims of the said company against a third-party debtor on the basis of their wage claims and completed lawful notice, reorganization proceedings were commenced against the debtor company, the attachment and collection order already made against the former company as debtor shall have effect against the third-party debtor or the reorganizing company without separate succession, a writ of execution by succession, or correction. The judgment of the court below, which determined to the foregoing effect, is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as an error of law concerning the status of the administrator under the Company Reorganization Act, the interruption of litigation and succession thereto, or the effect of attachment of claims, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\nc. On Issue 4\\n\\nThe nonexistence or extinguishment of the claim subject to execution is a ground to be asserted by the execution debtor in an action to object to a claim, and not a matter that the Defendant, as third-party debtor, may assert as a defense in an action for collection and thereby refuse performance of the debt (see Supreme Court Decision 94DA34012, decided November 11, 1994). Therefore, the court below’s determination to the same effect is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as an error of law concerning the principle of good faith or abuse of the right to sue, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal. The precedents cited in the grounds for final appeal (Supreme Court Decision 4292MINSANG656, decided November 3, 1960; Supreme Court Decision 84DAKA572, decided July 24, 1984) concern different factual situations and are not applicable to this case.\\n\\nd. On Issue 5\\n\\nThere is no basis whatsoever to conclude that the present action for collection is a case in which the Defendant cannot be directly ordered to make payment to the Plaintiff and must instead be ordered to make a deposit. And, the argument that there was a competing attachment with respect to the attached claim in this case, and that the Defendant therefore refused the Plaintiff’s claim for collection, is raised for the first time at the stage of final appeal, and thus does not constitute a lawful ground for final appeal; moreover, even on the basis of the circumstances asserted, it cannot be said that the Defendant cannot be directly ordered to make payment to the Plaintiff and must necessarily be ordered to make a deposit. An argument to the contrary, to the effect that the court below erred in law by misapprehending the legal principles governing an action for collection, cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all final appeals are dismissed, and the costs of the final appeal are to be borne by each party, and the judgment is rendered as follows by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning appeals is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: In a damages action, where the Plaintiff prevailed in full with respect to pecuniary damages and lost in part with respect to non-pecuniary damages, and then appealed the portion in which the Plaintiff lost, during the pendency of the appellate proceedings the Plaintiff may expand the claim not only with respect to non-pecuniary damages but also with respect to pecuniary damages.
B: A judgment dismissing the Plaintiff's claim by accepting the Defendant's defense of set-off gives the Plaintiff, as well as the Defendant who prevailed in full, an interest in appeal.
C: Even if, in an appellate proceeding concerning all of several joined claims, the objection as to some of those claims was withdrawn, it has no effect whatsoever on the efficacy of the appeal itself.
D: The scope within which the appellee may file an incidental appeal is limited to the scope in which the appellant challenged the judgment by the principal appeal.
E: In an action for delivery of a building, where only the Plaintiff appealed a judgment ordering concurrent performance that accepted the Defendant's assertion of simultaneous performance based on the Defendant's monetary claim, for the appellate court to change the amount of the said monetary claim to a larger amount and render a judgment ordering concurrent performance, absent special circumstances, violates the principle against unfavorable modification.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2001DA68914]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding Ground 1 of the final appeal\\n\\nA cross-appeal is a system under which, even after the appellee’s right to appeal has extinguished and the appellee is no longer able to appeal independently, the appellee, premised on the existence of the appeal filed by the opposing party, seeks a modification of the original judgment in its favor in connection therewith; and the scope within which the appellee may file a cross-appeal is not limited by the scope of the challenge raised by the appellant through the principal appeal (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 94DA58261 rendered on June 30, 1995; Supreme Court Decision 99MEU1596, 99MEU1602 rendered on November 26, 1999). In this case, the Plaintiff filed an action for recovery of money, joining a claim based on the First Performance Bond Insurance Contract and a claim based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, and the Plaintiff’s claims were all granted in the first instance. Even if, in response thereto, the Defendant filed an appeal only with respect to the delayed damages portion among the claim based on the First Performance Bond Insurance Contract and the claim based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, and did not file an appeal with respect to the principal amount portion among the claim based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, since the Plaintiff, who prevailed entirely in the first instance, could expand the claim sought based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract by way of a cross-appeal while the appellate proceedings were pending, it cannot be said that, even if the court below accepted the Plaintiff’s cross-appeal based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract and granted the Plaintiff’s claim in excess of the amount awarded in the judgment of first instance, there was any error of law concerning the principle of prohibition against unfavorable modification or the scope of trial in the appellate instance (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 91DA21688 rendered on September 24, 1991; Supreme Court Decision 91DA43015 rendered on December 8, 1992; Supreme Court Decision 97DA30066 rendered on February 25, 2000).\\n\\nAccordingly, the argument on this part of the grounds for final appeal is without merit.\\n\\n2. Regarding Ground 2 of the final appeal\\n\\na. The determination of the court below\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, after comprehensively examining the evidence it admitted, found the facts set forth in the opinion, and then held that, in light of such factual relation, the defect repair obligation borne by Line Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Line Construction”) and the defect repair obligation borne by Imkwang Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Imkwang Construction”) as a joint surety are each independent and separate obligations, so it cannot be said that Line Construction performed the defect repair obligation guaranteed by the Defendant under the insurance contract merely because Imkwang Construction performed the defect repair obligation, and furthermore, since it cannot be deemed that the damage suffered by the Korea National Housing Corporation due to Line Construction’s nonperformance of the defect repair obligation was not incurred from the outset, but rather was compensated by Imkwang Construction’s direct performance of that defect repair obligation because Line Construction failed to perform its defect repair obligation, the Defendant’s assertion that the Korea National Housing Corporation suffered no damage from the nonperformance of the defect repair obligation is without merit.\\n\\nb. This Court’s determination\\n\\nHowever, the foregoing determination of the court below cannot be accepted for the following reasons.\\n\\nSince a performance bond insurance is intended to compensate the insured for loss arising from the policyholder’s nonperformance of obligations, in order to exercise the right to claim the insurance proceeds based thereon, two requirements are necessary: the “occurrence of an insured event,” namely the policyholder’s nonperformance of obligations under the principal contract, and the “occurrence of property damage to the insured” arising therefrom (see Supreme Court Decision 99DA3693 rendered on June 22, 1999).\\n\\nAccording to the statements in Exhibits A-1-1 to A-1-4 and Exhibit A-6-3, which were admitted by the court below, Article 1 of the general terms and conditions of the performance bond insurance for defect repair performance in this case provides: “The insurer shall compensate, in accordance with the matters stated in the insurance policy and these terms and conditions, for the loss suffered by the creditor-insured by reason of the policyholder-debtor’s failure to perform, in accordance with the contract stated in the insurance policy, the repair or supplementation, notwithstanding receipt of a request therefor regarding defects occurring within the defect liability period after the completion inspection has been passed in relation to the contract for work.” In addition, Article 18 of the General Conditions of the Construction Contract, which was concluded for the construction contract stated in the insurance policy and pursuant to which the insurance policy was issued, provides in Paragraph 1 that, in order to secure defect repairs for the construction, the contractor shall deposit or submit to the construction either cash or a guarantee certificate under each item of Paragraph 1 of Article 3, including the insurance policy in this case, the amount calculated by multiplying the defect repair deposit rate prescribed in the contract by the contract amount (hereinafter referred to as the “defect repair deposit”), until payment of the construction price after completion inspection; in Paragraph 4, that if the contractor or joint surety, during the defect liability period under Paragraph 3, receives a request for defect repair from the construction and fails to comply therewith, the defect repair deposit under Paragraph 1 shall belong to the Korea National Housing Corporation; and in Paragraph 5, that the defect repair deposit under Paragraph 1 shall be returned upon the contractor’s request after the defect liability period ends.\\n\\nUnder these provisions, this performance bond insurance for defect repair performance in this case compensates for the contractor’s loss arising when the policyholder, having received a request for defect repair within the defect liability period, fails to perform the same in accordance with the contract for work; and since it is clear that the scope of the joint surety’s guarantee liability under the contract for work includes the defect repair obligation, the policyholder, when it receives a demand for defect repair performance from the insured, may itself perform the defect repair directly or cause the joint surety to perform the defect repair, and the insured may also directly demand performance of the defect repair from the joint surety. In such a case, where the policyholder or the joint surety receives a request for defect repair from the insured pursuant to the contract for work and performs the same, all such performance is performance under the contract for work, and it shall be deemed that the contractor thereby does not suffer loss arising from nonperformance of the defect repair obligation.\\n\\nAccording to the factual relation found by the court below, Imkwang Construction Co., Ltd., which was the joint surety of the contractor under the construction contract in this case, received a request for defect repair from the insured, the Korea National Housing Corporation, and performed the defect repair in its capacity as joint surety. Accordingly, it shall be deemed that the insured contractor did not suffer any loss arising from the policyholder’s nonperformance of the defect repair obligation by reason of the joint surety’s fulfillment of the defect repair obligation under the construction contract, and as a result, the right to claim the insurance proceeds under the performance bond insurance contract in this case did not arise.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below held that the principal obligor’s defect repair obligation and the joint surety’s defect repair obligation are each independent and separate obligations, and that the Korea National Housing Corporation’s loss was compensated by the joint surety’s defect repair obligation, and thus that the Defendant had an obligation to pay the insurance proceeds under the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract. In so holding, the judgment below contains an error of law regarding the payment of insurance proceeds that affected the result of the judgment; therefore, the ground for final appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Ex officio, we examine the interest in final appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Plaintiff filed against the Defendant an action for recovery of money, joining the claims based on the First Performance Bond Insurance Contract and the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract between the Defendant and Line Construction, and the first instance court rendered a judgment in favor of the Plaintiff in full, ordering the Defendant to pay 310,724,642 won (being the sum of 281,214,642 won based on the First Performance Bond Insurance Contract and 29,510,000 won based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract) and delayed damages thereon. Thereafter, when the Defendant filed an appeal only with respect to the remaining portion of the claims, excluding the principal amount of 29,510,000 won based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, the Plaintiff filed a cross-appeal and expanded both the claims based on the First Performance Bond Insurance Contract and the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, and the court below dismissed the Defendant’s appeal and accepted the Plaintiff’s expanded claims, thereby modifying the first instance judgment and rendering a judgment in favor of the Plaintiff in full, ordering the Defendant to pay the Plaintiff 406,031,775 won (being the sum of 347,011,775 won based on the First Performance Bond Insurance Contract and 59,020,000 won based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract) and delayed damages thereon.\\n\\nAmong the first instance judgment that fully granted the Plaintiff’s claims, with respect to the claim based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, the Plaintiff filed a cross-appeal in order to expand the claim; however, where the Defendant did not file an appeal or a cross-appeal with respect to the principal amount portion among the claims based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract, the principal amount portion among the claims based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract in the first instance judgment in favor of the Plaintiff was transferred to the appellate court by the Defendant’s appeal as to the remaining portion, but it did not become the subject matter of appellate review.\\n\\nAnd a modified judgment in the appellate instance is, in substance, the same as a judgment of partial reversal that, with respect to the portion for which the appeal is well-founded, accepts the appeal and reverses part of the first instance judgment, and with respect to the portion for which the appeal is not well-founded, dismisses the appeal; it is merely a matter of convenience, adopted to avoid making the contents of the operative part complicated and to make them easier to understand (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 80DA2566 rendered on February 22, 1983; Supreme Court Decision 91DA35953 rendered on August 18, 1992).\\n\\nIn this case, the appellate court’s modified judgment, which fully granted the Plaintiff’s claims including the expanded portion, is the same as a judgment dismissing the Defendant’s appeal and accepting the Plaintiff’s cross-appeal to grant the Plaintiff’s expanded claims, and is limited to the portion of the Defendant’s appeal and the portion of the Plaintiff’s cross-appeal that were the subject matters of review by the court below; as to the principal amount portion of 29,500,000 won among the claims based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract in the first instance judgment in favor of the Plaintiff, the appellate court did not render any judgment.\\n\\nAccordingly, the Defendant, who did not raise any objection as to the principal amount portion of 29,500,000 won among the claims based on the Second Performance Bond Insurance Contract in the first instance judgment in favor of the Plaintiff, has filed an appeal with respect to that portion, and such appeal is an appeal against a portion that cannot be the subject of appeal, and thus is unlawful (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DA5357 rendered on May 22, 1998; Supreme Court Decision 2001DA63131 rendered on February 5, 2002).\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, among the judgment below, the portion against the Defendant that ordered payment to the Defendant in excess of 29,510,000 won with respect to the insurance claim under the Second Insurance Contract shall be reversed, and this case, to the extent of that portion, shall be remanded to the court below for further proceedings and determination, and the Defendant’s remaining final appeal shall be dismissed. The judgment is so rendered by the unanimous opinion of the Justices."}

{"[2016DA241249]": "The grounds of appeal shall be determined, insofar as the statement in a supplementary brief of grounds of appeal filed after the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal has elapsed supplements the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding the claim for delivery of share certificates and the claim for registration of transfer of title\\n\\na. A withdrawal of an appeal must be made as to the entirety of the appeal, and a partial withdrawal of an appeal has no effect; therefore, even where, in an appeal filed against all of several joined claims, the appellant withdraws the challenge to some of those claims, this merely has the effect of reducing the scope of the challenge and changing the subject of adjudication, and insofar as the appellant may expand the scope of the challenge again by written or oral statement at any time until the conclusion of oral argument in the appellate instance, it has no effect whatsoever on the validity of the appeal itself.\\n\\nb. The appellate court, after recognizing that: the Plaintiff had brought a claim for confirmation of shareholder rights (hereinafter referred to as the “First Claim”), a claim for delivery of share certificates (hereinafter referred to as the “Second Claim”), and a claim for registration of transfer of title (hereinafter referred to as the “Third Claim”); the trial court rendered a judgment dismissing each of the Plaintiff’s claims; the Plaintiff thereupon appealed from the entirety of the first-instance judgment; on 2015. 10. 30. the Plaintiff filed an application to amend (reduce) the prayer for appeal, the content of which withdrew the appeal as to the portions concerning the above Second Claim and Third Claim; and thereafter, on 2015. 11. 11., the Plaintiff filed an application to amend (reduce) the prayer for appeal seeking partial grant of the Second Claim and the Third Claim, dismissed each of the appeals in this part on the ground that, by the above application to amend (reduce) the prayer for appeal dated 2015. 10. 30., the Plaintiff withdrew the appeal as to all of the Second Claim and the Third Claim, and that the Plaintiff had newly lodged an appeal only on 2015. 11. 11. as to part of the Second Claim and the Third Claim, after two weeks had elapsed from 2015. 9. 30., the date on which the Plaintiff received service of the certified copy of the first-instance judgment, and that such appeal was therefore improper as having been filed after the expiration of the appeal period.\\n\\nc. However, the above determination by the appellate court is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the content of the Plaintiff’s application to amend (reduce) the prayer for appeal dated 2015. 10. 30. was to reduce the prayer for appeal from all of the existing First, Second, and Third Claims to only the First Claim, thereby excluding the Second Claim and the Third Claim from the scope of the challenge, and the content of the application to amend (reduce) the prayer for appeal dated 2015. 11. 11. was to include again within the scope of the challenge part of the Second Claim and the Third Claim.\\n\\nExamining this in light of the legal principles stated above, the application to amend the prayer for appeal dated 2015. 10. 30. did not have the effect of withdrawing part of the appeal, but merely changed the scope of the challenge seeking alteration of the first-instance judgment to a narrower scope than that stated in the petition of appeal; and it should be regarded only as meaning that, by the application to amend the prayer for appeal dated 2015. 11. 11., which was filed before the conclusion of oral argument in the appellate instance, part of the claims previously excluded from the scope of the challenge as above was included again within the scope of the challenge, and it cannot be regarded as a renewed filing of an appeal that had been withdrawn. Therefore, the appellate court should have proceeded to review and determine part of the Second Claim and the Third Claim, which were again included within the scope of the challenge as above, but instead dismissed them on the ground that the appeal was improper as stated in its holding; in this respect, the appellate court’s determination contains an error of law that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning withdrawal of an appeal and amendment of the prayer for appeal. The assertion in the grounds of appeal pointing out this point is well founded.\\n\\n2. Regarding the claim for confirmation of shareholder rights\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the appellate judgment in light of the relevant legal principles, the appellate court’s determination that the Plaintiff had no interest in seeking confirmation of shareholder status against the Defendants is proper, and there is no error of law, as asserted in the grounds of appeal, in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the supplementary nature of an action for confirmation.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nAccordingly, the part of the appellate judgment concerning the claim for delivery of share certificates and the claim for registration of transfer of title is reversed, and this case is remanded to the appellate court for further review and determination of this part, and the Plaintiff’s remaining appeal is dismissed. It is so adjudged, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court participating in the decision, as stated in the dispositive part."}

{"[2022DA211928]": "The grounds for final appeal (the statements in the supplemental brief for final appeal filed after the period for submitting the statement of grounds for final appeal has elapsed are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for final appeal) are examined.\\n\\nOutline of the Case\\n\\nA. The Debtor, Taechang Transport Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “Debtor Company”), transferred to the Plaintiff on May 29, 2015 the business rights including 35 buses operated by the Debtor Company, bus routes, and ancillary facilities, etc. (hereinafter referred to as “the transfer in this case”).\\n\\nB. At the time of the transfer in this case, the transfer price was set as “KRW 3.5 billion, and the Plaintiff succeeds to the entirety of the retirement allowances and wage claims arising from the succession of employment of the employees,” and out of the KRW 3.5 billion, it was agreed that KRW 1 billion would be assumed from the KRW 1 billion of the Debtor Company’s loan obligations to IBK Savings Bank Co., Ltd.\\n\\nC. On October 6, 2015, the Chuncheon District Court rendered a decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings against the Debtor Company.\\n\\nD. On June 27, 2016, the said court rendered a decision granting the Debtor Company manager’s avoidance claim (hereinafter referred to as “the avoidance decision in this case”), and the main operative part of the decision is as follows.\\n\\nParagraph 1: The Plaintiff shall implement, in favor of the Debtor Company, the procedure for registration of avoidance concerning each ownership transfer registration completed under the corresponding receipt number on the corresponding registration date stated in the attached list to the judgment of the lower court, with respect to the 30 buses listed in Attached List 1 to the judgment of the lower court.\\n\\nParagraph 2: The Plaintiff shall deliver to the Debtor Company the vehicles listed in Paragraph 1 of the operative part and all ancillary facility equipment installed inside the vehicles.\\n\\nParagraph 3: The business transfer agreement dated May 29, 2015, concluded between the Debtor Company and the Plaintiff with respect to the passenger transport business concerning the 40 bus routes listed in Attached List 2 to the judgment of the lower court, is avoided.\\n\\nE. The Plaintiff, dissatisfied with the decision in this case, filed the action for objection in this case, seeking primarily cancellation of the decision in this case and, alternatively, as a common-benefit creditor, return of the existing benefit.\\n\\n2. Judgment on the Plaintiff’s Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nA. With respect to the assertion that the transfer is not subject to intentional avoidance\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the lower court determined that the transfer in this case constitutes an act harmful to rehabilitation creditors or rehabilitation secured creditors as prescribed in Article 100(1)1 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Debtor Rehabilitation Act”), that the Debtor Company also had fraudulent intent, and that it was insufficient to find that the transfer in this case was socially necessary and appropriate, or unavoidable, at the time, and further insufficient to recognize the Plaintiff’s good faith.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the lower court’s above determination does not contain, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, any error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning intentional avoidance.\\n\\nB. With respect to the assertion that the amount of compensation for value is excessive\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the lower court determined the value of the business rights, the subject matter of the transfer in this case, to be KRW 4.2 billion.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the lower court’s above determination does not contain, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, any error that affected the judgment by contravening the rules of logic and experience or by exceeding the limits of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\nC. With respect to the assertion that the principle prohibiting disadvantageous modification was violated\\n\\n(1) Since the appellate court may determine only the propriety of the first-instance judgment within the scope of the party’s appeal, even if the first-instance judgment is found to be improper, modifying that judgment to the disadvantage of the appealing party would amount to determining the propriety of the first-instance judgment beyond the limits of the appeal as requested by the party, and thus is impermissible (Supreme Court Judgment dated December 27, 1983, 83DAKA1503). Where only one party has appealed, the appellate court may not render a judgment more unfavorable to the appellant than the first-instance court did.\\n\\nWhether the judgment has been modified to the party’s disadvantage is determined by reference to the scope of res judicata; however, in the case of a judgment that accepted one party’s assertion of concurrent performance based on a monetary claim, the opposing party cannot enforce its own claim without first tendering performance regarding that monetary claim. Accordingly, where only the party asserting concurrent performance has appealed, it violates the principle prohibiting disadvantageous modification, absent special circumstances, for the appellate court to recognize the monetary claim based on the first-instance judgment by changing the assertion of concurrent performance into an assertion of deduction or set-off and thereby alter the content of the monetary claim to the appellant’s disadvantage (see, e.g., Supreme Court Judgment dated August 19, 2005, 2004DA8197, 8203).\\n\\n(2) The first-instance court, after determining that the Plaintiff had a duty to return the specific property upon exercise of the avoidance right and that KRW 1,452,389,384 of the common-benefit claims asserted by the Plaintiff were recognized, changed Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the operative part of the avoidance decision in this case to read: “The Plaintiff shall, at the same time as receiving KRW 1,452,389,384 in common-benefit claims from the Defendant, implement against the Defendant the procedure for registration of avoidance concerning each ownership transfer registration completed under the corresponding receipt number on the corresponding registration date stated in Attached List 1 to the judgment of the lower court with respect to the 30 buses listed in the same list, and shall deliver the respective buses listed in the same list and all ancillary facility equipment installed in the buses,” thereby partially granting the principal claim, and, by ordering the Defendant, at the same time as receiving performance of the above duty of return in kind from the Plaintiff, to pay KRW 1,452,389,384 to the Plaintiff, partially granted the alternative claim.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff alone appealed this ruling. The lower court determined that return in kind was impossible or substantially difficult, and therefore the Plaintiff must make compensation for value of KRW 4.2 billion as restoration to the original state; and, since KRW 1,122,305,321 of the common-benefit claims asserted by the Plaintiff were recognized, it concluded that the compensation for value after deducting that amount was KRW 3,077,694,679. The lower court then changed Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the operative part of the avoidance decision in this case to read: “The Plaintiff shall pay to the Defendant KRW 3,077,694,679, together with interest thereon at the rate of 5% per annum from January 9, 2016 to January 14, 2022, and at the rate of 12% per annum from the following day until the date of full payment,” thereby partially granting the principal claim, and dismissed the alternative claim on the ground that no remaining common-benefit claims existed.\\n\\n(3) However, in light of the legal principles stated above, the lower court’s measure of reducing the amount of the Plaintiff’s common-benefit claims is difficult to accept.\\n\\nThe first-instance judgment recognized the Defendant’s right to claim restoration to the original state on the condition of concurrent performance with the payment of the Plaintiff’s common-benefit claims in the amount of KRW 1,452,389,384, and only the Plaintiff appealed therefrom; therefore, for the lower court to recognize common-benefit claims in an amount less than the above amount and to order payment of compensation for value after deducting that amount would, absent special circumstances, constitute a modification of the first-instance judgment to the disadvantage of the appellant Plaintiff, and thus cannot be permitted.\\n\\nThe lower court judgment contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the principle prohibiting disadvantageous modification (meanwhile, although the lower court stated that the amount of the Plaintiff’s common-benefit claims was to be deducted from the Defendant’s compensation for value, it is pointed out that the Debtor Company’s claim for compensation for value and the common-benefit claims of the counterparty to the avoided act are not in a relationship of automatic deduction, but only in a relationship that permits set-off against each other).\\n\\nD. With respect to the assertion that the benefit from the counter-performance exists\\n\\n(1) According to Article 108(3) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act, where the debtor’s act is avoided, if the entirety of the benefit generated by the counter-performance received by the debtor exists in the debtor’s property, the counterparty may, as a common-benefit creditor, claim return of the existing benefit (Item 2); and if part of the benefit generated by the counter-performance received by the debtor exists in the debtor’s property, the counterparty may, as a common-benefit creditor, claim return of the existing benefit and, as a rehabilitation creditor, claim reimbursement of the difference between the counter-performance and the existing benefit (Item 4). Meanwhile, where what has been acquired by unjust enrichment is a monetary benefit, that money is presumed to exist regardless of whether the acquirer has consumed it (see Supreme Court Judgment dated August 18, 1987, 87DAKA768; Supreme Court Judgment dated May 28, 2009, 2007DA20440, 20457, etc.). Thus, where the counter-performance acquired by the debtor from the counterparty to the avoided act is a monetary benefit, the benefit generated by the counter-performance is presumed to exist, absent special circumstances.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the lower court judgment, it can be seen that the Plaintiff remitted KRW 2.5 billion, the transfer price in this case, to the Debtor Company.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing factual relation and the legal principles stated above, the counter-performance acquired by the Debtor from the Plaintiff is a monetary benefit, and therefore, absent special circumstances, the benefit generated by the counter-performance is presumed to exist. Even if the Debtor used that money to make preferential payments to some of its existing creditors, such preferential payments would again be subject to the avoidance right, and it cannot be said that the benefit arising from the counter-performance of the transfer in this case does not exist.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court determined that, in light of the process of payment of the transfer price in this case, the flow of funds, and the use of those funds, it is difficult to find, based solely on the evidence submitted by the Plaintiff, that the KRW 2.5 billion paid in cash by the Plaintiff to the Debtor Company exists as a benefit in the Debtor Company.\\n\\nThe lower court judgment contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning whether the benefit exists where the counter-performance paid by the counterparty to the avoided act is money.\\n\\n(2) Meanwhile, the lower court’s determination that the benefit from the Plaintiff’s assumption and repayment of the Debtor Company’s loan obligations to IBK Savings Bank Co., Ltd. cannot be deemed to exist does not contain, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, any error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning whether the benefit exists.\\n\\n3. Judgment on the Defendant’s Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nThe lower court recognized the facts as stated in its opinion and then determined that, since there are circumstances making the return in kind of the business rights, which were the subject of the transfer in this case, impossible or substantially difficult, the Plaintiff has an obligation to make compensation for value to the Defendant as restoration to the original state upon exercise of the avoidance right.\\n\\nIn light of the reasons of the lower court judgment and the record, the above determination of the lower court does not contain, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, any error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning return in kind as the effect of exercise of the avoidance right.\\n\\n4. Scope of Reversal\\n\\nThe lower court judgment partially granted the Plaintiff’s principal claim and dismissed the alternative claim. Since the Plaintiff’s final appeal concerning the principal claim has merit, the portion of the Plaintiff’s loss regarding the principal claim must be reversed, and the portion concerning the alternative claim, which is inseparably connected thereto, must also be reversed.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the lower court judgment that dismissed the Plaintiff’s principal claim and the portion concerning the alternative claim are reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination. Since the Plaintiff’s remaining final appeal and the Defendant’s final appeal are without merit, they are dismissed. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[94DA3063]": "We review the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nAs to Point 1\\nIn a claim for damages arising from injury to life or body, as in this case, it is this Court’s view that a claim for property damages and a claim for consolation money do not have the same object of litigation (see this Court’s decision rendered on 1990. 6.22. in 89DAKA27901), so the argument that the judgment of the court below, premised on this, erred in law by misapprehending the legal doctrine concerning the object of litigation cannot be accepted.\\nAccordingly, the argument on this point is without merit.\\n\\nAs to Point 2\\n1. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below found that the Plaintiff, in the court of first instance, sought compensation in the amount of 44,238,808 won, consisting of 39,238,808 won as property damages and 5,000,000 won as consolation money, on the ground that he suffered injury due to the operation of a cargo truck owned by the Defendant, and that while he entirely prevailed on the property damages portion, only 3,000,000 won of the consolation money was awarded, resulting in a judgment of partial defeat; that only the Plaintiff filed an appeal and thereafter expanded the claim in the sense of additionally requesting payment of 39,963,294 won as property damages (negative damages); and dismissed the claim on the ground that the Plaintiff’s claim at first instance was, in an objectively joined form, a combination of a claim for compensation for property damages and a claim for compensation for consolation-money damages arising from the Defendant’s tort, and that unless it was expressly stated that only the remainder was being claimed while reserving part of the property damages claim, the res judicata effect of the judgment extended to the entirety of the property damages, so that the Plaintiff had no interest in appealing the portion seeking compensation for property damages on which he had entirely prevailed, and that expansion of the prayer for relief was also not permitted.\\n2. Since an appeal is taken in order to seek a favorable reversal or modification of a judgment that is adverse to the appellant, it should be said, as a general rule, that an appeal is not permitted against a judgment in which the appellant has prevailed in full; however, even in such a case, the law permits, where the opposing party has filed an appeal and finality has been precluded, a cross-appeal for the expansion of the prayer for relief or an expansion of the prayer for relief at the appellate stage so that the remaining part of the claim may be pursued (see this Court’s decisions rendered on 1991.9.24. in 91DA21688 and on 1992.12.8. in 91DA43015, respectively), and the denial of an appealing party’s interest in appealing with respect to a matter in which that party has formally prevailed in full as to one object of litigation cannot be said to be absolute.\\n3. Furthermore, upon examining the record, it appears that, in seeking property damages (negative damages) in this case, the Plaintiff, at first instance, omitted part of the damages for lost earnings by erroneously determining the combined disability rate in the case of overlapping disabilities or the point in time at which a temporary disability was recovered; as in this case, where the Plaintiff formally prevailed in full with respect to property damages (negative damages) but partially lost with respect to consolation money, and where the Plaintiff filed an appeal in the form of challenging the portion of the judgment against the Plaintiff, thereby precluding finality as to the entire case and causing the entirety of the object of litigation to remain pending in the appellate court, moreover since property damages and consolation money in damages for a tort are merely being classified, for convenience, as separate objects of litigation although they are based on a single cause, it would be reasonable to grasp this substantively and to permit expansion of the claim in the appellate court not only as to consolation money but also as to property damages (negative damages); such an interpretation would not unfairly impair the Defendant’s legal stability or infringe substantive rights, and if, contrary thereto, as in the judgment of the court below, the interest in appealing as to property damages (negative damages) is denied and expansion of the prayer for relief is not permitted, the Plaintiff would be absolutely deprived of the opportunity to claim the remaining part before the judgment becomes final, which cannot but be unfair. Accordingly, the argument pointing out this point has merit.\\nAs to the portion of the judgment of the court below concerning consolation money, there is no ground for appeal asserted by the Plaintiff.\\nTherefore, we reverse and remand the portion of the judgment of the court below that dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim, and dismiss the appeal as to the portion concerning consolation money, with the costs of appeal as to that portion to be borne by the Plaintiff, and so, with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices, we render judgment as stated in the disposition."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning divorce-related litigation procedure is incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, the case law shall apply)
A: In a case concerning a claim for division of property, the court may, without being bound by the parties’ allegations, investigate and determine ex officio the subject matter and value of the property division.
B: If one spouse dies while a divorce action is pending, that action terminates.
C: The court must first determine whether the grounds under Article 840 subparagraphs 1 through 5 of the Civil Act, among the causes for divorce alleged by the Plaintiff, exist as grounds for judicial divorce, and only if they are not established can the court then determine whether there exists under subparagraph 6 a “grave reason making it difficult to continue the marriage.”
D: In the case of a judicial divorce, even if there is no claim by the parties, the court must determine ex officio the person with parental authority and the custodian for minor children, and if the court, when pronouncing the divorce judgment, did not determine the person with parental authority and the custodian for minor children, there is an omission in the judgment.
E: Even if the Plaintiff receives a declaration of bankruptcy while the first-instance litigation concerning divorce and a claim for division of property is pending, absent special circumstances, the bankruptcy trustee cannot succeed to the procedure concerning the claim for division of property.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2013MEU2397]": "The grounds of appeal (the statements in the documents submitted after the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal had elapsed, to the extent that they supplement the grounds of appeal) are examined.\\n\\n1. Regarding the grounds of appeal alleging the grounds for divorce by judgment and a spouse at fault’s claim for divorce, etc.\\n\\nThe court, taking into account the entire purport of the pleadings and the results of the examination of evidence, shall determine by free conviction, on the basis of the ideals of social justice and equity and in accordance with the rules of logic and experience, whether factual allegations are true or not (Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Act), and facts lawfully found by the judgment of the court below, so long as the judgment of the court below does not go beyond the limits of such free evaluation of evidence, bind the appellate court (Article 432 of the same Act).\\n\\nThe lower court, based on the circumstances as stated in the judgment, found that the marital relationship between the Plaintiff and the Defendant had broken down to such an extent that it was irretrievable, that forcing the continuation of marital life would constitute intolerable suffering for the Plaintiff, and that the Plaintiff’s responsibility for the cause of the breakdown of the marital relationship could not be said to be heavier than the Defendant’s, and thus determined that the divorce claim in this case involved grounds for divorce prescribed in Article 840, item 6, of the Civil Act.\\n\\nThe grounds of appeal purporting to challenge such determination by the lower court merely amount, in substance, to faulting the selection and assessment of evidence, which belongs to the free evaluation of evidence by the trial court of fact, and the factual findings based thereon. Moreover, even upon examining the reasons of the lower court judgment, together with the above legal principles and the relevant legal principles stated by the lower court, in light of the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination does not contain any illegality, such as misconstruing the legal principles concerning grounds for divorce by judgment and a spouse at fault’s claim for divorce as argued in the grounds of appeal, or violating the constitutional right to equality and the principle of guarantee of marriage and family life, or going beyond the limits of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\n2. Regarding the grounds of appeal alleging the failure to designate a person having parental authority and a custodian, etc.\\n\\na. Article 909, paragraph 5, of the Civil Act provides that, in cases of divorce by judgment, etc., the Family Court shall determine the person having parental authority ex officio. And Article 837 of the Civil Act provides that, in the event of divorce, the parties shall determine matters concerning child rearing by agreement (paragraph 1); that such agreement shall include matters concerning the determination of the custodian, the burden of child-rearing expenses, whether the right of visitation and access is exercised, and the method thereof (paragraph 2); that where no agreement on matters concerning child rearing has been reached or where no agreement can be made, the Family Court shall determine such matters ex officio or upon a party’s request (main clause of paragraph 4); and Article 843 of the Civil Act provides that Article 837 shall apply mutatis mutandis to matters concerning the responsibility for child rearing, etc. following a divorce by judgment.\\n\\nIn light of the textual content of the above provisions, which require that matters concerning the person having parental authority and child rearing in the course of divorce be determined mandatorily, as well as the purport of those provisions to ensure the welfare of children in the course of divorce, together with the legislative history and evolution of the Civil Act provisions concerning designation of the person having parental authority and determination of matters concerning child rearing upon divorce, and the relationship between parental authority and the right of custody and upbringing, it is reasonable to construe that, in the case of divorce by judgment, even where there is no request by the parties, the court must ex officio determine the person having parental authority and the custodian for minor children, and therefore, if the court, while rendering a divorce judgment, does not determine the person having parental authority and the custodian for minor children, there has been an omission of adjudication.\\n\\nHowever, in the case of an omission of adjudication, the litigation concerning that portion must be regarded as still pending before the lower court, and thus the lower court must continue to adjudicate under Article 212 of the Civil Procedure Act, and since it does not become the subject of a lawful appeal, an appeal as to that portion is improper (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DA24083, decided August 30, 2004).\\n\\nb. According to the record, the lower court, while granting the Plaintiff’s alternative claim for divorce by judgment and rendering judgment that the Plaintiff and the Defendant shall be divorced, made no determination in the judgment’s operative part or reasoning concerning the person having parental authority and custodian for the minor daughters, and did not determine such matters.\\n\\nc. In light of the foregoing legal principles, the above factual circumstances show that the lower court judgment contains an error of omission of adjudication with respect to the designation of the person having parental authority and custodian for the daughters; however, since the litigation concerning this portion is still pending before the lower court and thus is not subject to a lawful appeal, the appeal on this point is improper, and solely on this ground alone it cannot be said that the lower court judgment, which recognized grounds for divorce by judgment and rendered a divorce decree, contains an illegality that affected the judgment.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed insofar as it concerns the designation of the person having parental authority and custodian, the remainder of the appeal is dismissed, and appellate costs shall be borne by the losing party. Accordingly, it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2024MEU10370]": "The grounds for appeal on points of law are examined.\\n\\n1. With respect to the portion of the judgment below concerning the claim for division of property\\n\\na. Overview of the case and the lower court’s decision\\n\\nAccording to the reasons for the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be ascertained.\\n\\n1) In around August 2019, the Plaintiff filed the present lawsuit against the Defendant seeking divorce, division of property, and the like.\\n\\n2) The court of first instance, in around September 2022, rendered judgment partially accepting the Plaintiff’s claim for divorce and claim for division of property and dismissing the claim for alimony, etc., while including each of the real properties at issue in this case in the property subject to division as the Defendant’s positive assets and recognizing their value as stated in the judgment.\\n\\n3) The Plaintiff appealed against the portion of the judgment of first instance concerning alimony and division of property.\\n\\n4) Upon reaching the lower court, the Plaintiff advanced an argument regarding the value of the real properties in this case, to the effect that, since the value of each of the real properties at issue in this case recognized as property subject to division in the judgment of first instance had been calculated based on the officially announced individual land price, he/she requests an appraisal of market value so that it may be reflected as a properly evaluated price for division of property.\\n\\n5) Thereafter, an appraisal report on market value concerning some of each of the real properties at issue in this case, following the Plaintiff’s application, etc., arrived on October 18, 2023, but the Plaintiff did not make any particular argument, and the lower court notified that the appraisal report had arrived on October 30, 2023 and closed the oral argument.\\n\\n6) The lower court, in around December 2023, rendered judgment dismissing the Plaintiff’s appeal, and in the reasons therefor, it cited the reasoning portion of the judgment of first instance without separately determining the appraisal result above and the value of each of the real properties at issue in this case.\\n\\nb. However, the lower court’s determination is difficult to uphold.\\n\\n1) One spouse in a marriage dissolved by agreement may claim division of property against the other spouse (Article 839-2(1) of the Civil Act), and Article 839-2 of the Civil Act applies mutatis mutandis to the right to claim division of property arising from divorce by adjudication (Article 843 of the Civil Act). A case concerning division of property falls under a Type Ma family non-contentious case [Article 2(1)2(b)4) of the Family Litigation Act], and, in the case of a Type Ma family non-contentious case seeking performance of a property obligation, such as payment of money, in principle the performance of an obligation may not be ordered beyond the relief sought by the petitioner (main text of Article 93(2) of the Family Litigation Rules). On the other hand, with respect to family non-contentious proceedings, unless otherwise specially provided for in the Family Litigation Act, the provisions of Part I of the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act apply mutatis mutandis (main text of Article 34 of the Family Litigation Act), and in non-contentious proceedings, unlike in civil litigation, the proceedings do not rely solely on the parties’ arguments, but are based on the so-called principle of ex officio investigation, under which the court collects, on its own authority and responsibility, the materials forming the basis for adjudication (Article 11 of the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act); accordingly, the court may investigate and determine ex officio the objects and value of property division without being bound by the parties’ assertions (see Supreme Court Decision 2021S766 dated November 10, 2022, and Supreme Court Decision 2023MU11819 rendered December 21, 2023, among others). Therefore, in a case concerning division of property, asserting the objects and value of property subject to division is merely requesting the court’s ex officio determination thereof.\\n\\n2) In the division of property premised on divorce by adjudication, the property subject to division and its amount are, in principle, determined as of the date of closure of fact-finding proceedings in the divorce action (see Supreme Court Decision 2000SU13 dated May 2, 2000, and Supreme Court Decision 2021MU16933 rendered May 12, 2022, among others). The value of the property forming the basis for calculating the amount of division of property need not necessarily be recognized by market value appraisal, but it must be assessed on the basis of materials having objectivity and rationality (see Supreme Court Decision 2002SU36 dated August 28, 2002, among others); accordingly, the court must determine the value of each item of marital property on the basis of objective materials appearing in the record up to the date of the above closure of oral argument [see Supreme Court Decision 99MU906 rendered September 22, 2000, and Supreme Court Decision 2022MU16282, 2022MU16299 (consolidated) rendered March 30, 2023, among others].\\n\\nc. Examining the factual relations found above in light of the foregoing legal principles, the lower court should have determined the amount of division of property to be paid by one party to the other by calculating, on the basis of objective and rational materials such as the market value appraisal results appearing in the record up to the date of closure of oral argument, the value of each of the real properties at issue in this case as of the date of closure of oral argument in the lower court or a date close thereto, and then calculating the shortfall among the amounts ultimately to belong to the parties according to the ratio of property division. Nevertheless, the lower court calculated the amount of division of property on the basis of the value of each of the real properties at issue in this case recognized by the materials on the officially announced individual land price at the time of oral argument in the court of first instance and by the Plaintiff’s and Defendant’s statements in the court of first instance based thereon. The lower court’s determination contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the law on division of property in divorce by adjudication and failing to conduct necessary deliberation. The ground of appeal pointing this out is well founded (provided, however, that it is appropriate that the lower court maintained the ratio of property division recognized in the court of first instance for the reasons stated in the judgment).\\n\\n2. With respect to the remainder of the portion of the judgment below unfavorable to the Plaintiff\\n\\nThe Plaintiff also appealed against the remainder of the portion of the judgment below unfavorable to the Plaintiff, but the petition of appeal and the petition for appeal on points of law do not contain any statement of grounds of appeal concerning this portion.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the judgment below concerning the claim for division of property is reversed (the determination of the remaining grounds for appeal concerning this portion is omitted), and this case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination on this portion; and the remainder of the Plaintiff’s appeal is dismissed. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[92MEU143]": "As to the grounds of appeal filed by the Plaintiffs’ counsel\\n\\nAccording to the record, the deceased nonparty, as Plaintiff, filed an action against the Defendant, his/her spouse, alleging that the Defendant frequently assaulted the Plaintiff and, moreover, on 1989.9.8. beat the Plaintiff, thereby causing the Plaintiff to undergo suturing for a laceration of the occipital scalp, and on the ground that the Defendant subjected the Plaintiff to severely unjust treatment, sought divorce and damages for mental suffering in the amount of KRW 70,000,000. The court of first instance, on 1991.3.13., partially accepted the deceased nonparty’s arguments and rendered a judgment ordering divorce and payment of damages for mental suffering in the amount of KRW 15,000,000; thereafter, the Defendant appealed and, while the action was pending before the court below, on 8.19. of the same year the deceased nonparty died, and it can be seen that the Plaintiffs, who are the deceased nonparty’s parents, filed an application for succession to litigation.\\n\\nIn response, the lower court held that, with respect to the divorce claim, the right to seek divorce by judicial decision is a strictly personal right, so that when either spouse dies while the divorce action is pending, the action terminates; and that, if the right to claim damages for mental suffering incident to divorce were deemed inheritable as compensation for mental suffering arising from the divorce itself, an odd conclusion would be reached whereby the surviving spouse among the spouses would inherit it; and that, considering matters such as the issue where there is a minor child between the spouses, ethical problems and de facto management issues when such child lives together with the remaining party to the marriage, and the fact that Article 2(1), Category D, Item 2 of the Family Litigation Act uses the expression “a claim for damages on the ground of divorce” with respect to a claim for damages for mental suffering incident to divorce, the right to claim damages for mental suffering is also, by its nature, a strictly personal right that cannot be subject to succession, and therefore, upon the death of a party, it does not pass by inheritance or succession to litigation, and the action terminates; accordingly, the lower court ruled that the Plaintiffs’ divorce and damages-for-mental-suffering action in this case terminated upon the death of the Plaintiff and that the application for succession to litigation in this case was improper.\\n\\nThe right to seek divorce by judicial decision is a strictly personal right of the spouses, and thus, when either spouse dies while a divorce action is pending, not only may the heir not succeed to the action, but there is also no special provision permitting the prosecutor to succeed to the action in such a case, so the divorce action terminates (see Supreme Court Decision 81MEU53, decided October 12, 1982).\\n\\nHowever, the right to claim damages for mental suffering incident to divorce is a claim for damages intended to compensate for the mental suffering incurred when the marital relationship has irretrievably broken down due to the other spouse’s blameworthy and unlawful conduct and divorce has become unavoidable; this right is fixed and assessed at the time of divorce, and is not created for the first time by the divorce. As to whether such a right to claim damages for mental suffering incident to divorce may be assigned or succeeded to, Article 806(3) of the Civil Act provides, with respect to a claim for damages arising from the breaking of an engagement, that a claim for damages for mental suffering may not be assigned or succeeded to, but that this shall not apply after an agreement concerning such compensation has already been formed between the parties or after a lawsuit has been filed; and since Article 843 of the Civil Act applies mutatis mutandis the foregoing provision to cases of judicial divorce, the right to claim damages for mental suffering incident to divorce is, in principle, a strictly personal right that is not subject to assignment or inheritance or other succession, but this is a strictly personal right as to exercise, not a strictly personal right as to vesting; and once the claimant has filed a lawsuit seeking payment of damages for mental suffering, thereby externally and objectively making clear the intention to exercise the claim, assignment or inheritance or other succession becomes possible.\\n\\nAs seen above, since the applicants for succession to litigation are the parents of the deceased nonparty and thus, together with the Defendant, are co-heirs to the estate, that part of the application for succession to litigation in this case concerning the divorce claim would be improper; however, that part concerning the action for damages for mental suffering incident to divorce would be proper within the scope of their respective shares of inheritance.\\n\\nThe lower court judgment cannot but be deemed unlawful in that it misunderstood the legal principle regarding the nature of the right to claim damages for mental suffering incident to divorce and thereby affected the judgment. The argument on this point is well founded.\\n\\nFor the foregoing reasons, the part of the lower court judgment concerning the claim for damages for mental suffering is reversed and this part of the case is remanded to the court below; as to the divorce claim, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal for this part are to be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating."}
{"[99MEU1886]": "The appeal is dismissed. The costs of appeal shall be borne by the Defendant."}

question: Among the explanations concerning appropriation of payment and judicial confession, which of the following are incorrect? (If there is a dispute, according to precedents)
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2009DA12399]": "We adjudicate the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. As to Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\na. The court below’s determination\\nAccording to the record, it can be found that the court of first instance ordered the Defendant to pay KRW 58,104,090 in total, comprising principal and delayed damages, and, among that amount, with respect to principal of KRW 33,775,000, interest calculated at the rate of 20% per annum from 2008. 4. 8. until the day of full payment, and that only the Defendant appealed therefrom; and that the Defendant, on 2008. 10. 17., after the judgment of the court of first instance was rendered, repaid KRW 2,000,000 to the Plaintiff, and the Plaintiff is stating in the courtroom of the court below that he received the said amount as part of the principal.\\n\\nHowever, the court below, as a result of its examination, premised that the Defendant is obligated to pay the Plaintiff principal of KRW 35,000,000, delayed damages of KRW 31,500,000, for a total of KRW 66,500,000, and held that even if the KRW 2,000,000 repaid by the Defendant after the judgment of the court of first instance was deducted therefrom, the Defendant is obligated to pay the Plaintiff KRW 64,500,000 in total, comprising principal and delayed damages, and delayed damages thereon calculated at the respective rates of 5% per annum provided in the Civil Act from 2008. 4. 8. until 2008. 12. 19., the date of judgment, and 20% per annum provided in the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings from the following day until the day of full payment; and then determined that the Plaintiff’s claim in this case is justified within the above recognized scope and should be granted, while the remaining claims are without merit and should be dismissed, but that the conclusion of the judgment of the court of first instance differs from this and is improper, yet in this case where only the Defendant appealed, the judgment of the court of first instance cannot be altered to the Defendant’s disadvantage, and therefore the Defendant’s appeal should be dismissed.\\n\\nb. Regarding the principle of prohibition of unfavorable alteration\\nSince, in the case of nonperformance of a monetary obligation, the principal claim and the claim for delayed damages are separate objects of litigation, whether the case constitutes an unfavorable alteration must be determined by comparing the principal and delayed-damages portions separately, and not by taking as the standard the total amount obtained by adding separate objects of litigation together (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DA40160, decided 2005. 4. 29.).\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principle and the record, although the Plaintiff did not appeal with respect to the principal claim of KRW 33,775,000 granted by the court of first instance and only the Defendant appealed, the court below determined that the Defendant is obligated to pay principal of KRW 35,000,000, which is more than that amount, and this constitutes an error of law regarding the principle of prohibition of unfavorable alteration and is therefore unlawful.\\n\\nc. Regarding the order of appropriation of performance\\nIn appropriation of performance toward costs, interest, and principal, the order of appropriation is statutorily prescribed in Article 479 of the Civil Act, and Article 476 of the same Act concerning designated appropriation of performance does not apply by analogy; therefore, as a matter of principle, appropriation must be made in the order of costs, interest, and principal, and neither the debtor nor even the creditor may unilaterally designate the order of appropriation contrary to the statutory order; however, where there is a special agreement between the parties, or where, as the other party does not raise an objection without delay to a unilateral designation by one party, it is deemed that an implied agreement has been formed, the order of appropriation may be recognized differently from the statutory order of appropriation (see Supreme Court Decision 90DAKA7262, decided 1990. 11. 9.; Supreme Court Decision 2002DA12871, 12888, decided 2002. 5. 10., etc.).\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principle and the record, even though it can sufficiently be recognized that, with respect to the KRW 2,000,000 repaid by the Defendant after the judgment of the court of first instance, there was an agreement between the parties to appropriate it to principal, the court below’s determination that did not specifically appropriate it to principal is unlawful, and the argument in the grounds for appeal pointing this out has merit.\\n\\nd. Regarding the scope of accrual of statutory delayed damages\\nThe statutory interest rate prescribed by the Civil Act or the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings applies to claims for which interest or delayed damages are stipulated by agreement, and in the money-lending contract at issue it can be found that interest or delayed damages were stipulated only with respect to the principal; nevertheless, the court below’s determination that delayed damages prescribed by the Civil Act or the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings accrue from the day following service of the application for modification of claim in this case with respect to the entirety of KRW 64,500,000, comprising principal and delayed damages, is unlawful, and the argument in the grounds for appeal pointing this out has merit.\\n\\n2. As to Grounds 2 and 3 of the grounds for appeal\\nPursuant to Article 2(1) of the Interest Limitation Act and the Regulations on the Maximum Interest Rate under Article 2(1) of the Interest Limitation Act, the contractual maximum interest rate for a money-lending transaction is limited to 30% per annum, and Article 7 of the former Interest Limitation Act (before amendment by Act No. 9344 on 2009. 1. 21.; hereinafter the same) provides that the Interest Limitation Act shall not apply to financial businesses and lending businesses that have completed authorization, permission, or registration under other Acts. In light of the language of the above provision, the legislative purpose of the Interest Limitation Act aimed at stabilizing the national economic life and realizing economic justice, and the legislative history for inducing unregistered lending businesses to register, etc., the Interest Limitation Act applies to a person who, without registering a lending business under Article 3 of the former Act on Registration of Loan Business and Protection of Financial Users (before amendment by Act No. 9344 on 2009. 1. 21.; hereinafter the “former Loan Business Act”), in substance carries on a lending business, and the maximum interest rate in the case where such lending business operator makes a loan should be deemed limited to 30% per annum.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below recognized that the Plaintiff, while in substance carrying on a lending business without registering the lending business, loaned the money in this case to the Defendant, and then determined that, because Article 8(1) of the former Loan Business Act provides that “where a loan business operator makes a loan to an individual or a small corporation prescribed by Presidential Decree, the interest rate shall not exceed the rate prescribed by Presidential Decree within the limit of 60/100 per annum,” and Article 11 of the former Loan Business Act provides for the applicability mutatis mutandis of the provisions of Article 8 to a person who, without registering a lending business, in substance carries on a lending business, only the maximum interest rate prescribed in Article 8(1) of the former Loan Business Act applies to the money-lending transaction in this case, and the maximum interest rate under the Interest Limitation Act does not apply.\\n\\nHowever, according to the legal principle above, insofar as the Plaintiff did not register a lending business, even if it had been in substance carrying on a lending business, the Interest Limitation Act applies, and from 2007. 6. 30., the effective date of the Interest Limitation Act, the maximum interest rate of 30% per annum should be deemed applicable; therefore, the court below’s determination contrary thereto is unlawful, and the argument in the grounds for appeal pointing this out has merit.\\n\\n3. As to Ground 4 of the grounds for appeal\\nIn cases where an interest agreement is made together with a money loan for consumption contract, in order to deem that interest agreement null and void as a juristic act containing matters contrary to good morals and other social order because the lender, by exploiting his superior position, obtains unjust enrichment and imposes excessive counterperformance or other unfair burdens on the borrower, circumstances must be recognized in which, due to the difference in economic power between the parties, the interest rate was set at a markedly high rate exceeding the limit permitted by social norms in light of the economic and social conditions at that time (see, e.g., Supreme Court en banc Decision 2004DA50426, decided 2007. 2. 15.).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below determined that, considering circumstances such as the interest rate and the rate of delayed damages at the time of the money lending in this case being lower than the excess-interest rate of 66% per annum under the former Loan Business Act, it is difficult to deem that the interest rate and the rate of delayed damages in this money-lending transaction were set at a markedly high rate exceeding the limit permitted by social norms; and in light of the foregoing legal principle and the record, the above determination by the court below is acceptable as proper, and there is no illegality such as misapprehension of the legal principle regarding Article 103 of the Civil Act as alleged in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n4. As to Ground 5 of the grounds for appeal\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below found that there is insufficient evidence to recognize the fact that fees and expenses of KRW 5,525,000 were deducted from the principal at the time of the money lending in this case, and furthermore determined that, in the case of the money lending in this case to which the Interest Limitation Act does not apply, pre-deducted interest, etc., as alleged by the Defendant, cannot be excluded from the principal; and in light of the record, the above determination by the court below is proper, and there is no illegality such as violation of the rules of evidence or misapprehension of the legal principle regarding Article 103 of the Civil Act.\\n\\n5.
