Conclusion\\n\\nAccordingly, all appeals are dismissed, and with respect to the allocation of appellate costs, Article 98 of the Civil Procedure Act is applied, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the order by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2005DA51495]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. On the first point of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nWhere several claims that are logically entirely unrelated and should be sought purely by simple joinder are joined and pleaded as alternative or preliminary claims, such pleading is improper and not permitted. Accordingly, if the Plaintiff filed an action in such form, in order for the court of first instance to hear and decide the merits, it should appropriately exercise its authority to direct proceedings and take measures such as requiring correction of the action into a simple joinder claim. Even if the court rendered a merits judgment without taking such measures, hearing and deciding only one of the claims, granting it, and omitting all hearing and decision on the remaining claims, the joinder structure of the claims cannot thereby be transformed into a lawful alternative or preliminary joinder relationship. Therefore, where only the Defendant appealed such a judgment, only the claim that the court of first instance heard and decided and granted would be transferred to the appellate court, and the remaining claims that were not heard and decided would still remain before the court of first instance.\\n\\nAccording to the record of this case, in filing the present action against the deceased non-party, the Plaintiff, as the cause of action, joined as alternative claims: ① a claim for damages in the amount of 5,989,000,000 won related to the acquisition work for the headquarters building, ② a claim for damages in the amount of 400,000,000 won related to a credit loan to Youngnam Ilbo Co., Ltd., ③ a claim for damages in the amount of 2,400,700,000 won related to the sale and purchase of development trust, etc., and ④ a claim for damages in the amount of 795,000,000 won related to real estate leasing work, and claimed 500,000,000 won out of the total amount of damages and delay damages thereon. In response, the court of first instance heard and decided only the above ① claim for damages related to the acquisition work for the headquarters building among the above causes of action, granted part of the amount claimed by the Plaintiff (however, it dismissed part of the claim for delay damages), and, as to the remaining claims, rendered a merits judgment omitting any decision on the ground that the Plaintiff did not wish any further determination if the full amount claimed under any one cause of action were granted. It can be seen that only the deceased non-party appealed against this judgment. Since each of the above causes of action is not logically related to one another and thus is of a nature that cannot be joined alternatively, and since the court of first instance took no measures to correct the erroneous joinder of claims and heard and decided only one of the causes of action while making no decision on the remaining claims, according to the legal principle stated above, in such a case only the above ① claim for damages related to the acquisition work for the headquarters building, which the court of first instance heard and decided, would be transferred to the appellate court and become the subject of review by the appellate court.\\n\\nMeanwhile, when the court below urged the Plaintiff to specify, by each claim for damages, the amount sought as a partial claim, the Plaintiff organized the prayer for relief by stating that the claim for 500,000,000 won in this case was based on the above ① claim for damages related to the acquisition work for the headquarters building, and further sought that, if the above claim were rejected, the remaining above ② through ④ claims asserted in the court of first instance also be heard and granted. This should ultimately be regarded as an application to amend the cause of action to add the above ② through ④ claims as preliminary claims to the claim for damages related to the acquisition work for the headquarters building, and, as noted above, the above ② through ④ claims are not logically related to the claim for damages related to the acquisition work for the headquarters building and therefore are claims that cannot be joined with it as preliminary claims. Accordingly, such an amendment to the cause of action cannot be permitted. Therefore, the court below was correct in not treating the above ② through ④ claims as subjects of review on the same ground, and there is no error in the court below’s judgment in misconstruing the legal principles on the principle of disposition, the principle of pleadings, partial claims, and alternative claims, nor any violation of precedent.\\n\\n2. On the second point of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nThe court below, on the basis of the factual findings stated in its opinion, rejected the Plaintiff’s claim with respect to the 743,000,000 won among the amounts paid as contract deposit that had not been settled, on the grounds that the suspension of construction was not attributable to Gapul Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Gapul Development”) but was effected at the request of Chosun Life Insurance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Chosun Life”), and that no proximate causal relation could be recognized between the Defendant’s breach of duty or tort related to Chosun Life’s failure to collect the contract performance bond and the unsettled amount. This is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any error of law in misconstruing the legal principles on causation. Furthermore, the argument to the effect that the construction work for the headquarters building of Chosun Life was suspended due to Gapul Development’s bankruptcy and thus Gapul Development was at fault merely attacks factual findings that are within the exclusive province of the trier of fact, and therefore cannot constitute a proper ground of appeal. In addition, the court below cannot be deemed to have violated the rules of logic and experience or to have found facts beyond the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence. Accordingly, the ground of appeal cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. The judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2013DA96868]": "The Court examines ex officio.\\n\\n1. Whether a joinder takes the form of optional joinder or preliminary joinder shall be determined on the basis of the nature of the joined claims, not the intent of the parties, and the scope of review in the appellate instance shall likewise be determined on the basis of such nature of the joined claims. Therefore, even where, with respect to two claims that are substantially in a relationship of optional joinder, a party has ranked them as primary and preliminary claims, and the first instance court has rendered a judgment dismissing the primary claim and granting only the preliminary claim, and only the Defendant has filed an appeal, the appellate court must take both claims as the subject of adjudication and determine them.\\n\\n2. a. According to the reasons for the judgment of the court below and the record, the Plaintiff’s claim in this case is basically a claim against the Defendant for payment of KRW 100 million and damages for delay thereon, namely: ① the Plaintiff, as the cause of action for this claim, alleged a loan against the Defendant and sought payment thereof, but during the course of the first instance proceedings changed this into the primary claim (hereinafter referred to as “the primary claim in this case”) and, in the alternative, added a claim for damages based on tort (fraud) (hereinafter referred to as “the preliminary claim in this case”); ② the first instance court, while dismissing the primary claim in this case, granted the preliminary claim in this case, and only the Defendant appealed therefrom; ③ the court below, after premising that, since only the Defendant appealed, the subject of adjudication is limited to the preliminary claim in this case, accepted the Defendant’s appeal on the ground that the Defendant’s tort was not established, and dismissed even the preliminary claim in this case; ④ meanwhile, it can be understood that the loan claim, which is the primary claim in this case, means that “the Plaintiff lent KRW 100 million to the Defendant,” and that the damages claim, which is the preliminary claim in this case, means that “the Plaintiff was deceived by the Defendant and paid KRW 100 million.”\\n\\n   b. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the factual relations as shown in the record, notwithstanding their names, the primary claim in this case and the preliminary claim in this case are in substance in a relationship of optional joinder. Therefore, the court below should not have taken only the preliminary claim in this case, which the Defendant made the subject of its appeal, as the subject of adjudication, but should have taken both claims as the subject of adjudication and determined them; nevertheless, by, as set forth above, taking only the preliminary claim in this case as the subject of adjudication and dismissing the claim, the court below misapprehended the legal principles concerning the subject of adjudication in the appellate instance and failed to conduct a full examination.\\n\\n3. Therefore, without the need to proceed to the determination of the grounds for appeal, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for a new trial and determination, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices, as set forth in the order."}

{"[98DA22253]": "1. On Ground of Appeal No. 1\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below found that Non-party 1 forged the relevant documents and thereby cancelled the registration of establishment of the mortgage over the forest land at issue, which had been made in the joint names of the Plaintiffs and Non-party Park Bong-nam, three persons in total; therefore, as of the time of such cancellation, Defendant Ko Seon-o, who was the owner of the forest land at issue, had the duty to perform the procedure for restoration registration with respect to the entirety of the registration of establishment of the mortgage over the forest land at issue or the 2/3 share in the Plaintiffs’ names, and that Defendant School Juridical Person Yongmun Academy, which acquired the forest land at issue thereafter, had the duty to make a manifestation of assent. As to the Plaintiffs’ assertion, the court below found that Defendant Ko Seon-o purchased the forest land at issue, owned by Non-party Lee Seong-jae, around 1990, paid part of the purchase price, and, while the balance remained unpaid, resold it without registration on or about April 12, 1991, to Non-party 1 and Park Bong-nam; that around that time Non-party 1 also resold a part of the forest land at issue without registration to the Plaintiffs; that Park Bong-nam requested Defendant Ko Seon-o to establish even a mortgage in the names of Park Bong-nam and the Plaintiffs in order to secure performance of the sale and purchase agreement; that Defendant Ko Seon-o received from Non-party Kim Sun, who was Lee Seong-jae’s spouse and agent, a blank power of attorney in Lee Seong-jae’s name, a mortgage contract, and a certificate of seal impression necessary for the registration of establishment of the mortgage, and handed them to Park Bong-nam; and that Park Bong-nam, with the mortgagee designated as the Plaintiffs and Park Bong-nam and the debtor designated as Lee Seong-jae, effected the registration of establishment of the mortgage over the forest land at issue. The court below further found that at that time, without knowing at all that Defendant Ko Seon-o had already resold the forest land at issue without registration to Non-party 1 and Park Bong-nam, and that Non-party 1 had also resold a part thereof again without registration to the Plaintiffs, Kim Sun, merely in accordance with Defendant Ko Seon-o’s request, who had paid a substantial part of the purchase price of the forest land at issue, delivered to him the documents necessary for the establishment of the mortgage, such as a mortgage contract and a power of attorney bearing only Lee Seong-jae’s seal and with the remaining portions left blank, in order to secure performance of the duty to register transfer of ownership to him; and that, however, when Defendant Ko Seon-o did not establish the mortgage in his own name but handed over all the relevant documents to Park Bong-nam, Park Bong-nam completed the blank portions of the mortgage contract and power of attorney, etc., designating the Plaintiffs and Park Bong-nam as the creditors and Lee Seong-jae as the debtor, and used them to complete the registration of establishment of the mortgage over the forest land at issue. The court below then held that, since there had been no agreement or assent whatsoever among Lee Seong-jae, the Plaintiffs, and Park Bong-nam regarding the establishment of the mortgage, it could not be said that the mortgage over the forest land at issue validly came into existence from the time of its establishment; and that, moreover, insofar as it was found that the Plaintiffs and Park Bong-nam had undergone no verification procedure as to whether Lee Seong-jae intended to bear, vis-à-vis the Plaintiffs and Park Bong-nam, who were not even the other contracting party, the burden of the existence of the mortgage over the forest land at issue and the liabilities arising therefrom, it could not be recognized as an apparent agency exceeding authority under Civil Act Article 126. Accordingly, the court below rejected the Plaintiffs’ claim based on this point, on the ground that even though the registration of establishment of the mortgage over the forest land at issue had been cancelled by the criminal act of Non-party 1, the Plaintiffs’ claim premised on the validity of the mortgage over the forest land at issue was without merit.\\n\\nUpon examination in light of the record, the above factual findings and determination of the court below are acceptable, and there is no illegality such as a factual misapprehension due to violation of the rules of evidence, incomplete examination, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning the probative force of dispositive documents or apparent agency under Civil Act Article 126, as alleged in the ground of appeal.\\n\\nThe arguments in the ground of appeal on this point are all without merit.\\n\\n2. On Ground of Appeal No. 2\\n\\nAccording to the record, it is clear that at the tenth hearing date of the first instance, counsel for the Plaintiffs stated the application dated April 3, 1997, for amendment of the prayer and cause of action, which included the purport that the Plaintiffs would additionally seek, against Defendant School Juridical Person Yongmun Academy, performance of the procedure for cancellation registration of the registration of transfer of ownership in Defendant Ko Seon-o’s name concerning the forest land at issue, by subrogating, in sequence, Defendant Ko Seon-o and Non-party 1. Accordingly, the ground of appeal that the Plaintiffs had never sought such a claim for performance of the cancellation registration procedure cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. On Ground of Appeal No. 3\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below found that when Non-party 1, together with Park Bong-nam, purchased the forest land at issue from Defendant Ko Seon-o, or when he sold the forest land at issue to the Plaintiffs, the real estate speculation had already been uncovered and he was either under investigative scrutiny by the prosecution and tax authorities or even subject to collection for nonpayment of capital gains tax; that the purpose of purchasing the forest land at issue was to obtain profit from resale; and that, at the time of purchase, he excluded himself from the purchaser’s name and concluded the contract only under Park Bong-nam’s name, while, at the time of sale, he did not indicate the seller’s name as himself, Non-party 1, but indicated it as Ko Seon-o against Non-party 1, and thus ultimately had the transfer registration of ownership completed directly from Defendant Ko Seon-o in the Plaintiffs’ names or in the Plaintiffs’ names through Park Bong-nam, thereby having no intention whatsoever to obtain permission for land transaction in his own name and have the transfer registration of ownership completed. The court below also found that when the Plaintiffs purchased a part of the forest land at issue from Non-party 1, the purpose of purchase was to spend their later years after returning from employment while residing in Seoul, and that, knowing that they could not obtain permission for land transaction, they concluded the instant sale and purchase agreement with the intention of obtaining permission for land transaction by receiving permission to install a wild-bird breeding facility on the forest land at issue, installing a pheasant breeding facility, and changing the land category to miscellaneous land. The court below then held that the sale and purchase agreement concerning the forest land at issue between the Plaintiffs and Non-party 1 was, from the outset, a contract excluding or evading permission for land transaction, and therefore was definitively void; accordingly, premising on the Plaintiffs having a claim for transfer registration of ownership concerning the forest land at issue against Non-party 1, it held that the Plaintiffs’ action seeking, against Defendant Ko Seon-o, performance of the procedure for application for permission for land transaction by subrogating Non-party 1 was unlawful.\\n\\nUpon examination in light of the record, the above determination of the court below is acceptable, and there is no illegality of misapprehension of the legal principles concerning permission for land transaction as alleged in the ground of appeal.\\n\\nThe ground of appeal on this point is likewise without merit.\\n\\n4. On Ground of Appeal No. 4\\n\\na. According to the record, as claims against Defendant Ko Seon-o, the Plaintiffs sought: (1) as principal claims, ① the performance of the restoration registration procedure on the ground that the registration of establishment of the mortgage over the forest land at issue had been unlawfully cancelled, and ② subrogating Non-party 1, performance of the procedure for application for permission for land transaction concerning the sale and purchase agreement dated April 12, 1991, with Non-party 1, as to the Plaintiffs’ purchased portion of the forest land at issue; and (2) in the alternative, ① compensation for damages arising from the tort of participation in double sale, ② return of unjust enrichment arising from the cancellation of the mortgage, and ③ return of the purchase price arising from impossibility of performance, etc. of the sale and purchase agreement. The first instance court upheld, among the principal claims, the claim for restoration registration of the registration of establishment of the mortgage only as to 2/3 of the Plaintiffs’ share, and dismissed all of the remaining claims, the claim for application for permission for land transaction, and the alternative claims. In response, Defendant Ko Seon-o appealed as to the portion lost by him and sought dismissal of that portion of the claims, and the Plaintiffs appealed as to the portion lost by them and again sought the above principal claims. The court below dismissed the claim for restoration registration of the registration of establishment of the mortgage among the Plaintiffs’ above principal claims and dismissed as inadmissible the action for the claim for application for permission for land transaction; however, even with respect to the above alternative claims, it stated that, although the first instance court had dismissed them, the Plaintiffs had not appealed therefrom, and therefore it would not separately examine them, and thus made no determination whatsoever.\\n\\nb. However, a subsidiary joinder of claims refers to a joinder form in which, among several joined claims, adjudication is sought, with the granting of a principal claim (the first claim) as a condition subsequent for the granting of an alternative claim (the second claim), in preparation for the event that the principal claim is not granted. In such a case of subsidiary joinder, adjudication must be made in the order designated by the plaintiff; when rejecting the principal claim, the court must adjudicate the alternative claim, but when granting the principal claim, there is no need to adjudicate the next-ranked alternative claim. Accordingly, a judgment granting the principal claim is a judgment on the whole, and if the defendant appeals against such a judgment, the next-ranked alternative claim that was not adjudicated in the first instance is also transferred to the appellate instance in its entirety, and if the appellate court rejects the principal claim that had been granted in the first instance, it must adjudicate the next-ranked alternative claim.\\n\\nIn such a case of subsidiary joinder, because the several claims are inseparably combined in one litigation procedure, a partial judgment such as granting only the alternative claim without first determining the principal claim, or rejecting only the principal claim without adjudicating the alternative claim, is contrary to the nature of subsidiary joinder and is not legally permissible. Nevertheless, if a judgment is rendered rejecting the principal claim while failing to adjudicate the alternative claim, then when an appeal is filed against that judgment, the omitted portion of the alternative claim is also transferred to the appellate instance, and that portion cannot be regarded as still pending before the court below on the ground that it constitutes an omission from adjudication. In contrast, if the court below rejected the principal claim but omitted to adjudicate the alternative claim, then the omitted portion of the alternative claim remains pending in the court below; accordingly, the Supreme Court precedents holding that an appeal on this point is unlawful because there is no subject matter thereof are hereby changed (Supreme Court Decision 80DA1881, 80DA1882 rendered April 14, 1981; Supreme Court Decision 88DAKA10647 rendered September 26, 1989; Supreme Court Decision 92DA18283 rendered October 13, 1992; Supreme Court Decision 99DA50422 rendered January 21, 2000, etc.).\\n\\nc. Here, although the Plaintiffs do not clearly state their intention regarding whether the instant alternative claim is an alternative claim to the entirety of the principal claims or only to a part of them, if the Plaintiffs had prevailed in the first instance with respect to part of the principal claims in this case, then at least the alternative claim portion related to the victorious portion could not, absent special circumstances, become the subject of adjudication by the first instance court; and even if the first instance court made a determination on a claim that could not become the subject of adjudication in this manner, such determination would have no effect (see Supreme Court Decisions 94DA29065 rendered January 24, 1995; 94DA62017 rendered July 25, 1995, etc.). Therefore, it cannot be said that the instant alternative claim is incapable of becoming the subject of adjudication by the court below merely because the Plaintiffs did not appeal the alternative claim dismissed in the first instance.\\n\\nThe principal claims in this case consist of a claim for restoration registration of the unlawfully cancelled registration of establishment of the mortgage and a claim for application for permission for land transaction pursuant to the sale and purchase agreement. In light of the relationship between these claims, if the first instance court had partially granted the claim for restoration registration of the registration of establishment of the mortgage among the principal claims in this case, then at least the related alternative claim should be regarded as not having become the subject of adjudication by the first instance court (the first instance court dismissed the claim for application for permission for land transaction among the principal claims in this case, and also adjudicated and dismissed the instant alternative claims; thus, the alternative claim dismissed in the first instance appears to concern the claim for application for permission for land transaction among the principal claims in this case). Accordingly, in the event that Defendant Ko Seon-o appealed against the portion of the claim for restoration registration of the registration of establishment of the mortgage, which is one of the principal claims in this case, that the Plaintiffs had partially won, and the court below, in consequence, were to reverse the first instance judgment on this portion and dismiss the Plaintiffs’ principal claim corresponding to the reversed portion, it would then have to further treat as the subject of adjudication the alternative claim related thereto and adjudicate it.\\n\\nd. Nevertheless, the court below, without clearly elucidating the relationship among the respective claims in this case by exercising its power to clarify, made no determination whatsoever regarding the alternative claim, relying solely on the reasons stated in its judgment. Thus, the judgment of the court below contains illegality that affected the judgment by violating the duty to clarify or by misapprehending the legal principles concerning subsidiary joinder of claims. The ground of appeal pointing this out is meritorious.\\n\\n5. Therefore, the portion of the judgment of the court below concerning the alternative claim against Defendant Ko Seon-o is reversed, and this part of the case is remanded to the court below; the remainder of the appeal by the Plaintiffs against Defendant Ko Seon-o and the appeal against Defendant School Juridical Person Yongmun Academy are all dismissed; and the costs of appeal between the Plaintiffs and Defendant School Juridical Person Yongmun Academy shall be borne by the Plaintiffs. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices."}

question: A filed a lawsuit against B seeking return of KRW 100 million in lease deposit upon termination of the lease, and B argued in the first-instance pleadings that he would set off against A a rent claim of KRW 10 million as the claim used for setoff. Which of the following explanations is incorrect? (Each statement is independent, and where there is a dispute, case law shall apply)
A: B's set-off, by using a rent claim that had already become time-barred during the continuance of the lease as the claim used for setoff after the termination of the lease, cannot be recognized unless there are special circumstances; however, overdue rent can be deducted from the lease deposit.
B: B's set-off defense gives rise to the substantive-law effect of setoff only when the court makes a substantive determination on setoff, including the existence of the passive claim.
C: B may withdraw the set-off defense in the first instance of the above lawsuit without the opposing party's consent.
D: It is procedurally improper for B, during the pendency of the above lawsuit, to file a separate action against A seeking payment of the above KRW 10 million rent.
E: If, during the continuance of the lease, B had already set off the overdue rent claim against the lease deposit return claim within the extent of equal amounts, and if B alleges and proves that fact in the above lawsuit, the effect of that setoff may be recognized.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2002DA52657]": "The Defendant’s appeal is dismissed. The Plaintiff’s incidental appeal is dismissed. The costs of the appeal shall be borne by the Defendant, and the costs of the incidental appeal shall be borne by the Plaintiff, respectively."}

{"[2011DA23323]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. On Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe absolute ground for appeal prescribed in Article 424(1)6 of the Civil Procedure Act, namely “where the judgment does not state the reasons,” refers to a case where the judgment states no reasons at all, omits part of the reasons, or where any part of the reasons is unclear, so that it is not clear how the court recognized the facts and interpreted and applied the law to reach the operative part of the judgment. Therefore, insofar as the judgment clearly indicates the process by which it reached the operative part, it cannot be said that there is an error of failing to state reasons for the judgment merely because it did not determine the parties’ arguments, and determinations concerning the parties’ assertions or defenses need not necessarily be made expressly, but may also be made by implicit or indirect means (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DA62597 rendered on May 26, 2006).\\n\\nThe lower court, by citing the first-instance judgment, held that, for the reasons stated in that judgment, the KRW 38.5 million paid by the Defendant to the Plaintiff was reasonably viewed as having been paid as a commission for separate sales activities in which the Plaintiff arranged and made efforts to enable the resumption of the Defendant’s delivery of soil improvement materials to Dongui Comprehensive Landscaping Co., Ltd. after such delivery was suspended, and further held that there was no evidence to recognize that it had been paid as an advance payment of commission in relation to deliveries to Incheon Metropolitan City Hall. In the portion of the judgment containing such holding, the court’s rejection of the Defendant’s argument that the said money had been paid as an advance payment of future commission to be paid in connection with the deliveries to the said company is included. It cannot be said that the lower court judgment erred by omitting a determination.\\n\\nFurthermore, in light of the evidence lawfully admitted by the lower court, the lower court’s above determination is reasonable and can be accepted, and there is no illegality, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, in that the court failed to conduct the necessary examination and thereby affected the outcome of the judgment.\\n\\n2. On Ground 2 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe lower court, by citing the first-instance judgment, rejected the Defendant’s set-off defense, namely, the argument that the Plaintiff forged the Defendant’s seal, sent official letters in the Defendant’s name to the Defendant’s business partners, and provisionally attached the claims the Defendant had against its business partners so as to prevent the Defendant from conducting business, and that, in addition, the Plaintiff committed tortious acts such as threatening the Defendant by stating that the Plaintiff would notify the Defendant’s business partners of the Defendant’s breach of contract with the Plaintiff, and therefore the Plaintiff set off, by way of claims for damages arising therefrom, the claim for which it sought satisfaction through this action, on the ground that no claim for damages as alleged in the argument was established.\\n\\nHowever, it is difficult to accept such determination of the lower court.\\n\\nA set-off defense as a litigation defense is a kind of preliminary defense made on the premise that the existence of the passive claim is established, and it may be withdrawn without the consent of the other party; in such case, the court may not adjudicate on it under the principle of party disposition. According to the record, at the first hearing date of the lower court, it can be seen that the Defendant’s litigation representative stated that the above set-off defense, as submitted in the first instance, was being withdrawn (see p. 485 of the record). Therefore, the above determination of the lower court adjudicated matters not asserted by the parties, and thus it should be deemed illegal in violation of the principle of party disposition and affecting the judgment (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 62DA760 rendered on February 14, 1963). The purport of the appeal pointing out this issue is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the lower court judgment shall be reversed and the case remanded to the lower court for a new trial and determination, and the judgment is rendered as ordered, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2013DA95964]": "The grounds of appeal shall be determined, and the statements in a supplemental brief submitted after the deadline for filing the statement of grounds of appeal shall be considered only to the extent that they supplement it.\\n\\n1. As to the First Ground of Appeal\\n\\nA. As to the argument concerning loans, management expenses, and deductions for non-management expenditures\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, based on the evidence it admitted, found the following facts: the Defendant lent to the Plaintiff a total of 37,698,000 won [= 17,498,000 won + 19,200,000 won + 1,000,000 won] on August 14, 2008, in the amount of 17,498,000 won, on August 26, 2008, in the amount of 19,200,000 won, and on October 1, 2008, in the amount of 1,000,000 won; and the Defendant disbursed, on behalf of the Plaintiff, a total of 40,010,829 won [= 3,514,600 won (July National Pension Insurance premium) + 1,540,000 won (August disbursed elevator maintenance expense) + 3,605,000 won (August National Pension Insurance premium) + 1,540,000 won (September disbursed elevator maintenance expense) + 10,476,500 won (excess remittance amount for Unit 508) + 780,000 won (refund of construction deposit for Unit B105) + 323,180 won (refund of double payment for Unit 902) + 300,000 won (refund of construction deposit) + 17,931,549 won (October labor cost)] as management expenses and non-management expenditures that the Plaintiff was to pay. The court then determined that the amounts withdrawn from the Plaintiff’s deposit accounts included amounts repaid in respect of the above loans, and that the money disbursed on behalf of the Plaintiff as management expenses and non-management expenditures was lawfully expended by the Defendant in the management of affairs and the like on behalf of the Plaintiff, and deducted the above respective amounts from the Defendant’s damages.\\n\\nIn light of the record, the above determination by the court below is proper, and there is no illegality such as, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating logic and rules of experience, or misconstruing the legal principles concerning loans, or failing to conduct sufficient deliberation.\\n\\nB. As to the argument concerning deduction of temporary advances\\n\\n1) According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, based on the evidence it admitted, recognized the circumstances as stated in its opinion, and then determined that the Defendant paid to the Plaintiff a total of 109,935,049 won as temporary advances [12,658,025 won as of December 31, 2007 + 15,552,979 won as of January 31, 2008 + 35,727,337 won as of February 28, 2008 + 1,972,067 won as of March 31, 2008 + 10,477,732 won as of April 30, 2008 + 13,546,909 won as of June 2, 2008 + 20,000,000 won as of July 31, 2008, hereinafter referred to as “the temporary advances in this case”], and that the amount corresponding to the above temporary advances among the amounts withdrawn from the Plaintiff’s deposits constituted repayment of the above temporary advances, and therefore should be deducted from the Defendant’s damages.\\n\\n2) However, such determination by the court below is difficult to accept as is for the following reasons.\\n\\nA) According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below and the evidence duly admitted and examined by the court below, the following facts or circumstances can be found.\\n\\n(1) The Defendant was appointed as the chairman of the Plaintiff around August 11, 2005. However, due to a dispute with Jeongdeok Enterprise, which had been entrusted with the management services for the officetel in this case, the Defendant was unable to receive the management fees, etc. held by Jeongdeok Enterprise, and because there were many delinquent management fee payments, the management expenses of the Plaintiff could not be fully covered by the management fees paid in, so the Defendant lent money to the Plaintiff in the name of temporary advances to cover the shortfall.\\n\\n(2) The temporary advances lent by the Defendant to the Plaintiff reached a total of 104,123,580 won around July 31, 2007, and the Plaintiff resolved on October 5, 2007 to repay the above temporary advances to the Defendant and, on the same day, remitted the above amount to the Defendant’s deposit account, thereby fully repaying the above temporary advances.\\n\\n(3) From August 1, 2007 to October 5, 2007, the Defendant again lent 61,216,694 won to the Plaintiff in the name of temporary advances, and the Plaintiff resolved on February 5, 2008 to repay the above temporary advances to the Defendant and, on the same day, remitted the above amount to the Defendant’s deposit account, thereby fully repaying those temporary advances as well.\\n\\n(4) Meanwhile, the Plaintiff spent between 50,000,000 won and 60,000,000 won each month as management expenses and the like, but as of the last day of each month from November 2007 to July 2008, the aggregate balance of the deposit accounts used by the Plaintiff ranged from slightly over 70,000,000 won to as much as slightly over 190,000,000 won, exceeding the management expenses to be disbursed in the following month. In addition, even after the Plaintiff paid to the Defendant 61,216,694 won in temporary advances from August 1, 2007 to October 5, 2007 on February 5, 2008, the deposit balance as of February 29, 2008 reached slightly over 110,000,000 won, and there is no circumstance showing that management expenses to be paid before December 31, 2007 were overdue and carried over.\\n\\n(5) In that most of the temporary advances in this case are recorded down to the unit of won, they appear to have been paid mainly by bank transfer rather than by cash transactions, but the Defendant has not been able to specify the transaction details in his deposit account records corresponding to the above temporary advances.\\n\\n(6) The substitute vouchers for the temporary advances in this case (Exhibits 6-1 through 7 for the Defendant) are documents attached to the minutes of the 62nd Management Body Representatives’ Meeting of the Plaintiff held on October 10, 2008, after an application was made for an injunction suspending the execution of duties against the Defendant because the issue of the Defendant’s status as representative had arisen. However, given that the signatures of the attending management body representatives are entered in the same order and in similar positions on each substitute voucher, they appear to have been prepared in a batch after the fact together with Exhibits 6-8 through 13 attached to the same minutes.\\n\\nB) In light of the above facts or circumstances, namely, that immediately after the Defendant took office as chairman of the Plaintiff, the Plaintiff’s management expenses were insufficient compared to the delinquent management fees, so there was a need for the Plaintiff to borrow temporary advances from the Defendant; however, all temporary advances up to October 5, 2007 had been repaid and there had been no instance of overdue management expenses that the Plaintiff was required to pay; and in light of the fact that from the end of November 2007 the balance in the Plaintiff’s deposit accounts exceeded the management expenses to be disbursed in the following month, it is difficult to see that there was a need for the Plaintiff to borrow new temporary advances from the Defendant. On the other hand, considering circumstances such as the fact that the Defendant, after asserting the temporary advances in this case, was unable to specifically explain why the temporary advances were necessary and by what method they were paid, it is also difficult to regard the evidence submitted by the Defendant regarding the temporary advances in this case as highly credible objective materials, and it is difficult to conclude solely from the circumstances found by the court below that the Defendant lent the temporary advances in this case to the Plaintiff.\\n\\nC) Nevertheless, the court below found, contrary to the foregoing, that the Defendant lent the temporary advances in this case to the Plaintiff and deducted them from the Defendant’s damages. The court below’s determination contains the illegality of failing to conduct the necessary deliberation as to whether the temporary advances in this case were necessary and the method of payment, and of finding facts in violation of logic and the rules of experience and beyond the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence. The portion of the Plaintiff’s grounds of appeal pointing out this issue is well-founded.\\n\\n2. As to the Second Ground of Appeal\\n\\nA. A setoff defense as a method of defense in litigation is ordinarily a type of preliminary defense raised on the premise that the existence of the counterclaim is established, and its effect does not arise definitively merely by a declaration of intent of setoff in litigation; rather, the effect of substantive-law setoff arises only when the court makes a substantive determination on setoff, including the existence of the counterclaim, in the relevant litigation (see Supreme Court Decision 2011DA3329 dated March 28, 2013).\\n\\nWhere, in response to such setoff defense raised by the Defendant in litigation, the Plaintiff again raises a counter-setoff defense in litigation to extinguish the Defendant’s active claim, if the court rejects the Defendant’s setoff defense in litigation on grounds unrelated to the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation, there is no need to rule on the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation. If the court determines that the Defendant’s setoff defense in litigation is well-founded, then the Plaintiff’s claim-based passive claim and the Defendant’s active claim will be deemed extinguished to the extent of equal amounts at the time when setoff becomes available, and therefore the Defendant’s active claim that is subject to setoff by the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation will not exist to that extent, so again there will be no need to rule on the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation. In addition, if the Plaintiff has another claim against the Defendant in addition to the claim that is the subject matter of the suit, the Plaintiff may assert that claim in the relevant litigation by amending the claim or may file a separate action. Accordingly, the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation generally lacks an interest warranting its allowance.\\n\\nTherefore, it is appropriate to view the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation against the Defendant’s setoff defense in litigation as not being allowable unless there are other special circumstances.\\n\\nB. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below and the record, in response to the Defendant’s setoff defense, the Plaintiff alleged that the Defendant, before July 31, 2008, arbitrarily took and used 534,505,058 won or 562,596,958 won by methods such as transfer from the Plaintiff’s deposit account to the Defendant’s deposit account, and that the Plaintiff thus has a claim for damages caused by tort against the Defendant in the amount of the above sum, and that if the Plaintiff’s above claim for damages against the Defendant and the Defendant’s claim for expenses of management of affairs and the like are set off against each other to the extent of equal amounts, the Defendant’s claim for expenses of management of affairs and the like would remain and therefore there would be no claim to be deducted from the Defendant’s damages. In response, the court below rejected the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation on the ground that the above claim for damages caused by tort alleged by the Plaintiff could not be recognized.\\n\\nAccording to the foregoing legal principles, the Plaintiff’s above counter-setoff defense in litigation is not acceptable as alleged, and although the court below erred in proceeding further to determine the existence or nonexistence of the claim alleged by the Plaintiff, its result in rejecting the Plaintiff’s counter-setoff defense in litigation is proper. Ultimately, the portion of the grounds of appeal on this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. Scope of Reversal\\n\\nThe court below, premising that the Defendant is obligated to pay the Plaintiff 45,167,830 won and delay damages thereon as damages for tort, determined, in response to the Defendant’s application seeking return of the provisionally paid amount paid by the Defendant to the Plaintiff pursuant to the prior appellate judgment with a declaration of provisional execution, that the Plaintiff is obligated to pay the Defendant 307,873,739 won and delay damages thereon.\\n\\nHowever, an application for restoration to the original state pursuant to Article 215(2) of the Civil Procedure Act is a type of action during litigation, and it is subject to the suspensive condition that the judgment on the merits is not altered. Since the appellate judgment on the merits is to be reversed for the above reason, the scope of the provisionally paid amount that the Plaintiff must return to the Defendant is bound to change as well. Therefore, not only the portion against the Plaintiff in the judgment of the court below, but also the portion against the Plaintiff in the judgment on the application for return of the provisionally paid amount, shall all be reversed.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the portions of the judgment of the court below against the Plaintiff and the portions of the judgment on the application for return of the provisionally paid amount against the Plaintiff shall each be reversed, and this case shall be remanded to the court below for further trial and determination of these portions, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2015DA252501]": "We decide the grounds of appeal (the statements in the supplemental brief on the grounds of appeal submitted after the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal shall be considered to the extent that they supplement the grounds of appeal).\\n\\n1. Article 131 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Debtor Rehabilitation Act”) provides that, with respect to rehabilitation claims, after the commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, no act that extinguishes such claims, including receipt of payment, may be performed except as otherwise provided, thereby restricting the individual exercise of rights by rehabilitation creditors (see Supreme Court Decision 2013DA69866 rendered on 2015. 7. 9.).\\n\\nBy contrast, Article 144(1) of the same Act provides: “Where, at the time of commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, a rehabilitation creditor or rehabilitation secured creditor is obliged to a debt to the debtor, if both the claim and the debt have become eligible for setoff before the expiration of the filing period, the rehabilitation creditor or rehabilitation secured creditor may set off only within that period without resorting to the rehabilitation proceedings. The same shall apply where the debt is a debt due at a fixed time.” Thus, even after the commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, setoff without resort to the rehabilitation proceedings is permitted within a certain scope. This is intended to protect the parties’ expectation that, where a rehabilitation creditor and a rehabilitation debtor mutually hold claims and debts against each other, they may offset them by setoff. In addition, the reason setoff is permitted even where the debt is a debt due at a fixed time is that, although the time of occurrence or performance of such a debt is contingent only upon a future event certain to occur or arrive, the obligation itself is already established, so the need to recognize setoff is no different from that in the case of ordinary claims. Furthermore, for setoff to be possible even after the commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, both the claim and the debt must have become eligible for setoff before the expiration of the filing period; accordingly, not only is it permitted where the fixed time of a debt due at a fixed time arrives before the expiration of the filing period, but it is also permitted for a rehabilitation creditor to waive the benefit of time and effect setoff.\\n\\nHowever, the main clause of Article 145(4) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act restricts a debtor of a rehabilitation debtor, whose rehabilitation proceedings have commenced, from setting off a rehabilitation claim as the claim to be used for setoff where that debtor acquired the rehabilitation claim while knowing of the existence of the rehabilitation debtor’s crisis condition, such as suspension of payments or a petition for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings. As an exception thereto, the proviso to subparagraph 4 of the same Article and item (b) of the proviso to subparagraph 2 allow setoff using the rehabilitation claim as the claim to be used for setoff where the debtor of the rehabilitation debtor acquired the rehabilitation claim by a cause arising before the debtor knew of the rehabilitation debtor’s suspension of payments, petition for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, and the like (hereinafter referred to as the “pre-existing cause”). The purpose of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act in restricting setoff by rehabilitation claims as above is that, if a debtor who was already obliged to the rehabilitation debtor could newly acquire a claim after the rehabilitation debtor entered a state of distress and then set it off, equality among rehabilitation creditors could be harmed and the rehabilitation of the rehabilitation debtor could also be impeded. On the other hand, where the rehabilitation claim was acquired after the rehabilitation debtor entered a state of distress, but the cause of the claim had already been formed before that time, there is a need to protect the rehabilitation creditor’s expectation of setoff; therefore, setoff is exceptionally permitted in such a case. In light of the purpose of these provisions, for a claim acquired after becoming aware of the existence of the crisis condition to be regarded as having arisen by a cause that existed beforehand, namely a “pre-existing cause,” the cause must not only be sufficiently direct to create in the creditor an expectation of setoff, but must also, taking all specific circumstances into account, be recognized as a legitimate one worth protecting the rehabilitation creditor’s reliance on the security function of setoff (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2013DA200513 rendered on 2014. 9. 24.).\\n\\n2. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the following facts may be known.\\n\\nA. From 1999. 8. 10. to 2003. 12. 1., the Plaintiff entered into membership agreements with the Defendant (hereinafter, the two golf courses collectively referred to as “the golf courses at issue,” and each membership agreement collectively referred to as “the membership agreements at issue”) concerning 32 membership units in ○○○○○ Country Club, a members-only golf course operated by the Defendant (total membership deposits: 13,080,000,000 won), and 9 membership units in △△△△ Country Club (total membership deposits: 700,000,000 won). The bylaws of the golf courses at issue provide that the membership deposits, which are security deposits for membership qualification, shall be held for a certain period of time (5 years after admission for ○○○○○ Country Club, and 2 years after admission for △△△△ Country Club) and thereafter returned when the member requests withdrawal from membership.\\n\\nB. As the owner of the land and buildings of the golf courses at issue, the Plaintiff leased to the Defendant: ① on 2004. 3. 5., the real property listed in Attached List 1 of the judgment of the court below, with a lease deposit of 9,300,000,000 won, monthly rent of 936,000,000 won, and lease term from 2004. 3. 5. to 2024. 3. 4.; and ② on 2005. 5. 30., the real property listed in Attached List 3 of the judgment of the court below, with a lease deposit of 1,000,000,000 won, monthly rent of 344,166,660 won, and lease term from 2005. 5. 30. to 2025. 5. 29. (hereinafter, each lease agreement referred to as “the lease agreements at issue”).\\n\\nC. On 2013. 10. 17., when the decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings was rendered with respect to the Defendant, the Plaintiff applied to the Defendant’s receiver for withdrawal from membership concerning the 41 membership units, and sent an official letter stating that the Plaintiff would set off 10,300,000,000 won of the Plaintiff’s claim for return of membership deposits (hereinafter referred to as “the claim for return of membership deposits at issue”) against the Defendant’s claim for return of lease deposit in the amount of 10,300,000,000 won arising under the lease agreements at issue, using the former as the claim to be set off. This official letter reached the Defendant’s receiver around 2013. 10. 22., before the expiration of the filing period for rehabilitation claims, etc.\\n\\n3. On the basis of the above facts, the court below determined that: ① since the Plaintiff, who was obliged to return the lease deposit to the Defendant, applied for withdrawal from membership on 2013. 10. 17. while knowing the fact that the Defendant had applied for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, and thereby acquired the claim for return of membership deposits at issue, the Plaintiff’s setoff using such claim as the claim to be set off conflicts with the main clause of Article 145(4) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act, which provides for grounds prohibiting setoff, and cannot be permitted; and ② since the claim for return of membership deposits at issue does not arise from the conclusion of the membership agreements at issue, but arises only when the Plaintiff manifests an intention to withdraw from membership, the membership agreements at issue cannot be deemed to constitute a direct causal act that would create in the Plaintiff an expectation of setoff based on the claim for return of membership deposits at issue, and because the claim for return of membership deposits at issue arising from the Plaintiff’s withdrawal from membership and the claim for return of the lease deposit under the lease agreements at issue cannot be said to be linked in a security sense, it is also difficult to view that a legitimate reliance worth protecting as to the security function of setoff had been formed in the Plaintiff; accordingly, it held that the case does not fall within the exception to the prohibition of setoff provided in the proviso to Article 145(4) and the proviso to Article 2(b) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act.\\n\\n4. However, the above determination by the court below is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nA. A lease deposit received in a real estate lease secures all of the lessee’s obligations arising from the lease, including obligations to pay rent and obligations to pay damages for loss or damage to the subject matter (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2015DA230020 rendered on 2016. 7. 27.), and, absent special circumstances, the lessor’s obligation to return the lease deposit comes due at the time of termination of the lease agreement, which is certain to occur in the future (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DA52657 rendered on 2002. 12. 10.). Moreover, since the lessor may maintain the real estate lease agreement even without a lease deposit, the lessor may, even while the lease agreement remains in force, waive the benefit of time with respect to the obligation to return the lease deposit and set off the lessee’s claim for return of the lease deposit as the passive claim (see Supreme Court Decision 2016DA211309 rendered on 2016. 11. 25.), and where the intention to set off is manifested during the continuance of the lease, such manifestation may be deemed a waiver of the benefit of time with respect to the obligation to return the lease deposit.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles concerning setoff of debts due at a fixed time, as noted above, together with the facts found by the court below, the Plaintiff’s manifestation of intention to set off included a waiver of the benefit of time with respect to the obligation to return the lease deposit owed to the Defendant; accordingly, the Plaintiff’s setoff may be deemed to have, at least prima facie, satisfied the requirements for exercise of a rehabilitation creditor’s right of setoff under Article 144(1) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act.\\n\\nB. Meanwhile, where the bylaws of a so-called deposit-based golf course provide that, for a member to receive a refund of the membership deposit, the member must first allow the prescribed holding period necessary for voluntary withdrawal to elapse and then manifest an intention to withdraw from membership, the claim for refund of the membership deposit arises in fact only upon manifestation of the intention to withdraw from membership (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2013DA100750 rendered on 2015. 1. 29.). Therefore, according to the facts found by the court below, the claim for return of membership deposits at issue arose on 2013. 10. 22., when the Plaintiff’s manifestation of intention to withdraw from membership reached the Defendant’s receiver. Accordingly, since the Plaintiff acquired the claim for return of membership deposits at issue while knowing of the fact that the Defendant had applied for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, the Plaintiff’s setoff using such claim as the claim to be set off cannot be permitted as it falls within the ground for prohibition of setoff provided in the main clause of Article 145(4) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act, namely, “where a debtor of a rehabilitation debtor, whose rehabilitation proceedings have commenced, acquires a rehabilitation claim while knowing that there has been an application for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings,” unless it falls within an exception to the prohibition of setoff.\\n\\nHowever, a so-called deposit-based golf membership right refers comprehensively to the member’s contractual status under the membership agreement with the golf course operator and the claim-based legal relationship arising from that membership agreement, and the holder of such a deposit-based golf membership right has individual rights such as the facility-use right, which is the right to preferentially use the golf course facilities as prescribed by the bylaws, and the claim for refund of the membership deposit, which is the right to receive, upon withdrawal from membership, a refund of the membership deposit entrusted to secure membership qualification (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2013DA100750 rendered on 2015. 1. 29.). Thus, the membership agreements at issue may be said to be the direct cause by which the Plaintiff acquired the claim for return of membership deposits at issue. In addition, as all of the holding periods for the membership deposits prescribed by the bylaws had already elapsed before the Defendant applied for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, the Plaintiff was already in a position where it could apply for withdrawal from membership and receive a refund of the membership deposits at any time, and because the lease agreements at issue concern precisely the land and buildings of the golf courses at issue as the objects of lease, it is sufficiently reasonable to expect that, upon the occurrence of a situation terminating the membership agreements at issue, the Plaintiff’s claim for return of membership deposits against the Defendant and the Defendant’s claim for return of lease deposits against the Plaintiff could be adjusted through setoff or other means by linking them to each other. Therefore, the Plaintiff’s reliance corresponding to such expectation should be regarded as having a legitimate basis worthy of protection.\\n\\nAccordingly, it is appropriate to view the claim for return of membership deposits at issue as a rehabilitation claim acquired by a cause arising before the debtor knew of the application for commencement of rehabilitation proceedings, which constitutes an exception to the prohibition of setoff under the proviso to Article 145(4) and the proviso to Article 2(b) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act.\\n\\nC. Nevertheless, the court below determined, for the reasons noted above, that the membership agreements at issue do not fall within the exception to the prohibition of setoff; in so doing, it erred by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the interpretation, etc. of the proviso to Article 145(4) and the proviso to Article 2(b) of the Debtor Rehabilitation Act.\\n\\n5. Therefore, we reverse the judgment of the court below without examining the remaining grounds of appeal and remand the case to the court below for further trial and determination. This decision was rendered with the unanimous agreement of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2016DA211309]": "We determine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Even if the lease deposit has been delivered to the lessor, the lessor may freely choose whether to apply the lease deposit to overdue rent while the lease relationship continues (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DA459, 466, rendered May 12, 2005). Accordingly, before the termination of the lease agreement, overdue rent is not automatically deducted from the lease deposit without a separate manifestation of intent, such as setoff, etc. (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2011DA49608, 49615, rendered February 28, 2013), and the lessee also may not refuse payment of rent on the ground that the lease deposit exists.\\n\\nMeanwhile, extinctive prescription cannot be excluded, extended, or aggravated by juristic acts (Civil Act Article 184(2)). Therefore, even if rent is in arrears during the continuance of the lease, unless there are special circumstances, such as an agreement that settlement will be made by a lump-sum deduction from the lease deposit at the time of delivery of the subject property after termination of the lease, the extinctive prescription of the rent claim must be deemed to run from the payment date stipulated in the lease agreement.\\n\\n2. Because the lease deposit is intended to secure all obligations of the lessee that may arise in the lease relationship, such as nonpayment of rent or loss or damage to the subject property, it may be said that the general intention of the parties is to expect that, if rent payment is overdue, it will in the future be applied to the lease deposit when the lease relationship terminates. The same shall apply even where the payment date of the rent claim was separately fixed and the extinctive prescription was running during the continuance of the lease, but the lessor had not manifested any intent to apply and deduct the overdue rent from the lease deposit. Moreover, in light of the realities of our society, where the amount of the lease deposit is often substantially larger than the rent, even if the obligation to pay rent has been overdue for a considerable period, if the lessor does not terminate the lease agreement and the lessee also continues the lease relationship relying on the fact that security for the overdue rent is sufficient, it may generally be said that both the lessor and the lessee trust that the rent claim is secured by the lease deposit irrespective of the statute of limitations, and furthermore, that they have an implied intent to allow future application and deduction from the lease deposit.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Civil Act Article 495 provides: “If a claim for which extinctive prescription has been completed could have been offset before such completion, the obligee may set it off.” This is intended to protect the trust of the parties by taking into account that, where the claims of both parties were in a position to be set off, the parties generally consider that the claim-debt relationship has already been settled and extinguished. However, this requires that “both claims had reached the stage where setoff was possible before the completion of the extinctive prescription of the active claim,” and since the lessor’s obligation to return the lease deposit only becomes due upon termination of the lease agreement (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DA52657, rendered December 10, 2002), if the extinctive prescription of the rent claim is completed during the continuance of the lease, then, unless there are special circumstances such as the lessor having actually waived the benefit of time regarding the obligation to return the lease deposit before such completion, it cannot be said that both claims were in a state capable of setoff. Therefore, although after that time, the lessor’s setoff of the already time-barred rent claim as the active claim against the obligation to return the lease deposit cannot be recognized even under Civil Act Article 495, in light of the lessor’s trust in not applying overdue rent from the lease deposit while the lease continued despite the rent being in arrears, and the lessee’s implied intent to continue the lease relationship in a state of rent arrears, it is reasonable to view that such overdue rent may be deducted from the lease deposit by analogical application of Civil Act Article 495.\\n\\n3. The lower court, by partially adopting the reasoning of the first-instance judgment, recognized the facts as stated in that decision and then held that the lease agreement between the Plaintiff and the Defendant was lawfully terminated by the Plaintiff’s content-certified mail dated March 27, 2014, which reached the Defendant around that time; that because the rent claims whose due date preceded March 27, 2011 had already become time-barred before the termination of the lease agreement, the amount corresponding to such rent claims could not be deducted from the lease deposit; and that, further, the Plaintiff could not thereafter, under Civil Act Article 495, set off against the obligation to return the lease deposit by treating as the active claim the rent claims whose extinctive prescription had already been completed before the termination of the lease agreement as described above.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, the lower court’s determination contains an error of misapprehending the legal nature of the lease deposit and the legal principles concerning the scope of its security, and the allegation of appeal to the same effect has merit.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the lower court judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination; it is so adjudged, by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices of the Supreme Court, as ordered."}

{"[2016DA211309]": "We adjudicate the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Even if a lease deposit has been delivered to the lessor, the lessor may freely choose whether to appropriate it toward rent in arrears while the lease relationship continues (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DA459, 466, decided May 12, 2005). Therefore, before termination of the lease agreement, rent in arrears is not automatically deducted from the lease deposit without a separate manifestation of intent such as set-off (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2011DA49608, 49615, decided February 28, 2013), and the lessee also may not refuse payment of rent on the ground that a lease deposit exists.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the Statute of Limitations cannot be excluded, extended, or aggravated by a juristic act (Civil Act Article 184(2)). Therefore, even if rent is in arrears during the continuation of the lease, unless there are special circumstances such as an agreement that settlement shall be made by the method of deducting the rent in arrears in a lump sum from the lease deposit upon delivery of the object after termination of the lease, the Statute of Limitations for the rent claim should be deemed to run from the payment date stipulated in the lease agreement.\\n\\n2. Since a lease deposit is intended to secure all obligations of the lessee that may arise in the lease relationship, such as nonpayment of rent and loss of or damage to the object, it may be said that, if payment of rent is in arrears, the parties generally intend that it will be appropriated by the lease deposit when the lease relationship is terminated in the future. The same shall apply even where the due date for the rent claim is separately fixed, the Statute of Limitations is running during the continuation of the lease, and yet the lessor has not made any manifestation of intent to appropriate and deduct the rent in arrears from the lease deposit. Moreover, in light of the actual conditions of our society, where the amount of the lease deposit is often considerably large compared to the rent, even if the obligation to pay rent is in substantial arrears, if the lessor does not terminate the lease agreement and the lessee also continues the lease relationship relying on the fact that sufficient security exists for the rent in arrears, it is generally reasonable to view both the lessor and the lessee as trusting that the rent claim is secured by the lease deposit irrespective of the Statute of Limitations, and further as having an implied intent to permit future appropriation and deduction from the lease deposit.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Civil Act Article 495 provides, “If a claim for which the Statute of Limitations has become complete was one that could have been set off before such completion, the creditor may set it off.” This is intended to protect the trust of the parties by taking into account that, where the claims of both parties were in a state fit for set-off, the parties generally consider that the claim-debt relationship has already been settled and extinguished. However, this requires that “both claims must have reached a state fit for set-off before the Statute of Limitations on the active claim became complete,” and since the lessor’s obligation to return the lease deposit reaches its due time only when the lease agreement is terminated (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DA52657, decided December 10, 2002), if the Statute of Limitations on the rent claim becomes complete during the continuation of the lease, then, unless there are special circumstances such as the lessor’s actual waiver of the benefit of time regarding the obligation to return the lease deposit before the completion of the Statute of Limitations, it cannot be said that both claims were in a state in which set-off was possible. Therefore, thereafter, even under Civil Act Article 495, it must be considered that the lessor cannot be recognized as seting off the already time-barred rent claim as the active claim against the obligation to return the lease deposit. However, in light of the lessor’s trust in not having appropriated rent in arrears from the lease deposit while the lease continued, and the lessee’s implied intent to continue the lease relationship in a state of rent arrears, it is reasonable to view such rent in arrears as deductible from the lease deposit by analogous application of Civil Act Article 495.\\n\\n3. The court below, by partially citing the reasoning of the first instance judgment and recognizing the facts as stated in that judgment, held that the lease agreement between the Plaintiff and the Defendant was lawfully terminated by the Plaintiff’s content-certified mail dated March 27, 2014, upon its delivery to the Defendant around that time; however, the rent claim whose due date was before March 27, 2011 had already become time-barred before termination of the lease agreement, and therefore the amount corresponding to such rent claim could not be deducted from the lease deposit. The court below further held that thereafter, under Civil Act Article 495, the Plaintiff could not set off such rent claim, which had already become time-barred before termination of the lease agreement, as the active claim against the obligation to return the lease deposit.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles set forth above, the court below’s determination contains an error of misunderstanding the legal nature of the lease deposit and the legal principles concerning the scope of its security, and the ground of appeal to the same effect is well founded.\\n\\n4. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2021DA275741]": "The grounds of appeal are determined as follows.\\n\\n1. Whether this constitutes duplicate litigation or is contrary to the principle against refiling (Grounds for Appeal, Point 2)\\n\\na. In a case where, at the time the set-off defense was raised, an action based on the same claim as the active claim had already been separately filed and was pending, it is desirable for the panel in charge of the trial on the facts to prevent conflict with or contradiction of res judicata and, in addition, to promote procedural economy by attempting severance, transfer, or consolidation of the pleadings so as to hear and determine the former and the latter actions at the same opportunity; however, that does not mean that, absent special circumstances, a claim of set-off in litigation using a claim pending in a separate action as the active claim is impermissible (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2000DA4050, rendered April 27, 2001). Likewise, after raising a set-off defense in the action first filed, it is also possible, during the pendency of that action, to file separately, by an independent action or counterclaim, an action based on the same claim as the active claim.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 267(2) of the Civil Procedure Act provides, “A person who has withdrawn a lawsuit after a final judgment on the merits has been rendered may not file the same lawsuit again.” This is a provision with a punitive purport, enacted to prevent the unreasonable situation in which the court’s efforts expended on adjudication become useless due to the withdrawal of the suit and the litigation system is abused by again raising the same dispute (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2018DA259213, rendered May 7, 2021). However, unlike withdrawal of a lawsuit, which, after the opposing party has submitted a preparatory brief on the merits or made a statement or oral argument at a preparatory proceeding for pleadings, is effective only with the opposing party’s consent, a set-off defense as a litigation defense is a kind of preliminary defense raised on the premise that the existence of the passive claim is established, and it may be withdrawn without the opposing party’s consent; in such a case, under the principle of party disposition, the court may not adjudicate it (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2011DA23323, rendered July 14, 2011). Therefore, even if a set-off defense was raised in the court of first instance of the earlier action and a merits determination was rendered by the judgment of the court of first instance, and then the set-off defense was withdrawn in the appellate court, this is merely a withdrawal of a litigation defense, so the principle against refiling under Article 267(2) of the Civil Procedure Act does not apply, and an action based on the same claim as the active claim may be separately filed.\\n\\nb. According to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be known.\\n\\nThe Defendant filed against the Plaintiff an action for the claim for the construction price under the construction contract at issue (hereinafter referred to as the “earlier action”). In the court of first instance of the earlier action (Busan District Court 2017GASO505896), the Plaintiff raised a set-off defense using as the active claim a claim for damages in lieu of repair of defects; however, the court of first instance of the earlier action, on September 5, 2017, rejected the Plaintiff’s set-off defense on the ground that proof regarding the existence of defects and other matters was insufficient, and rendered a judgment fully in favor of the Defendant. On April 5, 2018, the Plaintiff separately filed the action at issue, seeking damages in lieu of repair of defects in the construction at issue against the Defendant, and thereafter withdrew the above set-off defense at the second pleading date in the appellate court of the earlier action (Busan District Court 2017NA56896).\\n\\nc. Examining these factual circumstances in light of the legal principles stated above, even though the Plaintiff had already raised a set-off defense in the earlier action using as the active claim a claim for damages in lieu of repair of defects, it is also permissible for the Plaintiff, during the pendency of the earlier action, to separately file the action at issue based on the same claim as that active claim. In addition, even if the Plaintiff withdrew the set-off defense in the appellate court after receiving a merits determination on the set-off defense in the court of first instance of the earlier action, this does not thereby render the claim for damages in lieu of repair of defects incapable of being pursued.\\n\\nAccordingly, the argument in this part of the grounds of appeal to the effect that the filing of the action at issue constitutes duplicate litigation prohibited by Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Act, or is contrary to the principle against refiling under Article 267(2) of the Civil Procedure Act, and that therefore the action at issue should have been dismissed, but the court below, by making a merits determination, overlooked the defect in the litigation requirement, which is subject to ex officio investigation, continued the trial, and rendered judgment, cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2.
