thereafter, on 1993.5.3., the acting representative director was changed to Nonparty 5, an attorney at law; and that, meanwhile, after Nonparties 1 and 6 obtained a judgment from Seoul Civil District Court on 1992.5.22. in Case No. 91GAHAP92470, an action seeking confirmation of share ownership filed by them against the Intervenor and others, confirming that the said Nonparties 1 and 6 were shareholders of the Defendant Company, they applied, in their capacity as shareholders, to the Seoul Civil District Court on 1992.8.25. for permission to convene an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for the removal of the Intervenor, who had been appointed as representative director at the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and board of directors held on 1991.5.6., and for the appointment of a successor director, and received an order granting permission to convene from the said court on 1992.11.12.; accordingly, they held an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and a board of directors of the Defendant Company on the same year 12.30., and again passed a resolution removing the Intervenor from the positions of representative director and director and appointing the said Nonparty 1 as representative director and director; that, despite the Intervenor and others having their performance of duties suspended by the said provisional disposition order, after they appeared as defendants in the action for confirmation of share ownership filed by the said Nonparty 1 and others and received a final judgment against them, the said Nonparty 1 and others, having obtained permission from the court to convene the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and the board of directors as stated above, prepared minutes as if they had resolved the removal of the Intervenor and others, and thereafter even completed the change registration accordingly; and based on this, the court below held that, although permission from the court had been obtained, the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and the board of directors held on 1992.12.30., convened not by a lawful acting officer, must be deemed nonexistent or void due to a formal defect; therefore, since the Intervenor remains registered as representative director and director, the Plaintiffs still have a legal interest in seeking confirmation of the invalidity of the said appointment resolution, and accordingly rejected the Defendant’s preliminary objection.\\n\\n   b. However, first, according to the records and the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, it can be ascertained that at the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and board of directors of the Defendant Company held on 1991.5.6., the Intervenor was again appointed as representative director and director of the Defendant Company, and the registration thereof was completed on 1991.5.10.; in the remand judgment, this Court held that, even if a director is removed from office before the expiration of his term by a resolution of the general meeting of shareholders for replacement of officers and a successor director is appointed, if the successor director is later appointed through lawful procedures, then even if the original resolution replacing the director is void, seeking confirmation of its invalidity would amount to seeking confirmation of a past legal relationship or rights relationship and would thus lack the requirements for protection of rights as an action for confirmation; however, if the resolution of the general meeting of shareholders appointing a successor director is found to be nonexistent due to procedural or substantive defects other than the defect that the meeting was convened by a person without the right to do so, then the issue of whether the original resolution appointing the officer is invalid is directly relevant to determining the present officers, and in such case there is a legal interest in seeking confirmation of the invalidity of the original appointment resolution; on that basis, this Court reversed and remanded the judgment of the court below before remand. Moreover, there is no ground or basis for construing that the “resolution appointing a successor director” mentioned in the remand judgment excludes cases in which the very person who had originally been removed from the office of director is appointed as the successor director and is limited only to resolutions appointing someone else as the successor director; unless there are special circumstances, it should be deemed to include a resolution appointing as successor director the very person who had originally been removed from the office of director.\\n\\n   If so, in determining whether the Plaintiffs have a legal interest in seeking confirmation of the invalidity of the said resolution of appointment dated 1988.8.26., the court below should first have determined whether there were special circumstances such that the resolution of appointment adopted at the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1991.5.6. was found to be nonexistent or void due to procedural or substantive defects other than the defect that the meeting was convened by a person without the right to do so; and as a result, if there were no such special circumstances in the resolution adopted at the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders of the Defendant Company on 1991.5.6., which again appointed the Intervenor as a director, it should have held that there was no legal interest in seeking confirmation of the invalidity of the appointment resolution of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1988.8.26.; conversely, if such special circumstances existed in the resolution of appointment adopted at the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1991.5.6., then it should further have determined whether the resolution appointing the successor director at the shareholders’ meeting held on 1992.12.30. also had such special circumstances.\\n\\n   Nevertheless, the court below did not determine whether there were special circumstances such as nonexistence or invalidity in sequence with respect to each resolution appointing a successor director at the extraordinary general meetings of shareholders held on 1991.5.6. and 1992.12.30., but instead determined the existence of legal interest in the action for confirmation in this case solely on the basis of the grounds for nonexistence or invalidity of the resolution of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1992.12.30.; this cannot but be said to contain an error of misunderstanding the essential purport of this Court’s remand judgment.\\n\\n   c. However, as will be seen in the determination of the grounds of appeal on the merits below, according to the facts lawfully determined by the court below and the record, at the time of convening the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders on 1991.5.6., as well as at the time of convening the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders on 1992.12.30., the three Plaintiffs and Nonparty 7 each owned 5,000 shares, being one-fourth of the Defendant Company’s total issued shares of 20,000; the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1991.5.6. prepared minutes of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders as if five persons, namely the Intervenor and Nonparties 8, 9, 10, and 11, who were shareholders each owning portions of the Defendant Company’s total issued shares of 20,000, had all attended and passed a resolution appointing the Intervenor and others as directors (Exhibit A Nos. 47-2 through 7); and it can be seen that the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1992.12.30., convened pursuant to permission from the court, was convened and held by the said minority shareholders, Nonparties 1 and 6, as shareholders owning all of the said issued shares of the Defendant Company, and that a resolution with the above content was passed thereat.\\n\\n   If the factual circumstances are as above, then at the respective extraordinary general meetings of shareholders held on 1991.5.6. and 1992.12.30., the Plaintiffs and Nonparty 7, who were shareholders jointly owning all of the 20,000 issued shares of the Defendant Company at the time, did not attend at all, and only persons who were not even lawful shareholders attended and passed the above resolution appointing officers; accordingly, this falls within a case in which there is a grave defect in the convening procedure and the method of resolution of the general meeting of shareholders such that the resolution of the general meeting of shareholders cannot be deemed to exist, and thus the resolution of the general meeting of shareholders must be deemed nonexistent. Therefore, the validity or nonexistence of the resolution of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on 1988.8.26., which originally appointed the Intervenor as a director, remains directly relevant to determining the present officers of the Defendant Company, and the Plaintiffs have a legal interest in seeking confirmation of the invalidity of the said appointment resolution.\\n\\n   In this light, the court below’s determination rejecting the Defendant’s preliminary objection is, in result, correct, and the error of the court below noted above does not affect the outcome of the judgment; and all of the arguments criticizing the judgment below as having misconstrued the law concerning the interest in confirmation in an action seeking confirmation of the invalidity of a resolution of a general meeting of shareholders and the authority of an acting representative director, or as containing illegality such as violation of the rules of evidence, lack of reasons, or insufficient deliberation, are without merit and cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. Regarding the merits\\n   a. The court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence cited by it, found the following facts: the Defendant Company was incorporated for the purpose of arranging housing construction, etc., and is a stock company with incorporation registration completed on 1985.3.25., a total number of issued shares of 20,000, a par value of 5,000 won per share, and total capital of 100,000,000 won; as of 1985.9.20., the distribution of share ownership was such that the Intervenor owned 6,000 shares, Nonparties 9, 8, and 11 each owned 4,000 shares, and Nonparty 10 owned 2,000 shares; Nonparty 8 was the Intervenor’s wife, Nonparty 11 was the Intervenor’s brother-in-law, and the above shareholders were related to one another by blood or marriage; the Intervenor, who was the representative director of the Defendant Company, around 1985.9.28. purchased from Samwon Housing Co., Ltd. all rights to the site and buildings for 170 apartment units that the said company was constructing on Lots 409 and 6 other parcels in Sasari, Banwol-myeon, Hwasung County, Gyeonggi Province, and had continued the apartment construction work; however, due to lack of funds, he borrowed a total of approximately 118,000,000 won from Nonparty 12 between around 1985.12.30. and around 1986.2. by discounting demand notes, and, as security for the loan claim, created a mortgage on the apartment site and on real property owned by the Intervenor; in addition, on 1986.2.3., the Intervenor, Nonparty 9, and Nonparty 10, who were shareholders of the Defendant Company, transferred 10,000 shares of the Defendant Company they owned to Nonparty 12, and it was agreed that Nonparty 12 would assume the position of co-representative director of the Defendant Company together with the Intervenor, but if the Intervenor and others repaid to Nonparty 12, by the 28th of the same month, the amount of 135,000,000 won, being the sum of the money already loaned or agreed to be loaned by him plus interest, then Nonparty 12 would resign as representative director of the Defendant Company and return the 10,000 shares purchased; on the date of the said agreement, the Intervenor additionally borrowed 54,000,000 won from Nonparty 12 and also transferred to Nonparty 12 the 4,000 shares owned by the Intervenor’s wife, Nonparty 8; pursuant to the said agreement, on the same day, registration was completed appointing Nonparty 12 as co-representative director and director of the Defendant Company, and appointing four persons, including Nonparty 13, designated by Nonparty 12, as each director of the Defendant Company; thereafter, when the checks issued by the Intervenor were on the verge of dishonor, he resigned from the position of co-representative director of the Defendant Company on the 12th of the same month and fled; in response, as Plaintiff 1, Nonparty 3, Nonparty 14, and Nonparty 7, who had supplied materials or contracted and carried out construction for the apartment building project undertaken by the Defendant Company and thus held claims against the Defendant Company, demanded repayment of debts from Nonparty 12, who had become the sole representative director of the Defendant Company at the time, Nonparty 12, on 1986.2.28., transferred 14,000 shares of the Defendant Company owned by him to Plaintiff 1, Nonparty 3, Nonparty 14, and Nonparty 7, 3,500 shares each, for a total price of 165,200,000 won; on the same day, Plaintiff 1 and others held an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and a board of directors, removed Nonparty 12, who was representative director and director, and the directors designated by him, and appointed Plaintiff 1, Nonparty 3, Nonparty 14, and Nonparty 7 as co-representative directors, and completed the change registration on 1986.3.3.; on the same day, Plaintiff 1 and others acquired from Nonparty 11, a shareholder of the Defendant Company, and from Nonparty 9, who attended as the agent of Kwak Il, 1,500 shares each out of the shares owned by Nonparty 11 and Kwak Il, thereby causing the distribution of share ownership of the Defendant Company as of 1986.2.28. to be such that Plaintiff 1, Nonparty 3, Nonparty 14, and Nonparty 7 each owned 5,000 shares, which is one-fourth of the total issued shares of 20,000. As such, in light of the record, the above fact-finding by the court below and the process of weighing evidence leading thereto are reasonable and persuasive, and there is no error such as misapprehension of facts or insufficient deliberation.\\n\\n   b. When the reasons of the above judgment of the court below are compared with the record, it can be seen that the court below accepted the Plaintiffs’ assertions and proof regarding the course of acquisition and transfer of shares, namely, that the shares were transferred solely by the manifestation of intent to transfer shares and the transfer of shareholder registration, and thereby determined the above facts; on the other hand, while rejecting the Defendant’s assertion that, as a result of the transfer of shares premised on the issuance of share certificates, Nonparties 1 and 6 and others ultimately became shareholders of the Defendant Company, the court below stated that 200 share certificates of the Defendant Company bearing an issuance date of 1985.9.25. (Exhibit B Nos. 21-1 through 200) do not impede the above factual finding; taking these points together, it is clear that the court below’s fact-finding and determination concerning the course of the above share transfers include the rejection of the Defendant’s assertion that the share certificates of the Defendant Company had already been issued as of around 1985.9.25. as well as at the time of the above share transfers found by the court below; accordingly, the ground of appeal alleging omission of judgment on this point lacks merit.\\n\\n   c. Moreover, if the factual relationship is as found by the court below, the agreement dated 1986.2.3. concluded between the Intervenor and others and Nonparty 12 should reasonably be regarded as a share transfer contract made for the purpose of securing a claim, and, since at the time of the said agreement more than six months had already elapsed after the formation of the Defendant Company but share certificates had not yet been issued, the said agreement must be deemed to have immediate effect as a transfer security over shares; it cannot, as alleged by the opposing argument, be deemed a secured claim contract under which the effect of transfer of shares arises only on condition that Nonparty 12 additionally pay the price for the shares in addition to the claim secured by the shares, or merely a preliminary agreement for the sale and purchase of shares.\\n\\n   Furthermore, where transfer security over shares is created in such a form, Nonparty 12, the transferee-secured creditor, is the owner of the shares vis-à-vis third parties; therefore, absent special circumstances, the Intervenor and others, as the parties creating the transfer security, cannot assert ownership against Plaintiff 1, Nonparty 3, Nonparty 14, and Nonparty 7, who later purchased the secured shares from Nonparty 12. Even if, as argued by the opposing argument, the transfer security arrangement was of the settlement type and a settlement issue remains, such matter is not of a nature that can be asserted against a purchaser of the secured shares. The argument merely contends, on premises contrary to this, that the court below’s judgment is defective for lack of reasons or misconstruction of the law, and cannot be accepted.\\n\\n   d. Since the court below held that Plaintiff 1 and Nonparties 3, 14, and 7 lawfully acquired the secured shares from Nonparty 12 and thereby became rightful shareholders of the Defendant Company, such holding necessarily includes rejection of the Defendant’s assertion that the transfer of shares among those persons was a sham declaration; accordingly, the argument that the judgment below is defective for omission of judgment on this point also cannot be accepted.\\n\\n   All of the arguments lack merit.\\n\\n3. Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties; it is so adjudged as per the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question:
Which of the following statements regarding directors of a juristic person are correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law)

(a) Although the articles of incorporation of a juristic person under the Civil Act contain a provision concerning restrictions on the power of representation, if the purport thereof has not been registered, the juristic person may not assert the provision against a third party, regardless of good faith or bad faith.
(b) Even if the circumstances of a juristic person under the Civil Act fall within a case where it is necessary to recognize the authority to perform duties for a director whose term has expired until a successor director is appointed, such expired director is not recognized as having the status of a director.
(c) Temporary directors appointed by a court under Article 63 of the Civil Act and interim directors appointed by a court under Article 386(2) of the Commercial Act are both unable to engage in acts not belonging to the ordinary affairs of the juristic person.
(d) An outgoing director of a stock company loses the rights and duties as a director only when there is a separate resolution of dismissal by the general meeting of shareholders, even if a newly appointed director takes office or an interim director is appointed pursuant to Article 386(2) of the Commercial Act.
(e) If the term of office of a director of a stock company expires between the last day of the final settlement period and the ordinary general meeting of shareholders for that settlement period, the term of office may be extended by the articles of incorporation until the close of the ordinary general meeting of shareholders.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2010DA13541]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Regarding Ground of Appeal 1\\n\\nArticle 383(3) of the Commercial Act provides that, notwithstanding paragraph (2) of the same Article, which stipulates that a director’s term of office may not exceed 3 years, the term may be extended by the articles of incorporation until the close of the ordinary general meeting of shareholders concerning the final accounting period during such term. The purpose of the above provision is that, with respect to a director whose term expires, it allows the director to assume responsibility for the accounts during the term and to be given an opportunity at the general meeting of shareholders to answer the shareholders’ questions concerning the financial statements and to explain himself or herself, while, on the other hand, it relieves the company of the inconvenience of having to convene an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and elect a director every time a director’s term expires before the ordinary general meeting of shareholders. In light of the legislative purpose and the content of the provision, the phrase “the ordinary general meeting of shareholders concerning the final accounting period during the term” in the above provision refers to the ordinary general meeting of shareholders concerning the final accounting period that arrives during the term, and does not mean the ordinary general meeting of shareholders concerning the accounting period first arriving after the expiration of the term or the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders to be convened. Therefore, the above provision should ultimately be understood as a provision permitting, where a director’s term expires between the last day of the final accounting period and the ordinary general meeting of shareholders for that accounting period, the extension of the term by the articles of incorporation until the close of the ordinary general meeting of shareholders.\\n\\nAccording to the facts lawfully determined by the court below and the evidence it admitted, Article 25 of the Defendant Company’s articles of incorporation provides that a director’s term of office shall be 3 years, but where the term ends before the close of the ordinary general meeting of shareholders concerning the accounting period, the term shall be extended until the close of that meeting; Non-party 1 assumed office as a director of the Defendant Company on April 7, 2005, and Non-party 2 on May 13, 2005; and, meanwhile, according to the Defendant Company’s articles of incorporation, the business year runs from January 1 to December 31 of each year (Article 33), and the ordinary general meeting of shareholders is to be convened within 3 months from the day following the last day of the business year (Article 17).\\n\\nExamining the above factual relation in light of the legal principles stated above, it is clear that the terms of office of Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 did not expire between the last day of the final accounting period falling during their terms of office (December 31, 2007) and the ordinary general meeting of shareholders provided for in the articles of incorporation (March 31, 2008); therefore, there is no room for application of the term-extension provision under the above articles of incorporation. The court below’s determination is in accordance with the above view and is proper, and there is no illegality in it, such as the misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the extension of a director’s term of office, as asserted in the grounds of appeal. The assertion in this part of the grounds of appeal cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. Regarding Ground of Appeal 2\\n\\nA resolution adopted at a shareholders’ meeting convened by a person without authority to convene a shareholders’ meeting, and without even a board resolution to convene the shareholders’ meeting, should be deemed to have no legal existence due to a serious defect in the formation process, even if there is in fact something that could be regarded as a meeting and a resolution, unless there are special circumstances such as a meeting of a one-person company by its sole shareholder, or a meeting held with all shareholders attending and agreeing to hold the meeting and a resolution adopted without any objection (see Supreme Court Judgment rendered on June 11, 1993, 93DA8702; Supreme Court Judgment rendered on October 11, 1996, 96DA24309; Supreme Court Judgment rendered on December 10, 2004, 2004DA25123, etc.). \\n\\nAccording to the facts lawfully determined by the court below and the evidence it admitted, the Defendant Company’s articles of incorporation provide that the number of directors shall be at least 2, that the person authorized to convene a board meeting is the Representative Director, and that resolutions thereof shall be adopted by the attendance of a majority of directors and a majority of the attending directors; that after Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 retired upon expiration of their terms, the Plaintiff, who was the Representative Director, and Non-party 3 were the directors of the Defendant Company; that, however, around July 23, 2008, after the expiration of the term, Non-party 1 notified the Plaintiff, etc. of the convening of a board meeting, and then held a board meeting at 10:00 on July 31, 2008; that at the above board meeting, Non-party 1, Non-party 2, and Non-party 3 attended and adopted a resolution to dismiss the Plaintiff as Representative Director and appoint Non-party 1 as Representative Director; that, meanwhile, Non-party 1 immediately convened the shareholders’ meeting at issue, and according to the minutes of that shareholders’ meeting, Non-party 1, Non-party 2, and Non-party 3 attended as shareholders and it is recorded that they removed the Plaintiff as director and appointed Non-party 1 and Non-party 4 as directors; and that, according to the shareholder registry of the Defendant Company, out of the 20,000 issued shares of the Defendant Company, the Plaintiff and Non-party 1 are each listed as owning 6,000 shares, Non-party 2 as owning 4,000 shares, and Non-party 5 and Non-party 3 as each owning 2,000 shares, but the Plaintiff received 100 shares from Non-party 1 and 4,000 shares from Non-party 2, respectively, on January 9, 2007.\\n\\nExamining the above factual relation in light of the legal principles stated above, the above board resolution appointing Non-party 1 as Representative Director was not only convened by Non-party 1, who had no authority to convene it, but also was adopted with only Non-party 3 present if Non-party 1 and Non-party 2, who were not directors, are excluded, and thus it violates the convocation procedure and quorum prescribed by the articles of incorporation and is void; further, there is no evidence whatsoever that there was a lawful board resolution for convening the shareholders’ meeting at issue, and there are no other special circumstances to be found, such as that the shareholders’ meeting at issue was held with all shareholders attending. Ultimately, therefore, the resolution at the shareholders’ meeting at issue was adopted at a shareholders’ meeting convened by Non-party 1, who had no authority to convene it, without a board resolution to convene the meeting, and the defect is so serious that it must be deemed not to exist in law.\\n\\nAlthough the court below’s judgment is not without some inadequacy in the explanation of its reasons, its conclusion that the shareholders’ meeting at issue does not exist is proper, and therefore the assertion in this part of the grounds of appeal also cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2020DA285406]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\na. As a matter of principle, a director of a stock company loses the status of director upon expiration of the term of office; however, in a stock company that takes the separation of ownership and management as a principle, not only the director’s interest in the stability of managerial status but also the shareholders’ interest in securing control over the company must be protected. Thus, in order to harmonize the interests of shareholders and directors as above, Article 385(1) of the Commercial Act provides that the company may dismiss a director at any time by resolution of the general meeting of shareholders, while, unlike the case of appointing a director, it requires a special resolution of the general meeting of shareholders when dismissing a director, and further provides that where a director with a fixed term of office is dismissed without just cause before the expiration of that term, he or she may claim damages against the company (see Supreme Court Decision 2004DA25123, decided December 10, 2004). Meanwhile, even a director who has retired upon expiration of the term of office may, pursuant to Article 386(1) of the Commercial Act, etc., acquire the rights and duties of a director until a newly appointed director takes office (hereinafter referred to as a “retiring director”); however, even in such a case, once a newly appointed director takes office or a person to perform the duties of a director on an interim basis is appointed pursuant to Article 386(2) of the Commercial Act, the director shall lose the rights and duties as a director without a separate resolution of dismissal by the general meeting of shareholders (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2004MA800, decided March 8, 2005, and Supreme Court Decision 2009MA1311, decided October 29, 2009, etc.). In light of the legislative intent of Article 385(1) of the Commercial Act and the status of a retiring director who is exercising the rights and duties of a director after the expiration of the term of office, it should be deemed that the term “director” designated as the subject of dismissal under Article 385(1) of the Commercial Act does not include a “retiring director who is exercising the rights and duties of a director after the expiration of the term of office.”\\n\\nb. The court below held that the resolution to dismiss at issue in this case, which was made pursuant to Article 385(1) of the Commercial Act, was invalid with respect to the Plaintiff, who had retired upon expiration of the term of office but was performing duties as a director until a successor director was appointed, on the ground that a retiring director cannot be dismissed pursuant to Article 385(1) of the Commercial Act.\\n\\nc. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the judgment of the court below is proper, and there is no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles regarding Article 385(1) of the Commercial Act, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, or by failing to fully examine the case, etc.\\n\\n2. Regarding Ground 2 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nThe court below held, for the reasons stated in its judgment, that it is difficult to find that there exists any ground restricting payment of severance pay as prescribed in Article 12 of the Defendant’s Executive Annual Salary Regulations with respect to the Plaintiff, and therefore that the Defendant is obligated to pay severance pay to the Plaintiff.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the judgment of the court below is proper, and there is no error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the interpretation, etc. of Article 12 of the Executive Annual Salary Regulations, or by failing to fully examine the case, violation of the rules of evidence, etc., as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged, with the concurrence of all Justices participating in the decision."}

{"[91DA24564]": "1. We examine the first ground of final appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the judgment of the court below, the court below, by comprehensively considering the evidence it admitted, found that the Defendant corporation, in connection with the non-party Gyeongwon Construction Co., Ltd. having been contracted by the Defendant corporation to perform the road paving works stated in the judgment and in purchasing the ready-mixed concrete required for the said paving works from the Plaintiff, had jointly and severally guaranteed to the Plaintiff the debt for the price of the said ready-mixed concrete in the manner and form stated in the judgment; and, in light of the record, the court below’s weighing of the evidence and finding of facts is persuasive, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality in violation of the rules governing the evaluation of evidence and in finding facts without evidence, as alleged. The argument on this point is without merit.\\n\\n2. We examine the second ground of final appeal.\\n\\nIf the articles of incorporation provide that, when the representative of a juristic person enters into a contract assuming the juristic person’s debt, approval must be obtained from the board of directors by resolution, then from the Presbytery and the founder, and then authorization must be obtained from the competent administrative authority, such a provision is a provision concerning restrictions on the representative authority of the juristic person, and such restrictions cannot be asserted against third parties unless registered (see this Court’s judgment of 1975.4.22. rendered in 74DA410; and judgment of 1987.11.24. rendered in 86DAKA2484). As argued, Article 10 of the articles of incorporation of the Defendant corporation contains a provision concerning restrictions on the representative authority of the juristic person to that effect; however, in this case, there being no assertion or proof that such effect has been registered, it must be deemed that the Defendant corporation cannot deny the validity of the guarantee agreement in this case by invoking this procedural defect against the third party Plaintiff, regardless of whether the Plaintiff was in good faith or bad faith with respect to such provision of the articles of incorporation.\\n\\nThe court below’s determination to the same effect is proper, and the contrary argument is without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the dispositive portion by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[96DA37206]": "The grounds for final appeal are examined.\\n\\nWith respect to Point 1\\n\\nAccording to the facts lawfully established by the lower appellate court and the record, the Plaintiff is seeking a declaration of nullity of the resolution of the Defendant corporation’s 6th regular board meeting dated August 20, 1993, which appointed Non-party Jang Gang-sam as chairman, and of the resolution of the extraordinary board meeting held on September 17 of the same year, which appointed Non-parties Im Hui-sun and Im Sun-jae as directors, respectively. Jang Gang-sam received, on April 20, 1994, from the competent authority, a disposition revoking approval of his assumption of office as chairman on the ground that he had grounds for disqualification as an executive officer prescribed in Article 5(6) of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations, and it can be found that Im Hui-sun and Im Sun-jae each submitted letters of resignation as directors to the Defendant corporation on October 13, 1993 and on the 14th of the same month, respectively, and resigned, and accordingly, as of April 26, 1995, the registration of removal of Jang Gang-sam, Im Hui-sun, and Im Sun-jae was completed in the Defendant corporation’s registry. In light of the foregoing facts found, the directors appointed by the respective board resolutions at issue, whose validity of appointment the Plaintiff is disputing, ultimately lost their status as directors by virtue of removal or resignation; therefore, seeking a declaration of nullity of those resolutions amounts to seeking a declaration of a past legal relationship or rights relationship, and thus there is no interest in the action.\\n\\nThe lower appellate court’s determination to the same effect is proper, and there is no error of law regarding the alleged insufficiency of deliberation or the interest in confirmation, as asserted. The Supreme Court decision cited in the argument addresses a different matter from the present case and is not appropriate for application here. The argument is without merit.\\n\\nWith respect to Point 2\\n\\nUnder civil law, the relationship between a juridical person and its directors, who are its organs, is akin to the legal relationship between a mandator and a mandatary, and as a general rule, when a director’s term expires, that mandate relationship terminates. However, if no director exists until a successor director is appointed, the juridical person, which can act only through its organ, would be placed in a situation where it cannot but immediately suspend normal activities. Accordingly, by analogical application of the provisions of Article 691 of the Civil Act, where there are special circumstances that do not justify having a former director perform the business of the juridical person and where it is necessary to have the former director handle the prior duties, the authority to perform duties is recognized, allowing the former director whose term has expired to perform the duties of a director until a successor is appointed (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 81DA614 dated March 9, 1982; Supreme Court Decision 83DAKA938 dated September 27, 1983; Supreme Court Decision 95DA40915 dated January 26, 1996).\\n\\nThe lower appellate court held that the Plaintiff took office as a director of the Defendant corporation on May 17, 1989 with the approval of the competent authority on May 3 of the same year, but that the Plaintiff’s term expired upon the passage of May 16, 1993 and thus the Plaintiff lost the status of director; however, thereafter, because the Defendant corporation’s resolution at its 6th regular board meeting dated August 20, 1993, which reappointed Non-parties Jang Gang-sam, Song Ho, Lee Yeong-jo, Lee Eun-ja, and the Plaintiff, each as directors, and the resolution of the extraordinary board meeting dated September 17, 1993, which appointed Non-parties Im Hui-sun and Im Sun-jae, each as directors, were all, as stated in the judgment, void as a matter of law, the result was that the Defendant corporation at that time had only directors whose terms had expired, which means that there was a vacancy among the directors constituting the organ of the Defendant corporation and therefore it was in a state where it could not carry on normal activities as a juridical person; thus, although circumstances can be seen in which it is necessary to have the directors whose terms had expired, including the Plaintiff, continue to perform their duties as directors, it dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim in this case seeking confirmation that the Plaintiff is a director of the Defendant corporation on the ground that the authority of a director whose term has expired to perform duties may be recognized only when, in order to resolve an urgent situation, it is necessary to have the retired director perform duties on an individual and concrete basis, and that it is not a status automatically and comprehensively granted merely because one is a retired director.\\n\\nIn light of the record and the legal principles set forth above, the lower appellate court’s findings and determination are all proper, and there is no error of law, as alleged, in misconstruing the legal principles concerning the status of directors in a foundation, and the Supreme Court decision cited in the argument addresses a different matter from the present case and is not appropriate for application here. The argument is also without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating, as set forth in the order."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the duty of disclosure borne by the policyholder or the insured at the time an insurance contract is concluded is incorrect? (Where there is dispute, in accordance with precedents)
A: In property insurance, the fact that double insurance has been concluded does not constitute a material matter subject to the duty of disclosure.
B: An insurer’s exercise of the right to terminate an insurance contract on the ground of a violation of the duty of disclosure may be made even after the insured event has occurred.
C: Even where the duty of disclosure has been violated, if one month has elapsed from the day on which the insurer became aware of the violation of the duty of disclosure, or if three years have elapsed from the date the contract was formed, the insurer may not terminate the insurance contract.
D: If it is proved that there is no causal relation between the fact of the violation of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event, the insurer may terminate the insurance contract on the ground of the violation of the duty of disclosure, but remains liable to pay the insurance proceeds.
E: If the violation of the duty of disclosure constitutes fraud, the insurer may terminate the insurance contract pursuant to Article 651 of the Commercial Act, but may not rescind the insurance contract pursuant to Article 110 of the Civil Act.
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2001DA49623]": "1. Judgment of the lower court\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the lower court judgment and the first-instance judgment cited therein, the lower court, upon comprehensively considering the evidence it admitted, found as follows: the Plaintiff, who manufactures machine parts under the trade name Bukwang Precision, entered into a fire insurance contract with the Defendant on November 20, 1997, under which the Defendant would compensate for any damage if, within one year of the insurance period, the machines listed in the attached schedule to the lower court judgment installed in the Plaintiff’s factory were damaged or destroyed by fire and loss thereby arose; on June 9, 1998, the Plaintiff separately entered into a fire insurance contract with the non-party American Home Assurance Company (hereinafter referred to as the “non-party company”) covering the same machines on the same terms (hereinafter referred to as “the separate insurance contract in this case”); however, on November 20, 1998, after the one-year insurance period of the initial insurance contract in this case had expired, the Plaintiff again entered into a fire insurance contract with the Defendant on the same terms (hereinafter referred to as “the insurance contract in this case”) without previously notifying the Defendant of the fact that the separate insurance contract in this case had already been concluded; according to the Fire Insurance General Terms and Conditions forming part of the insurance contract in this case (hereinafter referred to as “the insurance terms and conditions in this case”), the policyholder, when entering into the contract, must notify the company without omission of all facts known to him or her concerning the matters stated in the insurance application (Article 7), and where the policyholder, intentionally or by gross negligence, fails to disclose truthfully the matters stated in the insurance application, the insurer may terminate the insurance contract, and even if such termination is effected after loss has occurred, the insurance company shall not compensate for such loss; provided, however, that if it is proved that the loss did not arise from the fact that the policyholder failed to disclose truthfully the matters stated in the insurance application, then compensation shall be made therefor (Article 11); a fire of unknown origin occurred at around 22:13 on December 19, 1998, in the factory building of the Plaintiff, and an accident occurred in which most of the machines that were the subject matter insured under the insurance contract in this case were burned (hereinafter referred to as “the insurance accident in this case”), causing the Plaintiff damage in the amount of 32,787,500 won; after the occurrence of the insurance accident in this case, the Defendant notified the Plaintiff that it was terminating the insurance contract in this case on the basis of Articles 7 and 11 of the insurance terms and conditions in this case, and that notice of termination reached the Plaintiff around March 4, 1999; based on these findings, the lower court determined that the insurance contract in this case and the separate insurance contract in this case constituted double insurance under Article 672, paragraph (1) of the Commercial Act because the insured interest and the insured event were the same, the insurance periods overlapped, and the total amount of each insurance amount exceeded the insured value under the insurance contract in this case and the insured value under the separate insurance contract in this case, respectively; that the fact that such double insurance had been concluded was a matter closely related to the management of risk, the burden of loss-prevention expenses, subrogation by the insurer, and the like, and therefore constituted an important matter to the Defendant; and that, since the Plaintiff failed, intentionally or by gross negligence, to notify the Defendant of the fact that the separate insurance contract in this case had been concluded at the time of entering into the insurance contract in this case, the insurance contract in this case was lawfully terminated pursuant to Articles 655, 651, and 672, paragraph (2) of the Commercial Act, or Articles 11 and 7 of the insurance terms and conditions in this case.\\n\\n2. This Court’s determination\\n\\nThe “important matters” prescribed in Article 651 of the Commercial Act, for which the policyholder or the insured bears a duty to notify the insurer at the time of the insurance contract, refer to matters that serve as standards for the insurer to measure the probability of the occurrence of the insured event and the burden of liability arising therefrom, and thereby determine whether to conclude the insurance contract or the contents of the insurance contract, such as the premium or the addition of special exemption clauses; objectively, they are matters which, if the insurer knew of them, it would be thought that the insurer would not conclude the contract, or would not conclude it on the same terms at least; and whether a particular fact falls within this category is a matter of factual determination that necessarily varies according to the type of insurance and must be objectively observed and determined in light of insurance techniques (see Supreme Court Decisions 96DA27971, rendered on December 23, 1996, and 95DA25268, rendered on September 5, 1997, among others).\\n\\nArticle 672, paragraph (2) of the Commercial Act provides that, in non-life insurance, where several insurance contracts are concluded with respect to the same subject matter of insurance and the same accident, the policyholder shall notify each insurer of the contents of each insurance contract; accordingly, where a policyholder who has already concluded an insurance contract enters into another insurance contract with respect to the same subject matter insured and the same insured event, there is a duty to notify as to the existing insurance contract. However, the purpose of requiring the policyholder in non-life insurance, as above, to notify and inform the insurer of the fact that multiple insurance contracts have been concluded is, in light of Article 672, paragraph (1) of the Commercial Act, which provides for the principle of joint and proportionate compensation in cases of double insurance in non-life insurance, and Articles 672, paragraph (3), and 669, paragraph (4) of the Commercial Act, which provide that double insurance caused by fraud is void, merely to prevent in advance the conclusion of an insurance contract by fraud for the purpose of obtaining unjust enrichment and to enable the insurer, in the event of an insured event, to jointly determine the investigation of loss or the scope of liability with other insurers; it cannot be regarded as intended to provide data by which the insurer can measure the risk of occurrence of the insured event and determine whether to conclude the contract or under what conditions to conclude it. According to the record, the insurance application in this case contains, in very small print at the top, as one of the matters that must be known, the statement that “if matters to be disclosed before the contract concerning the object of insurance or the location, structure, occupation, surrounding circumstances of the building accommodating it, and the existence of other insurance contracts concluded with respect to the same object of insurance are untrue, the insurance contract may become void, lose effect, or be terminated”; however, no separate item is provided for “other insurance contracts concluded with respect to the same object of insurance,” and although the basic particulars merely divide the items for “insured amount” and “premium paid” into “This company” and “(Total)” columns, there is no explicit indication of matters to be disclosed concerning other insurance contracts concluded with respect to the same object of insurance; moreover, there is no indication whatsoever that, at the time the Defendant entered into the insurance contract in this case, it would have calculated the premium rate differently depending on the existence or nonexistence of other insurance contracts concluded with respect to the same object of insurance or depending on the insured amount, or that it would have refused to enter into the insurance contract in this case; therefore, the fact that double insurance was concluded in the instant insurance, which is a kind of non-life insurance, does not constitute an important matter subject to the duty of disclosure under Article 651 of the Commercial Act, and accordingly Article 11 of the insurance terms and conditions in this case, which provides that the insurance contract may be terminated when the policyholder, intentionally or by gross negligence, fails to disclose truthfully the matters stated in the insurance application, should be deemed not applicable in cases where the fact of the conclusion of double insurance was not disclosed.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court judgment, which held that the insurance contract in this case was lawfully terminated pursuant to the Commercial Act and the insurance terms and conditions in this case on the premise that the fact of the conclusion of double insurance constituted an important matter under Article 651 of the Commercial Act, contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the object of the duty of disclosure in insurance contracts and the legal principles governing double insurance in non-life insurance.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds for appeal, the lower court judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further proceedings and determination. The judgment is rendered as stated in the Disposition, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2010DA25353]": "The grounds of appeal are examined (the statements in the supplemental brief on the grounds of appeal submitted after the expiration of the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal shall be considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds of appeal).\\n\\n1. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, after finding the facts as stated in the judgment, held that whether the non-party had been diagnosed with hypertension and had received medication and treatment is an important matter that serves as the standard for the insurer, the Defendant, to determine whether to conclude the insurance contract or the contents of the insurance contract at issue, such as the premium or the addition of special exemption clauses, by assessing the probability of the occurrence of the insured event and the resulting burden of liability, and that, as a matter inquired about by the Defendant in writing, it falls within the scope of the duty of disclosure; and that, although the Plaintiff and the non-party had in fact been diagnosed with hypertension and had received medication within the preceding 5 years as above, they stated in the insurance application form that no such facts existed, and thus, in entering into the insurance contract at issue, the Plaintiff and the non-party violated the duty of disclosure by failing, with intent or gross negligence, to disclose truthfully the matters to be disclosed to the Defendant. In light of the record, such determination by the court below is proper and persuasive, and there is no illegality such as an error of law as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. The main clause of Commercial Act Article 651 provides: “If, at the time of the insurance contract, the policyholder or the insured, due to intent or gross negligence, has failed to disclose an important matter or has made a false disclosure, the insurer may terminate the contract only within 1 month from the day on which it learned of the fact and within 3 years from the day on which the contract was concluded.” Article 655 provides: “Even after the occurrence of the insured event, if the insurer has terminated the contract pursuant to Articles 650, 651, 652, and 653, it shall not be liable to pay the insured amount and may demand the return of any insured amount already paid. However, this shall not apply if it is proved that the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure, or the fact of a material change in or increase of risk, did not affect the occurrence of the insured event.”\\n\\nAs Article 651 of the Commercial Act is a general provision concerning termination of a contract due to breach of the duty of disclosure, it does not require a causal relationship between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event; Article 655 of the Commercial Act is a provision concerning a claim for the insured amount when the contract is terminated due to breach of the duty of disclosure, and therefore it is reasonable to construe not only its main clause but also its proviso as provisions concerning the existence or nonexistence of the right to claim the insured amount; if the policyholder or the insured, at the time of the insurance contract, intentionally or through gross negligence fails to disclose or makes a false disclosure of an important matter, the requirements for breach of the duty of disclosure are thereby satisfied, whereas the causal relationship between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event is determined only at the time the insured event occurs; accordingly, even if the insurer becomes liable to pay the insured amount under the proviso to Article 655 of the Commercial Act because no causal relationship is recognized between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event, it is reasonable to interpret that, separately therefrom, the insurer may terminate the contract on the ground of breach of the duty of disclosure pursuant to Article 651 of the Commercial Act; if termination of the contract under Article 651 of the Commercial Act were not permitted on the ground that no causal relationship is recognized between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event, an unreasonable result would arise in that, before the occurrence of the insured event, the contract may be terminated on the ground of breach of the duty of disclosure pursuant to Article 651 of the Commercial Act, whereas after the occurrence of the insured event, the contract cannot be terminated even after payment of the insured amount on the ground that there is no causal relationship ex post facto, and the insured amount would have to continue to be paid so long as no causal relationship is recognized; and, considering comprehensively that interpreting that an insurance contract in breach of the duty of disclosure may be terminated by the insurer regardless of the causal relationship between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event is consistent with the good-faith nature and collective character of insurance contracts, the insurer may terminate the contract pursuant to Article 651 of the Commercial Act on the ground of breach of the duty of disclosure regardless of the causal relationship between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event. However, with respect to the right to claim the insured amount, when the insurer terminates the insurance contract after the occurrence of the insured event on the ground of breach of the duty of disclosure, the obligation to pay the insured amount is to be determined according to the causal relationship between the fact of breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event, and the effect of termination of the contract may be limited within that scope.\\n\\nThe court below, for the reasons stated above, held that, even if no causal relationship is recognized between the Plaintiff’s and the non-party’s breach of the duty of disclosure and the occurrence of the insured event that the non-party developed leukemia, the Defendant may terminate the insurance contract at issue on the ground of the Plaintiff’s and the non-party’s breach of the duty of disclosure; this is proper as being in accordance with the foregoing legal principles, and there is no illegality such as an error of law as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAnd the Supreme Court Decision rendered on February 25, 1994, 93DA52082, and the Supreme Court Decision rendered on January 5, 2001, 2000DA40353, cited by the Plaintiff, concern cases in which the existence or nonexistence of the right to claim the insured amount arising from the occurrence of the insured event was disputed, and differ from this case, which disputes the effect of termination of the insurance contract, and are therefore not appropriate to be invoked.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal are to be borne by the losing party; it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2014DA234827]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Where an insurance policyholder concludes an insurance contract for the purpose of illegally acquiring insurance proceeds through a plurality of insurance contracts, the insurance contract is void as being contrary to good morals and other social order under Article 103 of the Civil Act. Causing insurance proceeds to be paid pursuant to such an insurance contract not only causes a departure from social propriety by encouraging speculative intent to obtain unlawful gains through the abuse of an insurance contract, but also undermines the purpose of the insurance system of the reasonable distribution of risk, destroys the fortuity of the occurrence of risk, and results in the sacrifice of a multitude of good-faith policyholders, thereby destroying the foundation of the insurance system. Even if there is no evidence directly establishing that the insurance policyholder concluded a plurality of insurance contracts for the purpose of illegally acquiring insurance proceeds, such purpose may be inferred from all the circumstances, such as the policyholder’s occupation and financial condition, the timing and circumstances of concluding the plurality of insurance contracts, the scale and nature of the insurance contracts, and the circumstances after the conclusion of the insurance contracts (see Supreme Court Decision 2009DA12115, rendered May 28, 2009, etc.).\\n\\nIn particular, if indirect facts are established, such as the circumstance that the insurance policyholder concluded excessive insurance contracts requiring regular payment of premiums in a substantial amount that would be difficult to bear in light of his or her income and other financial circumstances; the circumstance that, although there was no reasonable reason to take out a plurality of insurance policies within a short period, the policyholder concentrated on taking out a plurality of insurance policies; the circumstance that, unlike the usual course of concluding insurance contracts, such as joining upon solicitation by an insurance broker, the policyholder actively and voluntarily concluded excessive insurance contracts; the circumstance that the policyholder took out a plurality of insurance policies with strong coverage features rather than savings-oriented policies and paid a large part of his or her income as premiums therefor; the circumstance that, at the time of concluding the insurance contracts, the policyholder stated false facts concerning the existence of other insurance policies of the same kind and concerning his or her occupation and income; or the circumstance that, shortly after concluding a plurality of insurance contracts, the policyholder filed and received insurance claims on the ground of an insurance accident in a concentrated manner, such indirect facts constitute powerful materials from which the purpose of illegally acquiring insurance proceeds may be inferred (see Supreme Court Decision 2013DA69170, rendered April 30, 2014; Supreme Court Decision 2014DA73237, rendered February 12, 2015, etc.).\\n\\nMeanwhile, where a policyholder’s breach of the duty to disclose material matters at the time of concluding an insurance contract constitutes fraud, the insurer may rescind the contract pursuant to the provisions of the Commercial Act, and may also cancel the insurance contract in accordance with the rescission provision stipulated in the insurance contract or the general principles of the Civil Act (see Supreme Court Decision 91DA1165, rendered December 27, 1991). Therefore, although voidness of the insurance contract on the ground of violation of Article 103 of the Civil Act and rescission or cancellation of the insurance contract on the ground of breach of the duty to disclose differ in their requirements and effects where multiple insurance contracts were concluded for the purpose of illegally acquiring insurance proceeds, if each of the respective requirements is satisfied in an individual case, the above remedies are recognized concurrently, and in such a case, the insurer may alternatively assert voidness, rescission, or cancellation of the insurance contract.\\n\\n2. The lower court held that the insurance contract in this case could be sufficiently inferred, based on the following circumstances such as the policyholder’s occupation and financial condition, the circumstances of concluding a plurality of insurance contracts, the scale of the insurance contracts, and the circumstances after the conclusion of the insurance contracts, to have been entered into for the purpose of illegally acquiring insurance proceeds, and that, as it undermines the purpose of the insurance system of the reasonable distribution of risk, destroys the fortuity of the occurrence of risk, and results in the sacrifice of a multitude of good-faith policyholders, thereby damaging the foundation of the insurance system, it is void as being contrary to good morals and other social order as prescribed in Article 103 of the Civil Act.\\n\\na. At the time the Defendants concluded the insurance contract in this case, they were in a de facto marital relationship and formed an economic community, and over approximately six years from around 2005 to around 2010, the spouses each separately took out 12 similar insurance policies in duplicate. At the time the insurance contract in this case was concluded on 2008. 12. 31., the total monthly premiums of the insurance policies subscribed to with the Defendants as the insured were 1,229,740 won, and the annual premiums to be paid were 14,756,880 won, whereas the Defendants’ income amount for 2008 was 16,353,155 won in total and the amount of income tax paid was 0 won.\\n\\nb. Defendant 1’s average annual income from 2005 to 2010 was 11,280,530 won, and the Defendants’ average annual income amount was 18,021,391 won in total; during the above period, Defendant 1’s average annual income tax payment was 57,005 won, and the Defendants’ average annual income tax payment was approximately 88,477 won in total.\\n\\nc. Based on 2010, the Defendants’ premium burden reached 20,046,480 won in total per year, which corresponds to approximately 76% of the Defendants’ income amount for 2010, namely 26,362,262 won.\\n\\nd. In the insurance contract in this case, 73.3% of the monthly premiums (= 47,650 won ÷ 65,000 won × 100) is the coverage portion, so it has little savings value, and if income is low or irregular, it is likely to place a burden on household finances. On the other hand, each insurance contract taken out by the Defendants was all hospitalization daily benefit insurance (meaning insurance that pays a fixed amount according to the number of days hospitalized) or insurance covering similar content, so there was little need for duplicate subscription, and in the case of Defendant 1, around the time the insurance contract in this case was concluded on 2008. 12. 31., he did not have a job with a particularly high risk of injury.\\n\\ne. Defendant 1 falsely disclosed his occupation and medical history, etc. at the time of concluding the insurance contract in this case.\\n\\nf. From around June 2006 for about six years, Defendant 1 received insurance proceeds totaling 53,335,860 won on 74 occasions in connection with various insurance accidents. The details of the hospitalization treatment that took place after the end of 2007, when the above Defendant was serving in the Special Warfare Command, included many cases based on diseases whose diagnosis depended on subjective symptoms such as sprains and strains and for which the necessity of hospitalization treatment was questionable, and the above Defendant received hospitalization treatment several times in the Gunsan area unrelated to his workplace or residence.\\n\\n3. The lower court’s determination is in accordance with the above legal principles and is proper, and, as argued in the grounds of appeal, there is no error in exceeding the limits of the free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience or in misapprehending the legal principles concerning Article 103 of the Civil Act.\\n\\n4. The Defendants’ appeals are without merit, and all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal are borne by the losing parties. Accordingly, the judgment is rendered in the form of the disposition, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning bona fide acquisition of a bill is incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law)
A: The scope of defects cured by bona fide acquisition of a bill includes not only the case where the transferor is a person without title, but also cases where the act of transfer is defective due to a defect in agency authority.
B: Even where the bona fide acquirer of a bill acquires it knowing the facts constituting the bill obligor’s personal defense to the detriment of the bill obligor, the personal defense is cut off.
C: Even in the case of a person who bona fide acquired a bill, once a judgment of nullification has been rendered with respect to that bill in the public notice and claim proceedings without filing a claim of rights, such person cannot assert rights under that bill until filing an action of objection and obtaining a revocation judgment.
D: Where a bill is acquired by the method of assignment of a nominative claim or by an assignment order, bona fide acquisition is not recognized.
E: A person who acquires the right from a bona fide acquirer acquires the full right, even if the assignor was in bad faith with respect to the fact that he or she had previously acquired it from a person without title.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[93DA32934]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. According to the facts found by the court below, on 1992. 2. 18. the Plaintiff, while in possession of one promissory note issued in the name of the Defendant, bearing the following particulars: payee, Non-Party; face amount, KRW 21,500,000; due date, 1992. 6. 21.; place of issuance and place of payment, Gumi City; place of payment, Korean Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Gumi Branch; date of issuance, 1992. 2. 17.; which the Plaintiff had received by endorsement and transfer from the first-instance co-defendant, Non-Party, presented it for payment at the place of payment on the due date, but payment was refused, and the Defendant, on the ground that the promissory note in question had been lost, filed an application for public notice and a declaration of invalidity with the Gimcheon Branch of the Daegu District Court, and on 1992. 10. 27. a declaration of invalidity was rendered.\\n\\n2. The effect of a declaration of invalidity concerning a promissory note is limited, after the judgment, to rendering the relevant note void and restoring to the applicant for public notice the status equivalent to that of a holder of the note, and it does not establish that the applicant for public notice is the substantive right holder. However, since the promissory note held by the acquirer loses its effect as a promissory note as the negative effect of the declaration of invalidity, the holder of the promissory note cannot claim the amount of the note by asserting that the void note is a valid note.\\n\\nAccordingly, the disposition of the court below, which dismissed the Plaintiff’s claim in this case for the amount of the promissory note on the basis of such view, is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality in misapprehending the law on bona fide acquisition of a negotiable instrument and a declaration of invalidity; nor is it otherwise on the ground that the Plaintiff acquired it in good faith before the public notice procedure and instituted this action (see Supreme Court Decisions 65DA1002, rendered 1965. 7. 27.; 79DA4, rendered 1979. 3. 13.; 82DA298, rendered 1982. 10. 26.; 83DA508 and 83DAKA1705, rendered 1983. 11. 8.; 89DAKA16215, rendered 1990. 4. 27., etc.).\\n\\nTherefore, the arguments are without merit.\\n\\nAccordingly, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal are assessed against the losing party, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[94DA55217]": "Regarding Grounds 1 and 2 of the Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nThe court below, having found that the Defendant had each issued and delivered to Non-party Company General Architectural Office Akibantieseussi Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “Non-party Company”) one promissory note with a face amount of KRW 86,200,000, date of issue 1993.3.3., due date 6.25. of the same year, and place of issue and place of payment each Seoul (hereinafter referred to as “Promissory Note No. 1 of this case”), and one promissory note with a face amount of KRW 25,160,000, date of issue 3.31. of the same year, due date 7.2. of the same year, and place of issue and place of payment each Seoul (hereinafter referred to as “Promissory Note No. 2 of this case”); that Promissory Note No. 1 of this case, on which successive endorsements had been entered from the Non-party Company to Non-party 1 and Plaintiff 1, and Promissory Note No. 2 of this case, on which successive endorsements had been entered from the Non-party Company to Plaintiff 2 and Non-party 2, had each been presented for payment on the respective due dates but payment had been refused; that Non-party 1 was an alias of Plaintiff 1, and Plaintiff 2, the endorsee of Promissory Note No. 2, had taken back Promissory Note No. 2 of this case from the above Non-party 2; and that the endorsement in the name of the Non-party Company had been forged by Non-party 3, who was then the head of the general affairs department, and that the Plaintiffs had acquired the promissory notes in this case from the said Non-party 3 by discounting them, held, with respect to the Plaintiffs’ defense of acquisition in good faith, that the scope of defects cured by good-faith acquisition of a bill, namely, the scope of the transferor, includes not only cases where the transferor is a person without rights but also cases such as lack of authority or defects in agency authority as in this case (see Supreme Court Decision 93DA32118 rendered on 1993.9.24.), and further found that Plaintiff 1, on 1993.3.4., through Non-party 4, had received from the above Non-party 3, a high school junior long known to him, a request to discount Promissory Note No. 1 of this case, had confirmed whether the said Non-party 3 was working for the Non-party Company, had telephoned Non-party 5, the bill-handling employee in the accounting department of the Defendant company, the issuer, to confirm whether the note was an accident note, and then had written the name of the said Non-party 5 and the date and time of such confirmation in the upper left-hand corner on the reverse side of the note and had received the note from the said Non-party 3; that Plaintiff 2 likewise, on the 31st of the same month, through the said Non-party 4, had received from the said Non-party 1 a request to discount Promissory Note No. 2 of this case, had confirmed whether the said Non-party 3 was working for the Non-party Company, had telephoned the Defendant company, the issuer, to confirm whether the note was an accident note, and then had received the note; that at the time of each such discounting of the notes, the name of the representative director of the Non-party Company, the first endorser, and his seal had already been affixed; and that there had been no prior bill transactions between the Plaintiffs and the Non-party Company, and then, on that basis, determined that the Plaintiffs had acquired each of the promissory notes in this case in good faith.\\n\\nThe above factual findings and determination by the court below are well-founded, and it cannot be said that there is any error in violation of the rules of evidence as argued, or any error of law regarding the scope of the transferor and gross negligence in the good-faith acquisition of a bill. Accordingly, all the arguments are without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of the appeal shall be borne by the losing Defendant. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: A granted B the authority to complete the amount of a promissory note within the limit of KRW 10,000,000, and issued and delivered a promissory note without stating only the amount of the note. Which of the following statements is incorrect? (In case of dispute, according to precedents)
A: If B, without completing the amount of the note, files an action against A seeking payment on the note, B must exercise the authority to complete it by the time the oral argument in the trial on the merits is concluded.
B: If B fills in the amount of the note as KRW 20,000,000 and then indorses and transfers the note to C, who believed it without gross negligence, A is liable on the note to C according to the wording entered.
C: If B presents the note to A for payment without completing the amount of the note, A does not bear liability for delay in performance.
D: If C, who received the note by indorsement and transfer from B before maturity, completes the amount after the period for presentment for payment has elapsed, B's indorsement is an indorsement after maturity.
E: Even if B loses the note without completing the amount of the note, B may obtain a judgment declaring the instrument void by public summons proceedings.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2008DA59230]": "We consider the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nWhere the holder of a promissory note first filed a suit for payment on the note (hereinafter referred to as the “prior suit”) based on a so-called blank promissory note that lacked some of the requirements of a negotiable instrument, then, after receiving a judgment dismissing the claim on the ground of such defect in the requirements of the negotiable instrument and after that judgment became final and conclusive, filled in the blank portion and again filed a suit for payment on the note against the defendant in the prior suit (hereinafter referred to as the “later suit”), even if the Plaintiff in the prior suit misunderstood some of the requirements of the negotiable instrument or did not know of the defect, the prior suit and the later suit are both aimed at determining the existence or nonexistence of the same right or legal relationship, and thus the subject matter of the litigation should be regarded as identical. And because the res judicata effect of a final and conclusive judgment extends, in litigation between the same parties, to all allegations and defenses that the parties asserted or could have asserted before the conclusion of oral argument at the trial on the merits{ see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 91DA24847, 24854 (consolidated), rendered October 27, 1992 }, where the holder of a promissory note could have exercised the right to complete the blank and claimed payment of the note amount until the conclusion of oral argument at the trial on the merits in the prior suit, but did not fill in the blank portion by that time, lost the case on that ground, the judgment became final and conclusive, and thereafter exercised the right to complete the blank and, on the ground that the note had been completed, again claims the same note amount against the defendant in the prior suit, the assertion of the exercise of the right to complete the blank is, absent special circumstances, barred by the res judicata effect of the judgment in the prior suit and should be deemed impermissible.\\n\\nThe judgment of the lower court to the same effect is correct, and there is no illegality such as a violation of precedent concerning the temporal scope of res judicata or the legal nature of the right to complete a blank, an error of law regarding Article 1 of the Bills of Exchange and Promissory Notes Act, or an error of law regarding the identity of the subject matter of the litigation, as alleged in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party; accordingly, the judgment is rendered as stated in the order, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[68DA1176]": "The grounds of appeal are considered.\\n\\nAccording to the facts lawfully determined by the judgment below, the Defendant issued and delivered to Nonparty 1 one blank promissory note with face amount of 50,000 won, maturity 66.1.20., place of payment and place of issue both Daejeon City, place of payment, Hanil Bank Daejeon Branch, payee blank, date of issue 65.12.13., and Nonparty 1 thereafter transferred and delivered it to Nonparty 2, Nonparty 2 to Nonparty 3, respectively, around that time, and on 66.1.10.
