{"[2009DO3505]": "1. Determination on the Grounds of Appeal\\n\\nThe court below, comprehensively considering the evidence it admitted, found that the Defendant cursed at Police Officer Non-party 1, approached him while pushing his shoulder and body as if to strike him and assaulted him, cursed at Police Officer Non-party 2 who was restraining him, threw off his upper garment, and body-checked him, thereby obstructing the lawful performance of the two police officers’ official duties concerning the handling of the report and investigative work, and determined that the crime of obstruction of performance of official duties was established against the Defendant; and, in light of the record, the above factual findings and determination of the court below are just and acceptable, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality such as a violation of the rules of evidence assessment.\\n\\n2. Ex Officio Determination\\n\\na. According to Article 323, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Procedure Act, the reasons for a conviction must specify the facts constituting the offense, the gist of the evidence, and the application of the laws; accordingly, where, in rendering a conviction, any one of these is entirely omitted from the reasons for the judgment, this constitutes a violation of law that affected the judgment as prescribed in Article 383, item 1 of the Criminal Procedure Act and is a ground for reversal.\\n\\nAccording to the statement of reasons in the judgment of the court below, the court below, ex officio, reversed the first-instance judgment and again rendered a conviction against the Defendant, but in the reasons for the judgment it stated only the application of the laws, wholly omitting the facts constituting the offense and the gist of the evidence; therefore, the judgment of the court below is unlawful and cannot avoid reversal.\\n\\nMeanwhile, since this case is recognized as sufficiently ready for judgment based on the case record and the evidence examined up to the court below, this Court shall directly render judgment pursuant to Article 396 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nb. Where assault or intimidation is committed against several public officials who are executing the same official duty, multiple crimes of obstruction of performance of official duties are established according to the number of public officials executing the official duty, and where such assault or intimidation is committed at the same place and on the same occasion and is evaluated as one act in social common sense, the multiple crimes of obstruction of performance of official duties are in a relation of ideal concurrence (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on September 28, 1961, 4294HYEONGSANG415).\\n\\nAccording to the factual relations lawfully established by the court below and the record, Police Officer Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 received a report of damage filed against the Defendant and were dispatched together, while executing duties relating to the handling of the report and investigation, and it can be seen that the Defendant cursed at the above police officers at the same place, first assaulted Police Officer Non-party 1, and then immediately assaulted Police Officer Non-party 2 who restrained him; thus, the act of assault committed at the same place and on the same occasion should be deemed, in social common sense, one act, and therefore the crime of obstruction of performance of official duties against Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 is in a relation of ideal concurrence as prescribed in Article 40 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\nNevertheless, the first-instance court’s action of aggravating the sentence on the view that each of the acts of obstruction of performance of official duties in this case stood in a relation of substantive concurrence is unlawful, and such error affected the judgment; accordingly, the first-instance judgment can no longer be maintained. Therefore, we reverse the first-instance judgment and render judgment as follows.\\n\\nSince the facts constituting the offense and the gist of the evidence are the same as those stated in the respective corresponding columns of the first-instance judgment, they are cited as is pursuant to Articles 399 and 369 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nThe Defendant’s acts described in the judgment each fall under Article 136, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Act; applying Articles 40 and 50 of the Criminal Act, the Defendant shall be punished by the penalty prescribed for the crime of obstruction of performance of official duties against Non-party 1, which is the more serious offense, and, selecting the fine among the prescribed punishments, the Defendant shall be sentenced to a fine of KRW 500,000. If the Defendant fails to pay the above fine, applying Articles 70 and 69, paragraph (2) of the Criminal Act, the Defendant shall be confined in a workhouse for the period converted at KRW 50,000 per day; applying Article 57 of the Criminal Act, one day of detention before the pronouncement of the first-instance judgment shall be credited toward the workhouse detention period relating to the above fine, and the judgment is rendered as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating."}

{"[2010DO10500]": "The grounds for appeal are determined as follows.\\n\\n1. Embezzlement is an offense that protects the owner’s right, such as ownership, in another person’s property as its protected legal interest, and it is an offense of danger that is completed if there is a risk of infringement of that legal interest even if the result of such infringement does not occur (see Supreme Court Decision 2002DO2219 rendered on 2002. 11. 13.).\\n\\nAlso, once a specific act of disposition (hereinafter referred to as the “preceding act of disposition”) has caused a risk of infringement of the legal interest, thereby causing the offense of embezzlement to be consummated, if a new act of disposition (hereinafter referred to as the “subsequent act of disposition”) is carried out before the final result of infringement of the legal interest occurs, then, if the subsequent act of disposition merely serves as a means of completing the risk caused by the preceding act of disposition into an actual infringement of the legal interest, or if it is something that could naturally be anticipated in the course thereof and does not add any new risk, the risk caused by the subsequent act of disposition shall be deemed to be included within the risk already assessed by the embezzlement offense that had already been established by the preceding act of disposition; thus, the subsequent act of disposition corresponds to what is called a non-punishable subsequent act.\\n\\nHowever, if the subsequent act of disposition goes beyond this and, by adding a new risk that could not have been anticipated from the preceding act of disposition, increases the risk of infringement of the legal interest, or causes the result of infringement of the legal interest by a method unrelated to the preceding act of disposition, then this falls outside the scope of the risk already assessed by the embezzlement offense that had already been established by the preceding act of disposition, and, absent special circumstances, it must be regarded as independently constituting embezzlement.\\n\\nAccordingly, even if a person who is in custody of another’s real property consummates an act of embezzlement by, with intent to unlawfully appropriate, completing the registration of the creation of a mortgage on such real property, if thereafter a separate mortgage is created on the same real property so as to add a new risk of infringement of the legal interest and thereby increase the risk of infringement of the legal interest, or if such real property is sold so as to cause a result of infringement of the legal interest irrespective of the existing mortgage, this is beyond the scope that could naturally be anticipated from the mortgage itself, such as a sale by compulsory auction for execution of the original mortgage, and thus adds a new risk of infringement of the legal interest or causes the result of infringement of the legal interest; therefore, absent special circumstances, it cannot be regarded as a non-punishable subsequent act, and it shall independently constitute embezzlement.\\n\\nSupreme Court Decision 96DO1755 rendered on 1996. 11. 29., Supreme Court Decision 96DO2731 rendered on 1997. 1. 20., Supreme Court Decision 97DO3282 rendered on 1998. 2. 24., Supreme Court Decision 99DO5 rendered on 1999. 4. 27., Supreme Court Decision 99DO2651 rendered on 1999. 11. 26., Supreme Court Decision 2000DO310 rendered on 2000. 3. 24., Supreme Court Decision 2006DO3636 rendered on 2006. 8. 24., Supreme Court Decision 2005DO8699 rendered on 2006. 11. 9., and other decisions to the contrary shall be altered to the extent they conflict with this judgment.\\n\\n2. Based on the evidence admitted by the lower court, the lower court found the following facts: Defendant 1, having been entrusted by title trust and holding in custody, on 1995. 10. 20., the following land owned by the victim clan association: a rice paddy of 2,337 square meters in Paju-si, Jeokseong-myeon (address 1 omitted), and a rice paddy of 2,340 square meters at (address 2 omitted) (hereinafter collectively referred to as “the land at issue”); in order to borrow money to use for repaying his personal debts, Defendant 1 created, on 1995. 11. 30., a mortgage on the land at issue with a maximum secured claim amount of 14,000,000 won, and on 2003. 4. 15., another mortgage on the land at issue with a maximum secured claim amount of 7,500,000 won; thereafter, the Defendants conspired and, on 2009. 2. 21., sold the land at issue to a third party for 193,000,000 won; and, after recognizing such facts, the lower court rejected the Defendants’ argument to the effect that the act of selling the land at issue was carried out after the preceding act of creating the mortgage and thus constituted a non-punishable subsequent act, and held that the Defendants’ act of selling the land at issue constituted embezzlement, thereby finding all of them guilty.\\n\\nIf the reasons stated in the lower court judgment are examined in light of the legal principle set forth above and the record, the lower court’s above determination is proper, and there is no illegality, such as a violation of the rules of logic and experience and thereby going beyond the limits of free evaluation of evidence, or an erroneous understanding of the legal principle regarding non-punishable subsequent acts, as argued in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n3. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, and judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition. Other than the separate opinions of Justice Lee Sang-hoon and Justice Kim Yong-deok, and the dissenting opinions of Justice Lee In-bok and Justice Kim Shin, the opinions of the participating Justices were in accord.\\n\\n4. The separate opinion of Justice Lee Sang-hoon and Justice Kim Yong-deok is as follows.\\n\\nThe majority opinion states that, “even if a person who is in custody of another’s real property consummates an act of embezzlement by, with intent to unlawfully appropriate, completing the registration of the creation of a mortgage on such real property, if thereafter a separate mortgage is created on the same real property so as to add a new risk of infringement of the legal interest and thereby increase the risk of infringement of the legal interest, or if such real property is sold so as to cause a result of infringement of the legal interest irrespective of the existing mortgage, this is beyond the scope that could naturally be anticipated from the mortgage itself, such as a sale by compulsory auction for execution of the original mortgage, and thus adds a new risk of infringement of the legal interest or causes the result of infringement of the legal interest; therefore, absent special circumstances, it cannot be regarded as a non-punishable subsequent act, and it independently constitutes embezzlement,” and thereby intends to alter a number of Supreme Court decisions rendered from 1996 through 2006 to the contrary. However, for the following reasons, we cannot fully concur with the majority opinion.\\n\\na. Embezzlement is an offense that is established when a person who keeps another’s property embezzles that property, and the act of embezzlement as an element of embezzlement means any and all acts that realize an intent to unlawfully appropriate. Accordingly, for example, when a person in possession of another’s property, with the intent to change that possession into possession for himself, performs an objective act by which such intent to appropriate can be externally recognized, the offense of embezzlement is established with respect to the entire property (see Supreme Court Decision 2010DO93 rendered on 2010. 2. 25., etc.).\\n\\nAnd embezzlement, as the majority opinion points out, protects the owner’s right, such as ownership, in another person’s property as its protected legal interest, and it is an offense of danger that is completed if there is a risk of infringement of that legal interest even if the result of such infringement does not occur. Therefore, when a person in custody of another’s real property completes the registration of the creation of a mortgage on such real property with intent to unlawfully appropriate, this indivisibly causes a risk of infringement of ownership or loss of ownership over the entire real property, and thereby the offense of embezzlement is established with respect to the entire real property.\\n\\nMeanwhile, a disposition act concerning embezzled property that is performed after the embezzlement act has been completed does not constitute a separate offense if, within the scope where it can be regarded as having already been assessed by the earlier embezzlement act, it does not involve a new infringement of legal interests, as a so-called non-punishable subsequent act (see Supreme Court Decision 92DO2999 rendered on 1993. 3. 9., Supreme Court Decision 2010DO93 rendered on 2010. 2. 25., etc.).\\n\\nThus, once a preceding embezzlement act consisting of creating a mortgage on another’s real property gives rise to a risk of infringement of ownership over the entire real property and the offense of embezzlement is thereby established, subsequent embezzlement acts, such as a separate act of creating a mortgage on the same real property or an act of selling the same real property, merely cause again a risk of infringement of ownership over the entire real property for which a risk of infringement of ownership had already arisen; therefore, absent special circumstances, it is logically natural to regard them as non-punishable subsequent acts that have already been assessed by the preceding embezzlement act.\\n\\nThe majority opinion does present and explain, using the expression “if, by adding a new risk that could not have been anticipated from the preceding act of disposition, it increases the risk of infringement of the legal interest, or causes the result of infringement of the legal interest by a method unrelated to the preceding act of disposition, absent special circumstances,” a standard for when an act does not become a non-punishable subsequent act. However, in short, according to such a standard, a separate mortgage-creation act on the same real property or an act of selling that real property, carried out after the preceding embezzlement act of creating a mortgage on another’s real property, is, in principle, not a non-punishable subsequent act that has already been assessed by the preceding embezzlement act, but rather independently constitutes embezzlement; the specific reason is said to be that it added a new risk of infringement of the legal interest or caused the result of infringement of the legal interest beyond “the scope that could naturally be anticipated from the mortgage itself, such as a sale by compulsory auction for execution of the original mortgage.” However, because the risk that “could naturally be anticipated from the mortgage itself, such as a sale by compulsory auction for execution of the original mortgage” is ultimately the risk of infringement of ownership over the entire real property at issue, unless the subsequent embezzlement act caused a risk of infringement of a separate ownership right in the real property or infringed a separate ownership right in the real property, it is very awkward not to regard the subsequent embezzlement act, in principle, as a non-punishable subsequent act of the preceding embezzlement act, and one cannot but say that this reverses the rule and the exception.\\n\\nb. Precedent should be changed cautiously. This remains true even if the possibility of changing precedent is institutionally open and it is assumed that the public will bear the change in legal relations that follows. Only then can legal stability be secured and the public be able to use precedent as a guide for decision-making or conduct, so that precedent can truly possess normative force. Where Supreme Court precedents have accumulated in a certain direction for a long period with respect to the interpretation of a legal provision that has not changed, the change of such precedent should be approached even more cautiously. In order to overturn the accumulated views of precedent, there must be circumstances so compelling that the view in question has, with changes in times and circumstances, become greatly contrary to the notion of justice or has markedly deviated from the purport of the relevant legal provision, and that changing it has a value far superior to leaving it intact, such that the sacrifice of legal stability thereby is justified; and it is not wise to overturn the accumulated views of precedent merely because a new legal view appears somewhat better or more reasonable. In particular, in criminal cases, changing precedent so as to newly bring within the scope of punishment through legal interpretation conduct that had previously been viewed as not subject to punishment has an effect no different from punishing already completed acts through retroactive legislation; therefore, in light of the purport and meaning of the principle of non-retroactivity of punishment, it should be exercised with even greater restraint, and it is desirable that it be done only in exceptional cases where the antisocial nature of the conduct is clear, punishability is sufficiently recognized, and an ordinary norm-addressee would think it proper to bear punishment despite the existing precedent. Furthermore, even where existing precedent must be changed due to unavoidable necessity, the scope should, as much as possible, be limited, and lightly reversing the rule and the exception or effecting an across-the-board change is difficult to justify.\\n\\nFor a long period, the Supreme Court has consistently held that where a title trustee of real property creates a mortgage at will on the entrusted real property, the embezzlement act is completed when the registration is completed, and that thereafter creating a mortgage again on the same real property or selling it is, in principle, an act of disposition of embezzled property and constitutes a so-called non-punishable subsequent act that does not involve a new infringement of legal interests, and therefore does not independently constitute embezzlement.\\n\\nHowever, the majority opinion treats as a matter subject to punishment, as a general rule, conduct that had previously been held by the existing Supreme Court decisions to be a non-punishable subsequent act and thus not subject to punishment, by stating that, absent special circumstances, it cannot be regarded as a non-punishable subsequent act and independently constitutes embezzlement. Yet, in light of the elements, protected legal interest, nature of the offense of embezzlement as discussed above, and the case law on non-punishable subsequent acts, the existing Supreme Court view that “a person who is in custody of another’s real property, after completing the registration of the creation of a mortgage on such real property with intent to unlawfully appropriate, creates a separate mortgage on the same real property or sells that real property” should be regarded as a non-punishable subsequent act and thus excluded, in principle, from the scope of punishment, cannot be said to have, with changes in times and circumstances, become greatly contrary to the notion of justice or to have markedly deviated from the purport of the criminal law provision punishing embezzlement. Even if it somewhat conflicts with the notion of justice or does not fully realize the purport of the embezzlement punishment provision, it does not appear that punishing all such subsequent embezzlement acts separately from the preceding embezzlement act has a value so superior as to justify broadly overturning the accumulated existing Supreme Court precedents and thereby undermining the legal stability based thereon, nor does it appear that the antisocial nature or punishability of such subsequent embezzlement acts is so obvious that they must be punished separately from the preceding embezzlement act.\\n\\nTherefore, without sufficiently considering such circumstances, the majority opinion’s attempt to broadly alter the views of the many accumulated Supreme Court decisions solely for the reasons mentioned above is highly unjust and cannot be endorsed.\\n\\nc. However, even under the existing Supreme Court precedents, with respect to a subsequent embezzlement act performed after the ownership infringement caused by the preceding embezzlement act has been restored, embezzlement is independently established (see Supreme Court Decision 78DO2175 rendered on 1978. 11. 28., Supreme Court Decision 96DO1755 rendered on 1996. 11. 29., Supreme Court Decision 2000DO310 rendered on 2000. 3. 24., etc.); therefore, where the risk of ownership infringement caused by the preceding embezzlement act is slight and can be eliminated or restored without excessive cost and effort, yet a subsequent embezzlement act causing a far greater risk is committed, the antisocial nature or punishability of the act is sufficiently recognized, and even from the standpoint of an ordinary person, it would seem proper to bear punishment for it. In such cases, it is necessary exceptionally to treat it not as a non-punishable subsequent act but as subject to punishment. This interpretation would be possible even without changing the existing precedent, and even if one were to think that a change in precedent is necessary in order to adopt such an interpretation, it would suffice to change it only within that scope in a limited manner. In other words, it is difficult to conclude that the Supreme Court decisions the majority opinion seeks to alter necessarily held that subsequent embezzlement acts should be regarded as non-punishable subsequent acts even in cases where, as above, there is a need to treat them as punishable; thus, there is no need to alter them in the first place, and even if there were a need to do so, it would be sufficient to alter them only to the extent that even in such cases subsequent embezzlement acts are regarded as non-punishable subsequent acts. Furthermore, among those Supreme Court decisions, at least Supreme Court Decision 96DO2731 rendered on 1997. 1. 20., Supreme Court Decision 99DO2651 rendered on 1999. 11. 26., Supreme Court Decision 2000DO310 rendered on 2000. 3. 24., Supreme Court Decision 2005DO8699 rendered on 2006. 11. 9., and others concern cases in which the risk of ownership infringement caused by the preceding embezzlement act was considerable, requiring no small amount of cost and effort to eliminate or restore it, or cases in which the risk caused by the subsequent embezzlement act was not so much greater than the risk caused by the preceding embezzlement act; therefore, these are decisions concerning matters in which it is appropriate to regard the subsequent embezzlement act as a non-punishable subsequent act, and it would rather be inappropriate to alter them.\\n\\nIn this case, the act by which Defendant 1, with respect to the land at issue that he had been entrusted with by title trust from the victim clan association and was holding in custody, created a mortgage on 1995. 11. 30. with a maximum secured claim amount of 14,000,000 won, or the act by which he created a mortgage on 2003. 4. 15. with a maximum secured claim amount of 7,500,000 won, caused a risk of infringing the ownership of the entire land at issue, and therefore constitutes embezzlement with respect to the entire land; however, it cannot be said that the risk of ownership infringement thus caused was slight and that the risk could be eliminated or restored without excessive cost and effort. Moreover, the act by which the Defendants thereafter conspired and sold the land at issue to a third party for 193,000,000 won may also be evaluated as having caused a risk far greater than the risk caused by the above preceding act of creating the mortgage, and as involving a new infringement of legal interests; thus, it is not proper to regard it as a non-punishable subsequent act that has already been assessed by the preceding embezzlement act. Accordingly, the conclusion of the lower court judgment that the Defendants’ act of selling the land at issue independently constitutes embezzlement is acceptable.\\n\\nd. For the foregoing reasons, although we do not oppose the conclusion of the majority opinion that all of the Defendants’ appeals should be dismissed, we believe that the reasoning should differ. We state this separately as a separate opinion.\\n\\n5. The dissenting opinion of Justice Lee In-bok and Justice Kim Shin is as follows.\\n\\nThe majority opinion, on the premise that when a new act of disposition is carried out after the offense of embezzlement has been consummated by a preceding act of disposition, the subsequent act of disposition merely serves as a means of completing the risk caused by the preceding act of disposition into an actual infringement of the legal interest, or is something that could naturally be anticipated in the course thereof and does not add any new risk, then the subsequent act of disposition constitutes the so-called non-punishable subsequent act and does not independently constitute an offense, and then holds that even if a person who is in custody of another’s real property has initially completed the offense of embezzlement by creating a mortgage on that real property with intent to unlawfully appropriate, if thereafter that person creates a new mortgage on the same real property or disposes of the entire real property by sale, such conduct results in a new risk or result of infringement of legal interests beyond the scope that could naturally be anticipated from the preceding act of embezzlement, namely the act of creating the mortgage, and therefore, absent special circumstances, it cannot be regarded as a non-punishable subsequent act.\\n\\nHowever, the offense of embezzlement prescribed in Article 355(1) of the Criminal Act is distinguished from breach of trust under paragraph (2) of the same Article, which concerns property benefits, in that it takes the appropriation of property as its constitutive act; and because the intent to unlawfully appropriate property essentially involves a total infringement of the victim’s ownership or other ownership right, if there is an act of embezzlement based on such intent to unlawfully appropriate, the result or risk of infringement of legal interests already necessarily extends to the entirety of the property, which is the object of such ownership or other right. Accordingly, once the above offense of embezzlement is established, it is a logical consequence that no separate result or risk of infringement of legal interests can arise merely because there is a new act of disposition by the custodian of the property.\\n\\nThe majority opinion says that although the preceding act of disposition concerning real property, namely the act of creating a mortgage, constitutes embezzlement, subsequent acts of disposition such as creating a new mortgage on the same real property or selling that real property result in a new risk or result of infringement of legal interests beyond the scope that could naturally be anticipated through the preceding embezzlement act. However, originally, the reason why the act of creating a mortgage on the real property at issue can be assessed as embezzlement with respect to the entirety of that real property is that, in light of the various objective circumstances surrounding that act, the act of creating the mortgage is recognized not as a mere diversion of some part of the property value, but as an objective expression, in the form of property, of the intent to unlawfully appropriate the entire real property at issue. Ultimately, there exists an incompatibility in legal evaluation between saying that a certain act of disposition constitutes embezzlement and saying that additional punishable risk or result of infringement of the legal interest concerning the object of embezzlement is possible.\\n\\nNevertheless, affirming both the establishment of the offense of embezzlement through the preceding act of disposition and the possibility of punishing the subsequent act of disposition can only be seen as the result of disregarding the above contradictory relationship and focusing solely on the need to punish the subsequent act of disposition. Moreover, the majority opinion, by additionally invoking the phrase “special circumstances,” the content and scope of which are difficult to gauge, appears to be adding uncertainty by positing exceptions to the punishability of subsequent acts of disposition, and for that reason it is difficult to agree.\\n\\nIn short, if a person who is in custody of another’s real property creates a mortgage not as an act of diverting some property value of the real property in violation of the relationship of trust, that is, not as an act of breach of trust, but rather with the intent to unlawfully appropriate the relevant real property itself as property, that is, as an act of embezzlement, then the result or risk of infringement of legal interests caused by such embezzlement already extends at that point to the entirety of the ownership rights relating to the real property, and in such a case any additional result or risk of infringement of legal interests caused by a subsequent act of disposition must be regarded as legally impossible.\\n\\nTherefore, in this case, to evaluate, as the lower court did, that the result or risk of infringement of legal interests caused by Defendant’s preceding act of creating a mortgage does not include the result or risk of infringement of legal interests caused by the subsequent act of disposition is possible only where the preceding act was carried out not as an embezzlement act based on intent to unlawfully appropriate the relevant real property, but as an act of breach of trust diverting some property value of that real property. Accordingly, the Supreme Court should not simply accept the lower court’s reasoning that, even if Defendant’s preceding act of creating a mortgage constitutes embezzlement, the subsequent act of disposition may not correspond to a non-punishable subsequent act; rather, it should point out that the possibility of punishment for the subsequent act of disposition can be affirmed only under the condition that the preceding act of creating the mortgage constitutes breach of trust rather than embezzlement, and should reverse the lower court judgment, which takes a different view, so that the lower court may further examine and determine whether the preceding act of disposition was indeed carried out as an act of embezzlement or merely as an act of breach of trust, and then reconsider the guilt or innocence of the facts charged in this case according to the result. And if, among the earlier precedents, there are any that held, in cases where a person in custody of another’s real property created a mortgage in favor of a third party, that intent to unlawfully appropriate is unconditionally presumed and embezzlement is established without specifically considering the intent or the nature of the act, then those precedents should also be altered to the extent they conflict with the legal principle stated above.\\n\\nFor the foregoing reasons, since I do not concur with the majority opinion, I state my dissent."}

{"[2012DO1895]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Ideal concurrence refers to a case in which one act substantially satisfies several elements of an offense, and statutory concurrence refers to a case in which one act outwardly appears to correspond to the elements of several offenses but in substance constitutes only one offense; whether it is in substance one offense or several offenses must be determined by considering the constituent-element evaluation and the protected legal interests (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DO6033, decided April 8, 2003; Supreme Court Decision 2012DO6503, decided August 30, 2012). The so-called “non-punishable accompanying conduct” falls within an absorption relationship, which is one form of statutory concurrence, and refers to a case in which, when the actor commits a certain offense, although it is not logically necessary, another constituent element is generally and typically satisfied, and because the unlawfulness or culpability inherent in that constituent element is minor compared with the principal offense, punishment is not separately considered.\\n\\nThe offense of obstruction of business and the offense of assault differ in their constituent elements and protected legal interests, and the formation of the offense of obstruction of business does not generally and typically involve an act of assault against a person, nor can an assaultive act be said to be so minor as not to be separately considered compared with obstruction of business; therefore, even if an act of assault against the victim became a means of committing the offense of obstruction of business against the same victim, such assaultive act cannot be deemed to constitute so-called “non-punishable accompanying conduct” and to be in an absorption relationship with the offense of obstruction of business.\\n\\n2. a. The court below, on the grounds stated in its holding, maintained the first-instance judgment that found not guilty the charge of violation of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (joint assault) among the facts charged in this case against the Defendants, on the ground that, in the course of the Defendants’ obstructing Victims 1 and 2’s taxi operation, there was an assault against the victims as stated in this part of the indictment; that this constituted part of the actus reus of the offense of obstruction of business, namely, “an act of obstructing business by force”; and that it was absorbed into the offense of obstruction of business, so that only one offense of obstruction of business was established and no separate offense of violation of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (joint assault) was established.\\n\\nb. However, examining the reasons of the court below’s judgment in light of the legal principles stated above, even if the assaultive act carried out in order to obstruct the victims’ taxi operation became a means of the offense of obstruction of business against the victims, such assaultive act is not ordinarily and typically attendant upon the formation of the offense of obstruction of business, and nor can it be said to be so minor as not to be separately considered compared with the offense of obstruction of business; accordingly, it cannot be said that the Defendants’ assaultive act is absorbed into the offense of obstruction of business and does not constitute a separate offense.\\n\\nMeanwhile, according to the evidence lawfully admitted by the court below, although the Defendants obstructed the victims’ taxi operation by means of joint assault, no circumstance is shown indicating that they obstructed the taxi operation by any other means; therefore, the single act of the Defendants’ joint assault corresponds to a case in which the elements of the offense of violation of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (joint assault) and the offense of obstruction of business are both satisfied, and the two offenses should be regarded as being in a relationship of ideal concurrence.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, by regarding the two offenses as being in an absorption relationship and finding the facts charged concerning the Defendants’ violation of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (joint assault) not guilty, erred in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the number of offenses of the offense of obstruction of business and the offense of violation of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (joint assault), and thereby misapplied the law. The ground of appeal pointing out this point is well-founded.\\n\\nc. Therefore, the portion of the judgment of the court below concerning the offense of violation of the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (joint assault) against the Defendants, and the portion concerning the offense of obstruction of business, which is in a relationship of ideal concurrence with it, must be reversed; accordingly, the entire portion concerning Defendant 4 must be reversed. Meanwhile, since the court below treated the offense of obstruction of business against Defendants 1, 2, 3, and 5 as multiple offenses in concurrence under the former part of Article 37 of the Criminal Act together with the remaining offenses against those Defendants and imposed a single sentence, the entire portion of the judgment of the court below concerning those Defendants must also be reversed.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further proceedings and determination. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2021DO16876]": "We determine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. If, by taking away, concealing, or damaging his own property, which was the object of the rights of several persons, he interfered with the exercise of the rights of those several persons, then the crime of interference with the exercise of rights is constituted separately for each right holder, and each offense stands in a relationship of ideal concurrence with the others. Where several persons entitled to a reserved share obtained a provisional attachment order for real property in order to preserve their respective claims for return of the reserved portion, and the registration of provisional attachment was completed, the said real property becomes the object of provisional attachment to preserve execution of each reserved-share claimant’s claim for return of the reserved portion, and this does not differ depending on whether the reserved-share claimants applied for provisional attachment individually or jointly.\\nMeanwhile, Article 328(1) of the Criminal Act provides, “A crime under Article 323 between lineal blood relatives, spouses, cohabiting relatives, cohabiting family members, or between their spouses shall be exempt from punishment.” Whether the requirements for exemption from punishment under the above provision are met must be examined for each offense.\\n\\n2. The court below, on the grounds stated in its judgment, found all the charged facts against the Defendants guilty, and then, regarding the portion of interference with the exercise of rights against Victim E among them, viewed it as falling within an offense committed among relatives, thereby reversing the first-instance judgment that determined a single punishment for all the charged facts or suspended the pronouncement of that punishment, and determined punishment only for the portion of interference with the exercise of rights against Victim D or suspended the pronouncement of that punishment, while applying Article 328(1) of the Criminal Act and exempting punishment for the portion of interference with the exercise of rights against Victim E. If the reasons of the court below’s judgment are examined in light of the legal principles seen above and the evidence properly admitted, there is no error in the court below’s determination that violated the rules of logic and experience and exceeded the bounds of free evaluation of evidence, or, as argued in the grounds for final appeal, misapprehended the legal principles concerning the effect of the provisional attachment order or the special rule of exemption for crimes among relatives.\\n\\n3. Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (X) regarding intent and negligence? (Where there is a dispute, case law applies.)
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2002DO4293]": "1. Summary of the Holding of the Lower Court Judgment\\n\\nThe gist of the facts charged in this case is that Defendant 1, who was the Head of County No. 1, and Defendant 2, who was the general affairs manager of the Non-party Limited Company, a farming association corporation (hereinafter referred to as the “Non-party Limited Company”), conspired together and, while knowing that the proposed waste landfill site stated in the waste disposal business plan submitted by the said Non-party Limited Company consisted of conserved forests and farmland, etc., and thus was a matter beyond the authority of the county head under the Farmland Act, the National Land Utilization and Management Act, the Forest Act, and other relevant statutes, and that the construction of a waste landfill was impossible because it was in the upstream area of the Okjeong Lake water source, so that the business plan was inappropriate, nevertheless, around 2000. 11. 15., in fact, after the aforementioned notice of inappropriateness had been issued, the Non-party Limited Company did not newly submit a waste disposal business plan to the County Office of County No. 1, no new review by the officials in charge of practical matters was conducted within the county office, and there had been no notice from County No. 1 to the Non-party Limited Company that the waste disposal business plan was suitable (conditional), but for the purpose of utterance/use, they falsely prepared one sheet of a “Notice of Suitability (Conditional) for Waste Disposal Business Plan” (hereinafter referred to as the “Notice in This Case”), as if the document had been prepared after review by the internal officials in charge and lawfully notified to the other party, thereby preparing one false official document in the name of the Head of County No. 1; and on the 24th of the same month, when Defendant 2 submitted bidding documents for the waste transfer landfill construction project to the official in charge of the Finance Division of Jeonju City Hall, he attached and submitted one copy to the bidding documents as if the Notice in This Case were a genuine document, thereby uttering it, and moreover, by attaching and submitting a copy of the Notice in This Case, which had been falsely prepared in this manner, they interfered by fraudulent means with Jeonju City’s work of screening bidding companies for the waste transfer landfill construction project.\\n\\nIn response, the lower court held that since the Non-party Limited Company, after first submitting the business plan, had received a notice of inappropriateness and a request for supplementation of the plan from County No. 1 in 10. of the same year, it had revised or supplemented the waste disposal business plan on two occasions and submitted the revised or supplemented business plans to County No. 1, even though the Non-party Limited Company did not submit an independent business plan to County No. 1 in 10. of the same year and did not again submit a business plan after receiving the notice of inappropriateness on 2000. 10. 27., the statement itself that “as a result of reviewing the waste disposal business plan submitted in 2000. 10.” cannot be said to be false; and furthermore, since the nominal issuer of the official document in this case is, in any event, the Head of County No. 1, and the said official document is not a document proving that it was reviewed by the officials in charge of practical matters, if Defendant 1 prepared the official document in this case in order to indicate an intention to give a notice of conditional suitability with respect to the waste disposal business plan being promoted by the Non-party Limited Company, on the condition that residents’ complaints be resolved and the requirements prescribed by the Waste Management Act be complied with and implemented, then even if there was a deficiency in the internal procedures and, as alleged in the facts charged, only Defendant 1 signed and sealed the official document without the signatures and seals of the officials in charge of practical matters, the official document in this case cannot be said to be false in that “no new review by the officials in charge of practical matters was conducted within the county office”; and also, the fact that “County No. 1 did not issue a notice to the Non-party Limited Company that the waste disposal business plan was suitable (conditional)” is a matter concerning how the official document in this case was used after it was prepared, and has no relation to whether the official document in this case is false, and therefore the official document in this case cannot be regarded as false. Accordingly, the lower court found that the official document in this case was not false, and further held that, as long as the charge of making a false official document cannot be recognized as above, the charge of uttering the false official document and the charge of obstruction of performance of official duties by fraudulent means based thereon likewise cannot be recognized; and also found that there was no other evidence sufficient to recognize that they interfered by fraudulent means with Jeonju City’s work of screening bidding companies for the waste transfer landfill construction project by submitting a copy of the official document in this case. Accordingly, it rendered a judgment of acquittal on all of the facts charged against the Defendants.\\n\\n2. Judgment of the Supreme Court\\n\\nA. Regarding the part concerning Defendants’ offense of making a false official document and the offense of uttering the same\\n\\nHowever, it is difficult to agree with the lower court’s conclusion that the Notice in This Case cannot be regarded as false and its judgment of acquittal on Defendants’ offense of making a false official document and the offense of uttering the same for the following reasons.\\n\\nSince the offense of making a false official document is established when a false statement contrary to the truth is entered in an official document, even if an official document is prepared by intentionally misapplying the law, the offense of making a false official document cannot be established if there is no falsity in the factual basis that formed the premise of the application of such law (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2000DO1858, decided on 2000. 6. 27.). However, a notice of suitability for a waste disposal business plan under Article 26(2) of the Waste Management Act is not merely a document stating that a waste disposal business is permitted in accordance with the relevant statutes, but a document confirming or certifying that the waste disposal business plan submitted by a person intending to engage in waste disposal business pursuant to Article 26(1) of the Waste Management Act conforms to the Waste Management Act and the provisions of the relevant statutes; therefore, if such a notice is prepared stating that the waste disposal business plan is suitable while knowing that it does not conform to the provisions of the relevant statutes, then such notice cannot but be regarded as a false official document.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Defendants well knew that the proposed waste landfill site stated in the waste disposal business plan submitted by the Non-party Limited Company was not only impossible to use for a waste landfill under the relevant statutes such as the Farmland Act, the National Land Utilization and Management Act, and the Forest Act because it consisted of conserved forests and farmland, but also even more impossible to use as a waste landfill because it was in the upstream area of the Okjeong Lake water source, and thus the business plan was not suitable; nevertheless, by preparing the Notice in This Case to the effect that it was suitable, on the condition only that civil complaints be resolved and that the standards for facilities, equipment, technical capability, etc. under the Waste Management Act be satisfied, it can be recognized that the Notice in This Case was ultimately prepared with contents stating that it was suitable under the relevant statutes such as the Farmland Act, the National Land Utilization and Management Act, and the Forest Act. It can also be recognized that the Defendants sufficiently knew that the Notice in This Case would be submitted as bidding documents to Jeonju City Hall, or at least used to other persons such as complainants. If so, the Defendants, for the purpose of utterance/use, cannot but be regarded as having falsely prepared the Notice in This Case, which confirms or certifies the fact that the waste disposal business plan submitted by the Non-party Limited Company conforms to the provisions of the relevant statutes; and although the prosecutor’s facts charged are not entirely clear, the portion of the facts charged stating that “County No. 1 did not issue a notice to the Non-party Limited Company that the waste disposal business plan was suitable (conditional)” can sufficiently be viewed as meaning, in the end, that the Notice in This Case is false in the above sense.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court, relying only on the reasons stated above, held that the Notice in This Case could not be regarded as a false official document and acquitted the Defendants of the offense of making a false official document, and further held that, insofar as the Notice in This Case is not false, the Defendants’ offense of uttering the same also could not be established and likewise acquitted them. It cannot but be said that the lower court either misunderstood the legal doctrine concerning false official documents or erred in fact-finding, thereby committing a violation that affected the conclusion of the judgment. The ground of appeal that appears to include the purport of pointing this out is well-founded (provided, however, that according to the record, Defendant 1 alleges in his defense that he prepared the Notice in This Case for Defendant 2 only after receiving a promise that it would not be submitted to Jeonju City, although it might be shown to complainants, and there are also traces that he actually attempted to prevent Defendant 2 from submitting the Notice in This Case to Jeonju City; if so, it appears necessary to examine whether Defendant 1’s above defense is true and whether he lacked intent as to the part of uttering the false official document charged in this case).\\n\\nB. Regarding the part concerning Defendants’ offense of obstruction of performance of official duties by fraudulent means\\n\\nIn the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties by fraudulent means, “fraudulent means” means causing the other party to form a misconception, mistake, or ignorance, and using that misconception, mistake, or ignorance, for the purpose of achieving the actor’s object of conduct; this offense is established only when the other party acts or disposes based on such misconception, mistake, or ignorance, and if the criminal act did not go so far as to obstruct a specific performance of official duties or make it actually difficult and remained at the attempt stage, it cannot be punished as obstruction of performance of official duties by fraudulent means (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2000DO102, decided on 2000. 3. 24.).\\n\\nReviewing in light of the record, although it was possible that Defendant 2 attached and submitted the Notice in This Case to the bidding documents and thereby interfered by fraudulent means with Jeonju City Hall’s work of screening bidding companies for the waste transfer landfill construction project, before such submission, Defendant 1 notified Jeonju City Hall that the Notice in This Case was invalid, so it is apparent that there was no possibility whatsoever that the official in charge at Jeonju City Hall would be in a state of misconception, mistake, or ignorance. If so, even if the Notice in This Case was submitted, it cannot be said that the matter ever went so far as to obstruct a specific performance of official duties by Jeonju City or make it actually difficult; therefore, it is clear that the above act cannot be punished as obstruction of performance of official duties by fraudulent means. Accordingly, although there is an error in the statement of reasons, the lower court’s judgment acquitting the Defendants of the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties by fraudulent means is, in conclusion, correct. The appeal on this point must therefore be dismissed.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, among the lower court judgment, the part concerning Defendants’ offense of making a false official document and the offense of uttering the same is reversed, and this part of the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination; the remaining appeal is dismissed. The judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2022DO3413]": "1. We determine the grounds for appeal (the statements in a written opinion submitted after the expiration of the period for filing the statement of grounds for appeal are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for appeal).\\n\\nThe crime of false accusation is established where the facts reported for the purpose of causing another person to be subjected to criminal punishment or disciplinary punishment are false facts contrary to objective truth. The intent required for false accusation need not necessarily be direct intent; conditional intent is sufficient. Accordingly, not only where the reporting person files a report of facts that he or she believes to be false, but also where the reporting person files a report of facts without being convinced that they are true, such intent may be found. In addition, in the crime of false accusation, the purpose of causing criminal punishment is satisfied if, while making a false report, there is awareness that another person will thereby be subjected to criminal punishment, and it is not even necessary to wish for the occurrence of that result; therefore, so long as the reporting person knowingly files a report containing false content, it cannot be said that there was no intent to falsely accuse on the ground that the purpose was to have a necessary investigation conducted, etc. (see Supreme Court Decision 94DO3271, decided December 12, 1995). Also, if, even according to the objective facts known to the reporting person, he or she did not recognize that the reported facts were false or that there was a possibility that they were false, the intent to falsely accuse may be negated; however, this does not include cases where, despite recognizing from the objective facts known to him or her that the reported facts were false or possibly false, the reporting person disregards that recognition and unconditionally believes his or her own assertion to be correct (see Supreme Court Decision 2000DO1908, 2000GAMDO62, decided July 4, 2000).\\n\\n2. For the reasons stated in its opinion, the lower court affirmed the first-instance judgment convicting the Defendant, rejecting the Defendant's argument that the complaint filed by the Defendant alleging that a pharmacist had instructed an unqualified employee to sell medicines to an unspecified number of patients or had actually sold medicines to the Defendant, etc., was false and contrary to the objective factual circumstances, and that the Defendant had the intent for false accusation, at least in the form of conditional intent, by recognizing the falsity or the possibility of falsity.\\n\\nExamining the reasons for the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the properly admitted evidence, there is no error in the lower court's determination that violated logic and the rules of experience, exceeded the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, or misapprehended the legal principles concerning the intent for false accusation, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as follows by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[88DO650]": "The grounds of appeal filed by the Defendants and the court-appointed defense counsel are examined together.\\n\\nBased on the evidence adopted in the first-instance judgment cited by the court below, the court below found that Defendant <REDACTED>, who had long harbored severe resentment because the victim <REDACTED> had been making teasing remarks such as asking the wife of the co-defendant, who was slightly mentally retarded, to give him milk, on 1987. 8. 8. at around 23:30, while drinking with the victim at the local cooperative store in <REDACTED> District, Goesan-gun, Chungbuk, heard from the non-indicted <REDACTED>, the owner of the said cooperative store, that even during the daytime that day the victim had teased the wife of the co-defendant by asking her for milk, and after striking the victim’s cheeks several times and otherwise assaulting him, together with Defendant <REDACTED> who had come there, and the victim, the three of them were going to nearby <REDACTED> to drink more liquor when, upon reaching the farm road in front of the village, the heavily intoxicated victim made abusive remarks such as pretending with his fingers as if he were going to gouge out eyes and saying, “You bastard, if you fool around, I’ll kill you,” whereupon Defendant <REDACTED> struck the victim’s cheeks several times with the palm of his hand, and Defendant <REDACTED> struck the victim’s abdomen twice, causing the victim to fall down, then, with anger suddenly flaring up, decided to kill the victim, and Defendant <REDACTED> climbed onto the victim’s abdomen and struck the victim’s chest twice with a stone measuring 20 centimeters in width and 10 centimeters in length (Exhibit No. 1), and Defendant <REDACTED> also joined in and struck the victim’s head twice with a stone measuring 13 centimeters in width and 7 centimeters in length (Exhibit No. 2), after which they again raised the victim to his feet and Defendant <REDACTED> struck the victim’s abdomen once, causing him to fall backward, and when the victim lost consciousness and went limp due to a concussion, etc., mistakenly believing him to be dead and for the purpose of secretly burying the corpse and destroying evidence, they dragged the victim to a stream bank about 150 meters away from there, dug a pit with a shovel, buried the victim, and thereby caused the victim to die of asphyxiation. Upon comparison with the record, the above finding is proper, and there is no illegality in that the court misapprehended the facts in violation of the rules of evidence as contended in the grounds of appeal. Furthermore, even if, as above, the factual relationship is such that the victim did not die directly from the assault committed by the Defendants with intent to kill, but died from the burial act performed for the purpose of destroying traces of the crime, when the entire process is viewed in outline, the initially foreseen fact of the victim’s killing was ultimately realized, and therefore the Defendants cannot escape liability for murder; accordingly, the court below’s action in upholding the first-instance judgment that convicted the Defendants of murder in the same purport is proper, and there is no error whatsoever therein.\\n\\nAlso, according to the record, it is acknowledged that Defendant <REDACTED> was somewhat intoxicated at the time of the above offense, but it does not appear that, as a result, that Defendant reached the degree of diminished mental and physical capacity; therefore, the argument on this point is also without merit.\\n\\nAnd the argument that the sentence imposed by the court below is excessive in this case, in which a sentence of imprisonment of less than 10 years was imposed, cannot, in light of Article 383 Item 4 of the Criminal Procedure Act, constitute a lawful ground of appeal. All of the arguments are without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeals by the Defendants are all dismissed, and by crediting each Defendant with a portion of the days of detention after appeal toward the principal sentence, it is adjudged as follows by the unanimous opinion of the participating judges.\\n\\n1988. 6. 28."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning Article 27 of the Criminal Act (Impossible Attempt) is correct? (In case of dispute, according to precedents)
A: Where a person, under the mistaken belief that adultery is criminally punishable, commits adultery, this constitutes an impossible attempt.
B: The impossibility of the occurrence of the result does not mean that, by the nature of the criminal act, realization of the elements of the offense is impossible in any case.
C: Dangerousness is determined objectively and ex post facto, in accordance with the general rules of experience, on the basis of the circumstances recognized by the actor at the time of the act and the circumstances that an ordinary person could have recognized.
D: Where a civil action for damages seeking payment of litigation costs is filed with the intent to fraudulently obtain litigation costs, impossible attempt of the crime of litigation fraud is established.
E: Where A, with intent to commit murder, attempted to have B ingest a lethal dose of poison, but by mistake caused B to ingest an amount of poison markedly below a lethal dose, and then repented and gave B an antidote, according to the view that requires a causal relationship between the preventive act and the non-occurrence of the result, an impossible attempt of murder is established.
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2005DO8105]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\nAs the standard for determining an impossible offense, the determination of dangerousness must be made by considering the circumstances recognized by the Defendant at the time of the act, and then asking whether, objectively, according to the judgment of the average person, there was a possibility that the result would occur (see Supreme Court Decision 77DO4049 dated March 28, 1978). On the other hand, since under the Civil Procedure Act a claim for litigation costs is prescribed to be made through the procedure for determination of the amount of litigation costs, seeking payment of litigation costs by a lawsuit such as an action for damages without following the above procedure would be an improper lawsuit lacking benefit of action and thus cannot be permitted. Accordingly, even if a party filed an action for damages seeking payment of litigation costs with the intent to embezzle litigation costs, objectively, according to the judgment of the average person having legal knowledge regarding the method of claiming litigation costs, there is no possibility that the result will occur, and dangerousness cannot be recognized.\\n\\nOn the same purport, the court below, based on the evidence admitted, recognized that although the Defendant had already received 1,000,000 won from Nonparty 1 through Nonparty 2 under the name of litigation costs, the Defendant filed an action for damages against Nonparty 1 seeking payment of an amount equivalent to litigation costs relating to several prior lawsuits that the Defendant had brought against Nonparty 1, and then, after receiving a recommendation from the judge in charge to determine the litigation costs through the procedure for determination of the amount of litigation costs, withdrew the said action; and, after finding such facts, held that the action for damages in this case filed by the Defendant is an improper lawsuit lacking the benefit of action and cannot escape dismissal, so that the Defendant could not prevail. If so, the Defendant’s act of litigation fraud in this part is not only impossible to bring about the result due to an error in the means of execution, but also lacks dangerousness; thus it cannot be viewed as falling under impossible attempt of the crime of litigation fraud, and ultimately it falls under a case in which no crime is constituted. Therefore, the measure of the court below in rendering a judgment of not guilty against the Defendant on this part was correct, and there is no illegality such as an error of law regarding dangerousness in impossible attempt as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and it is so adjudged as follows by the unanimous opinion of the Supreme Court Justices involved."}

{"[2019DO97]": "We consider the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Background of the Case\\n\\na. The gist of the facts charged in this case is that the Defendant and the non-indicted person, who resided in Vietnam, agreed that if the non-indicted person sent methamphetamine, a psychotropic drug (hereinafter referred to as “Philopon”), to Korea, the Defendant would receive it in Korea and sell it; that the non-indicted person, around October 21, 2017, concealed 30 g of Philopon in Vietnam by placing it inside a “Water Ball” toy and dissolving it by pouring water into it, and then sent it by international mail using an aircraft; and that the Defendant, around October 23, 2017, received in Korea the Water Ball concealing the Philopon that had been brought into the country through Incheon International Airport at around that time, thereby, in conspiracy with the non-indicted person, importing 30 g of Philopon.\\n\\nb. The trial court rejected the Defendant’s defense that the Philopon had not been dissolved in the Water Ball sent by the non-indicted person, and while convicting the Defendant of Violation of the Act on the Control of Narcotics, Etc. (psychotropic substances), it found the Defendant not guilty in its reasoning of Violation of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes (psychotropic substances), on the ground that there was no proof that the value of the imported Philopon was KRW 5 million or more.\\n\\nc. Unlike the trial court, the court below found the foregoing facts charged not guilty on the ground that, based solely on the evidence submitted by the prosecutor, there was insufficient evidence to show that the liquid contained in the Water Ball sent by the non-indicted person contained dissolved Philopon.\\n\\nHowever, the court below further held that the Defendant and the non-indicted person conspired to bring the Water Ball containing dissolved Philopon into the country by international mail and sell it, and that the Defendant had commenced the execution of the offense of importing Philopon by informing the non-indicted person of the domestic address to which the Philopon was to be sent and having the non-indicted person send it, but that because the Water Ball sent by the non-indicted person did not contain Philopon, the offense remained at the attempted stage; and that if the non-indicted person had actually sent Philopon, there would have been a risk of the result of importation of Philopon occurring, so the Defendant’s conduct constituted an impossible attempt at the offense of importing Philopon. On that basis, the court below found the Defendant guilty without going through the procedures for amendment of the indictment.\\n\\n2. The Supreme Court’s Determination\\n\\na. Article 27 of the Criminal Act (impossible attempt) provides: “A person shall be punished if there is danger even though the occurrence of the result is impossible due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution. However, the punishment may be mitigated or remitted.” An impossible attempt means a case in which, although the actor has criminal intent and there is an act that may be deemed commencement of execution, there is from the outset no possibility of the occurrence of the result or infringement of a legal interest due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, but the actor is punished as an attempted offender because of the dangerousness of the act (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DO2313, rendered on October 23, 1998). Here, “the occurrence of the result is impossible” means that realization of the constituent elements is impossible under any circumstances due to the nature of the criminal act.\\n\\nb. The risk of harm arising from the importation of psychotropic substances prescribed by the Act on the Control of Narcotics, Etc. occurs upon landing or bringing the psychotropic substances ashore, and the offense is completed when those substances are unloaded from a vessel or aircraft or brought onto land (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DO2734, rendered on November 27, 1998). And, in a case such as this one, where psychotropic substances are imported through international mail, etc., it may be deemed that the commencement of execution of the offense occurs when a person residing in Korea is designated as the addressee and a mail item containing psychotropic substances is submitted to the post office, etc. of the sending country. Therefore, even if the Defendant informed the non-indicted person of the domestic address to which the Philopon was to be sent, unless it is established that the non-indicted person submitted to the post office, etc. of the sending country a mail item containing Philopon, such act of the Defendant and others may be regarded as preparatory conduct for the importation of psychotropic substances, but it cannot be said that this alone constitutes commencement of execution of the importation of psychotropic substances.\\n\\nc. The Defendant intended to import Philopon from the non-indicted person residing in Vietnam by dissolving the Philopon in the liquid inside the Water Ball, concealing it, and then receiving it through international mail. It is manifest that such conduct is not a case in which the occurrence of the result is impossible due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, under the nature of the offense.\\n\\nd. Nevertheless, the court below determined that an impossible attempt of Violation of the Act on the Control of Narcotics, Etc. (psychotropic substances) was established against the Defendant on the basis of the circumstances as determined in its holding. The judgment of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misunderstanding the legal doctrine on impossible attempt under Article 27 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[77DO4049]": "We examine the grounds of appeal submitted by defense counsel.\\n\\nThe judgment below, adopting the trial court judgment, found that the defendant mixed ephedrine, glacial acetic acid, and other chemical agents, heated them to 80°C-90°C, and manufactured 1 kilogram of methamphetamine (commonly called philopon), but, due to his lack of manufacturing skill and experience, produced only methylephedrine hydrochloride rather than a finished philopon product, and thus remained at the stage of an attempt; and it held to the effect that, in order to produce methamphetamine with the methylephedrine hydrochloride prepared by him, ephedrine hydrochloride must be used as a raw material, and although it may be acknowledged that ephedrine hydrochloride can be produced from methylephedrine hydrochloride, the defendant's act can by no means be an impossible crime.\\n\\nUpon review, the judgment below was based on the defendant's statements made during the investigation and to the effect that he intended to make philopon and, by making it by the method originally stated, unexpectedly obtained another substance, methylephedrine hydrochloride, and therefore it was an attempt; however, from the contents of the respective interrogation records of witnesses Kim Jeong-hyeon and Lee Yeong-suk prepared by the prosecutor, the fact that the defendant purchased 1.5 kilograms of methylephedrine hydrochloride from the said Kim Jeong-hyeon for 30 man-won can be sufficiently recognized, and according to the record methylephedrine hydrochloride is an over-the-counter medicine, a cold remedy and antipyretic, so the purchase of such methylephedrine hydrochloride cannot be deemed the commencement of execution of the manufacture of a habit-forming drug. The judgment below attached importance to the defendant's confession, but under the above circumstances in which the fact of purchasing methylephedrine hydrochloride can be recognized, when the defendant's explanation at trial that he had confessed under coercive interrogation during the investigation is also taken into account, it would be contrary to experience to believe the confession and treat it as evidence. Moreover, unless it is recognized that what was purchased is different from the substance produced as found by the judgment below, it is our experience that it cannot be regarded as the same substance. If so, in recognizing that there was commencement of execution in this case, the judgment below either erred in its factual findings by evaluating evidence in violation of the rules of experience or, by misunderstanding the legal principle of commencement of execution, left an illegality affecting the result; accordingly, the portion of the argument asserting this point is well-founded, and without needing to consider the other points, it is well-founded, and the judgment below cannot avoid reversal.\\n\\nNext, we turn to the alternative holding. The judgment below held that if the methylephedrine hydrochloride recognized as having been produced by the defendant undergoes chemical action, the methyl group can be removed, and then it can become ephedrine hydrochloride and thus serve as a raw material for the manufacture of philopon, so there is dangerousness and it is not an impossible crime. The holding that, if dangerousness is recognized, it cannot be an impossible crime is correct, but there is the following illegality.\\n\\nThat is, from the evidence cited by the court below, it may be recognized that it cannot be recognized that the hydrochloride group can be removed from methylephedrine hydrochloride, so the lower court's finding cannot escape the illegality of insufficient examination or erroneous interpretation of the evidence, and in order to judge the dangerousness of the defendant's act in this case, the circumstances the defendant recognized at the time of the act, that is, as found by the lower court, namely the circumstance of mixing ephedrine with glacial acetic acid and heating it to 80°C-90°C, should have been examined as to whether, objectively, there was a possibility of causing the result from the standpoint of an ordinary person (a scientifically informed layperson) who knows the pharmaceutical manufacturing method; yet, without this inquiry procedure, in other words, because no reason was stated as to why it was dangerous, the measure finding dangerousness contains an illegality of lack of reasons or a mistake in misunderstanding the legal doctrine of impossible crime or dangerousness, so the portion of the argument making this point cannot be said to be without merit.\\n\\nFor the foregoing reasons, by unanimous opinion, the Court renders judgment as stated in the disposition."}

question: 14th Korean Bar Examination, Criminal Law, Multiple-Choice Question 5. Which of the following statements are correct? (In cases of dispute, according to precedent) (a) In a situation where a married couple is living separately during divorce proceedings, even if spouse A, in order to exercise the right of visitation and contact, brought child A (5 years old), who had been living abroad with the other spouse B, into the Republic of Korea, and, although the visitation period had expired, did not return the child to B and, by failing to comply with the court's order to hand over the child, severed the relationship between child A and B, if A lawfully brought child A, this cannot be regarded as abduction; therefore, the offense of kidnapping a minor is not established. (b) An act of abandonment in the offense of abandonment consists in endangering life or body by leaving a person in need of help in a state without protection; therefore, it is established not only by an act but also by an omission, and, in addition to the possibility of creating danger to the life or body of the person abandoned, it requires that there be no possibility of protection whatsoever. (c) The offense of arrest is a continuing offense, and the act of arrest reaches completion only when there is a temporal duration sufficient to clearly recognize that it restrains a person's personal liberty; if the restraint on personal liberty does not reach such a level and remains merely temporary, only an attempted offense of arrest is established. (d) Even if the actor made some demand to the other party on the basis of a profession or position that can influence the other party officially or in fact, one must not immediately conclude that the demand itself constitutes a threat of harm for the establishment of the offense of coercion. (e) In order for the offense of violation of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment, etc. of Sexual Crimes (threat by using filmed materials, etc.) to be established, it is not necessary that the actor threaten by directly presenting the filmed materials, etc. to the victim, but it does require that the actor possess the filmed materials, etc. or be in a position to disseminate them at the time of the threat.
label: D

{"[2016DO18713]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Determination on the defendants’ grounds for appeal\\n\\na.
