As to Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe offense of arrest is a crime that directly and actually imposes restraint on a person’s body and deprives that person of freedom of bodily movement, and the time when execution begins is when an act is commenced, with intent to arrest, that actually infringes another person’s freedom of bodily movement (see Supreme Court Decision 2018. 2. 28. rendered 2017DO21249).\\n\\nThe lower court, based on the circumstances as found in its opinion, affirmed the first-instance judgment that found the defendants guilty of attempted arrest, on the ground that the defendants had initiated execution of the offense of arrest by commencing acts that infringed Non-Party 1’s freedom of bodily movement, such as pulling Non-Party 1 by the arm or pushing the back, thereby dragging Non-Party 1 away, and that the defendants also had intent to arrest Non-Party 1; the lower court accordingly rejected the defendants’ arguments in their grounds for appeal on this point.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles reviewed above and the duly admitted evidence, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning the objective and subjective constituent elements of the offense of arrest, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nb. As to Ground 2 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe lower court, based on the circumstances as found in its opinion, rejected the defendants’ arguments in their grounds for appeal by determining that Non-Party 1 could not be deemed to have expressly or impliedly consented to the defendants’ act of arrest, nor could it be deemed that the defendants proceeded with the arrest act under a mistaken belief that Non-Party 1 had consented.\\n\\nIn light of the duly admitted evidence, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning the victim’s acquiescence, as asserted in the grounds for appeal, or exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in contravention of the rules of logic and experience.\\n\\nc. As to Ground 3 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe lower court determined, for the reasons stated in its opinion, that (1) it could not be deemed obvious that Non-Party 1 had committed a crime or that there was a necessity to arrest Non-Party 1 as a flagrant offender, and thus the defendants’ act of attempting to arrest Non-Party 1 could not be deemed a lawful act under statutes and therefore a justifiable act; (2) it could not be deemed a justifiable act not contrary to social norms because the appropriateness of the means and method was not recognized and it could not be deemed an urgent and unavoidable measure; and (3) it could not be deemed self-defense because the defendants’ act could not be deemed socially appropriate as a defensive act.\\n\\nIn light of the duly admitted evidence and the relevant legal principles stated in the lower court’s opinion, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the above determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning justifiable acts and self-defense, which are grounds excluding wrongfulness, as asserted in the grounds for appeal, or having contradictions in the reasons for the judgment.\\n\\nd. As to Ground 4 of the grounds for appeal\\n\\nThe lower court, based on the circumstances as found in its opinion, determined that even if the defendants themselves mistakenly believed that their conduct was not criminal, there was no justifiable reason for such mistaken belief; accordingly, the defendants’ conduct did not constitute a mistake of law prescribed in Article 16 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\nIn light of the duly admitted evidence and the relevant legal principles stated in the lower court’s opinion, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the above determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning a mistake of law prescribed in Article 16 of the Criminal Act, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n2. Determination on the prosecutor’s grounds for appeal\\n\\na. As to the portion concerning obstruction of performance of official duties by the defendants on 2013. 7. 25.\\n\\n1) Regarding the argument that it was lawful as an order-maintenance line pursuant to the Act on Assembly and Demonstration\\n\\ni) Article 2, Item 5 of the Act on Assembly and Demonstration (hereinafter referred to as the “Assembly and Demonstration Act”) provides: “The term ‘order-maintenance line’ means a boundary marker, such as a cordon, barricade, or lane marking, established by the chief of the competent police station or the chief of the provincial police agency by demarcating a place or marching route for an assembly or demonstration in order to protect a lawful assembly or demonstration and maintain order or ensure smooth traffic flow.” In addition, Article 13(1) of the Assembly and Demonstration Act provides: “If the chief of the competent police agency deems it necessary for the protection of assemblies and demonstrations and for the maintenance of public order, he/she may establish an order-maintenance line by setting the minimum necessary scope.” Article 13(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Assembly and Demonstration, issued pursuant to the delegation under the above provision (hereinafter referred to as the “Enforcement Decree of the Assembly and Demonstration Act”), enumerates in each item the cases in which an order-maintenance line may be established. Meanwhile, Article 24, Item 3 of the Assembly and Demonstration Act provides for punishment of a person who, without justifiable reason, intrudes for a considerable time upon an order-maintenance line established pursuant to Article 13 of the Assembly and Demonstration Act, or damages, conceals, moves, removes, or otherwise harms its utility.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant provisions of the Assembly and Demonstration Act and the Enforcement Decree of the Assembly and Demonstration Act concerning the establishment of the above order-maintenance line, it is reasonable to view the order-maintenance line prescribed by the Assembly and Demonstration Act as being able to be established not only in the boundary area outside the place where the assembly or demonstration is being held, but also inside the place where the assembly or demonstration is being held, if the situation falls under the grounds set forth in Article 13(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Assembly and Demonstration Act, provided that it is a case deemed necessary for the protection of the assembly or demonstration and the maintenance of public order; however, even in such a case, the order-maintenance line must be established by setting only the minimum necessary scope deemed necessary for the protection of the assembly or demonstration and the maintenance of public order, and if the order-maintenance line is established beyond that scope, it violates Article 13(1) of the Assembly and Demonstration Act and cannot be deemed lawful.\\n\\nAlso, in light of the definition of an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act and the text and purpose of the penal provision concerning acts such as intrusion upon an order-maintenance line, it is reasonable to regard an order-maintenance line as an object that can function as a boundary marker, such as a cordon, barricade, or lane marking, or as a safety sign under the Road Traffic Act; therefore, even if police officers perform, in substance, the role of an order-maintenance line by standing in rows on the outskirts of or within the place where an assembly or demonstration is being held, such conduct cannot be called an order-maintenance line prescribed by the Assembly and Demonstration Act.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 19(1) of the Assembly and Demonstration Act provides: “A police officer may, after notifying the organizer of an assembly or demonstration, enter the place of such assembly or demonstration wearing a uniform. Provided, that entry into the place of an indoor assembly may be made only when urgently necessary for the performance of duties.” Article 19(2) of the same Act provides: “The organizer of an assembly or demonstration, the order maintainer, or the venue manager shall cooperate with the performance of duties by police officers for the maintenance of order.” Thus, the Act permits police officers to enter the place of an assembly or demonstration for the purpose of maintaining order. Although Article 19 of the Assembly and Demonstration Act prescribes only notice to the organizer and wearing of a uniform as requirements for police officers to enter the place of an outdoor assembly or demonstration for the maintenance of order, in light of the constitutional value and function of freedom of assembly, the legislative purpose of the Assembly and Demonstration Act, namely the harmonization of guaranteeing the right of assembly and demonstration with public peace and order, and similar considerations, police entry into the place of an outdoor assembly or demonstration for the maintenance of order should also, by analogy to the provisions concerning the establishment of an order-maintenance line, be carried out only within the minimum necessary scope when necessary for the protection of the assembly or demonstration and the maintenance of public order (see Supreme Court Decision 2019. 1. 10. rendered 2016DO21311, etc.).\\n\\nii) The lower court, for the reasons stated in its opinion, determined that: ① since an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act must be established not in the form of occupying part of the assembly site but certainly at the outer boundary of the assembly site, the order-maintenance line at issue, which was established inside the assembly site on 2013. 7. 25., could not be deemed lawfully established; and ② even if the so-called manned order-maintenance line is formed by deploying police officers for the purpose of installing an order-maintenance line, it cannot be deemed an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act, and thus the fact that, during the assembly in question, police officers stood in a row inside the assembly site under the name of a manned order-maintenance line and occupied part of the assembly site could not be deemed to constitute the establishment of an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act; on such grounds, the lower court held, in substance, that the establishment of the order-maintenance line at issue and the deployment of police officers were in violation of the Assembly and Demonstration Act and therefore could not be deemed lawful performance of official duties.\\n\\nIn light of the above legal principles, as well as the record, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals that it is not appropriate for the lower court to have determined that the establishment of the order-maintenance line at issue was unlawful on the premise that an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act must necessarily be established at the outer boundary of the place where the assembly is held, or to have immediately determined that the duties of the police officers were unlawful on the sole ground that the police officers deployed at the assembly site could not constitute an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act.\\n\\nHowever, in light of the circumstances and form of establishment of the order-maintenance line at issue as found by the lower court and ascertainable from the record, the location and area of the assembly site on 2013. 7. 25., and the area occupied by the order-maintenance line at issue within the assembly site, it is difficult to deem that the order-maintenance line at issue was established by setting only the minimum necessary scope required for the protection of the assembly or demonstration and the maintenance of public order. In addition, the fact that police officers entered the assembly site in advance, remained there, and occupied part of it cannot, as the lower court determined, be viewed as the establishment of an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act, and it is also difficult to view such deployment of police officers as having been carried out within the minimum necessary scope required for the protection of the assembly or demonstration and the maintenance of public order.\\n\\nTherefore, the lower court’s conclusion that the establishment of the order-maintenance line at issue, or the conduct of the police officers who continuously occupied part of the assembly site under the name of a manned order-maintenance line, cannot be deemed lawful is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning an order-maintenance line under the Assembly and Demonstration Act, the principle of prohibition of excess, or lawful performance of duties, which is protected under the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties, or, in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n2) Regarding the argument that it was lawful as an immediate compulsion under the Act on the Execution of Duties by Police Officers\\n\\nThe lower court, based on the circumstances stated in its opinion, such as that during the assembly on 2013. 7. 25. there was no participant who intruded into or attempted to damage the flowerbed inside the assembly site or engaged in conduct not following the organizer’s control, and that in light of the scale of the dispatched police officers and the assembly participants, there was no necessity for police officers to enter the assembly site in advance and occupy it, determined that there was no urgent police obstacle to the extent that it was necessary to install an order-maintenance line inside the assembly site; therefore, the act of installing the order-maintenance line at issue inside the assembly site could not be deemed lawful performance of duties as an administrative immediate compulsion pursuant to Article 5(1) and Article 6 of the Act on the Execution of Duties by Police Officers.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles stated in the lower court’s opinion and the record, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the lower court’s determination that the establishment of the order-maintenance line at issue did not satisfy the requirements prescribed by the Act on the Execution of Duties by Police Officers, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning administrative immediate compulsion under the Act on the Execution of Duties by Police Officers, the discretion in the exercise of police authority, or lawful performance of duties protected under the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties, as asserted in the grounds for appeal, or in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\nb. As to the portion concerning obstruction of performance of official duties by Defendant 3 on 2013. 8. 21.\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the lower court upheld the first-instance judgment that, because the police officers affiliated with the Seoul Namdaemun Police Station used physical force against assembly participants or attempted to arrest Non-Party 2 as a flagrant offender under the pretext of carrying out order-maintenance duties at the assembly site on 2013. 8. 21., such acts could not be viewed as lawful performance of duties, and thus Defendant 3’s act of trying to prevent them could not be deemed to constitute the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties.\\n\\nAmong the grounds for appeal, the arguments disputing the factual findings that formed the basis of the lower court’s determination are, in substance, nothing more than criticism of the selection of evidence and assessment of probative value, which fall within the free evaluation of evidence of the trial court as the trier of fact.\\n\\nEven in light of the legal principles reviewed above and the record, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the above determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning an order-maintenance line prescribed by the Assembly and Demonstration Act or lawful performance of duties protected under the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties, or, in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nc. As to the portion concerning the offense of arrest resulting in injury by the defendants\\n\\n1) Regarding the argument that the offense of arrest was completed\\n\\nThe offense of arrest, as a continuing offense, is completed only when there is temporal continuity sufficient to clearly recognize that the act of arrest has indeed restrained a person’s bodily freedom; where the restraint on bodily freedom does not reach such a level and merely remains temporary, only an attempt of the offense of arrest is established.\\n\\nThe lower court, based on the circumstances stated in its opinion, determined that the defendants’ acts merely deprived Non-Party 1 of freedom of bodily movement temporarily and partially, and therefore could not be deemed to have reached completion of the offense of arrest, and rejected the prosecutor’s arguments in the grounds for appeal disputing this point.\\n\\nIn light of the above legal principles and the record, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning completion of the offense of arrest, as asserted in the grounds for appeal, or in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\n2) Regarding the argument that it constitutes injury under the offense of arrest resulting in injury\\n\\n“Injury” under the offense of arrest resulting in injury means that the victim’s state of health deteriorates and an impairment of life functions is caused. If the wounds suffered by the victim are extremely minor so that no treatment is necessary, there is no hindrance whatsoever to daily life even without treatment, and the wounds can heal naturally over time, it is difficult to deem that the victim’s state of health was thereby detrimentally changed or that an impairment of life functions was caused, and thus such wounds cannot be said to constitute “injury” under the offense of arrest resulting in injury (see Supreme Court Decision 2003. 7. 11. rendered 2003DO2313, Supreme Court Decision 2009. 7. 23. rendered 2009DO1934, etc.).\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its opinion, upheld the first-instance judgment that found the defendant not guilty on this part of the charged facts, on the ground that it was difficult to deem that the fact that the victim suffered an impairment of life functions or a detrimental change in health condition and thus injury as a result of the defendants’ act of arrest had been proved beyond a reasonable doubt; the lower court rejected the prosecutor’s arguments in the grounds for appeal disputing this point.\\n\\nAmong the grounds for appeal, the arguments disputing the factual findings that formed the basis of the lower court’s determination are, in substance, nothing more than criticism of the selection of evidence and assessment of probative value, which fall within the free evaluation of evidence of the trial court as the trier of fact.\\n\\nEven in light of the above legal principles and the record, examination of the reasons given in the lower court judgment reveals no error in the lower court’s determination, such as misapprehending the legal principles concerning injury under the offense of arrest resulting in injury, the probative value of a medical certificate of injury, or the causal relationship between the arrest and the injury, as asserted in the grounds for appeal, or in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\nThe Supreme Court decision cited in the grounds for appeal concerns a different factual context from this case, and is therefore not appropriate to invoke in this case.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and it is adjudged as follows by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2018DO9809]": "1. The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\nA. As to the assertion of grounds for appeal concerning the portion of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights by Defendant 1\\nThe court below held that even if Defendant 1, who is a non-status person and not a public official, sequentially conspired with Non-indicted Person 1, also a non-status person, and with former President Non-indicted Person 2 (hereinafter referred to as “the former President”), it could be recognized that the offense of co-principal liability for abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights in connection with support for the Non-indicted Person 3 incorporated association of XX Group (hereinafter referred to as “the Non-indicted Person 3 Center”) was established as to Defendant 1.\\nExamining the reasons of the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence duly admitted, there is no error in the above determination by the court below, such as misunderstanding the legal principles concerning status and accomplice liability, or the establishment of co-principal liability, as alleged in the grounds for appeal.\\nMoreover, the assertion to the effect that there is an error of law concerning status and accomplice liability, and the establishment of co-principal liability, in the portion of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights related to support for the Non-indicted Person 3 Center by Non-indicted Company 4 Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Non-indicted Company 4”) cannot constitute a lawful ground for appeal, because it is being raised for the first time at the stage of final appeal with respect to something that Defendant 1 did not make a ground of appeal or that the court below did not, ex officio, make the subject of adjudication (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2017DO16593-1, rendered March 21, 2019, etc.).\\n\\nB. As to the assertion of grounds for appeal by Defendant 2\\nAccording to the record, Defendant 2 appealed against the first-instance judgment only on the ground of unreasonable sentencing, and the court below dismissed Defendant 2’s appeal. Therefore, the assertion to the effect that there is an error such as misapprehension of legal principles in the portion of leakage of official secrets and the portion of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights related to support for the Non-indicted Person 3 Center by Non-indicted Company 4 in the court below’s judgment cannot constitute a lawful ground for appeal (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2017DO16593-1, rendered March 21, 2019, etc.).\\nAnd the assertion to the effect that the court below’s sentencing determination contains an error in violation of the principle of proportionality between crime and punishment or the principle of culpability substantially amounts to an assertion of unreasonable sentencing. Under Article 383, Subparagraph 4 of the Criminal Procedure Act, an appeal on the ground of unreasonable sentencing is permitted only in cases where the death penalty, life imprisonment, or imprisonment or detention for not less than 10 years has been imposed; therefore, in this case, where a lighter sentence than that was imposed on Defendant 2, the assertion that the sentence is unreasonable does not constitute a lawful ground for appeal.\\nThe Supreme Court decisions cited as grounds for appeal involve different facts from this case, and therefore are not appropriate for citation in this case.\\n\\nC. As to the Prosecutor’s assertion of grounds for appeal\\n1) The portion concerning violation of the Subsidy Management Act and fraud as to Defendant 1\\nThe court below held that, at the time of each application for the subsidy in this case, Defendant 1 did not intend to execute the self-burdened contribution as stated in the business plan, and yet it is difficult to view it as having been proven beyond a reasonable doubt that Defendant 1 obtained each subsidy in this case by disguising that it would normally be executed as so stated, and otherwise there is no evidence to recognize that Defendant 1 deceived the public official in charge of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (hereinafter referred to as “the MCST”) and thereby obtained each subsidy in this case, or received a national subsidy by a false application or other unlawful means; accordingly, it reversed the first-instance judgment, which had found the charges in this part guilty, and rendered a judgment of acquittal.\\nExamining the reasons of the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the above determination by the court below, such as violating the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning causation between the deceptive act and the grant of the subsidy.\\n2) The portion concerning abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights and coercion related to support for the Non-indicted Person 3 Center of XX Group as to Defendant 2\\nThe court below held that it could not be deemed that Defendant 2 conspired with Defendant 1, Non-indicted Person 1, and the former President to commit each of these offenses, or that Defendant 2 exercised functional control by role-sharing, beyond a reasonable doubt; accordingly, it maintained the first-instance judgment, which found each charge in this part not guilty.\\nExamining the reasons of the court below’s judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the above determination by the court below, such as violating the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the establishment of a conspiratorial relationship.\\n\\n2. The Court decides ex officio.\\n\\nA. The offense of coercion is an offense that, by assault or intimidation, obstructs a person’s exercise of rights or causes the person to do something to which the person is under no duty. Here, intimidation refers to the notice of harm that would objectively be sufficient to cause fear to the extent of restricting a person’s freedom of decision or obstructing the freedom to act. For such intimidation to be recognized, there must be a notice of specific harm that can be thought of as a possible occurrence. Where an actor, based on his or her occupation or status, demands the provision of some benefit, etc. from the other party, whether that act of demand constitutes a notice of harm as a means of the offense of coercion must be determined comprehensively, taking into account not only the actor’s status but also the content and circumstances of the words and conduct, the situation at the time of the demand, and the character, career, and mutual relationship of the actor and the other party, as well as whether it can be deemed that the other party was made to recognize that failure to comply with the demand would lead to some harm, and whether the actor and the other party could recognize or reasonably foresee the harm that the actor could inflict on the other party by virtue of the actor’s status. Where a public official, as the actor, has demanded the provision of some benefit, etc. from the other party, if it cannot be recognized as such a notice of harm, then it may amount to abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights or a demand for bribery, etc., but it is difficult for the offense of coercion, which requires intimidation, to be established (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2018DO13792, rendered August 29, 2019, etc.).\\n\\nB. The court below recognized that (i) the act by Defendant 1, in sequential conspiracy with Non-indicted Person 1 and the former President, of demanding support for the Non-indicted Person 3 Center from Vice Chairman Non-indicted Person 5, etc. of XX Group, (ii) the act by the Defendants, in conspiracy with Non-indicted Person 1, of demanding support for the Non-indicted Person 3 Center from Representative Director Non-indicted Person 6, etc. of Non-indicted Company 4, and (iii) the act by Defendant 2, in sequential conspiracy with Non-indicted Person 1, Non-indicted Person 7, and the former President, of demanding that the above-mentioned Non-indicted Person 6, etc. establish a sports team and conclude a service contract, correspond to intimidation under the offense of coercion, and thereby maintained the first-instance determination that found the coercion offenses in this part guilty.\\nC. However, examining the reasons of the court below’s judgment and the first-instance judgment in light of the legal principles seen above, it is difficult to recognize that each of the above demands constitutes intimidation, which is a requirement for the offense of coercion, namely, a notice of harm.\\nThe fact that the President and the Second Vice Minister of the MCST demanded, on the basis of their status, the provision of some benefit, etc. from enterprises, etc. over which they could exert influence in the course of their duties or in fact does not mean that such demand can immediately be evaluated as a notice of harm; the various circumstances examined above must be comprehensively considered.\\nEven when examining the reasons of the first-instance judgment and the evidence duly admitted, it is difficult to see that, at the time of each of the above demands, there were circumstances relating to the content and circumstances of the words and conduct, the situation at the time of the demand, and the character, career, and mutual relationship of the actor and the other party, such as would warrant the evaluation that the other party was made to recognize that failure to comply with the demand would lead to harm. The circumstances cited by the first instance—that the Second Vice Minister of the MCST oversaw supervisory affairs over Non-indicted Company 4, and that the Social Contribution Foundation of Non-indicted Company 4 was also under the supervision of the tourism policy office under the Second Vice Minister of the MCST, and that Chairman Non-indicted Person 8 of the above Social Contribution Foundation testified, in the investigative authorities and in the first-instance courtroom, to subjective matters such as that Representative Director Non-indicted Person 6 of Non-indicted Company 4 felt burdened by Defendant 2’s demand or was in a situation in which it was difficult to refuse—are insufficient to evaluate the above demands as a notice of harm.\\nNevertheless, the court below, on the sole basis of the insufficient circumstances as stated in its opinion, premised that each of the above demands constituted a notice of harm and found the coercion charges in this part guilty. The court below’s determination contains an error that affected the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning intimidation under the offense of coercion.\\n\\n3. Scope of reversal\\nThe portion of the court below’s judgment concerning coercion as to Defendant 1, and the portion concerning coercion related to Non-indicted Company 4, etc. as to Defendant 2, must be reversed for the reasons stated in section 2 above, and the portion standing in an ideal concurrence relationship with the reversed portion, as well as the portion in which a single sentence was imposed in a concurrent-offense relationship under the first sentence of Article 37 of the Criminal Act, must also be reversed together; accordingly, the guilty portion of the court below’s judgment as to the Defendants must ultimately be reversed.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds for appeal by Defendant 1, the guilty portion of the court below’s judgment as to the Defendants is reversed, and this case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination on this part; and the Prosecutor’s appeal is dismissed. Accordingly, it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2019DO16421]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Facts of the case and the judgment of the lower court\\na. Established facts\\n1) The Defendant married a French national, a person other than the accused, in Japan on 2007. 3. 24., and a daughter, the victim child, was born ((date of birth omitted)). The person other than the accused and the victim child lived in France from around 2009. 4., and the Defendant remained in Japan, completed his studies, then lived together in France from around 2010. 4., before returning to the Republic of Korea alone around 2012. 3.\\n2) Around 2012. 7., the person other than the accused filed a divorce action against the Defendant in a French court, and the court, around 2013. 11. 15., issued a provisional measure decision to the effect that the victim child's habitual residence would be the residence of the person other than the accused and that the Defendant could have visitation and contact.\\n3) The Defendant, for one month of visitation and contact, brought the victim child (then 5 years old) to the Republic of Korea on 2014. 7. 5. and promised to take her back to the person other than the accused in France on 2014. 8. 6., but he did not take the victim child back and cut off contact with the person other than the accused.\\n4) On 2015. 4. 17., the person other than the accused filed a petition with the Suwon District Court against the Defendant seeking designation of herself as the person with parental authority and custodian of the victim child and demanding delivery of the victim child, and the Suwon District Court, on 2016. 7. 20., issued an adjudication designating the person other than the accused as custodian of the victim child and ordering delivery of the victim child, but dismissing the request for designation of the person with parental authority on the ground that the French court's divorce judgment had not become final and conclusive. Although the Defendant appealed, the Suwon District Court dismissed the appeal on 2016. 11. 3., and the judgment became final and conclusive on 2016. 11. 29.\\n5) The person other than the accused applied to the Suwon District Court four times for provisional dispositions for video calls with the victim child, instruction in French, visitation and contact, etc., until the above adjudication became final and conclusive, and received grants thereof, but because the Defendant did not properly comply or cooperate, contact with the victim child was only very limited, and execution pursuant to the above granted provisional dispositions could not be carried out.\\n6) The French court, on 2016. 4. 13., rendered a judgment declaring divorce due to the Defendant's unilateral fault, designating the person other than the accused as the person with parental authority and custodian, and reserving the Defendant's right of visitation and contact, and that judgment became final and conclusive on 2016. 9. 29.\\n7) At the active request of the person other than the accused, etc., lawful attempts to execute for taking the victim child were made, namely, ① compulsory execution under the Civil Execution Act pursuant to the adjudication ordering delivery of the child with provisional execution on 2016. 8. 23., and ② compulsory execution based on an order of performance for delivery of the child under Article 64 of the Family Litigation Act on 2017. 10. 24., but they failed due to the victim child, who had already largely forgotten French and become accustomed to life in Korea, refusing.\\n8) The Defendant delivered the victim child to the person other than the accused on 2019. 10. 15., while the detention matter arising from the violation of the provisional disposition and the court below in this case were pending.\\n\\nb. Summary of the charged facts at issue\\nThe Defendant was indicted on the charged facts that, for the purpose of visitation and contact with the victim child, he received the victim child from the person other than the accused, who had been protecting and raising the victim child, brought her into the country, and then made her continue to reside at the Defendant's residence without returning her against the will of the person other than the accused and the victim child, thereby abducting the victim child.\\n\\nc. The judgment of the court below\\nThe court below, based on the following circumstances, held that the Defendant's act, even without any further physical relocation of the victim child, was equivalent to moving the victim child under his de facto control by using unlawful de facto force as the means, and therefore upheld in its entirety the first-instance judgment that found the above charged facts guilty.\\n\\n1) The Defendant and the person other than the accused lived separately in Korea and France and were in divorce litigation, and the French court, by provisional measure, designated the victim child's habitual residence as the residence of the person other than the accused, and accordingly the person other than the accused was in fact exercising rights concerning the victim child's protection and upbringing.\\n2) The Defendant exercised the visitation and contact right granted by the French court, brought the victim child to Korea, and even after the expiration of that period, not only failed to deliver her to the person other than the accused, but also for a long period obstructed contact between the person other than the accused and the victim child and prevented them from meeting each other.\\n3) Such conduct by the Defendant can be evaluated as significantly infringing the person other than the accused's rights of protection and upbringing over the victim child, and as causing the victim child, against her will, to depart from the free living relationship or the protective relationship of the person other than the accused and to be placed under the Defendant's de facto control.\\n\\n2. The Supreme Court's judgment\\na. Relevant legal principles\\n1) As an element of the offense of abduction of a minor under Article 287 of the Criminal Act, abduction means the act of using violence, intimidation, or unlawful de facto force as the means to cause the victim, against the victim's will, to depart from a free living relationship or protective relationship and to place the victim under one's own or a third person's de facto control, and whether a certain act in a specific case constitutes abduction must be determined by comprehensively considering relevant circumstances such as the purpose and intent of the act, the circumstances at the time of the act, the manner and type of the act, the means and method, and the victim's condition (see Supreme Court Decision 2009DO3816 rendered on 2009. 7. 9., etc.).\\n2) Even a person who protects and supervises a minor may be the principal offender of the offense of abduction of a minor when he or she infringes another guardian's rights of protection and upbringing or abuses his or her own rights of protection and upbringing to infringe the minor's own interests (see Supreme Court Decision 2007DO8011 rendered on 2008. 1. 31., etc.), and where, in a situation in which parents are divorced or separated, one parent is peacefully protecting and raising a minor child, and the other parent, by exercising violence, intimidation, or unlawful de facto force, breaks that state of protection and upbringing and places the child under his or her own or a third person's de facto control, such conduct, absent special circumstances, constitutes the offense of abduction of a minor (see Supreme Court Decision 2015DO10032 rendered on 2017. 12. 13.).\\n\\nb. Issue\\nThe issue in this case is whether, in a situation where the parents are separated, the Defendant, who was one spouse, brought the 5-year-old victim child, who was living with the other spouse in France, to the Republic of Korea in order to exercise his visitation and contact right, and then, even after the visitation period ended, did not take the child back to France and prevented the victim child from properly meeting her biological mother, such conduct can be viewed as “abducting the victim child by exercising unlawful de facto force.”\\n\\nc. Determination\\nIn a situation of parental separation or divorce, where one spouse lawfully takes the child for purposes of exercising visitation and contact and then, even after the visitation period ends, does not take the child back to the custodial parent, that circumstance alone cannot always be deemed to constitute the offense of abduction of a minor.\\n\\nHowever, based on the foregoing legal principles and comprehensively considering the following circumstances discernible from the facts set forth above, the Defendant's conduct in this case may be evaluated, in criminal law terms, as an act equivalent to the active act of using unlawful de facto force to cause the victim child, against her will and welfare, to depart from the free living and protective relationship and to place her under his de facto control; therefore, it is proper to conclude that it falls under the abduction conduct constituting the offense of abduction of a minor under Article 287 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\n1) From the standpoint of the purpose and intent of the act, looking at the series of actions taken by the Defendant since around 2014. 8., the Defendant appears to have refused to return the victim child for the purpose of continuing to protect and raise her thereafter, thereby causing her to depart from the existing free living and protective relationship and placing her under his de facto control.\\n2) From the standpoint of the circumstances at the time of the act and the victim's condition, the victim child was then only a 5-year-old infant, and the place to which the victim child had to return was France, a foreign country; therefore, unless the Defendant performed his duty to act and took the victim child back, the victim was in a state in which she herself had no ability to cope with the threat of departure from the free living and protective relationship.\\n3) In relation to the principle of prioritizing the maximum welfare of the child, because the family court, when making decisions concerning the designation of a minor child's custodian, etc., gives first priority to the child's welfare, conduct that violates such a family court decision may, absent special circumstances, be viewed as infringing the child's welfare.\\nAs noted above, the Defendant repeatedly violated not only the French court's decision designating the custodian for a long period, but also various decisions of the courts of the Republic of Korea, including the decision designating the custodian and ordering delivery of the infant, the order of performance thereof, and the provisional disposition for visitation and contact; and the victim child, at the age of 5, while living in the Republic of Korea, where communication was not easy, with the Defendant, with whom she had not formed a close relationship, was not only prevented from contacting the caregiver with whom she had previously had a bond, but, due to the Defendant's continued conduct thereafter, ultimately became completely separated from the living relationship in France and from the protective relationship of the person other than the accused as caregiver, forgot French, and even lost the bond with the person other than the accused, her biological mother; this can, in substance, be viewed as infringing the victim child's welfare.\\n\\n4) Although the relevant statutes, including the Family Litigation Act, contain provisions concerning adjudication ordering delivery of the child and its execution, the Defendant, while keeping the victim child without following the adjudication ordering delivery of the child and thereby fixing her upbringing environment, made compulsory execution under lawful procedures impossible, and such conduct of the Defendant resulted in the inability to secure the effectiveness of the court's final and conclusive adjudications, etc.\\n\\nAccordingly, the court below did not err, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in misapprehending the legal principles concerning abduction, offenses by omission, etc. of the offense of abduction of a minor, and there is no other error in exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience or in misapprehending the legal principles concerning justifiable act, grounds for exclusion of responsibility, etc., without fully conducting the necessary trial.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the decision, as set forth in the disposition."}

question: Which of the following explanations concerning causation is incorrect? (In cases of dispute, according to case law)
A: In the case of an aider and abettor, for causation to be recognized between the aiding act and the realization of the principal offender’s crime, the aiding act must be closely related to the realization of the principal offender’s crime and must be evaluated as having made an actual contribution to the realization of the principal offender’s crime, such as by causing the principal offender to realize a specific risk or increasing the opportunity for the criminal result to occur.
B: If the driver of a motor vehicle failed to fulfill the duty of care sufficient to avoid the result in preparation for ordinarily foreseeable situations, and that failure became the direct cause of the occurrence of a traffic accident, then even if the motor vehicle did not directly strike the pedestrian and the pedestrian was injured by falling onto the road in surprise at the sudden braking of the motor vehicle, proximate causation may be recognized between the breach of the duty of care in the course of business and the occurrence of the traffic accident.
C: Where the Defendant struck the victim’s cheek once and hit the victim’s neck with his right hand, causing the victim to fall and strike his head against the ground and thereby inflicting injury, and as a result caused the victim, who suffered head trauma, to receive inpatient treatment at a hospital and die from complications, causation is recognized between the Defendant’s act and the victim’s death.
D: In the offense of rape, there must be causation between violence or intimidation and sexual intercourse, and the violence or intimidation must necessarily precede the act of sexual intercourse.
E: Proximate causation is recognized between an act of using violence or intimidation to forcibly take another person’s property and the injury suffered while, out of extreme excitement and fear, attempting to avoid it.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2011DO17648]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding the Defendant's grounds for appeal\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the lower court judgment, the lower court, based on the evidence it adopted, determined that it is recognized that the Defendant, as stated in the facts charged, struck the victim's cheek once with the palm of his hand and struck the victim's neck with his right hand, causing the victim to fall backward as is and hit his head against the ground, thereby inflicting injuries such as skull fracture, traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, traumatic subdural hemorrhage, etc. on the victim.\\n\\nIn light of the record, the foregoing measure of the lower court is reasonable and acceptable, and there is no illegality such as violation of the rules of logic and experience, departure from the limits of free evaluation of evidence, or use of evidence lacking admissibility.\\n\\n2. Regarding the Prosecutor's grounds for appeal\\n\\na. Even if the Defendant's act was not the direct cause of the victim's death, where another indirect cause arising therefrom was combined to bring about the result of death, there is a causal relationship between the act and the death (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 82DO2525 rendered on December 28, 1982).\\n\\nb. The lower court, taking into account the circumstances as stated in its holding, namely, ① immediately after the victim sustained the injury on November 2, 2010, the victim was transported to the emergency room of Pusan National University Hospital and received emergency measures such as various examinations and blood transfusions, and was hospitalized at Maryknoll Hospital from November 3, 2010 to December 2, 2010, and from the time the victim came to Maryknoll Hospital, the victim had remained conscious, had been breathing spontaneously, and had also been able to take food by himself; ② also, at Maryknoll Hospital, the victim was not in a condition requiring emergency surgery (craniotomy and hematoma evacuation), and the hospital carried out observation and drug treatment, as a result of which there were no aggravating findings such as an increase in the amount of hemorrhage or the occurrence of cerebral edema, and, as time passed, the hemorrhage appeared to be naturally absorbed, and by around November 21, 2010, the hemorrhage appears to have been almost absorbed and the condition had greatly improved; ③ accordingly, in light of the improvement in condition, from December 2, 2010, the victim was transferred to Busan Nara Hospital for the victim's \"rehabilitation treatment,\" and from the time of admission the victim continued to breathe spontaneously and was able to take food by himself, but, on the other hand, the victim's condition increasingly deteriorated, showing mental problems such as almost daily shouting and violent behavior, and also showing hemoptysis; ④ Busan Nara Hospital recommended to the victim's family that the victim be transferred to another hospital because it was difficult to treat the victim's aggravated condition, and while the victim was at Busan Nara Hospital, there were no symptoms such as pneumonia or sepsis; ⑤ the victim was hospitalized in the intensive care unit of Busan Medical Center from December 6, 2010 to December 14, 2010, and from the time of admission the victim remained in a clouded state of consciousness and was in an extremely emotionally unstable state, but at the time of admission the victim was breathing spontaneously and showed no sign of pneumonia; ⑥ at Busan Medical Center, signs of pneumonia were observed in the victim on December 9, 2010, and this worsened and led to death on December 14 (5 days from onset to death); ⑦ in patients who have suffered the same head injury as the victim, even if the bleeding itself improves due to craniotomy and hematoma evacuation or natural absorption of the bleeding, the decrease in consciousness due to the head injury lowers the airway defense mechanism and the bronchial ciliary sputum-excretion function and increases the possibility of aspiration into the airway, so complications such as pneumonia and aspiration pneumonia are likely to occur, and if organic personality disorder or violent and aggressive tendencies appear as sequelae of the head injury, the sedative effect of tranquilizers, etc. that are administered may lower coughing and sputum-excretion function, thereby making complications such as pneumonia and aspiration pneumonia more likely to occur, but this is ultimately considered to be due to the \"continuing decrease in consciousness, etc.\" that occurred after the head injury, and it is difficult to regard it as having a direct relation to the head injury suffered by the victim; ⑧ Maryknoll Hospital determined that the relationship between the victim's pneumonia and sepsis and the traumatic cerebral hemorrhage was not very high, and Busan Medical Center also determined that the victim is presumed to have died from sepsis, etc. due to pneumonia, a complication of traumatic cerebral hemorrhage, but that preexisting diseases such as liver cirrhosis and various other social and economic factors would also have contributed to the aggravation of the disease; ⑨ according to the findings stated in the autopsy report on the victim, the victim showed a skull fracture and a small amount of old subdural hemorrhage and showed findings of old traumatic cerebral hemorrhage, but there were no findings of fatal cerebral edema or brain herniation sufficient to lead to death, and widespread pneumonia was seen in the lungs, which appears to have caused death, and pneumonia is considered to be a complication during the treatment process; ⑩ the victim moved among several hospitals and had been hospitalized for a long time, during which it cannot be excluded that the victim may have contracted pneumonia unrelated to treatment—when these circumstances are taken together, it cannot be concluded that a causal relationship is recognized between the injury inflicted by the Defendant on the victim and the victim's death, and furthermore, taking those circumstances into account, the lower court determined that it was difficult to find that the Defendant, at the time of the assault, foresaw that the victim had suffered a head injury and would die from multiple organ failure due to complications of pneumonia in the course of treating the head injury.\\n\\nc. However, the foregoing determination of the lower court is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nEven based on the circumstances relied upon by the lower court, in patients who have suffered the same head injury as the victim, even if the bleeding itself improves due to craniotomy and hematoma evacuation or natural absorption of the bleeding, the decrease in consciousness due to the head injury lowers the airway defense mechanism and the bronchial ciliary sputum-excretion function and increases the possibility of aspiration into the airway, so complications such as pneumonia and aspiration pneumonia are likely to occur, and if organic personality disorder or violent and aggressive tendencies appear as sequelae of the head injury, the sedative effect of tranquilizers, etc. that are administered may lower coughing and sputum-excretion function, thereby making complications such as pneumonia and aspiration pneumonia more likely to occur; the victim, after sustaining injuries such as the skull fracture, traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, and traumatic subdural hemorrhage at issue in this case, received inpatient treatment at a hospital and then died from sepsis, etc. due to pneumonia, a complication. Therefore, in light of the legal principles seen above, the Defendant's offense in this case was not the direct cause of the victim's death, but as a result of that offense, injuries such as skull fracture, traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, and traumatic subdural hemorrhage occurred to the victim, and in the course of treating those injuries, complications such as pneumonia and sepsis, which were the direct cause of the victim's death, were induced; accordingly, even if the victim's preexisting diseases such as liver cirrhosis affected the induction of the direct cause of death, the existence of a causal relationship between the Defendant's offense in this case and the victim's death cannot be denied.\\n\\nAnd when a person is knocked down onto the surface of an asphalt road and strikes his head forcefully, death may result from a skull fracture, cerebral hemorrhage, etc., and if the Defendant struck the victim's cheek once and struck the victim's neck with his right hand, causing the victim to fall backward as is and hit his head against the ground, thereby inflicting injuries such as skull fracture, traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, and traumatic subdural hemorrhage on the victim, there is ample room to find that there was foreseeability of the result of death.\\n\\nd. Nevertheless, the lower court, solely on the basis of the reasons as stated in its holding, determined that no causal relationship is recognized between the injury inflicted by the Defendant on the victim and the victim's death, and that there was no foreseeability as to the occurrence of the result of death, and therefore held that the facts charged of the instant offense of bodily injury resulting in death constituted a case where there is no proof of criminal facts and thus were not guilty; accordingly, the foregoing action of the lower court contains illegality that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning causality and foreseeability in the offense of bodily injury resulting in death. The argument in the grounds for appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nThe part of the lower court judgment that acquitted the Defendant of the offense of bodily injury resulting in death must be reversed, and since the offense of bodily injury resulting in death and the offense of bodily injury, which the lower court found guilty, are in a relation of one offense, the entire lower court judgment must necessarily be reversed.\\n\\nTherefore, the lower court judgment is reversed, and in order to have the case retried and redetermined, it is remanded to the lower court. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2017DO9835]": "The grounds for appeal are examined (the statements in the supplemental brief on the grounds for appeal filed after the expiration of the period for filing a statement of the grounds for appeal shall be considered to the extent that they supplement the grounds for appeal).\\n\\n1. Relevant legal principles\\n\\nArticle 32(1) of the Criminal Act provides that “a person who aids another in the commission of a crime shall be punished as an accessory.” Aiding and abetting means an act of assistance that, with knowledge of the principal offender’s specific preparation for or facts of the offense, makes the principal’s execution act possible, promotes it, or facilitates it, or an act that, before the principal offender’s criminal act is completed, strengthens or increases the infringement of the legal interests caused by the principal offender, and thus refers to an act that is closely related to the realization of the principal offender’s crime. Since an accessory offense is a crime established in dependence upon the principal offense, a causal relationship is required between the aiding and abetting act and the realization of the principal offender’s crime. In order for the offense of aiding and abetting to be established, the aiding and abetting act must be closely related to the realization of the principal offender’s crime and must be capable of being evaluated as having made a real contribution to the realization of the principal offender’s crime, such as by causing the principal offender to realize a specific danger or by increasing the opportunity for the criminal result to occur. Where the act merely assisted an act that is not closely related to the realization of the principal offender’s crime, the offense of aiding and abetting is not established.\\n\\nWhere an act of industrial action constitutes the offense of interference with business, if a third party, knowing such circumstances, facilitates the execution of the industrial action, the offense of aiding and abetting interference with business may be established. However, in order to substantively guarantee the three labor rights prescribed in Article 33(1) of the Constitution, it is necessary to allow workers or a labor union to receive broad assistance from third parties when exercising the three labor rights, and furthermore, third parties who assist workers or a labor union also have freedom of expression under Article 21 of the Constitution and general freedom of action inherent in Article 10 of the Constitution. Therefore, when determining whether an act of assistance to an unlawful industrial action constitutes aiding and abetting interference with business, the scope of establishment of the offense of aiding and abetting interference with business must be carefully determined so that the above fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution are not chilled (see Supreme Court En Banc Decision dated September 9, 2021, 2017DO19025, and Supreme Court Decision dated September 16, 2021, 2015DO12632, among others).\\n\\n2. Summary of the facts charged\\n\\nThe Defendants are the heads and other executives of the XX Headquarters of the National Railway Workers’ Union (hereinafter referred to as the “Railway Union”) (Defendant 7 was the former head of the XX Vehicle Branch).\\n\\nNonparty 1 and Nonparty 2, who are members of the Railway Union, from around 06:20 on April 9, 2014, climbed up to the midway waiting area of a lighting tower approximately 15 meters high installed at the XX Vehicle Depot, on the pretext of opposing the rotational reassignment to be implemented by Korea Railroad Corporation, and after setting up a two-person tent, occupied the site by hanging a banner stating, “Not a single person can be sent away. Withdraw the forced transfer,” thereby causing Korea Railroad Corporation, from around 08:35 on the same day until around 13:00 on May 2, 2014, to cut off the power to the said lighting tower for their safety, making it impossible to use the tower’s essential function as a lighting facility during the above period, and thereby obstructing the nighttime shunting operations of Korea Railroad Corporation by force.\\n\\nAccordingly, the Defendants, in order to support the above sit-in by Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2, installed a tent beneath the lighting tower, held a support rally (hereinafter referred to as “the rally at issue”), and facilitated their obstruction of business by providing food, books, and other items needed by Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2, or by climbing up the lighting tower and consoling them, thereby aiding and abetting the same.\\n\\n3. Determination on the grounds for appeal\\n\\na. Examining the following circumstances ascertainable from the record in light of the legal principles discussed above, it is difficult to recognize a causal relationship between the Defendants’ acts and the realization of the offense of interference with business by the principal offenders, Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2; therefore, the Defendants’ acts cannot be deemed to constitute the offense of aiding and abetting interference with business.\\n\\n1) The Railway Union was preparing a struggle against Korea Railroad Corporation’s policy of rotational reassignment, and Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2 appear to have occupied the lighting tower independently of the Railway Union’s prior plan, and it cannot be seen that the Defendants were involved in the initiation of their occupation.\\n\\n2) The Defendants’ acts of installing the tent and holding the rally at issue were basically carried out as part of labor union activities aimed at expressing opposition to the company’s policy of rotational reassignment and inducing its withdrawal. Even if there were some statements at the rally at issue supporting the occupation of the lighting tower, in light of the content and circumstances thereof, it cannot be said that such words and conduct fell outside the protected sphere of freedom of expression, general freedom of action, or the right of association, and it is difficult to view them as having made a real contribution to the realization of the crime by Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2 through their occupation of the lighting tower.\\n\\n3) Considering the nature of the items provided by the Defendants to Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2, the frequency, timing, and circumstances of such provision, and the characteristics of the occupation site, it cannot be denied that the provision of food and similar items by the Defendants was conduct required for the survival and safety of Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2, who were isolated for a long period in a narrow space installed at a great height and had no other means of receiving food; accordingly, the company also appears to have permitted the delivery after confirming the contents each time the Defendants provided the items. And Defendant 4’s act of climbing up the lighting tower on the night of the first day of the occupation and meeting Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 2 is sufficiently open to interpretation as having been carried out to confirm their well-being.\\n\\n4) Taking the above circumstances together, even if the Defendants’ acts, viewed as a whole, had some aspect of assisting the occupation of the lighting tower, it is difficult to conclude that they constitute acts of assistance to the principal offenders’ crime of obstructing nighttime shunting operations by making the lighting tower’s essential function unusable, or acts that strengthen or increase the infringement of the legal interests, and thus acts closely related to the realization of the principal offenders’ crime. Therefore, the Defendants’ acts cannot be regarded as causally related to the act of interference with business to such an extent as to establish the offense of aiding and abetting.\\n\\nb. Nevertheless, the court below, on a different view, found all of the facts charged concerning aiding and abetting interference with business against the Defendants to be guilty solely on the grounds stated in its reasoning. The judgment of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the establishment of the offense of aiding and abetting interference with business, and thus the Defendants’ grounds for appeal are well founded.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2022DO1401]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Summary of the facts charged and the determination of the court below\\n\\na. Summary of the facts charged\\n\\nThe Defendant, a person engaged in the driving of a Bongo 3 vehicle (Vehicle No. 1 omitted), drove past the crosswalk in front of B in Ilsanseo-gu, Goyang-si, at about 16:30 on April 8, 2020, proceeding from the direction of the Ilsan 1-dong Welfare Center toward the direction of Ilsan Market at an unknown speed. At that time, because a crosswalk with no traffic signal was installed there, a person engaged in the driving of an automobile had a duty of care in the course of duties to prevent an accident in advance by slowing down in anticipation of pedestrians’ presence.\\n\\nNevertheless, the Defendant, having neglected this duty and proceeding as he was, belatedly discovered the victim C (9 years old, female, fourth grade of elementary school), who was crossing near the crosswalk from left to right in the Defendant’s direction of travel, and applied the brakes, but failed to stop in time and struck the victim’s right knee area with the front bumper portion of the Defendant’s vehicle, thereby causing the victim to suffer injuries such as a sprain of the right tarsal joint requiring approximately 2 weeks of treatment; yet, the Defendant fled without taking measures such as rescuing the victim.\\n\\nb. The determination of the court below\\n\\nThe court below reversed the first-instance judgment, which had found the facts charged in this case guilty, and found the Defendant not guilty on the ground that it was difficult to find that the Defendant failed to fulfill the duty of care in the course of duties to foresee or avoid the occurrence of the accident described in the facts charged, as follows.\\n\\n1) It is difficult to conclude that the above accident occurred within the crosswalk.\\n\\n2) Since the victim appears to have sustained injuries by falling, it is difficult to conclude solely from the victim’s statement that the Defendant’s vehicle struck the victim’s body, and the possibility cannot be excluded that the Defendant was slowing down to such an extent that he could have prevented the accident by making a sudden stop.\\n\\n3) There is no material from which it can be known whether, if the Defendant had exercised due care, he could have recognized the victim’s presence earlier and prevented the victim from falling.\\n\\n2. The Supreme Court’s determination\\n\\na. Relevant legal principles\\n\\nArticle 27(5) of the Road Traffic Act provides that “the driver of any vehicle shall, when a pedestrian is crossing a road where no crosswalk is installed, make a temporary stop at a safe distance so that the pedestrian may cross safely.” Therefore, when there is a pedestrian crossing a crosswalk where no pedestrian signal device for crosswalk use is installed, the driver of a motor vehicle, except where continuing straight ahead would not impede the pedestrian’s crossing or create a danger to passage, has a duty to ensure that the pedestrian’s passage is not impeded by taking measures such as temporarily stopping the vehicle, regardless of whether the vehicle entered the crosswalk first (see Supreme Court Decision 2020DO8675, decided December 24, 2020; Supreme Court Decision 2020DO17724, decided April 14, 2022).\\n\\nArticle 10(4) of the Road Traffic Act provides, to the effect, that “a pedestrian shall not cross directly in front of or behind a vehicle at a place other than a crosswalk-marked area,” and thus it is natural for the driver of any vehicle to trust that a pedestrian will not suddenly cross from a place without crosswalk pavement markings while passing through a crosswalk-marked area, and it cannot be said that the driver must fulfill a duty of care by anticipating even the occurrence of an extraordinary situation in which such trust would not hold. However, such principle of trust is excluded where there are special circumstances such that the other traffic participant cannot be trusted to observe all laws and regulations related to road traffic and to drive or walk accordingly (see Supreme Court Decisions 85DO833, decided July 9, 1985; 2002DO4134, decided October 11, 2002; 2010DO4078, decided July 29, 2010, among others).\\n\\nIf the driver of a motor vehicle failed to fulfill the duty of care to avoid the result to the extent possible in preparation for normally foreseeable situations, and that failure was the direct cause of the occurrence of a traffic accident, then, even if the vehicle did not directly strike the pedestrian and the pedestrian fell on the road in surprise at the vehicle’s sudden stop and suffered injuries, a substantial causal relationship may be recognized between the violation of the duty of care in the course of duties and the occurrence of the traffic accident.\\n\\nb. Determination in this case\\n\\n1) According to the reasons stated in the court below’s judgment and the evidence duly admitted, the following circumstances can be ascertained.\\n\\na) The Defendant, while driving a truck on a clear afternoon with no obstruction to visibility, immediately after passing through the crosswalk, belatedly discovered the victim, who was attempting to cross the road from the left side to the right side in the direction of travel of the vehicle near the crosswalk, and took emergency braking measures.\\n\\nb) The place where the accident occurred was a road with a relatively narrow width of one lane in each direction, and because there were stores on both sides, there were many pedestrians passing on the edge of the roadway or on the sidewalk near the crosswalk, and since no pedestrian signal device for crosswalk use was installed at the crosswalk, it was a situation in which a pedestrian could cross at any time.\\n\\nc) The victim stated to the police that she had “fallen after being hit by the Defendant’s truck,” and the police statement of an eyewitness to the accident is consistent therewith.\\n\\nd) From the day of the accident, the victim complained of pain in the leg and knee and received outpatient treatment for “sprain of the right ankle joint and contusion of the foot,” requiring approximately 2 weeks of treatment.\\n\\n2) Examining the above circumstances in light of the legal principles seen above, the determination of the court below is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\na) Considering the road conditions near the accident site, the time of the accident, the traffic volume at the time, and the pedestrian situation near the crosswalk, the Defendant, who was driving the truck, could have sufficiently foreseen that there might often be pedestrians attempting to cross the road near the crosswalk immediately after passing through the crosswalk section where no pedestrian signal device for crosswalk use is installed; therefore, he had a duty of care in the course of duties to prevent the accident in advance by slowing down further below the speed limit so as to be able to stop safely immediately upon discovering a pedestrian crossing without permission, and by driving safely while closely watching ahead and to the left and right.\\n\\nb) In light of the circumstances before and after the accident and the statements of the persons concerned, there is ample room to find that the Defendant directly struck the victim’s right knee area with the front bumper portion of the truck, causing the victim to fall onto the road. Even if the Defendant’s truck did not directly strike the victim, it is reasonable to view the direct cause of the victim’s fall onto the road as the sudden stop of the Defendant’s vehicle, which had not reduced speed while passing through the crosswalk.\\n\\nc) Even if the Defendant’s truck did not directly strike the victim, because the accident could have been sufficiently avoided if the Defendant had slowed down safely near the crosswalk, it is difficult to deny the substantial causal relationship between the Defendant’s violation of the duty of care in the course of duties and the occurrence of the accident.\\n\\n3) Nevertheless, the court below found the facts charged in this case not guilty solely for the reasons stated in the judgment. In the determination of the court below, there is an error that affected the judgment by either exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience without fully conducting the necessary examination, or by misapprehending the legal principles concerning violation of the duty of care in the course of duties, etc. in the offense of violation of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes (injury by fleeing the scene). The Prosecutor’s argument pointing this out has merit.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for retrial and determination. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[96DO1142]": "We consider together the grounds of appeal by the Defendant and court-appointed defense counsel.\\n\\n1. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below found as follows: The Defendant, from around 21:00 on November 17, 1994 until around 05:50 the following day, played gambling known as “Seven Odi and Baduk” with 52 cards together with Nonparty 2 and the victim, Nonparty 3, in the inner room of Nonparty 1’s house located in Hwado-eup, Namyangju City, and, when Nonparty 3 lost the 32,000,000 won he had on his person, the Defendant, while discussing with Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 4, who were there, how to recover that money, resolved to threaten Nonparty 3 by mobilizing the Defendant’s younger associates, including Nonparty 5 and Nonparty 6, and then rob him of the money. Accordingly, around 05:30 on the 18th of the same month, Nonparty 5, Nonparty 6, Nonparty 7, and others, having received a call from Nonparty 1 and Nonparty 4 to come quickly to that house, each carrying burlap sacks and the like, arrived at the house and threatened Nonparty 8 and others, who were with Nonparty 3 in the living room of the house, by brandishing burlap sacks, hand exercisers, and the like. Immediately after Nonparty 5 and the others arrived at the house, the Defendant picked up a kitchen knife from the kitchen, entered the inner room where the gambling had been taking place, and attempted to steal money from Nonparty 3. When Nonparty 3 discovered this and hurriedly locked the inner-room door to prevent it from being opened and resisted so that the door would not open, the Defendant loudly threatened Nonparty 3, saying, “I will kill you, you bastard,” inserted the kitchen knife through the gap in the door in an attempt to release the locking mechanism, and repeatedly kicked and shoved the door hard with his foot several times, eventually opening the door and forcing his way into the inner room. Thereupon, Nonparty 3 fled through the window of that room to the veranda, then, in extreme fear, jumped down from the open veranda window to the ground below the house, approximately 8 meters below, and fell to the ground, thereby suffering injuries such as burst fractures of the first, third, and fourth lumbar vertebrae requiring treatment for 5 months and 17 days; Nonparty 4, having been instructed by the Defendant to go and take the money possessed by Nonparty 3, who was lying as above, went to where Nonparty 3 had fallen and robbed Nonparty 3, who had lost consciousness, by taking away the vinyl bag containing 32,000,000 won in cash. Reviewing and comparing the evidence adopted by the judgment of the first instance, as cited by the court below, with the record, the above factual findings by the court below are proper, and it cannot be said that there was any error of law in violation of the rules of evidence, or any failure to fully examine the case. The argument is without merit.\\n\\n2. An act of robbing another’s property by violence or intimidation and the fact that, as a result, the victim, overcome by extreme excitement and fear and attempting to avoid it, suffered injury, are in a substantial causal relationship; and in such a case, if the person committing the robbery could have foreseen the occurrence of the result of injury, the act may be punished as the crime of robbery causing injury.\\n\\nAs seen above, after the Defendant lost 32,000,000 won while gambling with Nonparty 3, the Defendant mobilized three younger associates in addition to the two companions who had been together with him since the gambling, and the Defendant even took a kitchen knife and attempted to take money from Nonparty 3. Nonparty 3, in order to avoid this, locked the inner-room door of the house where the gambling had been taking place and was stubbornly resisting so that the door would not open.
