evaluation of evidence, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights, or omitting a determination.\\n\\nb) The part of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights against H and I\\n\\nHowever, the lower court’s determination that the part of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights against H and I, public officials belonging to Institution L, was not guilty is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\n(1) Where the other party to an act of abuse of authority is a private person, in the absence of special circumstances, he has no duty to comply in response to the official authority, so if he is made to do something, it may fall within “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do.” However, where the other party is a public official or an employee of a public institution, etc. who has been assigned certain public duties pursuant to statutes and regulations, since he is in a position to perform duties in accordance with statutes and regulations, whether what he did in response to the official authority was something he was under no duty to do must be determined individually in accordance with the contents of the relevant statutes and regulations, etc.\\n\\nThe administrative organization must respond to modern administration, which is becoming increasingly complex, diverse, and specialized, while also realizing the demands of democracy. Accordingly, the administrative organization needs to be operated efficiently with a unified hierarchical structure, must be operated democratically, and requires close cooperation and rational coordination in order to achieve administrative objectives. As a result, the decision-making and execution of administrative agencies ordinarily take place through various preparatory processes, reviews, and cooperation with other public officials, departments, or related agencies, etc. Such cooperation or exchange of opinions, etc. is necessary to enhance administrative efficiency and may occur not only between parties of equal standing but also between superior and subordinate agencies, and between supervisory and supervised agencies. In such a relationship, where one party listens to the other party’s request and responds to it by stating his own opinion or by cooperating, etc., such conduct cannot be deemed, in the absence of special circumstances, to be something he is under no duty to do under statutes and regulations.\\n\\nUltimately, where a public official abuses his authority to make a person do something, if the other party is a public official or an employee of a related institution, whether what he did was within the scope of his duties in form and substance, and whether he violated the principles, standards, procedures, etc. that must be observed in the course of performing duties pursuant to statutes and other relevant regulations, must be examined to determine whether the case falls within “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do” (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2018DO2236 rendered on January 30, 2020).\\n\\n(2) Article 56 of the State Public Officials Act provides: “All public officials shall comply with statutes and faithfully perform their duties.” Article 4 of the Special Act on the Truth-Finding Regarding the F Disaster and the Construction of a Safe Society, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the “F Truth-Finding Act”) provides, with respect to the independence of the F Disaster Special Investigation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Committee”), that “the Committee shall maintain political neutrality and preserve the independence and objectivity of its work when performing duties within its authority”; Article 9(1) of the same Act provides, with respect to the official independence of Committee members, that “members shall perform their duties independently without receiving any external instructions or interference”; Article 21(2) provides that, where a public official or employee belonging to a state agency, a local government, or a public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as “state agencies, etc.”) is dispatched to the Committee, “the public official or employee shall perform the work of the Committee independently of the state agency, etc. to which he belongs”; and Article 39 provides, with respect to the duty of cooperation of state agencies, etc., that “state agencies, etc. shall actively cooperate in the performance of the Committee’s work for the truth-finding.” These provisions may be understood as setting standards for the performance of duties to be followed by public officials belonging to Institution L or employees of the Committee.\\n\\nAs can be seen from the content of the above provisions and the evidence lawfully admitted by the lower court, ① at the time, Defendants B and E were serving as Secretary J and Secretary K of the Presidential Secretariat, respectively, while H and I were serving as public officials belonging to Institution L; in particular, H was in charge of work related to the preparation for the establishment of the Committee as the Head of Division M of Institution L, and I had been serving in support work as Team Leader N of the Committee from around December 2014 pursuant to a personnel order of Institution L; ② there may be cases where work cooperation is necessary between the Presidential Secretariat and Institution L for the consultation and coordination of pending issues, and H and I may have to respond to requests from Defendants B and E for cooperation, etc.; ③ however, considering that H and I have the duty to ensure the Committee’s political neutrality and the independence and objectivity of its work, and that I, who was assigned to support work as Team Leader N of the Committee, is required to have official independence comparable to that of a dispatched public official, Defendants B and E may be regarded as having caused H and I to perform their work in violation of the principles and standards of duty performance by having them prepare the Background and Response Measures Document, which included a plan to intervene in the activities of the Committee Establishment Preparatory Team through prospective members of the Committee, etc.\\n\\n(3) Examining the above circumstances in light of the legal principles stated above, there is room to view that Defendants B and E, by conspiracy, caused H and I to do something they were under no duty to do under statutes and regulations. Nevertheless, the lower court found this part of the charged facts not guilty on the grounds stated in its judgment; therefore, the lower court’s determination contains an error that affected the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights and by failing to conduct the necessary examination. The Prosecutor’s assertion pointing out this point is well-founded.\\n\\nc. The part concerning the document titled “Government Response Strategy Regarding Committee Activities” by Defendants A, B, and E\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone was insufficient to establish that the above Defendants had been involved in the preparation of the above document.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience without fully conducting the necessary examination.\\n\\nd. The part concerning Defendant A’s request to suspend and withdraw the review of statutory interpretation\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to conclude that Defendant A’s act constituted an “abuse” of official authority.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights.\\n\\ne. The part concerning the preparation and implementation of the document titled “Composition and Operation Plan of the Committee Support Team” by Defendants A, B, and E\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to conclude that the instructions of Defendants A and B constituted an “abuse” of official authority, and that it was difficult to establish that Defendant E had been involved in the preparation and implementation of the above document.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights.\\n\\nf. The part concerning the collective recall of dispatched public officials by Defendants A, B, and E\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to establish Defendant A’s intent to abuse authority or the fact that he obstructed O’s exercise of rights, and that it was difficult to establish that Defendants B and E conspired with Defendant A in this part of the offense.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights or the relationship of conspiracy.\\n\\ng. The part concerning the preparation and explanation of the organizational structure and budget draft by Defendants A, B, and E\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that it was difficult to conclude that the acts of Defendants A, B, and E constituted, under statutes and regulations, “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do” with respect to I and P.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights or omitting a determination.\\n\\nh. The part concerning Defendants A and E’s monitoring and reporting of Committee developments\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to establish that Defendants A and E had sequentially or tacitly conspired with and participated in Defendant B’s offense.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the relationship of conspiracy.\\n\\ni. The part concerning Defendants B’s monitoring and reporting of Committee developments, among the parts concerning G, H, I, Q, R, S, T, and U (hereinafter referred to as “G and 8 others”) (excluding the part concerning R in Number 1 of the crime list 2 in the lower court’s judgment)\\n\\n1) The lower court’s determination\\n\\nThe lower court, for the following reasons, found this part of the charged facts not guilty.\\n\\nThe act of Defendant B of instructing G and 8 others to monitor and report on the Committee’s developments constitutes an abuse of the authority falling within the general official authority of Secretary J or V of Institution L externally; however, Defendant B merely had G and 8 others, who were the persons in charge of practical affairs, perform factual acts assisting the execution of his official duties, and therefore does not fall within “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do.”\\n\\n2) The Supreme Court’s determination\\n\\nHowever, the lower court’s above determination is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\na) As seen above, “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do” as used in the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights means that a public official abuses his authority to make another person do something he is under no duty to do under statutes and regulations. Where a public official abuses his authority to make a person do something, if the other party is a public official or an employee of a related institution, whether what he did was within the scope of his duties in form and substance, and whether he violated the principles, standards, procedures, etc. that must be observed in the course of performing duties pursuant to statutes and other relevant regulations, must be examined to determine whether the case falls within “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do.”\\n\\nb) As noted above, Article 56 of the State Public Officials Act, which provides for the duty of public officials to comply with statutes; Article 4 of the F Truth-Finding Act, which provides for the independence of the Committee; Article 9(1) of the same Act, which provides for the official independence of Committee members; and Article 39 of the same Act, which provides for the duty of cooperation of state agencies, etc., may be understood as setting standards for the performance of duties to be followed by public officials belonging to Institution L or employees of the Committee. Meanwhile, Article 41 of the F Truth-Finding Act provides, with respect to the duty of confidentiality, that “a person who is, or was, a Committee member or a Committee employee shall not divulge any official secret of the Committee or use it for any purpose other than the performance of the Committee’s duties,” and this may also serve as a standard for the performance of duties to be followed by a Committee employee or a public official belonging to Institution L who performs duties together with such employee.\\n\\nAs can be seen from the content of the above provisions and the evidence lawfully admitted by the lower court, ① G and 8 others received instructions from Defendant B, etc. to ascertain and report the internal developments of the Committee, and then acquired internal information of the Committee through Committee employees dispatched from Institution L, either in fact or formally, and reported it to Defendant B; ② there may be cases where G and 8 others, administrative officers of the Office of Secretary J or public officials of Institution L, have to obey official orders from Defendant B, who is Secretary J, or respond to requests for cooperation, etc., and such circumstances remained the same even after October 21, 2015, when Defendant B took office as V of Institution L; ③ however, G and 8 others have the duty to ensure the Committee’s political neutrality and the independence and objectivity of its work, and the act of ascertaining internal Committee developments through Committee employees and reporting them to Defendant B may, depending on the circumstances, be evaluated as an act of participating in a violation of the duty of confidentiality punishable under Article 51(3)1 of the F Truth-Finding Act; taking these circumstances together, Defendant B may be regarded as having caused G and 8 others to perform their duties in violation of the principles and standards of duty performance by having them acquire internal Committee information through Committee employees dispatched from Institution L to the Committee and report it.\\n\\nc) Examining this in light of the legal principles stated above, there is room to view that Defendant B caused G and 8 others to do something they were under no duty to do under statutes and regulations. Nevertheless, the lower court found this part of the charged facts not guilty based only on the circumstances stated in its judgment; therefore, the lower court’s determination contains an error that affected the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights and by failing to conduct the necessary examination. The Prosecutor’s assertion pointing out this point is well-founded.\\n\\nj. The part concerning Defendants B’s monitoring and reporting of Committee developments, among the parts concerning P and R in Number 1 of the crime list 2 in the lower court’s judgment\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to establish that Defendant B’s instructions constituted an “abuse” of official authority.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights.\\n\\nk. The part concerning the preparation of the document titled “Response Measures for Pending Issues Concerning the Committee” by Defendants A, B, C, and D\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to conclude that the acts of Defendants A, B, and C constituted, under statutes and regulations, “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do” with respect to H, T, and S, and that it was difficult to establish that Defendant D had conspired in and participated in this part of the offense.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding or omitting a determination regarding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights, the relationship of conspiracy, etc.\\n\\nl. The part concerning the preparation of the document titled “Review of the Possibility of a Committee Investigation into the President” by Defendants A, B, C, and D\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to conclude that Defendant A’s instruction to prepare the document constituted an “abuse” of official authority, and that it was difficult to establish that Defendants B, C, and D had conspired in and participated in Defendant A’s offense.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights, the relationship of conspiracy, etc.\\n\\nm. The part concerning the preparation of each of the documents titled “F Special Investigation Committee Requiring Special Investigation” and “Reference Materials for Breakfast with the Vice Chairperson of the Committee, etc., and Other Ruling Party-Recommended Commissioners” by Defendants A, B, C, and D\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found this part of the charged facts not guilty, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Prosecutor alone made it difficult to conclude that the acts of Defendants A, B, and C constituted, under statutes and regulations, “when a person is made to do something he is under no duty to do” with respect to H, T, and S, and that it was difficult to establish that Defendant D had conspired in and participated in this part of the offense.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding or omitting a determination regarding the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights, the relationship of conspiracy, etc.\\n\\nn. The part of dismissal of prosecution\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, held that, with respect to the part concerning “planning” and “implementation” of the various documents in this case (excluding the part concerning “implementation” of the document titled “Composition and Operation Plan of the Committee Support Team”), because the date, place, method, etc. of each individual act could not be specified, it could not be deemed that sufficient specificity had been achieved to such an extent that it would not impede the Defendants’ exercise of their right of defense, and therefore, in the reasons, held this to be a dismissal of prosecution.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, there is no error in the lower court’s above determination, such as misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the specificity of the charged facts.\\n\\n2. Determination on the grounds of appeal by Defendant B\\n\\nThe lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, found some of the parts concerning the monitoring and reporting of Committee developments among the charged facts against Defendant B guilty. Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, there is no error in the lower court’s determination, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the establishment of the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights, the timing of consummation, etc.\\n\\n3. Scope of reversal\\n\\nAmong the lower court judgment, the parts concerning the preparation of the Background and Response Measures Document against Defendant B, the parts concerning the monitoring and reporting of Committee developments (including the guilty parts), and the part concerning the preparation of the Background and Response Measures Document against Defendant E are all subject to reversal, as there are grounds for reversal or they are parts in a comprehensive single offense relationship with those parts, as seen above.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the parts of the lower court judgment concerning the preparation of the Background and Response Measures Document against Defendant B, the parts of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights concerning the monitoring and reporting of Committee developments (including the guilty parts), and the part of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights concerning the preparation of the Background and Response Measures Document against Defendant E are all reversed, and this case is remanded to the lower court for retrial and determination of those parts. The Prosecutor’s appeal against Defendants A, C, and D and the remaining appeals by Defendants B and E are all dismissed, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question: X, around 2024. 7. 5., asked A, “I am going to commit insurance fraud; if you hit me, I will give you money.” A hit X, and X paid cash as promised. Meanwhile, as a result of A’s act, X suffered injuries such as multiple contusions. Thereafter, in order to falsely accuse A, around 2024. 7. 10., X filed a complaint with the investigative authorities against A to the effect that “A assaulted me and then took the cash away.” Among the explanations concerning this case, which is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: Even if A assaulted X at X’s request, and in the process X suffered injuries such as multiple contusions, such request by X is ethically and morally contrary to social norms, so it is difficult to regard it as the victim’s consent, which is a ground excluding unlawfulness.
B: Although A’s act may constitute the offenses of assault or injury, X’s complaint alleges that A committed extortion or robbery, so it falls under a case in which part of the complaint facts is false.
C: Whether X was beaten according to X’s own will is an important part affecting the establishment of the offense of extortion or robbery, so the above complaint content corresponds to changing the character of the entire facts alleged in the complaint.
D: Because the offense of false accusation is a crime that incidentally protects the interest that an individual not be unjustly punished or disciplined, even if A consented to X’s complaint, it has no effect on the establishment of the offense of false accusation.
E: If the prosecutor determined that X was guilty of false accusation and indicted X for false accusation while deciding not to prosecute A, and X confessed to the false accusation in the trial proceedings regarding X’s own false-accusation offense, then because the non-prosecution decision against A was rendered, it does not fall under “before the judgment becomes final” prescribed by Articles 157 and 153 of the Criminal Act, and therefore the mitigation provisions for confession and voluntary surrender cannot be applied to X.
label: E

{"[2008DO9606]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nUnder Article 24 of the Criminal Act, the victim’s consent, by which unlawfulness is negated, must not only be the consent of a person who may legally dispose of the property in cases where personal legal interests are infringed, but such consent must also not be contrary to social norms in an ethical and moral sense (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 85DO1892 rendered on December 10, 1985).\\n\\nThe court below, after recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion, determined that, if the Defendant inflicted injury on the victim for the purpose of defrauding insurance proceeds by colluding with the victim and feigning a traffic accident, then even if the victim had consented, such consent was intended to be used for an unlawful purpose, and therefore it could not be said that the Defendant’s act was rendered lawful by the victim’s consent. In light of the legal principle stated above and the record, the court below’s determination is proper, and there is no illegality in it, such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the victim’s consent, as argued in the grounds for appeal, or violation of the principle of definiteness under the principle of legality.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and some of the period of detention after the filing of the appeal is counted toward the principal sentence. It is so adjudged, by unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the operative part."}

{"[2010DO2745]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. As to the point of violation of the rules of evidence\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment of the court below, the court below, after finding the circumstances as stated in its opinion based on the evidence it adopted, determined that even though the Defendant first asked Non-indicted Persons 1 and 2 (hereinafter referred to as “Non-indicted Persons 1, etc.”) to hit him and promised to give them money if they did so, and Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. then hit the Defendant and received the wallet from the Defendant and took the cash therein, it was sufficiently established that the Defendant falsely accused Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. by reporting false facts to the effect that “Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. assaulted the Defendant and then took away the cash” in order to counter the fact that Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. reported the Defendant as a sexual molestation offender, and thus affirmed as is the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged in this case guilty. In light of the record, such measures of the court below are based on the reasonable free evaluation of evidence by the fact-finding judge and are proper, and it cannot be deemed that there is any illegality in violation of the rules of evidence as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. As to the point of misunderstanding of legal principles\\nThe crime of false accusation is established when a person reports false facts to a public office or a public official for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal punishment or disciplinary punishment. Here, the reporting of false facts means reporting while recognizing, definitively or at least contingently, that the reported facts are contrary to objective facts. Thus, even if some false facts are included in the reported facts, if the false portion is not an important part affecting the establishment of the crime and is merely an exaggeration of the reported facts, it does not constitute false accusation. However, where the partly false facts change the overall character of the complaint to such an extent that they are likely to mislead the State’s adjudicatory function or infringe upon an individual’s legal stability not to be punished unjustly, false accusation may be established (see Supreme Court Decision dated January 16, 2004, 2003DO7178).\\nFirst, according to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the evidence lawfully adopted by the court below, it can be understood that the Defendant requested to be hit and said that he would give money if they did so, and Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. assaulted the Defendant, and in the course of that, the Defendant suffered injuries such as multiple contusions; under such circumstances, even if the Defendant first asked Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. to hit him, such request by the Defendant would be morally and ethically contrary to social norms, and therefore cannot be deemed to constitute the victim’s consent as a ground excluding unlawfulness. However, even if Non-indicted Persons 1, etc.’s above acts are ultimately unlawful, they may constitute the crimes of assault or injury, whereas the facts reported by the Defendant were that Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. committed the crime of extortion or robbery, so it is clear from any perspective that part of the reported facts is false. Meanwhile, whether the Defendant was assaulted pursuant to his own will is an important part affecting the establishment of the crime of extortion or robbery, and cannot be regarded as merely an exaggeration of the reported facts. Moreover, insofar as it is clear that Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. did not assault the Defendant with the intent of extortion or robbery but did so at the Defendant’s request, the Defendant’s report to the effect that “Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. assaulted the Defendant and took his money” is deemed to have changed the overall character of the complaint to such an extent that the false facts concerning only the circumstances of the assault may mislead the State’s adjudicatory function or infringe upon an individual’s legal stability not to be punished unjustly.\\n\\nAccordingly, in light of the foregoing legal principles, the Defendant’s above report is deemed to fall under “the reporting of false facts,” which is the objective element of the crime of false accusation, and furthermore, since the Defendant also recognized that the contents of his report concerning the circumstances of the assault were contrary to objective facts, the intent for false accusation is also established; therefore, the court below’s measure of affirming as is the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged in this case guilty on the same basis is proper, and there is no illegality of misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of false accusation as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\nOn the other hand, the argument that the Defendant’s act is a justifiable act that does not violate social norms is a new argument raised at the final appeal stage and cannot constitute a lawful ground of final appeal, and even if examined based on the record, the Defendant’s act cannot be viewed as a justifiable act that does not violate social norms.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the case."}

{"[2010DO2745]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. As to the point of violation of the rules governing the weighing of evidence\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the lower court judgment, the lower court, after recognizing the circumstances as set forth in its opinion based on the evidence adopted, determined that, although the Defendant had first said to Non-indicted Persons 1 and 2 (hereinafter referred to as “Non-indicted Persons 1, etc.”) that he would give them money if they beat him, and Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. beat the Defendant and took the wallet from the Defendant and carried away the cash contained therein, the Defendant, after Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. reported him as a sexual harassment offender, falsely reported facts to the effect that “Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. assaulted the Defendant and then took the cash away” in order to counter that report, thereby sufficiently constituting a false accusation against Non-indicted Persons 1, etc.; accordingly, it affirmed the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged in this case guilty. In light of the record, such disposition by the lower court is based on the reasonable free evaluation of evidence by the judge of fact and is justifiable; there is no illegality of the kind asserted in the grounds of appeal, namely, a violation of the rules governing the weighing of evidence.\\n\\n2. As to the point of misunderstanding of legal principles\\n\\nThe crime of false accusation is established when a person reports false facts to a public office or public official for the purpose of causing another to receive criminal punishment or disciplinary action. Here, a report of false facts means reporting while definitively or at least contingently recognizing that the reported facts are contrary to objective truth. Thus, even if false facts are included in part of the reported facts, if the false portion is not an important part affecting the establishment or non-establishment of the crime and is merely an exaggeration of the reported facts, it does not constitute false accusation; however, when the false part changes the nature of the entire facts alleged in the complaint to such an extent as to risk misleading the State’s adjudicative function or infringing upon an individual’s legal stability not to be punished unjustly, the crime of false accusation may be established (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2004. 1. 16., 2003DO7178).\\n\\nFirst, according to the reasons stated in the lower court judgment and the evidence lawfully adopted by the lower court, it can be understood that the Defendant made a request to be beaten and said that he would give money if they beat him, and Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. assaulted the Defendant, and in the process the Defendant suffered injuries such as multiple contusions. Under such circumstances, even if the Defendant had first asked Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. to beat him, such request by the Defendant would be ethically and morally contrary to social norms, and thus cannot be regarded as the victim’s consent as a ground excluding unlawfulness. However, even if the above acts by Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. were ultimately unlawful, they may correspond to the crime of assault or injury, whereas the facts reported by the Defendant were that Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. had committed the crime of extortion or robbery, so that the fact that part of the reported facts was false is manifest from any perspective. Yet whether the Defendant was assaulted according to his own will is an important part affecting the establishment or non-establishment of the crime of extortion or robbery, and cannot be regarded as merely an exaggeration of the reported facts. Moreover, since it is clear that Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. did not assault the Defendant with the intent of extortion or robbery, but rather did so at the Defendant’s request, the Defendant’s report to the effect that “Non-indicted Persons 1, etc. assaulted the Defendant and took his money” is deemed to have changed the nature of the entire facts alleged in the complaint to such an extent that the false facts concerning the circumstances of the assault alone could mislead the State’s adjudicative function or infringe upon the legal stability of the individual who should not be unjustly punished.\\n\\nTherefore, in light of the legal principles above, the Defendant’s above report is deemed to fall under “reporting false facts,” the objective element of the crime of false accusation; furthermore, since the Defendant also recognized that the content of his report regarding the circumstances of the assault was contrary to objective facts, the intent for false accusation is also established. Accordingly, the lower court’s disposition, which affirmed the first-instance judgment finding the facts charged in this case guilty on the same reasoning, is justifiable, and there is no illegality of misunderstanding of legal principles concerning the crime of false accusation as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the argument that the Defendant’s act is a justifiable act not contrary to social norms is a new argument at the appellate trial stage and therefore cannot serve as a lawful ground of appeal; furthermore, even upon review of the record, the Defendant’s act cannot be regarded as a justifiable act not contrary to social norms.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the order by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2018DO7293]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Articles 157 and 153 of the Criminal Act provide that if a person who has committed the offense of false accusation confesses or voluntarily surrenders before the judgment or disciplinary disposition on the reported case becomes final and conclusive, the punishment shall be reduced or exempted, thereby establishing such confession before the judgment becomes final and conclusive as a mandatory ground for mitigation or exemption. As to the procedure for such confession, there are no statutory restrictions; therefore, confession to the agency handling the case reported by the person, or appearing again as a witness before the court handling that case and confessing that the report previously made by the person was false, as well as confession through examination by a court or investigative agency as a defendant or suspect in a false accusation case, falls within the concept of confession (see Supreme Court Decision 73DO1639, Nov. 27, 1973; Supreme Court Decision 2012DO2783, June 14, 2012, etc.).\\n\\nThe “before the judgment becomes final and conclusive” under Article 153 of the Criminal Act also includes cases where, as a result of the investigation of the Defendant’s complaint case, the suspicion of false accusation against the Defendant is revealed, an indictment is filed against the Defendant, and a non-prosecution disposition is rendered against the complainant, so that judicial proceedings have not been commenced.\\n\\n2. a. According to the record, the following circumstances can be ascertained.\\n\\n(1) The Defendant filed a complaint against Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 alleging the offense of fraud, and as a result of the investigation into that complaint case, the suspicion of false accusation against the Defendant was revealed, and the Defendant was indicted in this case.\\n\\n(2) The Defendant denied the facts charged in this case at the first instance, but, as the Defendant appealed the first-instance conviction on the ground of improper sentencing, it can be seen that, on the first trial date before the lower court, the Defendant stated a written statement of grounds for appeal containing the purport of both an appeal on the ground of improper sentencing and admission of all the facts charged in this case.\\n\\nb. Examining these facts in light of the above legal principles, it is clear that the Defendant confessed before the lower court that he or she had filed a false complaint. Therefore, the lower court should have examined the result of handling the complaint case falsely filed against Non-party 1 and Non-party 2, and if no non-prosecution disposition, etc. had been rendered against them and their judgment had never become final and conclusive, the lower court should have taken mandatory measures to reduce or exempt the punishment pursuant to Articles 157 and 153 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\n3. Nevertheless, without conducting such examination, the lower court dismissed the Defendant’s appeal. The lower court’s determination contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles regarding confession, which is a mandatory ground for reduction or exemption of punishment, while failing to conduct the necessary examination. The grounds of appeal pointing out this issue are well taken.\\n\\n4. Since the Defendant’s appeal is well-founded, the judgment of the lower court is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court as ordered."}

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: If the defendant, fearing that he himself would directly be subjected to criminal punishment or disciplinary action, destroyed material that would serve as evidence for his own benefit, then even if that act simultaneously resulted in the destruction of evidence relating to another accomplice’s criminal case or disciplinary case, it cannot be punished as the crime of destruction of evidence.
B: If the defendant, with the intent to drive under the influence of alcohol, got drunk and then proceeded to drive and caused a traffic accident, the defendant had foreseen the risk of causing a traffic accident while intoxicated, and therefore falls under the case of voluntarily causing a state of mental and physical disorder; accordingly, under Article 10(3) of the Criminal Act, mitigation or other reduction on account of mental and physical disorder cannot be granted.
C: If a sworn witness, after being notified of the right to refuse testimony, did not exercise the right to refuse testimony and made a false statement, then since it cannot be said that there was no possibility of expecting lawful conduct, the witness cannot be exempted from punishment for perjury.
D: The review of “justifiable reason” under Article 16 of the Criminal Act presupposes that the actor had an opportunity to deliberate on or inquire into the possibility that his act was unlawful, and made a sincere effort to avoid it by exerting all of his intellectual capacity; at that time, the degree of effort required is to be assessed by considering the concrete circumstances of the act and the individual actor’s cognitive capacity, but not differently depending on the social group to which the actor belongs.
E: Even if a person has a mental disorder, if at the time of the offense he or she had normal capacity to distinguish objects or to control conduct, that person cannot be regarded as falling under the mental and physical disorder prescribed in Article 10 of the Criminal Act.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2014DO12773]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Facts charged\\n\\nThe gist of the facts charged in this case is that “the Defendant, as the manager of a private school, ○○○○○○○ School (hereinafter referred to as “○○ School”), despite the fact that a private school manager may not transfer or lend revenues belonging to the school accounting to another accounting, lent KRW 220 million of revenues belonging to the school accounting of ○○ School to △△△△△ School (hereinafter referred to as “△△ School”) on 2011. 1. 4., and, from then until 2011. 5. 31., lent a total of KRW 13,642,300,000 of revenues belonging to the school accounting of ○○ School to △△ School on 12 occasions in total, as stated in the attached schedule of offenses to the judgment of the court below (hereinafter referred to as the “schedule of offenses”).”\\n\\n2. Judgment on the criminal acts stated in items 6 and 8 of the schedule of offenses\\n\\nThe court below found the Defendant not guilty of the facts charged at issue, holding that, with respect to the offenses stated in items 6 and 8 of the schedule of offenses among the facts charged in this case, it could not be ruled out that the chief administrator of ○○ School, a person not indicted, may have independently instructed the transfer, and therefore it was difficult to find, based only on the evidence submitted by the prosecution, that the above facts charged were proven to the extent of excluding a reasonable doubt.\\n\\nAs grounds for final appeal, the Prosecutor contends that the court below violated the rules of evidence and erroneously found facts, thereby finding the above facts charged not guilty. However, so long as fact-finding, the selection and evaluation of evidence do not exceed the limits of free evaluation of evidence, they fall within the exclusive authority of the fact-finding court. Even upon examining the reasoning of the judgment of the court below in light of the record, there is no error in the court below’s determination, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, in that it ran counter to the rules of logic and experience and exceeded the limits of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\n3. Judgment on the criminal acts stated in items 1 through 5, 7, and 9 through 12 of the schedule of offenses\\n\\nA. The court below acquitted the Defendant of the offenses stated in items 1 through 5, 7, and 9 through 12 of the schedule of offenses among the facts charged in this case for the following reasons.\\n\\nAlthough the Defendant reported the lending of the above funds at the School Operation Committee of ○○ School attended by public officials from Gyeonggi-do and Suwon City, the said public officials did not raise any particular objection, and the accounting firm, after auditing ○○ School, also did not point out that the lending of funds to △△ School violated the relevant statutes. The Defendant mistakenly believed that, although lending of funds between general schools could be unlawful, lending of funds between foreign schools was an act permitted under the statutes and thus did not constitute a crime, and it can be assessed that he made earnest efforts to avoid the possible unlawfulness of his own conduct; accordingly, there is justifiable reason for not having recognized its unlawfulness.\\n\\nB. However, the above determination of the court below cannot be sustained for the following reasons.\\n\\n(1) Article 16 of the Criminal Act provides that a person who acts under a mistake that his or her act does not constitute a crime under the statutes shall not be punished only when there is a justifiable reason for such mistake. This means that, generally, although an offense is established, if a person mistakenly believes, in light of his or her special circumstances, that the act is permitted under the statutes and thus does not constitute a crime, and there is a justifiable reason for such belief, the person shall not be punished. In such a case, whether there is a justifiable reason should be determined depending on whether, had the actor had an opportunity to deliberate upon or inquire into the possibility that his or her act was unlawful and had made earnest efforts to avoid it by exerting his or her intellectual capacity to the fullest, the actor would have been able to recognize the unlawfulness of his or her act, yet failed to do so and, as a result, did not recognize the unlawfulness of the act. The degree of effort required for such recognition of unlawfulness should be assessed differently depending on the concrete circumstances of the act, the individual actor’s capacity for recognition, and the social group to which the actor belongs (see Supreme Court Decision 2005DO3717 rendered on 2006. 3. 24., etc.).\\n\\nThe former Private School Act (as amended by Act No. 12125 on 2013. 12. 30.; hereinafter the same) aims to promote the sound development of private schools by securing their autonomy and enhancing their public character in light of the special nature of private schools (Article 1). Under this Act, a “private school manager” means a juridical person or natural person other than a public entity that establishes and manages a private school pursuant to this Act, the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, etc. (Article 2(3)); among the accounts of a school foundation, the accounts belonging to the school are classified into the school accounting and the affiliated hospital accounting (only where there is an affiliated hospital) (Article 29(1), (2)); and revenues belonging to the school accounting may not be transferred or lent to another accounting (Article 29(6)). Furthermore, Articles 51 and 73-2 of the former Private School Act provide that a private school manager shall be punished when he or she violates Article 29(6), and Article 67, while setting forth a special rule that the provisions of Articles 52 through 66-2 concerning the qualifications, appointment and dismissal, service, status guarantee and social security, and disciplinary measures for private-school teachers shall not apply to foreign schools, does not exclude the application of Article 29(6).\\n\\nConsidering the wording and structure of the above provisions together with the legislative purpose of the former Private School Act, if a private school manager who operates a private foreign school transfers or lends revenues belonging to the school accounting to another accounting, he or she shall be punished (see Supreme Court Decision 2011DO12408 rendered on 2012. 5. 10., etc.).\\n\\nThe former Elementary and Secondary Education Act (as amended by Act No. 11384 on 2012. 3. 21.; hereinafter the same) provides that national and public elementary schools, middle schools, high schools, and special schools shall have school accounting established (Article 30-2(1)), and provides that Article 30-2, etc. shall not apply to foreign schools (Article 60-2(1)). However, this merely clarifies that the provisions concerning the establishment and operation of school accounting for national and public schools (Articles 30-2 and 30-3) do not apply to foreign schools, which the former Elementary and Secondary Education Act and the relevant statutes contemplate only as private schools; this does not mean that, for that reason, the application by analogy of Article 29 of the former Private School Act is excluded for the manager of a private foreign school.\\n\\n(2) According to the reasoning of the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts may be found.\\n\\n(a) The Defendant operated △△ School, a private foreign school, as its superintendent from around 1996. 9.\\n\\n(b) On 2005. 1. 27., the Defendant concluded an agreement on the establishment and operation of ○○ School with Gyeonggi-do and Suwon City, stipulating that “Gyeonggi-do will provide construction costs, Suwon City will lease the school site free of charge, and the Defendant will operate the school,” and received approval for the establishment of ○○ School from the Superintendent of the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education around 2006. 6. 12., thereafter managing it as superintendent.\\n\\n(c) While promoting a project to newly construct and relocate the school building of △△ School, the Defendant lent KRW 220 million of revenues belonging to the school accounting of ○○ School to △△ School on 2011. 1. 4. when construction funds were insufficient, and thereafter, until 2011. 5. 31., lent a total of KRW 11,442,300,000, as stated in items 1 through 5, 7, and 9 through 12 of the schedule of offenses.\\n\\n(d) At the board of directors meeting of ○○ School held on 2009. 9. 3., a resolution was adopted to the effect that “○○ School lends funds to △△ School within the scope financially feasible according to Korean law standards,” but the Defendant did not, with respect to whether such lending of funds was lawful, obtain a reply by inquiring of the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education or seek advice from a legal expert.\\n\\n(3) In light of the above facts and the contents of the relevant statutes as examined above, ○○ School and △△ School are separate schools, each of which received approval for establishment; therefore, lending revenues belonging to the school accounting of ○○ School to △△ School is prohibited under Article 29(6) of the former Private School Act. The Defendant did not take measures such as accurately providing information to and obtaining a reply from the public official in charge at the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education, which is the competent authority, or seeking advice from a legal expert regarding whether the above lending act was lawful. The mere facts that the Defendant was a foreigner and not proficient in the Korean language, or that he reported the agenda item of lending funds to △△ School at the School Operation Committee of ○○ School attended by public officials from Gyeonggi-do and Suwon City, who were merely parties to the agreement on the establishment and operation of ○○ School, do not mean that the Defendant made earnest efforts to avoid the possibility of unlawfulness by exerting his intellectual capacity to the fullest. Nor can this be viewed differently on the basis of circumstances such as that, after the lending of funds to △△ School was completed as above, the accounting firm did not point out its unlawfulness, or that the public official in charge at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education responded to a civil complaint to a third party to the effect that “Article 29 of the former Private School Act does not apply to foreign schools.” Therefore, even if the Defendant mistakenly believed that the act of lending revenues belonging to the school accounting of ○○ School to △△ School was legally permitted and thus did not constitute a crime, such mistaken belief cannot be deemed to have had a justifiable reason.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below found the facts charged relating to this portion not guilty, and thus the court below’s determination contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal doctrine on mistake of law. The ground for final appeal asserting this point is well-founded.\\n\\n(4) Accordingly, the not-guilty portion concerning items 1 through 5, 7, and 9 through 12 of the schedule of offenses in the judgment of the court below must be reversed, and since this portion and the portion concerning items 6 and 8 of the schedule of offenses, which the court below found not guilty, stand in a relationship of a comprehensive single offense, they necessarily must be reversed together; ultimately, the entire judgment of the court below must be reversed.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nThe Prosecutor’s final appeal is well-founded, and the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for a new trial and determination. Accordingly, the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by unanimous agreement of the Justices of the Supreme Court participating in the decision."}

{"[92DO1425]": "We consider the grounds of appeal by the Defendant’s counsel.\\n\\n1. The criminal facts recognized by the judgment of the first instance court are that the Defendant, at the place and in the manner stated in the judgment, took out in his right hand and swung a kitchen knife 34 cm in length that he had been carrying in the inner pocket of his jumper, because Nonparty 1, an employee at a tea room who had gone to have a meal with the Defendant, intended to return before the time despite having received the time charge, and, enraged because the victim Nonparty 2 (female, ○○ years old), who was working in the kitchen of the restaurant, blocked and restrained the Defendant, stabbed the victim once each in the left shoulder, left back, and left abdomen with the kitchen knife he was holding, thereby causing the victim to die at a hospital at around 11:20 on the same day from cardiac arrest due to penetration of the left ventricle by a stab wound to the left side of the abdomen and back. The court below, with respect to the Defendant’s assertion that he committed the above offense in a state of loss of capacity or diminished capacity due to mental disorder arising from mental abnormality, held that, when the circumstances leading to the Defendant’s commission of the instant offense as recognized by various pieces of evidence lawfully examined and admitted by the first instance court (particularly the contents of the psychiatric evaluation report prepared by Doctor Nonparty 3), the means and method of the offense, the Defendant’s conduct before and after the offense, and the circumstances after the offense are comprehensively reviewed, it cannot be recognized that the Defendant was in a state of loss of capacity or diminished capacity at the time of the instant offense, and accordingly rejected the above assertion and upheld the first instance judgment sentencing the Defendant to imprisonment for 10 years.\\n\\n2. However, mental disorder prescribed in Article 10 of the Criminal Act requires, as a biological element, a mental impairment such as psychosis, mental retardation, or an abnormal mental state, and also, as a psychological element, that due to such mental impairment the capacity to distinguish matters and the corresponding capacity to control conduct have been lost or diminished; therefore, even if a person has a mental impairment, he or she cannot be regarded as suffering from mental disorder if, at the time of the offense, he or she had normal capacity to distinguish matters or control conduct. However, where the mental impairment is a fixed mental illness such as schizophrenia, even if the offender’s state of consciousness in the process leading to the offense and in feeling the impulse to commit the offense appears to be the same as that of a normal person, failure to suppress the impulse to commit the offense is often likely to be related to the mental illness, and in such a case there is room to view it as diminished capacity because the mental illness has lowered the capacity to control conduct.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Defendant is a person suffering from paranoid schizophrenia, and on 1983.10.28, as his schizophrenic symptoms flared up and he murdered his wife, he was subjected to a treatment and custody disposition and had a history of receiving treatment and custody until 1990.12.5. Further, in the prosecution investigation concerning this case, the Defendant stated, “For about 3 months, it seemed as if someone was watching me and following me, trying to kill me, and when I thought about it that morning, I felt I could no longer endure it, so I put a kitchen knife in the inner pocket of my jumper and thought I would meet the above person and confront him, but as I could not find him anywhere, I came to Gangneung intending to drink as much as I could and commit suicide,” and “···This time I came to commit suicide, but because I got drunk from drinking, my emotions suddenly exploded and I swung the knife; if I had not been drunk, I would not have done such an act.” Meanwhile, according to the psychiatric evaluation report prepared by Doctor Nonparty 3, which the court below admitted, although the Defendant has paranoid schizophrenia, the instant offense was not related to auditory hallucinations or persecutory delusions; rather, it is presumed that the instant homicide was caused by the Defendant’s suppressed anger, which had been intended for suicide, not being suppressed due to alcohol and being directed toward another person. In conclusion, the report evaluates to the effect that although the Defendant biologically has schizophrenia, it is difficult to think that he did not know the unlawfulness of homicide at the time of the offense, and although his inhibitory function was lowered due to alcohol, it is difficult to view him as lacking decision-making capacity.\\n\\nIn light of the above factual relationship, it can be seen that the Defendant, as a person with a mental impairment of paranoid schizophrenia, was unable to suppress the impulse to commit the offense at the time of the offense and came to commit the offense; even if the impulse to commit the offense felt by the Defendant did not directly arise from the auditory hallucinations or persecutory delusions that are symptoms of the above mental illness, if a normal person could suppress such an impulse with only that amount of alcohol (the Defendant stated in the prosecution that he was slightly drunk), but the Defendant’s suppressive capacity was lowered by his mental illness so that he could not suppress the impulse and proceeded to commit the offense, there would be room to view the mental illness as constituting the cause of diminished capacity to control conduct.\\n\\nThe court below should have determined whether the Defendant’s reduced ability to suppress the impulse to commit the offense was related not only to alcohol but also to the mental illness from which the Defendant was suffering, and then should have determined whether there was diminished capacity; however, without doing so, it made the above determination, and in doing so committed an error of failing to conduct sufficient deliberation, thereby affecting the judgment. The argument is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed and remanded, and the judgment is rendered as ordered, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[92DO999]": "We examine the grounds of appeal filed by counsel for the Defendant.\\n\\n1. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below found the Defendant guilty of both the offense of violating Article 5-3(2) item 1 of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes and the offense of violating Article 107-2 item 1 of the Road Traffic Act, and punished him as concurrent offenses; however, since there was a decision of the Constitutional Court that Article 5-3(2) item 1 of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes is unconstitutional as of 1992.4.28., said provision must be deemed to have retroactively lost its effect, and therefore the judgment of the court below applying said provision is unlawful and can no longer be maintained, so the grounds of appeal pointing out this point are well-founded.\\n\\n2. In addition, the grounds of appeal criticize as unlawful the court below’s action of applying Article 10(3) of the Criminal Act and not mitigating the punishment for the Defendant due to mental and physical disorder.\\n\\nArticle 10(3) of the Criminal Act provides that “the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall not apply to the act of a person who, foreseeing the occurrence of danger, voluntarily caused his mental and physical disorder,” and this provision includes not only a free act in the cause by intent but also a free act in the cause by negligence, so that it would also apply where a person, although able to foresee the occurrence of danger, voluntarily caused his mental and physical disorder.\\n\\nThe court below, in the same purport, determined that in this case, where the Defendant, with the intent to drive under the influence of alcohol, got drunk and then proceeded to drive, causing the traffic accident as stated in the judgment, the Defendant had foreseen the risk of causing a traffic accident while drinking and voluntarily caused his mental and physical disorder, and therefore mitigation, etc. due to mental and physical disorder could not be granted pursuant to Article 10(3) of the Criminal Act. Such determination is proper and there is no illegality as alleged; accordingly, the grounds of appeal on this point are without merit.\\n\\n3. Therefore, omitting determination on the remaining grounds of appeal, and reversing and remanding the judgment of the court below for the reason pointed out in paragraph 1 above, we render judgment as follows by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating in the case."}

{"[94DO2608]": "1. The grounds of appeal by Defendant 3 and Defendant 4 are examined.\\n\\nIn light of the record, the evidence admitted by the judgment of the first instance cited by the judgment of the court below sufficiently supports the criminal facts of the making of false official documents and the utterance and use thereof as found in the judgment against Defendant 3 and Defendant 4; it is also clear that the passenger safety inspection record referred to in the judgment constitutes an official document, as a document prepared by a ship inspector who inspected a passenger vessel every month pursuant to the Passenger Ship Safety Management Guidelines (Directive of the Maritime and Port Administration) and entered the results therein. Since the said Defendants fabricated the document referred to in the judgment as if they had carried out the ship safety inspection and safety training at the stated time, without actually doing so, they must be deemed to have had knowledge of the false nature of the official document. Accordingly, the judgment of the court below, which found the said Defendants guilty, is correct, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality such as an error of fact due to violation of the rules of evidence, incomplete examination, or misapprehension of legal principles, as alleged. The judgment of this Court cited by the argument is distinguishable in its facts and cannot be invoked in this case.\\n\\nAll the arguments are without merit.\\n\\n2. The grounds of appeal by Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 (including the portions supplementing the grounds of appeal in each supplemental statement of grounds of appeal submitted by Defendant 2 after the expiration of the period) are examined.\\n\\n(a) On the offense of damage to public documents\\n\\nIn light of the record, the evidence set forth in the judgment of the first instance cited by the judgment of the court below sufficiently supports the criminal facts of damage to public documents as found in the judgment against Defendant 1 and Defendant 2, and the judgment of the court below is not flawed, as alleged, by violation of the rules of evidence, incomplete examination, or lack of reasoning, in that it found facts based on evidence lacking credibility. Moreover, it is clear that the certificate of overcapacity operation referred to in the judgment was arbitrarily removed from the boarding and inspection file kept at the government office, and thus constitutes the object of the offense of damage to public documents. Further, in light of the circumstances of the conspiracy and execution of the offense revealed by the evidence above, the said Defendants should be deemed co-principals in the offense of damage to public documents. Therefore, the judgment of the court below, which held to this effect, is correct, and no illegality such as misapprehension of legal principles, as alleged, can be found therein. Even upon examining the statement of grounds of appeal filed by Defendant 1, it cannot be regarded as asserting the alleged error of fact or misapprehension of legal principles as a ground of appeal, and thus the judgment of the court below cannot be said to be illegal for failure to decide this point.\\n\\nAll the arguments on this point by the said Defendants are without merit.\\n\\n(b) On the offense of destruction of evidence\\n\\nThe offense of destruction of evidence is established when a person destroys evidence concerning another person’s criminal case or disciplinary case. Therefore, if a Defendant, fearing that he himself would directly be subjected to criminal punishment or disciplinary action, destroyed material to be used as evidence for his own benefit, then even if such act simultaneously resulted in the destruction of evidence concerning another accomplice’s criminal case or disciplinary case, it cannot be punished as the offense of destruction of evidence (see Supreme Court Decision 75DO1446, rendered June 22, 1976). This legal principle should likewise apply even if the act resulted in the destruction of evidence concerning a criminal case or disciplinary case of a person who is not the Defendant’s accomplice.\\n\\nThe court below, upon finding that the said Defendants, when the Prosecutors’ Office requested submission of documents concerning the Port Authority’s performance of duties related to the safe operation of the vessel in connection with the sinking incident of the vessel at issue, were already aware that officials of the Maritime Affairs Division of the Port Authority had discovered the fact that the said vessel had operated in excess of its capacity and had received and kept four certificates of overcapacity operation from the captain and others, but had taken no measures in response and left the matter unattended, and that the Port Authority officials, including the said Defendants, were fearing criminal punishment and disciplinary action, held, as stated in the judgment below, that they sequentially instructed the co-defendant in the first instance, who was not a party to this appeal, to burn the four certificates of overcapacity operation, and that the said co-defendant burned them, thereby impairing the utility of the said documents and at the same time destroying evidence in the case concerning violation of the Ship Safety Act against the co-defendant in the first instance who had been indicted and detained in connection with the vessel’s overcapacity operation, and on that basis cited the factual findings of the first instance. The court below further punished the said Defendants for the concurrent offenses of damage to public documents and destruction of evidence. However, even according to the criminal facts themselves as found by the court below, the said Defendants destroyed the material that would constitute evidence for their own benefit because they feared that they themselves would directly be subjected to criminal punishment or disciplinary action. Thus, even though the act of the said Defendants simultaneously resulted in the destruction of evidence concerning a separate offense against the co-defendant in the first instance, it cannot be punished as the offense of destruction of evidence.\\n\\nTherefore, the above determination by the court below contains an illegality in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the offense of destruction of evidence. Meanwhile, since the court below found all several offenses in the relation of ideal concurrence to be guilty, and such finding, as distinguished from the case where only part thereof is found guilty, creates a difference in considering sentencing factors and thus affects the result of the judgment (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 80DO384, rendered December 9, 1980), the portion of the judgment below concerning the said Defendants cannot be saved from reversal.\\n\\n3. Accordingly, the portion of the judgment below concerning Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 is reversed, and this case is remanded to the court below for further proceedings on that portion. The appeals by Defendant 3 and Defendant 4 are all dismissed. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: A (age 5)'s father, A, recognized that A (age 5) was in danger of drowning at a place about 10 m away from himself at a beach, but, thinking that it did not matter even if A (age 5) drowned, took no action, and in the end A (age 5) died. Which of the following explanations concerning this case is incorrect? (In case of dispute, according to case law)
A: Causation between the omission of not performing the act and the result of death is recognized only where it is recognized that, had A carried out the duty to act, the result would not have occurred.
B: If A had only thought that someone was in danger of drowning and had not recognized that the person was A (age 5), then, according to the view that guarantor status is an element of the offense but the guarantor duty is an element of unlawfulness, A's omission constitutes the offense and is unlawful, but liability is excluded as a mistake of law only when there is a justifiable reason for such mistake.
C: In order for commencement of the execution of murder by omission to be recognized for A, the omission must be committed in a situation where the risk of A (age 5)'s death has become concrete, and at the time of omission A must recognize that he is engaging in conduct in violation of his duty to rescue and that, as a result, the risk of A (age 5)'s death arises.
D: If B was a lifeguard at the beach, and A and B each failed to discharge their duty of care and did not know that A (age 5) was in danger of drowning, and thereby failed to rescue A (age 5), then A may constitute negligent homicide by omission, and B may constitute occupational negligent homicide by omission, respectively.
E: In order to evaluate A's omission as the act of execution of murder, A must control the situation in which A (age 5) is placed so that the result of death can be easily prevented by performing the duty to rescue.
label: B

{"[2022DO16120]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nA person who bears a legal duty to act to prevent the occurrence of a result that infringes a protected legal interest and prohibited by the Criminal Act may be punished as an offense by omission if, although the occurrence of the result could easily have been prevented by performing that duty, he or she tolerated and stood by the occurrence of the result and failed to perform the duty, and such failure is deemed to be an act of execution of the crime (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2015DO15227 rendered on April 15, 2016).\\n\\nIn the offense of causing a fire by negligence, where a fire occurs due to the concurrence of mutual negligence, so long as each act of negligence has been one condition for the occurrence of the fire, the persons who jointly caused the fire cannot each be exempt from liability for the offense of causing a fire by negligence (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 82DO2279 rendered on May 10, 1983).\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in the judgment below, the court below found negligence by the Defendants in that they threw cigarette butts in the direction of the separated-waste collection area, while each Defendant, despite having a duty of care to prevent a fire in advance by checking whether the embers of the cigarette butts discarded by himself and the other person were still alive and completely extinguishing them, neglected such duty and casually left the scene, and further found that each Defendant’s negligence concurred and caused the fire at issue in this case, thereby recognizing each Defendant’s liability for the offense of causing a fire by negligence and convicting the Defendants on the alternative facts of the indictment.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the judgment below in light of the relevant legal principles and the admissible evidence properly admitted, there is no error in the court below’s determination that, by violating the rules of logic and experience, it did not go beyond the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, nor any error of misunderstanding the legal principles concerning breach of the duty of care and proximate causation in the offense of causing a fire by negligence.\\n\\nHowever, the portion of the court below’s determination to the effect that it is insufficient to find that the fire at issue in this case was caused by the act of any one of the Defendants may be misconstrued as meaning that the causative act of the occurrence of the result was not identified. Yet this may be construed as meaning that there is insufficient evidence to find which Defendant’s cigarette butt caused the fire at issue in this case, and this is an additional determination to the effect that, considering the Defendants’ work details, the time and place of the fire and the circumstances thereof, and the ease of the act for preventing infringement of the protected legal interest, the Defendants could sufficiently foresee that a fire could occur due to the cigarette embers of themselves and the other person, so they had a duty of care to check whether embers remained in each other’s cigarette butts and completely extinguish them, but in violation of that duty they flicked cigarette embers and threw away cigarette butts near the separated-waste collection area and left the scene without any measure, and that a causal relation is recognized between each Defendant’s breach of the duty of care and the occurrence of the fire at issue in this case; therefore, it is difficult to accept the Defendants’ argument, made on a different premise, that “because the causative act is unknown, the Defendants are not punishable for an attempted offense of causing a fire by negligence, or at least one of the Defendants cannot be found guilty of the offense of causing a fire by negligence.”\\n\\nAccordingly, we dismiss all appeals, and so adjudicate as follows by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

question:
14th Bar Examination, Criminal Law, Multiple-Choice Question 18. Which of the following is the correct combination of the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (X) regarding the offense of rape and indecent act by deceit or force? (In cases of dispute, according to precedents)
