question: A asked his friend B and C to contact them and proposed, “Let us snatch the bag of the person who withdraws money from the bank as he comes out.” Accordingly, B and C searched for a target for the offense outside the bank door, and A decided to wait with a passenger car parked on the roadway in front of the bank so as to pick up B and C after the snatching theft and flee. A few days later, B and C saw that A had withdrawn cash of 10 million won from the bank, put it in a bag, and was coming out, and began following behind A. While A was driving and following behind them, he suddenly became afraid of punishment, turned the steering wheel, and fled alone without saying a word. When A entered a narrow alley, B kept watch at the entrance, and C snatched away the bag A was holding in his hand as it was and ran off. The prosecutor indicted A, B, and C on the above criminal charges, and the court is conducting a combined trial of them. Which of the following statements concerning this is incorrect? (Where there is controversy, according to case law)
A: A fled alone and did not express an intention to withdraw to B and C, and B and C nevertheless proceeded with the criminal act; therefore, it is difficult to regard A as having withdrawn from the conspiracy relationship.
B: If, before the execution act, B clearly expressed to A and C his intention to withdraw and fled alone, he does not bear criminal liability as a co-principal offender with respect to the snatching theft that occurred thereafter.
C: Although A did not directly share in the execution act of the snatching theft at the scene, since his act can be evaluated as having committed the offense by using the acts of B and C as means of his own intent, he falls under co-principal offender of special larceny.
D: Even if B, a co-offender whose proceedings were severed, appeared as a witness at C's trial, was informed of the right to refuse to testify, and nevertheless made false statements to defend himself without exercising the right to refuse to testify, he is not punished for perjury.
E: If all other co-offenders except B deny the offense entirely and there is no other evidence, B cannot be convicted based solely on B's confession.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2007DO7835]": "We consider together the grounds of appeal filed by the Accused and the court-appointed defense counsel.\\n\\n1. Where the confession of the Accused is the sole evidence unfavorable to that Accused, it may not be used as evidence of guilt (Article 310 of the Criminal Procedure Act); therefore, if the facts charged are found guilty on the sole basis of the Accused’s confession without corroborative evidence, that very circumstance must be regarded as an illegality that affected the outcome of the judgment.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below maintained the judgment of the court of first instance, stating that although the court of first instance erred in failing to set forth, in the summary of evidence, corroborative evidence sufficient to support the Accused’s confession as to each of the offenses stated in paragraphs 7 and 8 of the facts charged, the statements recorded in the suspect interrogation protocol concerning Kim Yun-gyeong prepared by the judicial police officer, and the contents of the investigation report prepared by the judicial police officer, each of which the prosecutor submitted and the court below lawfully completed evidentiary examination of and admitted into evidence, were sufficient to support the Accused’s confession as to each of the offenses stated in the above facts charged, and therefore the above error by the court of first instance did not affect the outcome of the judgment. However, the judgment of the court below contains illegality that affected the outcome of the judgment by misinterpreting and misapplying Article 310 and Article 361-5, item 1 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\n2. Therefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the judgment below is reversed; and, because it is recognized as sufficient to render judgment based on the case record and the evidence examined up to the court below, this Court shall directly render judgment pursuant to Article 396 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nSince the judgment of the court of first instance contains error in finding the facts charged in paragraphs 7 and 8 guilty solely on the confession of the Accused without corroborative evidence, the judgment of the court of first instance is reversed, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, and a new judgment shall be rendered as follows.\\n\\nThe outline of the criminal facts and evidence is the same as the corresponding parts of the judgment of the court of first instance, except that, as corroborative evidence for paragraphs 7 and 8 of the facts charged, the statements recorded in the suspect interrogation protocol concerning Kim Yun-gyeong prepared by the judicial police officer and the contents of the investigation report prepared by the judicial police officer (Investigation Record, pp. 197 and 198) are added; accordingly, this is adopted as is pursuant to Article 399 and Article 369 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nIn light of the law, among each of the acts stated in the judgment, each offense of forging an official document stated in the judgment corresponds to Articles 225 and 30 of the Criminal Act, each offense of using a forged official document stated in the judgment corresponds to Articles 229, 225, and 30 of the Criminal Act, each offense of forging a private document stated in the judgment corresponds to Articles 231 and 30 of the Criminal Act, each offense of using a forged private document stated in the judgment corresponds to Articles 234, 231, and 30 of the Criminal Act, and each offense of obstruction of business stated in the judgment corresponds to Articles 314(1), 313, and 30 of the Criminal Act. Since there is a relation of ideal concurrence between the offense of using a forged official document and each offense of using a forged private document stated in paragraph 1 of the criminal facts found by the court of first instance, and between the offense of using a forged official document and the offense of using a forged private document stated in paragraph 4 of the criminal facts found by the court of first instance, the punishment shall be imposed by the sentence prescribed for each of the offenses of using a forged official document, which is the gravest or more grave offense. As to the remaining offenses other than each offense of forging an official document and using the forged official document, imprisonment shall be selected from among the prescribed punishments for each offense, and since the above offenses are concurrent offenses under the first sentence of Article 37 of the Criminal Act, within the range of the term of imprisonment increased by concurrent-offense aggravation pursuant to Article 38(1)(2) and Article 50 of the Criminal Act, the Accused shall be sentenced to imprisonment for 1 year and 6 months by applying concurrent-offense aggravation to the sentence prescribed for the offense of using a forged official document stated in paragraph 4 of the criminal facts found by the court of first instance, which has the heaviest punishment and the gravest offense, and pursuant to Article 57 of the Criminal Act, 65 days of detention before the pronouncement of the judgment of the court of first instance shall be credited toward the above sentence.\\n\\n3. For the foregoing reasons, the judgment below is reversed and decided as above, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the Disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2008DO1274]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe joint principal offense under Article 30 of the Criminal Act is the commission of a crime jointly by two or more persons, and, for a joint principal offense to be established, there must be, as a subjective requirement, a common intent to engage in joint perpetration, and, as an objective requirement, the factual commission of the crime through functional control over the act based on a common intent; and a common intent to engage in joint perpetration is not satisfied merely by recognizing another person’s criminal act and yet failing to restrain and acquiescing in it, but must consist in the joint undertaking of a specific criminal act in a common intent and in the execution of one’s own intent by utilizing the acts of other persons (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DO7477 rendered on March 28, 2003). And in the case of a co-principal based on conspiracy, if one of the conspirators withdraws from the conspiracy relationship before another conspirator reaches the act of execution, he or she shall not bear liability as a co-principal for the acts of the other conspirator thereafter (see Supreme Court Decision 95DO955 rendered on July 11, 1995), but because withdrawal from the conspiracy relationship requires eliminating the functional control over the act assumed through the conspiracy, if a conspirator participated in the conspiracy in a leading manner and influenced the execution by the other conspirator, he or she cannot be deemed to have withdrawn from the conspiracy relationship unless the influence exerted on the execution is removed, such as by actively endeavoring to prevent the crime.\\n\\nAccording to the evidence adopted by the court below and the record, the Defendant, who was 21 years old, conspired to commit robbery at around 11:00 p.m. on the night before the robbery and injury offense in this case with co-defendants 1, 2, and 3 in the lower court, who were 14 or 15 years old, and at that time the Defendant led the conspiracy by, among other things, holding a shovel and pretending to strike a person; after committing the offense of special larceny at around 1:30 a.m. on the day in question together with the above co-defendant 1, etc., the Defendant wandered around the area together with them and searched for a target for robbery until committing the robbery and injury offense in this case at around 4:30 a.m.; when the above co-defendants 1 and 2 discovered the victim and chased after him, the Defendant merely said, “Huh?” and told the above co-defendant 3 to follow them, and then, because of his corpulent build, could not follow the above co-defendants 1 and 2 and remained seated about 200 meters away from the scene of the crime; and in the end, the above co-defendants 1 and 2 chased the victim, assaulted him and rendered him unable to resist, and then robbed the victim of his wallet from the back pocket and inflicted on the victim injuries including a fracture of the right patella requiring about 7 weeks of treatment. From this, it can be seen that the Defendant is recognized to have committed the crime through functional control over the act based on a common intent to engage in joint perpetration with the above co-defendant 1, etc., and therefore is deemed to have been in a conspiracy relationship regarding the robbery and injury offense as described in the judgment; and if, when the above co-defendants 1 and 2, who were in such a conspiracy relationship, identified the victim as a target of robbery and chased after him, the Defendant merely reacted by saying, “Huh?”, then it cannot be said that the Defendant withdrew from the conspiracy relationship by, for example, dissuading the crime until the above co-defendants 1 and 2 commenced execution of the robbery and injury offense; accordingly, the Defendant cannot be exempted from criminal liability as a co-principal of the robbery and injury offense as described in the judgment.\\n\\nThe court below’s determination to the same effect is proper, and there is no violation of the rules of evidence assessment or misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the requirements for the establishment of a co-principal based on conspiracy or withdrawal from the conspiracy relationship, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and it is ordered that part of the number of days of detention after the appeal be included in the principal sentence, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices in attendance."}

{"[2023DO7528]": "We decide on the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. The lower court’s determination\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the lower court, on the premise that a co-defendant who is a co-offender may testify as a witness regarding the facts charged against another co-defendant, but even if such person becomes a witness, with respect to questions concerning his or her own criminal facts the status of defendant still continues to exist and such status takes precedence over the status of witness, and therefore even if a defendant made false statements within the scope of the right of defense, the defendant cannot be punished for perjury, maintained the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged in this case not guilty, holding that the statements made by the defendants in the underlying case were statements made within the scope of their right of defense and thus could not be punished as perjury even if false.\\n\\n2. The Supreme Court’s determination\\n\\na. Relevant legal principles\\n\\nArticle 12(2) of the Constitution provides that “all citizens shall not be compelled to make statements unfavorable to themselves in criminal cases,” and Article 283-2(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act also provides that “the defendant may not make a statement or may refuse to answer each question.” Accordingly, a co-defendant who is a co-offender has the status of a defendant in the relevant proceedings and therefore cannot testify as a witness concerning the facts charged against another co-defendant; however, once the proceedings are separated and such person is no longer in the status of a defendant, he or she may testify as a witness concerning the facts charged against another co-defendant (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2008DO3300 rendered on June 26, 2008).\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 148 of the Criminal Procedure Act recognizes the right to refuse testimony that may reveal facts for which the person himself or herself may be found guilty, in order to guarantee a defendant’s privilege against self-incrimination, and for the purpose of ensuring such right to refuse testimony, Article 160 of the Criminal Procedure Act provides that the presiding judge must notify the witness of the right to refuse testimony before examination. Therefore, even if witness competency is recognized for a co-defendant who is a co-offender whose proceedings have been separated, and such person is examined regarding his or her own criminal facts, it cannot be said that this infringes the defendant’s right to refuse to make a statement or privilege against self-incrimination.\\n\\nAccordingly, if, despite being notified of the right to refuse testimony pursuant to Article 160 of the Criminal Procedure Act in the witness examination procedure, a defendant whose witness competency is recognized as above gives false testimony without exercising the right to refuse testimony regarding his or her own criminal facts, perjury is established (see Supreme Court Decision 2012DO6848, 2012JEONDO143 rendered on October 11, 2012).\\n\\nb. The following facts can be ascertained from the record.\\n\\n1) In the first instance of the case in which the defendants were indicted on charges that they conspired to commit violations of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Economic Crimes (Embezzlement), etc. (Seoul Central District Court 2010GOHAP1732), at the trial date, when the prosecutor applied to have Defendant 1 testify as a witness against Defendant 2 and Defendant 2 testify as a witness against Defendant 1, respectively, the trial panel granted the applications.\\n\\n2) On the 37th trial date, on November 14, 2012, the court notified the defendants of its decision to separate each defendant’s case from the criminal case against the other co-defendant, and on the 38th trial date, on November 20, 2012, it notified the same decision with respect to Defendant 1, and thereafter examined the defendants as witnesses.\\n\\n3) Although the presiding judge of the above court notified the defendants on November 14, 2012 and on November 20 of the same month that they had the right to refuse testimony, the defendants, after taking the oath as witnesses, made statements without exercising the right to refuse testimony in response to the prosecutor’s questions concerning their own criminal facts.\\n\\nc. Examining these facts in light of the legal principles set forth above, the lower court judgment, which maintained the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged in this case not guilty, cannot be upheld for the following reasons.\\n\\n1) In the above case, each defendant’s criminal case was separated from the proceedings of the other co-defendant, and therefore a defendant in the status of a co-defendant who is a co-offender has witness competency against the other co-defendant.\\n\\n2) If, while the proceedings were so separated, the defendants, despite being notified of the right to refuse testimony, made false statements without exercising that right, then even if they were examined as witnesses regarding their own criminal facts, it cannot be said that their right to refuse to make a statement as defendants or their privilege against self-incrimination was infringed, and it is appropriate to view perjury as established.\\n\\nd. Nevertheless, the lower court, without making any determination as to whether the defendants’ testimony constituted false statements, maintained the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged in this case not guilty solely for the reasons stated above; thus, the lower court’s determination contains an error that misapprehended the legal principles concerning the establishment of perjury and affected the judgment.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the lower court judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further hearing and determination, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[71DO2277]": "Upon reviewing the grounds of appeal by Acting Prosecutor Kim Jin-wan for the Chief Prosecutor of the Gwangju High Prosecutors' Office,\\n\\nin the case of so-called co-principal offenders by conspiracy, it has been this Court’s prior precedent that, once a criminal act has been conspired, even if one does not thereafter directly participate in the act of execution, unless there are other special circumstances, one cannot escape the guilt of co-principal liability for the acts separately executed by the other conspirator(s) (Decided 1948.1.2, 4281HYEONGSANG4 Judgment). However, where one of the conspirators withdraws from the conspiratorial relationship before another conspirator reaches the act of execution, it should be held that he bears no responsibility as a co-principal for the acts of the other conspirator thereafter, and the manifestation of intent to withdraw need not necessarily be express.\\n\\nIn this case, according to the facts lawfully established by the lower court, the defendant was not present, having taken Victim 2 to a pharmacy in a nearby village around the time the offense causing the death of Victim 1 occurred; and further, upon examining the evidence stated in the first-instance judgment and cited by the lower court according to the record, it may be seen that, because of the facts constituting offense (1) among the facts charged (the facts of violating the Act on Punishment of Violent Acts, etc.), the defendant, upon seeing Victim 2 suffer the injuries as stated in the judgment and go to the drugstore, realized his own wrongdoing, restrained the other conspirators from trying again to assault the same person, and took the same person to a pharmacy about 400 meters away from there to receive emergency treatment (thereafter, the defendant returned home); and the facts suggest that the offense under Count (2) of the indictment (aggravated assault causing death) was committed solely by the other accomplices after the defendant had gone to the above pharmacy as stated above. Therefore, even if the defendant participated in the offense of violating the Act on Punishment of Violent Acts, etc. stated in Count (1) of the indictment, with respect to the offense of aggravated assault causing death, which is the fact stated in Count (2), the defendant may be deemed to have withdrawn, expressly or impliedly, from the conspiratorial relationship; accordingly, the lower court’s judgment premised on such purport is proper, and the argument premised on a contrary view cannot be accepted.\\n\\nTherefore, by the unanimous opinion of all participating Justices, the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition."}

{"[98DO231]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe gist of the facts charged for the offense of fraud against the Defendants, which the court below found not guilty, is that the Defendants conspired to purchase a vehicle on which installment payments remained outstanding and then sell that vehicle as if it were a vehicle with no remaining installment payments, thereby defrauding the purchase price; specifically, although the Credos passenger car purchased by Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 from Non-Indicted Party 1 still had outstanding installment payments, on February 21, 1997, Defendant 2, while disguising himself as if he were Non-Indicted Party 1, falsely told victim Non-Indicted Party 2 that there were no installment payments remaining on the said passenger car, and thus, deceiving the victim, entered into a contract to sell the said passenger car for 9,500,000 won, and on the spot received 9,500,000 won in the name of the purchase price and thereby defrauded it; and Defendant 1, having purchased an Avante passenger car from Non-Indicted Party 3 for 1,000,000 won on the condition of assuming the installment debt, on the 22nd of the same month, Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 falsely told victim Non-Indicted Party 4 that there were no remaining installment payments on the said vehicle, and thus, deceiving the victim, entered into a contract to sell the said passenger car for 6,000,000 won, and on the spot received 6,000,000 won in the name of the purchase price and thereby defrauded it. According to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below held that, even based on all of the prosecutor’s evidence, there was no evidence to find that the Defendants conspired to falsely tell the victims that there were no remaining installment payments on the said Credos passenger car and Avante passenger car, thereby deceiving the victims, entering into each vehicle sales contract, receiving the purchase price, and defrauding it, and accordingly acquitted the Defendants on each of the above facts charged. Upon examination of the record, the above determination of the court below can be accepted, and there is also no evidence to find that, in selling the said Credos passenger car to Non-Indicted Party 2, the Defendants acted as if Defendant 2 were Non-Indicted Party 1; therefore, it cannot be said that the court below’s determination contains any illegality such as violation of the rules of evidence assessment, as argued.\\n\\nMeanwhile, in a transactional relationship concerning property rights, where one party, knowing that by failing to disclose to the other party a certain matter relating to the transaction, a risk may arise that the rights to the subject matter of the contract may not be secured in the future, nevertheless fails to disclose it and enters into the transaction, receiving delivery of property or obtaining a property benefit from the other party, and where it is clear according to the rules of experience that, had the other party been informed of such circumstances, it would not have entered into that transactional relationship, the recipient of the property shall, under the principle of good faith and fair dealing, owe the other party a duty to disclose such circumstances, and the recipient’s failure to disclose it shall constitute deception by concealing a fact that should have been disclosed, thereby constituting fraud (see this Court’s decisions dated September 25, 1984, 84DO882, March 12, 1985, 84DO93, and December 24, 1991, 91DO2698, among others). However, upon examination of the record, since Defendant 1 purchased the said Credos passenger car from Non-Indicted Party 1 and the said Avante passenger car from Non-Indicted Party 3 on the condition of assuming the installment-debt obligations, and the Defendants sold these vehicles to Non-Indicted Party 2 and Non-Indicted Party 4 respectively without disclosing the existence of the installment-debt obligations, the question is whether such conduct constitutes deception of the other party by breach of the duty to disclose. The record suggests that Non-Indicted Party 1 purchased the said Credos passenger car by obtaining financing from Non-Indicted Company 5 Co., Ltd. and was bearing installment-debt obligations to Non-Indicted Company 5 Co., Ltd., and that Non-Indicted Party 3 purchased the said Avante passenger car on installments under the guarantee of a surety insurance company; however, it appears that no mortgage was created on the said Credos passenger car or Avante passenger car themselves, nor were there circumstances such as execution of a provisional attachment (see the entries in each automobile registration certificate at pages 25 and 284 of volume 5 of the investigation record). Also, there is no basis in the record to conclude that Non-Indicted Party 1’s or Non-Indicted Party 3’s installment-debt obligations would naturally be assumed by the purchaser pursuant to the automobile sales contract. If the circumstances are as such, then even if the former owners, Non-Indicted Party 1 and Non-Indicted Party 3, respectively bore installment-debt obligations in relation to the automobiles that were the subject of sale, it cannot be said that, by reason thereof, a risk arose that the automobile purchasers, Non-Indicted Party 2 and Non-Indicted Party 4, would in the future fail to secure ownership of the contractual subject matter, namely, the automobiles; therefore, it cannot be said that, if Non-Indicted Party 2 or Non-Indicted Party 4 had been informed of the existence of such installment-debt obligations, it would have been clear according to the rules of experience that they would not have purchased the respective automobiles, and accordingly it cannot be said that the Defendants had a duty to disclose such matters, nor can the Defendants’ omission be regarded as deception.\\n\\nHowever, as to the fact that Defendant 1 purchased the said Credos passenger car from Non-Indicted Party 1 on the condition of assuming Non-Indicted Party 1’s installment-debt obligations, deceived Non-Indicted Party 1 into handing over his seal, and then, without Non-Indicted Party 1’s knowledge, stamped the seal on the power of attorney for transfer of the vehicle and thereby forged it, and that the Defendants, when selling the said Credos passenger car to Non-Indicted Party 2, delivered and used it, the court below found this guilty and it became final as is; and according to the record, the Defendants can be seen to have sold the said Credos passenger car to Non-Indicted Party 2 while posing as agents of Non-Indicted Party 1 (see the receipt at page 568 of the investigation record No. 1997HYEONGJE29186 of the Seoul District Prosecutors’ Office). If that is the case, there may be a suspicion that, although the Defendants had not been granted authority by Non-Indicted Party 1 to sell the said Credos passenger car, they deceived Non-Indicted Party 2 by posing as if they had been granted such authority, and that Non-Indicted Party 2, being deceived thereby, purchased the said Credos passenger car. However, on the other hand, Non-Indicted Party 2 states that, when purchasing the said Credos passenger car, it received, in addition to the said power of attorney for transfer of the vehicle, documents necessary for transfer registration, such as a seal certificate in the name of Non-Indicted Party 1, a vehicle inspection certificate, a resident registration abstract, and a liability insurance receipt (see the statement of Non-Indicted Party 2 prepared by a judicial police officer; see page 91 of the above investigation record), and the manner in which the Defendants obtained those documents has not been examined (in the complaint against the Defendants, Non-Indicted Party 1 states, in substance, that after selling the said Credos passenger car to Defendant 1, Defendant 1 said that the car was urgently needed, so he first delivered the said Credos passenger car without following the procedure for assumption of the installment-debt obligations, and that at the time of delivery he had kept the seal certificate, vehicle inspection certificate, resident registration abstract, liability insurance receipt, and the like, which were necessary for transfer registration, in the said passenger car, but then, thinking that nothing would happen, he delivered the car as is. However, the above complaint was not adopted as evidence, and the Defendants deny such facts).\\n\\nAlso, a fraud charge to the effect that they deceived Non-Indicted Party 2 by posing as if they had authority even though they had no authority is different in the content of the offense from the fraud stated in the above facts charged, and recognizing such fraud against the Defendants without following the procedure for amendment of the indictment would exceed the scope of adjudication limited by the facts charged and would substantially infringe the Defendants’ right of defense, and therefore cannot be permitted. (Meanwhile, according to the record, Non-Indicted Party 3 sold the said Avante passenger car to Defendant 1 on the condition of assuming the installment-debt obligations, and appears to have delivered the power of attorney for transfer of the vehicle and the seal certificate necessary for automobile transfer registration even before Defendant 1 followed the procedure for assuming the installment-debt obligations. Although there is no material in the record by which to determine in what form the Defendants sold the said Avante passenger car to Non-Indicted Party 4, in light of the fact that ownership transfer registration for the said Avante passenger car was made directly from Non-Indicted Party 3 to Non-Indicted Party 4, it may be inferred that the Defendants likewise posed as agents of Non-Indicted Party 3. Even though it was a defective expression of intent caused by deception, it is reasonable to view Non-Indicted Party 3 as having granted authority to sell the said Avante passenger car by delivering the power of attorney for transfer of the vehicle and the seal certificate to Defendant 1, and as long as such authority existed, even if the purchaser, Non-Indicted Party 4, believed that the Defendants had been granted authority by Non-Indicted Party 3 and purchased the said Avante passenger car, it cannot be said that there was any mistake caused by deception.)\\n\\nIn the end, it cannot be said that the judgment of the court below contains any illegality of misapprehension of the legal doctrine concerning fraud, as argued by the prosecutor. All arguments are without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices as stated in the disposition."}

question: In the following case, A and B, without conspiring with each other, where Defendant A first struck A’s head several times with intent to inflict bodily injury, and about 1 hour later Defendant B approached A, who was lying on the ground, and struck A’s head several times with intent to inflict bodily injury, A suffered an injury to the head requiring 4 weeks of treatment from the above assault, but it was not determined whether that injury was caused by the assault of Defendant A or Defendant B (ⓐfacts of the offense). Defendant A and Defendant B were each indicted for the offense of bodily injury and, after being convicted in the court of first instance, appealed. The appellate court lawfully concluded the hearing of the trial and notified the date for pronouncement of judgment, but immediately thereafter A’s injury to the head worsened and A died in the hospital. Among the explanations concerning this, which of the following are all correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents)
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2021DO5777]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding Grounds of Appeal Nos. 1 and 2\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its judgment, the court below found the facts charged in this case guilty. Examining the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the relevant legal principles and the duly admitted evidence, the court below’s determination does not violate the principle of the presumption of innocence or the rules of logic and experience, does not exceed the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, and does not contain any error in misunderstanding the legal principles concerning quasi-rape and rape causing injury.\\n\\n2. Regarding Ground of Appeal No. 3\\n\\nA. Relevant legal principles\\n\\n1) Article 51 of the Criminal Act concerning the conditions for sentencing prescribes the matters to be considered in determining punishment. Since the determination of punishment is a matter of judicial discretion, unless the appeal ground concerning the propriety of sentencing is being reviewed in a case where the death penalty, life imprisonment, or imprisonment or confinement for not less than 10 years has been imposed pursuant to Article 383(4) of the Criminal Procedure Act, an argument that the facts forming the basis of sentencing were mistaken by the fact-finding court, or that the court did not properly conduct proceedings regarding the circumstances constituting sentencing conditions, does not constitute a lawful ground for appeal. However, the fact-finding court’s discretion concerning sentencing also has inherent limits recognized within the scope of sentencing determinations regarding the culpability of the offense as alleged in the defendant’s facts charged, in light of the principle of proportionality between crime and punishment, which requires an appropriate balance between crime and punishment, and the principle of responsibility, which requires that punishment be based on responsibility and be proportionate thereto (see Supreme Court Decision 2008. 5. 29. rendered in 2008DO1816, etc.).\\n\\n2) The Constitution, in the latter sentence of Article 12(1), declares the principle of due process, and in Article 27 guarantees the right to receive a trial. To substantially realize this, the Criminal Procedure Act adopts as basic principles the adversarial system and the principle of trial centered on public hearings, under which a substantive hearing of a criminal case must be conducted in open court through the prosecutorial and defensive activities of both the prosecutor and the defendant; the principle of direct hearing and the principle of trial by evidence, under which the finding of facts charged must be based only on evidence directly examined before the judge (see Supreme Court Decision 2021. 6. 10. rendered in 2020DO15891). In criminal trials, facts must be found by evidence (Article 307 of the Criminal Procedure Act), the authority to request evidence belongs to the prosecutor, the defendant, and defense counsel (Article 294 of the Criminal Procedure Act), and when requesting evidence, evidence concerning sentencing circumstances must be requested with its purport specified (Article 132-2(2) of the Rules on Criminal Procedure). In addition, in order to allow the defendant to invoke as favorable the results of evidence examination that are favorable to him or her and to have an opportunity to rebut the results of examination that are unfavorable to him or her, the defendant is procedurally guaranteed an opportunity to state opinions on the results of evidence examination and the right to request evidence (see Article 293 of the Criminal Procedure Act). Meanwhile, a written statement in lieu of the victim’s opinion must have its purport notified to the defendant, and the purport of the written statement must be made clear in open court (Article 134-11(2) and (3) of the Rules on Criminal Procedure). In light of the foregoing basic principles of criminal trials and the relevant provisions in their totality, if, after the close of arguments at the fact-finding stage, materials concerning new sentencing conditions adverse to the defendant are submitted to the court by the prosecutor, the victim, or others, the fact-finding court must reopen the arguments and, by going through the necessary sentencing-hearing procedures, such as giving the defendant an opportunity to state opinions regarding such sentencing materials, substantially guarantee the defendant’s right of defense.\\n\\nB. The following facts and circumstances are established from the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the record.\\n\\n1) The defendant was indicted for a violation of the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth Against Sexual Abuse (hereinafter, the “Juvenile Sexual Protection Act”) (rape, etc. causing injury) on the grounds that he had had sexual intercourse with the victim, who was in a state of being unable to resist, thereby causing an hymenal laceration with unknown days of treatment and post-traumatic stress disorder, and at trial the charge was found guilty in the first instance, resulting in a sentence of 4 years’ imprisonment and his being taken into custody in court.\\n\\n2) Both the defendant and the prosecutor appealed. While in custody until the date on which arguments were concluded in the court below, the defendant consistently asserted his innocence and mainly contested the victim’s state of loss of mental and physical capacity or inability to resist and the causal relationship between the quasi-rape act and the injury; he did not confess the offense or actively argue sentencing. Meanwhile, the prosecutor, on the date on which arguments were concluded in the court below (2021. 3. 17.), requested a sentence of 7 years’ imprisonment, as in the first instance.\\n\\n3) On 2021. 4. 8., before the pronouncement of the judgment of the court below (2021. 4. 21.), the victim’s attorney submitted a written opinion stating, with an attached death certificate indicating that the victim had died on the 4th day of that month, that “since the victim ended her own life due to secondary harm caused by the defendant, please punish the defendant severely.”\\n\\n4) The court below did not reopen the arguments, but on the scheduled date for pronouncement of judgment, it recognized the violation of the Juvenile Sexual Protection Act (rape, etc. causing injury) as guilty, as in the first instance, yet reversed the first-instance judgment and sentenced the defendant to 9 years’ imprisonment. The court below stated that it was imposing 9 years’ imprisonment by departing from the basic recommended sentence range for the offense under the sentencing guidelines [imprisonment for 5 years to 8 years], and in the section of the reasons for judgment entitled “Determination on the defendant’s and the prosecutor’s arguments of improper sentencing,” it stated, “The victim’s extreme choice can ultimately only be seen as having resulted from the physical and mental suffering experienced by being subjected to the offense in this case by the defendant.”\\n\\nC. We examine this case in light of the foregoing facts and legal principles.\\n\\nConsidering the record together with the first-instance judgment and the reasons of the judgment of the court below, no particular change in sentencing conditions is apparent between the first-instance judgment and the judgment of the court below, other than the fact of the victim’s death. It can be seen that, based on the victim’s death certificate submitted by the victim’s attorney after the close of arguments in the court below, the court below determined that “the victim committed suicide because of the pain caused by the defendant’s offense in this case,” and then, taking this as a core sentencing-aggravating factor, reversed the first-instance judgment, which had sentenced the defendant to 4 years’ imprisonment and ordered 40 hours of completion of a program, and imposed 9 years’ imprisonment and an 80-hour completion order.\\n\\nHowever, the victim died after the close of arguments in the court below, and that fact was only confirmed by the materials submitted by the victim’s attorney shortly before the pronouncement of the judgment of the court below; no dispute whatsoever was made during the trial proceedings regarding the relationship between the victim’s death and the offense in this case. In such a case, the court below should have reopened the arguments and additionally examined the new sentencing conditions related to the victim’s death, including by hearing the defendant’s opinion regarding the victim’s death or the relationship between the victim’s death and the offense in this case, thereby giving the defendant an opportunity to defend himself or herself.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below did not give the defendant an opportunity to defend himself or herself regarding new sentencing conditions adverse to the defendant, such as the fact of the victim’s death, which it came to know only after the close of arguments through materials submitted by the victim’s side, or the relationship with the offense in this case, which could be determined through additional proceedings. Furthermore, after determining that the victim’s death and that death being caused by the defendant’s offense in this case constituted a significant change in aggravating sentencing conditions, it reversed the first-instance judgment, which had sentenced the defendant to 4 years’ imprisonment, and imposed 9 years’ imprisonment, exceeding the recommended sentence under the sentencing guidelines.\\n\\nIn these measures of the court below, there is an error in failing to conduct the necessary proceedings by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the sentencing-hearing procedures that a fact-finding court must follow when sentencing materials unfavorable to the defendant are submitted after the close of arguments, and it is deemed that such error affected the judgment. Therefore, the ground of appeal pointing out this issue is well founded.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, we reverse the judgment of the court below and remand the case to the court below for a new trial and determination, and so decide as per the operative part by the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2022DO4624]": "We consider the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAn amendment to the indictment made before the court has concluded the hearing of the trial shall be permitted to the extent that it does not infringe the identity of the facts charged. However, with respect to an amendment to the indictment made by the Prosecutor after the trial hearing has been lawfully concluded and notice has been given until the date for pronouncement of judgment, the court has no duty to reopen the concluded hearing and permit the amendment to the indictment, even if it was made together with an application to reopen oral argument (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2001DO6484, rendered on 2003. 12. 26.).\\n\\nThe court below did not grant the Prosecutor's application to reopen oral argument and application for permission to amend the indictment, which were submitted after the close of oral argument and before the date for pronouncement of judgment, and found the Defendant not guilty on the ground that there was no proof of the crime as to the obstruction of business portion among the facts charged in this case. In light of the record, the legal principle examined above reveals no error in the judgment of the court below, such as a violation of the statutes concerning the procedure for amendment of the indictment, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAccording to the record, it can be seen that the Defendant submitted a waiver of the right to appeal against the judgment of the court below on 2022. 4. 19., and court-appointed counsel submitted to the Supreme Court, on 2022. 5. 6., a written submission entitled “Statement of Grounds for Appeal in Cassation.” Even if construed as a petition of appeal in cassation, the appeal by court-appointed counsel was filed after the right to appeal had been extinguished by the Defendant's waiver of the right to appeal, and is therefore unlawful.\\n\\nAs the Prosecutor's appeal in cassation is without merit, it is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court."}

{"[84DO488]": "We examine the grounds of appeal by the Defendants.\\n\\n1. According to the reasons of the first-instance judgment upheld by the court below, the first instance court found that Defendant 1, on the ground that the victim had intervened to stop the Defendants from fighting with each other, head-butted the victim’s face once with his forehead and thereafter struck the victim’s face and chest five or six times, and that Defendant 2 joined in and struck the victim’s left cheek once with his fist; and further found that one of the Defendants picked up a shard of broken glass bottle lying there and struck the victim’s nose downward, thereby causing an open fracture of the nasal bone requiring 47 days of treatment, and convicted the Defendants of violation of the Act on the Punishment of Violent Acts, etc.\\n\\n2. Upon examination of the record, as to whether the Defendants’ above-described assaultive conduct actually occurred, there is no evidence other than the Defendants’ own assertions and the victim’s statement, such as the testimony of witnesses that would determine the truth or falsity thereof; and examining the contents of the victim’s statement, the following appears.\\n\\n(1) In the statement report prepared by a judicial police officer concerning the victim (investigation record pp. 12, 13), the victim stated: “... while I was holding with both arms the waist of Defendant 2, who was about to collapse from intoxication, suddenly Defendant 1 head-butted the left side of my head once with his forehead, and again grasped both my shoulders with both hands and head-butted my left eye area once with his forehead; when I pushed Defendant 1’s chest away, Defendant 1 then struck my abdomen about five times and my face about five times with both fists, ... when Defendant 2 struck my face area seven or eight times with both fists, I too swung my fists in resistance, but feeling as if I would be beaten to death there, I was trying to retreat about 2 or 3 meters, and at the moment an unidentified person approached and struck my face area three or four times with both fists, one of the three accused persons picked up a glass bottle and struck my nose once, and I then collapsed on the spot...”\\n\\nFirst, even according to the above statement, it appears that Defendant 2 was in a state of standing while being supported by the victim, in that he was being supported by the victim while he was intoxicated and about to collapse; and it is difficult to readily accept as a statement that such Defendant, who was so intoxicated that he could not properly control his body, joined in Defendant 1’s assault and participated in the violence by striking the face of the victim, who was supporting him, seven or eight times.\\n\\n(2) Moreover, thereafter the victim made conflicting statements concerning the third person who joined the Defendants in attacking the victim: unlike the contents of the above statement, he said that the third person struck the victim’s back from behind with his fist (part of the confrontation questioning in the statement report concerning Ji Dong-jun prepared by a judicial police officer, investigation record pp. 46, 47; part of the confrontation questioning in the victim interrogation report concerning Defendant 1, investigation record pp. 86, 87), or that the back was kicked with a foot, etc. (statement report of the prosecutor concerning the victim, investigation record p. 133); and as to the act of striking the victim’s face with a glass bottle, at first he stated that it was struck by one of the three persons consisting of the Defendants and an unidentified person, but thereafter changed his statement to one of the two Defendants (part of the confrontation questioning in the third suspect interrogation report concerning Defendant 1 prepared by a judicial police officer, investigation record pp. 100, 101, and statement report of the prosecutor concerning the victim, investigation record p. 133).\\n\\nAs above, the contents of the victim’s statement itself are inconsistent, making it difficult to ascertain the exact circumstances of the offense. Even according to the victim’s statement, while being beaten by the Defendants he retreated about 2 or 3 meters in an attempt to flee, and at the moment he was assaulted by a third person he was struck in the face with a weapon; therefore, as the victim contends, before concluding solely from the above victim’s statement that the weapon assault was committed by one of the two Defendants, it is difficult to determine whether the positions where the Defendants were standing and the position to which the victim had retreated when he was attacked by the third person should be compared, and whether the Defendants were at such positions and distances as to be able to strike the victim’s face with the weapon at the moment when the victim was assaulted by the third person.\\n\\nIn the offense of injury, where two or more persons commit assaultive acts and thereby cause injury, if it is not clear from whose assault the injury resulted, all of the assailants are to be treated as joint principals; therefore, it goes without saying that a person whose commission of the assault itself is not clear cannot be punished as a simultaneous offender.\\n\\nIf it is found that the Defendants struck the victim with their fists or foreheads as alleged by the victim, they cannot escape criminal liability for that point; however, if there is no possibility that the act of striking the victim’s face with a weapon was committed by either one of the Defendants, then in this case, in which it cannot be deemed that there was a meeting of minds among the Defendants and the third person, the Defendants cannot be held criminally liable for the part of the injurious act committed with the weapon.\\n\\nIn this respect, the court below committed an error of incomplete examination, and the above ground of appeal is well-founded.\\n\\nTherefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the judges participating in the case as ordered."}

question:
Which of the following statements concerning constitutional adjudication are correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents)

(a) Where a vacancy arises among the Justices of the Constitutional Court elected by the National Assembly and appointed, the National Assembly bears a constitutional duty to elect a successor to the vacant Justice within a reasonable period.

(b) The Constitution prescribes the term of office of a Justice of the Constitutional Court as 6 years, but allows reappointment in accordance with the law.

(c) A party may file an application for disqualification against a Justice of the Constitutional Court, but may not do so if the party has appeared on the date of oral argument and made a statement on the merits.

(d) If the Chief Justice of the Constitutional Court deems it necessary, oral argument in the trial may be held at a place other than the courtroom, but the pronouncement of the final decision may not be made at a place other than the courtroom.

(e) In adjudications on jurisdiction disputes and constitutional complaint adjudications, except where special provisions are prescribed in the Constitutional Court Act, the laws and regulations concerning civil litigation and the Administrative Litigation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis together to the extent not contrary to the nature of constitutional adjudication; however, where the Administrative Litigation Act conflicts with the laws and regulations concerning civil litigation, the laws and regulations concerning civil litigation shall not apply mutatis mutandis.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2012HEONMA2]": "[Appendix] Relevant Provisions\\n\\nConstitutional Court Act (as amended by Act No. 10546 of April 5, 2011)\\n\\nArticle 6 (Appointment of Justices) (1) Justices shall be appointed by the President. In this case, the President shall appoint 3 persons elected by the National Assembly and 3 persons designated by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.\\n\\n(2) Justices shall be appointed, elected, or designated after a personnel hearing by the National Assembly. In this case, before appointing a Justice (excluding persons elected by the National Assembly or designated by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court), the President shall request a personnel hearing, and before designating a Justice, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall request a personnel hearing.\\n\\n(3) Where the term of office of a Justice expires or the mandatory retirement age is The term “motion for consent to appointment, etc.” means a motion for consent to appointment, a motion for election under the provisions of Article 46-3(1) of the National Assembly Act, a motion requesting a personnel hearing for a Prime Minister nominee requested by the President-elect, and a motion requesting a personnel hearing for a candidate for public office for whom another Act requires a personnel hearing by the National Assembly pursuant to the provisions of Article 65-2(2) of the same Act.\\n\\nArticle 6 (Referral of Motions for Consent to Appointment, etc.) (1) When a motion for consent to appointment, etc. is submitted, the Speaker shall immediately report it to the plenary session and refer it to the Committee, and after the examination thereof or the personnel hearing is completed, shall submit it to the plenary session or have the Chairperson report it to the plenary session. question: Which of the following statements concerning adjudication on competence disputes are correct? (In case of dispute, in accordance with precedent)
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2003HEONRA1]": "1. Outline of the Case and Subject Matter of Adjudication\\n\\na. Outline of the Case\\n\\n(1) Petitioner Gwangyang-si is a local government established by the integration, pursuant to Article 2 of the Act on the Establishment, etc. of 2 City-County Integrated-Type Municipalities Including Gwangyang-si, Jeollanam-do (enacted as Act No. 4801 on 1994. 12. 22.), of Donggwangyang-si and Gwangyang-gun, Jeollanam-do on 1994. 12. 22., and Respondent Suncheon-si is a local government established by the integration, pursuant to Article 7 of the Act on the Establishment, etc. of 33 City-County Integrated-Type Municipalities Including Namyangju-si, Gyeonggi-do (enacted as Act No. 4774 on 1994. 8. 3.), of Suncheon-si and Seungju-gun, Jeollanam-do on 1994. 8. 3.\\n\\n(2) Jeollanam-do, around December 1982, planned and promoted a project to reclaim the sea adjacent to the then four cities and counties, including Gwangyang-eup, Gwangyang-gun, Donggwangyang-si, Yeocheon-gun Yulchon-myeon, and Seungju-gun Haeryong-myeon, pursuant to the Act on Industrial Site and Development, in order to create a local industrial complex. The above project had planned, by December 1994, to reclaim a total of 12,266,000㎡, consisting of 1,839,000㎡ of land and 10,427,000㎡ of sea surface, but owing to various circumstances the reclamation area was reduced to 9,227,213㎡ and the project period was extended to December 2005, and the project was carried forward.\\n\\nThe original four cities and counties incorporated into the above project were thereafter changed, following the integration of administrative districts, into three cities: Petitioner Gwangyang-si, Respondent Suncheon-si, and non-party Yeosu-si, and the name was also changed to “Yulchon No. 1 Local Industrial Complex.”\\n\\n(3) OO Co., Ltd. (formerly XX Co., Ltd.) was allotted from Jeollanam-do 446,283㎡ of the above industrial complex site, the reclamation of which had been completed; then, on 1997. 2. 25., it obtained approval for use before completion of reclamation of public waters; and on 1999. 3. 6., in the “Block 1-1” area of the above industrial complex, it completed and is operating a factory and ancillary facilities for the purpose of manufacturing cold-rolled products. However, when the former maritime boundary, based on the national base maps published in 1988 by the National Geographic Information Institute (formerly the National Geography Institute), is applied, the land and buildings such as the factory of the above company have been constructed on land located on the boundary between the jurisdictional areas of Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si, both local governments.\\n\\n(4) After the buildings of the above company were completed, the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si imposed property tax, aggregate land tax, business establishment tax, etc. on the company’s entire land and buildings from 1999 to 2002, and on 2003. 7. 1. imposed urban planning tax and joint facilities tax.\\n\\n(5) On the ground that the above tax dispositions by the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si were illegal and improper, the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si filed a petition for dispute mediation under Article 140 of the Local Autonomy Act with the Governor of Jeollanam-do on 2000. 6. 15., but when the Governor of Jeollanam-do withheld any decision, the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si imposed local tax assessments, from 2001 onward, on the land and buildings of the above company within the jurisdictional area of Petitioner Gwangyang-si. Accordingly, from 2001 onward, the said company deposited the amounts of tax at the Gwangju District Court, Suncheon Branch, regarding each tax disposition by the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si and the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si, on the ground that the recipient entitled to receive them could not be identified.\\n\\n(6) Accordingly, Petitioner Gwangyang-si and the Mayor of Gwangyang-si filed this petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute with the Constitutional Court on 2003. 8. 28., seeking confirmation that, among the 446,283㎡ of industrial complex land allotted by the company from Jeollanam-do and the factory (196,734㎡) and ancillary facilities (6,325,377㎡) in Block 1-1 of the above industrial complex, the portion to the right of the line sequentially connecting points 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 as marked on the map attached as Appendix 2 (hereinafter referred to as “the disputed area”) belongs to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, and that the tax impositions of urban planning tax, joint facilities tax, etc. imposed by the Respondents on the company as of 2003. 7. 1. are void as having infringed the petitioners’ local autonomy rights (autonomous fiscal authority).\\n\\nb. Subject Matter of Adjudication\\n\\nBy combining the claims in the petitioners’ petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute (2003. 8. 28.) and the claims in the 6th preparatory brief (2005. 6. 22.) correcting the same, the subject matter of adjudication in this case is specified as follows.\\n\\n(1) Whether, among the reclaimed land of Yulchon No. 1 Local Industrial Complex located in Gwangyang-si, Suncheon-si, and Yeosu-si, Jeollanam-do, the portion to the right of the line sequentially connecting points 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 as marked on the map attached as Appendix 2 (hereinafter referred to as “the disputed area in this case”) among the 446,283㎡ (135,000 pyeong) industrial complex land allotted by OO Co., Ltd. from Jeollanam-do, the factory with a total floor area of 231,192.92㎡ in Block 1-1 of the above industrial complex, and the office, etc. with a total floor area of 10,171.85㎡ (hereinafter referred to as “the reclaimed land in this case”) belongs to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si\\n\\n(2) Whether the tax dispositions, such as urban planning tax and joint facilities tax, imposed by the Respondents on the above company on 2003. 7. 1. are void as having infringed the petitioners’ local autonomy rights (autonomous fiscal authority)\\n\\n2. The Petitioners’ Arguments, the Respondents’ Response, and the Opinion of the Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs\\n\\nAs stated in Appendix 4.\\n\\n3. Determination on the Procedural Requirements\\n\\na. Admissibility of the Petition for Adjudication on a Jurisdictional Dispute\\n\\nArticle 61(1) of the Constitutional Court Act provides that when there is a dispute regarding the existence or scope of authority between State organs, between a State organ and a local government, or among local governments, the relevant State organ or local government may file a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute with the Constitutional Court. Article 61(2) of the same Act provides that a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute may be filed only when the disposition or omission of the respondent has infringed, or presents a clear risk of infringing, the petitioner’s authority granted by the Constitution or by law. Therefore, in order to file a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute, there must be a dispute between the petitioner and the respondent as to the existence or scope of authority granted by the Constitution or by law, and the respondent’s disposition or omission must have infringed, or present a clear risk of infringing, the petitioner’s authority granted by the Constitution or by law (see Constitutional Court 1998. 6. 25. 94HEONRA1, Collection of Cases 10-1, 739, 751-752).\\n\\nb. Whether the petition filed by the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Respondents and the petition filed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si are admissible\\n\\nA petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute is a constitutional litigation in which a person granted authority by the Constitution and by law disputes infringement of that authority. As to the person who may file such a petition, the Constitution and the Constitutional Court Act provide as follows: Article 111(1)(4) of the Constitution provides for adjudication on jurisdictional disputes between State organs, between a State organ and a local government, and among local governments; and Article 62(1)(3) of the Constitutional Court Act provides only the following types of adjudication on jurisdictional disputes among local governments: a. adjudication on jurisdictional disputes among special cities, metropolitan cities, or provinces; b. adjudication on jurisdictional disputes among cities, counties, or autonomous districts; c. adjudication on jurisdictional disputes between a special city, metropolitan city, or province and a city, county, or autonomous district. Therefore, the head of a local government, in principle, cannot be a party to a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute.\\n\\nHowever, if the tax disposition by the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si against OO Co., Ltd. constitutes a State-delegated affair and the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si made the tax imposition in the status of a State organ, then this could also be viewed as a dispute over authority arising between a local government and a State organ. But the imposition of tax by the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si against OO Co., Ltd., as will be seen below, is a matter falling within the authority of a local government rather than a State affair; accordingly, the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si merely made the above disposition as the executive organ of local government affairs under Articles 92 and 94 of the Local Autonomy Act, and thus, under the current law, which does not permit a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute by a local government organ, he lacks capacity to be a party. Likewise, the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, in the context of local tax impositions, only has the status of an organ of a local government and is not a local government that can be a party to a jurisdictional dispute; therefore, he also lacks capacity to be a party. Accordingly, both the petition by the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Respondents and the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si are inadmissible as petitions filed by persons lacking capacity to be a party.\\n\\nc. Whether the petition filed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against Respondent Suncheon-si is admissible\\n\\nBoth Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si are local governments as provided by Article 111(1)(4) of the Constitution and Article 62(1)(3) of the Constitutional Court Act, and thus have capacity to be a party to file a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute under Article 61(1) of the Constitutional Court Act.\\n\\nHowever, Article 61(2) of the Constitutional Court Act provides that a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute may be filed only when the respondent’s disposition or omission has infringed, or presents a clear risk of infringing, the petitioner’s authority granted by the Constitution or by law; in light of the tax impositions, etc. issued by Respondent Suncheon-si, this petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute would be admissible only if the disposition or future disposition of Respondent Suncheon-si has infringed, or presents a clear risk of infringing, the authority of Petitioner Gwangyang-si.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 2 of the Local Tax Act provides that “local governments may levy and collect ordinary taxes and objective taxes as local taxes in accordance with this Act,” and Articles 5(2) and 5(3) of the Local Tax Act specifically enumerate the types of ordinary taxes and objective taxes that are local taxes; property tax falls under ordinary tax under paragraph (2) item 6, while urban planning tax and joint facilities tax are local taxes that fall under objective taxes under paragraph (3) items 1 and 2.\\n\\nHowever, on 2003. 7. 1., Respondent Suncheon-si, through the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si, imposed urban planning tax, joint facilities tax, etc. on the buildings of OO Co., Ltd., and imposed urban planning tax, etc. in a lump sum even on the buildings on the disputed area in this case. Thereupon, Petitioner Gwangyang-si argues that the taxing authority over the disputed area in this case belongs to Petitioner Gwangyang-si and that the foregoing tax disposition by Respondent Suncheon-si infringes the local autonomy rights of Petitioner Gwangyang-si. Ultimately, the above dispute between Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si is a dispute over the local governments’ taxing authority, that is, local fiscal authority, and concerns the infringement of authority pertaining to affairs granted to local governments by the Constitution (Article 117(1) of the Constitution) and by law (Article 9(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, Article 2 of the Local Tax Act). However, as a result of the merits review in this case, depending in particular on the extent of the jurisdictional area, there is a possibility that Petitioner Gwangyang-si may be recognized as having constitutional and statutory autonomous authority over the disputed area in this case; and in that event, there exists a clear risk that the above tax disposition by Respondent Suncheon-si, which would infringe Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s autonomous authority, will infringe Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s autonomous authority over the disputed area in this case. Accordingly, the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against Respondent Suncheon-si is admissible.\\n\\nd. Conclusion on the procedural requirements\\n\\nTherefore, the petition by the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Respondents and the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si are inadmissible as petitions filed by persons lacking capacity to be a party, and the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against Respondent Suncheon-si is admissible.\\n\\n4. Determination on the Merits\\n\\na. The Legal Issues in This Case\\n\\nIn this case, the key legal issue is whether, in the Yulchon No. 1 Local Industrial Complex created by reclaiming the sea adjacent to the eastern sea area of Sinseong-ri, Suncheon-si, Jeollanam-do, from the sea adjacent to Petitioner Gwangyang-si, Respondent Suncheon-si, and non-party Yeosu-si, the authority over the portion to the right of the line sequentially connecting points 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 as marked on the map attached as Appendix 2 among the reclaimed land in this case (the disputed area in this case) belongs to Petitioner Gwangyang-si.\\n\\nb. The Jurisdictional Area and Autonomous Authority of Local Governments over Public Waters\\n\\nThe local autonomy of local governments guaranteed by Article 117(1) of the Constitution includes the authority to exercise their autonomous power within their own territory. The territory of a local government is an element of the local government together with the residents and autonomous authority, and refers to the spatial scope within which autonomous power may be exercised, thereby clearly distinguishing the scope of jurisdiction from that of other local governments.\\n\\nUnder Article 9(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, a local government has the authority to handle its own affairs within its jurisdictional area and affairs belonging to local governments under statutes, and also has the authority to handle affairs concerning the territory, organization, and administrative management of local governments listed in Article 9(2) item 1. Accordingly, a local government has autonomous authority or jurisdictional authority granted by Article 117(1) of the Constitution, Article 9 of the Local Autonomy Act, and other individual statutes within its jurisdictional area. However, as to the jurisdictional area of a local government, Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act provides that “the name and territory of a local government shall be determined according to the former provisions, and when changing them or abolishing or merging local governments, they shall be determined by statute, provided that changes to the boundary of the jurisdictional area of a city, county, or autonomous district shall be determined by Presidential Decree.”\\n\\nHere, with regard to the scope of the area over which a local government exercises jurisdiction, the question particularly arises whether the sea, which is public waters, is included in the jurisdictional area over which the autonomous authority of a local government extends. Our Court has held that the territory of a local government prescribed in Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act is an element of the local government together with the residents and autonomous authority, and that the scope of the jurisdictional area over which autonomous authority extends includes not only land but also the sea, and therefore local governments possess autonomous authority over public waters (Constitutional Court 2004. 9. 23. 2000HEONRA2, Collection of Cases 16-2, 404, 428; Supreme Court 2002. 12. 24. decided 2000DO1048).\\n\\nc. Boundary of Local Governments’ Jurisdictional Areas over Public Waters and Reclaimed Land\\n\\n(1) Issue\\n\\nAs noted above, local governments possess autonomous authority over public waters; therefore, we examine whether there exists a boundary of jurisdictional area over public waters that can identify the area over which a specific jurisdictional authority extends.\\n\\n(2) Legislative History of Provisions Concerning Local Governments’ Jurisdictional Areas\\n\\nIn the current Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, the term “former” does not mean only the contents of prior statutes and regulations, but must be interpreted broadly to include even entries in cadastral registers, and the phrase “the jurisdictional area of a local government shall be according to the former provisions” means that the territory existing at the time of the Act’s enforcement is as is followed (Constitutional Court 2004. 9. 23. 2000HEONRA2, Collection of Cases 16-2, 404, 430).\\n\\nHowever, since the territories existing at the time of the effective date of the above provision would again be determined by the pre-amendment statutes then in force, it is necessary to examine the legislative history relating to the above provision.\\n\\nThe former Temporary Measures Act concerning Local Administration (Act No. 8 of 1948. 11. 17.), which first prescribed the territories of local governments of the Republic of Korea, provided in Article 5: “The following cities and provinces shall be established in the localities: Seoul City, Gyeonggi-do, Chungcheongbuk-do, Chungcheongnam-do, Jeollabuk-do, Jeollanam-do, Jeju-do, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Gyeongsangnam-do, Hwanghae-do, Pyeonganam-do, Pyeonganbuk-do, Gangwon-do, Hamgyeongnam-buk, and Hamgyeongbuk-do. The location and jurisdictional areas of the cities and provinces shall be determined by Presidential Decree.” Article 12 provided: “Districts, bu, counties, and do shall be established in cities; the names, locations, and jurisdictional areas of the districts, bu, counties, and do shall be determined by Presidential Decree.” As to the reference date for such determination, the Decree Concerning the Names, Locations, and Jurisdictional Areas of Local Administrative Bodies (Presidential Decree No. 34, enacted on 1948. 11. 18.) provided that “the locations and jurisdictional areas of cities and provinces, and the names, locations, and jurisdictional areas of districts, bu, counties, do, police stations, and fire stations shall be based on 1948. 8. 15.,” and the supplementary provisions provided that “this Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.” According to this, the jurisdictional boundary as of 1948. 8. 15. becomes the standard for determining the territory of local governments.\\n\\nThe former Local Autonomy Act enacted thereafter (enacted as Act No. 32 on 1949. 7. 4., and prior to amendment by Act No. 563 on 1960. 11. 1.) provided in Article 4: “The names and territories of local governments shall, except for the renaming of former bu as cities, all follow the former provisions, and when changing them or abolishing and merging the local governments, it shall be done by statute. When abolishing and merging local governments or changing their names or territories by statute, the opinions of the relevant local council shall be heard.” It further provided in Article 145: “Counties shall be established in provinces, districts in Seoul Special City and cities with a population of 500,000 or more, and neighborhoods in cities, eup, myeon, and districts. The names and jurisdictional areas of counties and districts shall follow the former provisions, and when changing them or abolishing and merging them, they shall be determined by statute. Provided, Ulleung-do shall be renamed Ulleung-gun. The territory of neighborhoods shall be based on natural villages, but the determination of their names and territories shall be made by city, eup, or myeon ordinances.” Supplementary Provision Article 4 provided that “matters necessary for the enforcement of this Act shall be determined by Presidential Decree,” while Supplementary Provision Article 1 provided that “this Act shall enter into force on 1949. 8. 15.” According to these provisions, the jurisdictional boundary as of 1949. 8. 15. should be the standard, which ultimately results in using the jurisdictional boundary as of 1948. 8. 15. established by the former Temporary Measures Act concerning Local Administration that had been in force before the enforcement of the above Act.\\n\\nArticle 145 among the above provisions was partially amended by the former Local Autonomy Act (Act No. 385 of 1956. 2. 13., Act No. 501 of 1958. 12. 26., Act No. 563 of 1960. 11. 1.), but the part stating that “the names and territories of counties and districts shall follow the former provisions, and when changing them or abolishing and merging them, it shall be done by statute” was maintained. Meanwhile, separately from the Local Autonomy Act, the former Temporary Measures Act concerning Local Autonomy (enacted as Act No. 707 on 1961. 9. 1., and prior to amendment by Act No. 2595 of 1973. 3. 12.) was enacted, but even under Articles 3 and 4 thereof, there was no change in the principle that the territories of counties and eup/myeon followed the former provisions, and thereafter it came to have a structure similar to the current law under Article 3 of the former Temporary Measures Act concerning Local Autonomy (amended by Act No. 2595 of 1973. 3. 12., and prior to repeal by Act No. 4004 of 1988. 4. 6.).\\n\\nThereafter, the former Local Autonomy Act (fully amended by Act No. 4004 on 1988. 4. 6., and prior to amendment by Act No. 6002 of 1999. 8. 31.) amended Article 4 and provided in paragraph (1): “The names and territories of local governments shall follow the former provisions, and when changing them or abolishing or merging local governments, they shall be determined by statute; provided that changes to the boundary of the jurisdictional area of a city, county, or autonomous district shall be determined by Presidential Decree.” In paragraph (2): “When abolishing or merging local governments or changing their names or territories pursuant to paragraph (1), the opinions of the council of the relevant local government (hereinafter referred to as the ‘local council’) shall be heard.” It then repealed the Temporary Measures Act concerning Local Autonomy under Supplementary Provision Article 6.\\n\\nUltimately, in determining the boundary of a local government’s jurisdictional area under Article 4(1) of the current Local Autonomy Act, the above provision prescribes that it shall follow the “former” provisions; and in light of the amendment history of the above provision, that “former” standard goes back sequentially to the earliest statutory provision, so the boundary of the jurisdictional area existing as of 1948. 8. 15. may be said to be the original standard. Provisions concerning jurisdictional areas, including Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, legally empower the boundaries of the jurisdictional areas of local governments that existed before the legislation of the laws of the Republic of Korea. And, as a rule, such boundaries of local governments’ jurisdictional areas remain in force to this day unless otherwise determined by statutes or Presidential Decrees that each respective statute uses as the standard for setting jurisdictional areas.
