Of course, if it is recognized that such boundaries have been changed on the basis of unwritten-law grounds such as administrative customary law, the changed boundaries may have effect as the jurisdictional boundaries of local governments.\\n\\n(3) Boundary of Local Governments’ Jurisdictional Areas over Public Waters and Reclaimed Land\\n\\nAccordingly, the boundary of a local government’s jurisdictional area over public waters must also be first confirmed by the boundary existing as of 1948. 8. 15. according to the above standard, which in the end is a matter of factual determination identifying the existence and form of the maritime boundary line at that time.\\n\\nThus, as to the origin of the jurisdictional boundary existing as of 1948. 8. 15., the former Order of the Governor-General of Korea No. 111, “Regarding the Location, Jurisdictional Areas, and Names, Locations, and Jurisdictional Areas of Bu and Gun,” issued on 1913. 12. 29., which prescribed the jurisdictions of bu, do, and gun, continued to remain effective by virtue of Article 11 of Military Government Ordinance No. 21 of 1945. 11. 5.; therefore, the jurisdictional areas of local governments in our country may be said to have inherited the government-administered local administrative districts of the Joseon Dynasty and the Japanese colonial period, and the local administrative districts existing at the time of liberation were maintained as they were (Constitutional Court 2004. 9. 23. 2000HEONRA2, Collection of Cases 16-2, 404, 429).\\n\\nThe maritime boundary lines among such local administrative districts are indicated on topographical maps produced by the Land Survey Department of the Government-General of Korea. During the Japanese colonial period, the “Regulations for General Map Survey Implementation” [Instruction No. 1 of the Temporary Land Survey Bureau of the Government-General of Korea, enacted on 1914. 1. 12. (Taisho 3)] prescribed the method of indicating administrative district boundaries on topographical maps. Article 239 provided: “When crossing a pond, marsh, lake, sea, etc., if the opposite banks are close, draw continuously; if they are far away, stop the drawing at a point 1 cm from the water’s edge.” Article 240 provided: “When passing through a strait or island, etc., draw it with an appropriate length so that the route is clear on the map.” Thus, the principle for indicating boundaries over the sea was prescribed.\\n\\nBy virtue of the above provisions, topographical maps produced by the Land Survey Department of the Government-General of Korea in 1918 (Taisho 7) showed maritime boundary lines dividing provinces and counties. When these provincial and county boundaries were first demarcated, it appears that the boundary lines were set with reference to mountain ranges, downstream areas, tidal flats, or the center of deep-water channels, which may be said to be boundary setting based on natural conditions. Such maritime boundary lines for provincial and county boundaries were mostly reflected unchanged in the national base maps (topographical maps) published after liberation.\\n\\nAccordingly, unless there are special circumstances, the maritime boundary line according to the former provisions should be confirmed on the basis of the topographical map produced by the Land Survey Department of the Government-General of Korea closest to 1948. 8. 15.; and on the basis of the various materials appearing in the record of this case, the topographical map produced in 1918 mentioned above (Exhibit 6 for the Petitioner, page 1225 of the adjudication record) serves as the standard for the above maritime boundary line. And, in light of the nature of a local government, which is composed of residents, territory, and autonomous authority, it is impossible to assume that a local government’s jurisdictional area has a portion without a boundary; therefore, even where a maritime boundary line is not expressly indicated on a topographical map, if administrative customary law exists, it should be based on that; and if administrative customary law has not been established, then the maritime boundary line reasonably inferred from the maritime boundary line indicated on the topographical map should be used. In confirming this, one must comprehensively judge by considering historical circumstances, natural conditions, the exercise of administrative power, and the actual state of handling such affairs (see Supreme Court 2002. 12. 24. decided 2000DO1048).\\n\\nFurther, as noted above, because the topographical maps produced by the Land Survey Department of the Government-General of Korea were mostly reflected unchanged even in the national base maps published after liberation by the National Geographic Information Institute (formerly the National Geography Institute, hereinafter referred to as the “National Geographic Information Institute”), the national base maps published by the National Geographic Information Institute should, unless there are special circumstances, serve as an important standard for determining the maritime boundary line; even in that case, unless the maritime boundary line has been lawfully changed by the repeal or amendment of statutes or Presidential Decrees, or by the establishment of administrative customary law, parts inconsistent with the maritime boundary line as of 1948. 8. 15. need to be corrected accordingly.\\n\\nFurthermore, the jurisdictional area of a local government prescribed by Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act applies regardless of whether the area is land or sea, and the boundary line must be continuous without gaps; thus, even if land changes into sea or sea into land, the boundary above it remains maintained. Accordingly, even when public waters that formerly belonged to the jurisdictional area of a particular local government are reclaimed, unless there is a boundary change by statute or Presidential Decree, the reclaimed land is incorporated into the jurisdictional area of the relevant local government (Constitutional Court 2004. 9. 23. 2000HEONRA2, Collection of Cases 16-2, 404, 443).\\n\\nd. Determination of the Maritime Boundary Line over the Reclaimed Land in this Case\\n\\n(1) Issue\\n\\nPetitioner Gwangyang-si argues that, since the change of jurisdictional area in 1973, the maritime boundary markings over the reclaimed land in this case and the surrounding sea area on the national base maps have been indicated with almost no change and remain so to this day, and specifically relies on the maritime boundary line on the national base map published by the National Geographic Information Institute in June 1988 (Exhibit 52 for the Petitioner).\\n\\nIn response, Respondent Suncheon-si argues that the maritime boundary line on the national base map has also changed each time the national base map was edited and published, and that from 1987 onward the boundary line has gradually been deleted so that now there is almost no boundary distinction, and that no administrative practice concerning the maritime boundary line can be said to exist, and thus the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si should be dismissed. Respondent further asserts that, if any part of Yulchon Industrial Complex belongs to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, then the maritime boundary should be based not on the maritime boundary markings on the national base map but on the compensation line according to customary fishing (Exhibit 16 for the Respondent).\\n\\nAs noted above, since the local government jurisdictional boundary exists even in public waters, what remains is the question of how to identify the specific maritime boundary line in public waters; first, we examine whether the maritime boundary line on the national base map exists in relation to the reclaimed land in this case, and further, whether that maritime boundary line can be recognized as the boundary of local governments’ jurisdictional area prescribed by Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act.\\n\\n(2) Changes in the Maritime Boundary Line on the National Base Maps\\n\\nTaking into account the entries in Exhibit 6 for the Petitioner, Exhibit 9-2 for the Petitioner, Exhibit 53 for the Petitioner, Exhibit 1-2 for the Respondent, and the results of the inquiry by our Court to the President of the National Geographic Information Institute, it can be seen, as shown on the map attached as Appendix 3, that the maritime boundary line over the reclaimed land in this case and the surrounding sea area has changed several times on the national base maps published by the National Geographic Information Institute. Accordingly, it is necessary to determine which of these multiple maritime boundary lines can be recognized as the boundary of the local governments’ jurisdictional area.\\n\\nAmong the above maritime boundary lines, the one in the sea area near the reclaimed land in this case that is closest to the maritime boundary line as of 1948. 8. 15. (the maritime boundary line marked as “old map” in Appendix 3) may be said to be the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1969. The maritime boundary line on the above national base map was not only the maritime boundary line that was temporally closest to 1948. 8. 15., the reference point for determining the jurisdictional boundary, but also, in that it corresponded to a line naturally extending the maritime boundary line as of 1948. 8. 15., it could, absent other circumstances, possibly be considered the boundary of a local government’s jurisdictional area according to the former provisions.\\n\\nHowever, with respect to the part of the boundary between Gwangyang-si and Suncheon-si related to the reclaimed land in this case, pursuant to the Regulations Concerning Changes to the Jurisdictional Areas of Cities, Counties, Districts, Eup, and Myeon (Presidential Decree No. 6542 of 1973. 3. 12.), on 1973. 7. 1. Jangdo and Songdo of Jeonnam Gwangyang-gun Golyak-myeon were transferred to the jurisdiction of Yeocheon-gun Yulchon-myeon, and this constitutes a change in the jurisdictional area prescribed by statute, which must be considered in confirming the jurisdictional boundary. Taking this into account, one may posit a national base map published in 1974 that reflects the above change in jurisdictional area after the national base map published in 1969; and among the maritime boundary lines on this national base map, the maritime boundary line in the sea area near the reclaimed land in this case coincides with the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1969 and may serve as the jurisdictional boundary for the reclaimed land in this case.\\n\\nThereafter, the boundary line in the sea near the reclaimed land in this case shows a changed form in the national base maps published in 1975, 2001, and 2004. After 1974, pursuant to Article 2 and Supplementary Provision Article 1 of the Act on the Establishment, etc. of 2 City-County Integrated-Type Municipalities Including Gwangyang-si, Jeollanam-do (enacted as Act No. 4801 on 1994. 12. 22.), on 1995. 1. 1. Donggwangyang-si and Gwangyang-gun of Jeollanam-do were abolished, respectively, and Gwangyang-si was established over the areas of the cities and counties being abolished. However, such abolition of local governments cannot be the legal basis for the above change in the maritime boundary line, because the boundary between Donggwangyang-si and Gwangyang-gun simply continued as Gwangyang-si and could not affect the boundary between Gwangyang-si and Suncheon-si that is at issue in this case. Therefore, the maritime boundary lines changed as above cannot be recognized as the boundary of the jurisdictional area prescribed by Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act.\\n\\nIf so, the jurisdictional boundary on the national base map published in 1974 should be regarded as conforming to the jurisdictional boundary as of 1948. 8. 15.; unless there are special circumstances to the contrary suggesting lawful change by repeal or amendment of statutes or Presidential Decrees, or by the establishment of administrative customary law, it is appropriate to regard it as the former-provisions-based jurisdictional boundary prescribed by Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act.\\n\\n(3) Existence of a Jurisdictional Boundary under Administrative Customary Law\\n\\n(a) Determination of the Petitioner's Argument\\n\\nNext, we examine whether the maritime boundary line claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si, which does not conform to the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1974, can be recognized as a boundary under administrative customary law.\\n\\nFirst, Petitioner Gwangyang-si argues that the jurisdictional boundary in Sepung reclaimed land, located north of the reclaimed land in this case, was formed by the maritime boundary line claimed by the Petitioner; and in this regard, taking into account the entries in Exhibits 49-1 and 49-2 for the Petitioner, Exhibit 58 for the Petitioner, Exhibit 64 for the Petitioner, and the result of the inquiry by our Court to the President of the National Geographic Information Institute, it can be recognized that Sepung reclaimed land, located north of the reclaimed land in this case, received approval of completion on 1968. 7. 28., that the land on the reclaimed site was divided between Seungju-gun and Gwangyang-gun, based on a small stream crossing Gwangyang-eup Sepung-ri and Haeryong-myeon Sinseong-ri, pursuant to the application of the Gwangyang Land Improvement Association dated 1968. 7. 23., and given separate parcel numbers, and that they were each registered in the cadastral registers on that basis; that the new boundary thus formed was, compared with before, shifted toward Suncheon-si and was a straight boundary line dividing the reclaimed land north and south, and did not coincide with the former maritime boundary line, but was not reflected in the national base maps published by the National Geographic Information Institute until 1986 and was first indicated only in the national base map published in 1987; that the above de facto boundary change indicated in the national base map published in 1987 has been maintained to this day; and that thereafter a maritime boundary line starting at the southern end of the above boundary line was newly indicated on the national base map published in 2001. In light of the above facts, after the completion of Sepung reclaimed land, a straight boundary line dividing the reclaimed land north and south was formed, different from the former maritime boundary line; after being indicated in the national base map published in 1987, it has been maintained to the present without any significant dispute; and with respect to the respective lands separately registered in the cadastral registers of Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si on the basis of the above boundary, the local governments’ local tax taxing authority, etc. would also have been exercised according to that boundary classification; therefore, there is room to see that administrative practice was established with respect to the changed land boundary line.\\n\\nHowever, the establishment of a new jurisdictional boundary in this manner, carried out under the leadership of the Gwangyang Land Improvement Association and with the understanding of both local governments, is merely the formation of a land boundary line as a means of determining the attribution of the reclaimed land as it became land; and it cannot be concluded that this naturally became the standard for the maritime boundary line in other sea areas that had not yet become land. And even though thereafter a maritime boundary line starting from the southern end of the boundary line on the Sepung reclaimed land was indicated, no legal basis for that maritime boundary line can be found; therefore, whether the maritime boundary line claimed by the Petitioner, lying on the extension of the land boundary shown on the national base map published in 1987, can be recognized as the boundary of the jurisdictional area ultimately depends on whether administrative customary law was separately established with respect thereto.\\n\\nAccordingly, examining further, there is no indication in the record that the basic local governments belonging to Jeollanam-do, namely Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si, independently exercised authority over fishery license dispositions, etc. originally belonging to Jeollanam-do, on the basis of the maritime boundary line claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si in the sea area near the reclaimed land in this case. Rather, as will be examined in detail below in subparagraph (b), the predecessors of the above local governments, namely Gwangyang-gun and Seungju-gun, had issued fishery licenses in a manner contrary to the above maritime boundary line; therefore, the actual state of authority exercise in public waters cannot support an administrative practice concerning the maritime boundary line claimed by the Petitioner, and may rather serve as strong counterevidence thereto.\\n\\nAlso, although Jeollanam-do had been establishing and implementing plans regarding the creation of Yulchon Industrial Complex on the basis of the maritime boundary line on the national base map, the result of our Court’s inquiry to the Governor of Jeollanam-do reveals that the national base maps used by Jeollanam-do from the time of plan formulation and whenever there was a plan change in connection with the industrial complex creation project were almost always different maps rather than the same national base map published in the same year, and that the publication year was not exactly consistent. Accordingly, it is difficult to recognize administrative practice centered on the maritime boundary line claimed by the Petitioner.\\n\\nPetitioner Gwangyang-si further argues that the administrative maps published by the Mayor of Suncheon-si and the Mayor of Gwangyang-si have the meaning of customary-law ordinances and that legal effect should therefore be recognized in the production of administrative maps; however, administrative maps are not produced as ordinances, and moreover, in producing administrative maps that require approval from the National Geographic Information Institute, mere transfer and depiction of the boundaries shown on national base maps published by the National Geographic Information Institute cannot be regarded as the establishment of administrative practice; thus, this argument by Petitioner Gwangyang-si is without merit.\\n\\nPetitioner Gwangyang-si also argues, in essence, that because Respondent Suncheon-si formulated a city plan only for areas excluding the disputed area in this case, it accepted the maritime boundary line as claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si and that administrative practice based thereon was formed. However, the fact that Respondent Suncheon-si took a prudent measure of excluding the disputed portion when formulating a city plan, which could greatly affect the interests of residents, does not mean that the boundary of the jurisdictional area was recognized or that administrative practice was established.\\n\\nIn addition, even though Jeollanam-do, from the time it approved the basic plan for Yulchon Industrial Complex, notified the relevant local governments whenever the area or location of the project site changed and instructed them to announce increases or decreases in the area incorporated into the jurisdictional area, and even though Respondent Suncheon-si did not raise any objection thereto, and even though in February 1997 OO Co., Ltd. applied to the Mayor of Gwangyang-si for a permit to install structures within the public waters in this case, and Petitioner Gwangyang-si granted a permit for occupancy, etc. under Article 4 of the Public Waters Management Act on 1997. 2. 28., these circumstances alone are insufficient to conclude that administrative practice existed with respect to the specific maritime boundary line as claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si.\\n\\n(b) Determination of the Respondent’s Argument\\n\\nRespondent Suncheon-si argues that, if a maritime boundary line over public waters is recognized, the compensation line according to customary fishing should be used as the standard. However, since the compensation for fishery rights arising from the creation of Yulchon No. 1 Local Industrial Complex was made on the basis of customary fishing, irrespective of the maritime boundary markings on the national base maps published by the National Geographic Information Institute, this is also acknowledged by the Respondent, so the above argument by Respondent Suncheon-si concerning the maritime boundary line cannot be accepted.\\n\\nHowever, taking into account the entries in Exhibits 35 and 36 for the Petitioner and Exhibits 13, 14-1 through 14-4, 15, and 16 for the Respondent, etc., with regard to fishery licenses, which originally fell within the authority of the metropolitan local government, the Governor of Jeollanam-do issued Jeollanam-do Instruction No. 660 on 1985. 2. 18., internally delegating part of the fishery licensing authority to the heads of cities and counties; and by virtue thereof, in fact, in the sea area near the reclaimed land in this case, the head of Gwangyang-gun, on 1985. 12. 12., acted on behalf in issuing fishery licenses with license numbers 10018, 10019, and 10020, and the head of Seungju-gun, on 1985. 11. 23., acted on behalf in issuing fishery licenses with license numbers 10053, 10054, and 10055; that the areas of the above fishery licenses issued by the head of Gwangyang-gun were all located on the side of Gwangyang-si, on the basis of the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1988 cited by Petitioner Gwangyang-si; but among the fishery licenses issued by the head of Seungju-gun, for which the license period was set until 1995, the area of license No. 10055 was located on the side of Suncheon-si, on the basis of the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1988; the area of license No. 10053 straddled the maritime boundary line between Gwangyang-si and Suncheon-si on the national base map published in 1988; and the area of license No. 10054 extended to the side of Gwangyang-si on the basis of the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1988. In light of these facts, at the time of the above fishery licenses, the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1988 as claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si did not function properly as a jurisdictional boundary unlike a land boundary line; rather, in light of the above evidence, it appears that fishery licenses in the sea area near the reclaimed land in this case were generally granted on the basis of the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1974, and that compensation for fishery damage was made on the basis of the compensation line established according to the actual distribution of customary fishing formed thereon.\\n\\nAccordingly, the actual state of such fishery licenses makes it difficult to recognize administrative practice concerning the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1988 as claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si, while it may be said to be an example showing that the boundary on the national base map published in 1974 was functioning as the actual boundary at that time.\\n\\n(c) Therefore, in this case, where no further evidence can be found to recognize the existence of administrative practice concerning each maritime boundary line claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si with respect to public waters near the reclaimed land in this case, it cannot be said that a maritime boundary line under customary law was established as claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si.\\n\\n(4) Conclusion on This Point\\n\\nTherefore, since neither a positive-law basis nor the establishment of administrative customary law can be found for concluding that the jurisdictional boundary changed after 1974 in the reclaimed land in this case and the surrounding sea area, the maritime boundary line on the national base map published in 1974, as noted above, should be regarded as the jurisdictional boundary in the public waters near the reclaimed land in this case; and as noted above, even when that public water is reclaimed, it has effect as the jurisdictional boundary over the reclaimed land.\\n\\ne. Determination of Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s Jurisdictional Authority\\n\\nIf the above boundary line is further indicated on the reclaimed land in this case, then the jurisdictional boundary between Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si in the reclaimed land in this case becomes the line sequentially connecting the points a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, and i as marked on the map attached as Appendix 1; accordingly, the left (western) side thereof belongs to the jurisdictional area of Respondent Suncheon-si, and the right (eastern) side thereof belongs to the jurisdictional area of Petitioner Gwangyang-si. Such jurisdictional area, based on the reclaimed land in this case, results in the boundary being shifted to the right (east) from the jurisdictional boundary claimed by Petitioner Gwangyang-si, thereby somewhat narrowing the jurisdictional area shown in the petition (the disputed area in this case).\\n\\nAccordingly, the right (eastern) portion of the reclaimed land in this case to the right of the line sequentially connecting the points a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, and i as marked on the map attached as Appendix 1 belongs to the jurisdictional authority of Petitioner Gwangyang-si.\\n\\nf. Whether the Tax Dispositions by Respondent Suncheon-si Are Void\\n\\nAnd the portion, among the tax dispositions imposing urban planning tax, joint facilities tax, etc. on OO Co., Ltd. on 2003. 7. 1., that was made with respect to the object belonging to Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s jurisdictional authority as above is a tax disposition made by a person lacking authority, thereby infringing Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s local autonomy rights (autonomous fiscal authority), and thus has no effect.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\n\\nAccordingly, the petition by the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si and the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si are inadmissible, and are therefore both dismissed; it is confirmed that the jurisdictional authority over the right (eastern) portion of the reclaimed land in this case to the right of the line sequentially connecting the points a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, and i as marked on the map attached as Appendix 1 belongs to Petitioner Gwangyang-si; the portion, among the tax dispositions imposing urban planning tax, joint facilities tax, etc. on OO Co., Ltd. on 2003. 7. 1., that was made with respect to the object belonging to Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s jurisdictional authority as above is confirmed to be void; and the remainder of Petitioner Gwangyang-si’s petition against Respondent Suncheon-si is dismissed as without merit. Accordingly, it is so decided as stated in the order.\\n\\nThis decision is in accordance with the unanimous opinion of all the other participating Justices, except for the dissenting opinion set forth below by Justices Kim Gyeong-il, Ju Seon-hwe, and Jo Dae-hyeon in 6.\\n\\n6. Dissenting Opinion of Justices Kim Gyeong-il, Ju Seon-hwe, and Jo Dae-hyeon\\n\\nWe dissent from the majority opinion, which held on the premise that the jurisdictional area of a local government includes the sea as well, that the reclaimed land indicated in paragraph 2 of the order among the reclaimed land in this case belongs to the Petitioner, and therefore state our opinion to dismiss as follows.\\n\\na. A local government’s autonomous authority over public waters does not exist.\\n\\n(1) Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act provides that “the territory of a local government shall follow the former provisions, and when changing it,” it shall be determined by “statute” in the case of changes between cities/provinces, and by “Presidential Decree” in the case of changes between cities/counties/districts. Historically, this provision was enacted on the assumption of territorial setting for land whose cadastral organization has been arranged or is capable of being arranged pursuant to cadastral-related statutes and regulations such as the Land Survey Ordinance; it was not enacted with the sea, which is public waters, in mind, and there has also been no instance where the jurisdictional area of a local government over the sea has been fixed by statute or regulation. Therefore, one cannot immediately interpret this provision to mean that the sea is included in the jurisdictional area of a local government.\\n\\nJust as there must be a basis such as cadastral records, including cadastral maps or forest maps, for assigning parcel numbers for the purpose of setting boundaries to distinguish the jurisdictional area of land, there must likewise be an authoritative register such as a maritime cadastral map for assigning sea parcel numbers and demarcating boundaries in order to set the sea as a local government’s territory. However, such a register does not yet exist.\\n\\n(2) Article 53 of the Fisheries Act provides that, when necessary for fishery coordination between cities/provinces, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may adjust fishing waters by means such as designating joint fishing waters, and, when necessary for fishery coordination between cities/counties/autonomous districts, the Mayor/Do Governor may adjust fishing waters. In addition, Article 14 of the Inland Waters Fisheries Act provides that, in the case of licensed fishing, permitted fishing, or reported fishing, when the inland waters for which a license, permission, or report is sought extend across two or more special cities, metropolitan cities, or provinces, the competent authority to accept the license, permission, or report shall be determined by consultation between the relevant mayors/governors; and when the inland waters for which a license, permission, or report is sought extend across two or more cities/counties/autonomous districts, the Mayor/Do Governor having jurisdiction over the relevant cities/counties/autonomous districts shall designate the authority that will accept the license, permission, or report. The fact that the above provisions allow the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or the Mayor/Do Governor to adjust fishing waters, etc. without resort to statute or Presidential Decree means that public waters are under the jurisdiction of the State, not under the jurisdiction of local governments. If public waters were not under State jurisdiction but necessarily had to belong to the jurisdiction of some local government, there would be no need to establish such adjustment procedures.\\n\\n(3) Meanwhile, under Article 41(1) of the Fisheries Act, offshore fisheries require permission from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries; under Article 8(1) of the same Act, set-net fishing and aquaculture fishing require licenses from the Mayor/County Governor or Head of Gu Office; and such licensing by the Mayor/County Governor/Head of Gu Office must be conducted in compliance with the Rules on the Management of Fishery Licenses, etc. (Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Ordinance No. 00251) and the basic guidelines for fishery ground use development plans prepared and circulated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries pursuant thereto (Fisheries Act Article 4, Enforcement Decree Article 2, Rules on the Management of Fishery Licenses, etc. Article 2). These provisions presuppose that jurisdiction over public waters is vested in the State and provide that the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, as the competent State administrative agency, exercises that authority. Accordingly, even if heads of local governments are made to exercise such fishery licensing authority with respect to coastal fisheries, etc., this is nothing more than the performance of delegated affairs by delegation from the State, and cannot be regarded as the exercise by a local government of its own inherent authority. These provisions, too, would serve as grounds for concluding that local governments do not possess jurisdictional authority over public waters.\\n\\n(4) The majority opinion views the maritime boundary lines indicated on the topographical maps produced in 1918 pursuant to the Regulations for General Map Survey Implementation (1914), an instruction of the Temporary Land Survey Bureau of the Government-General of Korea, as well as the maritime boundary lines indicated on the topographical maps published in 1974 by the National Geographic Information Institute, as the basis for dividing jurisdictional boundaries among local governments. However, the official view of the National Geographic Information Institute is that these maritime boundary lines indicated on topographical maps merely indicate the affiliation of islands and do not have any legally binding force in determining the jurisdictional area of a local government, and there is no dispute among government ministries on this point. Therefore, local government boundaries cannot be fixed on the basis of maritime boundary lines indicated on topographical maps; and in order for, as the majority opinion does, maritime boundary lines on topographical maps to have such a function, one would need to assign sea parcel numbers to public waters and prepare a maritime cadastral map to create an authoritative register. However, as noted above, such work has not yet been carried out.\\n\\n(5) Of course, we do not oppose the granting of jurisdiction over public waters to local governments through legislation. If legislation grants local governments jurisdiction over public waters, then local governments may have jurisdiction over public waters in that case. However, the State, instead of granting local governments jurisdiction over public waters as above, may set various management zones, such as the scope of fishing waters, the jurisdictional area of the Maritime Safety Tribunal, and the jurisdictional area of the maritime police station, according to national marine policy objectives and needs, and may also delegate, while leaving jurisdiction over public waters vested in the State, so that local governments may exercise management authority on the basis of provisions in individual statutes, etc. There may be various policy-based methods for deciding who shall have jurisdiction over public waters and how management shall be conducted. Accordingly, unless jurisdiction over public waters has been granted to local governments by statute, there is no reason to regard local governments as having jurisdiction over public waters; rather, in such a case, the jurisdiction should be regarded as belonging to the State. However, the majority opinion proceeds on the premise that, on the basis of Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, which prescribes the setting of boundaries for land, jurisdiction over public waters necessarily belongs to local governments, and we cannot agree with that.\\n\\n(6) In conclusion, since there is no basis on which to recognize that local governments have jurisdiction over public waters, the jurisdictional authority of local governments over public waters should be regarded as nonexistent, and only the jurisdictional area may be determined by statute.\\n\\nb. Even if local governments have jurisdiction over public waters, the jurisdictional authority of local governments cannot be recognized with respect to newly created land formed by reclaiming public waters unless statutes are newly enacted to determine the jurisdictional area thereof.\\n\\nThe meaning of Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, which provides that “the territory of a local government shall follow the former provisions,” is that when an administrative district was previously established, the established territory is left unchanged as it is. Therefore, where land that did not previously exist is newly created, it cannot be said to follow the former provisions. Land created by reclaiming the sea is land newly created from what did not previously exist; it is not that the form of the same land has simply changed from sea to land while maintaining identity. Therefore, in determining jurisdictional areas, the boundary standard concerning the jurisdictional area that existed in the former public waters cannot be applied as it stands. This is because the issue here is not one of standards for demarcating administrative districts over public waters—namely, how to determine the administrative district of the sea—but rather one of how to determine the jurisdiction over newly created land, which is a question concerning the standards for demarcating administrative districts on land. In other words, this is the issue of constitutively determining the jurisdictional area of newly created, unassigned land. However, no statute has yet been prepared as to how the jurisdictional area of newly created land is to be determined. It is only that Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act provides that “changes to the boundary of the jurisdictional area of a city, county, or autonomous district shall be determined by Presidential Decree”; and since incorporating an area whose boundaries have not been established into a city also constitutes a boundary change in a broad sense, the jurisdictional area over land created by reclaiming public waters between cities/counties and autonomous districts should also be determined by Presidential Decree pursuant to Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act. If the jurisdictional area is determined by Presidential Decree, of course it must be determined from a social and public-interest perspective by considering general principles for the demarcation of administrative districts for land, such as social common sense, geographic location, efficient management of national land, management of administrative districts, and efficiency in port management, rather than the principles for boundary setting for the sea that already existed. However, as for the reclaimed land in public waters between Gwangyang-si and Suncheon-si in this case, no Presidential Decree has yet been enacted to determine the jurisdictional boundary.\\n\\nc. As seen above, unless statutes granting local governments autonomous authority over public waters have been enacted, local governments do not have jurisdictional authority over public waters; and even if such authority is assumed to exist, statutes determining the jurisdiction over newly created reclaimed land in public waters would need to be newly enacted. In the reclaimed land in this case, for which no Presidential Decree has been enacted, it cannot be said that the autonomous authority indicated in paragraph 2 of the order has been granted to the Petitioner; therefore, this petition for adjudication should be dismissed.\\n\\nJustice Yoon Young-cheol (Presiding Justice), Kwon Seong (unable to sign and seal due to retirement), Kim Hyo-jong, Kim Gyeong-il, Song In-jun, Ju Seon-hwe (Presiding Justice), Lee Gong-hyeon, Jo Dae-hyeon\\n\\n[Appendix 1] Diagram (Order)\\n\\n[Appendix 2] Diagram (Petition)\\n\\n[Appendix 3] Diagram (Changes in Maritime Boundary Lines on Topographical Maps)\\n\\n[Appendix 4] The Petitioners’ Arguments, the Respondents’ Response, and the Opinion of the Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs\\n\\n1. Summary of the Petitioners’ Arguments\\n\\na. With respect to the procedural requirements\\n\\nRespondent Suncheon-si has standing as a party.\\n\\nAs the head of the executive organ of a local government, the head of a local government has authority to administer, execute, control, and represent the affairs of the local government; accordingly, Respondent Suncheon-si has standing as a party in this case because, on 2003. 7. 1., it imposed and notified OO Co., Ltd. of urban planning tax and joint facilities tax.\\n\\nb. With respect to the merits\\n\\n(1) Public waters belong to the jurisdictional area of a local government.\\n\\n(a) National base maps are produced and published pursuant to the Survey Act and the Rules on Map Drawing, and individual statutes related to the sea, such as the Fisheries Act, the Fishery Ground Management Act, the Public Waters Management Act, the Public Waters Reclamation Act, and the Coastal Management Act, are also enacted and enforced on the premise that public waters belong to the jurisdictional area of a local government; and since local governments and the general public process permits and approvals concerning occupation and use of public waters based on such maps, the maritime boundary on the national base map has normative force.\\n\\n(b) Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act provides that the names and territories of local governments shall follow the former provisions, and when changing them or abolishing and merging local governments, they shall be determined by statute, provided that changes to the boundary of the jurisdictional area of a city, county, or autonomous district shall be determined by Presidential Decree; the phrase “shall follow the former provisions” does not refer only to land but is a concept including the sea surface.\\n\\n(c) Since the 1960s, our country has reclaimed many sea areas and used them as farmland, factory sites, residential sites, etc.; with respect to such reclaimed lands, local governments that had jurisdiction over the sea surface have, without any change in jurisdictional area under Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, newly registered them under Article 17 of the Cadastral Act according to the boundary line of the jurisdictional area indicated on national base maps.\\n\\n(d) Respondent Suncheon-si also, in planning urban development, established its city plan for public waters in accordance with the maritime boundary line shown on the national base map.\\n\\n(e) In order for a local government to exercise various authorities over the sea surface delegated by the State and also exercise its inherent local autonomy authority, the scope of that authority must be demarcated according to the boundaries among local governments based on the national base map, and lawful exercise of authority is possible only within that demarcated territory.\\n\\n(2) The reclaimed land in this case belongs to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si.\\n\\n(a) According to the national base map, the reclaimed land in this case is land that was reclaimed from the sea previously under the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, and since after that sea became land there was no measure under statutes to change this, the reclaimed land in this case naturally belongs to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, which had previously exercised jurisdiction over that sea.\\n\\n(b) Maritime boundary markings in local administrative districts can be found even on Kim Jeong-ho’s Daedong Yeojido and maps of our country produced by the Government-General of Korea, and they have continued to be indicated on national base maps; although the maritime boundary markings on national base maps differ somewhat depending on the time of compilation due to reflection of administrative district changes, the degree of divergence is not such as to cast doubt on the reliability of the national base maps, and since the residents of Gwangyang-si and Suncheon-si, as well as the general public and administrative authorities, all accept without objection the maritime boundary lines marked on national base maps, customary-law effect has formed with respect to the maritime boundary lines on national base maps.\\n\\n1) Even the administrative maps published by Respondent Suncheon-si every three years with approval from the National Geographic Information Institute show the boundaries among local governments over the sea surface.\\n\\n2) Jeollanam-do, the project implementation entity for the construction of Yulchon Industrial Complex, from the planning and development stage through to the present, sent official documents to the relevant local governments, namely Yeocheon-gun (current Yeosu-si), Seungju-gun (current Suncheon-si), Gwangyang-gun (current Gwangyang-si), and Donggwangyang-si (current Gwangyang-si), notifying them of the location and area incorporated into the jurisdictional area, and also informed them when the area increased or decreased due to changes in the development plan.\\n\\n3) Around April 1991, when Yulchon Industrial Complex was designated, the relevant city and county heads, namely the head of Yeocheon-gun (current Mayor of Yeosu-si), the head of Seungju-gun (current Mayor of Suncheon-si), the head of Gwangyang-gun (current Mayor of Gwangyang-si), and the Mayor of Donggwangyang-si (current Mayor of Gwangyang-si), announced the designation of Yulchon Industrial Complex in local media and collected the opinions of local residents; at that time, no one expressed any objection regarding the jurisdictional area.\\n\\n4) Formerly, the heads of Gwangyang-gun and Gwangyang-si exercised authority over 267 fishery licenses, temporary dock construction for the transport of equipment and materials for the creation of Yulchon Industrial Complex, permits for occupation of public waters, etc. with respect to the public waters in this case before reclamation, pursuant to local autonomy rights of Gwangyang-si and delegated authority from State affairs.\\n\\n(c) In connection with the construction of Yulchon Industrial Complex, Petitioner Gwangyang-si provided about 1,677 hectares of licensed fishing grounds, the livelihood basis of fishermen; paid the construction costs for road construction up to the Gwangyang Interchange on the Namhae Expressway within Yulchon Industrial Complex and the compensation for the incorporated land; and made many contributions, including allowing Gwangyang Port to be used as a unloading site for raw materials for OO Co., Ltd.’s products; and it is also bearing, not only disadvantages such as subsidence of the road foundation due to transport of raw materials and cracks in houses along the roadside, but also environmental problems arising from the creation of the industrial complex.\\n\\n(d) Even if, as Respondent claims, the land created by reclaiming the sea is newly created land unrelated to jurisdiction over the former public waters, the reclaimed land in this case cannot be said to belong to the jurisdiction of Respondent Suncheon-si until a Presidential Decree is enacted under Article 4(1) of the Local Autonomy Act to newly demarcate the jurisdictional area.\\n\\n(3) The tax disposition by the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si infringes the Petitioners’ local autonomy rights.\\n\\nThe Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si’s imposition of local taxes on the land and buildings of the above company located within the jurisdictional area of Petitioner Gwangyang-si is a tax disposition by a person lacking authority, and is an illegal and void disposition that infringes the local autonomy rights (local fiscal authority) granted to the Petitioners, etc. by Article 117(1) of the Constitution, Articles 9 and 10 of the Local Autonomy Act, and Article 2 of the Local Tax Act.\\n\\n2. Summary of the Respondents’ Response\\n\\na. Response concerning the procedural requirements\\n\\nThe Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si and the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si lack standing as parties.\\n\\nSince the imposition and collection of local taxes are autonomous affairs, which are the inherent affairs of a local government, the authority to impose and collect local taxes belongs to the local government; the head of a local government, as a representative of the local government, merely performs the duties of imposing and collecting local taxes and does not possess independent authority to impose and collect local taxes. Therefore, the head of a local government cannot be a party to a petition for adjudication on a jurisdictional dispute concerning the existence or nonexistence of local tax imposition authority. Accordingly, the petition by the Mayor of Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Respondents and the petition by Petitioner Gwangyang-si against the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si are inadmissible and should be dismissed. Furthermore, the core issue in this case is which local government the land reclaimed from public waters belongs to; thus, there is no practical benefit in recognizing standing as a party for the head of a local government.\\n\\nb. Response on the merits\\n\\n(1) Public waters do not belong to the jurisdictional area of a local government.\\n\\nThe provisions of Article 4 of the Local Autonomy Act concerning the territory of local governments are provisions concerning land, whose boundaries can be easily determined; maritime boundaries are not included therein, and, technically, it is still impossible to accurately survey maritime boundaries.\\n\\n(2) The reclaimed land in this case does not belong to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si.\\n\\n(a) The maritime boundary on the national base map cannot be regarded as the maritime boundary between local governments.\\n\\n1) According to the relevant statutes concerning the preparation of national base maps, administrative district boundaries are to be indicated on topographical maps only when they are clear; in actual fact, however, topographical maps published after 1987 indicate the boundaries of land areas and island areas, but maritime boundaries are not indicated.\\n\\n2) The National Geographic Information Institute, which produces and publishes national base maps, also takes the position that maritime boundary markings on topographical maps merely indicate the affiliation of islands and are not administrative district boundaries.\\n\\n3) The Central Dispute Mediation Committee also held, in the case concerning the application for mediation of a boundary dispute over reclaimed public waters in the Gunja district of Siheung-si, that it is difficult to determine the boundaries of administrative districts over public waters, and that the maritime boundary line shown on the city planning map cannot be regarded as the standard for boundary adjustment.\\n\\n4) The maritime boundary line indicated on the city planning maps of Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si simply followed the maritime boundary line on the national base map for administrative convenience, and cannot be taken to mean that the maritime boundary between Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si was definitively fixed as the maritime boundary on the national base map.\\n\\n(b) Standards for attribution of the reclaimed land in this case\\n\\n1) The maritime boundary on the national base map has no normative effect, and there is no other material showing that the reclaimed land in this case belongs to Petitioner Gwangyang-si. Moreover, since the public waters existing before reclamation were already extinguished for public use, the maritime boundary of the public waters cannot serve as the boundary standard for the land in this case.\\n\\n2) The sending of official documents by the Governor of Jeollanam-do, the project implementation entity, to the relevant local governments in the course of project implementation was prompted by concerns over infringement of the legal and factual interests their residents had previously enjoyed; and since the attribution relationship of the reclaimed land could not be determined at the project implementation stage, the selection of the relevant local governments for administrative convenience followed the maritime boundary markings on the national base map, which cannot serve as a basis for saying that the reclaimed land in this case belongs to the Petitioners’ jurisdiction.\\n\\n3) The standard for attribution of reclaimed land should be determined by comprehensively considering the land connected to the reclaimed land, the various natural and geographic conditions around the reclaimed land, the purpose of reclamation of public waters, the social and economic function of the reclaimed land, and convenience in the exercise of administrative power.\\n\\n(c) Reasons why the reclaimed land in this case should belong to Respondent Suncheon-si\\n\\n1) Respondent Suncheon-si endured environmental damage in the reclamation process and provided reclaimed soil, and also made many direct and indirect contributions and efforts to the development of Yulchon Industrial Complex, including investing city budget in the access road project for Yulchon Industrial Complex.\\n\\n2) If Yulchon Industrial Complex were divided into three parts among three cities as the Petitioners argue, administrative inconvenience for the project operator would be expected, and there would be a risk of disagreement among local governments, which would obstruct activation of the industrial complex.\\n\\n3) Yulchon Industrial Complex is adjacent to Haeryong-myeon, Suncheon-si, on the land side, whereas it is about 600 meters away from Gwangyang-si across the sea; thus, in terms of accessibility, convenience for tenant companies, and strengthening corporate competitiveness, it is reasonable for it to belong to Suncheon-si. In addition, the entire 450 employees of OO Co., Ltd. use Suncheon-si as their living base; compensation was provided for the loss of fishery rights suffered by fishermen of Gwangyang, whereas no compensation was provided for losses suffered by residents of Suncheon-si due to permits for soil and stone extraction; when accidents occurred in the areas of Yulchon No. 1 Industrial Complex that, according to the maritime boundary markings on the national base map, belong to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, the Gwangyang Police Station and Gwangyang Fire Station did not respond to accident reports on the ground that the accident site was within the jurisdiction of Suncheon-si; Jeollanam-do granted, on 1997. 2. 25., permission for use before completion with respect to the 135,000 pyeong site of OO’s cold-rolled steel plant within Yulchon No. 1 Industrial Complex, and when Respondent Suncheon-si granted building permission upon OO’s building permit application, Petitioner Gwangyang-si made no objection or request for consultation at that time (it is only later alleged that a request for consultation was made); considering these circumstances, too, the reclaimed land in this case should properly belong to Suncheon-si.\\n\\n(d) The Constitutional Court’s decision in the jurisdictional dispute between Dangjin-gun and Pyeongtaek-si does not apply to this case.\\n\\n1) The Constitutional Court determined the maritime boundary between Dangjin-gun and Pyeongtaek-si according to the maritime boundary markings on the national base map because the administrative agencies of local governments, etc. had been conducting administrative acts recognizing the above maritime boundary as the maritime boundary between Gyeonggi-do and Chungcheongnam-do, and a legal conviction had been formed among administrative agencies and the general public. However, no such practice or legal conviction has formed between Petitioner Gwangyang-si and Respondent Suncheon-si that the maritime boundary markings on the national base map are to be the boundary; therefore, the maritime boundary markings on the national base map cannot serve as the standard for the maritime boundary. In other words, the maritime boundary markings on national base maps showing the maritime boundary between Gwangyang-si and Suncheon-si differed in location depending on the year of publication of the national base map, and the maritime boundary markings near Yulchon No. 1 Industrial Complex were gradually deleted in topographical maps published after 1987, and at present there are almost no boundary markings in the sea except in the land boundary area and the sea near Jangdo.\\n\\n2) Furthermore, in compensating for fishery rights arising from the creation of Yulchon No. 1 Industrial Complex, the relevant local governments compensated on the basis of customary fishing, through which actual local fishermen had maintained their livelihoods, regardless of the maritime boundary markings on the national base map; therefore, it cannot be said that there existed an administrative practice by which administrative agencies of local governments recognized the maritime boundary line on the national base map as the boundary line of administrative districts.\\n\\n3) Even if a part of Yulchon No. 1 Industrial Complex belongs to the jurisdiction of Petitioner Gwangyang-si, the maritime boundary should be based not on the maritime boundary markings on the national base map but on the compensation line according to customary fishing.\\n\\n(3) The tax disposition by the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si did not infringe the Petitioners’ authority.\\n\\nEven if, arguendo, the reclaimed land in this case belongs to Petitioner Gwangyang-si, the local tax imposition disposition by the Mayor of Respondent Suncheon-si does not infringe the Petitioners’ local autonomy rights (autonomous fiscal authority). This is because, even if the Mayor of Suncheon-si imposed local taxes on the above company, the Mayor of Gwangyang-si could also impose local taxes on the above company if the Petitioners had legitimate authority.\\n\\n3. Summary of the Opinion of the Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs\\n\\na. The “territory” in Article 4 of the Local Autonomy Act does not include the sea.\\n\\nGenerally, the jurisdictional area of a local government is interpreted as including the sea as well, but in light of history and application examples, the “territory” of a local government under Article 4 of the Local Autonomy Act does not include the sea. However, the fact that the sea is not included in the territory under Article 4 of the Local Autonomy Act does not deny the need to demarcate sea boundaries among local governments; various management zones may be established by custom or according to the State’s policy objectives.\\n\\nb. Standards for setting maritime boundaries among local governments and for attributing reclaimed land\\n\\n(1) Under current law, there is no statute serving as the basis for setting sea boundaries, so maritime boundaries among local governments should be determined case by case, taking into comprehensive consideration all circumstances such as boundary markings on national base maps, practice, historical circumstances, natural conditions, and location. However, the standard for demarcating sea boundaries is appropriately applied ex post in the event of a dispute, and overall redemarcation of sea boundaries is inappropriate because it may cause confusion and new disputes.\\n\\n(2) Although there is no express provision on the attribution of land reclaimed from public waters, reclaimed land is also part of the national territory and, in essence, has the character of an administrative district; therefore, it is desirable to determine jurisdiction by comprehensively considering all conditions such as the geographic location of the reclaimed land, the living sphere of the residents, and administrative convenience.\\n\\n(3) Currently, with regard to the procedure for attribution of reclaimed land from public waters, since reclaimed land is newly created land and constitutes a new incorporation of unassigned land, it has a different nature from adjustment of districts assigned parcel numbers, and is therefore subject not to the administrative district adjustment procedure under the Local Autonomy Act but to the cadastral registration procedure under Article 17 of the Cadastral Act (application for new registration).\\n\\nc. Attribution of Local Tax Taxing Authority\\n\\nThe authority to levy local taxes is effective within the scope of the administrative jurisdiction of the relevant local government; therefore, once the boundary of administrative jurisdiction is established, the scope of taxing authority will be determined accordingly."}
