{"[2006DA18228]": "1. With respect to the first ground of appeal by the Defendant and the first ground of appeal by the Plaintiff’s Successor Intervenor\\nThe court below, after finding the facts as stated in its opinion based on the evidence it adopted, held that the administrative guidance that the Defendant gave to the Plaintiff before 1995. 1. 3. was a non-coercive, non-power exercise intended to achieve the administrative purpose with the Plaintiff’s voluntary cooperation and thus did not exceed the limits of administrative guidance, but that the administrative guidance given on 1995. 1. 3. constituted an unlawful administrative guidance that departed from those limits by improperly coercing the Plaintiff, who had no intention of complying, and therefore constituted a tort; accordingly, the Defendant was liable to compensate the damages incurred by the Plaintiff from 1995. 1. 3. until 1998. 4. 30., when the Plaintiff received from the Defendant a notice to the effect that “the Plaintiff’s fishing right is valid and the fish farm facility construction may be resumed in the future, but compensation for the fishing right and facilities cannot be paid,” in that the Plaintiff was in fact unable to exercise the fishing right. The court below further held that, since the Defendant caused, in substance, the same result as a suspension of the fishing right by having the Plaintiff cease the aquaculture facility construction and thereby preventing the Plaintiff from engaging in fishing without taking any measure such as revoking or restricting the Plaintiff’s fishing license, damages should ultimately be calculated by analogical application of the provisions relating to the amount of compensation in cases where a fishing right is suspended.\\n\\nIn light of the record, the foregoing factual findings and determination by the court below are all correct and persuasive, and there is no error such as a misconception of the legal principles concerning compensation for loss arising from the suspension of fishing rights prescribed by the Fisheries Act and related statutes, or concerning the commencement point for calculation of the amount of damages and the calculation of the period of suspension of the fishing right, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nAnd if the Defendant’s administrative guidance before 1995. 1. 3. was a non-coercive, non-power exercise that did not depart from the limits of administrative guidance, then even if the Plaintiff thereby suffered some damage, the Defendant would not be liable for damages therefor; furthermore, since from 1998. 4. 30., when the Defendant notified the Plaintiff to the effect that the Plaintiff could resume the fish farm facility construction, there can be no said to have been any obstacle to the Plaintiff’s exercise of the fishing right, and thus it cannot be deemed that the Plaintiff thereafter suffered damages from inability to exercise the fishing right, the arguments in each ground of appeal on this point are without merit.\\n\\nThe Supreme Court Decision 98DA3498, 98DA3504 rendered on 1998. 9. 22. cited in the grounds for appeal concerns a different matter and is not appropriate to invoke in this case.\\n\\n2. With respect to the second ground of appeal by the Defendant\\nFor the offsetting of gains and losses to be allowed in calculating the amount of damages, not only must the injured party have obtained a new benefit as a result of the act giving rise to liability for damages, but that benefit must correspond to the scope of the damage to be compensated by the party obliged to compensate (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DA3229 rendered on 2007. 11. 16.). Even if the Plaintiff sold the fish-farming right at issue to a third party and thereby obtained a benefit equivalent to the sale price, such benefit cannot be deemed to be in a proximate causal relationship with the act giving rise to liability for damages in this case, namely, the Defendant’s unlawful administrative guidance, and, while the damages to be compensated by the Defendant are those arising from the Plaintiff’s inability to exercise the fishing right for a certain period due to the unlawful administrative guidance, the benefit obtained by the Plaintiff is the sale price of the fishing right itself, so it cannot be said that such benefit corresponds to the scope of the above damages.\\n\\nOn the same reasoning, the court below’s measure of not deducting from the amount of damages to be compensated by the Defendant the benefit equivalent to the sale price obtained by the Plaintiff is correct, and there is no error such as a misconception of the legal principles concerning the offsetting of gains and losses or the calculation of the amount of damages, as alleged in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n3. With respect to the second ground of appeal by the Plaintiff’s Successor Intervenor\\nIn light of the record, the court below’s calculation of the amount of damages in this case by determining the Plaintiff’s ordinary annual income, pursuant to Article 62(10) of the former Enforcement Decree of the Fisheries Act (before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 15241 of 1996. 12. 31.), as 50% of the fishing performance of the same-type fishery in the nearby area, was correct and persuasive, and there is no error such as a misconception of the legal principles concerning the standard for calculating the amount of damages, as alleged in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nThe argument in the grounds for appeal is that, because in cases where a fishing right is suspended compensation for loss is to be based on the date of the disposition that gives rise to compensation, the Plaintiff’s amount of damages should be calculated by applying the amended Enforcement Decree (amended by Presidential Decree No. 15241 of 1996. 12. 31.) in force at the time when the Defendant obtained approval for the implementation plan for the public waters reclamation project on 1997. 2. 28., or, since the Fisheries Act Enforcement Decree was amended on 1996. 12. 31., during the period in which the Plaintiff was unable to exercise the fishing right, the amount of fishing losses incurred after the amended Enforcement Decree entered into force should be calculated by applying the amended Enforcement Decree. However, according to the facts lawfully determined by the court below, the Defendant did not actually carry out the public waters reclamation project, so the public waters reclamation project cannot be said to have caused the damages in this case, and thus it cannot be deemed that the amount of damages must be calculated in accordance with the Enforcement Decree in force at the time of approval of the implementation plan. Moreover, in light of Addenda Article 11(2) of the amended Enforcement Decree, which provides that “as for the calculation of losses arising from restrictions, suspension, revocation, etc. of fishing licenses, fishing permits, notified fishing, etc., or from a vessel mooring disposition, under the former provisions as of the time this Decree enters into force, the former provisions shall apply,” it cannot be said that, with respect to fishing damages occurring during the period after the amended Enforcement Decree entered into force, the amount of damages must necessarily be calculated in accordance with the method for calculating fishing losses prescribed in the amended Enforcement Decree; therefore, the foregoing ground of appeal is without merit.\\n\\n4. With respect to the third ground of appeal by the Plaintiff’s Successor Intervenor\\nWhere there are several different appraisal results concerning the same matter, if facts are found on the basis of one of them, it is lawful so long as it does not violate the rules of experience or the rules of logic (see Supreme Court Decisions 2004DA4942 rendered on 2005. 8. 19., 2001DA81320 rendered on 2005. 1. 14., 82NU289 rendered on 1983. 7. 26., etc.).\\n\\nThe court below adopted the appellate appraiser’s appraisal result and rejected the first-instance appraiser’s appraisal result among the appraisal results concerning the Plaintiff’s fishing losses; in light of the record, the appellate appraiser’s exclusion of the reservoir area from the aquaculture-possible area in evaluating the Plaintiff’s fishing losses, the calculation of the average annual sales price by averaging the average annual sales price of mullet in Gyeonggi-do and the average annual sales price of mullet of the Seoul Metropolitan Government Agricultural and Marine Products Corporation, and the calculation of ordinary annual fishing expenses at 52,300,000 won cannot be deemed arbitrary evaluations without any basis or evaluations contrary to the rules of experience and logic. Therefore, the court below’s measure of adopting the above appraisal cannot be deemed to violate the rules of experience or logic, and the argument in this part of the ground for appeal is without merit in the end.\\n\\n5. With respect to the fourth ground of appeal by the Plaintiff’s Successor Intervenor\\nAcknowledgment of debt as a ground for interruption of the statute of limitations is established when the debtor, who is the party entitled to the benefit of the statute of limitations, manifests that he or she recognizes the existence of the right against the person who would lose the right upon completion of the statute of limitations; no particular form is required for such manifestation, and although the manifestation need not necessarily be express and may also be made implicitly, such implied manifestation of acknowledgment must be made in a manner by which, on the premise that the debtor is aware of the existence and amount of the debt, the other party receiving the manifestation can infer through it that the debtor recognizes the debt (see Supreme Court Decisions 2005DA64552 rendered on 2007. 11. 29., 2006DA22852, 22869 rendered on 2006. 9. 22., etc.).\\n\\nThe court below held that the part of the damages claim arising from the infringement of the fishing right in this case that accrued up to 1995. 3. 1., which is five years retroactively from 2000. 3. 2., the date of filing of this action, had been extinguished by the statute of limitations, and then, with respect to the Plaintiff’s Successor Intervenor’s argument that since the Defendant had acknowledged the above damages debt until 1998. 4. 6., the statute of limitations began to run from 1998. 4. 6., rejected the same on the ground that the reason the Defendant sent to the Plaintiff the official letters on 1998. 3. 20. and 1998. 4. 6. stating, in substance, that “the matter of compensation for the Plaintiff’s fishing right and facilities must be handled through consultation with the relevant departments, inquiries to higher authorities, and materials from specialized institutions, so please understand that the processing period is delayed” did not suffice to show that the Defendant had acknowledged its own debt. The above official letters sent by the Defendant to the Plaintiff were prepared before the basic plan for the public waters reclamation project was changed as of 1998. 4. 29., and before the Plaintiff’s fishing-license area was excluded from the public waters reclamation site; their content merely notified the future processing plan and the status of processing delay concerning compensation for the resulting loss on the premise that the public waters reclamation project at issue would be implemented, and cannot be deemed to express an intention to bear liability for the damages in this case arising from the administrative guidance given on 1995. 1. 3. Therefore, the court below’s above determination accords with the legal principle stated above and is correct, and there is no error such as a misconception of the legal principles concerning the statute of limitations, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the exercise by a debtor of the defense based on the expiration of the statute of limitations is also governed by the general principles of good faith and the prohibition of abuse of rights, which are the fundamental principles of our Civil Act; thus, if the debtor, before completion of the statute of limitations, made it impossible or extremely difficult for the creditor to exercise the right or interrupt the statute of limitations, or acted in a manner inducing the creditor to believe that such measures were unnecessary, or if there existed objective grounds that made it impossible for the creditor to exercise the right, or if, once the statute had been completed, the debtor acted in a manner appearing not to invoke the statute of limitations and thereby caused the right holder to rely on that appearance, or if there are special circumstances such that there is a strong need to protect the creditor and other creditors under the same conditions are receiving performance of the debt, making it manifestly unjust or inequitable to recognize the refusal to perform the obligation, then the debtor’s assertion of the completion of the statute of limitations is contrary to the principle of good faith and may not be allowed as an abuse of rights (see Supreme Court Decision 2006DA43651 rendered on 2007. 7. 26., etc.), as argued in the grounds for appeal. However, on the basis of the circumstances cited by the Plaintiff’s Successor Intervenor alone, it cannot be said that the Defendant, before the statute of limitations was completed, acted in a manner inducing the Plaintiff to believe that measures to exercise the damages claim or interrupt the statute of limitations were unnecessary, or that, after completion of the statute of limitations, it acted in a manner appearing not to invoke the statute of limitations; therefore, the Defendant’s assertion of the completion of the statute of limitations cannot be said to violate the principle of good faith or the prohibition of abuse of rights, and the argument in the grounds for appeal on this point is also without merit.\\n\\n6. Conclusion\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by each party; it is so adjudged, in unanimous opinion of the Justices involved, as stated in the Disposition."}

{"[2009HEONMA330]": "1. Overview of the Case and Subject Matter of Adjudication\\na. Overview of the Case\\n(1) The Complainants are workers employed at public institutions (members of labor unions of public institutions), labor unions of public institutions, or their branches.\\n(2) The Respondent, the Minister of Strategy and Finance (hereinafter referred to as the “Minister of Strategy and Finance”), has the authority, pursuant to the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, to designate public institutions, and, upon deliberation and resolution by the Steering Committee for the Management of Public Institutions, to formulate plans concerning functional reorganization, etc., of public institutions, and to evaluate and supervise them.\\n(3) As the Government around 2008 presented the goals of “regulatory reform, advancement of the public sector, and proactive openness,” the Ministry of Strategy and Finance became the competent ministry and decided to promote a plan for the advancement of public institutions, and the Minister of Strategy and Finance announced, in six rounds from 2008. 8. 11. to 2009. 3. 31., a plan for promoting the advancement of public institutions, the gist of which is as shown in the table below, for privatization, consolidation, functional reorganization, etc., of public institutions (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Advancement Plan at Issue,” and each round individually referred to as the “First Plan,” etc.).\\n<TABLE0>\\n<TABLE1>\\n<TABLE2>\\n(4) Meanwhile, while the “Standards for Integrated Disclosure by Public Institutions,” enacted on 2007. 4. 25., were revised four times until 2009. 3. 31., matters concerning labor unions (the scope of union membership, the union membership rate, the number of full-time union officers, the upper-level union, collective agreements, etc.) were added to the matters to be disclosed by public institutions, and the average remuneration of employees, the starting salary of new recruits, etc. became subject to disclosure.\\n(5) The Ministry of Strategy and Finance held the 2nd Workshop on the Advancement of Public Institutions on 2009. 5. 19., and discussed the achievements and case presentations concerning the promotion of the advancement of public institutions to date, policy directions, and future tasks, and the Minister of Strategy and Finance stated, in the opening remarks at that workshop, his intention to continue promoting the Advancement Plan at Issue.\\n(6) The Respondent, the Minister of Labor (hereinafter referred to as the “Minister of Labor”), around 2009. 4., analyzed the contents of collective agreements of 7 public institutions among 11 institutions classified as public institutions under the Ministry of Labor, including the Workers’ Compensation and Welfare Service, which had established labor unions and concluded collective agreements (Title: Analysis of Collective Agreements of Public Institutions under the Ministry of Labor and Improvement Measures), and sent the results of the analysis of the collective agreements to the relevant public institutions around 2009. 5. 1., together with the statement, “Each institution is requested to improve unreasonable elements as soon as possible through autonomous consultation between labor and management within the bounds of law and principle” (hereinafter referred to as the “Improvement Demand at Issue”).\\nThe matters pointed out by the Minister of Labor as unreasonable cases for each of the above public institutions were those that excessively guaranteed union membership and union activities, such as guaranteeing union activities during working hours and giving preferential personnel treatment to full-time union officers; excessive participation by unions in management; excessive scope and period of recognition for leave for congratulatory and condolence occasions; and failure to specify the subjects of collective bargaining.\\n(7) The Respondent, the Chairman of the Board of Audit and Inspection (hereinafter referred to as the “Chairman of the Board of Audit and Inspection”), under the purpose of “ending reckless management of public institutions under the guise of labor-management agreement and advancing labor-management relations,” inspected, from around 2009. 4., 60 public institutions through on-site inspection and document inspection with respect to the implementation status of the advancement plan, the promotion status of advancement of labor-management relations, labor costs, welfare benefits, etc., and, on 2009. 6. 30., at the meeting of audit managers of public institutions, presented an improvement direction to allow autonomous correction according to the type of problem (hereinafter referred to as the “Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue”).\\n(8) The Complainants’ constitutional complaint applications\\n(a) Case 2009HEONMA330\\nThe Complainants filed a constitutional complaint adjudication on 2009. 6. 17., alleging that the Advancement Plan at Issue infringes their fundamental rights, such as the right to equality, the right to human dignity and the pursuit of happiness, the freedom of occupation choice, the right of association, and the right to collective bargaining.\\n(b) Case 2009HEONMA344\\nThe Complainants filed a constitutional complaint adjudication on 2009. 6. 26., alleging that the Advancement Plan at Issue, the Improvement Demand at Issue, and the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue infringe their right of association, right to collective bargaining, right to conclude collective agreements, property rights, freedom of occupation choice, right to equality, the dignity and value of human beings and the right to pursue happiness, and the right to work.\\nb. Subject Matter of Adjudication\\nThe subject matter of adjudication in this case is whether the following acts infringe the Complainants’ fundamental rights, and the contents of the relevant provisions are as follows.\\n[Subject Matter of Adjudication]\\n(1) The act by which the Minister of Strategy and Finance finalized and announced the plan for promoting the advancement of public institutions in six rounds between 2008. 8. 11. and 2009. 3. 31. (the “Advancement Plan at Issue”)\\n(2) The act by which the Minister of Labor analyzed the contents of collective agreements of 7 public institutions under the Ministry of Labor in 2009. 4. and demanded around 2009. 5. 1. that unreasonable elements be improved (the “Improvement Demand at Issue”)\\n(3) The act by which the Chairman of the Board of Audit and Inspection inspected, around 2009. 4., the implementation status of the advancement plan for public institutions, the promotion status of advancement of labor-management relations, etc., with respect to 60 public institutions, and, on 2009. 6. 30., presented an improvement direction to allow autonomous correction at the meeting of audit managers of public institutions (the “Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue”)\\n[Relevant Provisions]\\nArticle 14 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (Functional Reorganization, etc. for Public Institutions)\\n(1) The Minister of Strategy and Finance shall, after consulting with the heads of competent institutions and after deliberation and resolution by the Steering Committee, inspect the appropriateness of the functions performed by public institutions and formulate a plan concerning consolidation of institutions, functional readjustment, privatization, etc.\\n(2) The head of the competent institution shall execute the plan formulated pursuant to paragraph (1) and submit a report on its performance to the Minister of Strategy and Finance.\\n(3) The Minister of Strategy and Finance may, by analyzing the contents of the report submitted pursuant to paragraph (2), confirm and inspect the implementation status, and, when necessary, request the head of the competent institution to take necessary measures for the smooth execution of the plan, upon deliberation and resolution by the Steering Committee.\\n(4) Necessary matters concerning the formulation and execution of the plan pursuant to paragraphs (1) through (3)\\nshall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.\\n2. Summary of the Complainants’ Arguments\\n(1) Concerning the Advancement Plan at Issue (2009HEONMA330, 2009HEONMA344)\\nThe Advancement Plan at Issue directly affects the fundamental rights of the people, and it may be expected that it will be implemented as is in the future with the support of statutes and regulations; and because there is no reasonable possibility of obtaining relief through other remedies such as administrative litigation against the measures such as workforce adjustments and wage reductions thereunder that infringe the Complainants’ freedom of occupation choice and the activities of labor unions, the Advancement Plan at Issue is subject to constitutional complaint adjudication.\\nThe Advancement Plan at Issue effects restructuring, job deprivation, and downward adjustment of working conditions such as wages on the ground that the workplaces where the Complainants work are public institutions; as such, by treating the Complainants working at public institutions unfavorably compared to workers at other workplaces, it infringes the right to equality, and by lowering working conditions, it infringes property rights, and by violating labor law principles and causing the loss of jobs, it infringes the freedom of occupation choice and the right to work.\\nIn addition, because the Advancement Plan at Issue places workers employed at public institutions in a position where they may be arbitrarily dismissed pursuant to government policy without their own attributable reasons or justifiable grounds, it infringes human dignity and the right to pursue happiness; and because, in formulating and promoting the Advancement Plan at Issue, it does not reflect the opinions of each labor union of the public institutions and does not consult on equal terms, but instead proceeds merely by resolutions of the board of directors of each institution, it infringes the three labor rights of workers at public institutions.\\nFurthermore, the Advancement Plan at Issue limits fundamental rights that may be restricted only by statute through a plan that is not a statute, and violates the principle of prohibition of excessive restriction and infringes the essential content of fundamental rights.\\n(2) Concerning the Improvement Demand at Issue and the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue (2009HEONMA344)\\nThe Improvement Demand at Issue and the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue, as concrete methods of implementation of the Advancement Plan at Issue, infringe the Complainants’ three labor rights, including the right of association, the right to collective bargaining, and the right to conclude collective agreements, as well as the right to equality, and the dignity and value as human beings and the right to pursue happiness.\\n3. Judgment on the Procedural Requirements\\na. Judgment on the Advancement Plan at Issue (2009HEONMA330, 2009HEONMA344)\\n(1) Overview of the Advancement Plan at Issue\\nThe Advancement Plan at Issue was formulated in six rounds from the First Plan to the Sixth Plan, and each plan differs slightly as to the relevant public institutions and contents, but has as its main contents the privatization, consolidation,\\nfunctional reorganization, and management efficiency of public institutions; and, if classified according to its contents, the First through Third Plans mainly concern the privatization, consolidation, and functional reorganization of public institutions, the Fourth and Sixth Plans concern management efficiency, and the Fifth Plan mainly concerns the sale of shares in 132 government-invested institutions.\\nLooking at the general process of the Advancement Plan at Issue, each government ministry prepares measures and deliberates on them at the Advancement Promotion Committee; opinion-gathering procedures such as public hearings are conducted under the supervision of the competent ministry; after comprehensive coordination by the Advancement Promotion Committee, the final plan is confirmed through deliberation and resolution by the Steering Committee for the Management of Public Institutions; the finally confirmed Advancement Plan is promoted by forming the Advisory Group for Promotion of Advancement of Public Enterprises and the Advancement Promotion Task Force for each ministry; and, where the enactment or amendment of statutes is required, related bills are submitted to the National Assembly and final execution is carried out pursuant to the statutes passed.\\n(2) Whether the Advancement Plan at Issue constitutes an exercise of public power\\n(a) The Advancement Plan at Issue is a policy plan that declares the basic policy of the State regarding the operation of public institutions through privatization, consolidation, functional reorganization, etc. of public institutions, and its legal nature shall be that of an administrative plan. However, whether an administrative plan constitutes an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication cannot be uniformly stated, and must be judged individually in consideration of the specific nature of the administrative plan. An administrative plan having binding force upon the people may be regarded as an exercise of public power, but an administrative plan that lacks binding force and is merely a de facto preparatory act, prior notice, or an internal guideline of an administrative agency cannot, in principle, be regarded as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication. However, even a non-binding administrative plan draft or administrative guideline shall be subject to constitutional complaint adjudication exceptionally as an act of public power when it directly affects the fundamental rights of the people and may be expected with certainty to be implemented as is in the future with the support of statutes and regulations (see Constitutional Court 2000. 6. 1. 99HEONMA538, Collection of Cases 12-1, 665, 680-682).\\nTherefore, we examine whether the contents of the Advancement Plan at Issue directly affect the fundamental rights of the people and whether it is expected with certainty that it will be implemented as is in the future with the support of statutes and regulations.\\n(b) The First through Third Plans concern privatization and consolidation of public institutions, etc.; in order for such privatization and consolidation of public institutions, etc. to be concretely realized, actual promotional acts by the Advisory Group for Promotion of Advancement of Public Enterprises and the Advancement Promotion Task Force for each ministry, and submission to the National Assembly and resolutions of related bills, are necessary, and in the course of such concrete realization there also exists the possibility that the original contents of the advancement plan may not be realized as is and that the contents may change.\\nIf so, the First through Third Plans cannot be regarded as directly affecting the fundamental rights of the people by themselves, and it is also difficult to view them as being expected with certainty to be implemented as is in the future with the support of statutes and regulations; therefore, they cannot be said to constitute an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication.\\n(c) The Fourth and Sixth Plans mainly contain matters such as wage reductions and workforce reductions; if divided again, they include matters concerning the working conditions of annual salary systems, etc. and collective labor-management relations, as well as matters concerning management decisions of the management entity related to the implementation of corporate restructuring such as the consolidation or merger of business organizations.\\nFirst, as to matters concerning the working conditions of workers such as annual salary systems and other matters concerning the operation of collective labor-management relations, such contents may be regarded as nothing more than the Government, which may be said to be the employer side of public institutions, presenting standards as a de facto preparatory act, prior notice, or internal guideline of an administrative agency, and, unless it directly intervenes in or compels collective bargaining, even if it indirectly affects the labor unions of public institutions, it is difficult to regard that alone as a direct exercise of public power.\\nNext, as to matters concerning layoffs for managerial reasons, the consolidation of departments and organizations, and the implementation of restructuring, it merely presents the overall direction of workforce reduction, etc., and does not target specific persons in any particular department; moreover, in order for the contents of the above plan to be actually executed, there must be an act of execution by the head of the relevant public institution upon a resolution of the board of directors, etc. of the relevant public institution, and thus it is also difficult to regard the above plan as something that will certainly be executed. Therefore, the above plan cannot be regarded as an exercise of public power, but shall be viewed as merely presenting standards as a de facto preparatory act, prior notice, or an internal guideline of an administrative agency.\\nIf so, the Fourth and Sixth Plans also cannot be regarded as constituting a direct exercise of public power.\\n(d) The Fifth Plan is a plan concerning the restructuring of government-invested companies, and contains the contents that 131 invested companies are to be liquidated, such as by selling their held shares, and 142 invested companies are to be retained but management strengthened through institutional improvements; since it is difficult to regard the contents, such as selling shares held in companies that are not public institutions, as directly affecting the fundamental rights of the people, this also cannot be regarded as an\\nexercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication.\\n(e) Ultimately, the Advancement Plan at Issue cannot be said to constitute an exercise of public power as the subject matter of constitutional complaint adjudication; therefore, the petition for adjudication concerning the Advancement Plan at Issue is unlawful.\\nb. Concerning the Improvement Demand at Issue (2009HEONMA344)\\n(1) Legal nature of the Improvement Demand at Issue\\nArticle 2, item 3, of the Administrative Procedures Act provides that “administrative guidance” means administrative action by which an administrative agency, within the scope of its jurisdiction, guides, recommends, or advises a specific person to do or not do a certain act in order to realize a certain administrative purpose.\\nThe Improvement Demand at Issue is not, by itself, intended to produce a certain legal effect, but seeks to produce de facto effects through the voluntary cooperation of the heads of the relevant public institutions by having the Labor Ministry, within the scope of its jurisdiction, request improvements concerning collective agreements from the relevant public institutions in order to realize the Advancement Plan at Issue; therefore, its legal nature shall correspond to administrative guidance.\\nThe Constitutional Court has stated that where noncompliance with administrative guidance is accompanied by the anticipation of certain adverse measures, thus effectively imposing upon the other party a duty to comply therewith, and thereby it goes beyond the limits of simple administrative guidance and acquires a considerably strong regulatory and binding character, it may be regarded as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication (see Constitutional Court 2003. 6. 26. 2002HEONMA337, Collection of Cases 15-1, 772).\\n(2) Whether the Improvement Demand at Issue constitutes an exercise of public power\\nAs seen above, the Improvement Demand at Issue consists of a portion stating the results of the analysis of the contents of the collective agreement and a portion stating that it wishes unreasonable elements to be improved through autonomous consultation.\\nHowever, although there is a statement that the standards for analyzing collective agreements, etc. are to be used as criteria for evaluating the management performance of public institutions and evaluating the heads of institutions, it is difficult to view such mere use as evaluation criteria as expressly anticipating disadvantages in the event of noncompliance with the Improvement Demand at Issue; otherwise, there is no content directly intervening in or compelling collective bargaining, and in the directive for implementation of the improvement demand, only general and abstract expressions such as “within the bounds of law and principle” are used.\\nIf so, since it is difficult to view the Improvement Demand at Issue as going beyond the limits of administrative guidance and as having a strong regulatory and binding character, it cannot be regarded as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication, and thus the petition for adjudication concerning the Improvement Demand at Issue is\\nunlawful.\\nc. Concerning the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue (2009HEONMA344)\\n(1) Legal nature of the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue\\nThe Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue is not, by itself, intended to produce a certain legal effect, but is a collection of materials and a presentation of an improvement direction by the Chairman of the Board of Audit and Inspection, within the scope of his jurisdiction, to inspect the implementation status of the Advancement Plan at Issue in the relevant public institutions in order to realize the Advancement Plan at Issue; therefore, its legal nature shall correspond to administrative guidance.\\n(2) Whether the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue constitutes an exercise of public power\\nAmong the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue, the inspection act shall be regarded as nothing more than the collection of materials within the Board of Audit and Inspection; therefore, it is difficult to regard it as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication.\\nAmong the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue, the improvement presentation stated, to the audit managers of the 60 public institutions inspected, the types of problems without specifically naming the public institutions, and presented an improvement direction for autonomous correction, while also stating future handling guidelines to continuously retain and manage the data from the inspection results as audit materials and to use them as checklists during audits; based on such contents alone, it is difficult to view it as expressly anticipating disadvantages in the event of noncompliance with the above improvement presentation, and therefore the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue cannot be regarded as having a strong regulatory and binding character beyond the limits of administrative guidance.\\nIf so, the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue cannot be regarded as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication, and thus the petition for adjudication concerning the Inspection and Improvement Presentation at Issue is also unlawful.\\n4. Conclusion\\nTherefore, since the Complainants’ petition for adjudication in this case is unlawful, it is all dismissed, and a decision as set forth in the Disposition is rendered by unanimous opinion of all Justices participating."}

{"[2019HEONMA1399]": "1. Outline of the Case\\n\\na. On 2019. 12. 16., the Government, jointly with the relevant ministries and agencies (Ministry of Economy and Finance, Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Financial Services Commission, National Tax Service), announced the “Housing Market Stabilization Measures.” The Government diagnosed the then-current housing market trends as “a resurgence of localized overheating in some areas including Seoul, expanded buying demand due to expectations of rising house prices, inflow of speculative demand such as gap investment, and sufficient supply in response to actual demand,” and then concluded that, because there was concern that opportunities for actual homebuyers to acquire their own homes would decrease due to some speculative demand, measures to prevent market disruption and manage supply and demand stably were necessary. In particular, it determined that stronger regulation of speculative lending demand was necessary in order to block speculative demand and guide the market toward actual demand, and announced the following 6 measures to “strengthen management of housing mortgage loans in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts.”\\n<TABLE0>\\n\\nb. Until the above announcement, in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts, a loan prohibition was applied to “multi-homehouseholds,” and the LTV 40% regulation was applied to “one-home households and households without homes,” but item ② of the above “Housing Market Stabilization Measures” prohibited, from 2019. 12. 17., the day after the above announcement, for “all borrowers,” including households, individual business owners, and corporations, home-purchase mortgage loans secured by ultra-high-priced apartments in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion).\\n\\nc. The Financial Services Commission, the competent authority for item ② of the above “Housing Market Stabilization Measures,” sent, on the same day as the above announcement, an official notice titled “Implementation of Financial Administrative Guidance on Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans” to financial institutions subject to the relevant regulations, including the Korea Federation of Banks, informing them that where either the market price quoted by KB Kookmin Bank or the market price quoted by the Korea Real Estate Board exceeds KRW 1.5 billion, housing mortgage loans cannot be handled, that this applies to new loan applications submitted on or after 2019. 12. 17., and that it remains effective until the relevant amended regulations come into force (with a plan to complete the regulation amendment procedure as soon as possible).\\n\\nd. The Petitioner is a person who holds one apartment with a market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion in a speculative area and overheated speculation district and seeks to obtain a new housing mortgage loan secured by that apartment for the purpose of purchasing an apartment anew, and on 2019. 12. 17. filed a constitutional complaint seeking a determination that the above measure was unconstitutional, asserting that the Petitioner’s fundamental rights were infringed by item ② of the above “Housing Market Stabilization Measures.”\\n\\n2. Subject Matter of Adjudication\\n\\na. The announcement of the “Housing Market Stabilization Measures” on 2019. 12. 16. was made jointly by the relevant ministries and agencies (Minister of Economy and Finance, Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission, Commissioner of the National Tax Service), and in response to the Petitioner’s request for adjudication in this case, “the Minister of Economy and Finance, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission, and the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service” jointly submitted an answer brief and a power of attorney for litigation on 2021. 1. 29. as Respondents; therefore, the identification of the Respondent is at issue.\\n\\nUpon review, among the various “Housing Market Stabilization Measures” announced jointly by the relevant ministries and agencies on 2019. 12. 16., the part the Petitioner specifically takes issue with is the measure prohibiting “home-purchase mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion) in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts.” Namely, ㉠ according to the Ministry of Economy and Finance’s “Press Release on Housing Market Stabilization Measures” dated 2019. 12. 16. and its “Attachment: Housing Market Stabilization Measures,” the competent authority for the relevant measure is listed as the “Financial Services Commission”; ㉡ according to the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission’s official notice dated 2019. 12. 16. titled “Implementation of Financial Administrative Guidance on Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans,” the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission sent an official notice informing the “Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service, the Chairperson of the Korea Federation of Banks, the Chairperson of the Life Insurance Association of Korea, the Chairperson of the Korea General Insurance Association, the Chairperson of the Korea Federation of Savings Banks, the Chairperson of the Credit Finance Association of Korea, the President of Korea Development Bank, the President of Industrial Bank of Korea, the President of the Export-Import Bank of Korea, the Chairperson of National Agricultural Cooperative Federation, the Chairperson of National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives, the Chairperson of National Credit Union Federation of Korea, the Chairperson of Korea Forestry Cooperative Federation, and financial institutions subject to the relevant regulations” of the implementation of the relevant measure; ㉢ according to the Financial Services Commission’s “Press Reference on the Holding of a Financial Sector Meeting Regarding Housing Market Stabilization Measures” dated 2019. 12. 16. and its attachment “Opening Remarks by the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission,” it is confirmed that the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission held a financial sector meeting for implementation of the relevant measure at 15:00 on the same day. Taking these circumstances together, it is proper to identify the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission as the Respondent in this adjudication request.\\n\\nb. The competent department for item ② of the “Housing Market Stabilization Measures” announced on 2019. 12. 16. is the Financial Services Commission. The Act on the Establishment, etc. of the Financial Services Commission (hereinafter referred to as the “Financial Services Commission Act”) provides that “The Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service shall endeavor to maintain fairness and ensure transparency in performing their duties and not to impair the autonomy of financial institutions” (Article 2), and provides that matters within the jurisdiction of the Financial Services Commission include “supervision and inspection and sanctions (制裁) concerning financial institutions,” while, as institutions subject to inspection by the Financial Supervisory Service, it provides “banks established with authorization under the Banking Act, insurance companies under the Insurance Business Act, mutual savings banks and their central association under the Mutual Savings Banks Act, credit cooperatives and their central association under the Credit Cooperatives Act, specialized credit finance companies and concurrent credit finance businesses under the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act,” etc. (Article 38). Considering that in the official notice concerning the above measure the Respondent listed “Banking Supervision Regulations, Insurance Business Supervision Regulations, Mutual Savings Bank Business Supervision Regulations, Mutual Finance Business Supervision Regulations, Specialized Credit Finance Business Supervision Regulations” as the “relevant laws and regulations,” at least “banks, insurance companies, mutual savings banks, credit cooperatives, and specialized credit finance companies” would fall under the direct counterparts of the relevant measure contemplated by the Respondent.\\n\\nHowever, the Petitioner sought to obtain a housing mortgage loan from a bank among the above direct counterparts, but was unable to receive the mortgage loan due to item ② of the above “Housing Market Stabilization Measures” announced on 2019. 12. 16., and the Respondent also explains the legal basis primarily through the Banking Act, the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act, and the Banking Supervision Regulations; therefore, it is proper to limit the subject matter of adjudication in this case to the part relating to banks.\\n\\nc. Accordingly, the subject matter of adjudication in this case is whether, among item ② of the above “Housing Market Stabilization Measures,” the part concerning the banking business, namely, the measure by which the Respondent prohibited, from 2019. 12. 17., commercial banks from granting home-purchase mortgage loans secured by ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion) in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts (hereinafter referred to as “the Measure in this case”), infringes the Petitioner’s fundamental rights. The relevant provisions are as follows.\\n\\n[Relevant Provisions]\\n\\nBanking Act\\n(as amended by Act No. 10303 on 2010. 5. 17.)\\n\\nArticle 34 (Guidance on Sound Management)\\n(1) When operating banking business, a bank shall secure sound management by faithfully maintaining its capital and appropriate liquidity.\\n(2) In order to maintain sound management, a bank shall comply with management guidance standards determined by the Financial Services Commission pursuant to what is prescribed by Presidential Decree concerning the following matters:\\n1. Matters concerning adequacy of capital\\n2. Matters concerning soundness of assets\\n3. Matters concerning liquidity\\n4. Other matters necessary to secure sound management\\n\\nEnforcement Decree of the Banking Act\\n(as amended by Presidential Decree No. 23427 on 2011. 12. 28.)\\n\\nArticle 20 (Management Guidance Standards, etc.)\\n(1) The management guidance standards under Article 34(2) of the Act shall include the following matters:\\n1. Matters concerning standards for holding capital corresponding to credit risk of a bank, such as the capital adequacy ratio for risk-weighted assets under the standards of the Bank for International Settlements\\n2. Matters concerning standards for classifying the soundness of assets held by a bank, such as loan claims\\n3. Matters concerning standards for managing credit extension to persons whom the Financial Services Commission deems necessary to manage credit extension in an integrated manner and designates and publicly notifies\\n4. Matters concerning standards for holding liquid assets against liquid liabilities\\n5. Other matters publicly notified by the Financial Services Commission for securing sound management of a bank\\n(3) Requests for submission of plans or agreements, procedures and methods for concluding agreements, and other necessary matters under paragraph (2) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Financial Services Commission.\\n\\nBanking Supervision Regulations\\n(Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2019-52 on 2019. 11. 20.)\\n\\nArticle 29-2 (Risk Management for Housing Mortgage Loans)\\n(1) When handling housing mortgage loans, a bank shall comply with the loan-to-value ratio, debt-to-income ratio, and other restrictions on handling housing mortgage loans and extending maturity prescribed in <APPENDIX_TABLE6> so that sound management is maintained pursuant to Article 34 of the Act.\\n(2) The Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service may, in cases deemed urgent in light of the soundness of a bank’s management, adjust upward or downward the loan-to-value ratio and debt-to-income ratio prescribed in <APPENDIX_TABLE6> within a range of 10 percentage points. In such case, the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service shall report the details to the Financial Services Commission without delay.\\n\\n<APPENDIX_TABLE6> Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans\\n(omitted)\\n\\nBanking Supervision Regulations\\n(Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2020-54 on 2020. 12. 3.)\\n\\n<APPENDIX_TABLE6> Risk Management Standards for Mortgage Loans Relating to Housing\\n\\nChapter 1 General Provisions\\n\\n1. (Definition of Terms) The definitions of the terms used in these standards are as follows:\\nBEO. “Ultra-high-priced apartment” means an apartment with a market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion.\\n\\nChapter 5 Restrictions and Matters of Note in Handling Mortgage Loans Relating to Housing\\n\\n8. (Restriction on Handling Mortgage Loans Relating to Housing for the Purpose of Purchasing an Ultra-High-Priced Apartment in a Speculative Area or Overheated Speculation District) A bank may not handle a housing mortgage loan (including a mortgage loan secured by housing-related beneficiary certificates) for the purpose of purchasing an ultra-high-priced apartment located in a speculative area or overheated speculation district. Provided, however, that the foregoing shall not apply if any of the following applies:\\na. Where debt is unavoidably assumed due to inheritance, participation in an auction for preservation of claims, or the like\\nb. Where there are unavoidable reasons, such as where a member of a reconstruction/redevelopment association, as a one-home household, has been confirmed to have resided there for at least 1 year until the approval for establishment of the association\\n\\nBanking Supervision Regulations\\n(Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2022-45 on 2022. 11. 23.)\\n\\n<APPENDIX_TABLE6> Risk Management Standards for Housing-Related Mortgage Loans, etc.\\n\\nChapter 5 Restrictions and Matters of Note in Handling Household Loans and Housing-Related Mortgage Loans\\n\\n8. <REDACTED>\\n\\nRegulations on the Operation of Financial Regulation\\n(Prime Ministerial Directive No. 812 on 2022. 4. 4.)\\n\\nArticle 2 (Definitions) The meanings of the terms used in these Directive shall be as follows:\\n4. “Financial administrative guidance” means an administrative act by which the Financial Services Commission or the Financial Supervisory Service, in order to achieve the purposes of financial administration such as securing the soundness of management of financial companies, etc. and protecting financial consumers, requests financial companies, etc., based on the voluntary cooperation of the financial companies, etc., to perform or refrain from certain acts (including acts in the form of provisions and acts in a general and abstract form). (Proviso omitted)\\n\\nArticle 7 (Principles of Financial Administrative Guidance)\\n(4) The Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service shall not take any adverse measures merely on the ground that the financial companies, etc. did not comply with the financial administrative guidance.\\n\\n3. The Petitioner’s Arguments\\n\\nThe Petitioner sought to obtain from a bank a new housing mortgage loan secured by an ultra-high-priced apartment with a market value of KRW 1.5 billion or more held in an overheated speculation district for the purpose of purchasing a new ultra-high-priced apartment, but the plan was thwarted by the Measure in this case. The act of a citizen providing property rights as security and borrowing money from a financial institution such as a bank is a representative form of exercising property rights, and restricting it is a restriction on property rights. However, the Measure in this case cannot be regarded as based on statute; therefore, it violates the principle of statutory reservation, which provides that fundamental rights may be restricted only by statute, and infringes the Petitioner’s property rights by violating the principle against excessive restriction.\\n\\n4. Determination on Procedural Requirements\\n\\na. Character as Exercise of Public Power\\n\\nArticle 68(1) of the Constitutional Court Act provides that a person whose fundamental rights are infringed by the exercise or non-exercise of public power may file a constitutional complaint. Here, “public power” refers to the sovereign acts of all state institutions and public bodies exercising legislative, executive, or judicial power (see Constitutional Court 2001. 3. 21. 99HEONMA139, etc.).\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 2 subparagraph 3 of the Administrative Procedures Act provides that “administrative guidance” means an administrative act by which an administrative agency, within the scope of its competent affairs, guides, recommends, or advises a specific person to perform or refrain from certain acts in order to realize a certain administrative objective. In addition, Article 48(2) of the same Act provides that “an administrative agency shall not take adverse measures on the ground that the other party to administrative guidance did not comply with the administrative guidance.” Such administrative guidance, as a rule, is a factual administrative act lacking external binding force and does not constitute a sovereign act. However, even if it is administrative guidance, where it has a regulatory character, such as having the effect of restricting the freedom or rights of the other party and exerting de facto coercive force on that other party, it is proper to regard it as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication (see Constitutional Court 2011. 12. 29. 2009HEONMA330, etc.).\\n\\nUpon review, according to the official notice titled “Implementation of Financial Administrative Guidance on Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans” sent by the Respondent to financial institutions including the Korea Federation of Banks on the day the Measure in this case was announced, the Measure in this case was implemented under the heading “financial administrative guidance,” and it contains a request for voluntary compliance before the completion of the amendment procedure, while announcing in advance that the risk management standards for housing mortgage loans would be amended within 1 year. In addition, the Measure in this case is accompanied by Article 7(4) of the Regulations on the Operation of Financial Regulation, which states that adverse measures shall not be taken merely on the ground that the financial companies, etc. did not comply with the financial administrative guidance. Therefore, both in form and content, the Measure in this case falls under the administrative guidance prescribed in Article 2 subparagraph 3 of the Administrative Procedures Act.\\n\\nHowever, on the other hand, because the Measure in this case, in certain cases, prohibits all banks from extending housing mortgage loans, it has a strong regulatory character with respect to the exercise of an individual’s property rights and freedom of contract with banks. In addition, in light of the fact that the Measure in this case was implemented in a situation where there was an urgent policy necessity to curb a surge in real estate prices, that it was scheduled to be amended shortly in the same content as the Measure in this case, and that field inspection teams were planned to be operated to confirm compliance with the Measure in this case and were in fact carried out, it appears that it would have been difficult for the banks, as counterparties, to expect not to comply with the Measure in this case; therefore, the Measure in this case is recognized as having exerted de facto coercive force on its counterparties. Accordingly, the Measure in this case, as administrative guidance with a regulatory and binding character, constitutes an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication.\\n\\nb. Interest in Adjudication\\n\\nIf, due to changes in factual relations or legal relations, etc., the ground for infringement of the fundamental rights asserted by the Petitioner has subsequently ceased, there is, in principle, no benefit in protecting rights because there is no practical interest in revoking the exercise of public power that caused the infringement. However, since constitutional complaint adjudication exists not only for the protection of citizens’ subjective fundamental rights but also for the protection and maintenance of the objective constitutional order, even if the ground for infringement of fundamental rights has already ceased and does not help the Petitioner’s subjective remedy, where a merits determination in the relevant case is an essential matter for the protection and maintenance of the constitutional order and the elucidation thereof has constitutionally important significance, or where there is a risk that such grounds for infringement may recur in the future, it is exceptionally necessary to recognize an interest in adjudication and determine whether it is unconstitutional (see Constitutional Court 1993. 7. 29. 89HEONMA31; Constitutional Court 1995. 7. 21. 92HEONMA144; Constitutional Court 2011. 12. 29. 2009HEONMA527, etc.).\\n\\nThe Petitioner filed this constitutional complaint seeking to nullify the effect of the “prohibition on home-purchase mortgage loans secured by ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion) in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts” through a determination of unconstitutionality regarding the Respondent’s Measure in this case. However, pursuant to the Respondent’s “Advance Notice of Rule Amendment regarding the Draft Amendment to the Banking Supervision Regulations” dated 2022. 11. 10. and the subsequent amendment of the “Banking Supervision Regulations” by Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2022-45 on 2022. 11. 23., from 2022. 12. 1. housing mortgage loans for the purchase of ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion) in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts became permissible for households without homes and one-home households (subject to disposal of the existing home); therefore, the Petitioner’s subjective interest in protection of rights concerning the Measure in this case has ceased. However, regulatory and binding financial administrative guidance such as the Measure in this case is likely to recur in the future. Moreover, this case concerns the constitutional limits on public power intervention in the guarantee of citizens’ property rights and freedom of contract with banks in the economic order of the Republic of Korea, which is based on respect for the economic freedom and creativity of individuals and enterprises (Article 119(1) of the Constitution). Accordingly, this case falls under a situation in which there is a risk that the same kind of infringement of fundamental rights may recur in the future, and the matter is essential for the protection and maintenance of the constitutional order, with the elucidation thereof having constitutionally important significance; therefore, an interest in adjudication is recognized.\\n\\n5. Merits\\n\\na. Issue in this Case\\n\\nThe Petitioner argues that, due to the Measure in this case, the Petitioner was unable to enter into a mortgage loan contract with a bank through the establishment (disposition) of a security right over existing real property already owned by the Petitioner, thereby restricting the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract; accordingly, the issue is whether the Measure in this case violates the principle of statutory reservation and the principle against excessive restriction, thereby infringing the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract.\\n\\nb. Whether the Principle of Statutory Reservation Was Violated\\n\\nFundamental rights may be restricted only when necessary for national security, maintenance of order, or public welfare pursuant to Article 37(2) of the Constitution, but the method of such restriction may, in principle, be only by statute, and the degree of restriction must not infringe the essential content of fundamental rights and must be limited to the minimum necessary. However, the principle of statutory reservation concerning the restriction of fundamental rights prescribed in the above provision does not call for “regulation by statute” but rather “regulation based on statute”; therefore, a statutory basis is required for the restriction of fundamental rights, but the form of the restriction of fundamental rights need not necessarily be the form of a statute. In addition, in determining whether a legal basis exists for the Measure in this case, the characteristics of the Measure in this case and the degree of restriction on fundamental rights resulting therefrom, as set out below, must be taken into account (see Constitutional Court 2005. 5. 26. 99HEONMA513, etc.).\\n\\nFirst, the Measure in this case prohibits housing mortgage loans in certain cases, and various regulations limiting or prohibiting the scope of housing mortgage loans have been continuously implemented through the Banking Supervision Regulations before and after the Measure in this case. When the Banking Supervision Regulations were amended by Financial Supervisory Commission Notice No. 2007-94 on 2007. 7. 26., Article 29-2(1) was newly established, providing that “when a financial institution handles housing mortgage loans, it shall comply with the loan-to-value ratio, debt-to-income ratio, and other restrictions on handling housing mortgage loans and extending maturity prescribed in <APPENDIX_TABLE6> so that sound management is maintained pursuant to Article 45 of the Act.” <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the above provision, under the heading “Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans,” details the specific contents of restrictions on housing mortgage loans.\\n\\nThe above <APPENDIX_TABLE6> has since been revised several times in step with changing policy needs. At the time the Measure in this case was implemented, too, Article 29-2(1) <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Banking Supervision Regulations (Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2019-52 on 2019. 11. 20.) contained detailed provisions on various forms of loan-handling restrictions, such as differently determining the permissible scope of mortgage loans according to regions such as speculative areas and overheated speculation districts (subparagraph 2(a), subparagraph 2-1(a), subparagraph 3, etc.), or prohibiting mortgage loans for specific persons or for specific purposes, such as households owning homes, minors, and the purpose of purchasing high-priced homes (subparagraph 2(e), (f), subparagraph 2-1(b), subparagraph 4, subparagraph 6, etc.). In particular, the Financial Services Commission amended <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Banking Supervision Regulations, “Risk Management Standards for Housing-Related Mortgage Loans,” by Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2020-54 on 2020. 12. 3., and prescribed a restriction on handling mortgage loans with the same content as the Measure in this case (main text of item 8).\\n\\nSecond, there is clear statutory basis for the regulation of housing mortgage loans to secure the soundness of bank management. Article 34 of the Banking Act grants the Financial Services Commission the authority to establish management guidance standards that banks must comply with. In addition, Article 20(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act provides that “matters concerning standards for managing credit extension” and “other matters publicly notified by the Financial Services Commission for securing sound management of a bank” must be included in the management guidance standards. Article 29-2(1) of the Banking Supervision Regulations explicitly states that Article 34 of the Banking Act is the delegated basis, and Article 29-2(1) <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Regulations was established based on the above delegation; therefore, it has a statutory basis.\\n\\nThird, according to the official notice titled “Implementation of Financial Administrative Guidance on Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans” sent by the Respondent to financial institutions including the Korea Federation of Banks on the day the Measure in this case was announced, the Measure in this case is administrative guidance that gives advance notice of the amendment of Article 29-2(1) <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Banking Supervision Regulations, an administrative rule then in force, and requests compliance with the contents to be amended for the time being until the amendment is made. According to the contents of the official notice, the effective period of the Measure in this case was set as “from 19. 12. 17. until the date on which the relevant amended regulations come into force (the effective period of administrative guidance is up to 1 year, but the plan is to complete the regulation amendment procedure as soon as possible).” In addition, the Financial Services Commission amended Article 29-2(1) <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Banking Supervision Regulations on 2020. 12. 3., less than 1 year after the implementation date of the Measure in this case, thereby codifying the Measure in this case exactly as announced.\\n\\nFourth, because the degree of binding force of the Measure in this case is not as great as the binding force of the Banking Supervision Regulations, the degree of restriction on the Petitioner’s fundamental rights by the Measure in this case is also less than the degree of restriction by the Banking Supervision Regulations. Of course, in light of the fact that social conditions were such that it was difficult for banks to expect not to comply with the Measure in this case, that field inspection teams were planned to be operated to confirm whether the Measure in this case was being implemented, and that field inspections were actually conducted, the Measure in this case has a binding character. However, the Measure in this case was issued in the form of administrative guidance, and pursuant to Article 7 of the Regulations on the Operation of Financial Regulation, it was explicitly notified that no adverse measures would be taken even if the Measure in this case was not complied with. Meanwhile, in the case of the Banking Supervision Regulations, if violated, pursuant to Article 34(4) of the Banking Act, the Financial Services Commission may request the bank that violated them to take measures necessary for management improvement, and in some cases may proceed to adverse measures such as corrective orders or partial suspension of business under Article 53 of the same Act. However, even if the Measure in this case is violated, the Financial Services Commission cannot take the above adverse measures on the ground of that violation; thus, the binding force of the Measure in this case is weaker than that of the Banking Supervision Regulations, and therefore the degree of restriction on fundamental rights resulting therefrom is also less.\\n\\nTaking the above circumstances together, namely that the Financial Services Commission has the authority at any time to amend <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Banking Supervision Regulations and impose regulations with the same content as the Measure in this case, that such authority has clear statutory grounds, that the content of the Measure in this case is to announce that the Financial Services Commission will exercise such authority to amend <APPENDIX_TABLE6> of the Banking Supervision Regulations and to request compliance even before the amended regulations take effect, and that the degree of restriction on fundamental rights resulting from the Measure in this case is less than the degree of restriction under the Banking Supervision Regulations, it is difficult to say that the degree of review regarding whether the legal basis required in relation to the Measure in this case is provided is very strong.\\n\\nUltimately, so long as the content of the Measure in this case, implemented through administrative guidance, does not go beyond the regulatory authority lawfully granted to the Financial Services Commission, it satisfies the principle of statutory reservation. Since the Measure in this case prohibits, in certain cases, housing mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced houses, and various regulations on the scope or permissibility of housing mortgage loans fall within the management guidance standards that the Financial Services Commission may establish pursuant to Article 34 of the Banking Act and Article 20(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act in order to secure the soundness of bank management, it satisfies the statutory reservation required for administrative guidance.\\n\\nAccordingly, the Measure in this case does not infringe the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract in violation of the principle of statutory reservation.\\n\\nc. Whether the Principle Against Excessive Restriction Was Violated\\n\\n(1) Legitimacy of Purpose and Appropriateness of Means\\n\\n(a) Housing is recognized as the foundation of our lives and at the same time one of the largest components of each household’s assets. The Government has implemented various policies for the stability of the people’s housing, and in particular has attempted various policies to prevent housing from becoming an object of speculation and prices rising excessively, making it difficult for citizens to acquire their own homes. Real estate, like ordinary goods, has its price and transaction volume determined by supply and demand in the market; however, due to the nature of real estate, supply is inelastic, so a sharp increase in demand causes a sharp increase in prices. Therefore, when increasing housing supply in the short term is difficult, demand suppression measures are necessary to stabilize housing prices. In addition, if speculative lending demand increases, then when there is an external shock such as a decline in housing prices, the extent of the decline in housing prices will expand, and eventually the possibility of recovering housing mortgage loans will be greatly reduced, undermining the soundness of financial institutions’ management.\\n\\nThe Measure in this case is intended to achieve overall housing market stabilization by suppressing the rise in housing prices through direct demand suppression, and at the same time to improve the excessive flow of funds into the real estate sector that has continued over time from the standpoint of managing the soundness of loans of banks, which are financial institutions; therefore, legitimacy of purpose is recognized.\\n\\n(b) In general, restrictions on housing mortgage loans suppress demand for housing purchases and can be seen as a policy tool for stabilizing the housing market, and prohibiting housing mortgage loans for apartments exceeding KRW 1.5 billion contributes to achieving the above purpose by suppressing demand for such ultra-high-priced housing. Therefore, the Measure in this case is also appropriate as a means.\\n\\n(2) Least Restrictive Means\\n\\n(a) At the time of the Measure in this case, housing prices in Seoul had been rising for 24 consecutive weeks starting from the first week of July 2019 (see Korea Real Estate Board, December 2019 National Housing Price Trend Survey Report), and the housing market was overheating as buying demand expanded due to expectations of house price increases and anxiety about price rises. Since housing transactions are large in scale and it is difficult to pay the transaction price only with one’s own capital, it is common to procure purchase funds through loans, etc., and housing mortgage loans also increased rapidly. In a situation where the share of real estate in household assets is high and the share of real-estate-related household loans executed by financial institutions is also increasing, if housing prices fall or interest rates rise, housing mortgage loans will inevitably deteriorate, and the negative ripple effects on financial stability and the national economy as a whole can be very large. Therefore, there was a need for regulations on housing mortgage loans in order to curb household debt increases and prevent instability in the financial system. In particular, at the time of the Measure in this case, the fluctuation rate of the national transaction price index rose to 0.19% in November 2019 and 0.38% in December, and in Seoul, especially Seocho-gu, Gangnam-gu, Songpa-gu, and Gangdong-gu, the fluctuation rate of the transaction price index in December 2019 was 1.82%, with high-priced apartments driving the rise in housing prices (see Korea Real Estate Board, December 2019 National Housing Price Trend Survey Report). However, because ultra-high-priced apartments involve large housing mortgage loan amounts, there is a significant risk of adverse effects on household finances and the financial soundness of financial institutions in an economic downturn, and since they lead the rise in housing prices, the necessity of regulating housing mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced apartments is also very great. In addition, at the time, the national average housing price was approximately KRW 310,734,000, the national average apartment price was approximately KRW 351,787,000, the average housing price in Seoul was approximately KRW 662,952,000, and the average apartment price in Seoul was approximately KRW 827,228,000 (see Korea Real Estate Board, December 2019 National Housing Price Trend Survey Report), so the proportion of ultra-high-priced apartments exceeding KRW 1.5 billion among apartments nationwide was very low. Accordingly, it can be seen that the Measure in this case targets only some ultra-high-priced apartments for which the need for regulation of housing mortgage loans is relatively great.\\n\\n(b) The Measure in this case can be viewed as part of the continued regulation of housing mortgage loans for high-priced houses since 2018, and is merely an expansion of the regulation of “prohibiting” housing mortgage loans that had previously been implemented in a limited manner for households owning two or more homes or one home; it is not a wholly new regulation different from the existing ones. After the measures of 2018. 9. 13., housing mortgage loans for high-priced houses (houses with officially announced land price exceeding KRW 900 million) were, in principle, prohibited in regulated areas (overheated speculation districts, speculative areas, and adjustment target areas), except in cases of actual residence (however, exceptions were allowed in certain cases for households without homes and one-home households). Likewise, under the measures of 2018. 9. 13., households owning two or more homes were prohibited from obtaining housing mortgage loans for the purchase of a new house in a regulated area, and one-home households were, in principle, prohibited from obtaining such housing mortgage loans, with only limited exceptions. The Measure in this case can be seen as a further strengthening of the policy when, despite the above measures, as noted above, housing prices surged and the achievement of the goals of stabilizing the housing market and managing the soundness of the financial market as a whole became difficult.\\n\\n(c) The Measure in this case applies to a limited place (within speculative areas and overheated speculation districts), a limited object (ultra-high-priced apartments with market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion), and a limited purpose (housing mortgage loans for the purchase of housing secured by ultra-high-priced apartments). In other words, if a case does not fall under any one of the above place, object, or purpose categories, housing mortgage loans remain possible; thus, the Petitioner may obtain a loan secured by the Petitioner’s house when the purpose is not housing purchase but living stabilization funds or operating funds for a business. In addition, the Measure in this case recognizes exceptions in cases where unavoidable reasons exist, such as where a housing sale and purchase contract was already concluded and a down payment paid before the date of announcement, where the loan application reception has been completed, where a member of a redevelopment/reconstruction association, as a one-home household, has actually resided for at least 1 year until project promotion (approval for establishment of the association), and for simple maturity extension and refinancing loans.\\n\\n(d) Considering that the scope of the Measure in this case is limited and exceptions are recognized, and that it was introduced when achievement of the purpose was difficult under the less restrictive existing housing mortgage loan restrictions, it cannot be viewed as an excessive restriction beyond what is necessary.\\n\\n(3) Balance of Legal Interests\\n\\nCompared with the disadvantage that a potential buyer of an ultra-high-priced apartment in a speculative area or overheated speculation district loses the economic opportunity to borrow from a financial institution and purchase an ultra-high-priced apartment, the public interest in stabilizing the housing market, promoting the stability of citizens’ housing lives, and securing the soundness of financial institutions and the financial market is manifestly greater; therefore, the balance of legal interests is also recognized.\\n\\n(4) Conclusion\\n\\nAccordingly, the Measure in this case does not infringe the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract in violation of the principle against excessive restriction.\\n\\n6. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, since the Petition in this case is without merit, it is dismissed, and a decision is rendered as stated in the disposition.
