This decision is based on the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, except for the separate opinion of Justices Lee Seon-ae, Lee Eun-ae, and Lee Jong-seok on the procedural requirements and the dissenting opinion on whether the principle of statutory reservation was violated, as well as the dissenting opinion of Justice Moon Hyung-bae on whether the principle against excessive restriction was violated, as set forth in 7. and 8. below.\\n\\n7. Separate Opinion of Justices Lee Seon-ae, Lee Eun-ae, and Lee Jong-seok on Procedural Requirements and Dissenting Opinion on Whether the Principle of Statutory Reservation Was Violated\\n\\nWe think that the constitutional complaint petition in this case is lawful because the Measure in this case constitutes an exercise of public power as a coercive factual act, and that the Measure in this case infringes the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract in violation of the principle of statutory reservation; therefore, we state the reasons as follows.\\n\\na. Separate Opinion on Procedural Requirements\\n\\n(1) The issue is whether the Respondent’s Measure in this case constitutes an “exercise of public power” subject to constitutional complaint adjudication as a “coercive factual act.”\\n\\n(2) Administrative factual acts can be divided into “non-coercive factual acts” lacking external binding force, such as information-providing acts like warnings, recommendations, and suggestions, and simple administrative guidance that seeks to produce factual effects through voluntary cooperation, and “coercive factual acts” that the administrative agency unilaterally enforces from a superior position; among these, coercive factual acts constitute an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication (see Constitutional Court 2017. 11. 30. 2016HEONMA503). Even if a measure takes the form of administrative guidance, if it goes beyond the limits of simple administrative guidance such as non-coercive and inducive recommendations or advice performed in expectation of voluntary cooperation from the counterparty and strongly has a regulatory and binding character, it constitutes an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication (see Constitutional Court 2003. 6. 26. 2002HEONMA337, etc.).\\n\\nIn general, whether an administrative act constitutes a coercive factual act subject to constitutional complaint adjudication must be determined individually by comprehensively considering concrete circumstances at the time the act was performed, such as ㉠ the relationship between the relevant administrative body and the counterparty, ㉡ the counterparty’s intent, degree of involvement, and attitude toward the factual act, ㉢ the purpose and background of the factual act, and ㉣ whether command or coercive means under statutes can be invoked (see Constitutional Court 1994. 5. 6. 89HEONMA35; Constitutional Court 2005. 3. 31. 2003HEONMA87; Constitutional Court 2018. 4. 26. 2016HEONMA46; Constitutional Court 2021. 11. 25. 2017HEONMA1384, etc.; Constitutional Court 2022. 1. 27. 2016HEONMA364, etc.).\\n\\n(3) The Respondent argues that the Measure in this case is merely non-coercive administrative guidance in the form of a guideline intended to present policy direction to individual banks and induce voluntary compliance, and that since individual banks had sufficient incentives to voluntarily comply with the Measure in this case for securing their own soundness and long-term interests, the Measure in this case does not amount to an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication.\\n\\nUpon review, the Measure in this case does not itself produce the legal effect of invalidating mortgage loan contracts between banks and citizens, but is merely a factual act that produces the effect of prohibiting loans to citizens through the cooperation of the counterparty banks, and no fact has been confirmed that the counterparty banks received direct sanctions from the Respondent for refusing to comply. However, in light of the facts ㉠ through ㉤ below, it can be seen that the Measure in this case was ultimately exercised as a “coercive factual act,” beyond the limits of simple administrative guidance, by the Respondent, who had various administrative powers over banks, from a superior position, as part of the existing financial regulations such as LTV, causing banks, the object of those administrative powers, to unilaterally comply with public power and thereby practically realizing, from the day after the announcement, the result of a complete prohibition on the relevant housing mortgage loans, rather than being exercised as a “non-coercive factual act” by merely inducing a certain act voluntarily through methods such as recommendation, advice, and information provision.\\n\\n㉠ In general, the Financial Services Commission handles matters concerning supervision, inspection, and sanctions of financial institutions, authorization and permission for the establishment, merger, conversion, acquisition and transfer of business, and management of financial institutions; and through the Financial Supervisory Service it can proceed to inspection, supervision, and sanctions against financial institutions, so the Respondent, as the administrative body of the Measure in this case, is in a superior position vis-à-vis the counterparty banks, and the counterparty banks are in a relationship in which they must follow the regulations and orders concerning such matters.<FOOTNOTE1>\\n\\n㉡ The Measure in this case was carried out as a unilateral act of the Respondent without the counterparty financial institutions’ banks being involved in the decision.<FOOTNOTE2>\\n\\n㉢ The Measure in this case was taken in the course of strengthening a series of “housing finance regulations” such as LTV and DTI that had been implemented by the Government for the purpose of stabilizing the housing market (background).<FOOTNOTE3>\\n\\n㉣ Regarding the Measure in this case, the Respondent unilaterally declared and repeatedly emphasized that it constituted “a complete ban on housing mortgage loans,” “to be implemented from December 17 (the day after the policy announcement),” “a prohibition on housing mortgage loans,” “the regulation prohibiting loans for ultra-high-priced houses will take effect from tomorrow,” “to help the regulatory measures take root at the front-line branches by forming field inspection teams so that the lending regulations can settle on site,” “items for immediate implementation (scheduled for implementation on 12.17),” “if either the market price of KB or the market price of the Korea Real Estate Board exceeds KRW 1.5 billion, handling of home mortgage loans is impossible,” and “cannot be handled,” thereby clearly declaring that the Measure in this case constituted “financial regulation” and that the relevant housing mortgage loans would be “completely prohibited” from the “day after the announcement” without the discretion of the counterparty financial institutions’ banks.<FOOTNOTE4>\\n\\n㉤ By announcing statements such as “the Government’s resolve is firmer than ever,” “a strong resolve to respond strictly,” “the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service will jointly form and operate field inspection teams until this measure takes root on the ground,” “Governor, please meticulously inspect in detail on site whether the measures are properly operating. The Financial Services Commission, too, though with a small number of personnel, will form field inspection teams so that the lending regulations can settle on the front-line branches and will help the smooth implementation of the regulations. I emphasize once again that the Government’s determination to stabilize housing prices contained in this ‘Housing Market Stabilization Measures’ is more resolute than ever,” and “the joint inspection team will conduct inspections and guidance through field inspections so that the detailed contents of this measure are implemented without setback at front-line business branches,” it could sufficiently be expected that there would be psychological pressure on the counterparty financial institution’s banks that some adverse treatment might be received if they did not comply,<FOOTNOTE5> and in fact, despite the Financial Supervisory Service’s inspection of Woori Bank, Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, and Hana Bank around 2020. 8., no case of violation of the Measure in this case was found at the above banks.\\n\\n(4) Accordingly, the Measure in this case constitutes an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint adjudication as a coercive factual act.\\n\\nb. Dissenting Opinion on Whether the Principle of Statutory Reservation Was Violated\\n\\n(1) Although property rights and freedom of contract, which are constitutional fundamental rights, may also be restricted by Article 37(2) of the Constitution, which prescribes the general principle of statutory reservation for restrictions on fundamental rights, such restrictions must, in principle, be by statute. Here, because the principle of statutory reservation concerning restrictions on fundamental rights calls for an exercise of public power based on statute, a restriction on fundamental rights through an exercise of public power lacking a statutory basis violates the principle of statutory reservation (see Constitutional Court 2015. 12. 23. 2014HEONMA1149).\\n\\n(2) Through an order of explanation dated 2021. 3. 31., the Constitutional Court required the Respondent to specifically explain the “legal basis of the Measure in this case.” In response, through the answer brief dated 2021. 5. 3., the Respondent replied, “The legal basis of the Measure in this case is Article 34 of the Banking Act, Article 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act, and Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations based thereon.” The Respondent then explained, “For guidance on sound management under Article 34 of the Banking Act, it is necessary to take measures so that banks can maintain sound management even in the face of external shocks by regulating ‘speculative lending demand’ through risk management for housing mortgage loans, such as Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations, and by adjusting and limiting the extent of housing price increases caused by housing mortgage loans. Accordingly, the Government, including the Financial Supervisory Service, is implementing administrative guidance for the actual implementation of the Housing Market Stabilization Measures based on the above regulations, and banks must operate in accordance with the regulations and orders concerning risk management for housing mortgage loans (Article 3(1) of the Banking Act).”\\n\\n(3) The contents of Article 3(1), Article 34 of the Banking Act, Article 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act, and Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations, which the Respondent claims as the legal basis for the Measure in this case, are as follows.\\n\\nArticle 3(1) of the Banking Act provides that all banks in the Republic of Korea shall be operated in accordance with this Act, the Bank of Korea Act, the Act on the Establishment, etc. of the Financial Services Commission, the Act on Corporate Governance of Financial Companies, and regulations and orders thereunder; and Article 34 of the same Act provides that a bank, when operating banking business, shall secure sound management by faithfully maintaining its capital and appropriate liquidity (paragraph 1), and that in order to maintain sound management, it shall comply with the management guidance standards determined by the Financial Services Commission pursuant to what is prescribed by Presidential Decree concerning “matters concerning adequacy of capital, matters concerning soundness of assets, matters concerning liquidity, and other matters necessary to secure sound management” (paragraph 2).\\n\\nArticle 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act provides that the management guidance standards under Article 34(2) of the Banking Act shall include “matters concerning standards for holding capital corresponding to credit risk of a bank, such as the capital adequacy ratio for risk-weighted assets under the standards of the Bank for International Settlements, matters concerning standards for classifying the soundness of assets held by a bank, such as loan claims, matters concerning standards for managing credit extension to persons whom the Financial Services Commission deems necessary to manage credit extension in an integrated manner and designates and publicly notifies, matters concerning standards for holding liquid assets against liquid liabilities, and other matters publicly notified by the Financial Services Commission for securing sound management of a bank” (paragraph 1), and provides that requests for submission of plans or agreements under this provision, procedures and methods for concluding agreements, and other necessary matters shall be determined and publicly notified by the Financial Services Commission (paragraph 3).\\n\\nAccordingly, Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations, a Financial Services Commission Notice, provides that “when handling housing mortgage loans, a bank shall comply with the loan-to-value ratio, debt-to-income ratio, and other restrictions on handling housing mortgage loans and extending maturity prescribed in <APPENDIX_TABLE6> so that sound management is maintained pursuant to Article 34 of the Act” (paragraph 1).\\n\\nThus, it can be seen that the Financial Services Commission has the general authority, through the Financial Services Commission Notice (Banking Supervision Regulations) specifically formed pursuant to the delegation under Article 3(1) and Article 34 of the Banking Act and the re-delegation under Article 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act, to determine matters for securing the soundness of bank management, and that banks bear the general obligation to comply with the specifically formed Financial Services Commission Notice (Banking Supervision Regulations) in accordance with such statutes and regulations.\\n\\n(4) In the Measure in this case, the Respondent specified the “effective date” as “2019. 12. 17.” and expressly and specifically “prohibited” from that date onward home-purchase mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion) in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts. Therefore, as the Respondent contends, in order for Article 3(1), Article 34 of the Banking Act, Article 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act, and Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations to become the concrete legal basis of the Measure in this case, the restrictions in the Measure in this case had to be prescribed in the “Financial Services Commission Notice,” i.e., “Banking Supervision Regulations <APPENDIX_TABLE6>,” which is the form of delegation established by the statute as of the effective date.\\n\\nHowever, in the “<APPENDIX_TABLE6> Risk Management Standards for Housing Mortgage Loans” prescribed in the Banking Supervision Regulations as of the effective date of the Measure in this case (2019. 12. 17.) (Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2019-52 on 2019. 11. 20.), there was no content whatsoever concerning the “prohibition of home-purchase mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced apartments in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts,” and there was not even a definitional provision concerning “ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion).”\\n\\nRather, it was only in the Banking Supervision Regulations implemented approximately 1 year after the Measure in this case (2020. 12. 3.) (Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2020-54 on 2020. 12. 3.) that, in “<APPENDIX_TABLE6> Risk Management Standards for Mortgage Loans Relating to Housing,” a definitional provision was newly established in “Chapter 1 General Provisions” stating, “BEO. Ultra-high-priced apartment means an apartment with a market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion,” and accordingly, in “Chapter 5 Restrictions and Matters of Note in Handling Mortgage Loans Relating to Housing,” the following was newly established: “8. (Restriction on Handling Mortgage Loans Relating to Housing for the Purpose of Purchasing an Ultra-High-Priced Apartment in a Speculative Area or Overheated Speculation District) A bank may not handle a housing mortgage loan (including a mortgage loan secured by housing-related beneficiary certificates) for the purpose of purchasing an ultra-high-priced apartment located in a speculative area or overheated speculation district. Provided, however, that the foregoing shall not apply if any of the following applies. / a. Where debt is unavoidably assumed due to inheritance, participation in an auction for preservation of claims, or the like / b. Where there are unavoidable reasons, such as where a member of a reconstruction/redevelopment association, as a one-home household, has been confirmed to have resided there for at least 1 year until the approval for establishment of the association,” and only then is it confirmed that the legal basis was completed.\\n\\n(5) If the matter is as such, then it is clear that Article 3(1), Article 34 of the Banking Act, Article 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act, and Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations, which the Respondent claims as the legal basis for the Measure in this case, could not, as of their effective date, 2019. 12. 17., become the concrete legal basis for the Measure in this case, which is a coercive factual act; and even upon examining the materials submitted by the Respondent and the relevant records, no other statutory basis sufficient to support the Measure in this case as of the effective date can be found. Therefore, ultimately, the Measure in this case infringes the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract in violation of the principle of statutory reservation.\\n\\n8. Dissenting Opinion of Justice Moon Hyung-bae on Whether the Principle Against Excessive Restriction Was Violated\\n\\nI agree with the majority opinion that the Measure in this case satisfies the character of an exercise of public power, but I believe that it infringes the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract in violation of the principle against excessive restriction; therefore, I state the reasons as follows.\\n\\na. Legitimacy of Purpose\\n\\nAt the time of the Measure in this case, ① on 2019. 12. 16., the Government announced in a joint statement of the relevant ministries and agencies that “The Government’s resolve regarding the stabilization of the housing market is firmer than ever. ... Based on this grave awareness, the Government has prepared the ‘Housing Market Stabilization Measures.’ ... First, we will significantly strengthen management of housing mortgage loans in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts. We will completely prohibit housing mortgage loans for apartments with a market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion for all borrowers, including households, individual business owners, and corporations,” ② the “Housing Market Stabilization Measures” attached to the joint press release of the relevant ministries and agencies on 2019. 12. 16. also included, under item “III. Housing Market Stabilization Measures,” the content prohibiting home-purchase mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced apartments, and ③ it is confirmed that, at the “Holding of a Financial Sector Meeting Regarding Housing Market Stabilization Measures” hosted by the Financial Services Commission on 2019. 12. 16., the Respondent stated in opening remarks that “The Housing Market Stabilization Measures jointly announced today by the relevant ministries contain the Government’s grave recognition of the situation and its firm resolve to stabilize the housing market. ... Let me explain the main contents of the measures. First, we will restrict housing mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced housing.”\\n\\nIn addition, in the item “Legitimacy of Purpose” of the supplemental brief dated 2021. 2. 26., the Respondent answered, “They were devised for the purpose of stabilizing the housing market by blocking the inflow of speculative demand concentrated in some overheated areas. ... The subject matter of adjudication in this case also has the purpose of improving the excessive flow of funds into the real estate sector that has continued from the standpoint of soundness management of individual financial companies and macroprudential management of the entire financial market.”\\n\\nAccordingly, it can be said that the Measure in this case is for “stabilization of the housing market,” “soundness management of individual bank management,” and “macroprudential management of the entire financial market,” and its purpose is legitimate.\\n\\nb. Appropriateness of Means\\n\\nIn the answer brief dated 2021. 5. 3., the Respondent replied, “The legal basis of the Measure in this case is Article 34 of the Banking Act, Article 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act, and Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations based thereon.” However, according to the above statutes cited by the Respondent, it can be seen that the Measure in this case must be exercised for the purpose of “soundness of bank management.” In other words, it cannot be used as a means for “stabilization of the housing market” or “macroprudential management of the entire financial market”; it must be used as a means for “soundness management of individual banks.”\\n\\nIn response to the Constitutional Court’s order of explanation on this matter, the Respondent replied in the answer brief dated 2022. 8. 18. that “The Measure in this case has, along with the purpose of maintaining and securing the ‘soundness of bank management’ expressly stated in the Banking Act, also the purpose of ‘stabilization of the housing market,’ given the characteristics of the Measure in this case, which targets the loan-handling-available amount of housing mortgage loans, and ‘stabilization of the housing market’ is an incidental purpose that can be achieved through maintaining and securing the ‘soundness of bank management’ under the Banking Act. ... It is not prohibited by the Banking Act to incidentally achieve the purpose of ‘stabilization of the housing market’ in the course of maintaining and securing the soundness of bank management related to housing mortgage loans.”\\n\\nOf course, it is not prohibited to incidentally achieve “stabilization of the housing market” and “macroprudential management” in the course of maintaining and securing “soundness of bank management” related to housing mortgage loans. However, the issue is that it is uncertain whether the Measure in this case contributes to maintaining and securing the “soundness of individual bank management,” the original purpose required by the statutes on which the Respondent relies. Before the Measure in this case, housing mortgage loans were regulated at a loan-to-value ratio (LTV) of 40%; therefore, in order for the Measure in this case, which prohibits home-purchase mortgage loans for ultra-high-priced apartments (market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion) in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts (i.e., changes the LTV to 0%), to contribute to maintaining and securing the “soundness of bank management,” it would have to have been foreseeable on 2019. 12. 17. that the market value of ultra-high-priced apartments in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts would soon plummet below 40%. In this regard, at the hearing on 2022. 6. 16., the Constitutional Court asked the Respondent whether there were specific and reliable materials at the time of the Measure in this case indicating that the market value of ultra-high-priced apartments would soon plunge below 40%, and requested the basis for that judgment; thereafter, in the order of explanation dated 2022. 7. 15., materials concerning this were again requested, but to date no such materials have been submitted.\\n\\nIf so, it is difficult to conclude that the Measure in this case was an appropriate means contributing to the original purpose required by the statutes, namely maintaining and securing “soundness of bank management,” and when the Measure in this case fails to contribute to the original purpose required by the statutes, it is difficult to view it as a means that can be used solely for the incidental purposes of “stabilization of the housing market” and “macroprudential management.” Accordingly, appropriateness of means is not recognized in the Measure in this case.\\n\\nc. Least Restrictive Means\\n\\nThe Measure in this case also does not satisfy the least restrictive means requirement for the following reasons.\\n\\n(1) The Measure in this case imposes a broader restriction than necessary.\\n\\nThe Measure in this case is intended to regulate “speculative lending demand” for the purpose of stabilizing the housing market for actual homebuyers to acquire their own homes. However, it did not exclude actual homebuyers from “speculative lending demand.” Even when compared to the previous regulation of housing mortgage loans for high-priced houses, which had been implemented “except for cases of actual residence,” the Measure in this case has an overly broad scope. Only if loans clearly determined to be actual demand are left open and only loans whose nature is not clearly speculative are regulated in addition to speculative demand, would the restriction not exceed the necessary degree.\\n\\nIn addition, the Measure in this case prohibits housing mortgage loans regardless of whether the household is a household without homes, one-home household, or multi-home household. The failure to recognize an exception for households without homes is a result of viewing “speculative lending demand” loosely as merely “borrowers expecting housing prices to rise borrowing housing mortgage loans to purchase homes.” However, it would be difficult to regard all “borrowers expecting housing prices to rise” as “speculative lending demand.” The national housing ownership rate has steadily increased to 49.9% in 1990, 54.2% in 2000, 54.3% in 2010, and 58% in 2019, but the increase in home ownership since 2000 has almost stopped. As reasons for the stagnation in the home ownership rate, the fact that housing became a means of real estate speculation centered on multi-home owners and the fact that the rise in housing prices raised the barrier to entry for owning a home are cited. However, the Measure in this case targets not only the speculative forces or multi-home owners who are the cause of the stagnation in the home ownership rate, but also households without homes, who are merely victims. For example, even if a salaried worker in their 40s who has never owned a home wants to purchase an apartment, unless he or she has KRW 1.5 billion in cash, it would not be possible to purchase a house that qualifies as an “ultra-high-priced apartment,” and this cannot but be considered an excessive restriction beyond what is necessary for the purpose of “regulating speculative lending demand.”\\n\\nMeanwhile, in regulating housing mortgage loans for “ultra-high-priced apartments,” the Measure in this case uses “market value” as the standard for ultra-high-priced apartments. Compared with the previous practice of determining “high-priced houses” based on officially announced land price of KRW 900 million, the standard for “ultra-high-priced apartments” can be seen as KRW 1.5 billion in market value, but market value fluctuates (in fact, after the Measure in this case was implemented, apartments with a market value of KRW 1.5 billion in speculative areas and overheated speculation districts increased sharply), so it cannot serve as a standard for the minimum restriction necessary to achieve the purpose. According to the market price provided by KB Kookmin Bank, as of August 2021 the average sale price of apartments in Seoul was KRW 1,216,390,000, and based on the price of a 30-pyeong apartment in Seoul, which is ordinarily occupied by a family of 4 (approximately 99.17 square meters), the average apartment price in the 11 districts south of the Han River was KRW 1,448,650,000, while the market prices of recently sold 30-pyeong or larger apartments in the 11 districts north of the Han River were mostly reported as KRW 1.5 billion or more; thus, the KRW 1.5 billion targeted by the Measure in this case is no longer “ultra-high-priced apartments” but merely average market prices, which shows that the regulatory scope is broad.\\n\\nAs such, considering that the areas falling under speculative areas and overheated speculation districts are broad, encompassing all of Seoul Metropolitan City, major areas of Gyeonggi-do, Sejong Special Self-Governing City, etc.; that apartments with market value exceeding KRW 1.5 billion, which qualify as “ultra-high-priced apartments,” continue to fluctuate and are numerous when based on Seoul and Gyeonggi-do, etc.; and that a broad restriction is imposed without recognizing exceptions for actual homebuyers or households without homes, etc., the range in which the property rights and freedom of contract of actual homebuyers seeking to purchase homes in those areas are restricted by the Measure in this case is excessively broad.\\n\\n(2) There exist means less restrictive than the Measure in this case.\\n\\nAccording to Article 29-2 of the Banking Supervision Regulations as of the effective date of the Measure in this case (2019. 11. 20. Financial Services Commission Notice No. 2019-52), a bank was required, when handling housing mortgage loans, to comply with the loan-to-value ratio, debt-to-income ratio, and other restrictions on handling housing mortgage loans and extending maturity prescribed in <APPENDIX_TABLE6> so that sound management is maintained pursuant to Article 34 of the Banking Act, and in the Chapter 2 loan-to-value ratio (LTV) part of <APPENDIX_TABLE6>, provisions were in place concerning “restrictions on handling housing mortgage loans for the purchase of homes in regulated areas for households owning homes” and “restrictions on handling housing mortgage loans for the purchase of high-priced houses in regulated areas.” For example, except in cases such as where the existing home is disposed of within 2 years, in principle, one-home households were prohibited from obtaining housing mortgage loans for the purchase of a new home in a regulated area; and except in cases such as where a household without homes moves in within 2 years after purchasing a home or a one-home household disposes of the existing home within 2 years, in principle, housing mortgage loans were prohibited for the purchase of high-priced houses in regulated areas (officially announced land price exceeding KRW 900 million).\\n\\nEven if “regulation of speculative lending demand” were considered necessary for sound management of banks, the Measure in this case, instead of using means such as restrictions on the loan-to-value ratio (LTV), debt-to-income ratio (DTI), or maturity extension, etc., simply “prohibits” housing mortgage loans from the outset, which exceeds the necessary range.\\n\\nd. Balance of Legal Interests\\n\\nWhile it is questionable whether the Measure in this case can achieve the public interest of stabilizing the housing market, promoting stability in citizens’ housing lives, and securing the soundness of financial institutions and the financial market, the restriction on the property rights and freedom of contract of prospective home purchasers, including actual homebuyers, is severe; therefore, the Measure in this case does not satisfy the balance of legal interests.\\n\\ne. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the Measure in this case infringes the Petitioner’s property rights and freedom of contract in violation of the principle against excessive restriction."}

{"[2019HEONMA941]": "1. Outline of the Case\\n\\nAs persons who passed the 8th Bar Examination on 2019. 4. 26. and thereby obtained attorney qualification, Petitioners all have no religion. Petitioners entered the Army Training Center in Nonsan-si, Chungcheongnam-do on 2019. 5. 30., were assigned to ○○ Regiment, ○○ Company, ○○ Platoon (□□ Platoon), received basic military training until 2019. 6. 27., and were newly appointed as public-service legal officers on 2019. 8. 1.\\n\\nAt around 8:30 a.m. on Sunday, 2019. 6. 2., which was the first week of basic military training, Squad Leader Jo○○, belonging to the Army Training Center, told the trainees to “choose and attend one of the Protestant, Buddhist, Catholic, or Won Buddhist religious events held within the Army Training Center.” In response, Petitioners approached Squad Leader Jo○○ and stated that they had no religion and did not wish to attend any religious event. Thereupon, the said Squad Leader stated, to the effect that “even if you have no religion, attend once for experience. Think about it once more, and if your mind does not change, come back and definitively state your intention not to attend.” Thereafter, Petitioners did not again state their intention not to attend and attended the religious events conducted at each religious facility within the Army Training Center.\\n\\nPetitioners filed this constitutional complaint on 2019. 8. 23., asserting that the Respondent’s measure on 2019. 6. 2. requiring them to attend one of the religious events held at religious facilities within the Army Training Center infringed their freedom of religion and violated the principle of separation of religion and state.\\n\\n2. Subject Matter of Adjudication\\n\\nThe subject matter of this adjudication is whether the Respondent’s act of requiring Petitioners on 2019. 6. 2. to attend one of the Protestant, Buddhist, Catholic, or Won Buddhist religious events held at religious facilities within the Army Training Center (hereinafter referred to as the “Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue”) infringes Petitioners’ fundamental rights. The relevant provision is as follows.\\n\\n[Relevant Provision]\\n\\nFramework Act on the Status and Service of Soldiers (as amended by Act No. 16034 on 2018. 12. 24.)\\n\\nArticle 15 (Guarantee of Religious Life) ① A commander shall guarantee the religious life of soldiers within the extent that it does not impede the performance of the unit’s mission.\\n\\n② A soldier with a duty to reside within the barracks may attend religious events held at religious facilities and other places designated by the commander (hereinafter referred to as “religious facilities, etc.”), and when a soldier wishes to attend a religious event held outside religious facilities, etc., he or she shall obtain the commander’s permission.\\n\\n③ No soldier shall be compelled to attend a religious event against his or her will, nor shall attendance be restricted.\\n\\n3. Petitioners’ Arguments\\n\\nThe Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue is an exercise of factual power and has already ended, but there is a risk of repetition and constitutional clarification is a matter of great importance; therefore, this petition is lawful.\\n\\nThe Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue includes the purpose of proselytization, so its legitimacy of purpose cannot be recognized, compelling attendance at religious events constitutes an irrational and unfair means. The failure to adopt alternatives that minimize infringement, such as providing an exception allowing one not to attend religious events, violates the principle of minimum infringement, and compelling attendance at religious events instead produces a counterproductive public effect of undermining military discipline, thus failing the balance of interests. Accordingly, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue violates the principle of proportionality and infringes Petitioners’ negative freedom of religion, and also violates the principle of separation of religion and state under Article 20(2) of the Constitution.\\n\\n4. Determination on the Requirements for Admissibility\\n\\nA. Whether the Subject of Constitutional Complaint Exists\\n\\nFactual acts by an administrative agency are divided into “non-power factual acts,” which have no external binding force, such as information-providing acts like warnings, recommendations, or suggestions, or simple administrative guidance that seeks to produce factual effects through voluntary cooperation, and “power factual acts,” which the administrative agency unilaterally compels from a superior position; among them, power factual acts constitute an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint. In general, whether a certain act constitutes a power factual act subject to constitutional complaint must be determined individually by comprehensively considering the specific circumstances existing at the time the act was performed, such as the relationship between the relevant administrative body and the counterparty, the counterparty’s intent, degree of involvement, and attitude toward the factual act, the purpose and background of the factual act, and whether compulsory measures under statutes could be invoked (Constitutional Court 2012. 10. 25. 2011HEONMA429; Constitutional Court 2017. 11. 30. 2016HEONMA503 reference).\\n\\nThe Respondent, as the highest administrator within the Army Training Center where Petitioners receive basic military training, is in a superior position with respect to Petitioners’ life in the training center. On 2019. 2. 28., during the weekly situation evaluation meeting, the Respondent emphasized efforts to enhance “faith-based combat power” so that combat capability of the armed forces could be strengthened through guaranteeing conditions for religious activities, and the Army Training Center’s “Guidelines for Discipline and Barracks Life Guidance” state that while guaranteeing the choice of religious activities according to individual will, they also encourage “one person, one religion” from the standpoint of fostering character and strengthening spiritual combat power through chaplaincy activities, and provide that “whether to attend religious events, etc. shall be carried out through the chain of command and duty officers.”\\n\\nThe Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue was carried out through Squad Leader Jo○○, who commanded Petitioners. Although the day on which the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue was taken was a holiday, Petitioners asked Squad Leader Jo○○, who was on duty, whether non-attendance at a religious event was possible in order to confirm that possibility, and Squad Leader Jo○○ may be evaluated as delivering an official response reflecting the above-mentioned guidelines of the Respondent; there is no room to view this as Squad Leader Jo○○, in his personal capacity and not as an Army Training Center squad leader, expressing his private opinion to Petitioners.\\n\\nIn addition, according to the materials submitted by the Respondent in relation to this case, during the week of admission of the trainees at issue (the 4th day after admission), attendance at religious events was encouraged for experience of the four religions, and from the second week until the week of completion, attendance or rest was possible upon one’s own request; and trainees who followed minority religions or were nonreligious could be absent from the second week onward upon personal request. Also, according to the statistical data submitted by the Respondent, all personnel attended the morning religious event in the week of admission, with no absentees remaining, whereas some were absent in the afternoon, and from the second week onward, there were a considerable number of absentees both in the morning and in the afternoon. If so, at least for the morning religious event in the week of admission, it may be viewed that non-attendance was in substance not permitted.\\n\\nTaking the foregoing into account, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue exceeded the limits of a non-power recommendation, advice, or similar simple administrative guidance made by the Respondent in expectation of Petitioners’ voluntary cooperation, and may be said to have been unilaterally compelled upon Petitioners from a superior position; this constitutes a power factual act subject to constitutional complaint.\\n\\nB. Interest in the Protection of Rights\\n\\nPetitioners have already completed basic military training and left the Army Training Center, and are no longer subject to a restriction of fundamental rights, so even if this petition is granted, it will not help provide subjective relief to Petitioners. However, even if a constitutional complaint does not provide much assistance to subjective relief, where there is a risk that such infringing act will be repeated in the future, or the resolution of the relevant dispute is an essential matter for the protection and maintenance of the constitutional order, so that constitutional clarification thereof has significant meaning, the interest in adjudication may be recognized (Constitutional Court 2002. 7. 18. 2000HEONMA327).\\n\\nIt may be acknowledged that the Respondent, through conducting religious events, goes beyond guaranteeing the freedom of religion of trainees and encourages “one person, one religion” for the enhancement of faith-based combat power; the possibility that an act such as in this case, which goes beyond recommending attendance at religious events and in substance compels attendance, will be repeated in the future is entirely possible. Also, given the importance of protecting freedom of religion, including negative freedom, and the principle of separation of religion and state, whether the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue is constitutionally justified is a matter requiring constitutional clarification for the protection and maintenance of the constitutional order; accordingly, this petition for adjudication has an interest in adjudication.\\n\\n5. Determination on the Merits\\n\\nA. Fundamental Rights Restrained\\n\\nArticle 20 of our Constitution provides in paragraph 1 that all citizens shall have freedom of religion, and in paragraph 2 that no state religion shall be recognized and religion and politics shall be separated, thereby declaring freedom of religion and the principle of separation of religion and state. Freedom of religion generally consists of three elements: freedom of belief, freedom of religious conduct, and freedom of religious assembly and association (Constitutional Court 2001. 9. 27. 2000HEONMA159). Freedom of religion includes freedom from religion as well (Constitutional Court 2010. 2. 25. 2007HEONBA131 et al.), and also protects negative freedom not to have a belief and not to attend religious conduct and religious assemblies.\\n\\nThe Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue compelled Petitioners to choose and attend one of the religious events held at the religious facilities of the four religions: Protestantism, Buddhism, Catholicism, and Won Buddhism. The religious events at issue are religious assemblies conducted by religion (see Article 2, item 6 of the Directive on Military Chaplaincy Affairs), and are conducted in order to guarantee the freedom of religious events by enabling soldiers who have beliefs to attend religious events of the relevant religion [Article 15(1) and (2) of the Framework Act on the Status and Service of Soldiers (hereinafter referred to as the “Soldiers’ Service Basic Act”)], and thus possess the character of a religious assembly in which religious conduct is contemplated.\\n\\nThe compulsion of religion or belief upon another person can ultimately be accomplished only through religious conduct, that is, external acts such as confession of faith, prayer, and attendance at worship services. Therefore, irrespective of whether Petitioners’ inner mind or beliefs actually changed as a result of the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue, the very compulsion to attend a religious event held at a religious facility may be evaluated as restricting Petitioners’ freedom not to have a belief and their freedom not to attend religious assemblies. Accordingly, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue restricts Petitioners’ freedom of religion.\\n\\nB. Whether Freedom of Religion Was Infringed\\n\\n(1) Whether the Principle of Separation of Religion and State Was Violated\\n\\n(a) Meaning\\n\\nThe principle of separation of religion and state set forth in Article 20(2) of the Constitution means the state’s neutrality toward religion, in which religion and politics are separated and do not exercise mutual interference or influence. Pursuant to the principle of separation of religion and state, the state shall not recognize the privileges of any specific religion and shall maintain neutrality toward religion. The state’s religious neutrality is also necessary for the full realization of freedom of religion, and the state’s encouragement of a specific religion may infringe the freedom of other religions or freedom from religion (see Constitutional Court 2010. 2. 25. 2007HEONBA131 et al.).\\n\\n(b) Freedom of Religion within the Military\\n\\nEven soldiers must have their freedom of religion guaranteed, and religion may be of even greater importance to soldiers, especially in situations where fear of death is maximized, such as when casualties arise in cases of national emergency including war or armed conflict and soldiers are actually mobilized for armed combat (see Constitutional Court 2003. 3. 27. 2002HEONBA35). Also, even during peacetime training periods, given the characteristic that group life continues, it may be acknowledged that religious belief can play a positive role in maintaining a sound barracks life and in establishing an ethical or value system to control the use of force within the military, which may otherwise be subject to lack of restraint or abuse.\\n\\nThe Soldiers’ Service Basic Act, in Article 15(1) and (2), guarantees the religious life of soldiers within the extent that it does not impede the performance of the unit’s mission, in order to guarantee the fundamental rights of soldiers whose mission is national defense and protection of the people, and provides that soldiers may attend religious events conducted at religious facilities, etc. However, under the principle of separation of religion and state, the state shall not encourage a specific religion or interfere with an individual’s choice of religion, and beyond guaranteeing a soldier’s voluntary and autonomous religious activities, it may not compel attendance at religious events against the soldier’s will; this point is explicitly confirmed in Article 15(3) of the Soldiers’ Service Basic Act.\\n\\n(c) The Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue\\n\\n1) Since the early days of establishment, our military has operated a chaplaincy system, and from around the 1970s has adopted work guidelines of “faith-based combat power enhancement,” which regards religious faith as intangible combat power. Under current statutes, faith-based combat power enhancement means the strengthening of intangible combat power by enabling service members to complete assigned missions through religious faith, views on life and death, views on the state, and values elevated through religious duties (Article 2, item 12 of the Directive on Military Chaplaincy Affairs). Taking into account that an individual’s religious faith also helps strengthen the mental force required by the military, guaranteeing freedom of religion within the military to the fullest extent and encouraging religious activities within the extent that does not impede the performance of the unit’s mission is to strengthen intangible combat power, including the soldier’s values and mental force, which are as important as the military’s tangible combat power, and may be said to accommodate the positive social role of religion.\\n\\nHowever, even if the above chaplaincy system and “faith-based combat power enhancement” are necessary for strengthening intangible combat power, religious activities in the military cannot go beyond the limits proclaimed by our Constitution, namely the negation of state religion and the principle of separation of religion and state, that is, the requirement that the state remain neutral toward all religions.\\n\\n2) As examined above, the religious events at issue may be acknowledged to possess the character of a religious assembly in which religious conduct is contemplated. The Respondent’s act of causing Petitioners to attend a religious event itself constitutes external compulsion of religious conduct, and also violates the express prohibition in Article 15(3) of the Soldiers’ Service Basic Act, which concretizes the principle of separation of religion and state in relation to the operation of religious events within the military.\\n\\nIn particular, the Respondent’s requiring Petitioners to attend one of the religious events of the four religions—Protestantism, Catholicism, Buddhism, and Won Buddhism—may be viewed as the Respondent’s approval and encouragement of the said four religions and as expressing a preference for having one of these four religions over other religions or over no religion. However, the principle of separation of religion and state under our Constitution is intended to ensure plurality, which forms the basis of a democratic society, by recognizing the possibility of diverse religious beliefs or atheism from a neutral position of the state; thus, the Respondent’s singling out only the above four religions and compelling Petitioners to attend their religious events violates the state’s neutrality toward religion and is tantamount to favoring specific religions, which is impermissible under the principle of separation of religion and state.\\n\\nAlso, even if the Respondent ultimately took the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue for the secular purpose of strengthening military power, such a measure causes a close entanglement between the state and religion because it makes religion a mere means for achieving its purpose, or conversely provides an opportunity for religious organizations to exercise influence by intervening in the military as state power and engaging in proselytizing activities. In this respect, the Respondent’s enhancing the mental combat power of soldiers by means of compelling them to attend religious events against their will, beyond guaranteeing an individual’s autonomous and voluntary religious life or religious activities, directly violates the principle of separation of religion and state, which requires the mutual separation of state and religion, and infringes freedom of religion.\\n\\n(2) Whether the Principle of Proportionality Was Violated\\n\\nThe Respondent may be viewed as having ultimately sought to strengthen the mental combat power of soldiers through the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue, and thus there is room to recognize the legitimacy of the purpose at first glance. However, compelling persons who do not have religion to attend religious events, going beyond merely recognizing and actively accommodating the positive aspects of religious belief or voluntary attendance at religious events that are autonomously formed by individuals, is more likely to generate resentment or discomfort toward the relevant religion and military life and thereby produce a countereffect, rather than contribute to strengthening the mental combat power needed in the military. Accordingly, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue, which seeks to enhance the mental combat power of soldiers by causing Petitioners to attend Protestant, Buddhist, Catholic, or Won Buddhist religious events against their will, cannot have the suitability of its means recognized.\\n\\nFurthermore, since the Respondent could have chosen other alternatives, such as general ethical education, apart from religious means, as a way to strengthen the mental combat power of trainees who do not have religion, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue was not an indispensable means and cannot be viewed as satisfying the minimum infringement requirement. Also, Petitioners were compelled to attend religious events during military service under the compulsory service system, and it is difficult to view that Petitioners had any real possibility of avoiding this; moreover, even if attendance at religious events was compulsory only during the first week of training and became optional from the second week onward, the infringement of religious freedom that had already occurred cannot be viewed as remedied or diminished.\\n\\nSince religion may be the most essential belief forming an individual’s personality, state coercion regarding religion constitutes a serious infringement of fundamental rights and is not something that can be sacrificed for the enhancement of a soldier’s mental combat power, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue also fails to satisfy the balance of interests.\\n\\nC. Conclusion\\n\\nAccordingly, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue infringes Petitioners’ freedom of religion by violating the principle of separation of religion and state and the principle of proportionality.\\n\\n6. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the Respondent’s act of requiring Petitioners on 2019. 6. 2. to attend one of the Protestant, Buddhist, Catholic, or Won Buddhist religious events held at religious facilities within the Army Training Center should be revoked as infringing Petitioners’ freedom of religion; however, since the Respondent’s act has already ended, we decide to make a finding of unconstitutionality in declaratory form in order to prevent repetition of the same or similar infringement of fundamental rights, and render the decision as stated in the order. This decision was unanimous among the remaining participating Justices, except for the dissenting opinion of Justice Lee Seon-ae, Justice Lee Eun-ae, and Justice Lee Yeong-jin as set forth in 7. below.\\n\\n7. Dissenting Opinion of Justice Lee Seon-ae, Justice Lee Eun-ae, and Justice Lee Yeong-jin\\n\\nWe find that the petition for adjudication regarding the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue cannot be viewed as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint, and is inadmissible because there is no interest in the protection of rights, and thus we state the dissenting opinion as follows.\\n\\nA. Whether It Is a Subject of Constitutional Complaint\\n\\n(1) Article 68(1) of the Constitutional Court Act provides that a person whose fundamental rights have been infringed by an exercise or non-exercise of public power may file a constitutional complaint, and “public power” here means the authoritative acts of all state institutions and public bodies exercising legislative, executive, and judicial power, and its exercise or non-exercise must directly produce legal effects on the rights and duties of the people, adversely changing the legal relationship or legal status of the complainant (see Constitutional Court 2021. 11. 25. 2017HEONMA1384 et al.).\\n\\n(2) It is true that the Respondent, as Petitioners’ superior officer (see Article 25 of the Soldiers’ Service Basic Act), was in a superior position regarding Petitioners’ life in the training center. However, whether a certain act constitutes a power factual act subject to constitutional complaint must be determined by comprehensively considering, in addition to the general relationship between the relevant administrative body and the counterparty, the specific circumstances at the time the specific factual act was carried out, such as the counterparty’s intent, degree of involvement, and attitude toward the factual act, the purpose and background of the factual act, and whether coercive measures under statutes could be invoked (see Constitutional Court 1994. 5. 6. 89HEONMA35; Constitutional Court 2018. 4. 26. 2016HEONMA46 et al.), and the mere fact that the Respondent was in a superior position over Petitioners does not mean that all acts of the Respondent constitute power factual acts.\\n\\nArticle 15(3) of the Soldiers’ Service Basic Act expressly provides that “no soldier shall be compelled to participate in a religious rite or be restricted from participation against his or her will,” and therefore the Respondent has no authority to order Petitioners to participate in a religious rite against their will. In such a situation, if the Respondent merely encouraged attendance at the religious event for the first week, it is difficult, absent special circumstances, to regard this as amounting to an order or coercion.\\n\\nThe Army Training Center’s “Guidelines for Discipline and Barracks Life Guidance” merely state that “one person, one religion” is encouraged, and do not contain anything stating that one must necessarily have one religion regardless of one’s will or must attend a religious event at least once. Rather, they only explicitly state that “those who do not attend religious events shall be guaranteed personal maintenance and free time.” Looking at the squad leader’s remarks as well, when Petitioners stated their intention not to attend, he merely said, to the effect that “think about it once more, and if your mind does not change, come back and definitively state your intention not to attend,” and did not categorically instruct that they must attend. Even assuming that Petitioners may have felt psychological pressure in again stating their intention not to attend, such subjective possibility alone is insufficient to evaluate the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue as having gone beyond a simple recommendation and reaching coercion.\\n\\nMeanwhile, according to the materials submitted by the Respondent, all personnel attended the religious event in the morning of the first week, while some did not attend in the afternoon, and from the second week onward there were a considerable number of absentees both in the morning and in the afternoon. However, attendance status may be influenced not only by the Respondent’s recommendation but also by various factors such as the trainees’ voluntary judgment or the atmosphere among the trainees at the time. In fact, looking at the attendance status at religious events in the first week of other training cohorts trained at the Army Training Center as reflected in the records, the 19-16th cohort preceding Petitioners (training from 2019. 4. 18. to 2019. 5. 16.) appears to have had 579 attendees in the daytime and 44 at night, so that out of a total of 732 personnel, at least 109 and at most 153 were absent; the subsequent 19-28th cohort (training from 2019. 7. 18. to 2019. 8. 14.) had 579 attendees in the daytime and 28 at night, so that out of a total of 689 personnel, at least 82 and at most 110 were absent; and the 19-34th cohort (training from 2019. 8. 29. to 2019. 9. 26.) had 579 attendees in the daytime and 4 at night, so that out of a total of 679 personnel, at least 96 and at most 100 were absent. If so, it is difficult to view that the Respondent was compelling attendance at the first-week religious event as a general policy of the Army Training Center, and there is no particular reason why the Respondent would have set a different guideline only for Petitioners’ cohort.\\n\\n(3) Furthermore, as to whether there was a sanction for non-performance of attendance at the religious event at issue, the Respondent and the squad leader did not notify that any disadvantage would result from not attending the religious event in the first week, and there is no material supporting the view that adverse treatment could be received in the event of noncompliance with the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue. Rather, compelling attendance at a religious event against one’s will would constitute a clear unlawful act prohibited by the Soldiers’ Service Basic Act. Then Petitioners could fully know that no disadvantage could be imposed for non-attendance and that, if imposed, its illegality could be challenged, and in such a situation it is difficult to conclude that the Respondent’s act of recommending attendance would have had the effect of amounting to de facto coercion upon Petitioners.\\n\\n(4) Accordingly, the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue cannot be viewed as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint.\\n\\nB. Interest in the Protection of Rights\\n\\n(1) Even if the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue were regarded as an exercise of public power subject to constitutional complaint, Petitioners already completed basic military training and left the Army Training Center as of 2019. 6. 27., and thus Petitioners’ subjective interest in the protection of rights for seeking adjudication regarding the Measure Compelling Attendance at the Religious Events at Issue no longer exists.\\n\\n(2) Furthermore, the Soldiers’ Service Basic Act not only stipulates the duty of the commander to guarantee the religious life of soldiers within the extent that it does not impede the performance of the unit’s mission and the right of soldiers to participate in religious rites conducted at religious facilities, etc. designated by the commander (see Article 15(1) and (2)), but was also amended by Act No. 16034 on 2018. 12. 24. to newly add the express provision that “no soldier shall be compelled to participate in a religious rite or be restricted from participation against his or her will” (Article 15(3)). Therefore, the proposition that compelling attendance at a religious rite against one’s will is not permitted in light of freedom of religion has already been reflected in statute. Accordingly, it is difficult to view that there is a risk that acts compelling attendance at religious events at the Army Training Center will occur several times in the future, or that the necessity for constitutional clarification regarding this point is recognized.\\n\\n(3) In the end, this petition for adjudication lacks an interest in the protection of subjective rights, and even the exceptional interest in adjudication for constitutional clarification is not recognized."}

question:
Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (X) concerning the freedom of occupation? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law)

(a) The former provision of the "Security Services Industry Act" that provides that a person who has been sentenced to a suspended execution of a sentence of imprisonment without prison labor or a heavier punishment and is within the suspension period cannot become a special security guard infringes the freedom of occupation because it requires a private worker special security guard to observe the law and act faithfully at the same level as a public official and thus excessively prioritizes only the public interest.
(b) The provision of the "Passenger Transport Service Act" that mandatorily revokes taxi driver qualifications for a person who committed the offense of forcible indecent act under the "Criminal Act," which constitutes a sexual crime under the "Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment, etc. of Sexual Crimes," and who has been sentenced to a suspended execution of a sentence of imprisonment without prison labor or a heavier punishment and is within the suspension period does not infringe the freedom of occupation.
(c) The provision of the "Infant Care Act" that provides that a person for whom 10 years have not elapsed since the date on which a fine sentence for a child abuse-related crime became final and conclusive may not establish or operate a child care center or work at a child care center does not infringe the freedom of occupation because there is recognized a need to thoroughly protect infants and toddlers in advance from the risk of child abuse.
(d) The provision of the "Act on the Management and Use of Livestock Excreta" that provides that, for an area where it is deemed necessary to restrict livestock breeding, a livestock-raising restriction area may be designated and publicly notified according to what is prescribed by the ordinance of the relevant local government infringes the freedom of occupation by, in effect, prohibiting engagement in the livestock industry in a specific area and rendering the freedom to perform one’s occupation nominal.
(e) The provision of the "Publication Industry Promotion Act" that imposes on sellers of publications the duty to sell at the fixed price and limits the scope of price discounts to no more than 15 percent of the fixed price by combining price discounts and economic benefits does not infringe the freedom of occupation because the extent to which overall consumer welfare is restricted as a result is not large.
