The petitioner completed alien registration on 2016. 6. 16., the status of sojourn is 'Residence (F-2)', and the petitioner's spouse and daughter are also foreigners who have completed alien registration.  \\nThe petitioner applied for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund at the community service center near the place of residence on 2020. 5. 13., but was told by an employee that, pursuant to internal guidelines, the petitioner could not be included in the recipients; and on 2020. 6. 18., the petitioner filled out and submitted an application for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund at the Seowon-dong Community Service Center in Gwanak-gu, Seoul, but the employee of the above community service center rejected the application, stating that foreigners were included among the recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund only in the case of permanent residents and marriage migrants, and that recognized refugees therefore could not be recipients.  \\nAccordingly, the petitioner argued that the inclusion only of permanent residents and marriage migrants among 'households composed solely of foreigners' as recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund, while excluding other foreigners, infringes the petitioner's right to equality and right to a life worthy of human dignity, and on 2020. 8. 11. primarily filed this constitutional complaint against the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's 'Detailed Implementation Plan for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund (Draft)' and, in the alternative, against the jointly issued by relevant ministries 'Criteria for Household Composition and Handling of Objections for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund (Second Round)'.  \\n\\n2. Subject Matter of Adjudication  \\nThe petitioner primarily filed a petition for adjudication against the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's 'Detailed Implementation Plan for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund (Draft)'; however, because the above plan does not include the content concerning the criteria for payment of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund to foreigners that the petitioner disputes, the subject matter of adjudication in this case is fixed as whether the portion concerning 'households composed solely of foreigners' among 'I. Criteria concerning household composition, ⊠ Detailed criteria for household composition' in the jointly issued by relevant ministries on 2020. 5. 13. 'Criteria for Household Composition and Handling of Objections for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund (Second Round)' (hereinafter referred to as the 'Criteria at Issue') infringes the petitioner's fundamental rights. The Criteria at Issue and the relevant provisions are as follows.  \\n[Criteria at Issue]  \\nJointly by Relevant Ministries 'Criteria for Household Composition and Handling of Objections for the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund (Second Round)'  \\nI. Criteria concerning household composition  \\n⊠ Detailed criteria for household composition  \\n○ (Overseas Koreans/Foreigners) Where overseas Korean nationals listed on the resident registration record by household and foreigners listed in households including at least one Korean national are subscribers to, dependents of, or Medical Aid recipients under the same (postpaid) National Health Insurance system as Korean nationals => included in payment recipients  \\n- However, even if the household is composed solely of foreigners, where a permanent resident (F-5) or marriage migrant (F-6) is a subscriber to, dependent of, or Medical Aid recipient under the same (postpaid) National Health Insurance system as Korean nationals* => included in payment recipients  \\n* (Example) Where a foreigner subject to special treatment for permanent residents or marriage migrants and receiving Basic Livelihood Security benefits is residing in a facility due to domestic violence, etc.  \\n\\n[Relevant Provisions]  \\nRefugee Act (enacted by Act No. 11298 on 2012. 2. 10.)  \\nArticle 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters concerning the status and treatment of refugees, etc. in accordance with the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees (hereinafter referred to as the \"Refugee Convention\") and the 1967 Protocol Relating to the Status of Refugees (hereinafter referred to as the \"Refugee Protocol\"), etc.  \\nArticle 30 (Treatment of Recognized Refugees) (1) Notwithstanding any other Act, recognized refugees staying in the Republic of Korea shall receive treatment pursuant to the Refugee Convention.  \\n(2) The State and local governments shall formulate and implement policies concerning the treatment of refugees, improve relevant laws and regulations, provide support to relevant ministries, etc., and take other necessary measures.  \\nArticle 31 (Social Security) Foreigners recognized as refugees and staying in the country shall receive social security at the same level as Korean nationals, notwithstanding Article 8 of the Framework Act on Social Security, etc.  \\nArticle 32 (Basic Livelihood Security) Foreigners recognized as refugees and staying in the country shall, notwithstanding Article 5-2 of the National Basic Livelihood Security Act, receive protection under Articles 7 through 15 of the same Act upon their own application.  \\nArticle 38 (Exclusion of Reciprocity for Recognized Refugees) Reciprocity shall not apply to recognized refugees notwithstanding any other Act.  \\n\\nFramework Act on Treatment of Foreigners Residing in Korea (enacted by Act No. 8442 on 2007. 5. 17.)  \\nArticle 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe basic matters concerning the treatment of foreigners residing in Korea, etc., so that foreigners residing in Korea can adapt to Korean society and fully exercise their individual abilities, and to contribute to the development and social integration of the Republic of Korea by creating a social environment in which Korean nationals and foreigners understand and respect each other.  \\nArticle 2 (Definitions) The definitions of terms used in this Act are as follows.  \\n1. The term \"foreigner residing in Korea\" means a person who does not have the nationality of the Republic of Korea and who is legally staying with the purpose of residing in the Republic of Korea.  \\n2. The term \"treatment of foreigners residing in Korea\" means the State and local governments treating foreigners residing in Korea appropriately according to their legal status.  \\n3. The term \"marriage migrant\" means a foreigner residing in Korea who has been or is in a marital relationship with a Korean national.  \\nArticle 12 (Treatment of Marriage Migrants and Their Children) (1) The State and local governments may support marriage migrants and their children in adapting quickly to Korean society through Korean language education, education on the institutions and culture of the Republic of Korea, childcare and educational support for the children of marriage migrants, medical support, etc.  \\nArticle 13 (Treatment of Permanent Residents) (1) The State and local governments may guarantee, to foreigners who have the legal status to reside permanently in the Republic of Korea (hereinafter referred to as \"permanent residents\"), entry into, stay in, or economic activities within the Republic of Korea, within the scope that does not harm the national security, maintenance of order, public welfare, or other interests of the Republic of Korea.  \\n(2) Article 12(1) shall apply mutatis mutandis to permanent residents.  \\n\\nFramework Act on Treatment of Foreigners Residing in Korea (amended by Act No. 11298 on 2012. 2. 10.)  \\nArticle 14 (Treatment of Refugees) (1) Where a refugee recognized pursuant to the Refugee Act wishes to reside in the Republic of Korea, support may be provided by applying mutatis mutandis Article 12(1).  \\n\\n3. Petitioner’s Arguments  \\nAlthough the economic blow caused by the worldwide spread of the infectious disease known as 'Coronavirus Disease-19' is universally borne not only by Korean nationals but also by foreigners staying in Korea, the Criteria at Issue, by including among foreigners only permanent residents and marriage migrants as recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund, infringes the petitioner's right to equality and right to a life worthy of human dignity as a recognized refugee.  \\n\\n4. Determination on the Requirements for Admissibility  \\nA. The status of foreigners as holders of fundamental rights  \\n\"Nationals\" or \"foreigners\" in a status similar to that of nationals may be holders of fundamental rights. The dignity and value of the human being, and the right to pursue happiness, are generally human rights, and foreigners should also be regarded as capable of being holders thereof; the right to equality is also a human right, with only inherent limitations on suffrage, etc. and limitations according to reciprocity (see Constitutional Court Decision 1994. 12. 29. 93HEONMA120; Constitutional Court Decision 2001. 11. 29. 99HEONMA494).  \\nThe Criteria at Issue include permanent residents and marriage migrants among foreigners as recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund while excluding recognized refugees therefrom; since the question in this case is whether such discriminatory treatment among foreigners infringes the right to equality, this is not a case where limitations are imposed by the nature of fundamental rights or where reciprocity is at issue, and the petitioner may be recognized as a holder of fundamental rights in this case (see Constitutional Court Decision 2014. 4. 24. 2011HEONMA474 et al.).  \\n\\nB. Exercise of public power  \\nThe Criteria at Issue are administrative rules; administrative rules generally have effect only within the administrative organization, but when an administrative rule is issued by law to grant an administrative agency authority to supplement the specific content of the law, or when a rule serving as a standard for the exercise of discretionary power is repeatedly implemented in accordance with its terms so that an administrative practice is established, it acquires external binding force in cases where, pursuant to the principle of equality or the principle of protection of trust, the administrative agency becomes subject to self-binding in relation to the other party and must follow the rule; in such cases, it may be the subject of a constitutional complaint (see Constitutional Court Decision 2001. 5. 31. 99HEONMA413).  \\nIt is appropriate to regard the Criteria at Issue as an administrative rule having the nature of a discretionary standard. The Criteria at Issue present internally and externally the standards regarding in what cases foreigners are included among recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund; the local governments that are the direct counterparts to the Criteria at Issue have, in substance, no choice but to process the affairs of paying the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund in accordance with the Criteria at Issue, and in this case too, the reason the Seowon-dong Community Service Center in Gwanak-gu, Seoul refused to pay the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund to the petitioner was that the petitioner did not fall under a permanent resident or marriage migrant designated as a recipient under the Criteria at Issue.  \\nIf so, the Criteria at Issue may be the subject of a constitutional complaint as an \"exercise of public power\" with external binding force.  \\n\\nC. Interest in protection of rights  \\nBecause payment of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund has ended, there is room to view that, regardless of whether the Criteria at Issue are unconstitutional, relief of the petitioner's rights is impossible and the subjective interest in protection of rights has already been extinguished.  \\nHowever, in the future, in the event of a re-spread of Coronavirus Disease-19 and in the face of other disasters, there is a possibility that support funds of the same kind as the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund will be paid, and in such a case, criteria identical or similar to the Criteria at Issue may be applied, making it likely that the exclusion of recognized refugees such as the petitioner from among foreigners belonging to households composed solely of foreigners will be repeated.  \\nThis matter may be seen as requiring constitutional clarification in relation to whether the right to equality has been infringed, and since this Court has not yet provided constitutional clarification on this point, the interest in adjudication may be recognized.  \\n\\n5. Overview  \\nA. Background and process of payment of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund  \\nDue to the spread of Coronavirus Disease-19 (hereinafter referred to as \"COVID-19\") in 2020 and the resulting contraction in consumer sentiment, etc., the Government came to prepare cash support measures in order to assist citizens who suffered economic damage. Initially, the Government announced that it would pay an Emergency Disaster Relief Fund of KRW 1,000,000 for a four-person household to the bottom 70% by income, but thereafter, through consultations between the ruling party and the Government, etc., it decided on a plan to pay all citizens. On 2020. 4. 29., when the National Assembly passed the second supplementary budget bill for the payment of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund, the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund was paid to all citizens in the form of a prepaid card, credit card points, local gift certificates, etc. from May 2020 and ended on 2020. 8. 31.  \\nThe petitioner is a case of exclusion from the above payment of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund for May 2020 targeting all citizens, and thereafter the Government carried out several more rounds of selective payment of Emergency Disaster Relief Funds targeting specific groups such as small business owners and crisis households. The Emergency Disaster Relief Fund paid to all citizens in May 2020 is ordinarily referred to as the \"First Emergency Disaster Relief Fund,\" and various Emergency Disaster Relief Funds subsequently paid several times are also referred to by numbering them as the second, third, etc., but hereinafter the first Emergency Disaster Relief Fund relevant to the petitioner will be referred to simply as the \"Emergency Disaster Relief Fund\" without specifying the number.  \\n\\nB. Status of recognized refugees  \\n(1) A person who flees the country of origin due to political persecution and escapes to a third country is generally called a \"refugee,\" and because such persons may face the risk of persecution or threats to life if they return to the country of origin, the international community bears the obligation to protect refugees.  \\nThe Republic of Korea ratified the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees and the 1967 Protocol Relating to the Status of Refugees in 1992, enacted the Refugee Act in February 2012, and has been implementing it since July 2013.  \\n(2) Under the Refugee Act, a \"refugee\" means a foreigner who, owing to a well-founded fear of being persecuted for reasons of race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group, or political opinion, is unable or unwilling to avail himself or herself of the protection of the country of nationality, or a stateless foreigner who, owing to such fear, is unable or unwilling to return to, or avail himself or herself of the protection of, the country of habitual residence where he or she resided before entering the Republic of Korea (Article 2(1) of the Refugee Act).  \\nRefugees in the Republic of Korea under the Refugee Act are divided into \"recognized refugees\" (Article 2(2)) and \"refugee applicants\" (Article 2(4)); and a foreigner who is not a refugee under the Refugee Act but who has reasonable grounds to believe that his or her life, bodily freedom, etc. may be substantially infringed due to inhuman treatment or punishment such as torture or other circumstances, and who has obtained permission to stay from the Minister of Justice as prescribed by Presidential Decree, is referred to as a \"humanitarian sojourn permit holder\" (Article 2(3)).  \\nThe Refugee Act contains separate protective provisions for \"recognized refugees,\" \"refugee applicants,\" and \"humanitarian sojourn permit holders,\" and among them, \"recognized refugees\" receive the most substantial protection with respect to status of sojourn, social security, and basic livelihood.  \\nFirst, recognized refugees staying in the Republic of Korea receive treatment pursuant to the Refugee Convention notwithstanding any other Act (Article 30(1) of the Refugee Act), are granted the status of sojourn \"Residence (F-2)\" and a sojourn period of 3 years while staying in the country (renewable), and as a rule are not subject to restrictions on employment activities under Article 23 of the Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Control Act.  \\nIn addition, foreigners recognized as refugees and staying in the country receive social security at the same level as Korean nationals, notwithstanding Article 8 of the Framework Act on Social Security, etc. (Article 31 of the Refugee Act), and, notwithstanding Article 5-2 of the National Basic Livelihood Security Act, receive protection under Articles 7 through 15 of the same Act upon their own application (Article 32 of the Refugee Act). Furthermore, if a recognized refugee or his or her child is a minor under the Civil Act, they receive elementary and secondary education the same as Korean nationals (Article 33(1) of the Refugee Act), and may also have their academic level corresponding to the degree of school education completed abroad recognized pursuant to Presidential Decree (Article 35 of the Refugee Act). The Minister of Justice may provide recognized refugees with education for social adaptation, such as Korean language education, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and, if a recognized refugee so desires, may provide support so that he or she may receive vocational training as prescribed by Presidential Decree (Article 34 of the Refugee Act); and where the spouse or minor child of a recognized refugee applies for entry, entry shall be permitted unless the case falls under Article 11 of the Immigration Control Act (Article 37(1) of the Refugee Act). Article 38 of the Refugee Act provides that reciprocity shall not apply to recognized refugees notwithstanding any other Act.  \\nMeanwhile, the Framework Act on Treatment of Foreigners Residing in Korea (Article 1, Article 2(1)), which prescribes basic matters concerning the treatment of \"foreigners residing in Korea,\" meaning persons who do not have the nationality of the Republic of Korea and are legally staying with the purpose of residing in the Republic of Korea, also contains provisions regarding \"recognized refugees\" under the Refugee Act. First, it provides that, with respect to \"marriage migrants,\" meaning foreigners residing in Korea who have been or are in a marital relationship with a Korean national, support may be provided to enable marriage migrants and their children to adapt quickly to Korean society through Korean language education, education on the institutions and culture of the Republic of Korea, childcare and educational support for the children of marriage migrants, medical support, etc. (Article 12(1), Article 2(3)); it further provides that Article 12(1) shall apply mutatis mutandis to \"permanent residents,\" meaning foreigners who have the legal status to reside permanently in the Republic of Korea (Article 13(1), (2)); and it also provides that, where a \"recognized refugee\" under the Refugee Act wishes to reside in the Republic of Korea, support may be provided by applying mutatis mutandis Article 12(1) (Article 14(1)).  \\n\\n6. Determination on the Merits  \\nA. Organization of the issues  \\n(1) We first examine whether the Criteria at Issue, which include only permanent residents and marriage migrants among foreigners as recipients of the disaster relief fund and exclude recognized refugees, infringe the petitioner's right to equality in relation to permanent residents and marriage migrants.  \\n(2) The petitioner argues that the provision subject to adjudication also infringes the petitioner's right to a life worthy of human dignity as a recognized refugee; however, this is ultimately no different from the argument that it is manifestly irrational to pay the disaster relief fund to permanent residents and marriage migrants while not paying it to recognized refugees, and thus, insofar as the question of infringement of the right to equality is determined, we do not separately determine this point.  \\n\\nB. Whether the right to equality has been infringed  \\n(1) Generally, the principle of equality requires that things that are essentially the same be treated equally and things that are essentially different be treated differently; it does not mean absolute equality denying all discriminatory treatment, but rather relative equality excluding discrimination that lacks a rational basis in legislation and application of law; therefore, discrimination with a rational basis does not run counter to the principle of equality (see Constitutional Court Decision 2001. 6. 28. 99HEONMA516; Constitutional Court Decision 2003. 12. 18. 2001HEONBA91; Constitutional Court Decision 2016. 3. 31. 2014HEONMA367).  \\n(2) The Emergency Disaster Relief Fund is a one-time and benevolent support fund, and policies of this kind of state support may, by comprehensively considering various reasons such as the purpose of the support policy, fiscal burden, and administrative reasons, be implemented targeting some of the people residing in the country; the matter of determining the scope of persons to whom such support fund policies apply may be said to be an area in which the State is afforded broad discretion.  \\nHowever, the fact that the Criteria at Issue include only \"permanent residents and marriage migrants\" among foreigners as recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund and exclude \"recognized refugees\" cannot be regarded as having a rational basis for the following reasons.  \\n(3) First, there can be no difference among permanent residents, marriage migrants, and recognized refugees in that they all suffered economic damage due to COVID-19; therefore, it cannot be said that there is also a difference in eligibility to be recipients of the support fund for recovery.  \\n\"Permanent residents and marriage migrants\" lawfully stay in Korea for the purpose of permanent residence or long-term residence, and \"recognized refugees\" also receive protection from the Republic of Korea pursuant to the obligation of non-refoulement, lawfully stay in the Republic of Korea, and are not subject to restrictions on employment activities; in this respect, it is difficult to see any difference from permanent residents and marriage migrants. Foreigners residing in the Republic of Korea are, as a rule, taxpayers; and even in light of the fact that \"recognized refugees\" also reside in the Republic of Korea, engage in work and economic activities, bear national taxes such as earned income tax and comprehensive income tax, and local taxes such as resident tax, property tax, and automobile tax, and contribute to part of our finances, there is no reason to exclude \"recognized refugees\" from the recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund differently from permanent residents and marriage migrants.  \\nThe Framework Act on Treatment of Foreigners Residing in Korea (hereinafter referred to as the \"Foreigners Treatment Act\"), which prescribes the basic matters concerning the treatment of \"foreigners residing in Korea,\" meaning persons who do not have the nationality of the Republic of Korea and are legally staying with the purpose of residing in the Republic of Korea (Article 1, Article 2(1)), defines the \"treatment of foreigners residing in Korea\" as the State and local governments treating foreigners residing in Korea appropriately according to their legal status (Article 2(2)).  \\nAs seen above, the Foreigners Treatment Act enables support for \"marriage migrants,\" meaning foreigners residing in Korea who have been or are in a marital relationship with a Korean national, so that marriage migrants and their children may quickly adapt to Korean society through Korean language education, education on the institutions and culture of the Republic of Korea, childcare and educational support for the children of marriage migrants, medical support, etc. (Article 12(1), Article 2(3)); it also applies Article 12(1) mutatis mutandis to \"permanent residents,\" meaning foreigners who have the legal status to reside permanently in the Republic of Korea (Article 13(1), (2)); and further provides that, where a \"recognized refugee\" under the Refugee Act wishes to reside in the Republic of Korea, support may be provided by applying mutatis mutandis Article 12(1) (Article 14(1)). From this, it can be seen that the Foreigners Treatment Act, the basic statute on the treatment of foreigners residing in Korea, recognizes \"marriage migrants,\" \"permanent residents,\" and \"recognized refugees\" among foreigners residing in Korea as subjects who are to receive the same treatment despite their differing legal statuses.  \\n(4) Meanwhile, from 1994 through the end of June 2023, there were 93,270 refugee applicants, of whom 1,381 were recognized as refugees; thus, it cannot be said that providing the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund to \"recognized refugees\" would cause serious financial difficulty.  \\nIn addition, because the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund is paid per household, there may be an argument that it is difficult to include \"recognized refugees\" among the recipients due to the practical problem that family relationship proof is difficult; however, in the case of \"recognized refugees,\" one may also consider the method of paying the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund not on a household basis but targeting the \"recognized refugee\" him- or herself, so the administrative reason that proof of family relationship is difficult likewise cannot constitute a rational reason to exclude \"recognized refugees\" from the recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund.  \\n(5) If so, because the Criteria at Issue include \"permanent residents and marriage migrants\" among foreigners as recipients of the Emergency Disaster Relief Fund while excluding \"recognized refugees,\" this constitutes discrimination lacking a rational basis; therefore, the Criteria at Issue infringe the petitioner's right to equality.  \\n\\n7. Conclusion  \\nSince the Criteria at Issue are in violation of the Constitution, the decision is made as stated in the disposition with the unanimous opinion of all participating Justices."}

question:
Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (X) regarding marriage and family life? (In case of dispute, based on case law)

(a) The parents’ right not to be interfered with by the State in accessing information about the sex of a fetus who will become a future member of the family is protected by the general personality right derived from Article 10 of the Constitution.  
(b) A provision of the Act on the Registration, etc. of Family Relationships that does not provide for allowing the biological father to file the birth registration of a child born between a married woman and a man other than her husband directly restricts the biological father’s custodial right with respect to a child born outside marriage.  
(c) The guarantee of marriage and family life prescribed in Article 36(1) of the Constitution means that, negatively, it protects the individual’s subjective right of defense against unjust infringement by State power by prohibiting State power from infringing upon the private sphere of marriage and family, and, positively, it means not only that the State must protect marriage and family from third parties, etc., but also that it imposes on the State the task of realizing a marriage and family system established and maintained on the basis of human dignity and equality of the sexes.  
(d) Since Articles 34 and 36 of the Constitution impose on the State the task of protecting family life and striving to improve the welfare of juveniles, even the interpretation of these constitutional provisions alone gives rise to a legislative duty to enact specific systems for effectively securing the performance of child support obligations, such as a child-support advance payment system.  
(e) The “right to be registered at birth,” immediately upon being born, is a right to have basic information relating to a child’s birth registered so that the State may manage such information at the “earliest possible point at which the child can be protected after birth,” and is an independent fundamental right not expressly provided for in the Constitution that has both the character of a liberty right guaranteeing the free realization of personality and the character of a social fundamental right guaranteeing a child’s healthy growth and development.
