Petitioner’s Arguments\\na. Article 32(1) of the Resource Circulation Act delegates to Presidential Decree matters concerning “facilities, equipment, etc.” among the registration standards for waste automobile recycling business. However, since the provisions at issue prescribe as a registration standard the requirement of “obtaining approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under Article 29(2) of the Waste Control Act or filing a report of installation,” which is unrelated to “facilities, equipment, etc.,” they exceed the scope of delegation under the Act and violate the principle of statutory reservation.\\nb. Although the facility standard provision at issue applies even where registration for waste automobile recycling business has been completed pursuant to the former statutes, if the newly established registration standards under the provisions at issue are not satisfied, it fundamentally makes the use of energy recovery facilities installed at enormous cost impossible; thus, it violates the principle against excessive restriction and infringes the Petitioner’s freedom of occupation.\\nc. Since the facility standard provision at issue newly requires energy recovery facilities installed and used pursuant to the former statutes to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under the Waste Control Act or to file a report of installation, it infringes the Petitioner’s property right through retroactive legislation. Even if the facility standard provision at issue does not constitute retroactive legislation, it infringes the Petitioner’s property right in violation of the principle of protection of trust because it does not provide an appropriate transitional measure to protect businesses that registered for waste automobile recycling business in reliance on the public view of the Minister of Environment that the facilities at issue do not constitute waste treatment facilities under the Waste Control Act.\\nd. Since the facility standard provision at issue requires approval for installation or a report of installation under the Waste Control Act only for facilities using crushed residue, it discriminates without reasonable grounds between operators of solid fuel product use facilities and operators of crushed residue use facilities. In addition, because the facility standard provision at issue restricts only the business of operators who installed crushed residue use facilities in places where waste treatment facilities cannot be installed, such as the Petitioner, and does not restrict the business of operators who installed crushed residue use facilities in places where waste treatment facilities can be installed, it treats persons who registered for crushed residue recycling business differently without reasonable grounds. Therefore, the facility standard provision at issue violates the principle of equality.\\ne. Since the addenda provision at issue imposes on persons who completed registration for waste automobile recycling business pursuant to the former statutes the duty to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or to file a report of installation, while granting only a three-year grace period, it violates the principle of protection of trust and infringes the Petitioner’s freedom of occupation.\\n\\n4. Overview of the Waste Automobile Recycling Business System\\na. Recycling of Waste Automobiles\\nThe Resource Circulation Act aims to contribute to the conservation of the environment and the sound development of the national economy by establishing a resource circulation system that efficiently utilizes resources by suppressing the use of hazardous substances, manufacturing products so as to facilitate recycling, and ensuring appropriate recycling of their waste, for the purpose of promoting the recycling of electrical and electronic equipment and vehicles (Article 1). In order to minimize the harm that waste automobiles cause to the environment, the Resource Circulation Act imposes legal restrictions, from the manufacturing and import stage of automobiles, to comply with standards for the content of hazardous substances such as heavy metals and flame retardants, which have a high degree of harm to the environment, as prescribed by Presidential Decree (see Article 9). Meanwhile, waste automobiles are recycled through the processes of automobile dismantling, crushing, and treatment of crushed residue, and automobile dismantling and recycling business operators, crushing and recycling business operators, and crushed residue recycling business operators must comply with the recycling ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree (see Article 25(1)) and recycle waste automobiles or facilitate recycling in accordance with the methods and standards prescribed by Presidential Decree (see Article 26).\\nb. Registration of Waste Automobile Recycling Business\\nWaste automobile recycling business under the Resource Circulation Act means business concerning recycling of residual parts, etc. of waste automobiles (see Article 32(1)). Waste automobile recycling business is divided into crushing and recycling business and crushed residue recycling business. Crushing and recycling business means business of crushing and recycling the residual parts of waste automobiles handed over from waste automobile dismantling and recycling business operators, and crushed residue recycling business means business of recycling crushed residue handed over from crushing and recycling business operators or recovering energy therefrom (see Article 32(2)).\\nA person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business shall register with the Minister of Environment by securing the registration standards for facilities, equipment, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree (Article 32(1)). The Minister of Environment shall grant registration unless the applicant does not satisfy the registration standards prescribed by Presidential Decree or has any disqualifying grounds prescribed by the Resource Circulation Act, or unless the registration would violate restrictions under the Resource Circulation Act or other statutes (Article 32(4)).\\nWith respect to the “registration standards for facilities, equipment, etc.,” Article 30 [Attached Table 7-3] of the Enforcement Decree of the Resource Circulation Act requires a person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business to possess conveyance/input facilities or equipment, storage facilities, and weighing facilities as essential facilities. A person who intends to engage in crushed residue recycling business must, in addition to the above facilities, possess a sorting facility capable of sorting out foreign substances such as metal pieces and soil, and as optional facilities must possess at least one of an energy recovery facility, oil manufacturing facility, or other crushed residue recycling facilities recognized by the Minister of Environment; in the case of an energy recovery facility, all of the detailed standards that it must be “a facility for which approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under Article 29(2) of the Waste Control Act has been obtained or which has been reported as installed” and “a waste incineration heat recovery facility or incineration facility that meets the energy recovery standards under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Resource Circulation Act” must be satisfied [see the facility standard provision at issue and Article 30 [Attached Table 7-3] 2(b) 2) (b) of the Enforcement Decree of the Resource Circulation Act]. Where a person who has registered waste automobile recycling business fails to secure the above facilities and equipment, the Minister of Environment may revoke the registration or order suspension of all or part of the business for a period not exceeding six months (see Article 34(1)4 of the Resource Circulation Act).\\nc. Approval for Installation and Installation Report of Waste Treatment Facilities under the Waste Control Act\\nA “waste treatment facility” means a facility prescribed by Presidential Decree as an intermediate disposal facility, final disposal facility, or recycling facility for waste (Article 2 subparagraph 8 of the Waste Control Act). Article 5 [Attached Table 3] of the Enforcement Decree of the Waste Control Act classifies incineration facilities as intermediate disposal facilities, and since Article 30 [Attached Table 7-3] 2(b) 2) (b) of the Enforcement Decree of the Resource Circulation Act provides, with respect to an energy recovery facility, that it shall be “a waste incineration heat recovery facility or incineration facility that meets the energy recovery standards under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Resource Circulation Act,” an energy recovery facility under the Resource Circulation Act can be viewed as corresponding to an intermediate disposal facility among waste treatment facilities.\\nWaste treatment facilities shall be installed and operated in accordance with the standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment (Article 29(1) of the Waste Control Act), and a person other than one who has obtained, or seeks to obtain, a license for waste treatment business under Article 25(3) of the Waste Control Act shall, in order to install a waste treatment facility, obtain approval from the Minister of Environment or file a report of installation (Article 29(2) of the Waste Control Act). A person who installs and operates a waste treatment facility shall undergo periodic inspections by a waste treatment facility inspection agency (Articles 30(1) and (2) of the Waste Control Act) and shall maintain and manage the facility in accordance with the management standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment (Article 31(1) of the Waste Control Act).\\nd. History and Legislative Purpose of the Provisions at Issue\\nArticle 2 subparagraph 7(b) of the Waste Control Act and Article 3(1)1(b) of the Enforcement Rule of the same Act pursuant to its delegation recognize as “energy recovery” under the Waste Control Act a case where the energy recovery efficiency (meaning the ratio obtained by dividing the total amount of recovered energy by the total amount of input energy) is at least 75%, whereas Article 2 subparagraph 7 of the Resource Circulation Act and Article 2 subparagraph 1 of the Enforcement Rule of the same Act pursuant to its delegation recognize energy recovery under the Resource Circulation Act where the energy recovery efficiency is at least 60%.\\nArticle 32(1) of the former Resource Circulation Act (as amended by Act No. 11913 on 2013. 7. 16., and before amendment by Act No. 15657 on 2018. 6. 12.) provided that a person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business shall secure facilities prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment and register with the Minister of Environment according to the business classification under paragraph (2), and Article 16 [Attached Table 3] 1(b) 2) (a) of the Enforcement Rule of the same Act pursuant to such delegation (as amended by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment No. 534 on 2013. 12. 31., and before amendment by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment No. 811 on 2019. 6. 12.) provided, with respect to an energy recovery facility, that it shall be “a facility capable of complying with the energy recovery standards under Article 2 of the Resource Circulation Act,” so registration for waste automobile recycling business was possible by securing an energy recovery facility with energy recovery efficiency of at least 60%. The legislative purpose of this was to facilitate the installation of energy recovery facilities, which are facilities for using crushed residue, thereby addressing the shortage of landfill sites caused by landfill of crushed residue and the problems of soil pollution and water pollution caused by hazardous substances such as heavy metals and Freon gas.\\nHowever, the Resource Circulation Act amended by Act No. 15657 on 2018. 6. 12. provides in Article 32(1) that a person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business shall register with the Minister of Environment by securing the registration standards for facilities, equipment, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree according to the business classification under paragraph (2) of the same Article, and pursuant to such delegation, the Enforcement Decree of the Resource Circulation Act amended by Presidential Decree No. 29843 on 2019. 6. 11. introduced the facility standard provision at issue, thereby requiring even energy recovery facilities under the Resource Circulation Act to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under the Waste Control Act or file a report of installation; and by introducing the addenda provision at issue, it strengthened the installation standards for energy recovery facilities by requiring persons who registered for crushed residue recycling business under the former statutes also to satisfy the registration standards prescribed by the facility standard provision at issue within three years from the time the facility standard provision at issue took effect. This was intended to address problems such as air pollution and harm to the human body caused by hazardous substances generated in the incineration process of crushed residue, and it can be said that the purpose of the amendment was to eliminate the environmental regulatory vacuum under the former statutes.\\n\\n5. Determination\\na. Issues\\n(1) The provisions at issue impose on persons who have completed registration for waste automobile recycling business under the former Resource Circulation Act and its subordinate statutes the duty to obtain again, within a certain period, approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or to file a report of installation under the Waste Control Act. Thus, they restrict the freedom of occupation of waste automobile recycling business operators.\\n(2) However, Article 32(1) of the Resource Circulation Act delegates matters concerning the “registration standards for facilities, equipment, etc.”, and thus it is examined whether the provisions at issue exceed the scope of delegation under the enabling Act and violate the principle of statutory reservation.\\n(3) In addition, because the facility standard provision at issue imposes on persons who intend to register for waste automobile recycling business the duty to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or to file a report of installation under the Waste Control Act, it is examined whether the facility standard provision at issue violates the principle against excessive restriction.\\n(4) The addenda provision at issue provides that a person who has registered for waste automobile recycling business according to the relaxed registration standards under the former statutes and who has not obtained a license for waste treatment business under Article 25(3) of the Waste Control Act shall be deemed to have satisfied the registration standards for waste automobile recycling business until the day three years have passed from 2019. 6. 13., the effective date of the Enforcement Decree of the Resource Circulation Act amended by Presidential Decree No. 29843 on 2019. 6. 11., and shall obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or file a report of installation under Article 29(2) of the Waste Control Act within that period. It is examined whether the addenda provision at issue violates the principle of protection of trust.\\n(5) The Petitioner argues that, although it invested enormous costs to install energy recovery facilities, the facility standard provision at issue added facility standards that cannot be supplemented afterward, making it impossible to use all or part of the energy recovery facilities for business, and thereby causing losses from business suspension or closure, so the facility standard provision at issue infringes the Petitioner’s property right by violating the principle prohibiting retroactive legislation.\\nHowever, since the property right guaranteed by the Constitution is a specific right with economic value that encompasses private utility and the principle right of disposal over it, a mere opportunity for profit that is not a specific right, or the factual and legal conditions for business activity, is not protected as property right (see Constitutional Court Decision 2020. 6. 25. 2018HEONMA974). The facility standard provision at issue imposes on energy recovery facilities the duty to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or file a report of installation under the Waste Control Act, and Article 34(1)4 of the Resource Circulation Act merely anticipates revocation of registration or suspension of all or part of business in the event that such standards are not satisfied; therefore, business suspension or closure resulting therefrom does not fall within the scope of property rights under Article 23 of the Constitution (see Constitutional Court Decision 2020. 6. 25. 2018HEONMA974). Accordingly, this part of the argument is not further considered.\\n(6) The Petitioner argues that the facility standard provision at issue discriminates without reasonable grounds between solid fuel product use facilities and crushed residue use facilities, thereby infringing the Petitioner’s right to equality. However, solid fuel products are recycled products manufactured in accordance with the quality standards prescribed by the Resource Circulation Act and are substances different in nature from unprocessed crushed residue. Thus, even if the provisions at issue set registration standards different from those applicable to energy recovery facilities using solid fuel products, it is difficult to view this as discrimination among groups where equality is at issue; therefore, this part of the argument is not further considered.\\nThe Petitioner also argues, to the effect that the facility standard provision at issue treats equally persons who can obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or file a report of installation for energy recovery facilities after the fact and persons who cannot, and thus violates the principle of equality; however, this is no different from arguing that the provisions at issue excessively restrict the freedom of occupation, and insofar as the issue of infringement of the freedom of occupation is being determined, this part of the argument is not separately considered.\\n\\nb. Whether the Provisions at Issue Violate the Principle of Statutory Reservation\\n(1) Under Article 37(2) of the Constitution, the fundamental rights of the people may be restricted only when necessary for national security, maintenance of order, or public welfare; however, in principle, the method of such restriction is possible only by statute. Here, the principle of statutory reservation concerning the restriction of fundamental rights requires regulation based on statute; therefore, even if the form need not necessarily be a statute, there must be a legal basis in statute. Accordingly, subordinate statutes that exceed the scope of delegation from the enabling Act are without statutory basis and violate the principle of statutory reservation (see Constitutional Court Decision 2012. 5. 31. 2010HEONMA139 et seq.).\\n(2) Article 32(1) of the Resource Circulation Act states, “A person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business shall, in accordance with the business classification under paragraph (2), register with the Minister of Environment by securing the registration standards for facilities, equipment, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree,” thereby delegating to Presidential Decree, a subordinate statute, various registration standards that cannot be detailed in the statute with respect to the facilities, equipment, etc. possessed by a person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business. Pursuant to such delegation, the provisions at issue regulate matters concerning energy recovery facilities possessed by waste automobile recycling business operators. An energy recovery facility is one of the facilities that a person who intends to register for crushed residue recycling business among waste automobile recycling businesses may possess, and the provisions at issue prescribe that such facility shall be “a facility for which approval for installation or a report of installation under the Waste Control Act has been made”; thus, the provisions at issue specify matters concerning the “facilities” to be secured in order to engage in waste automobile recycling business.\\n(3) While formally setting the facility standards for energy recovery facilities, the provisions at issue in substance require waste automobile recycling business operators to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility, thereby ensuring that the environmental regulatory standards under the Waste Control Act also apply to energy recovery facilities under the Resource Circulation Act.\\nHowever, Article 3 of the Resource Circulation Act explicitly states that “This Act shall take precedence over other Acts with respect to the promotion of recycling of electrical and electronic equipment and vehicles,” making clear that, with respect to “promotion of recycling,” the Resource Circulation Act takes precedence over other Acts.\\nNevertheless, because Article 1 of the Waste Control Act provides that “The purpose of this Act is to contribute to environmental conservation and the qualitative improvement of the lives of the people by minimizing the generation of waste and environmentally soundly treating generated waste,” the Waste Control Act may be said to have the status of a general Act with respect to environmental conservation through environmentally sound treatment of all waste.\\nMeanwhile, Article 2 subparagraph 1 of the Waste Control Act defines “waste” as “substances no longer needed for human life or business activities,” Article 2 subparagraph 5-3 defines “treatment” as “collection, transportation, storage, recycling, and disposal of waste,” and Article 2 subparagraph 7 defines as “recycling” both “activities of reusing or recycling waste, or of making it reusable or recyclable” and “activities of recovering energy under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Energy Act from waste, or of making it recoverable, or activities of using waste as fuel as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment.” Thus, the activity of incinerating crushed residue to recover energy also falls under the “treatment” of “waste” under the Waste Control Act. Ultimately, even facilities for recycling under the Resource Circulation Act, if they are facilities used for the “treatment” of “waste,” may be viewed as being subject to the Waste Control Act with respect to environmental conservation through environmentally sound treatment of waste.\\nAccordingly, it is difficult to view the legislative content as having exceeded the scope of delegation under the enabling Act merely because the provisions at issue, even for energy recovery facilities under the Resource Circulation Act, require approval for installation or a report of installation under the Waste Control Act and thereby ensure compliance with the environmental regulatory standards under the Waste Control Act.\\n(4) If this is the case, the provisions at issue fall within the scope of delegation under Article 32(1) of the Resource Circulation Act and do not violate the principle of statutory reservation so as to infringe the Petitioner’s freedom of occupation.\\n\\nc. Whether the Facility Standard Provision at Issue Violates the Principle Against Excessive Restriction\\n(1) Legitimacy of Purpose and Suitability of Means\\nArticle 9 of the Resource Circulation Act provides that a person who intends to manufacture or import automobiles shall, from the manufacturing or import stage of automobiles, comply with the standards for the content of hazardous substances such as heavy metals and flame retardants, which have a high degree of harm to the environment. However, not only at the manufacturing or import stage of automobiles but also in the process of recycling waste automobiles, substances harmful to the environment or the human body may still be generated. The facility standard provision at issue requires a person who intends to engage in crushed residue recycling business to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or file a report of installation with respect to energy recovery facilities under the Waste Control Act, thereby ensuring that the environmental regulatory standards under the Waste Control Act also apply to energy recovery facilities under the Resource Circulation Act. This is intended to preserve the environment and qualitatively improve the lives of the people by blocking harmful substances generated in the recycling process of crushed residue, and its legislative purpose is legitimate. Moreover, if approval for installation of a waste treatment facility is obtained or a report of installation is filed with respect to energy recovery facilities, the recycling ratio of automobiles can be increased and a resource circulation system can be established; thus, it is a suitable means to achieve the above legislative purpose.\\n(2) Minimum Restriction\\n(a) Article 32(1) of the former Resource Circulation Act (as amended by Act No. 11913 on 2013. 7. 16., and before amendment by Act No. 15657 on 2018. 6. 12.) provided that a person who intends to engage in waste automobile recycling business shall secure facilities prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment and register with the Minister of Environment, and Article 16 [Attached Table 3] 1(b) 2) (a) of the Enforcement Rule of the same Act pursuant to such delegation (as amended by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment No. 534 on 2013. 12. 31., and before amendment by Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment No. 811 on 2019. 6. 12.) provided that registration for crushed residue recycling business may be made where the energy recovery facility possessed by the operator falls under a “facility capable of complying with the energy recovery standards under Article 2 of the Resource Circulation Act.”\\nHowever, as discussed above, although waste automobiles correspond to “waste” under Article 2 subparagraph 1 of the Waste Control Act, and the activity of recovering energy by incinerating crushed residue corresponds to the “treatment” of waste under Article 2 subparagraphs 5-3 and 7 of the Waste Control Act, the former Resource Circulation Act and the former Enforcement Rule of the Resource Circulation Act did not contain clear provisions on whether energy recovery facilities using crushed residue constitute waste treatment facilities under the Waste Control Act. Since hazardous substances harmful to the environment and the human body may be generated in the process of recovering energy by incinerating crushed residue, quality control of crushed residue and environmentally sound management of facilities using crushed residue are important. In particular, because the heat from incinerating crushed residue is increasingly important and utilized as a renewable energy source, such as being recovered and used to supply steam or for power generation, environmental regulation of such facilities is indispensable even for sustainable development of the waste automobile recycling business.\\nAccordingly, Article 32(1) of the Resource Circulation Act, as amended by Act No. 15657 on 2018. 6. 12., provides that the registration standards for facilities, equipment, etc. to be secured by a waste automobile recycling business operator shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the facility standard provision at issue pursuant to such delegation requires energy recovery facilities to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under Article 29(2) of the Waste Control Act or file a report of installation, thereby applying by analogy the environmental regulatory standards under the Waste Control Act also to energy recovery facilities under the Resource Circulation Act.\\n(b) Meanwhile, restrictions on the location of waste treatment facilities under the Waste Control Act, the Clean Air Conservation Act, and the Act on Industrial Location and Development are intended to contribute to important public interests such as environmental conservation, prevention of harm to health and the environment, and balanced national land development, while at the same time protecting the interests of third parties such as the health and environmental rights of nearby residents. In particular, in the case of facilities such as the facility at issue that recover energy such as incineration heat by incinerating waste, air pollutants may be generated and may seriously harm the air environment of the surrounding area and the health of residents; thus, even if only ex post measures such as periodic inspection or facility management are used without preemptively restricting their location, it is difficult to view such measures as sufficient to achieve the legislative purpose. Therefore, requiring persons who install and operate energy recovery facilities to obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility or file a report of installation cannot be viewed as excessive.\\nAccordingly, the facility standard provision at issue does not violate the principle of minimum restriction.\\n(3) Balance of Legal Interests\\nThe facility standard provision at issue adds, with respect to energy recovery facilities, the registration standard that the facility must be “a facility for which approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under the Waste Control Act has been obtained or which has been reported as installed,” and the facility at issue possessed by the Petitioner was installed at a place where a waste treatment facility cannot be installed, so there exists a circumstance in which approval for installation of a waste treatment facility cannot be obtained and no report of installation can be filed. Thus, the business loss that the Petitioner will suffer due to the facility standard provision at issue cannot be viewed as small. However, such loss cannot be said to be greater than the public interest in preserving the environment by blocking harmfulness generated in the recycling process of crushed residue and in establishing a resource circulation system by increasing the automobile recycling rate.\\nAccordingly, the facility standard provision at issue does not violate the balance of legal interests.\\n(4) Conclusion\\nThe facility standard provision at issue does not violate the principle against excessive restriction and does not infringe the Petitioner’s freedom of occupation.\\n\\nd. Whether the Addenda Provision at Issue Violates the Principle of Protection of Trust\\nIn general, when a citizen has formed a certain legal status based on a reasonable expectation that a particular law or system will continue to exist unchanged in the future, the State must, in relation to the repeal or amendment of laws or systems concerning such legal status, protect the citizen’s trust to the maximum extent and promote legal stability in accordance with the principle of a rule-of-law State (Constitutional Court Decisions 97HEONBA10; 2000HEONMA152). Therefore, when enacting or amending laws, if the trust of the parties in the former legal order is reasonable and justified, and the loss suffered by the parties due to the enactment or amendment of the law is so severe that the public interest sought to be achieved by the new legislation cannot justify the destruction of such trust, then such new legislation cannot be permitted (Constitutional Court Decision 2003HEONMA226 et seq. on 2004. 12. 16.).\\nHowever, in this case, the requirement, through amendment of the statutes, that energy recovery facilities obtain approval for installation of a waste treatment facility under the Waste Control Act or file a report of installation is based on the public interest purpose of blocking harmfulness generated in the recycling process of crushed residue, preserving the environment, and qualitatively improving the lives of the people. The Petitioner argues that it installed and operates the facilities at issue in reliance on the public view of the Minister of Environment that energy recovery facilities under the Resource Circulation Act do not correspond to waste treatment facilities under the Waste Control Act. However, the public view of the Minister of Environment is merely an interpretation of the former statutes, and statutes may be amended at any time due to changes in actual circumstances or changes in legislative policy, and the damage caused by such amendment can be protected by setting an appropriate grace period after considering various factors.\\nThe addenda provision at issue, as a transitional provision, sets a grace period of three years from the effective date of the Enforcement Decree of the Resource Circulation Act and provides that persons who completed registration for waste automobile recycling business pursuant to the former statutes shall satisfy the registration requirements prescribed by the facility standard provision at issue within that period; this is not so short as to be an unreasonable period for appropriately coping with changes in circumstances caused by the amendment of the statutes.\\nAccordingly, the addenda provision at issue does not violate the principle of protection of trust and does not infringe the Petitioner’s freedom of occupation.\\n\\n6. Conclusion\\nAccordingly, since the petition in this case is without merit, it is dismissed in its entirety, and the decision is rendered unanimously by all Justices participating, as stated in the Order."}

During the pendency of the appellate trial, the Claimant filed an application for a motion to request a constitutional review of Article 31(4), Subparagraph 2 and Article 34 of the former “Act on Dam Construction and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc.”; upon service of the decision dismissing the application on 2018. 12. 21. (Seoul High Court 2018KAGI20038), it filed this constitutional complaint on 2019. 1. 18.\\n\\n2. Subject Matter of Review\\n\\nThe Claimant filed a petition for review of Article 31(4), Subparagraph 2 and Article 34 of the former “Act on Dam Construction and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc.”, but the present case is an action seeking compensation for losses arising from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport’s disposition of change of dam use right pursuant to Article 31(4), Subparagraph 2 of the former “Act on Dam Construction and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc.”; thus, the subject matter of review is limited to the parts related thereto.\\n\\nAccordingly, the subject matter of this review is whether Article 31(4), Subparagraph 2 of the former “Act on Dam Construction and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc.” (amended by Act No. 11690 on 2013. 3. 23. and, before amendment by Act No. 15624 on 2018. 6. 8.; hereinafter, regardless of the amendment history, referred to as the “Dam Construction Management Act”) (hereinafter referred to as the “Dam Use Right Change Provision”) and the parts concerning Article 31(4), Subparagraph 2 in each of Article 34(1) and (2) (hereinafter referred to as the “Contribution Refund Provision,” and, together with the Dam Use Right Change Provision, the “Provision Subject to Review”) are contrary to the Constitution. The Provision Subject to Review and related provisions are as follows.\\n\\n[Provision Subject to Review]\\n\\nFormer Act on Dam Construction and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc. (amended by Act No. 11690 on 2013. 3. 23. and before amendment by Act No. 15624 on 2018. 6. 8.)\\n\\nArticle 31 (Revocation of Dam Use Right) (4) Where it is difficult to maintain the dam use right as is because any of the following applies, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may render a disposition of revocation or change of the dam use right. In this case, the opinion of the dam use right holder shall be heard in advance.\\n\\n2. Where the use status, etc. of stored water in the dam has changed\\n\\nArticle 34 (Refund of Contributions, etc.) (1) When the State has rendered a disposition of revocation or change with respect to a dam use right pursuant to Article 31, it shall refund a part of the contribution paid pursuant to Article 20(1) or the payment paid pursuant to Article 33.\\n\\n(2) The amount to be refunded pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be calculated by the same method as the calculation method of the relevant contribution or payment; provided that the amount to be refunded to a person granted a dam use right pursuant to Article 24(4) shall not exceed the amount obtained by deducting the depreciation amount calculated as prescribed by Presidential Decree from the contribution under Article 20(1).\\n\\n[Related Provisions]\\n\\nFormer Act on Dam Construction and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc. (amended by Act No. 11690 on 2013. 3. 23. and before amendment by Act No. 15624 on 2018. 6. 8.)\\n\\nArticle 20 (Burden of Multipurpose Dam Construction Costs) (1) A prospective holder of a dam use right shall bear the cost calculated as prescribed by Presidential Decree among the construction costs of a multipurpose dam.\\n\\n(3) The amount obtained by deducting the contribution under paragraph (1) from the construction costs of a multipurpose dam shall be borne by the national treasury.\\n\\n(4) If a prospective holder of a dam use right fails to be granted a dam use right, the State shall refund to the prospective holder of the dam use right the contribution paid pursuant to paragraph (1).
