assets, the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act permits anonymous withdrawals indefinitely (however, an additional charge is imposed after six months from the implementation of the real-name system), and with respect to time deposits and the like, it allows, by way of exception, continued anonymous transactions within the existing amount even after maturity, whereas the Emergency Decree in this case prohibits all anonymous withdrawals (see Article 9 and Article 11(2) of the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and Article 5 of the Emergency Decree in this case).\\n\\nThird, with respect to taxation of financial assets converted to real-name status, the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act exempts all investigation into the source of funds and taxation except for financial assets in excess of 7,000,000 won held in the name of minors, whereas the Emergency Decree in this case exempts investigation into the source of funds and taxation only within differentiated amounts of up to 50,000,000 won depending on age, and provides that, with respect to existing anonymous assets converted to real-name status, the previously insufficiently collected interest income tax shall be retrospectively withheld at source (see Article 10 of the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and Articles 6 and 8 of the Emergency Decree in this case).\\n\\nFourth, in addition, the Emergency Decree in this case sets stricter provisions than the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act with respect to the collection of additional charges or imposition of penalties for failure to perform the obligation to convert to real-name status, differential taxation of anonymous assets, and the guarantee of confidentiality of financial information.\\n\\nIn his special statement for the issuance of the Emergency Decree in this case, the President stated that the contents of the existing Real-Name Financial Transactions Act, as above, would undermine the true meaning and effectiveness of the real-name financial transaction system even if such system were implemented. From this, it can be understood that the President issued the Emergency Decree in this case on the judgment that the existing Real-Name Financial Transactions Act could not overcome the above-mentioned fiscal and economic crisis situation. Since it cannot be recognized that such presidential judgment is manifestly irrational or arbitrary, it should be respected. At the time, the National Assembly was not only in recess, but if, in such a situation, the National Assembly were convened, deliberated, and then the existing Real-Name Financial Transactions Act were amended to the same contents as the Emergency Decree in this case and implemented, black money would leave the financial market and move into the real estate market, thereby causing a credit crunch and making corporate financing difficult on the one hand, thus deepening the economic slowdown, and on the other hand, there would be the risk of a recurrence of real estate speculation or of capital flight overseas; in particular, temporary funding shortages for small and medium-sized enterprises highly dependent on the private lending market and confusion in the securities market, which has a high rate of anonymous transactions, would be sufficiently foreseeable, and, as noted above, the fiscal and economic crisis situation in Korea was so serious that there was not enough time to delay the implementation of the real-name financial transaction system.\\n\\nIf so, as regards the issuance of the Emergency Decree in this case, the requirement that “there is no time to await the convening of the National Assembly even though emergency measures are necessary” can also be deemed satisfied.\\n\\n3) The contents of the Emergency Decree in this case prescribe only the implementation of the real-name financial transaction system and the guarantee of confidentiality of financial information, and other incidental matters related thereto, all of which are “minimally necessary” in relation to overcoming the above-mentioned fiscal and economic crisis situation.\\n\\n4) However, by its very nature, emergency power is a provisional authority intended to respond to an emergency situation, so the exercise of emergency power must be limited to the shortest period necessary to achieve its purpose, and must be lifted without delay once the cause has disappeared. Nevertheless, the Emergency Decree in this case has remained in force even now, more than two years after its issuance. Although prolonging the state of issuance of such an emergency decree is not desirable, that reason alone cannot mean that the Emergency Decree in this case, which was constitutional at the time of issuance, has thereby become unconstitutional.\\n\\n5) In addition, the National Assembly approved the Emergency Decree in this case at the first extraordinary session convened on 1983.8.19. after its issuance, and no problem can be found regarding whether the other procedural requirements were satisfied.\\n\\n(3) Accordingly, the Emergency Decree in this case was issued within the limits of the Constitution, in accordance with the procedures and requirements prescribed by the Constitution, and thus the infringement of the petitioner’s fundamental rights resulting from the issuance of the Emergency Decree in this case falls within the limits of the constitutional duty to endure it.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, as to the portion of the petition in this case concerning the National Assembly’s omission to adopt a resolution of impeachment, it is procedurally improper and is dismissed; and as to the portion concerning the Emergency Decree in this case, it is without merit and is dismissed. It is so decided unanimously by all participating Justices.\\n\\n1996. 2. 29."}

question:
Which of the following statements concerning the case are all correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents)

According to the former statutes and regulations on the Promotion of Installation of Waste Disposal Facilities and Support for Surrounding Areas, etc., in the case of a waste disposal facility to be installed by the head of a local government, where the site-selection area is one city, county, or district, experts selected by the mayor, county governor, or district head and recommended by resident representatives must be included in the composition of the site-selection committee. However, A, the county governor of B County in A Province, arbitrarily constituted the site-selection committee without including experts selected by the county governor and recommended by resident representatives while making a waste site-selection decision, and made a site-selection disposition through the resolution of the committee. Thereafter, A applied to B, the Governor of A Province, for approval to install the waste disposal facility pursuant to the former Waste Management Act and its subordinate statutes and regulations, and B rendered a disposition approving this application.

(a) A's site-selection disposition is not void by operation of law, but it is unlawful and subject to revocation.
(b) The defect in A's site-selection disposition can be cured by A before the filing of an administrative lawsuit challenging it.
(c) The subsequent disposition, namely B's disposition approving the installation of the waste disposal facility, which was made on the basis of A's site-selection disposition, also becomes unlawful.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DU20150]": "1. The Developed Area of the Waste Disposal Facility at Issue and the Applicable Statute\\n\\nArticle 9(1) of the former Act on the Promotion of Installation of Waste Disposal Facilities and Support for Adjacent Areas (the version before amendment by Act No. 7169 on February 9, 2004; hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) provides that the Minister of Environment or the head of a local government (hereinafter referred to as the “waste disposal facility installation authority”), who intends to install and operate a waste disposal facility of at least the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree, shall determine and publicly announce a site selection plan, and paragraph (3) provides that, when the waste disposal facility installation authority has publicly announced the site selection plan, it shall without delay establish a Site Selection Committee in which resident representatives participate, in accordance with the Presidential Decree, and cause it to select the site of the relevant waste disposal facility. Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the former Act on the Promotion of Installation of Waste Disposal Facilities and Support for Adjacent Areas (the version before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 18514 on August 10, 2004) provides, as one of the “waste disposal facilities of at least the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree,” in subparagraph 3, “facilities prescribed by ordinance of a local government,” and Article 3 of the Hwasun-gun Ordinance on the Promotion of Installation of Waste Disposal Facilities and Support for Adjacent Areas (Ordinance No. 1696 on July 1, 2001; hereinafter referred to as the “Hwasun-gun Ordinance”) enacted accordingly provides, as a waste disposal facility subject to determination of a site selection plan, in subparagraph 1, “waste landfill facilities with a developed area of at least 30,000m².” Meanwhile, Article 2 subparagraph 7 of the Wastes Control Act defines “waste disposal facility” as “a facility for intermediate treatment and final disposal of wastes, prescribed by Presidential Decree,” and Article 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act provides in [Attached Table 2], while designating “controlled landfill facilities” as one of the final disposal facilities, that they “include ancillary facilities such as leachate treatment facilities and gas incineration, power generation, and fuelization treatment facilities.” Therefore, the “developed area” under Article 3 subparagraph 1 of the Hwasun-gun Ordinance must be understood to include, in the case of a controlled landfill facility, not only the site area of the landfill proper but also the site areas of all related ancillary facilities.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Hwasun-gun Rural Waste Integrated Treatment Facility at issue (hereinafter referred to as the “treatment facility at issue”) is a controlled landfill facility consisting of a landfill proper, a leachate treatment plant, an internal road, an external road, an incineration facility, and a recycling sorting facility, and it can be seen that the site areas of each facility are 24,720m² for the landfill proper, 1,950m² for the leachate treatment plant, 1,980m² for the internal road, 4,330m² for the external road, and 9,830m² for the incineration facility and recycling sorting facility. Since the above facilities other than the landfill proper are also functionally linked to the landfill proper and are all ancillary facilities included in the treatment facility at issue, which is a controlled landfill facility, the developed area of the treatment facility at issue must ultimately be regarded as the total 42,810m² obtained by adding the site area of the landfill proper and the site areas of the remaining facilities. Accordingly, the treatment facility at issue falls under Article 3 subparagraph 1 of the Hwasun-gun Ordinance and, consequently, in its installation, it becomes subject to the procedures prescribed by the Act, such as determination and public announcement of a site selection plan and the organization and resolution of the Site Selection Committee.\\n\\nAlthough the reasoning stated in this part of the lower appellate court judgment is somewhat insufficient, the conclusion that the developed area of the treatment facility at issue is 42,810m² is correct, and there is no illegality, such as a mistake in fact finding due to a violation of the rules of evidence evaluation, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. Whether the Disposition at Issue Is Lawful\\n\\nArticle 7 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act, pursuant to the delegation under Article 9(3) of the Act, provides in [Attached Table 1] that, in the case of a waste disposal facility to be installed by the head of a local government, the composition of the Site Selection Committee shall, where the site selection area is one city/gun/gu, have a membership limit of no more than 11 persons, and the appointment standards shall be 2 members of the city/gun/gu council, 2 public officials of the city/gun/gu, 3 resident representatives selected by the city/gun/gu council, 2 experts selected by the mayor, county governor, or district head, and 2 experts recommended by resident representatives, provided that the experts shall be appointed from among those who hold qualifications of assistant professor or higher in an environment-related department of a junior college or higher, or of senior researcher or higher at a national or public research institution. Article 11(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act provides that a meeting of the Site Selection Committee shall be resolved with the attendance of at least two-thirds of the incumbent members and the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present. According to the foregoing provisions, the Site Selection Committee is a deliberative body that selects the site of a waste disposal facility. The purpose of requiring a certain number of resident representatives, etc. to participate in the composition of the Site Selection Committee is, in the site selection procedure for a waste disposal facility, to ensure residents’ participation so that their interests and views are represented, thereby preventing unjust infringement of residents’ rights and securing democratization and trust in administration. Therefore, where the method or procedure for constituting the Site Selection Committee is unlawful, such as where it is formed without the participation of resident representatives or experts recommended by resident representatives, the disposition determining the site of a waste disposal facility made on the basis of the resolution of such a defective Site Selection Committee is also unlawful (see Supreme Court Decision 2003DO7118 rendered on November 14, 2003, among others).\\n\\nThe lower appellate court, by comprehensively examining the evidence it adopted, found that, before selecting the site of the treatment facility at issue, the Hwasun-gun County Governor arbitrarily constituted a Site Selection Committee consisting of a total of 280 members, including 210 local residents, 25 heads of social organizations, 16 county council members, 13 journalists, and 16 county officials, while excluding entirely the experts selected by the county governor and the experts recommended by resident representatives; that the said Site Selection Committee, by vote, selected Hancheon-myeon Gaap-ri, Hwasun-gun (the upper area of Juamje) as the target site for the treatment facility at issue from among five candidate sites; and that thereafter the Hwasun-gun County Governor applied to the Defendant for approval for installation of a waste disposal facility, stating that the site area of the treatment facility at issue was 28,650m² (the area excluding the site areas of the external road, the incineration facility, and the recycling sorting facility from the developed area of 42,810m² found in 1. above), and, accordingly, the Defendant made the disposition at issue approving the above application pursuant to Article 30(2) of the Wastes Control Act and Article 21(2) of the Enforcement Rules of the same Act. Then, as stated in 1. above, since the actual developed area of the treatment facility at issue exceeds 30,000m², the installation thereof should have followed the relevant procedures, including the organization of the Site Selection Committee under the Act and the Enforcement Decree of the Act. However, the Hwasun-gun County Governor arbitrarily constituted the Site Selection Committee, wholly different from the method of composition prescribed by the Enforcement Decree of the Act, selected the site of the treatment facility at issue, and applied to the Defendant for approval; in response, the Defendant made the disposition at issue approving the above application pursuant to the Wastes Control Act and the Enforcement Rules of the same Act. Accordingly, the lower appellate court determined that the disposition at issue was unlawful as a disposition that misapplied the statutes. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the lower appellate court’s such findings of fact and determination are correct and well-founded, and there is no illegality, such as an error in the interpretation of law concerning the composition of the Site Selection Committee as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Whether the Defect in the Disposition at Issue Constitutes a Ground for Invalidity\\n\\nIn order for an administrative disposition to be deemed void ab initio, it is not enough that there be merely a ground of illegality in the disposition; the defect must be serious as a violation of an important part of the relevant laws and regulations and must be objectively apparent. In determining whether a defect is serious and apparent, the purpose, meaning, and function of the relevant laws and regulations must be examined teleologically, and the particularity of the concrete case itself must also be reasonably considered (see Supreme Court Decision 2005DO14363 rendered on June 30, 2006, among others).\\n\\nThe lower appellate court determined that the legislative intent of the Enforcement Decree of the Act, which requires that the composition of the Site Selection Committee include 2 persons selected by the mayor, county governor, or district head and 2 experts recommended by resident representatives, lies in enabling experts with specialized knowledge to examine in advance, in depth and fairly, the various problems expected to arise from the installation of a waste disposal facility and to present them concretely, thereby allowing residents’ participation to become more substantive by having them represent the interests and views of all residents, and preventing unjust infringement of residents’ rights caused by the arbitrary exercise of power by local governments or rash decisions by a small number of resident representatives, and restoring democratization and trust in administration. Therefore, in light of this purpose, the participation of 4 experts, in particular 2 experts recommended by resident representatives, in the Site Selection Committee is an indispensable element. Accordingly, in the present case, the defect in not constituting the Site Selection Committee in accordance with the method of composition under the Enforcement Decree of the Act due to misapplication of the relevant law, while arbitrarily constituting a Site Selection Committee without including the 2 experts selected and recommended by the county governor and resident representatives respectively, is serious and objectively apparent. Thus, the lower appellate court held that the defect in the disposition at issue constitutes a ground for invalidity.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the lower appellate court’s such determination is correct and well-founded, and there is no illegality, such as an error in the interpretation of law concerning the ground for invalidity of an administrative disposition as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Supreme Court Decision 2002DO394 rendered on April 26, 2002, cited in the grounds of appeal, concerns a different matter from the present case and is not appropriate to invoke in this case.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[96NU5308]": "We consider the grounds for final appeal (a supplemental brief of grounds for final appeal submitted after the deadline for filing the statement of grounds for final appeal shall be considered only to the extent that it supplements the grounds for final appeal).\\n\\nIt is appropriate to construe the individual notice in lieu of inspection of the contents of the land grade determination, as prescribed in Article 43(2) of the Enforcement Rule of the Local Tax Act (as in effect prior to its amendment by Ordinance of the Ministry of Home Affairs No. 668 on Dec. 30, 1995), as a requirement for the land grade determination to take effect; therefore, where such procedure is omitted, the determination cannot produce any effect vis-à-vis third parties (see this Court’s judgment dated Nov. 27, 1992, 92NU1476). Since the purpose of requiring such individual notice is to inform the landowner in detail of the contents of the determination or revision of the land grade and thereby facilitate the decision whether to object thereto and the filing of such objection, the notice must specify the land subject to the land grade determination so that the landowner can know in detail the contents of the disposition of land grade determination, and must specifically state the newly determined land grade, etc. for that land.\\n\\nAccording to the facts established by the court below, the Defendant, as of Sept. 1, 1989, made a determination to set or revise the grades of some of the lands owned by the Plaintiff and used as the site of the Jungmun Golf Course located in Saekdal-dong, Seogwipo-si, Jeju-do, and in giving individual notice thereof, entered in the land location column of the land grade revision result notice “Saekdal 2542 <TOURIST_COMPLEX_IN_ALL_PARCELS_REVISED>,” and in the category column, the pre-determination land grade and grade value columns, and the post-determination land grade and grade value columns, entered the contents corresponding to the above parcel 2542 and notified the Plaintiff. Such individual notice is unlawful because, as to the remaining lands other than the above Saekdal-dong 2542 land, it does not specifically reveal which land was subject to land grade determination and how the contents of that grade determination were made. In addition, considering the following facts recognize by the record, namely, that the Plaintiff owned other lands within the tourist complex in addition to the lands used as the site of the Jungmun Golf Course; that the lands whose grades were determined as a result of the land grade determination at issue were only some of the lands used as the site of the Jungmun Golf Course, and that there was no land grade determination as to the remaining lands and the lands located within the tourist complex other than the site of the Jungmun Golf Course; and that, among the lands whose grades were set or revised together with the above Saekdal-dong 2542 land as a result of the land grade determination at issue, not all were determined to have the same grade as that land (grade 180), but many were determined to have different grades, even if the land location column of the land grade revision result notice had indicated, in addition to the above Saekdal-dong 2542 land, “revision of all parcels within the tourist complex,” such notice cannot be regarded as notice of the contents of the land grade determination with respect to the other lands, namely, the lands listed in Attached Table 1-1 of the judgment of the court below, other than the above 2542 land. Therefore, the land grade determination at issue concerning the above lands is a void disposition that cannot take effect.\\n\\nMoreover, since it cannot be said that there was individual notice of the contents of the land grade determination in this manner and the land grade determination is void, even if the landowner knew the contents of the land grade determination before or after that determination, or even if the results of the annual regular grade revision after that determination were made available for inspection by the landowner, etc., the defect in the individual notice at issue is not cured (see this Court’s judgment dated Mar. 22, 1988, 87NU986).\\n\\nAlthough there are some insufficiencies in the reasoning stated in the judgment of the court below, its conclusion is to the same effect and is therefore proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as misapprehension of the legal principle concerning individual notice of a land grade determination. The judgments cited by the appellant involve different facts from this case and are therefore not appropriate for citation. The argument is without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. The opinions of the participating Justices being in accord, the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition."}

{"[97NU6780]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding the first ground for appeal\\n\\nAccording to the proviso to Article 38(2) of the Housing Construction Promotion Act, Article 6(1) and (2) of the Apartment House Management Decree, and Articles 4 and 4-2 of the Apartment House Management Rules, where the owner, occupant, user, and managing body of an apartment house and ancillary facilities and welfare facilities intend to carry out construction work on a building subject to reporting, as a minor matter prescribed by the Ordinance of the Ministry of Construction, they may carry out such construction work so long as they file only a report satisfying the lawful requirements prescribed in the relevant statutes, and there is no need to await any separate measure such as an acceptance disposition by the administrative agency; and where an administrative agency receives such a report, it shall examine whether the report falls within a case in which construction is permitted by report alone under this Act and its Enforcement Decree and other relevant statutes, and whether the accompanying documents, etc. are in order, and, insofar as it conforms to the statutory provisions, it must accept it, and it may not refuse acceptance of the report on the basis of reasons not prescribed in the same Act.\\n\\nIn light of the reasons of the judgment below and the record and relevant statutes, even if the gate-installation report in this case submitted by the Plaintiff (Defendant's Exhibit No. 10) is not in the form of Separate Form No. 1-2 (Defendant's Exhibit No. 9) prescribed in Article 4 of the Apartment House Management Rules, all of the contents required by that form are stated therein, and the written consent of the Residents' Representative Council is attached to the report; meanwhile, since there were no applicable documents and drawings prescribed in Article 6 of the Enforcement Rules of the Building Act, and therefore they were not attached, the Plaintiff's gate-installation report in this case should be deemed a report satisfying the lawful requirements without formal defect, so that its effect arose without needing to await any separate measure such as the Defendant's issuance of a certificate of receipt or acceptance disposition; and although the gate in this case was lawful, the demolition order of the gate in this case issued by the Defendant against the Plaintiff should be deemed null and void ab initio because its defect is grave and apparent, and the subsequent disposition of warning in this case likewise should be deemed null and void ab initio; the judgment of the court below to such effect is proper, and there is no illegality of misapprehension of the legal principle concerning the Housing Construction Promotion Act as alleged by the Defendant. The gist of the grounds for appeal on this point is without merit.\\n\\n2. Regarding the second ground for appeal\\n\\nThe gist of the grounds for appeal that, because the Plaintiff's act of installing the gate in this case violated Article 26 of the former Building Act (as in effect before amendment by Act No. 4919 on January 5, 1995; hereinafter referred to as the Building Act), the Defendant's order to restore the original state, issued against the Plaintiff, who is the owner of the gate in this case, pursuant to Article 69(1) of the Building Act, was a disposition by proper authority, and therefore the disposition of warning in this case was lawful, is a ground newly asserted at this appellate stage by the Defendant and was not asserted in the court below, and is merely directed at the supplementary determination of the court below; moreover, insofar as the Plaintiff's report of gate installation in this case was lawful, the gate in this case cannot be regarded as an illegal building in violation of Article 26(1) of the Building Act, so there is no need to further examine it, and it is without merit.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged as the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following explanations concerning public-law contracts is not correct? (Where there is a dispute, in accordance with the precedents)
A: Under the "Administrative Basic Act," an administrative agency may conclude a public-law contract, where necessary to achieve an administrative purpose, to the extent that it does not violate statutes, etc., and in such case it shall prepare a contract document that clearly states the purpose and contents of the contract.
B: A contract concluded pursuant to the "Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party" is a public-law contract, and therefore the provisions concerning bidding procedures and standards for determining the successful bidder under that Act and its Enforcement Decree cannot be said to be merely internal rules of the State.
C: Even if the termination of the employment contract of a public health physician, who is a professional public official, is an adverse disposition depriving him or her of status by a unilateral declaration of intent by the competent provincial governor, it cannot immediately be determined that such declaration of intent is an administrative disposition made by the competent provincial governor in the exercise of public authority as an administrative agency.
D: Because the termination of the employment contract of a fixed-term public official is a declaration of intent made by the State or a local government as one party to the employment contract relationship in an equal position, it is not required, as with an administrative disposition, to state the grounds and reasons pursuant to the "Administrative Procedures Act."
E: The cancellation by the Industrial Complex Management Corporation of a contract for change of occupancy under the former "Act on the Activation of Industrial Clusters and Factory Establishment" is an administrative disposition subject to an appeal litigation, because the Industrial Complex Management Corporation, entrusted with management duties by the manager, who is an administrative agency, causes certain legal effects to arise for the tenant companies from a superior position.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2001DA33604]": "The grounds of appeal by the Debtor and its auxiliary intervenors (hereinafter referred to simply as the \"Intervenors\") (the statements in the respective supplemental briefs of grounds of appeal submitted after the expiration of the period for submitting the petition of appeal shall be considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds) are examined together.\\n\\n1. Summary of the judgment of the court below\\n\\na. The court below acknowledged the following facts based on the evidence.\\n\\n(1) On 2000. 11. 4., the Debtor issued a notice of invitation for bids concerning the construction project for the Gwangju No. 2 Agricultural and Fishery Products Wholesale Market (hereinafter referred to as \"the construction project in question\"), and ① restricted the qualification to participate in the bid to \"companies with a construction record of at least 40,686㎡ of gross floor area in domestic single-award construction projects corresponding to wholesale markets and retail markets among the sales and business facilities in [Attached Table 1] related to Article 3-4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act, completed within the most recent 10 years as of the date of the notice of invitation for bids,\" and ② as to the method of determining the successful bidder, designated as the person to be selected, pursuant to Article 42 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party (hereinafter referred to as the \"State Contracts Act\") and the Detailed Criteria for Qualification Review of Facility Construction Contracts by Local Governments (Ministry of Government Administration and Home Affairs Directive No. 49 and No. 60, hereinafter referred to as the \"Detailed Criteria\"), the person whose bid was the lowest at or below the estimated price and whose ability to perform the relevant contract was examined in the qualification review procedure in order of lowest bid, and who obtained a comprehensive score of 90 points or more.\\n\\n(2) At the on-site explanation concerning the construction project in question on 2000. 11. 13., the Debtor's accounting officer distributed an explanatory document stating, with regard to the scope of recognition of the construction records of \"sales and business facilities\" set forth in the qualification for participation in the bid, that \"the intended use is sales facilities (for mixed-use facilities, only the sales facilities are applicable), wholesale markets and retail markets among the 'sales and business facilities' in [Attached Table 1] related to Article 3-4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act (meaning markets, large stores, large-scale retail stores, and others similar thereto under the Distribution Industry Development Act).\"\\n\\n(3) As a result of the bid conducted on 2000. 12. 18., five joint supply and demand consortia participated, and the joint supply and demand consortium composed of the Intervenors became the third-lowest bidder, while the joint supply and demand consortium represented by the Creditor became the fourth-lowest bidder; however, the lowest bidder and the second-lowest bidder failed to submit the qualification review documents and were therefore excluded from the subject of the qualification review, and accordingly the joint supply and demand consortium of the Intervenors became the subject of the qualification review.\\n\\n(4) According to the Detailed Criteria, with respect to the evaluation of construction experience in the evaluation of performance capability, in the case of a joint supply and demand consortium, the evaluation is made by multiplying the evaluation standard for the relevant construction project and each member's construction experience by each member's share of participation in the construction project and then aggregating the resulting performance, and with respect to the allocation of points for the total construction performance, 20 points are to be given for 100% or more of the scale of the evaluation standard for the relevant construction project, 18 points for 70% or more, 14 points for 40% or more, and 12 points for less than 20%.\\n\\n(5) When the Debtor reviewed the qualification of the Intervenor Geumgwang Construction Co., Ltd. based on the documents submitted by it, the Debtor, in the construction experience evaluation item, treated the construction performance of Geumgwang Construction Co., Ltd., which had constructed the Songwon Department Store building with a gross floor area of 41,268.65㎡ and the Suncheon Carrefour building with a gross floor area of 48,171㎡, as total construction performance of 49,191.8075㎡{=(41,268.65㎡ + 48,171㎡) × 0.55} in accordance with Geumgwang Construction Co., Ltd.'s 55% share of participation in the construction project in question, and recognized that it exceeded the evaluation standard scale for the construction project in question of 40,686㎢, thereby assigning the full score of 20 points, and as a result the total score became 90.18, so it was found to be qualified under the above qualification review criteria.\\n\\n(6) Thereafter, on 2000. 12. 30., the Debtor determined the joint supply and demand consortium of the Intervenors as the successful bidder and concluded a subcontract for the construction project in question on 2001. 1. 5., and the Intervenors submitted the commencement report for construction on the 12th of the same month and thereafter cleared the land and installed a site office.\\n\\nb. However, for the following reasons, the court below held that the joint supply and demand consortium of the Intervenors did not obtain the comprehensive score of 90 points, which was the qualification review criterion set forth in the notice of successful bidder, and therefore that the determination of the successful bidder for the joint supply and demand consortium of the Intervenors was void.\\n\\n(1) The invitation for bids and the explanatory document must be viewed as a single invitation for bids as a whole, and the purpose of adding the phrase \"the intended use is sales facilities (for mixed-use facilities, only the sales facilities are applicable)\" in the explanatory document was to make the qualification for participation in the bid more specific and clear; therefore, in examining construction performance, even if a completed building corresponds to wholesale markets and retail markets among the sales and business facilities in [Attached Table 1] related to Article 3-4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act (markets, large stores, large-scale retail stores, and others similar thereto under the Distribution Industry Development Act), if it is a mixed-use facility, only the construction performance of the sales facilities among them should be taken as the criterion, and among such sales facilities, only facilities whose intended use is \"sales facilities\" and facilities used as an ancillary use to the \"sales facilities\" prescribed in Article 2(1)14 of the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act are included, while the remainder should be excluded.\\n\\n(2) The Songwon Department Store building has a gross floor area of 41,268.65㎡, but its uses are classified as sales facilities totaling 24,410.83㎡, parking facilities totaling 10,614.36㎡, machine/electrical rooms 842.03㎡, general restaurants 1,260.80㎡, exhibition and assembly facilities 687㎡, sports facilities 3,378.76㎡, air-conditioning rooms 74.87㎡, and the like, and is therefore a mixed-use facility. Accordingly, only the 24,410.83㎡ of sales facilities and the ancillary-use parking facilities of 10,614.36㎡, machine/electrical rooms 842.03㎡, and air-conditioning rooms 74.87㎡ among them should be regarded as subject to recognition as construction performance specified in the invitation for bids and the explanatory document, and since this falls short of the construction performance evaluation scale of 40,686㎡ under the qualification for participation in the bid, the above Songwon Department Store cannot ultimately be aggregated and evaluated as construction performance.\\n\\n(3) Even if the 48,171㎡ of sales facilities of the above Suncheon Carrefour building were included in construction performance, taking into account Geumgwang Construction Co., Ltd.'s share of participation in the consortium, it would amount to 65.11% ((48,171㎡ × 0.55) / 40,686㎡) of the above evaluation standard of 40,686㎡, and thus the construction experience score to be allocated to the Intervenors would be 16 points; in the end, the total score would be only 86.18, and they would fail to obtain the 90-point comprehensive score required by the qualification review criteria.\\n\\nc. Furthermore, on that premise, the court below held that the joint supply and demand consortium represented by the Creditor became the next-ranked lowest bidder and thus held the status of a subject of qualification review, and that if the consortium were found to have obtained 90 points or more in the qualification review, it would acquire the status of successful bidder; in this case, the Creditor would also have the right to seek that the Debtor prevent the Intervenors, who are the counterparties to the construction contract in question, from carrying out the construction project in question. Accordingly, after finding that a prima facie showing had been made as to the right to be preserved in this case, it provisionally determined that the joint bidders including the Creditor in this bid have the status of subjects of qualification review, and issued a provisional injunction ordering that the Debtor shall not cause the Intervenors to perform the construction under the construction contract in question until the judgment in the principal action concerning this provisional injunction becomes final and conclusive.\\n\\n2. Determination by the Supreme Court\\n\\nHowever, the above determination of the court below cannot be readily accepted for the following reasons.\\n\\nPublic contracts, so-called, to which a local government is a party pursuant to the State Contracts Act applied mutatis mutandis by the Local Finance Act, are contracts under private law concluded by the local government in the position of an equal counterpart with the other party as a subject of private economic activity, and their essential content is no different from contracts between private persons; therefore, unless the relevant statutes provide otherwise, the principles of private law, such as private autonomy and freedom of contract, apply as they are.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the State Contracts Act provides that, in principle, when the State concludes a contract, it shall do so by competitive bidding (Article 7), and that in competitive bidding entailing a burden on the national treasury, the successful bidder shall be determined to be the person who submitted the bid most advantageous to the State according to the evaluation criteria specified in the notice of invitation for bids or the bid instructions (Article 10(2)2), and the same Act's Enforcement Decree provides that detailed review criteria shall be established and determined according to the review standards prescribed by the Minister of Finance and Economy, taking into comprehensive consideration the relevant bidder's performance record, technical capability, financial condition, past faithfulness in contract performance, appropriateness of the prices for materials and labor procurement, degree of compliance with contract order, quality of past construction works, and bid price, etc.; however, these provisions merely prescribe the necessary matters concerning contract administration that relevant public officials must observe so that the State can fairly and reasonably and efficiently process contractual relations with private persons, and are nothing more than internal regulations of the State (see Supreme Court Decision 95DA11436 rendered on 1996. 4. 26.).\\n\\nAccordingly, the mere fact that the contract officer conducted a qualification review in the bidding procedure contrary to the above statutes or their detailed review criteria does not, by itself, render the determination of the successful bidder or the contract concluded on that basis void; rather, such a violation will be void only where the defect is so serious that it markedly infringes the public nature and fairness of the bidding procedure, and the other party knew or could have known of such circumstances, or where it is clear to anyone that the determination of the successful bidder and the conclusion of the contract were made through conduct contrary to good morals or other social order, or where there are special circumstances such that, unless it is deemed void, the purpose of the State Contracts Act provisions governing the procedure would be nullified.\\n\\nTurning to this case, the record shows that the scope of recognition of construction performance of the same kind, which is prescribed as a factor in the evaluation of construction experience in the detailed review criteria, refers to a performance record of one unit structure with a completed construction, the scale of which is at least 40,686㎡, that can be evaluated as making it possible to achieve the purpose of the contract because the construction content is substantially identical to the construction currently to be ordered by the ordering agency. Thus, even if, as held by the court below, the general restaurants, exhibition and assembly facilities, and sports facilities within Songwon Department Store do not, in the interpretation of the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act, fall within the sales facilities themselves among the classifications of use, and therefore cannot be included within the scope of performance recognition described in the invitation for bids and the explanatory document, still, in light of the record, these are consumer convenience facilities ancillary to the sales facilities and, together with the main sales facilities, constitute one unit structure forming a department store, which is a type of large-scale retail store under the Distribution Industry Development Act; meanwhile, the content of the construction project in question is the new construction of a vegetable building, produce building, fisheries building, management services building, guard room, and waste disposal building, and the management services building includes convenience facilities and management facilities such as a large conference room, financial institution, restaurant, and coffee shop, as well as user convenience facilities; and there is no material to conclude that the construction of the sales facilities among the construction project in question is especially more difficult in execution than the general restaurants, exhibition and assembly facilities, and sports facilities of Songwon Department Store. Therefore, it is difficult to regard the Debtor's recognition in the qualification review of the Songwon Department Store, including the above consumer convenience facilities, as construction performance as a serious defect to the extent of markedly infringing the public nature and fairness of the bidding procedure in this case; nor can any other material be found in the record showing that the determination of the successful bidder and the conclusion of the contract in this case were made through conduct contrary to good morals or other social order.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, contrary to this, sustained the application for provisional disposition in this case on the premise that the determination of the successful bidder and the subcontract in this case were void, and thus it cannot be said that the judgment of the court below did not err by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the State Contracts Act and the effect of the invitation for bids, and by failing to conduct adequate deliberation, thereby affecting the outcome of the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing out this issue is well taken.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and in order to have the case reheard and decided, it is remanded to the court below; the judgment is rendered by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the operative part."}

{"[2002DU5948]": "We consider the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nIn light of the provisions of the current statutes and regulations concerning contract-based public officials, the expression of intention to terminate the employment contract of a contract-based public official differs from a disciplinary disposition against a general public official and is not recognized as having the nature of a disposition, etc. subject to administrative appeal litigation; rather, it is understood as being treated as an expression of intention made by the State or a local government, as one party to the employment contract relationship, from a position of equality when certain grounds exist (see Supreme Court Decision 95NU10617 dated May 31, 1996). Accordingly, it is not the case that, as in a disciplinary dismissal, the validity thereof must be determined only with respect to the disciplinary grounds, nor that, as in an administrative disposition, grounds and reasons must be presented pursuant to the Administrative Procedures Act.\\n\\nFrom the same perspective, there is no error in law regarding the grounds for termination of the employment contract or error in fact, as alleged as grounds of appeal, in the appellate court judgment that determined whether the Defendant’s termination of the employment contract against the Plaintiff was valid.\\n\\nThe argument in the grounds of appeal concerning this point lacks merit.\\n\\n2. With respect to Grounds 2 and 3 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nThe court below, in a continuing contractual relationship such as the employment contract at issue, premised that because such a relationship is founded on an unceasing relationship of trust between the parties, if there are special circumstances in which the relationship of trust forming the basis of the contract between the parties has been destroyed and has reached such a degree that it is difficult to maintain the contractual relationship as it stands, then even if that does not fall under either an agreed ground for termination or a statutory ground for termination, the other party may immediately terminate the contractual relationship and thereby extinguish its effect prospectively. The court then held that, as a military newspaper, Defense Daily is a special newspaper whose principal mission is to raise the public’s security awareness, form a shared security consensus between the military and the civilian population, establish servicemembers’ view of the nation and view of the enemy, ideological armament, and mental education, and that there is ample room for the content of its articles to be construed as the official views of the Ministry of National Defense or the Government; that the Plaintiff, as the highest responsible person at the Defense Public Relations Agency, which publishes Defense Daily, directs and supervises the subordinate employees and bears final and ultimate responsibility for the production and editing of Defense Daily; and that, by publishing in Defense Daily an article on the revolutionary opera entitled “Sea of Blood,” created by Kim Il Sung and adapted by Kim Jong Il and which became the model for all subsequent revolutionary operas, while adding subtitles reading “Revolutionary drama created under the guidance of Chairman Kim” and “A masterpiece perfectly embodying Juche ideology,” there was a serious concern that its readers, especially servicemembers, would take the title or content of the article as the official view of our Government, and accordingly it must be concluded that there was also a considerable possibility that it would confuse servicemembers’ security awareness and adversely affect the morale or combat capability of the entire military. On that basis, the court below held that the relationship of trust forming the basis of the contract under which the Minister of National Defense, under the Defendant, employed the Plaintiff as the head of the Government Information Agency, who was responsible for the publication of Defense Daily, had already been destroyed, and therefore the Defendant could terminate the employment contract with the Plaintiff and extinguish its effect prospectively, and thus the expression of intention to terminate the employment contract at issue was justified.\\n\\nA continuing contract is founded on a relationship of trust between the parties; therefore, if, during the existence of the relevant contract, one party violates its contractual obligations and thereby destroys the relationship of trust forming the basis of the contract, reaching such a degree that it is difficult to maintain the contractual relationship as it stands, it is appropriate to view that the other party may immediately terminate the contractual relationship and thereby extinguish its effect prospectively (see Supreme Court Decision 94DA17826 dated March 24, 1995). When all the circumstances appearing in the record, including the points raised by the court below, are taken together, in the end the Plaintiff, in performing affairs concerning the production of Defense Daily by directing and supervising the public officials subordinate to the Defense Public Relations Agency, was required to faithfully perform his duties in accordance with the employment contract at issue and the statutes and regulations concerning that contract (see Article 56 of the State Public Officials Act), but, in violation of such duty, he neglected to direct and supervise his subordinate employee, causing the article at issue to be published in Defense Daily and thereby creating social controversy. Accordingly, it must be viewed that the relationship of trust between the Plaintiff and the Defendant was destroyed and that it reached such a degree that it was difficult to maintain the employment contract at issue as it stood. Thus, although there are some inappropriately worded or insufficient portions in the appellate court judgment, the conclusion of the court below that the expression of intention to terminate the employment contract at issue is not invalid is acceptable as just, and there can be no illegality in the appellate court judgment, such as error in law, inconsistency in reasons, error in fact, or inadequate deliberation, as alleged as grounds of appeal, affecting the outcome of the judgment.\\n\\nThe argument in the grounds of appeal concerning this point likewise lacks merit.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2014DU46843]": "We consider the grounds for appeal (the statements in the supplementary brief filed after the expiration of the period for filing the statement of grounds for appeal are considered only to the extent that they supplement the grounds for appeal).\\n\\n1. Grounds for appeal concerning the dispositional nature of the cancellation of the modification contract\\n\\nThe issue of whether a certain act by an administrative agency may be the subject of administrative appeal litigation cannot be determined abstractly and generally. In a concrete case, bearing in mind that an administrative disposition is an act that directly affects the rights and obligations of the people as an enforcement of laws concerning specific facts conducted by an administrative agency as the holder of public authority, it must be individually determined by considering the content and purpose of the relevant statutes, the actor, content, form, and procedure of the act, the substantial nexus between the act and the disadvantage suffered by the counterparty and other interested persons, and the principles of administration under the rule of law as well as the attitudes of the administrative agency and interested persons regarding the act (see, e.g., Supreme Court en banc Decision rendered on 2010. 11. 18. in 2008DU167).\\n\\nAccording to the former Act on the Activation of Industrial Clusters and Factory Establishment (as amended by Act No. 11690 on March 23, 2013; hereinafter the “former Industrial Cluster Act”), the management authority for a general industrial complex is the Mayor or Governor of the relevant City/Do (Article 30(1)2), and the Defendant incorporated association Seongnam Industrial Complex Management Corporation (hereinafter the “Defendant Corporation”) is a management institution entrusted with management affairs by the management authority (Article 30(2)3 of the same Act). A person who engages, or intends to engage, in manufacturing in an industrial complex shall conclude an occupancy contract with the management institution in accordance with the Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy (main clause of Article 38(1)), and if such person intends to modify any matter among the occupancy contract terms prescribed by the Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy, a new modification contract must be concluded (Article 38(2)). In cases where an occupancy contract and a modification contract are concluded, approval for factory establishment, etc. shall be deemed to have been granted (Article 13(2)2 and (1)). If a person violates the occupancy contract or modifies any matter prescribed by the Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy without concluding a modification contract, the management institution may order correction within a prescribed period and, if such order is not complied with, may, after hearing the opinion of the contractual party in advance, terminate the occupancy contract (Article 42(1)4, 5, and 5). In such case, the person whose occupancy contract has been terminated shall immediately cease the business, except for the handling of remaining affairs, etc. (Article 42(2) of the same Act), and shall dispose of the industrial land and factory buildings owned by such person (Article 43). In addition, if a person who acquires industrial land or factory buildings, etc. fails to conclude an occupancy contract within a prescribed period, such industrial land, etc. must be transferred to a third party or the management institution, etc. (Articles 40 and 40-2), and a person who conducts manufacturing, etc. without concluding an occupancy contract or who continues such business in violation of the duty to suspend business following termination of the occupancy contract shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 15 million won (Article 52(2)5 and 6), while a person who engages in manufacturing, etc. without concluding a modification contract shall be punished by a fine not exceeding 15 million won (Article 53(4)) or become subject to an administrative fine (Article 55(2)9). A person who fails to perform the duty to dispose of or transfer property after termination of the occupancy contract shall be subject to an administrative fine (Article 55(1)4), and a compulsory performance fine may be imposed (Article 43-3).\\n\\nWhen the status of the Defendant Corporation, as discerned from these provisions, the effects of the occupancy contract and the modification contract, the duty to conclude the occupancy contract and the modification contract and the criminal or administrative sanctions for failure to perform such duty, the procedure for termination of the occupancy contract, the legal duties accompanying notice of termination, and the criminal or administrative sanctions for failure to perform such duties are comprehensively considered, the cancellation of the modification contract at issue should be deemed an administrative disposition subject to administrative appeal litigation, as it is an act by which the Defendant Corporation, which has been entrusted with management affairs by the management authority, as an administrative agency, causes certain legal effects to arise for the Plaintiffs from a superior position (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2011. 6. 30. in 2010DU23859).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below and the reasons stated in the first-instance judgment cited by the court below, the court below, after comprehensively examining the evidence it admitted, found the facts as stated in its opinion, and then held, on the grounds stated in its opinion, that the cancellation of the modification contract at issue constitutes an administrative disposition.\\n\\nThis determination by the court below is consistent with the foregoing legal principle and is correct, and there is no error in misapprehending the legal nature of the cancellation of the modification contract. The Supreme Court Decision cited by the Defendants in the grounds for appeal, rendered on 1995. 9. 29. in 95NU8447, concerns an occupancy contract under the former Act on the Arrangement of Industrial Sites and Factory Establishment (before amendment by Act No. 4720 on January 7, 1994), and the facts are different from those of this case.\\n\\n2. Grounds for appeal concerning the illegality of the cancellation of the modification contract at issue and the disposition denying building permission\\n\\nWhere, through a certain administrative disposition, a citizen acquires a certain benefit and right, an administrative disposition that, on the premise that the previous administrative disposition was defective, cancels it ex officio is a separate administrative disposition depriving the citizen of the already acquired existing benefit and right. Accordingly, the disposition to be canceled must be defective; furthermore, even if the administrative disposition is defective, it may be canceled only when, after comparing and weighing the public-interest necessity for cancellation against the disadvantage to be suffered by the party, including the infringement of vested rights, protection of trust, and stability of legal life, the public-interest necessity is sufficiently strong to justify the disadvantage the party will suffer. The burden of proving the defect or the necessity of cancellation lies with the administrative agency that issued the disposition infringing the existing benefit and right (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2014. 11. 27. in 2014DU9226). The purpose of such protection of trust and balancing of interests applies equally to cases of cancellation of an occupancy contract or modification contract under the Industrial Cluster Act.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below and the reasons stated in the first-instance judgment cited by the court below, the court below, after comprehensively examining the evidence it admitted, found the facts as stated in its opinion, and then held that it is difficult to regard the defect in the modification contract at issue as attributable to the Plaintiffs’ concealment of facts or other application acts by fraudulent means. The court below further held that, considering the following circumstances: ① although several plating businesses have been operating in the industrial complex at issue since around 2003, no civil complaints, etc. concerning pollution resulting therefrom had been raised; ② if the pollution prevention facilities presented by the Plaintiffs are properly installed and operated, it is expected that damage arising from environmental pollution and pollution generation, etc. can be substantially reduced, and thus it is difficult to regard the maintenance of the modification contract at issue as causing nearby residents damage exceeding the socially accepted tolerable limit; ③ the Defendants had initially stated the opinion that the plating business does not fall under a pollution-generating industry subject to occupancy restriction; ④ the Plaintiffs appear to have already invested a large amount of funds and effort in reliance on the modification contract at issue, including by concluding a service contract for permission to install emission facilities, and as to the knowledge industry center that the Plaintiffs will establish in the future, it appears that damage to the surrounding environment and nearby residents can be minimized through thorough prior and post management pursuant to the relevant statutes, and other circumstances, there is difficulty in finding a serious public-interest necessity sufficient to justify the disadvantage the Plaintiffs will suffer from cancellation of the modification contract at issue, and therefore the cancellation disposition of the modification contract at issue is unlawful; accordingly, the building-permission-denial disposition premised on the cancellation of the modification contract at issue is also unlawful.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principle and the record, the foregoing determination by the court below is correct, and there is no error exceeding the bounds of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehending the legal principle concerning the principle of protection of trust.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing parties. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the Disposition."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning administrative legislation are correct? (In case of dispute, according to case law)
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2018DU45633]": "The grounds for final appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. a. Article 20 of the Administrative Procedures Act provides in Paragraph (1), “An administrative agency shall, in light of the nature of the disposition concerned, establish and publish the necessary criteria for disposition as concretely as possible. The same shall also apply when changing the criteria for disposition.” It further provides in Paragraph (2), “Where there are reasonable grounds deemed to exist that publication of the criteria for disposition under Paragraph (1) would be markedly difficult in light of the nature of the disposition concerned or would significantly harm public safety or welfare, the criteria for disposition need not be published.”\\n\\nb. The reason why administrative agencies are required to establish and publish the criteria for disposition concretely in this manner is to enable the relevant disposition to be made, as far as possible, in accordance with criteria published in advance, thereby enhancing the foreseeability of the result for the party to whom the disposition is addressed and, through this, securing fairness, transparency, and reliability in administration and preventing arbitrary exercise of authority by the administrative agency. However, if the criteria for disposition are published in advance in light of the nature of the disposition, there may be cases in which the administrative purpose cannot be achieved, or in which it would rather be more appropriate for public safety or welfare to grant the administrative agency discretion within a certain scope so that the disposition may be made flexibly, taking account of individual circumstances in the concrete case. In such cases, pursuant to Article 20, Paragraph (2) of the Administrative Procedures Act, the criteria for disposition may be published separately or only in outline (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2018DU41907, decided December 13, 2019). Even when the administrative agency changes the criteria for disposition initially published, it must republish the changed criteria for disposition unless the case falls under the exception set forth in the above Paragraph (2).\\n\\nc. Even if an administrative agency, in violation of the duty under Article 20, Paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedures Act to publish criteria for disposition in advance, has made a disposition by applying criteria not previously published, such circumstance alone cannot be said to immediately mean that the disposition contains a defect amounting to a ground for cancellation. However, if there are specific circumstances showing that the criteria applied to the disposition violated provisions of superior statutes and regulations or general principles of law, such as the principle of protection of trust, or that they were objectively unreasonable, the disposition may be evaluated as unlawful. The specific reasons are as follows.\\n\\n(1) The criteria for disposition established and published by an administrative agency pursuant to Article 20, Paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedures Act should, unless there are special circumstances that they were enacted and promulgated upon a specific delegation from the statutes and regulations serving as the basis for the relevant disposition, in principle be regarded as administrative rules that lack externally binding force.\\n\\n(2) Whether a disposition is lawful must be determined not by whether it conforms to administrative rules, but by whether it conforms to the provisions and legislative purpose of superior statutes and regulations (see Supreme Court Decision 2011DU10584, decided September 12, 2013). A disposition does not immediately become unlawful merely because it violates administrative rules (see Supreme Court Decision 2009DU7967, decided December 24, 2009), and compliance with administrative rules does not guarantee lawfulness either. Just as whether the administrative agency followed the criteria previously published, namely administrative rules, cannot be a decisive indicator in determining the lawfulness of a disposition, whether the administrative agency applied criteria that were not previously published also cannot be a decisive indicator in determining the lawfulness of a disposition.\\n\\n(3) Whether the criteria for disposition established and published by the administrative agency are indeed concrete, or whether they fall within the exception to the duty to publish criteria for disposition in advance set forth in Article 20, Paragraph (2) of the Administrative Procedures Act, is difficult to determine uniformly and must be separately judged according to the specific case. If it were deemed that a disposition can be lawfully made only when concrete criteria for disposition have been published in advance pursuant to Article 20, Paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedures Act, the lawfulness of dispositions would become excessively unstable and the execution of individual statutes and regulations would in effect be suspended or delayed.\\n\\nd. In cases where an administrative agency, pursuant to the provisions of the relevant statutes and regulations or based on its own judgment, adopts and operates so-called a “renewal system,” under which it grants the party to whom the disposition is addressed certain rights, interests, or status, and then reviews the matter at fixed intervals to determine whether renewal is warranted, the party to whom the disposition is addressed should be deemed to have the right to demand a fair review based on reasonable criteria regarding renewal, with the expectation that renewal will be granted absent special circumstances if the criteria are satisfied after receiving a fair review based on reasonable criteria.\\n\\nHere, “fair review” means not only that the renewal decision must be reviewed according to objective and reasonable criteria rather than the administrative agency’s arbitrariness, but also that review criteria must be prepared and published in advance so as to provide the party to whom the disposition is addressed with foreseeability regarding the review standards and methods and to enable post hoc review of whether the renewal decision was made fairly according to reasonable criteria (see Supreme Court Decision 2010DU1835, decided January 13, 2011, and others).\\n\\nTo change a minor matter among the review criteria previously published, or to clarify or make more concrete a somewhat unclear and abstract part, but going beyond that and making a material change at a point when the review period has already elapsed or substantially elapsed so as to determine the renewal decision of the party to whom the disposition is addressed, is directly contrary to the nature of the renewal system and the requirement that a fair review be conducted according to the review criteria published in advance. Therefore, unless there are special circumstances such as the existence of a substantial public interest necessity compelling abolition of the renewal system itself or a drastic reduction from the previous number of renewal candidates, or the enactment or amendment of the relevant statutes and regulations, such change should be deemed impermissible.\\n\\n2. According to the reasons of the judgment below and the evidence duly admitted, the following circumstances can be found.\\n\\na. The Defendant enacted the “Guidelines for the Implementation of the Duty Travel Agency for Attracting Chinese Group Tourists” (hereinafter referred to as the “Guidelines at Issue”) in order to carry out the designation and management, etc. of the “Duty Travel Agency for Attracting Chinese Group Tourists” (hereinafter referred to as the “Duty Travel Agency”) to be recommended to the Chinese government. Around May 2013, the Defendant newly established Article 3-2 of the Guidelines at Issue and introduced a “Duty Travel Agency renewal system,” under which the status of Duty Travel Agency is renewed through a reexamination once every two years.\\n\\nb. Around September 2013, when the Defendant had introduced the above “Duty Travel Agency renewal system,” it set the criterion that the status of Duty Travel Agency would be renewed if the total score for each evaluation area, item, and indicator was 75 points or more (hereinafter referred to as the “prior disposition criteria”), and notified the Duty Travel Agencies thereof through the President of the Korea Association of Travel Agents.\\n\\nc. The Plaintiff was newly designated as a Duty Travel Agency pursuant to the Guidelines at Issue on April 11, 2006. The Defendant conducted a renewal review under the prior disposition criteria and renewed the Plaintiff’s status as a Duty Travel Agency on December 5, 2013. Around that time, the Defendant notified the Plaintiff and other Duty Travel Agencies that it would continuously monitor occupancy performance, product prices, administrative sanction history, whether low-priced products were sold, and the ratio of sales of high-value-added products, which had generally been considered under the prior disposition criteria as well, and reflect such matters in the renewal-system evaluation conducted every two years.\\n\\nd. When the Defendant found that some Duty Travel Agencies had increasingly caused harm by violations such as hiring unqualified guides and failing to properly fulfill the duty to report unauthorized departures, the Defendant, in order to strengthen sanctions therefor, partially changed the respective evaluation areas, items, indicators, and point allocations, etc. of the prior disposition criteria around March 23, 2016, and decided not to renew the status of Duty Travel Agency for those agencies whose evaluation score was below 70 points or for those agencies with 70 points or more but had been deducted 6 points or more due to administrative dispositions (such as unqualified guides), but applied these changed criteria without publishing them in advance to the renewal review (hereinafter referred to as the “changed disposition criteria”).\\n\\ne. Under the changed disposition criteria, the Plaintiff received 77 points, exceeding the 70-point renewal threshold, but during the renewal-system evaluation period from around January 2014 to around October 2015, the Plaintiff had been deducted 8 points due to administrative dispositions imposed for violations such as hiring unqualified guides and failing to report unauthorized departures, thus exceeding the 6-point disqualification threshold.\\n\\nf. The Defendant initially notified the Plaintiff on March 28, 2016, that it would redesignate the Plaintiff as a Duty Travel Agency, but later, upon belatedly confirming that it had overlooked the fact that the Plaintiff’s deduction due to administrative dispositions was 8 points, thereby exceeding the 6-point disqualification threshold for redesignation, the Defendant again notified the Plaintiff on November 4, 2016, that it was ex officio canceling the Plaintiff’s redesignation as a Duty Travel Agency (hereinafter referred to as the “Disposition at Issue”).\\n\\n3. Examining these facts in light of the foregoing legal principles, the following conclusion may be reached.\\n\\na. The changed disposition criteria constitute a material change to the prior disposition criteria, which had determined renewal based on the total score, by making renewal of the Duty Travel Agency status be denied solely on the ground that 6 points or more had been deducted due to administrative dispositions, regardless of the total score. In addition, after the two-year review period (January 2014 to December 2015) had already ended, and during the process of reviewing whether renewal would be granted, the Defendant materially changed the review criteria around March 23, 2016, and, by applying the changed review criteria, ex officio canceled the Plaintiff’s redesignation as a Duty Travel Agency, thereby ultimately issuing the Disposition at Issue that denied renewal.\\n\\nb. The Defendant argues that because some Duty Travel Agencies had increasingly engaged in violations such as hiring unqualified guides, there was a need to strengthen sanctions; however, this merely constitutes a reason to intensify enforcement against violations and to impose strict sanctions as prescribed by the Tourism Promotion Act and other relevant statutes and regulations. It is difficult to view this as a substantial public interest necessity requiring a change in the criteria previously published by the Defendant in connection with the Duty Travel Agency renewal system so that the number of designated Duty Travel Agencies had to be drastically reduced. Imposing an additional sanction of renewal denial according to the changed criteria after the fact also violates the principle that sanctions for violations must be imposed not according to the statutes, regulations, or disposition criteria at the time of the sanctioning disposition, but according to the statutes, regulations, or disposition criteria at the time of the violation (see Supreme Court Decision 2015DU50474, decided February 18, 2016, and others).\\n\\nc. Therefore, the Defendant’s decision, based on the criteria changed after the fact, to deny renewal of the Plaintiff’s status as a Duty Travel Agency should be deemed unlawful, contrary to the legislative purpose of the system of prior publication of disposition criteria and also contrary to the demand for fair review derived from the nature of the renewal system and the principle of due process, unless there are other special circumstances such as the existence of a substantial public interest necessity compelling abolition of the Duty Travel Agency renewal system itself or a drastic reduction in the number of Duty Travel Agencies to be renewed, or the enactment or amendment of the relevant statutes and regulations.\\n\\n4. Nevertheless, the court below determined that the Disposition at Issue did not violate Article 20, Paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedures Act and did not constitute unlawfulness arising from deviation from or abuse of discretion in a discretionary act. The court below’s judgment contains an error that affected the result by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the duty to publish disposition criteria in advance under the Administrative Procedures Act, and the assertion of the grounds for final appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n5. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated in the case."}

{"[2018DU52204]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Requirements for the application of a request for measures under Article 84(1) of the Credit Cooperatives Act (Ground One of the Grounds for Appeal)\\na. Contents of the relevant statutes and notice\\n(1) Article 83 of the Credit Cooperatives Act provides for the Financial Services Commission’s supervision, etc. over credit cooperatives.
